targets.name: AdderBoard: smallest transformer (fewest unique parameters) adding two 10-digit numbers
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: AdderBoard (github.com/anadim/AdderBoard) is a public leaderboard for the smallest autoregressive transformer that adds two integers in [0, 9,999,999,999] with >= 99% accuracy on verify.py's fixed test (10 edge cases + 10,000 random pairs, seed 2025). Two boards: 'Trained weights' (learned by a generic algorithm) and 'Hand-coded weights' (constructive proofs). README at the last commit (07061de, 2026-03-26): trained leader 36 params, 100% (tbukic, 1-layer Qwen3-style, d=3, 1 head, head dim 4, ff 2, circular-arc embedding, K=rotation(Q), V=Q, tied O=Q^T); then 39 (99.91%), 41, 44, 45. Hand-coded leader 6* params (zcbtrak; the README footnote says strict counting gives 10 unique weight values, see issue #75), then 8, 10, 12, 20. IMPORTANT, checked live 2026-10-08: open issue #83 (lokimorty, 2026-03-11) claims a 28-parameter TRAINED model at 100% (d=3, 1h, hd=4, ff=2, signed-pair Q, tied K=V); on 2026-03-25 the maintainer wrote that code review confirms '28 parameters verified, no hidden buffers' and asked for the training pipeline before accepting it on the trained board; lokimorty posted training code the same day and the issue has had no further activity. Issue #76 (zcbtrak 6p 'trained' by coordinate descent) was rejected for the trained board. Other open claims: #89 warlockee 6p hand-coded, #85 Kiguli 7p hand-coded, #91/#90/#88 warlockee 49/58/62 trained, #74 lokimorty 47 trained. The repository has had no commits since 2026-03-26 (34 commits; README trained leader still 36). A new wave of unaccepted issue claims arrived 2026-10-14..19 (checked 2026-10-20): trained #98 Skyway1111 6p (d=2, 100% on verify.py), #103 cyz14 4 learned scalars (100% locally, architecture/counting review requested), #99 abgri 4 learned scalars in Skyway1111's d=2 family (99.71%, review request), #100 neilbauman21-hub 28p and 34p; hand-coded #97 Skyway1111 5p, #101 harishsg993010 5p, #102 cyz14 4 scalars, #100 4p (constructive) and 6p (strict). None is accepted. The effective (unaccepted) trained frontier is now 4-6 parameters, not 28, and the README still says 36.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a submission file (build_model + add) that (1) passes the repository's verify.py (sha256 1135b7cd1e335a3b50121cc9ebe68fdacafa235ba82e1d4d65554408db009ec9, commit 07061de) with seed 2025 at >= 99% on all 10,010 cases, run on this Mac from the saved file; (2) is a trained model: weights produced by a generic learning algorithm (gradient-based or otherwise generic optimiser that would train any architecture on any dataset) from freshly sampled addition data, with the training script, seed and checkpoint saved and re-runnable; (3) satisfies the README rules re-read at verification time (at least one self-attention layer, generic autoregressive decode, no addition-specific control flow in forward or the generation loop); and (4) has a unique-parameter count, counted conservatively (every tunable or hand-set non-universal scalar counts, including hard-coded projection values and norm weights; fixed sinusoidal/RoPE tables with a conventional base are free), that is STRICTLY LESS (direction: min) than the smallest entry in the 'Trained Weights' table of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anadim/AdderBoard/main/README.md re-fetched live immediately before claiming, AND strictly less than the conservatively re-counted parameter count of every trained claim in the live issue/PR list https://github.com/anadim/AdderBoard/issues (open or closed, including #83's 28) whose code the skeptic can download and which passes verify.py on this Mac. On 2026-10-20 the open trained claims go as low as 4 (#103, #99) and 6 (#98), so the bar is below those unless they fail the skeptic's re-run or conservative re-count. Submitting to the repository is NOT part of the target (would require the human's permission).

partial_wins.statement: A hand-coded (constructive) model passing verify.py at >= 99% whose unique-parameter count under conservative counting (every tunable or hand-set non-universal scalar counts, fixed RoPE/sinusoidal tables free) is strictly below the smallest entry of the live 'Hand-Coded Weights' table (counted the same conservative way, i.e. 10 for the current 6* leader) and below every hand-coded claim in the live issues (#89: 6, #85: 7, #97: 5, #101: 5, #102: 4, #100: 4 and 6) that passes verify.py, each re-counted conservatively.

A trained model (conditions 1-3 of the success criterion) whose conservatively counted unique-parameter count is strictly below the live README 'Trained Weights' leader (36 today) but not below the lowest verify.py-passing trained claim in the live issues (as low as 4 in #103 and #99 and 6 in #98, all unaccepted, on 2026-10-20): beats the published board, not the pending frontier.

A trained model with d_model = 2 (every width hyperparameter strictly smaller than the live trained leader's d=3/hd=4) that passes verify.py at >= 99%, with the training run reproducible from a saved seed on this Mac within 4 hours, even if its conservatively counted parameter count only ties the live leader.

targets.verification_method: Clone the repo at commit 07061de and confirm sha256 of verify.py matches the pin; run `python verify.py submissions/<file>.py` (CPU, PyTorch) and require QUALIFIED. Independently count parameters: enumerate every tensor and Python scalar used in forward, deduplicate tied tensors by identity, exclude only fixed sinusoidal/RoPE tables, count hard-coded non-universal values, and report the count. Read forward and add to confirm no carry logic or digit pairing in Python, that at least one attention layer with softmax over keys exists, and that decoding is generic token-by-token argmax. For the trained claim, re-run the saved training script with the saved seed and confirm it reaches a passing checkpoint, or load the saved checkpoint and confirm count and accuracy; also re-test on a different seed as a leakage sanity check. Re-fetch README and the issues list; download and run the code of every lower trained claim (today #83) and re-count it the same way. Under an hour on a 10-core Mac excluding any from-scratch retraining.
angles: Reproduce the 36-parameter architecture (d=3, 1 head, hd=4, ff=2, circular-arc digit embedding, K = rotation(Q), V = Q, O = Q^T) and ablate: tie or drop the remaining norm scales and the FF bias, share the embedding and unembedding, replace learned scalars by fixed constants that the rules treat as architecture (RoPE period), each time retraining to 100%.

Search architectures with d=2 and hd=2 (the hand-coded 6-12 param designs prove d=2 suffices for the computation) and train them with curriculum (reversed-digit format, carry-chain-heavy sampling) and many seeds in parallel on 10 cores; grokking-style long training with weight decay.

Distillation from the hand-coded 6-10 parameter solutions: initialise a d=2 model near a hand-coded solution's basin and train with noise so the result is legitimately 'trained' (keep the training log; declare the init).

Parameter-sharing tricks already accepted on the board (phase-tied Q, gate tying, norm folding) applied to the trained d=3 model, then re-train from scratch with the sharing structure fixed so the weights are learned rather than set.
Automated search: evolutionary search over tying patterns and fixed-vs-learned scalar choices with a 10-minute training budget per candidate, selecting on verify.py accuracy.
pitfalls: A model that passes because add does digit pairing, carry handling or any problem-specific control flow in Python is disqualified by the rules even if verify.py says QUALIFIED; verify.py checks accuracy only.

Undercounting: hard-coded non-universal scalars (e.g. a chosen RoPE period, a fixed Q projection matrix) are contested (issue #75); the skeptic counts conservatively, so a 'win' that depends on the lenient count is not a win here.

Test-set leakage: training on the seed-2025 test pairs is trivial cheating; the training script must sample fresh random pairs and the skeptic re-tests on a different seed as a sanity check (not for the record, which is seed 2025).
Nondeterministic training: a single lucky seed that cannot be reproduced is weak; save the checkpoint and seed so the result is checkable from the saved object.

Stale README: last commit 2026-03-26, last issue 2026-04-15; issue #83 (28 params trained, maintainer-verified count, acceptance pending) is the real bar unless the skeptic cannot run it or it fails verify.py; a 'win' at 29-35 params is partial win p2 only.

Generic-training rule: the maintainer rejected coordinate-descent 'training' of a hand-designed architecture (#76) and questioned #83 on the same ground; keep the training loop generic and document the init.

targets.name: MOONSHOT - 4x4 matrices with 47 multiplications in characteristic 0, or 3x3 matrices with 22
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: Two headline open problems of small-format fast matrix multiplication. (a) <4,4,4>: AlphaTensor (2022) found rank 47 over GF(2) only; AlphaEvolve (May 2025) found 48 over C; Dumas-Pernet-Sedoglavic (2025, arXiv:2506.13242) gave 48 over any ring with 1/2, with a 'more accurate' rational variant in March 2026 (arXiv:2603.18699); the Lille catalogue lists 48 and matmulcatalog lists F2 47 / Z 49 / C 48. No rank-47 scheme is known in characteristic 0 (or in any characteristic other than 2), and no integer rank-48 scheme is known. (b) <3,3,3>: Laderman's 23 (1976) is unbeaten; the general lower bound is 19, and Sep 2026 preprints prove 21 over GF(2) (arXiv:2609.06725, arXiv:2609.18722); a 2026 Zenodo note (record 18514533, 'On the Tensor Rank of 3x3 Matrix Multiplication: Barriers and Open Problems') surveys the barriers. Epoch AI lists the rank of the 4x4 tensor as a FrontierMath open problem. Any rank-47 scheme for 4x4 valid over Q (or over GF(3)), or any rank-22 scheme for 3x3 over any field, would be a major result. Live check 2026-10-08: Lille 4x4x4.html lists <4,4,4>:48 (Dumas-Pernet-Sedoglavic variant of AlphaEvolve, raw scheme uses 1/2, 1/4, 1/8); 3x3x3.html lists <3,3,3>:23 (Laderman 1976); Perminov table 4x4x4: ZT 49 / Z 49 / Q 48 and 3x3x3: 23/23/23; matmulcatalog 4x4x4: F2 47 / R-Q-Z 49 / C 48.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an explicit bilinear scheme, exactly verified over the claimed field, with EITHER (a) rank STRICTLY LESS (direction: min) than the rank listed on https://fmm.univ-lille.fr/4x4x4.html for <4,4,4> in a field of characteristic not equal to 2 (i.e. 47 or fewer over Q, Z or GF(p) with p odd; a scheme over Z/Q must be verified with exact integer/fraction arithmetic, a GF(p) scheme mod p), OR (b) rank STRICTLY LESS than the rank listed on https://fmm.univ-lille.fr/3x3x3.html for <3,3,3> over any field (22 or fewer, including GF(2)); with both pages, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sedoglavic/fmm_digest/master/fmm_sota.json, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dronperminov/FastMatrixMultiplication/master/docs/ranks.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/solven-eu/matmulcatalog/master/generated/COVERAGE.md re-fetched live immediately before claiming and none of them already listing an equal or lower rank in the claimed characteristic. A GF(2)-only rank-47 scheme for <4,4,4> does not count (AlphaTensor 2022). These two formats are excluded from fmm-catalogue-small-format-rank so a win is claimed once, here.

partial_wins.statement: A rank-48 scheme for <4,4,4> with all coefficients in Z (or in {-1,0,1}), exactly verified over Z, strictly below the live 'Z rank' / 'ZT rank' entries for 4x4x4 in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dronperminov/FastMatrixMultiplication/master/docs/ranks.md and absent from that repository's live schemes/results/Z and /ZT directories and from MerlijnW70's repository (this format is excluded from fmm-ternary-integer-ring-upgrade so it is counted only here).

A lifting milestone for 4x4: a rank-47 scheme for <4,4,4> exactly verified over Z/4Z (all Brent equations hold mod 4) where the live Lille page, Perminov's table and COVERAGE.md list no rank-47 scheme outside GF(2); the certificate is the scheme file plus the mod-4 check.

A machine-checked lower bound: a proof that no rank-22 scheme for <3,3,3> exists over GF(2) (i.e. rank >= 23 over GF(2), improving the published bound of 21 from arXiv:2609.06725 / 2609.18722), delivered as a SAT encoding plus DRAT/LRAT-checked UNSAT certificate or a Lean proof, with the encoding independently re-derived by the skeptic. Recorded as a result; claimed only after the 3-skeptic confirmation.

targets.verification_method: Load U, V, W (or the product list), verify the Brent equations exactly over the claimed field (integer/fraction arithmetic, or mod p), count rank-one terms. For the 4x4 claim, confirm the coefficients are meaningful in the stated characteristic (no 1/2 in an odd-characteristic claim unless reduced mod p; no 1/2 at all for Z). Re-fetch the two Lille pages, fmm_sota.json, Perminov's docs/ranks.md and COVERAGE.md. For p2 verify mod 4; for p3 re-run drat-trim/cake_lpr or lake build on the certificate. Minutes on this Mac (the DRAT check may take longer but must finish within an hour or the certificate is rejected as unverified).
angles: Lift the GF(2) rank-47 AlphaTensor scheme: treat it as a solution mod 2 and attempt Hensel lifting to Z/4, Z/8 ... with the linearised Brent system; an obstruction at the first step is informative, a successful lift to Z/2^k plus rational reconstruction would be the result.
Flip-graph walks from the rank-48 schemes (Dumas et al. rational variant, AlphaEvolve C variant, and the Z/ZT 49s) over GF(3) and GF(5) looking for a 47 in odd characteristic, then lift.

Symmetric ansatz: impose the Z3 cyclic symmetry (A->B->C) or the (4x4) isotropy subgroups used in Flip Graphs with Symmetry, reducing 4x4x4 rank-47 to a much smaller polynomial system; try Groebner/SAT on the reduced system over GF(3).

For 3x3x3 rank 22 over GF(2): a SAT encoding with full symmetry breaking is large but the Sep 2026 lower-bound-21 papers give structure (which orbits are forced); use their invariants to prune and run a bounded search for 22 over GF(2) rather than Q.
Addition-count side (p3): run Perminov's ternary_addition_reducer and plinopt on the ZT rank-23 scheme with randomized common-subexpression elimination to try to beat the listed count.
pitfalls: Rank 47 over GF(2) is known (AlphaTensor 2022) and rank 48 with 1/2 is known; re-deriving either is not a win. Verify the characteristic claim exactly.
Border rank 47 or numerically approximate decompositions (residual 1e-6) are not rank; floating-point ALS output needs exact rounding and re-verification.
Lower bounds: 19 for 3x3 general and 21 over GF(2) (Sep 2026); claims of rank 20 or less over GF(2) contradict proven bounds and indicate a checker bug.
Addition-count improvements for 3x3x3:23 or 4x4x4:48 are the fmm-additive-complexity-records target, not a partial win here.

targets.name: Fast matrix multiplication: fewer additions for a fixed best-known rank (straight-line program records)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: For a fixed FMM scheme rank, the number of additions/subtractions in the straight-line program (SLP) that evaluates the scheme is a secondary but citable record: <2,2,2>:7 needs 15 (proved optimal), <3,3,3>:23 was reduced to 58 additions in Perminov, arXiv:2512.21980 (Dec 2025; cf. arXiv:2601.05272 claiming 59 total operations under its own convention), and the repository now holds a 55-addition file (3x3x3_m23_cr55_cn122_ZT_reduced.json; CHANGELOG 19/10/2026: 'Add November 2025 benchmark schemes with fewer additions required'), and Perminov's repository publishes addition-reduced ternary schemes for every format up to 16x16x16 (schemes/results/addition_reduced_ZT, reduced_known.json; tool ternary_addition_reducer) while the Lille catalogue cites 'best-known complexity' variants per format (e.g. 4x4x4:48 by Dumas-Pernet-Sedoglavic-Stapleton-Tichavsky 2026) and matmulcatalog publishes an 'adds' column (naive count nz(U)+nz(V)+nz(W)-2r-np) and warns its SLP counts are upper bounds from a greedy heuristic. Addition reduction is a well-posed combinatorial optimisation (common-subexpression elimination over ternary linear maps) where heuristics still find improvements, so laptop-scale search is realistic. This entry owns ALL addition-count wins (including for <3,3,3>:23 and <4,4,4>:48); rank improvements belong to the catalogue/moonshot entries. Live check 2026-10-20: addition_reduced_ZT holds 329 files (195 on 2026-10-08), several formats with multiple counts (3x3x3_m23_cr55_cn122, cr56_cn120, cr57_cn119, cr58_cn119/120/122 and cr60; 2x2x9_m32_cr50 and cr59; 4x4x4_m49_cr156_cn474 and cr159_fv100_cn474, i.e. the ternary 4x4 files are rank 49, not 48); reduced_known.json (read 2026-10-08, not re-read) lists '3x3x3-23': Z 60, Z2 60 and '4x4x4-49': Z 325, Z2 196.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an explicit straight-line program (list of linear forms over the inputs, r products, and linear forms producing the outputs) for a format <n,m,p> with max(n,m,p) <= 8 and rank r equal to the best rank listed for that format in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sedoglavic/fmm_digest/master/fmm_sota.json (re-fetched live), that (1) is verified symbolically to compute the full product A*B exactly over Z, and (2) uses a number of additions/subtractions STRICTLY LESS (direction: min) than the smallest reduced addition count for that format and rank in Perminov's live repository (the addition_reduced_ZT scheme file for the format, reduced_known.json, docs/additions.md, README and CHANGELOG) re-fetched live immediately before claiming, counted under Perminov's 'reduced' convention (each binary +/- between already-computed quantities counts one; multiplication by -1 is free; multiplication by any other scalar is not allowed in a ternary SLP), AND below any lower count published for that format and rank on the live Lille per-format page's cited complexity variant and in matmulcatalog's live COVERAGE.md 'adds' column. If the Lille rank for the format is attained only with non-ternary coefficients, the comparison is against the best count in the same coefficient class as the candidate. The reference count is the MINIMUM cr value over all files for that format and rank in the live directory (formats have several files). Each scheme is claimed once: a scheme that also lowers the rank is a rank target, not this one.

partial_wins.statement: A rank-23 SLP for <3,3,3> with strictly fewer additions than the live reduced count for 3x3x3 in Perminov's repository (55 in the live directory on 2026-10-20; 58 in arXiv:2512.21980), verified symbolically, under the same counting convention.

A rank-48 SLP for <4,4,4> over Q with strictly fewer total operations than the 'best-known complexity' variant cited on https://fmm.univ-lille.fr/4x4x4.html (Dumas-Pernet-Sedoglavic-Stapleton-Tichavsky 2026), counted under that paper's convention (additions plus scalar multiplications), verified symbolically.
Strict reduced-addition improvements for at least three distinct formats with max dim <= 8 in one shift, each verified symbolically and each below the live addition_reduced_ZT count.

targets.verification_method: Parse the SLP (sequence of assignments t_k = +/- t_i +/- t_j over inputs A_ij, B_jl, intermediate sums, r products, and output assignments). Evaluate it with sympy (or exact integer evaluation at many random integer matrices plus one symbolic pass) and confirm every output equals the corresponding entry of A*B. Count the additions under the stated convention (exclude negations, exclude the r multiplications). Load the reference scheme from Perminov's addition_reduced_ZT directory (and reduced_known.json), recount its additions with the same counter to calibrate the convention, and compare. Re-fetch the repository, the Lille page and COVERAGE.md. Minutes on this Mac.
angles: Run Perminov's ternary_addition_reducer and werekorren's fmm_add_reduction with many random seeds and different pairing heuristics on each addition_reduced_ZT scheme for max dim <= 8; the tools are heuristic, so parallel restarts on 10 cores often shave a few additions.

Change the scheme, not just the SLP: walk the flip graph among rank-equal schemes (the 'alternative scheme finding' in Perminov's repo) and reduce additions for each; sparser U, V, W typically give shorter SLPs.

Exact CSE as an optimisation problem: encode common-subexpression elimination for the three linear maps (U, V, W^T) as an ILP or SAT instance for small formats (<2,2,3>, <2,3,3>, <3,3,3>) with a bound one below the record, to either find a shorter SLP or certify optimality for the given scheme.

Exploit the W map's structure: outputs share many subexpressions; try the 'alternative basis' trick (Karstadt-Schwartz) with change of basis counted separately only if the record's convention allows it; otherwise keep the standard basis.
Search over the sign/orientation choices of the ternary scheme (U, V, W defined up to scaling of each product by +/-1 and permutation) to maximise shared subexpressions before CSE.
pitfalls: Convention mismatch: additions-only vs total operations vs 'alternative basis' counts; a candidate must be compared under the reference's convention after recounting the reference with the same counter.

Counting bugs: negations are free but a subtraction is one operation; reusing a subexpression across U and V is allowed only if it is actually the same linear form of the same inputs (A-forms and B-forms never share).
Rank must equal the catalogue's best rank for the format; fewer additions at a higher rank is not a record here.
Perminov's repo updates weekly and may already contain a lower count in a file the attacker did not look at; re-fetch the directory listing and CHANGELOG at verification time.
An SLP that is correct only modulo 2 (from working over GF(2)) is not a valid integer SLP; verify over Z.
Multiple files per format: compare against the smallest cr in the live directory, not the first one found.

targets.name: Fast matrix multiplication: beat a best-known rank in the Lille FMM catalogue for a small format
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: For a matrix-multiplication format <n,m,p> with max(n,m,p) <= 16, OTHER THAN <3,3,3> and <4,4,4> (those two are the separate moonshot target fmm-4x4x4-rank47-3x3x3-rank22), find a bilinear (non-commutative) scheme with strictly fewer multiplications (tensor rank) than the best known value over ANY ring. Live scoreboards: Sedoglavic's Lille catalogue (fmm.univ-lille.fr; JSON digest fmm_sota.json, 5456 formats with 2<=n<=m<=p<=32, regenerated 2026-10-19), Perminov's status table (docs/ranks.md since the 22 Oct 2026 move out of the README; ZT/Z/Q columns) and MerlijnW70's fmm-schemes. Ranks checked live 2026-10-08: <2,2,2>:7, <2,2,3>:11, <2,3,3>:15, <2,4,5>:32, <3,4,5>:47, <3,3,6>:40, <3,4,7>:63, <5,5,5>:93, <6,6,6>:153, <2,4,6>:39, <2,3,10>:50. The frontier moved a lot in 2025-2026 (AlphaEvolve May 2025; flip graphs with symmetry arXiv:2502.04514; Perminov's open-source flip-graph framework arXiv:2603.02398 and meta flip graph arXiv:2606.02480, which improved 207 formats up to 16x16x16; Perminov CHANGELOG rank improvements as late as 28 Sep 2026, e.g. <4,4,8>:95, <7,7,15>:507, <15,16,16>:2223; after the 2026-10-08 check, fmm_sota.json of 2026-10-09 adds Khoruzhii, Gelss and Pokutta (-1 on even square formats 14..32) and M. Stoch (cloudroom-math; Perminov CHANGELOG 09/10/2026), which within max dim 16 gives <4,6,15>:261, <9,11,11>:710, <14,14,14>:1593, <14,14,15>:1789, <14,14,16>:1894 and <16,16,16>:2236; the 2026-10-19 regeneration (Witteveen's new results) adds <8,10,13>:684, <8,10,14>:724, <9,11,13>:833, <10,13,14>:1150, <11,13,15>:1362, <11,14,14>:1367 and <13,13,15>:1591; MerlijnW70 ternary batches merged 29 Sep and 2 Oct 2026). Most formats with max dim <= 6 are heavily mined; mid-size rectangular formats (max dim 7-16) are where new ranks keep appearing. Perminov's table marks many ZT/Z cells '(?)' (meaning undocumented; the table says previous ranks are 'given in brackets'), so do not read '(?)' as 'open'.
targets.success_criterion:
Success means an explicit bilinear scheme (U, V, W coefficient matrices or an equivalent list of rank-one terms) for a format with max(n,m,p) <= 16 and sorted(n,m,p) not in {(3,3,3),(4,4,4)}, whose number of rank-one terms r is STRICTLY LESS (direction: min) than ALL of: the rank listed for the sorted format in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sedoglavic/fmm_digest/master/fmm_sota.json, the rank on https://fmm.univ-lille.fr/xx

.html, the minimum over the ZT/Z/Q columns for that format in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dronperminov/FastMatrixMultiplication/master/docs/ranks.md, and the lowest rank for that format in https://github.com/MerlijnW70/fmm-schemes (every one re-fetched live immediately before claiming; the scheme beats the minimum over all four). The scheme must be verified in exact arithmetic (integers/fractions, or mod p for GF(p)) over the ring it claims; a scheme valid only over GF(2) counts here ONLY if r is also strictly below the GF(2) rank (F2 column) for that format in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/solven-eu/matmulcatalog/master/generated/COVERAGE.md (otherwise see partial win p2). A scheme obtained by composing, padding or block-splitting known schemes does not count if the resulting rank equals a value already listed (the Lille table has a 'construction' column listing such derivations). Ternary/integer re-derivations of a rank already attained over Q are NOT this target (see fmm-ternary-integer-ring-upgrade); fewer additions at an existing rank is NOT this target (see fmm-additive-complexity-records).

partial_wins.statement: A new rank for a format with 17 <= max(n,m,p) <= 32 (outside Perminov's 16x16x16 table but inside the Lille catalogue): an exactly verified scheme whose rank is strictly below the live fmm_sota.json entry and the live Lille per-format page for that format, and not a plain composition already listed in the Lille 'construction' column.

A GF(2)-only improvement: an exactly verified (mod 2) scheme whose rank is strictly below the F2 column for its format in the live matmulcatalog COVERAGE.md AND below every GF(2)-valid scheme for that format in Perminov's live repository and MerlijnW70's repository, for a format where the characteristic-0 best rank is already <= the new GF(2) rank (so it is not a new rank overall).

targets.verification_method: Parse the candidate scheme (JSON U, V, W integer/rational matrices, or a Maple-style product list as in the Lille *_raw.mpl files). With exact fractions/sympy, form the r products m_k = (sum_ij U_k,ij A_ij)*(sum_jl V_k,jl B_jl) and check that for every (i,l) sum_k W_k,il m_k equals the symbolic entry (A*B)_il with exact coefficients over the claimed ring (reduce mod p for GF(p)); equivalently check the Brent equations. Count r after dropping zero terms. Re-fetch fmm_sota.json, the Lille per-format page, Perminov's docs/ranks.md (all three ZT/Z/Q columns) and MerlijnW70's repo, and compare against the sorted format (rank is invariant under axis permutation/transposition). For p2 also re-fetch COVERAGE.md and the GF(2) schemes. Whole check runs in minutes on a 10-core Mac even for 16x16x16.
angles: Flip-graph random walks (Kauers-Moosbauer) with 'plus' transitions and reductions, seeded from the current best scheme of a '(?)'-marked format and its neighbours (e.g. start from <2,4,6>:39 or <2,3,10>:50 and from one-larger formats, then restrict).

Meta flip graph (Perminov): run flips on a larger format and project/peel to smaller formats; alternate ternary {-1,0,1} and GF(2)/GF(3) coefficient domains, then lift via Hensel/rational reconstruction to Z or Q.

Symmetry-restricted search: impose a cyclic Z3 or S3 symmetry (or the stabilizer listed on the Lille page) to shrink the flip-graph state space and search for rank r-1 schemes with that symmetry, as in Flip Graphs with Symmetry (arXiv:2502.04514).

Alternating least squares / Levenberg-Marquardt CP decomposition with sparsity and rounding to ternary, then exact verification, for rectangular formats with max dim 7-10 where the gap between rank and naive product is largest.

SAT/SMT encoding over GF(2) for rank r-1 of small formats (<2,2,k>, <2,3,k>) with symmetry breaking, then lift to Z; the GF(2) lower-bound literature (arXiv:2609.06725) tells you where this is futile.
pitfalls: Numerical 'decompositions' with floating-point residual 1e-8 are not schemes: only an exactly verified identity counts. Border-rank (approximate) decompositions are a different quantity and do not beat a rank entry.

Permutations and transposes: <n,m,p> rank is invariant under axis permutations and transposition; compare against the catalogue entry for the sorted format. Also check Perminov's and MerlijnW70's tables: the Lille digest lags them by days.
Schemes valid only in characteristic 2 (e.g. AlphaTensor's 4x4x4:47) do not beat a characteristic-0 entry; state the ring and verify exactly in it. A scheme using 1/2 is not valid over Z or GF(2).

Trivial composition of known schemes (Kronecker products, padding, block splits) reproduces catalogue entries; the catalogue already lists those constructions, so an 'improvement' that equals a composition is a bookkeeping error.
Counting bugs: r must be the number of rank-one terms after removing zero terms and merging duplicates; a term with a zero W-row still counts.

Scope split: <3,3,3> and <4,4,4> belong to the moonshot entry; ring upgrades (ternary/integer at an existing rank) belong to fmm-ternary-integer-ring-upgrade; addition counts belong to fmm-additive-complexity-records. Do not double-claim.
The Lille digest lags Perminov/MerlijnW70 by days and the catalogue front page says underlying data are being reconstructed; the bar is the minimum over all live tables, never the Lille number alone.

targets.name: Fast matrix multiplication: best-known rank with ternary/integer coefficients where only rational or complex schemes are known
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: Several best-known FMM ranks are attained only with coefficients outside {-1,0,1} or outside Z (denominators), so they do not run over GF(2) or rings without 1/2. Confirmed live 2026-10-08 from Perminov's status table (ZT / Z / Q columns): <2,4,5>: 33 / 33 / 32 (the Lille 2x4x5 rank-32 scheme uses 1/2 throughout); <3,4,7>: 64 / 64 / 63; <4,4,4>: 49 / 49 / 48 (uses 1/2, 1/4, 1/8; this format is handled by the moonshot entry's partial win, not here). Across the 680 formats up to 16x16x16 (2026-10-20): 297 rows have ZT > Q, 16 rows have ZT > Z (integer known, ternary not), and the repo's coefficient-set status is 383 ZT / 10 Z / 287 Q schemes. The June 2026 paper (arXiv:2606.02480) closed 84 such ring gaps; MerlijnW70 ternary batches merged 29 Sep and 2 Oct 2026 and a ZT 2x9x10:140 rediscovery on 30 Sep 2026 closed more; cloudroom-math schemes (matyasstoch, 9 Oct 2026) and near-optimal ZT schemes from mizopl (19 Oct 2026) changed the table again. Finding a ternary or integer scheme at the known Q rank (or any strictly lower ZT/Z rank that does not beat the overall best rank) is a citable 'ring upgrade' and exactly what the 2026 flip-graph tooling targets.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an explicit bilinear scheme for a format <n,m,p> with max(n,m,p) <= 16 and sorted(n,m,p) != (4,4,4), whose coefficients all lie in {-1,0,1} (ternary, 'ZT') or all in Z (integer), with rank r such that (1) r is STRICTLY LESS (direction: min) than the 'ZT rank' (for a ternary claim) or the 'Z rank' (for an integer claim) listed for that format in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dronperminov/FastMatrixMultiplication/master/docs/ranks.md re-fetched live immediately before claiming; (2) r is GREATER THAN OR EQUAL to the minimum over the live ZT/Z/Q columns for that format and to the live fmm_sota.json rank, i.e. the scheme does NOT beat the overall best rank (a scheme that does is the catalogue target fmm-catalogue-small-format-rank, never both); (3) no scheme of rank <= r in the same coefficient class already exists in the live schemes/results/ZT (or /Z) directory of that repository or in https://github.com/MerlijnW70/fmm-schemes; (4) the Brent equations are verified exactly over Z with integer arithmetic (so the scheme is valid over every ring), not merely mod 2. Equalling the format's Q rank is the natural goal but any strict ZT or Z improvement satisfying (1)-(4) counts.

partial_wins.statement: A lifting milestone: for a format where the live ZT and Z columns both exceed the live Q column, an exactly verified scheme of rank equal to that Q rank with all coefficients in Z/4Z (or Z/p^2 for an odd prime p), i.e. a modular lift one step beyond GF(p) that is not yet an integer scheme, where no integer or ternary scheme of that rank exists in the live repository.

A verified negative result for a specific format with max(n,m,p) <= 5 where the live ZT column exceeds the live Q column (e.g. <2,4,5>: ZT 33 vs Q 32): a SAT/ILP encoding of 'rank <= Q rank over GF(2) (or with ternary coefficients)' together with a DRAT/LRAT-checked UNSAT certificate (checked by drat-trim or cake_lpr on this Mac), with the encoding re-derived and spot-checked by the skeptic. Recorded as a result, not claimed as a record.

targets.verification_method: Load the candidate as U, V, W matrices (Perminov's JSON format, 'Scheme File Formats' in the README). Assert every coefficient is in {-1,0,1} (ternary claim) or in Z (integer claim). Verify the Brent equations exactly with integer arithmetic: for all i,j,k,l,s,t, sum_r U_r[i,j] V_r[k,l] W_r[s,t] = [j==k][i==s][l==t] (mind the file's index convention; permute axes if it stores the transposed product). Count r after removing zero terms. Re-fetch Perminov's docs/ranks.md (all three columns) and the ZT/Z directories, fmm_sota.json, the Lille per-format page and the MerlijnW70 repo; confirm condition (2) (r does not beat the overall best rank) and condition (3) (no existing scheme of rank <= r in the same coefficient class). For p1, verify the Brent equations modulo the stated modulus. For p2, re-run the DRAT checker on the certificate. Seconds to minutes on this Mac for formats up to 16x16x16.
angles: Ternary flip-graph search started from the known Q scheme after clearing denominators: multiply through by 2^k, reduce mod a prime, run flips in GF(p) to find a rank-equal scheme with small coefficients, then lift to Z by Hensel lifting / rational reconstruction and verify exactly.

Direct ternary flip graph (dronperminov/ternary_flip_graph) seeded from the nearest ZT scheme of rank r+1 for the target format, running 'reduction' moves with coefficient constraint {-1,0,1}; parallel walks on 10 cores with restarts.

Change of basis: a Q scheme with denominators 2^k is sometimes equivalent under invertible sparse basis changes (A -> PAQ etc.) to an integer scheme; search the orbit of the 48-term 4x4x4 scheme and the 32-term 2x4x5 scheme under the isotropy group with lattice-reduction-style pruning for an integral representative.

SAT/ILP in GF(2) for <2,4,5> rank 32 (the F2 rank is 33): if a GF(2) rank-32 scheme exists, try lifting; if a short UNSAT proof emerges, that is a separate (non-claimed here) negative result worth recording.
Meta flip graph: search a bigger format (e.g. <2,4,10>, <4,4,8>) in ternary coefficients and peel zero slices to recover ternary schemes of the smaller target format.
pitfalls: Verifying only mod 2 and claiming an integer scheme: a ternary scheme must satisfy the Brent equations over Z exactly (signs matter), otherwise it is a GF(2) scheme only.

Perminov's table columns are the best ranks found in that coefficient set; 'Q rank' already includes schemes with 1/2. A scheme with coefficients in {-2,...,2} is 'Z', not 'ZT'; label the claim precisely.

Duplicate work: the repository adds rediscoveries weekly (ZT 2x9x10:140 on 30 Sep 2026; MerlijnW70 batches on 29 Sep and 2 Oct 2026). Re-fetch docs/ranks.md, README, CHANGELOG and the ZT/Z directories at verification time; a scheme already present is not a win.

Index-convention errors (row-major vs column-major, which factor is transposed) make a correct scheme look wrong or a wrong scheme look right under a permuted test; verify against the explicit symbolic product A*B.
If the new ternary/integer scheme also beats the overall best rank, it is the catalogue target's win, not this one; never claim the same scheme under two targets.
<4,4,4> is excluded here: a ternary/integer rank-48 scheme for 4x4 is partial win p1 of the moonshot entry fmm-4x4x4-rank47-3x3x3-rank22.

targets.name: Packomania csqv: circles in the unit square with maximised sum of radii (AlphaEvolve problem), beat a table entry
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: Place N circles of variable radii inside the unit square, non-overlapping, maximising the sum of radii: AlphaEvolve's 'packing circles to maximise sum of radii' problem (N=26, 32). Packomania (E. Specht) revived the csqv table on 23 Jul 2026; it is the primary record table, covering N=1..500 except N = 493 (no row on csqv.html or in txt/sumradii.txt, and csqv493.txt returns 404, 2026-10-18) plus 84 larger N up to 10000, last update 30-Sep-2026 (per the page), with coordinates at csqv/txt/csqv<N>.txt and a one-column digest csqv/txt/sumradii.txt. Records now come from LLM-evolved optimisers (OpenEvolve/ShinkaEvolve, Haowei Lin, Jason Liang's circle-packing-sota, Wes Sander's MoltFire, Jean-Rene Denoual's 200+ entries in Sep 2026, arXiv:2609.05093 'Breaking 10 Packomania records for $28'). Live values 2026-10-08: N=26: 2.635983084919, N=27: 2.685978684198, N=30: 2.842668747462, N=32: 2.939572771205, N=46: 3.539571078547, N=48: 3.616465058812. CRITICAL FREEZE: packomania.com/pending-requests.html states that all csqv submissions in October 2026 are saved but not processed until November 2026, and lists Jason Liang's 05-Oct-2026 submission of 472 candidates for N=63..10000; his public repo (jasonzliang/circle-packing-sota, commits 2026-10-04/05) claims 462 wins above N=100 versus the 2026-10-05 table and publishes the coordinates. So for N>62 the live table is NOT the frontier; the public repos are the admissible secondary record sources and must be beaten too.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an explicit list of N circles (x_i, y_i, r_i) with N <= 200, such that (1) every circle lies inside [0,1]^2 and every pair is interior-disjoint, certified rigorously (exact rational arithmetic on the saved decimal coordinates, or interval arithmetic with a positive margin after shrinking radii by the rounding error), and (2) the sum of radii computed from the certified (possibly shrunken) radii is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max), by at least 1e-11, than the 'sum of radii' value for that N in https://www.packomania.com/csqv/csqv.html re-fetched live immediately before claiming, AND strictly greater by at least 1e-11 than the best value for that N in the live public repositories https://github.com/jasonzliang/circle-packing-sota (every sota/*/comparison.md and every .pck for that N, re-fetched live and re-certified with the same exact checker) and https://github.com/RasimAbiyev/circle-packing-explorations, AND for N=26 also strictly greater than the live EinsteinArena leaderboard best. Ties, improvements below the table's 12-decimal precision, and improvements over the frozen table that do not also beat the public repositories are not wins. The claim is for the verified construction; emailing Packomania needs explicit permission from the human.

partial_wins.statement: A certified improvement for some N <= 50 (the heavily mined range where AlphaEvolve, Yiping Wang, Pokutta, Specht, Liang, Heap and Garg all compete), strictly above the live table value AND above every value for that N in the live jasonzliang / RasimAbiyev repositories by >= 1e-11, with the same exact-rational feasibility certificate.

A certified improvement for N = 26 or N = 32 (the two AlphaEvolve benchmark instances), strictly above the live Packomania value, above the live jasonzliang/RasimAbiyev values, and above the best value on the live EinsteinArena circle-packing leaderboard (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/circle-packing, currently 2.6359830849176076 for N=26), evaluated with the exact feasibility check (no 1e-6 or 1e-9 slack).

Certified improvements for three or more distinct N in 51..200 in one shift, each strictly above the live table value AND above every live jasonzliang/RasimAbiyev value for that N by >= 1e-11 (beating only the frozen table is explicitly NOT a win for N > 62: jasonzliang's public .pck files already beat it for most N > 100), with the solver code and seeds saved so the skeptic can re-run one of them.

targets.verification_method: Independent checker in pure Python with fractions.Fraction: read the saved coordinates as decimal strings, convert to exact rationals, check 0 <= x_i - r_i, x_i + r_i <= 1 (same for y), and (x_i-x_j)^2 + (y_i-y_j)^2 >= (r_i+r_j)^2 for all pairs, as exact inequalities (touching allowed). If the submitted radii violate by a tiny epsilon, the attacker must supply shrunken radii that pass exactly; the score is the exact sum of the passing radii. Compare with the live table value for that N parsed from csqv.html / sumradii.txt (12 decimals) and with csqv<N>.txt's radii summed exactly; then fetch every jasonzliang .pck / comparison.md value and RasimAbiyev table value for that N and apply the same exact checker to their coordinates (their verify_and_compare.py uses float64 with 1e-9 tolerance and is only a second opinion; solver-sm-radical-v6-n27/exact_check.py in that repo is their exact variant). Minutes on this Mac for N <= 200.
angles: Start from the published csqv<N>.txt configuration, perturb (swap two circles, move one circle to a gap, change the contact graph) and re-solve the KKT system by sequential linear programming / SLSQP on (x, y, r) with the overlap constraints active; repeat with thousands of restarts across 10 cores.

Contact-graph enumeration: the table lists 'contacts' per N; generate alternative rigid contact graphs near the record's and solve each graph's polynomial system exactly (Newton with exact refinement), which also yields exact certificates.

Transfer structures between N: take the record for N+1 and delete the circle with the smallest 'marginal loss', or add a circle to the record for N-1 in the largest hole, then polish; the Sep 2026 'old favorites in new guises' entries came from exactly this.

Evolutionary program search over the initialiser (OpenEvolve-style) is what broke 10 records for N=101-114 (arXiv:2609.05093); replicate with a cheap local LLM-free mutation operator library and the same penalty-method polisher.
Exploit symmetry classes (D1, D2, D4 rows in the table): search symmetric ansatz families for N where the record has no symmetry and vice versa.
pitfalls: Float-tolerance 'records': OpenEvolve's 1e-6 slack produces infeasible packings whose sum exceeds the record; only an exact-rational or interval certificate counts, and shrinking radii to fix overlaps usually erases a sub-1e-6 'gain'.

Comparing with the wrong objective: csq (equal circles, minimise container) and csqv (variable radii, maximise sum) are different pages; AlphaEvolve's 'sum of radii' uses the unit square, not the unit-diameter square.
Reading the table wrong: it prints 12 decimals; improvements must exceed rounding (>= 1e-11) and be computed from the certified radii, not the solver's float output.
Submitting to Packomania is by email; do not send anything without the human's explicit permission.

The live table is frozen for October 2026 (pending-requests.html) with 472 queued candidates from Jason Liang for N=63..10000 and 462 public wins above N=100 in his repo: for N > 62 the frozen table is far below the public frontier, so beating the table alone is meaningless; always beat the public repos too.
jasonzliang's repository is updated daily by automation; re-fetch at verification time and check every sota/* subdirectory for the N in question.

Small circles can always be added, so the bar for N is the best sum at any N' <= N; at margin 1e-11 txt/sumradii.txt has no row below such a bar (checked 2026-10-20 with kit/propagated_bar.py --direction up, PR #573).

targets.name: Akkadian: restore masked/damaged signs in Oracc/eBL transliterations, beating the Lazar et al. 2021 held-out benchmark with frozen predictions
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: Lazar, Saret, Yehudai, Horowitz, Wasserman and Stanovsky (EMNLP 2021, arXiv 2109.04513) framed filling gaps in Akkadian transliterations as masked language modelling on about 1M words / 2.3M signs scraped from Oracc. Their best model (MBERT+Akk, greedy decoding) reports hit@5 = 0.89 and MRR = 0.83 on a 20% held-out split with 15% random masking. These are token-level (BERT word-piece) scores: the paper says 'Table 2 compares token level evaluation', and the repository's evaluate_bert.py masks and scores each word piece separately (positions with label_ids != -100); multi-sign and word prediction is evaluated separately (its Figure 3). They released code and the scraped data (github.com/SLAB-NLP/Akk, MIT, data/akk_from_jsons.jsonl 21 MB, last commit 2022-11-10). The paper's split is a random 80/20 split by text (about 8K train / 2K test texts, its Table 1). The code fixes the seed (preprocessing/main_preprocess.py: SEED = 2, train_test_split(test_size=0.2, random_state=SEED)), but it splits a fresh Oracc scrape written to data/raw/akk_jsons.jsonl, which is not in the repository; the shipped data/akk_from_jsons.jsonl is not referenced by the code and holds 23,211 records, more than Table 1 reports, so the paper's exact test set is not known to be reproducible. The shipped data file (data/akk_from_jsons.jsonl, 21.2 MB, repository commit dfd2a66d of 2022-11-10) is the frozen corpus. Vetter re-check 2026-10-08: two literature searches found no later work reporting hit@k/MRR on this task (later Akkadian work is NMT: Gutherz et al. 2023, TabletCraft 2026). The real-world task is restoring the editorial gaps ('x', [...]) that remain unrestored in Oracc and eBL editions; eBL alone has 625,844 transliterated lines, a large fraction containing bracketed editorial restorations that can serve as a natural held-out test.
targets.success_criterion: On the SLAB-NLP/Akk released data (data/akk_from_jsons.jsonl at commit dfd2a66d or a later recorded commit), with an 80/20 split by text, the frozen list of masked positions published (hash) before any model is trained, and the token-level protocol of the paper's Table 2 and the repository's evaluate_bert.py reproduced with a documented fixed seed (the masked units are word-piece tokens, not whole words): every text is preprocessed as the repository's main_preprocess.py does with the flags its README names for the paper's models (--remove_subscripts --remove_superscripts; no --remove_hyphens, --use_pseudo_words or --remove_missing, so hyphens and the '...' break marks stay in the text; every 'x', gap mark or not, becomes the missing-sign character U+1F607, which the repository injects as a token and never masks; the code also turns '+' into '-' and deletes every 'o', every 'v' and backslash codes such as \t); each test text is then tokenized with the MBERT+Akk tokenizer that the repository code builds from the training split (the tokens it puts into M-BERT's 99 free slots published, with the sha256 of the resulting vocab.txt) and truncated to 128 tokens including [CLS] and [SEP], as ORACCDataset does; every token except the special tokens and the missing-sign token (U+1F607) is masked independently with probability 0.15 and then shown as [MASK] (80%), a random token (10%) or unchanged (10%), as DataCollatorForLanguageModelingAkkadian does, and the frozen list records what is shown at each masked position, so that every system sees the identical input; each masked token, whichever of the three it shows, is scored by exact match with its original word piece (the positions with label_ids != -100, as compute_mrr_and_all_hit_ks does): (1) the claimant retrains the paper's MBERT+Akk baseline with the repository code and default hyperparameters on the same frozen split and freezes its top-5 predictions (hash) - its hit@5 must land within 0.02 of 0.89 on the frozen masked positions, otherwise the split is not comparable and no full win is possible; (2) a prediction file (top-5 per masked token) for the new system, frozen (hash) before scoring and trained/tuned ONLY on the training split, scores BOTH hit@5 and MRR strictly above the paper's values (re-read from the arXiv/ACL paper immediately before claiming) AND strictly above the reproduced baseline on the identical masked positions. A whole-word or whole-sign score is a different unit and is never compared with 0.89 or 0.83. Any use of test documents, of eBL/Oracc texts that duplicate test documents (same P/Q number or same composition), or of a corpus fetched after the split was frozen voids the claim.

partial_wins.statement: Same protocol as the full criterion (including the reproduced baseline), beating only hit@5 or only MRR by at least 1 absolute point over both the paper's value and the reproduced baseline; or beating both metrics on a genre subset for which the paper reports a per-genre number (re-read from the paper's per-genre table/figure; genre defined by Oracc project as in the paper).

Natural-lacuna holdout: a permanent held-out set of at least 2,000 editorially restored signs (text inside [ ] in eBL fragments with joins == [] and no corpus-chapter manuscript link, sampled by a published deterministic rule from fragments fetched on a recorded date, hashed before training) is masked and predicted with frozen top-5 predictions. All training material must exclude any line sharing 6 or more consecutive signs with the 20-sign context window around any holdout gap (parallel/duplicate exclusion, re-checked by the verifier). hit@1 at least 0.50 and hit@5 at least 0.75, with BOTH a unigram-frequency baseline and a k-NN retrieval baseline over the filtered training set reported alongside and beaten by at least 20 absolute points on hit@1.

targets.verification_method: The verifier re-creates the split, the preprocessing, the word-piece tokenization (M-BERT's vocabulary with the published injected tokens) and the masks from the published seed/rule on the recorded data commit, checks the hashes of both frozen prediction files (baseline and new system) against the hashes committed before training (timestamps from the pre-registered holdout protocol), rescores hit@k/MRR for both with independent code on the identical masked positions, and checks that no test document or duplicate (same Oracc P/Q number, composition, or eBL museum number) appears in the training material. Rescoring is minutes; the verifier never retrains.
angles: Character/sign-level n-gram or small transformer LMs trained from scratch on signs with genre tags, predicting the frozen word-piece positions. Note that the 2021 models already work below the word (the paper's M-BERT tokens split a-na into 'a', '-', 'na'), and its from-scratch BERT+AKK(mono) reached 0.60 hit@5 (Table 2).
Retrieval-augmented restoration: Akkadian royal inscriptions and omens are highly formulaic, so k-NN over duplicate passages in the training split can restore many gaps exactly.
Ensemble a forward and backward sign LM with a lexicon constraint (only attested sign sequences for the word), which directly targets MRR.
Build the natural-lacuna holdout (p2) from eBL bracketed restorations, stratified by genre and gap length, and seal it before any training.
Report per-gap-length curves; long gaps dominate the real editorial need and are where the 2021 model fails.
pitfalls: 0.89 and 0.83 are token-level scores, and a token is not a word. M-BERT splits off every sign delimiter: in the 1,882 test documents that main_bert.py --do_eval keeps under the SEED = 2 split of the shipped file, at least 62% of the 174,632 words are two or more tokens (76% with the plain M-BERT vocabulary), and a third to two fifths of the maskable tokens are '-' or '.' (33% with the plain vocabulary, at most 41%); about two thirds of these inside the 128-token window (three quarters over whole documents) are sign delimiters, the rest the dots of the '...' break marks that the preprocessing keeps. The repository's 80/10/10 rule also leaves the original token in place at a tenth of the masked positions. Masking whole words or signs is a much harder task: the paper's Figure 3 puts one masked sign at about 0.55 hit@5, against about 0.9 for one token (read off the chart). Never compare such a score with 0.89 or 0.83.

The 2021 split is produced by code (SEED = 2) on a fresh Oracc scrape, not shipped as files; a different scrape yields a different test set. Only the reproduced-baseline control makes a beat meaningful.
Massive duplication in Oracc (parallel manuscripts of the same composition, RINAP duplicates) leaks test text into training; deduplicate by composition/Q number or report leakage.

data/akk_from_jsons.jsonl repeats records: 5,666 id_text values occur 2 to 5 times (8,781 extra records; 8,691 lines are exact repeats), although the repository's scraper skips an id_text it has already written. Splitting this file as the repository's --do_preprocessing path does (preprocess_akk_file keeps all 23,211 records in order, then train_test_split(test_size=0.2, random_state=2)) gives 18,568 train / 4,643 test records and puts a byte-identical copy of 2,606 of the 4,643 test documents (56.1%) in training. The repository's evaluation (main_bert.py --do_eval) then scores only test documents whose id_text is neither in training nor earlier in the test file: it drops 2,761 (2,616 with the id_text in training, 145 repeats within the test set) and scores 1,882. Remove repeated records (same id_text) before splitting, or apply the same id filter, and report how many were removed.

Exact-match filters (same id_text, same text) do not remove composition-level duplicates: under the SEED = 2 split of the shipped file, test documents can be largely covered by a composite text (Q number) in train. Example: test record P229143 (19 words) shares 10 to 11 of its 12 distinct word 8-grams with Q002268 in train, depending on how editorial marks are normalised. Compute each test document's n-gram share against train before accepting a claim, and report it.
Editorial restorations are themselves often made from parallels: hit rates on bracketed text overstate performance on truly unknown gaps.
LLM-judged 'plausibility' of restorations is not a criterion; only frozen top-k predictions scored against held-out text count.

targets.name: Cuneiform sign detection on the open MaiCuBeDa 3D-rendering benchmark: beat a reproduced RepPoints baseline (AP@50/AP@75) on a fixed, period-filtered split
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: The Mainz Cuneiform Benchmark Dataset (MaiCuBeDa Hilprecht, heiDATA doi:10.11588/DATA/QSNIQ2, CC BY-SA 4.0, version 1.1 released 2025-08-06 with description dated 2023-08-29, its 11 files (ids, sizes, MD5) unchanged from version 1.0 released 2023-08-30; about 9.3 GB: three ~3 GB zips (MSII / VirtualLight / Mixed) that hold only char/line/word/wedge crops and W3C JSON-LD annotation files, not whole-segment renderings, plus annotations.ttl, line/word/translit metadata; Journal of Open Archaeology Data 2025, doi:10.5334/joad.172) is the open benchmark for locating cuneiform signs on 3D-scan renderings. Stotzner, Homburg and Mara (ICCV 2023 workshops, arXiv 2308.11277) train a RepPoints/ResNet-18 single-class detector on 512x512 patches cut from 873 segments of 490 tablets (10,311 patches, 21,228 sign annotations) with a 2:1:1 segment-level split, and report in Table 2 (VOC 11-point interpolated AP, section 4.1) per training base and test rendering; best per test rendering: Mixed test AP@50 0.636 / AP@75 0.431 ('Complete with IA' = all renderings + CDLI photographs the authors mapped onto the renderings, illumination augmentation); VL test AP@50 0.626 / AP@75 0.545 (Complete with IA) and AP@90 0.364 (VL with IA); MSII test AP@50 0.632 (Complete) / AP@75 0.437 (MSII). The release is not that 2023 working set: the Mixed zip's 1,088 sign-annotation files hold 35,130 annotations, about 28,800 of them signs on 1,070 segments of 596 tablets. Section 3 of the paper dates its tablets to 2500-2000 BC (one Old Babylonian and one Akkadian exception), and the release's translitmetadata.csv gives each tablet's CDLI period: its ED IIIb, Old Akkadian and Ur III tablets hold about 22,200 signs on 921 segments of 508 tablets (about 5% above Table 1, at the same 24 signs per segment), while about 6,600 signs on 149 segments are Old Assyrian, Old Babylonian and other tablets the paper did not use. The annotations carry no dates (creation ran until 31 August 2023, JOAD 2025) and the paper's segment list and split are not published, so no split of the release is the paper's, and a RepPoints baseline retrained on the release need not land near Table 2 (one reproduction on all segments, #254, unverified: Mixed-to-Mixed AP@50 0.80 with the paper's AP definition, against 0.609). A June 2026 eBL paper (arXiv 2606.22608, DETR on a separate photo dataset of Lewenstein et al. 2026) does not evaluate on MaiCuBeDa and releases only weights and inference outputs on Zenodo, so MaiCuBeDa remains the only open, checkable benchmark. Status 2026-10-08 (vetter): no published result found exceeding the 2023 Table 2 values on MaiCuBeDa (the JOAD 2025 dataset paper cites only the 2023 baselines); heiDATA's HTML landing page is behind the Anubis bot filter, but the Dataverse API and /api/access/datafile/{id} return 200 to plain curl GET (HEAD returns 503; ranged GET returns 206), verified on readme.txt, utils.zip and the first KB of both large zips.
targets.success_criterion: On MaiCuBeDa version 1.1 (heiDATA file ids and MD5s recorded), the claimant names one test rendering R in {Mixed, VirtualLight, MSII} and uses this entry's FIXED SPLIT (set 2026-10-29, the same for every claim). Its units are the segments whose whole-segment image the sign annotation files charannotations/*.json target, one heidIcon IIIF image per segment; the back files of HS_1139, HS_1333 and HS_1340 target their front images and are left out. It keeps only Hilprecht tablets (files HS_*) whose CDLI period in the release's translitmetadata.csv (Time_period) is ED IIIb, Old Akkadian or Ur III, the paper's 2500-2000 BC range, and counts as signs the annotations classified Character or carrying a transliteration, not classified Wedge, that target such an image: 921 segments of 508 tablets with about 22,200 signs. A segment goes to test if the first hexadecimal digit of the sha256 of its IIIF identifier (the path segment after /iiif/2/ as ASCII, e.g. 1126689:591075) is 0-3, to val if it is 4-7 and to train otherwise (469 train, 241 val and 211 test segments in version 1.1); for VirtualLight and MSII the segment's HeiCuBeDa side view takes the place of its IIIF image. The claimant publishes a deterministic 512x512 patch-cropping rule and freezes (hash) the patch list and the sha256 of every whole-segment image used, before any training; no patch and no image may occur in two splits. Because the release is not the paper's working set, Table 2 is context, not the bar: the bar is a reproduced baseline. The claimant retrains the paper's RepPoints/ResNet-18 baseline (section 2.2: ResNet-18 c4 without FPN, k = 9, IoU thresholds 0.6 / 0.7, loss weights 50 / 100 / 1, SGD learning rate 5e-4, momentum 0.9, weight decay 1e-5, the stated dropout, NMS at 0.4 IoU, best epoch on val) on the fixed train split, with the training base of one pure-rendering Table 2 row (VL, MSII or Mixed renderings), and freezes its config, training log and detections (hash). A detector trained ONLY on the train split (val for model selection) produces a frozen class-agnostic detections file (COCO JSON, hash committed before scoring). Both files are scored on the test patches of rendering R with VOC 11-point interpolated AP (Everingham et al. 2010, the definition of Table 2, section 4.1 of arXiv 2308.11277), pycocotools AP reported alongside. The bar for each of AP@50 and AP@75 is the higher of the claim's own reproduced baseline and the best baseline already accepted on this split for rendering R, whatever its training base (the reproduced baselines in merged packages under known-knowns/cuneiform-sign-detection-maicubeda/; none on 2026-10-29). A full win needs AP@50 AND AP@75 each at least 0.02 above the bar, and the claim's baseline AP@50 at least that Table 2 row's value minus 0.03 (a baseline weaker than the paper's is not a faithful reproduction). Evaluation is sign-class-agnostic (localisation only) at 512x512 patch level, with the fixed split's sign filter applied to both files.

partial_wins.statement: Same protocol (fixed split, frozen detections, reproduced baseline with the same floor, the same bar), beating the bar by at least 0.04 AP@50 with AP@75 not below the bar's, or beating by at least 0.05 on VirtualLight test patches the VirtualLight bar's AP@90 (the higher of the claim's reproduced VirtualLight baseline and the best one already accepted on this split).

Cross-rendering generalisation: a detector trained only on one rendering type (e.g. MSII) scores AP@50 on the held-out test patches of another rendering (e.g. VirtualLight) at least 0.05 above the bar for that train-to-test direction (the higher of the RepPoints baseline the claim reproduces in that direction and the best one already accepted on this split), with frozen detections, the fixed split, and the same baseline floor against that direction's Table 2 row.

targets.verification_method: The verifier downloads via plain curl GET the sign annotation files (charannotations/*.json from any MaiCuBeDa rendering zip, about 5 MB contiguous in the Mixed zip, ranged GET on /api/access/datafile/{id}; HEAD does not work) and the whole-segment images of rendering R that the claim's hash list names, since the rendering zips hold only crops: for Mixed the heidIcon IIIF images that the annotation targets name (about 920 GETs for the fixed split, about 150 MB; robots.txt allows /iiif/), for VirtualLight and MSII the matching side views in HeiCuBeDa Hilprecht (doi:10.11588/data/IE8CCN; HeiCuBeDa_A2_Images_Sideviews_VirtualLight.zip and HeiCuBeDa_A1_Images_Sideviews_MSII_Filter.zip, about 1 to 2 MB per image, read member by member from their central directories with ranged GETs). It verifies the hashes, regenerates the fixed split from this entry's rule (469 / 241 / 211 segments) and the patch list from the published cropping rule, checks that both frozen detections files' hashes predate scoring, checks the baseline's config and training log against section 2.2 of the paper, takes the bar from the claim's baseline and any baseline already accepted on this split, rescores both files (new system and reproduced baseline) with its own VOC 11-point AP code and with pycocotools, and checks that no patch or image occurs in two splits. No retraining by the verifier; under one hour on a 10-core Mac with a normal connection (VirtualLight and MSII images add about 0.5 GB for the test split).
angles: Small anchor-free detectors (YOLO-n/s, FCOS-lite) at 512 px train in CPU-hours on 10k patches; sign boxes are small and dense, so tune anchor-free heads and NMS thresholds for crowded scenes.
Multi-rendering fusion: stack MSII curvature, VirtualLight and Mixed renderings of the same patch as channels (the paper trains them separately).
Test-time augmentation with illumination rotations (the dataset's VirtualLight directions) and box-level weighted fusion directly targets AP@75/AP@90.
Use the wedge-level annotations (4,700 wedges in the dataset) as auxiliary supervision for sign boundaries.
Reproduce the RepPoints baseline first on the frozen split; without it no comparison survives the CRITERION skeptic.
pitfalls: The paper's exact split and segment list are not shipped, and the release is a larger set than the paper's working set (873 segments, 21,228 signs), mostly by tablets outside the paper's 2500-2000 BC range (the fixed split's period filter on translitmetadata.csv Time_period comes within about 5%), so Table 2 numbers are not like-for-like on any split of the release; only the reproduced baseline makes a comparison. 'Complete' and 'Photos' rows use CDLI photographs that the authors mapped onto the renderings with the Cuneur Transformer, and 'VL with IA' uses 7,344 extra VirtualLight renderings; neither is released, so only the pure-rendering rows can be reproduced from released files.

Patches overlap at segment level: a random patch-level split leaks near-identical crops into test and inflates AP by 10+ points. Split by segment (as the paper does) and verify no patch overlap across splits.

AP numbers depend on the AP definition, the IoU protocol and which annotations are counted. Table 2 is VOC 11-point interpolated AP (section 4.1: 'we use the interpolated precision/recall curve with 11 recall levels', citing Everingham et al. 2010), not the pycocotools 101-point default named in the criterion; 18 of its 28 AP@90 values and 4 of its 28 AP@75 values are exact multiples of 1/11 (0.364 = 4/11, 0.545 = 6/11). Score the same frozen detections both ways, say which number is set against Table 2, and document any annotation filtering.

The rendering zips contain no whole-segment rendering, so the 512x512 patches cannot be cut from the rendering zips. Their central directories (listed 2026-10-18) hold only PNG crops (85,821 to 86,711 per zip in char/, croppoly_char/, word/, line/, wedge/ and croppoly_wedge/, each named after its parent segment) and 3,258 to 3,282 JSON annotation files (charannotations/, lineannotations/, wordannotations/). The 1,080 sign annotation files (charannotations/*.json) present in all three zips are byte-identical, and their targets name one heidIcon IIIF image per segment (heidicon.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/iiif/2/...), the Mixed rendering (the dataset readme: 'The mixed version is also available using the IIIF service heidIcon'). Whole-segment VirtualLight and MSII images are the HeiCuBeDa Hilprecht side views (doi:10.11588/data/IE8CCN, A2 and A1 zips, e.g. HS_1153_HeiCuBeDa_GMOCF_SolidColor_03_front.png): for HS_1153_03_front all three sources are 1088x1990 and reproduce the dataset's own crops (correlation 0.9996 to 0.9999, checked 2026-10-28). Name and hash the images of rendering R.

Not every annotation is a sign: charannotations/HS_0044_03_front.png.json (the same file in all three zips) holds four editor test annotations ('Ein Polygon!', 'Ein Rechteck!', 'Knie', 'Fuss') with no image source, so 'all annotations counted' also counts non-signs. The fixed split's sign filter removes them; apply it identically to both detections files. The Mixed zip's charannotations/ also holds 8 files that are not Hilprecht tablets (six Haft Tappeh 'HT_' files and the front and back of one Kurth tablet; 319 annotations, 282 of them on gitlab.rlp.net images and 37 on one heidIcon photograph), 21 annotations with no target image, and front and back files of HS_1139, HS_1333 and HS_1340 that target the same image; the fixed split leaves those three back files out, so no image lands in two splits.
Training-time augmentation that uses the test rendering (e.g. VirtualLight directions reserved for test) is leakage.
The eBL 2026 DETR dataset is not released; its numbers cannot be used as a record or checked here.
heiDATA HEAD requests return 503 and the HTML landing page sits behind a bot filter: use plain GET (ranged if needed) on /api/access/datafile/{id}; never retry through a challenge page.

targets.name: Greek literary papyri: identify DCLP 'unidentified' fragments as witnesses of known works via open-corpus text matching
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: The Digital Corpus of Literary Papyri (DCLP, papyri.info; open EpiDoc XML in github.com/papyri/idp.data, DCLP/ folder) held 14,845 records at commit 67e8445 (2026-10-08), 2,276 of them with a transcription (<ab>). Re-count by the vetter on 2026-10-08: the 'unidentified' label lives in the work-level metadata, i.e. <title type="main" level="m"> elements carrying a trismegistos.org/authorwork ref that read 'Opus incertum' (about 80 transcribed records), <author>/<surname> = 'Anonymus' (about 70), <term type="overview"> 'unknown work' (4) and principal-edition titles naming unknown works; roughly 150-250 transcribed records are genuinely unidentified-work records (the stocker's 1,941 included 'unknown' inventory numbers and provenances and is not the pool). Many of these are Herculaneum (PHerc.) opera incerta of Philodemus or Demetrius Laco, i.e. lost works absent from every corpus, so the realistic pool is smaller still. Open Greek corpora exist in full text (OpenGreekAndLatin/First1KGreek, PerseusDL/canonical-greekLit; Latin: PerseusDL/canonical-latinLit), so identification can be attempted mechanically by aligning the supplement-free letters of each unidentified fragment against every open text, which scholars still do by hand (e.g. the 2024 re-identification of P.Oxy. 2258 'Unidentified Fragment 11' as Demosthenes). Status 2026-10-08 (vetter): no systematic machine identification campaign published (searches found only writer-identification, character-detection, dating and stylometric authorship work); idp.data actively maintained (last commit 2026-10-08); raw.githubusercontent.com and papyri.info/dclp return 200 to plain curl; a sparse clone of DCLP/ takes about a minute.
targets.success_criterion: At least 1 DCLP record meeting ALL of: (a) at the recorded idp.data commit, every work-level author/title element of the record (the <author>/<surname> elements and the <title type="main" level="m"> elements that carry a trismegistos.org/authorwork ref, plus <term type="overview">) reads Opus incertum / Adespota / Anonymus / unidentified / unknown, and no <bibl>, <note>, <head> reference title, <term> or <change> entry in the record names the matched author or work; (b) the alignment uses ONLY letters outside editorial supplements ([ ]) and outside <supplied>/<gap> elements, with underdotted (uncertain) letters excluded from the count; (c) the fragment's stripped letters align to one passage of one open-corpus text (First1KGreek, canonical-greekLit or canonical-latinLit; repository commit hash recorded) over at least 12 consecutive legible letters spanning at least 2 papyrus lines with at most 1 letter mismatch, and the line-break positions are consistent with a plausible column width (constant +/-3 letters per line); (d) the alignment score has p < 1e-4 against a null formed by aligning the same fragment to the whole open corpus with line order shuffled, Bonferroni-corrected over all fragments searched; (e) the matched passage is not a formula or quotation attested in at least 5 distinct open-corpus works (Homeric formulae, LXX/NT verses, proverbs, gnomic sentences), verified by exhaustive corpus-wide counting; (f) the identification is not already recorded in the papyri.info HTML/XML record, in the Trismegistos/LDAB authorwork entry linked from the record's <idno type="LDAB">, or in the editions cited in the record's <head>, all re-fetched live immediately before claiming. Claim as 'candidate identification'; CONFIRMED only when a papyrologist or the papyri.info editorial board accepts it.

partial_wins.statement: A DCLP record meeting (a), (b), (d), (e), (f) whose alignment covers 8-11 consecutive legible letters over at least 2 lines with 0 mismatches, where the matched 8+ letter string occurs exactly once in the entire open corpus (rarity verified by exhaustive search) and the line-break constraint of (c) holds.

targets.verification_method: The verifier sparse-clones idp.data (DCLP/ only, about 1 minute) at the claimed commit, checks the record's work-level elements per (a) with independent code, strips supplements/gaps/underdots with independent code, re-runs the alignment of the claimed fragment against the open corpus at the recorded commit, re-runs the shuffled-line null, counts corpus-wide occurrences of the matched string, and re-fetches the papyri.info record and the LDAB authorwork entry live to confirm no prior identification. Under one hour on a 10-core Mac.
angles: Index both open corpora as accent-stripped, lower-cased letter n-grams (n=6..8) and run seed-and-extend alignment of each unidentified fragment's supplement-free letters; score by length and corpus rarity.
Treat papyrus line breaks as constraints: a correct match must place line ends at a near-constant letter count per line, which prunes chance hits.
Prioritise fragments whose DCLP title says 'prose' or 'hexameter' with 3+ lines and few lacunae; verse fragments can be matched on metrical position as well.

Run the identified transcribed records blind (identification fields hidden, supplements stripped) as a calibration set to tune thresholds before claiming any new identification (calibration is a prerequisite, not a win).
Cross-check candidate hits against the record's own <bibl> and the TM authorwork field via the papyri.info JSON/HTML page before claiming.
pitfalls: Editorial supplements in [ ] were often restored FROM a suspected source text: matching on them is circular. Strip all bracketed text and also dotted (uncertain) letters when counting.
Homeric formulae, LXX/NT verses, proverbs, school exercises and gnomic sentences recur across many works; condition (e) must be enforced by corpus-wide counting.

TLG is not open and First1KGreek is incomplete: absence of a match proves nothing, and a match to a fragmentary author (e.g. Menander) may reflect a quotation in a later author rather than the primary work.

Some 'unidentified' DCLP metadata is stale: the record may have been identified in a later edition (P.Oxy. re-editions, BKT) or in Trismegistos without idp.data being updated. Check live before claiming.
Leiden-convention markup (dots, underdots, brackets, line numbers) must be parsed carefully; a naive strip can glue letters across lacunae and produce fake 12-letter runs.

'unknown'/'incertum' also appears in inventory numbers, provenances and editorial notes: only the work-level author/title elements (with trismegistos authorwork ref) and the overview term define the pool.
Lost works (Philodemus/Demetrius Laco opera incerta, lost tragedies, novels) can never match an open corpus; a null result on them is expected and is not evidence of anything.

Clause (a) read literally leaves a pool of 6 transcribed records, not 150-250 (counted 2026-10-16 at idp.data commit f0fcec2): most 'Opus incertum' records carry a named author (Menander, Archilochus, Philodemus, Demetrius Laco, 'Paulus?'), and a named author fails (a). 656 further transcribed records carry no work-level element at all (vacuous (a)); by title about half of those are magical, medical, liturgical and school texts. Say whether 'unknown work of a named author' is in scope, and whether records with no work-level element are.

Clause (c)'s junction requirement ('12 consecutive legible letters spanning at least 2 papyrus lines') can only be met when both lines are preserved at the junction. 63% of DCLP's transcribed, identified fragments (651 of 1,028 whose author is in the open corpora) lose both line ends and cannot form such a run whatever their text; a Homer papyrus with 423 legible letters (BKT 9 120) scores zero under the clause and 22 letters at Iliad without it. A lacuna-bridging rule (letters on two lines of one passage, with a lacuna of unknown length between) is needed for the typical fragment.

Twelve letters with one mismatch is chance-level against the open corpora (170 M Greek letters): 254 of 662 unidentified-or-unlabelled records reach it, and order-2 Markov controls of the same line lengths reach 16-17. Length does no discriminating work; what does is clause (e) (distinct works) and a within-line-shuffle or Markov null. Even then the survivors are quotations (Psalms, Homer), recipe parallels (Galen, De compositione medicamentorum, already cited in the records' re-editions), liturgical formulae and philosophical commonplaces, not witnesses.

Clause (d)'s null ('line order shuffled') re-creates the real junction of two lines about once in n-1 controls, so a one-junction hit ties its own null and can never reach p < 1e-4 under it (13 of 13 shortlisted parallels tied or lost on 2026-10-16). Pre-register a within-line letter shuffle and a Markov text of the same line pattern instead, and state a reachable level: with 400 controls per record the floor is 1/401, far above 1e-4 / (number of fragments).

Counting <supplied> letters as legible manufactures criterion-grade hits: on 2026-10-16, 110 of 662 records reached 12 letters only through restored text (29 of them with windows of 20 or more). The stripping rule must also keep <supplied>, <unclear>, <ex> and counted <gap> positions as wildcards (so the corpus text stays aligned through them) rather than deleting them, and treat gaps of unknown extent as hard breaks; deleting restored letters glues the surrounding text and creates fake runs.

The live checks of clause (f) are not reachable with an honest client: papyri.info serves an Anubis proof-of-work challenge to plain curl (2026-10-16) and trismegistos.org answered plain GETs with connection failures and a 403 challenge page. A verifier must read the idp.data XML (the same data) and leave the HTML and LDAB pages to a human; say so in the verification method.

targets.name: Cuneiform: fragment-to-fragment overlaps among UNIDENTIFIED eBL fragments (new witnesses of unknown compositions, 'indirect joins')
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: The electronic Babylonian Library (eBL) public API reported 38,530 transliterated fragments and 625,844 lines on 2026-10-08 (/api/statistics). The existing bank target ebl-fragment-identification matches unassigned fragments against KNOWN compositions (eBL chapters). This target is the complementary, harder case: two or more fragments that are each unidentified (genre 'OTHER:Uncertain' or no genre, no joins, no chapter manuscript link) but overlap each other textually, i.e. duplicate witnesses of a composition nobody has reconstructed yet. Simonjetz et al. (LREC-COLING 2024) formalised fragment matching and reported Precision@3 on 965 artificial fragments against chapters only, noting that all-pairs fragment-to-fragment matching 'does not seem feasible at this point'. eBL's own ngram-matcher (GitHub) exposes the baseline. Status 2026-10-08 (vetter): open-ended ongoing work; the public API query endpoint (/api/fragments/query?genre=OTHER:Uncertain) returned 200 with 1,144 records, fragment records (/api/fragments/{id}) are public GET (HEAD returns 405) and expose joins, genres, references, uncuratedReferences, notes and a sign-name 'signs' field; the in-platform matcher endpoint /api/fragments/{id}/match returns 403 to the public, but eBL's ngram-matcher Python library (github.com/ElectronicBabylonianLiterature/ngram-matcher, last commit 2025-11-18) reads only the public API (https://www.ebl.lmu.de/api/) and needs no credentials, so it is the executable baseline. Simonjetz et al. (LREC-COLING 2024) state that all-pairs matching of fragments 'does not seem feasible at this point'.
