targets.name: PoseBusters benchmark set (428 complexes): raise the PB-valid RMSD<=2A redocking rate above the published classical-docking rate

partial_wins.statement: A reproduction artefact: the attacker's own end-to-end harness (download, prepare, dock, score with the official posebusters package) reproducing a published classical-docking PB-valid rate on all 428 systems to within 2 percentage points, with runtime reported - valuable infrastructure, reported as a reproduction and not a record.

A subset result: a strictly higher PB-valid RMSD<=2A rate than the attacker's own reproduced baseline (same inputs, same scorer, margin >= 5 percentage points, bootstrap-confirmed) on a declared, pre-registered subset of at least 150 complexes selected by a rule that does not use the crystal pose (e.g. ligand heavy-atom count below a threshold, or single-chain receptors).

A failure-mode map: a per-complex table showing, for the attacker's method and its reproduced baseline, which posebusters checks fail (clash, internal geometry, stereochemistry, RMSD) with counts, identifying at least one systematic, fixable failure class and demonstrating the fix raises the overall rate - independently checkable from the published pose files.

pitfalls: Empty-leaderboard false win: polaris/posebusters-v1 lists no results, so a first submission is NOT a record. The operative bar is the published rate plus the attacker's own reproduced baseline, and this must be stated in any claim.

Crystal-pose leakage, the signature failure of this field: defining the docking box, the pocket centre, the ligand conformer, or any restraint from the test complex's own crystal ligand inflates success enormously. The box/pocket rule must be uniform, pose-independent and published, and the skeptic must check the run script for it.

Holo-receptor and preparation leakage: using the holo receptor is standard for redocking but must be declared, as must any use of the deposited ligand's protonation/tautomer state; silently taking the crystal ligand's exact protomer is a subtle form of leakage.

Scorer drift: posebusters versions, modes (redock vs dock vs mol) and RMSD conventions (symmetry-corrected or not, heavy atoms only) change the rate by several points. The package version and mode must be pinned in the manifest and re-run by the skeptic, not taken from the attacker's output.

Subset substitution: quietly dropping complexes that fail preparation, or scoring on fewer than all 428 systems, inflates the rate. The denominator must be all 428 systems, with failures counted as failures, unless a pre-registered subset partial win is being claimed.

Benchmark-set contamination for learned components: any learned scoring or pose-prediction component trained on PDB structures released after 2021 may have seen these very complexes; provenance and training cutoffs must be declared, which is also how the PoseBusters paper frames its own fairness analysis.
targets.statement: PoseBusters (Buttenschoen, Morris & Deane, Chem. Sci. 2024) is the standard physics-aware pose-validity benchmark: 428 carefully selected protein-ligand crystal complexes released since 2021, with an open-source scorer (the posebusters pip package / github.com/maabuu/posebusters) that checks chemical validity, intramolecular geometry, intermolecular clashes and RMSD to the crystal pose, and the headline metric is the fraction of predictions that are both RMSD<=2A and 'PB-valid'. The paper's finding - that classical docking (AutoDock Vina) beats deep-learning co-folding and pose-prediction methods on PB-valid rate - makes this an unusual benchmark where CPU docking is the method to beat, not a handicap. Polaris mirrors the set as polaris/posebusters-v1 (428 test systems, main metric rmsd_coverage) and that leaderboard currently lists NO results, while the related plinder-org/runs-n-poses preview table shows how weak the co-folding field is on a harder split (AlphaFold3 15.1% success, Boltz-1 5.6%, Chai-1 4.7%, Protenix 1.5%). The data are public (Zenodo record 8278563, 200 OK) and the Polaris dataset parquet/zarr download anonymously, so a laptop can redock all 428 systems with open-source docking in hours and score with the official package.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a saved set of predicted ligand poses (one SDF per complex for all 428 PoseBusters systems, plus the receptor files used and a manifest with the sha256 of every input structure, the exact method, software versions, seeds and total wall-clock CPU time) such that (a) the skeptic, running the official posebusters package (version pinned in the manifest) with the standard redock configuration on the attacker's SDFs against the crystal ligands from the public PoseBusters distribution, obtains a PB-valid RMSD<=2A rate that is strictly HIGHER (direction: max) than BOTH (i) every entry listed in the live leaderboard table at https://polarishub.io/benchmarks/polaris/posebusters-v1 , re-fetched immediately before claiming - a first entry on an empty table is explicitly NOT a record - and (ii) the attacker's OWN reproduction, with the same inputs and the same scorer, of a documented classical docking baseline (e.g. AutoDock Vina with a declared box and exhaustiveness), reported with its rate, and (iii) the best PB-valid RMSD<=2A rate for the same 428-system benchmark reported in the PoseBusters paper and in any paper found by the NOVELTY skeptic from the last 24 months, (b) the margin over (ii) and (iii) is at least 3 percentage points and a paired bootstrap over the 428 complexes (10,000 resamples) confirms superiority in at least 95% of resamples, (c) no crystal ligand pose, crystal-ligand coordinates, or ligand-pose-derived restraint for a test complex was used as input - only the receptor structure (holo or declared apo), the ligand's 2D/SMILES identity, and the binding-site definition rule, which must be stated and applied uniformly (e.g. derived from a non-test cognate ligand or from a pocket-detection algorithm, never from the test ligand's own coordinates), and (d) the pose files, the run script and the posebusters output table are published so the whole rate can be recomputed from scratch.
targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the PoseBusters benchmark set from its public distribution (Zenodo record 8278563 / the posebusters repo), checks input sha256s against the manifest, installs the pinned posebusters package, runs the official 'redock' mode on the attacker's 428 SDFs against the crystal ligands, and reads the PB-valid and RMSD<=2A columns to recompute the rate; repeats the same scoring on the attacker's reproduced baseline poses; runs the paired bootstrap; verifies from the run script that no test-complex crystal ligand coordinates entered pose generation or box definition; and re-fetches the live Polaris leaderboard table. Scoring 428 poses takes minutes; re-docking 428 complexes on 10 CPU cores is hours.

angles: AUPRC-matched training: optimise average precision directly with a pairwise/listwise ranking loss restricted to positive-negative pairs, or use focal/asymmetric loss with prevalence-matched reweighting; log-loss-trained boosters leave AUPRC on the table at these class ratios.

Multi-task across the three CYP inhibition datasets (train_val only): the same compounds and the same qHTS platform underlie all three, so a shared-representation multi-task booster or a stacked model that uses the other two endpoints' out-of-fold predictions as features is both legitimate and cheap.

Feature-union stacking at scale: hashed ECFP4/6, FCFP, Avalon, MACCS, RDKit 2D, plus atom-pair and topological-torsion counts, each fed to its own LightGBM, then stacked by logistic regression on scaffold-grouped out-of-fold predictions - the straightforward way to pass a single MapLight+GNN entry.

CROSS-DOMAIN (coding theory / ECOC over related endpoints): build codewords from the three inhibition labels plus the three substrate labels and decode the target bit by minimum-distance decoding, which extracts cross-endpoint redundancy as error correction.

CROSS-DOMAIN (statistical physics / graph diffusion and belief propagation): construct a similarity graph over all molecules (structures only) and run label propagation from train_val labels as an additional transductive feature; diffusion handles scaffold-split shift better than i.i.d. learners and costs seconds.

CROSS-DOMAIN (compression / NCD) as an ensemble member, and CROSS-DOMAIN (linguistics / SMILES BPE n-grams with tf-idf) as a second orthogonal view; both are fast enough at 13k molecules and decorrelate the errors of fingerprint models.

Threshold-free calibration and rank aggregation across seeds: average predictions in rank space (Borda) across seeds and model families, which is the right aggregation for a ranking metric like AUPRC.

targets.name: TDC ADMET CYP inhibition leaderboards (CYP2C9/CYP2D6/CYP3A4_Veith, 12-13k molecules, AUPRC): beat MapLight+GNN

partial_wins.statement: The full strict win on CYP2D6_Veith (live rank 1 0.790), the weakest of the three records and the one with the largest rank-1-to-rank-2 gap.

A reproduction-plus-margin result on any of the three: an independently re-implemented MapLight-style baseline (fingerprints + RDKit descriptors + gradient boosting, code and features reported) whose 5-seed mean AUPRC is within 0.005 of the live rank-1 value, PLUS an ablated addition that pushes it above the live rank-1 value under the margin rule.

A low-prevalence-slice result: AUPRC restricted to the test molecules outside the 10 most populous Bemis-Murcko scaffolds (count reported, at least 500 molecules) that exceeds the pooled live rank-1 value, evidencing generalisation rather than scaffold memorisation.

pitfalls: Assay-source leakage: the Veith CYP inhibition labels come from a public PubChem qHTS assay, so downloading that assay (or using a model pretrained on it, including several public ADMET predictors) recovers test labels exactly. This is the single most likely false positive; provenance declarations and InChIKey checks are mandatory.

Scaffold-split mis-tuning and re-splitting: hyper-parameters chosen under random CV are mis-set for a scaffold-split test set, and locally regenerated scaffold splits are incomparable. Use group.get() and scaffold-grouped internal CV.

Metric swap: these three are scored by AUPRC (TDC uses AUPRC where positives are scarce). Reporting AUROC - which is much higher and less sensitive - as if it were the record is an easy, invalid 'win'.

Seed cherry-picking against near-zero listed stds (0.000-0.003): the leaderboard value is a 5-seed mean, so the margin must exceed both stds and the bootstrap must pass; CYP3A4's 0.916 +- 0.000 in particular leaves no room for sloppy reporting.

Duplicate/salt-form leakage across the scaffold boundary within TDC itself: report the stereo-stripped InChIKey overlap between train_val and test, and a 1-NN-on-ECFP baseline as a floor, so a 'win' is distinguishable from better memorisation.

Novelty trap: MapLight, ADMET-AI, MiniMol, ZairaChem and 2024-2026 tabular/pretrained submissions report numbers on these exact splits; the NOVELTY skeptic must check the last 24 months for a higher published AUPRC on the same benchmark before any claim.
targets.statement: Three TDC ADMET benchmarks are large enough for real modelling yet still topped by a classical fingerprint+GNN hybrid: CYP2C9_Veith (12,092 molecules, AUPRC, rank 1 MapLight+GNN 0.859 +- 0.001, rank 2 ContextPred 0.839 +- 0.003), CYP2D6_Veith (13,130, AUPRC, rank 1 MapLight+GNN 0.790 +- 0.001, rank 2 ContextPred 0.739 +- 0.005) and CYP3A4_Veith (12,328, AUPRC, rank 1 MapLight+GNN 0.916 +- 0.000, rank 2 ContextPred 0.904 +- 0.002). The protocol is the group's scaffold split with 5 seeds and mean +- std from group.evaluate; the leaderboard pages are undated and the TDC repo's last commits are April 2025. CYP2D6 is the obvious target: rank 1 is 0.051 AUPRC above rank 2, the task is a well-defined qHTS inhibition readout from a single PubChem assay (Veith et al.), and 13k molecules with fingerprint features is minutes per fit on 10 CPU cores, so hundreds of model variants can be explored honestly inside train_val.

Success means 5 saved prediction files (seeds 1-5 from tdc.benchmark_group.admet_group, no re-splitting, official test order, probabilities in [0,1], manifest with sha256 of the test SMILES and labels) such that (a) the test split is byte-identical to the group's own, (b) the mean AUPRC over the 5 seeds, recomputed by the skeptic through the group's own evaluate call, is strictly HIGHER (direction: max) than the rank-1 AUPRC in the live leaderboard table for that dataset at tdcommons.ai, re-fetched immediately before claiming, (c) the improvement exceeds max(listed rank-1 std, attacker's own 5-seed std) and is at least 0.005 absolute, with a stratified 10,000-resample bootstrap over test molecules putting the attacker ahead in at least 95% of resamples, (d) fitting used only the official train_val rows of that seed, and (e) no external PubChem/ChEMBL record of the SAME assay endpoint for any test molecule was used, and every pretrained component is declared with provenance and shown to be free of the test molecules by stereo-stripped InChIKey. Transfer from the other two CYP inhibition datasets' train_val rows is allowed if declared and leakage-checked.

A full 5-seed retrain on 12-13k molecules with fingerprint features must be shown to run in under an hour on 10 CPU cores.

angles: Optimise the metric that is actually scored: train with a differentiable rank surrogate (pairwise logistic / LambdaRank-style objective over train_val pairs, or SoftRank) instead of MSE. Spearman is invariant to monotone transforms, so rank-learning models have a structural advantage nobody on these four leaderboards appears to have used.

Physiology-informed features for PK endpoints: fraction unbound proxies, ionisation state at pH 7.4 (acid/base/zwitterion class from pKa predictions), logD7.4, molecular volume, and the classic Lombardo VDss descriptor set; plus known mechanistic couplings (VDss and plasma protein binding, half-life ~ VDss/clearance) as engineered ratio features.

CROSS-DOMAIN (ecology / rank-abundance statistics): model the endpoint as a rank-abundance curve and fit a copula between descriptor-space neighbourhood rank and label rank; copula/rank-transform regression is distribution-free and directly maximises monotone association, which is exactly Spearman.

CROSS-DOMAIN (coding theory / ordinal ECOC): discretise the endpoint into K ordered bins, train binary classifiers for every threshold (and for Hadamard-coded bin subsets), and decode a rank score by minimum-distance decoding; threshold ensembles are robust to the heavy label noise of hepatocyte/microsome clearance assays.

CROSS-DOMAIN (statistical physics / cavity-style resampling): bagged ensembles over scaffold-grouped bootstrap replicas with a Boltzmann weighting by out-of-fold Spearman, to pick a 'temperature' (regularisation) that maximises the rank statistic rather than squared error.

CROSS-DOMAIN (signal processing): treat the 5 seeds as repeated measurements of one noisy channel and average predictions in rank space (Borda/Kemeny aggregation across seeds and across model families) rather than in label space; rank-space aggregation is the right estimator for a rank metric and is free.

Transfer from the other three endpoints and from related public PK data (declared, InChIKey-filtered), since half-life, hepatocyte clearance and microsome clearance are mechanistically coupled; multi-task gradient boosting with endpoint one-hots is a few CPU-minutes.

targets.name: TDC ADMET Spearman leaderboards (Half_Life_Obach, Clearance_Hepatocyte_AZ, Clearance_Microsome_AZ, VDss_Lombardo): beat rank 1

partial_wins.statement: The full strict win on Clearance_Hepatocyte_AZ, where the gap between rank 1 (0.536) and rank 2 (0.498) is the largest of the four and the metric is most noise-dominated - verified live at https://tdcommons.ai/benchmark/admet_group/17clhepa/ .

A monotone-physiology result: a model whose predictions for one of the four endpoints are generated from a small, interpretable set of mechanistically motivated descriptors (<= 20 features, named) and still beat the live rank-1 Spearman under the same margin rule - a genuine 'small model beats leaderboard' claim, with the feature list and fitted signs reported.

A cross-endpoint multi-task win: one single multi-task model (trained jointly on the official train_val splits of all four Spearman endpoints, same seed, no test rows) that beats the live rank-1 value on at least two of the four datasets simultaneously under the same margin rule.

pitfalls: Seed and ties manipulation: with 135-243 test molecules, the Spearman standard error is roughly 0.05, far larger than the leaderboard's quoted 5-seed std; best-of-N-seeds or best-of-N-models reporting will cross any of these records by chance. Enforce the full 5-seed mean, the std-based margin and the permutation test.

Scaffold leakage via pretrained descriptors: these endpoints are inside widely used ADMET training collections (ADMET-AI, ZairaChem, commercial descriptor servers), so a pretrained predictor may have seen the exact test molecules and their labels. Declared provenance plus InChIKey overlap checks are mandatory.

Re-splitting / wrong split convention: the four benchmarks use TDC's scaffold split with a 20% test fraction produced by group.get(); regenerating it locally (different RDKit, different seed) silently changes the test set.

Metric substitution: reporting Pearson or R^2 (or Spearman on log-transformed labels of a different unit) instead of the group's Spearman. Only the group's own evaluate output counts, and VDss/clearance unit conventions (L/kg, uL/min/1e6 cells, mL/min/g) must match TDC's.

Measurement-duplicate leakage: Obach half-life and the AZ clearance sets contain the same drugs measured in multiple assays and the same chemical series across train/test; a 1-nearest-neighbour baseline already scores deceptively high, so any claim must beat an explicitly reported 1-NN-on-ECFP baseline as a sanity floor.

Novelty trap: 2024-2026 submissions and papers (MiniMol, CFA, MapLight variants, TabPFN-style tabular models) may already report higher Spearman on these same splits than the stale table; the NOVELTY skeptic must check the last 24 months of literature naming the dataset.
targets.statement: Four TDC ADMET benchmarks are scored by Spearman correlation on a fixed scaffold split, 5 seeds: Half_Life_Obach (667 molecules, rank 1 'CFA' 0.576 +- 0.025, runner-up MapLight 0.562 +- 0.008), Clearance_Hepatocyte_AZ (1,020, rank 1 'CFA' 0.536 +- 0.020, runner-up MapLight+GNN 0.498 +- 0.009), Clearance_Microsome_AZ (1,102, rank 1 MapLight+GNN 0.630 +- 0.010, runner-up MiniMol 0.628 +- 0.005) and VDss_Lombardo (1,130, rank 1 MapLight+GNN 0.713 +- 0.007, runner-up MapLight 0.707 +- 0.009). TDC itself notes Spearman is used for 'benchmarks that depend on factors beyond the chemical structure', i.e. these are rank-only, noisy, small-data PK endpoints where classical descriptor models already hold the top spots and the per-seed std is 0.005-0.025. The leaderboards carry no dates and the TDC repo's latest commits are April 2025. Open question: can a CPU-only model push the 5-seed mean Spearman above the listed rank-1 value on any of the four?

targets.verification_method: As for the MAE leaderboards: PyTDC admet_group, group.get(<Benchmark>) for seeds 1-5, hash-check the test SMILES, load the attacker's 5 prediction vectors, call group.evaluate to get mean/std Spearman, apply the margin and permutation-test rules, then re-fetch the live leaderboard page and parse every listed Spearman. Spearman only needs the predicted ranking, so the skeptic must additionally confirm the prediction vector has no ties-by-construction tricks (e.g. constant blocks) that inflate the statistic, and should re-run the attacker's script for all 5 seeds (minutes to an hour on CPU at 667-1,130 molecules).

angles: Descriptor-space brute force on CPU: RDKit 2D + Mordred-style descriptors + several fingerprint families, feature selection by out-of-fold permutation importance, then LightGBM/CatBoost/ExtraTrees/kernel-ridge stacked with a non-negative least-squares meta-learner fit on out-of-fold predictions of train_val only. The current leaders are exactly this class of model, so the gap is engineering, not scale.

Scaffold-aware internal validation: because the official split is scaffold-based, use Bemis-Murcko-grouped CV inside train_val (GroupKFold on scaffolds) for every hyper-parameter choice; models tuned under random CV are systematically mis-tuned for this test set, which is a cheap, often-ignored 1-3% MAE.

CROSS-DOMAIN (signal processing / robust statistics): MAE is an L1 target while most boosters optimise L2. Train with Huber/quantile (median) objectives, and post-process with an isotonic or median-calibrated mapping fit out-of-fold, which reduces MAE even when correlation is unchanged - directly exploiting the metric rather than the chemistry.

CROSS-DOMAIN (ecology / species-distribution thinking): treat each molecule as a site described by physicochemical 'environment' variables (logP, TPSA, charge state at pH 7.4, H-bond counts) and fit a Gaussian-process / GAM 'response surface' with monotonicity constraints from known permeability and plasma-protein-binding physiology; mechanistic monotone priors buy accuracy where data are sparse (Caco2, PPBR).

CROSS-DOMAIN (combinatorial search / cryptanalytic hill climbing): treat the recipe (descriptor blocks, transforms, model family, loss, calibration) as a discrete string and run a scaffold-CV-scored simulated-annealing/genetic search over it with a strict evaluation budget, exactly as one would search key schedules - CPU-cheap on 1-8k molecules and far more thorough than hand-tuning.

Target transforms: for PPBR (percent bound, 0-100) model logit(fraction unbound) and invert; for LD50 model the log-dose directly but weight by assay-duplicate counts. Inverting a variance-stabilised transform is a classic few-percent MAE gain that leaderboard entries often skip.

Semi-supervised use of unlabelled chemical space: self-training / pseudo-labelling on a large unlabelled set (ZINC/ChEMBL structures only, no labels) to regularise the feature space, with explicit InChIKey filtering against the test split.

targets.name: TDC ADMET Benchmark Group, MAE regression leaderboards (Caco2_Wang, PPBR_AZ, LD50_Zhu): beat rank 1 on the official scaffold split

partial_wins.statement: The full strict win on Caco2_Wang alone (906 molecules, smallest and stalest of the three), verified against the live table at https://tdcommons.ai/benchmark/admet_group/01caco2/ .

A reproduction-plus-margin result: an independently re-implemented runner-up-class baseline (plain XGBoost or Chemprop-RDKit) plus a declared, ablated addition (e.g. a conformal shrinkage step or a new descriptor block) whose 5-seed mean MAE beats the live rank-1 value on one dataset, with an ablation table showing the addition, not the baseline, produced the gain.
A strict win on any OTHER TDC ADMET regression leaderboard listed on the group overview page (Lipophilicity_AstraZeneca MAE, Solubility_AqSolDB MAE) under the identical protocol and margin.

pitfalls: Re-splitting instead of using the group's split: the TDC scaffold split must come from group.get(); any locally generated scaffold split (different RDKit version, different seed, different 80/10/10 convention) gives an incomparable number. The skeptic must hash the test SMILES list.

Seed cherry-picking: the leaderboard value is a mean over 5 seeds with a listed std. Reporting the best of 5 seeds, or using fewer seeds, is the single most common false positive here; the margin must exceed the larger of the two stds.

Scaffold leakage through pretraining: ADMET-pretrained models and public descriptor services (and some AutoML submissions) were trained on datasets that INCLUDE Caco2_Wang / PPBR_AZ / LD50_Zhu rows, so the official 'test' molecules are inside their training data. Any pretrained component must have declared provenance and be checked for test-molecule overlap.

Duplicate/near-duplicate molecules inside TDC itself (salts, tautomers, repeated measurements) crossing the scaffold boundary; a nearest-neighbour or memorising model then scores unrealistically well. Check stereo-stripped InChIKey overlap between train_val and test and report it.

Metric mismatch: TDC uses MAE for these three and Spearman for others; computing MAE on standardised/z-scored labels, or on a different unit (log10 cm/s vs cm/s for Caco2, percent vs fraction for PPBR), silently changes the number. Score only through the group's own evaluate call.

Novelty trap: published papers (ADMET-AI, MapLight, ZairaChem, CaliciBoost, MiniMol and 2024-2026 TabPFN-style submissions) report numbers on these same splits that may be better than the stale leaderboard row; the NOVELTY skeptic must search the last 24 months for the same benchmark name before any win is called.

The open question per dataset: can a better featurisation + ensembling recipe lower the 5-seed mean MAE below the listed rank-1 value?

Success means saved per-seed prediction files (5 files, seeds 1-5 as produced by tdc.benchmark_group.admet_group with the default path and no re-splitting, each giving one predicted value per official test molecule in the official order, plus a manifest with the sha256 of the downloaded TDC data files and of the train_val/test SMILES lists) such that (a) the test set is byte-identical to the group's own test split for that benchmark, (b) the mean MAE over the 5 seeds, recomputed by the skeptic with the group's own evaluate call, is strictly LOWER (direction: min) than the rank-1 MAE in the live leaderboard table at the dataset's tdcommons.ai page, re-fetched immediately before claiming, (c) the improvement is at least max(the listed rank-1 std, the attacker's own std across the 5 seeds) and at least 1.5% relative, (d) every model is fit only on the official train_val rows of that same seed (any internal validation must be carved out of train_val), and (e) no external dataset containing any test molecule's measured endpoint is used; if an external training set is used at all, the attacker must list it and show zero stereo-stripped-InChIKey overlap with the test split. Beating only the runner-up does not count.
targets.verification_method: Skeptic pip-installs PyTDC, instantiates admet_group(path='data/'), calls group.get(<Benchmark>) for seeds 1-5 exactly as the submission instructions prescribe, checks the test SMILES list sha256 against the attacker's manifest, loads the 5 prediction files, calls group.evaluate_many / evaluate to obtain mean and std, confirms the margin rule, then re-fetches the dataset's leaderboard page and parses all listed MAE values. Re-running the attacker's training script for all 5 seeds must fit in under an hour on 10 CPU cores (906-7,385 molecules).

angles: Metric-matched training: for the AUPRC benchmarks optimise a precision-recall surrogate (weighted/focal loss, AP-surrogate, or direct ranking loss on positive-negative pairs) rather than log-loss; with 30-60 positives in the test set, ranking the positives above the ambiguous middle is what moves AUPRC.

Substrate-specific mechanistic features: CYP substrate recognition depends on site-of-metabolism accessibility, so add SMARTS counts for known soft spots (N-dealkylation, O-demethylation, aromatic hydroxylation motifs), partial charges on candidate atoms, and SASA-like proxies from a single fast 3D embedding - cheap on 667 molecules and orthogonal to fingerprints.

CROSS-DOMAIN (linguistics / morphological parsing): parse SMILES into substituent 'morphemes' (BRICS/RECAP fragments) and build a fragment-presence language model per class, scoring molecules by log-likelihood ratio - a naive-Bayes-over-fragments classifier that is strong exactly when data are tiny and labels noisy.

CROSS-DOMAIN (compression / NCD similarity): k-NN and kernel SVM with a normalised-compression-distance kernel over canonical SMILES; parameter-free, uncorrelated with ECFP Tanimoto, and ideal as a diversity component in a small-data ensemble.

CROSS-DOMAIN (coding theory / error-correcting output codes over related endpoints): train the three CYP-substrate tasks plus the three CYP-inhibition tasks as a 6-bit codeword per molecule and decode the target bit by minimum-distance decoding; inhibition data (12k molecules each) act as a large, legitimate auxiliary signal for the 667-molecule substrate tasks.

CROSS-DOMAIN (statistical physics / belief propagation on similarity graphs): build a molecular similarity graph over train_val+test structures (structures only, no test labels) and run label propagation / graph-diffusion from the train labels; transductive diffusion is a well-matched estimator for scaffold-split tasks and runs in seconds.

Variance control: with 95-135 test molecules, the main lever is reducing prediction variance - average over many featurisations and many scaffold-grouped folds, and shrink probabilities toward the train prevalence where out-of-fold uncertainty is high.

targets.name: TDC ADMET small classification leaderboards (CYP substrates, hERG, DILI, Bioavailability): beat rank 1 on the official scaffold split

partial_wins.statement: The full strict win on CYP3A4_Substrate_CarbonMangels (AUROC, live rank 1 0.667) - the weakest absolute record in the whole ADMET group.
The full strict win on CYP2C9_Substrate_CarbonMangels (AUPRC, live rank 1 0.474), where the positive class is small and the listed std is 0.025, so the bootstrap and 5-seed rules must both pass.

A calibration-only result: using a published or re-implemented baseline's raw scores, show that a declared post-hoc transform fit only on train_val out-of-fold predictions (e.g. isotonic/Platt or a prevalence-corrected ranking) raises the 5-seed AUPRC of that baseline above the live rank-1 value on one of the two AUPRC benchmarks, with the untransformed baseline reported alongside.

pitfalls: Tiny-test-set luck: 95-135 test molecules with 20-40 positives means the AUPRC/AUROC standard error is roughly 0.04-0.08. Any search over models selected on test will 'beat' these records; only out-of-fold selection on train_val plus the 5-seed, std-margin and bootstrap rules can distinguish signal from noise.

Metric swap: CYP2C9/CYP2D6 substrate are AUPRC while CYP3A4 substrate, hERG, DILI and Bioavailability are AUROC. Reporting AUROC where AUPRC is scored (or vice versa) looks like a large gain and is a pure artefact; use the group's own evaluate output.

Scaffold leakage via pretrained models and public AutoML pipelines: hERG, DILI and the CarbonMangels CYP sets are standard ingredients of ADMET pretraining collections, so a pretrained encoder may have memorised the test molecules' labels. Provenance must be declared and InChIKey overlap with test checked.

Label-noise/duplicate traps: the CarbonMangels substrate sets and the hERG set contain near-duplicate structures and some contradictory labels across sources; de-duplicating or 'cleaning' the OFFICIAL test rows (or dropping hard test molecules) invalidates the comparison entirely.

Threshold leakage: choosing a probability threshold, calibrating, or selecting an ensemble weight using the test labels. All calibration must be fit on train_val out-of-fold predictions only, and AUROC/AUPRC must be computed from raw scores.

Novelty trap: MiniMol, CFA, ZairaChem, ContextPred and newer 2024-2026 tabular/pretrained submissions report numbers on these same splits; a claim must beat the live rank-1 value AND any higher number published for the same benchmark in the last 24 months.

The protocol is TDC's: official scaffold split from group.get(), 5 seeds, mean +- std from group.evaluate. Leaderboard pages are undated; the TDC repo's last commits are April 2025.

targets.verification_method: PyTDC admet_group; group.get(<Benchmark>) for seeds 1-5; hash-check the test SMILES and labels; load the attacker's 5 probability vectors; call group.evaluate to obtain the dataset's own metric mean/std; apply margin and bootstrap rules; re-fetch the live leaderboard page and parse every listed value. All six datasets are <700 molecules, so the skeptic can re-run the attacker's whole 5-seed pipeline in minutes on CPU and confirm the numbers from scratch.

angles: Make the genetic algorithm smarter, not bigger: Graph-GA with zero parameters is the record, so the headroom is in the search operators - fragment libraries mined from the best-scoring hits so far, adaptive mutation rates, crowding/fitness sharing to avoid premature convergence, and an explicit archive (MAP-Elites style) binned by scaffold and size so diversity and %Pass do not collapse the way Graph-GA's do.

Surrogate-assisted screening under a hard call budget: fit a cheap docking-score surrogate (fingerprint booster or Gaussian process) on the calls made so far and spend real oracle calls only on surrogate-predicted elites with high acquisition value - classic Bayesian optimisation over a discrete space, which the current leaderboard (one BO-free GA and four RL/VAE methods) never applied here.

CROSS-DOMAIN (cryptanalysis / key-space hill climbing with restarts): treat the molecular graph edit sequence as a key, run many short simulated-annealing climbs with tabu lists over recently tried fragments, and restart from an elite pool - the standard recipe for beating a plain GA in a rugged discrete landscape at a fixed evaluation budget.

CROSS-DOMAIN (coding theory / sphere packing in fingerprint space): maintain a covering code over fingerprint space so oracle calls are spent on mutually distant candidates (maximising information per call), which simultaneously raises the Diversity column that Graph-GA sacrifices.

CROSS-DOMAIN (statistical physics / parallel tempering and population annealing): run several populations at different mutation 'temperatures' with periodic swaps, which escapes the local optima that fixed-rate GAs settle into.

CROSS-DOMAIN (ecology / island biogeography and niche construction): island-model GA with migration between sub-populations defined by scaffold niches, with niche-specific selection pressure - a well-studied way to keep diversity while improving the best score.

Pose-quality filtering before counting a hit: re-score elites with a second, independent scoring function and discard molecules whose score depends on an implausible pose, which protects the %Pass and plausibility columns and avoids scoring-function exploitation.
