targets.name: Binary Gupta nanoalloys (Ag-Au, Cu-Ag, Cu-Au 55-atom; Cu-Au 38-atom; Li-Na and Na-K 55-atom): lower the best homotop energy for some composition

partial_wins.statement: Audit: a merged machine-readable table of all compositions in the six archives, recomputed from coordinates, listing every file whose header energy is not reproduced within 1e-5 eV or that polishes lower by more than 1e-4 eV, and every cell where a later paper (with fetchable values) already beats the archive.

A batch of at least five certified homotop improvements (same rules) in one system, found by exchange-only moves on the posted geometries (no change of the geometric motif), reported with the improvement sizes.

pitfalls: Parameter sets: the Ag-Au, Cu-Ag and Cu-Au archives use one published parameter table and the alkali archives another; header energies inside files are not evidence. Recompute every comparator from coordinates.
Composition mix-ups: the record is per composition; a lower energy at a different n, or with A and B labels swapped, is not an improvement.
Later papers (Wu-Cheng 2014, Rondina-Da Silva 2013, Du et al. 2019) may already beat an archive cell; beating the CCD file alone is not novel.
Differences below 1e-4 eV are numerical; the distinct-basin test is mandatory.
targets.statement: The Cambridge Cluster Database hosts composition-resolved putative global minima for binary Gupta clusters: Ag_nAu_{55-n}, Cu_nAg_{55-n}, Cu_nAu_{55-n} and Cu_nAu_{38-n} for every n from Lai Xiangjing, Huang Wenqi and Xu Ruchu (J. Chem. Phys. 135, 164109, 2011; rar archives with the energy in each file header), and Li_nNa_{55-n} and Na_nK_{55-n} from Andres Aguado (J. Chem. Phys. 133, 094302, 2010; tar archives). Each composition is a separate cell (about 300 cells), and the problem combines geometry with the homotop (atom-labelling) problem. Later algorithms benchmarked on some of these systems include Xia Wu and Wen Cheng's BDLS-ILS (J. Chem. Phys. 141, 124110, 2014), Rondina and Da Silva's revised basin hopping (J. Chem. Inf. Model. 53, 2282, 2013) and Du et al. (R. Soc. Open Sci. 2019, Ag-Au and Cu-Au at 1:1, 1:3, 3:1 up to 108 atoms); a claim must beat all of them where they overlap. Checked live 2026-10-15: CCD index page and all six archives HTTP 200.
targets.success_criterion: Success means coordinates and species labels for one system and composition listed in a CCD archive (for example Cu_12Au_26) such that E* under the exact Gupta parameter set used for that archive (calibrated first: the checker reproduces the header energies of every file in that archive to 1e-6 eV from coordinates) is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) by at least 1e-4 eV than the checker's evaluation of the archive structure for that composition (archives re-downloaded immediately before claiming) AND than any published value for the same system, parameters and composition found by an arXiv / Google Scholar search (at least the four papers named in the statement); AND the structure is a certified local minimum: polish in float128 or mpmath (30 digits) to gradient norm < 1e-10 (reduced units of the table), then the 3N x 3N Hessian in double precision has exactly 6 near-zero modes (|lambda| < 1e-6) and no negative eigenvalue; AND polishing the archive structure gives an energy at least 1e-4 eV higher.
targets.verification_method: Checker (< 10 min): download the archive (bsdtar reads .rar), parse every file, recompute energies with the Gupta form E = sum_i [ sum_{j!=i} A_ab exp(-p_ab (r_ij/r0_ab - 1)) - sqrt( sum_{j!=i} xi_ab^2 exp(-2 q_ab (r_ij/r0_ab - 1)) ) ] with the parameters from the source paper; calibration; evaluate the claim in float64 and mpmath; polish; Hessian; composition check; margins.

angles: Build the merged record table first (p2): it immediately shows which cells were improved by Huang-Ye/Kolossvary/Goedecker and therefore which neighbouring cells (N +- 1, adjacent ratio) were never revisited; those neighbours are the cheapest targets.

Two-level search: for fixed geometry, the A/B labelling is a quadratic binary problem; alternate continuous relaxation with exhaustive or simulated-annealing swaps of labels (the 'exchange move' of Sicher-Mohr-Goedecker) and seed from polytetrahedral and core-shell templates of the neighbouring N.
Import from alloy materials science: core-shell 'chemical ordering' heuristics (small atoms in the core, large on the surface, as in Ag-Cu nanoalloys) give strong starting labellings; then relax.

Import from protein-design / graph coloring: treat the label assignment on a fixed contact graph as a max-weight cut-like problem and solve it exactly with a small MIP or QUBO solver for each geometry visited by basin hopping.

Use structural motifs of the 1.3 ratio (Frank-Kasper / Z16 polytetrahedral cores) as seeds at 1.25, and vice versa; Doye-Meyer's own phase diagram shows motif boundaries where both families are close in energy.

targets.name: Binary Lennard-Jones clusters: lower a putative global minimum in the Doye-Meyer table (N <= 100, size ratios 1.05-1.30) or its published improvements

partial_wins.statement: A certified improvement for some (N, ratio) with N in 101..150 over the best value in a fetchable published table (DOI or arXiv plus table reference); reported as a literature frontier, not a CCD record.

Audit: a machine-readable merged table of all 600 cells (min over the CCD table and all hosted archives, each re-evaluated from coordinates), listing every cell where the live table is beaten by a hosted file by > 1e-4 and any posted point file that does not reproduce its own posted energy within 1e-5.

A certified improvement at a size ratio in 1.4..2.0 for N <= 50 over Takeuchi's published value for the same (N, ratio) (his supplementary data), or a first certified putative global minimum for ratio 1.4..2.0 at N in 51..100 reported as a literature frontier.

pitfalls: The live CCD table is NOT the record: several cells are beaten by archives hosted elsewhere on the same site and by Takeuchi 2015. Beating only the table is not a win; re-evaluate every hosted file.
Wrong mixing rule or units: sigma_AB must be the arithmetic mean and all eps equal to 1; a Lorentz-Berthelot variant with different eps or a cutoff/shift changes every energy.
Composition: the record for (N, ratio) is minimized over composition; an improvement at a fixed n that is still above the cell minimum is not a record.
Under-converged posted coordinates polish to slightly lower energies; the distinct-basin test (>= 1e-4) is mandatory.
Header energies inside archive files are not evidence; always recompute from coordinates.
softmattertheory.lu's 180,000-cluster BLJ database (Mravlak et al. 2016) uses eps_BB, eps_AB != 1. It is a different potential, not a comparator.
targets.statement: Jonathan Doye and Lars Meyer (PRL 2005, 'Mapping the magic numbers in binary Lennard-Jones clusters') tabulated putative global minima of two-species LJ clusters A_{N-n}B_n with eps_AA = eps_AB = eps_BB and sigma_AB = (sigma_AA + sigma_BB)/2, for every N up to 100 and size ratios sigma_BB/sigma_AA in {1.05, 1.1, 1.15, 1.2, 1.25, 1.3} (the composition n is free: the record for (N, ratio) is the lowest energy over all n). The live Cambridge Cluster Database (CCD) table lists energy and point group per cell with point files. It is known to lag the literature: improved structures from Sicher, Mohr and Goedecker (JCP 2011), Istvan Kolossvary (PRE 2010) and Huang Wenqi and Ye Tao (JCIM 2011, two zip archives) are hosted separately on the CCD index page and NOT folded into the table (for example ratio 1.15, N = 73: table -404.046888, Huang-Ye file -404.0955878), and Takeuchi (Comput. Theor. Chem. 2015) reported further new minima (N = 59 and 68 at 1.15, N = 70 at 1.2). Six hundred cells, one 2005 search plus scattered patches: the cells N = 60..100 are the realistic frontier.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an xyz file with N atoms labelled A/B (any composition) for a size ratio in {1.05,...,1.3} and N <= 100, whose energy E* = sum_{i<j} 4 eps (sigma_ij^12/r^12 - sigma_ij^6/r^6) (sigma_AA = 1, sigma_BB = ratio, sigma_AB = (1+ratio)/2, eps = 1, no cutoff) is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) by at least 1e-4 than the minimum of: the energy for that (N, ratio) on the CCD BLJ table re-fetched live immediately before claiming, the energies in every improvement archive linked from https://www-wales.ch.cam.ac.uk/CCD.html (re-downloaded and re-evaluated by the checker, not read from headers), and any value for that cell in Cassioli et al. (population basin hopping, 95 new minima), Marques-Pereira 2010 (Chem. Phys. Lett. 485, 211), Kolossvary-Bowers 2010, Sicher-Mohr-Goedecker 2011, Ye-Xu-Huang 2011, Rondina-Da Silva 2013 (J. Chem. Inf. Model. 53, 2282), Wu-Cheng 2014 (J. Chem. Phys. 141, 124110), Takeuchi (Comput. Theor. Chem. 1050, 68), or any later paper found by an arXiv/Google Scholar search for 'binary Lennard-Jones clusters global minima'; AND the structure is a certified local minimum: polish in float128 or mpmath (30 digits) to gradient norm < 1e-10 in reduced units, then the 3N x 3N Hessian in double precision has exactly 6 near-zero modes (|lambda| < 1e-6) and no negative eigenvalue; AND polishing every posted structure for that cell with the same routine gives an energy at least 1e-4 higher (distinct basin).
targets.verification_method: Checker (< 10 min): curl the live table, parse the cell; download all.tar plus the four improvement archives and re-evaluate every candidate for the cell with the same energy function; evaluate the claim in float64 and mpmath (30 digits), L-BFGS then Newton polish, Hessian eigenvalues (6 zero modes, none negative); confirm composition and ratio; assert margin >= 1e-4 over the minimum. Calibration first: the checker must reproduce the posted energy of 10 random table point files to 1e-6.

angles: Short-range potentials reward maximal nearest-neighbour contacts: enumerate decahedral (Marks, Ino) and close-packed (truncated octahedra, twinned) frameworks with the highest contact counts per N, as Doye-Wales did for short-range Morse, then relax.
Seed from the CCD Morse rho = 14 (short-range) global minima at the same N, rescaled to the C60 nearest-neighbour distance; Doye's own work maps C60 onto short-range Morse behaviour.
Import from colloid science: sticky-sphere maximal-contact clusters (Hoy, Holmes-Cerfon enumerations; Hoy's packings are hosted on the CCD) give exact contact-graph candidates for small N.
Import from integer programming: maximise the number of unit-distance contacts on a lattice fragment exactly with a MIP, then relax off-lattice.

targets.name: (C60)_N molecular clusters (Pacheco-Prates-Ramalho N <= 105, Girifalco N < 81): lower a putative global minimum in the Doye-Wales tables

partial_wins.statement: A certified improvement for PPR at N in 106..150, or for Girifalco at N in 81..150 against Cheng-Cai-Shao 2005, with a fetchable published comparator (DOI/arXiv plus table reference); a literature frontier, not a CCD record.
Audit of both tables: posted point files that do not reproduce their posted energies or that polish lower by > 1e-4.

pitfalls: Two different potentials with different units (eV vs well-depth units); compare only within one table.
The Leary tetrahedron at N = 98, suggested by experiment, is NOT the PPR minimum per Doye et al.; reproducing experiment-motivated structures is not a record unless the energy beats the table.
Precision: the PPR table lists eV values; margins below 1e-4 are noise.
Under-converged posted coordinates; distinct-basin test mandatory.

PPR without its three-body term, or with a sign or prefactor error in it, gives energies below the table. This exact coding error produced wrong 'global minima' in an earlier PPR study (see Doye et al. 2001).
targets.statement: Jonathan Doye, David Wales, W. Branz and Florent Calvo (PRB 2001) located putative global minima of clusters of rigid-sphere C60 molecules interacting through the Pacheco and Prates-Ramalho potential up to N = 105 (icosahedral up to N = 15, then decahedral and close-packed); Doye and Wales (CPL 1996) did the same for the shorter-ranged Girifalco potential for N < 81. Both tables are on the Cambridge Cluster Database with point files. The short effective range makes landscapes strongly multi-funnel; Shao et al. (IEICE Trans. 2013) revisited only N <= 25. N = 26..105 for PPR has not been re-searched systematically (search 2026-10-13).
targets.success_criterion: Success means centre-of-mass coordinates of N molecules such that E* under the exact potential of that table (PPR = pair term plus Axilrod-Teller three-body term as in Doye et al. PRB 64, 235409; or Girifalco; calibrated by reproducing ten posted point-file energies to 1e-6 in the table's units) is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than the live table energy for (potential, N) re-fetched immediately before claiming by at least 1e-4, AND than Shao et al. 2013 (PPR, N <= 25), Cheng-Cai-Shao 2005 (Girifalco, N <= 150, ChemPhysChem 6, 261) and any other published value for the same potential found by an arXiv/Google Scholar search; AND the structure is a certified local minimum: polish in float128 or mpmath (30 digits) to gradient norm < 1e-10 in reduced units, then the 3N x 3N Hessian in double precision has exactly 6 near-zero modes (|lambda| < 1e-6) and no negative eigenvalue; AND polishing the posted point file gives an energy at least 1e-4 higher.
targets.verification_method: Checker (< 10 min): curl the live table; parse; evaluate PPR as pair + Axilrod-Teller triple sum (O(N^3), fine for N <= 150) or the Girifalco closed form, in float64 and mpmath; calibrate on posted files (PPR calibration must FAIL if the three-body term is omitted); polish; Hessian; polish the posted structure; margins.

angles: Build structures as networks of interpenetrating 13-atom icosahedra (the motif Doye et al. identified) combinatorially: enumerate linear, ring and 3D network topologies of icosahedral units for each N and relax, instead of random starts.
Import from quasicrystal and Frank-Kasper phase crystallography: carve clusters from the sigma, A15, C15 and dodecagonal approximant phases that Dzugutov's potential is known to stabilise in bulk.

Import from graph theory: the disclination network of a polytetrahedral cluster is a graph; search over disclination graphs (as in the Nelson / Frank-Kasper description) as a discrete outer loop with continuous relaxation inside.
Cross-potential seeding: relax every Z1/Z2 minimum under Dzugutov and vice versa, and every Dzugutov minimum under the modified form for N <= 100.
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.name: Dzugutov, modified-Dzugutov and Z1/Z2 clusters: lower a putative global minimum in the Doye-Wales polytetrahedral tables

partial_wins.statement: A certified improvement for the modified-Dzugutov potential at N in 101..250 (the largest, least-revisited range) counts as the primary realistic win; report it with the structural motif (icosahedral network type).
Audit: any posted point file whose energy is not reproduced to 1e-6 or that polishes lower by > 1e-4.

pitfalls: The Dzugutov potential has a smooth cutoff and a repulsive hump; implementing it without the exact cutoff function or constants gives slightly different energies that can masquerade as improvements. Calibrate first.
Original and modified Dzugutov tables are different potentials; never compare across them.
Very flat, rough landscapes: many near-degenerate minima differ by < 1e-4; the margin and distinct-basin rules are mandatory.
Saddle points: L-BFGS can stop at index-1 saddles on these landscapes; the Hessian check is required.
targets.statement: Jonathan Doye, David Wales and Sergei Simdyankin (Faraday Discuss. 2001) and Doye-Wales (PRL 2001) found putative global minima of clusters bound by the Dzugutov pair potential (N <= 100) and a modified Dzugutov potential (N <= 250); Doye, Wales, Fredrik Zetterling and Mikhail Dzugutov (JCP 2003) did the same for the Z1 and Z2 potentials (N <= 80). These glass-former potentials favour non-compact polytetrahedral structures with very rough, multi-funnel landscapes; the minima were found by seeded basin hopping in one campaign and the CCD invites improvements. No later systematic re-search was found (search 2026-10-13).
targets.success_criterion: Success means coordinates for N particles such that E* under the exact pair potential of that table (Dzugutov 1992 form with the published constants, the modified form, or Z1/Z2; calibrated by reproducing ten posted point-file energies to 1e-6) is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) by at least 1e-4 than the live table energy for (potential, N) re-fetched immediately before claiming, AND than any value found by an arXiv/Google Scholar search for that potential's clusters; AND the structure is a certified local minimum: polish in float128 or mpmath (30 digits) to gradient norm < 1e-10 in reduced units, then the 3N x 3N Hessian in double precision has exactly 6 near-zero modes (|lambda| < 1e-6) and no negative eigenvalue; AND polishing the posted point file gives an energy at least 1e-4 higher.
targets.verification_method: Checker (< 10 min): curl the live table; parse; compute the pair energy with the smooth cutoff exactly as in the potential definition page; polish; Hessian; polish the posted structure; assert margins.

angles: bcc-aware seeding: build rhombic-dodecahedral and bcc-fragment candidates (the bulk structure of both metals) alongside icosahedral and decahedral ones for every N, relax, and compare; most cluster codes seed only fcc/icosahedral families.
Basin hopping with dynamic lattice search on surface vacancies, as used for Gupta silver (Lai et al. 2025), restricted to the outer shell of the posted minima.
Materials-science import: use the known low-energy grain-boundary and twin motifs of bcc Mo/Fe to construct twinned cluster candidates.
Statistical-physics import: parallel tempering with replica exchange between N and N+1 (grand-canonical moves) to move between growth sequences.
Cross-potential transfer: relax the Sutton-Chen, Gupta and glue global minima of the same N under Finnis-Sinclair; structures optimal for one many-body potential are good seeds for another.
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.name: Finnis-Sinclair molybdenum and iron clusters (N = 3..100): lower a putative global minimum in the Elliott-Shibuta-Wales tables

partial_wins.statement: Audit: recompute all 2 x 98 posted point files and list every row whose posted energy is not reproduced within 1e-6 eV or that polishes lower by more than 1e-4 eV.

A certified improvement for N in 101..150 for either metal against a fetchable published comparator using the same parameters (DOI or arXiv plus table reference); a literature frontier, not a CCD record.

pitfalls: The iron table uses the 1986 modified Finnis-Sinclair parameters, not the 1984 ones; mixing them gives different energies that look like records. Calibrate per metal.
Finnis-Sinclair V and phi are piecewise polynomials with cutoffs; a sloppy cutoff implementation shifts energies by more than 1e-4 eV. Reproduce the posted energies to 1e-7 eV first.
The tables list 10 decimals; differences below 1e-4 eV are not records, and a polished posted structure that drops slightly is under-convergence, not a new minimum.
Some cluster codes report cohesive energy per atom or binding energy relative to isolated atoms with the opposite sign; compare total energies only.
targets.statement: James Elliott, Yasushi Shibuta and David Wales (Phil. Mag. 89, 3311-3332, 2009) located putative global minima of Mo_N and Fe_N clusters, N = 3..100, bound by the Finnis-Sinclair many-body potential (Finnis and Sinclair, Phil. Mag. A 50, 45, 1984; the iron table uses the modified parameters of Phil. Mag. A 53, 161, 1986). The two Cambridge Cluster Database tables give energies in eV to 10 decimals with point files (points.tgz) and say the results were only 'partially reported' in the paper. These body-centred-cubic metals favour unusual cluster motifs, and no independent systematic re-search of these two tables was found (searches 2026-10-15; a 2017 force-biased Monte Carlo study of Fe_N, N <= 60, arXiv:1708.00096, only reproduced energies 'very close' to the CCD values). Checked live 2026-10-15: both pages HTTP 200.
targets.success_criterion: Success means Cartesian coordinates for N atoms (N in 3..100) for Mo or Fe such that E* under the exact Finnis-Sinclair parameters of that table (calibrated first: reproduce the posted energies of ten randomly chosen point files of that metal to 1e-7 eV) is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) by at least 1e-4 eV than the table energy for (metal, N) re-fetched live immediately before claiming, AND than any published value for the same potential and N found by an arXiv / Google Scholar search for 'Finnis-Sinclair clusters global minima' plus the metal; AND the structure is a certified local minimum: polish in float128 or mpmath (30 digits) to gradient norm < 1e-10 (reduced units of the table), then the 3N x 3N Hessian in double precision has exactly 6 near-zero modes (|lambda| < 1e-6) and no negative eigenvalue; AND polishing the posted structure for that N with the same routine gives an energy at least 1e-4 eV higher (distinct basin).
targets.verification_method: Checker (< 10 min): curl the live table, parse (N, energy) pairs; download points.tgz; implement E = sum_i [ 1/2 sum_{j!=i} V(r_ij) - A sqrt(rho_i) ], rho_i = sum_{j!=i} phi(r_ij), with the cubic-polynomial V and phi and cutoffs c, d of Finnis-Sinclair (1984 for Mo; 1986 modified Fe) and confirm by calibration; evaluate the claim in float64 and mpmath; polish; Hessian; polish the posted structure; assert margins.

angles: Frank-Kasper import from metallurgy: build cluster candidates by carving spheres out of the Z, H, sigma, C15 and C14 Frank-Kasper phases (the bulk analogues Doye identified) at many centres and orientations, then relax.

Disclination-network enumeration from soft-matter defect theory: enumerate polytetrahedral clusters by their disclination graph topology (as in Nelson's curved-space picture) and relax one representative per topology.
Seeded basin hopping from N-1 and N+1 minima of the same table and from the Dzugutov and modified-Dzugutov tables, which share polytetrahedral motifs.
Lead tables: Doye showed the lead glue and lead Gupta potentials give very different structures; relax the Gupta lead minima (CCD Pb Gupta table) under the glue potential as seeds.
Population annealing with resampling (statistical-physics import) to keep many funnels alive at once.

targets.name: Glue-potential aluminium (N <= 190) and lead (N <= 160) clusters: lower a putative global minimum in Doye's polytetrahedral tables

partial_wins.statement: A reproducible open implementation of both glue potentials (from the archived Fortran sources) that reproduces every posted energy of both tables to 1e-6 eV, plus a list of any row that is not reproduced or that polishes lower by more than 1e-4 eV.

A certified improvement for Al glue clusters at N in 190..250 against a fetchable published comparator for the same potential (DOI/arXiv plus table reference); a literature frontier, not a CCD record.

pitfalls: Spline implementation drift: OpenKIM lists several spline variants (cubic natural, quintic clamped, quintic Hermite) of the same Al potential, with slightly different energies. Only the implementation that reproduces the posted CCD energies counts.
The lead glue potential (Lim-Ong-Ercolessi) is not the Gupta lead potential of the separate CCD Gupta table; never compare across them.
Margins below 1e-4 eV are noise for 6-decimal tables; under-converged posted structures polish slightly lower (distinct-basin test mandatory).
Glue potentials have finite cutoffs; an L-BFGS run can end on a cutoff kink with a nonzero gradient. The Hessian and gradient checks are required.
targets.statement: Jonathan Doye located putative global minima for clusters bound by the Ercolessi-Adams aluminium glue potential for N = 3..189 (J. Chem. Phys. 119, 1136, 2003; nearly all minima polytetrahedral, with ordered disclination networks like Frank-Kasper phases) and, with Shaun Hendy, for the Lim-Ong-Ercolessi lead glue potential for N = 3..160 (Eur. Phys. J. D 22, 99, 2003). Both tables are on the Cambridge Cluster Database with 6-decimal energies in eV and point files (all.tar), and invite improvements. Polytetrahedral landscapes are rough and multi-funnel, each table comes from one basin-hopping campaign, and no later systematic re-search of either table was found (searches 2026-10-15). Both glue potentials are tabulated spline functions: Ercolessi's original pages (fisica.uniud.it) do not respond (2026-10-15) but are archived in the Wayback Machine (2017 snapshots, HTTP 200), and OpenKIM carries several spline implementations of the Ercolessi-Adams Al potential. Checked live 2026-10-15: both table pages HTTP 200.
targets.success_criterion: Success means Cartesian coordinates for N atoms such that E* under the exact glue potential of that table (Al: Ercolessi-Adams 1994; Pb: Lim-Ong-Ercolessi 1992; calibrated first: the checker reproduces the posted energies of ten randomly chosen point files of that table to 1e-6 eV) is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) by at least 1e-4 eV than the table energy for (metal, N) re-fetched live immediately before claiming, AND than any published value for the same potential and N found by an arXiv / Google Scholar search for 'glue potential clusters' plus the metal; AND the structure is a certified local minimum: polish in float128 or mpmath (30 digits) to gradient norm < 1e-10 (reduced units of the table), then the 3N x 3N Hessian in double precision has exactly 6 near-zero modes (|lambda| < 1e-6) and no negative eigenvalue; AND polishing the posted structure for that N gives an energy at least 1e-4 eV higher (distinct basin).
targets.verification_method: Checker (< 15 min): curl the live table; parse (N, energy); download all.tar; load the glue potential from the archived Ercolessi Fortran routines (Al cross-checked against OpenKIM EAM_ErcolessiAdams_1994_Al); E = sum_{i<j} phi(r_ij) + sum_i U(sum_{j!=i} rho(r_ij)); evaluate the claim in float64 and mpmath with the same splines; polish; Hessian; polish the posted structure; assert margins.

angles: Port the 2025 iterated dynamic lattice search (monotonic basin hopping + surface-atom perturbation + lattice search over vacant surface sites) that improved 47 Gupta silver clusters; the cobalt landscape is similar (decahedral vs icosahedral competition), and the code ideas are described in the open author copy.

Seed from neighbours: add or remove one surface atom from the best N-1 and N+1 structures (including the Co.zip improvements) and relax; the ten posted improvements cluster near shell closures, so look at N = 80..125 and 190..200 first.

Crystallography import: build Marks decahedra, truncated octahedra and twinned hcp/fcc fragments (cobalt is hcp in bulk) in every size and filling pattern, relax, and keep the best; hcp-based candidates are rarely tried in Gupta cluster searches.

Combinatorial optimisation import: treat surface-site occupation on a fixed core as a binary quadratic program (pair-energy surrogate fitted to Gupta energies) and solve it with tabu search or simulated bifurcation before a continuous polish.
Machine-learning import: train a cheap graph or SOAP-kernel surrogate on thousands of relaxed Co_N minima and use it to rank millions of lattice-based candidates before Gupta relaxation.

targets.name: Gupta cobalt clusters (N = 2..200): lower a putative global minimum on the Cambridge Cluster Database cobalt table or its posted improvements

partial_wins.statement: Audit: recompute all 199 table point files plus the ten Co.zip files with the calibrated potential and publish a merged table, listing every N where the posted energy is not reproduced within 1e-5 eV or a posted structure polishes lower by more than 1e-4 eV.

A certified improvement (same rules) for N in 201..250 against a fetchable published comparator for the same parameter set (DOI or arXiv id plus table reference); reported as a literature frontier, not a CCD record.

pitfalls: Several Gupta cobalt parameter sets exist (Cleri-Rosato 1993 and later refits); a lower energy under a different set is meaningless. Calibrate on the posted files before evaluating any claim.

The table rows for N = 84, 95, 101, 113, 121, 122, 196, 197, 198, 200 are already beaten by Co.zip; beating the table there is not a record unless the Co.zip energy is beaten too. Note the page text lists '107' but the archive contains Co197; trust the files.
Under-converged posted coordinates can polish to slightly lower energies; that is not a new minimum (distinct-basin test with margin 1e-4 eV is mandatory).

Energies are in eV, and the point files give coordinates in units of r0 (the posted Co2 bond length is 0.879): evaluate E with r_ij in units of r0 as posted. Converting the coordinates to Angstrom without dividing by r0 = 2.497 A, or rescaling the energies, changes the numbers.

The posted table point files carry 6 decimals and are not stationary points (gradient norms 6e-5 to 2.2e-2 eV per r0). As posted, only 84 of the 199 reproduce their posted energy within 1e-6 eV, and eight (N = 163, 175, 179, 183, 185, 188, 189, 190) miss it by more than 1e-5 eV; after a local polish 198 of 199 match within 5e-8 eV and N = 102 lies 1.1e-6 eV below its posted value. The calibration step against table files therefore only works after polishing (audit in PR #484).
targets.statement: The Cambridge Cluster Database (CCD) hosts a table of putative global minima for cobalt clusters Co_N, N = 2..200, bound by a many-body Gupta (second-moment tight-binding) potential, from Zhan Lixin, Jeff Z. Y. Chen, Wing-Ki Liu and S. K. Lai (J. Chem. Phys. 122, 244707, 2005), with energies in eV to about 10 significant digits and point files (points.tgz). Below the table the CCD links improved minima from Lai Xiangjing, Huang Wenqi and Ni Hanwen for ten sizes (84, 95, 101, 113, 121, 122, 196, 197, 198, 200; archive Co.zip), so the table rows for those N are no longer the record. Apart from that one patch, the 2..200 range rests on the 2005 search and one later re-search: Yang, Yu, Huang, Shao, Liu and Wen (J. Chem. Inf. Model. 63, 6727, 2023; self-adaptive differential evolution with basin hopping) searched Co_N, Pt_N and Fe_N for N = 3..200 against the CCD; their abstract reports lower-energy structures for 13 Fe_N clusters and does not mention Co or Pt (the full text was not read here); Gupta silver clusters in the same size range were improved at 47 sizes as recently as 2025 (Lai, Hao, Guo, Wen and Fu, Comput. Phys. Commun. 2025, iterated dynamic lattice search), which suggests the cobalt table is not converged at N > 100. The page states no potential parameters; the Cleri-Rosato cobalt values (A = 0.0950 eV, xi = 1.4880 eV, p = 11.604, q = 2.286) with distances in units of r0 reproduce all ten Co.zip energies of Co/Energy.txt within 4.8e-7 eV (audit in PR #484). Checked live 2026-10-15 (table page HTTP 200, Co.zip HTTP 200); page, points.tgz and Co.zip unchanged on 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-24.
targets.success_criterion: Success means Cartesian coordinates for N atoms (N in 2..200) such that E* under the exact Gupta parameter set of the CCD cobalt table (calibrated first: the checker must reproduce the posted energies of ten randomly chosen table point files to 1e-6 eV, and of all ten Co.zip files) is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) by at least 1e-4 eV than the minimum of (a) the table energy for that N on the live CCD cobalt page re-fetched immediately before claiming, (b) the energy recomputed from the Co.zip file for that N if one exists, and (c) any published value for the same potential and N found by an arXiv / Google Scholar / Crossref search for 'cobalt clusters Gupta global minimum'; AND the structure is a certified local minimum: polish in float128 or mpmath (30 digits) to gradient norm < 1e-10 (reduced units of the table), then the 3N x 3N Hessian in double precision has exactly 6 near-zero modes (|lambda| < 1e-6) and no negative eigenvalue; AND polishing every posted structure for that N with the same routine gives an energy at least 1e-4 eV higher (distinct basin).
targets.verification_method: Checker (< 10 min): curl the live cobalt table and parse (N, energy) pairs; download points.tgz and Co.zip; implement E = sum_i [ sum_{j!=i} A exp(-p (r_ij/r0 - 1)) - sqrt( sum_{j!=i} xi^2 exp(-2q (r_ij/r0 - 1)) ) ] with the parameter set that reproduces the posted files (start from Cleri-Rosato cobalt values and confirm by calibration); evaluate the claim in float64 and mpmath; L-BFGS then Newton polish; Hessian eigenvalues; polish posted structures for the same N; assert margins.

angles: Na Gupta/MM N = 150..380: grow-and-relax from the posted N-1 and N+1 structures (add/remove the least-bound surface atom, then short basin hopping); one-campaign tables at large N usually have isolated sizes that missed the neighbours' motif.

Cross-potential seeding: the Gupta-Na and MM-Na tables cover the same metal and N range; relax each table's structure under the other potential; any cell where the cross-seeded structure wins exposes a missed basin.

Import from nuclear physics / shell models: electronic-shell-closing sizes are irrelevant for these classical potentials, but geometric shell closings (Mackay 147, 309; decahedral 192) guide where to build complete-shell seeds and their vacancy/adatom variants.
Import from evolutionary computation: cut-and-splice genetic crossover (Deaven-Ho) with niche preservation by structural fingerprints, run on 10 cores in parallel per N.

partial_wins.statement: A certified improvement for Ag Gupta (A = 0.09944, p = 10.12, q = 3.37, reduced units) at some N in 141..310 over the minimum of the Lai-Huang-Xu 2011 file (https://www-wales.ch.cam.ac.uk/~wales/CCD/Gupta_Ag141-Ag310.zip) and the Lai-Hao-Guo-Wen-Fu 2025 values (Comput. Phys. Commun. 109655, Table 2; author copy https://leria-info.univ-angers.fr/%7Ejinkao.hao/papers/LaietalCOMPHY2025.pdf), same local-minimum and distinct-basin rules.

Audit of all posted point files (Zn, Cd, Pb, Na Gupta; Na MM) listing any row whose posted energy is not reproduced to 1e-5 eV (5e-5 eV for the 4-decimal Na MM table), or that polishes lower by > 1e-4 eV.

The Pb Gupta table page text says 'zinc Gupta potential' (a page typo); do not infer parameters from page prose, use the cited paper.
Hosted improvement files (Pb_Gupta.rar, Ag141-310 zip) are part of the record; check them before claiming.

targets.statement: Jonathan Doye (PRB 2003, Comp. Mater. Sci. 2006) and Eva Noya, Doye, David Wales and Andres Aguado (EPJD 2006) posted putative global minima for many-body Gupta-potential clusters of zinc and cadmium (N <= 125), lead (N <= 150) and sodium (N <= 379), and Murrell-Mottram sodium clusters (N <= 380), on the Cambridge Cluster Database with point files (energies in eV, to 6 decimals for the Gupta tables and 4 decimals for the Murrell-Mottram Na table). Doye found these 'disordered' clusters have rough landscapes with no single dominant motif, so the large-N Na tables (hundreds of atoms, one search campaign) are the realistic frontier. Separately hosted CCD files from Lai Xiangjing, Huang Wenqi and Xu Ruchu (Pb Gupta 2011; Ag Gupta N = 141..310, CPL 2011) are additional comparators.
targets.success_criterion: Success means coordinates for N atoms such that E* under the exact Gupta (or Murrell-Mottram) parameter set used for that table (calibrated by reproducing ten posted point-file energies to 1e-5 eV for the 6-decimal Gupta tables, or 5e-5 eV for the 4-decimal Murrell-Mottram Na table) is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) by at least 1e-4 eV for the 6-decimal Gupta tables, or 1e-3 eV for the 4-decimal Murrell-Mottram Na table, than the live table energy for that (metal, N) re-fetched immediately before claiming, AND than any hosted CCD improvement file and any published value found by an arXiv/Google Scholar search for that metal and potential; AND the structure is a certified local minimum: polish in float128 or mpmath (30 digits) to gradient norm < 1e-10 in reduced units, then the 3N x 3N Hessian in double precision has exactly 6 near-zero modes (|lambda| < 1e-6) and no negative eigenvalue; AND polishing the posted point file gives an energy higher by at least the same margin.
targets.verification_method: Checker (< 15 min for N <= 380): curl the live table; parse (N, energy); evaluate the Gupta energy E = sum_i [ sum_{j!=i} A exp(-p (r_ij/r0 - 1)) - sqrt( sum_{j!=i} xi^2 exp(-2q (r_ij/r0 - 1)) ) ] with the table's parameters (or the Murrell-Mottram form for MM Na) in float64 and mpmath; polish; Hessian (sparse eigen-solver for N > 200); download points/all.tar and polish the posted structure; assert margins.

angles: Crystallographic enumeration: generate every rock-salt cuboid, cuboid-with-adatom and cuboid-with-vacancy arrangement with 2N+1 ions and charge -1 exhaustively (a finite lattice-animal enumeration), relax all, then basin-hop only from the best few.
Mineralogy import: include hexagonal (wurtzite-like and h-BN-like sheet) and stacked-ring motifs known from (NaCl)_n DFT studies; the ionic model can favour them at small N.
Charge-ordering moves: swap a Na+/Cl- pair or move the excess Cl- to a corner, edge or face site; the extra-anion position drives many of the near-degenerate funnels.
Electrostatics import: use Ewald-free fast multipole or exact pair sums with compensated summation so 1e-8 eV comparisons are reliable.
Graph-theory import: canonicalise relaxed structures by their nearest-neighbour graph to avoid re-exploring isomorphic minima.

targets.name: (NaCl)_N Cl- cluster anions (N <= 35, Tosi-Fumi Coulomb plus Born-Mayer and Welch potentials): lower a putative global minimum in the Doye-Wales table

partial_wins.statement: The same certified improvement (margin 2e-3 eV, same checks) for the Welch polarizable potential column, using a checker that solves the induced dipoles self-consistently and reproduces every posted Welch point file to 1e-3 eV.

A certified C+BM putative global minimum for N in 36..60, with the structure type (cuboid, column, sheet) and the full lowest-10 list, against a fetchable published comparator if any exists; a literature frontier, not a table record.

pitfalls: Table energies are rounded to 1 meV; any claim within 2 meV of the table is indistinguishable from rounding and must be judged against the checker's own evaluation of the posted coordinates.
Units: coordinates are in bohr and energies in eV; mixing bohr and angstrom in the Born-Mayer exponent produces huge fake 'improvements'.
The Welch potential includes polarization; evaluating Welch structures with the rigid-ion C+BM model (or vice versa) is not comparable.
Wrong total charge: a claim must have exactly N Na+ and N+1 Cl-; a neutral or doubly charged cluster is a different problem.
targets.statement: Jonathan Doye and David Wales (Phys. Rev. B 59, 2292, 1999) tabulated putative global minima of (NaCl)_N Cl- for N = 1..35 under two potentials: a rigid-ion Coulomb plus Born-Mayer (Tosi-Fumi) model and the polarizable Welch potential. The Cambridge Cluster Database table (dated 1997) gives energies in eV to 3 decimals with point files in bohr (all.tar). Ionic clusters have rock-salt cuboid minima with competing column and sheet structures, so the landscape has many near-degenerate funnels. No later paper reporting lower energies for these exact potentials was found (searches 2026-10-15). Because the table rounds to 1 meV, a new minimum must be recomputed from coordinates and differ by a real margin. Checked live 2026-10-15: table page HTTP 200.
targets.success_criterion: Success means Cartesian coordinates of N Na+ and N+1 Cl- ions (N in 1..35) such that E* under the Coulomb plus Born-Meyer potential exactly as in Doye-Wales 1999 (calibrated first: the checker reproduces the 3-decimal posted energies of every C+BM point file and agrees to 1e-8 eV with its own evaluation of the posted coordinates) is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) by at least 2e-3 eV than the checker's own evaluation of the posted C+BM structure for that N, polished, AND than the table value re-fetched live immediately before claiming, AND than any published value for the same potential found by an arXiv / Google Scholar search for '(NaCl)nCl- global minima'; AND the structure is a certified local minimum: polish in float128 or mpmath (30 digits) to gradient norm < 1e-10 (reduced units of the table), then the 3N x 3N Hessian in double precision has exactly 6 near-zero modes (|lambda| < 1e-6) and no negative eigenvalue.
targets.verification_method: Checker (< 5 min): curl the live table; parse the C+BM and Welch columns; download all.tar (coordinates in bohr); evaluate E = sum_{i<j} [ q_i q_j / r_ij + A_ij exp(-r_ij / rho) ] with the Tosi-Fumi parameters of Doye-Wales 1999 (arXiv cond-mat/9801152) in float64 and mpmath; calibration on all posted files; polish; Hessian (6 zero modes, none negative); polish the posted structure; assert margins.

angles: Start where the 1998 unseeded search was weakest (10-8, N = 40..80): seed from the 12-6 and 9-6 structures at the same N and from the Morse/LJ global minima (CCD), since all three families share decahedral/fcc/icosahedral competitors.

Lattice-based construction (dynamic lattice searching, as used by Shao and Huang for LJ 310..1000): enumerate Marks decahedra, truncated octahedra and anti-Mackay icosahedra, fill/remove surface sites greedily, then relax.
Import from crystallography: generate twinned and stacking-fault close-packed fragments (hcp/fcc mixtures, labelled 'c' in the tables) as seeds; these are under-sampled by random-start basin hopping.

Import from machine learning: train a cheap surrogate on local-environment descriptors (coordination, common-neighbour analysis) over all posted minima, then use it to rank surface-site additions before expensive relaxations.

targets.name: Sutton-Chen metal clusters (12-6, 9-6, 10-8; N <= 80): lower a putative global minimum in the Doye-Wales tables

partial_wins.statement: A certified improvement for N in 81..150 for one variant against a fetchable published value (DOI/arXiv plus table reference) for the same parameters.
Audit: re-polish all 3 x 78 posted point files and report any whose posted energy is not reproduced within 1e-4 or whose polished energy drops by > 1e-3.

pitfalls: Parameter drift: c differs between variants and between sources (bulk-fitted vs reduced); a claim computed with the wrong c is meaningless. Calibrate on posted files first.
Energies are in reduced units (eps = a = 1); rescaling by element constants before comparing produces fake differences.
The table carries 4 decimals; differences below 1e-3 are not records.
Polishing a posted structure to a slightly lower number is under-convergence, not a new minimum (distinct-basin test).

The live CCD SC tables lag the literature at 12-6 N = 68 and 10-8 N = 58 (GrowPAL 2024). Reproducing those structures is not novel. GrowPAL's SI coordinates are behind an ACS 403, so the energy in its Table 3 (Europe PMC full text) is the comparator.
targets.statement: Jonathan Doye and David Wales (New J. Chem. 1998) located putative global minima of clusters bound by the many-body Sutton-Chen potential E = eps sum_i [ 1/2 sum_{j!=i} (a/r_ij)^n - c sqrt(rho_i) ], rho_i = sum_{j!=i} (a/r_ij)^m, for the (n,m) = 12-6 (Ag, Rh), 9-6 (Ni, Cu) and 10-8 (Au, Pt) parameterizations, all N <= 80, posted on the Cambridge Cluster Database with point files (reduced units eps = a = 1, energies to 4 decimals). Their own basin-hopping runs found only 95% / 94% / 85% of the final minima unseeded, the landscapes are multi-funnel (decahedral vs icosahedral vs close-packed competition), and the CCD invites improvements. The 10-8 table had the lowest unseeded hit rate. Two cells are already beaten in the literature and the CCD tables have not been updated (checked 2026-10-15): Lopez-Castro, Ortiz-Chi and Merino (GrowPAL, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 20, 4939, 2024) report new lowest minima for 12-6 N = 68 and 10-8 N = 58, and Shao, Liu and Cai (J. Chem. Theory Comput. 1, 762, 2005) a new Ag68 minimum; remaining cells N <= 80 have been re-searched by GrowPAL without improvement, so expected headroom is small.
targets.success_criterion: Success means coordinates for N atoms (N <= 80) for one of the three Sutton-Chen variants such that E* computed with the exact (n, m, c) of Doye-Wales 1998 (calibrated by reproducing ten posted point-file energies to 1e-4) is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) by at least 1e-3 than the minimum of the table energy for that (variant, N) re-fetched live immediately before claiming and every published value for that cell, at least GrowPAL 2024 (Table 3 and SI) and Shao-Liu-Cai 2005, plus any value found by an arXiv/Google Scholar search for 'Sutton-Chen clusters global minima'; for 12-6 N = 68 and 10-8 N = 58 beating the CCD table alone is explicitly NOT a win; AND the structure is a certified local minimum: polish in float128 or mpmath (30 digits) to gradient norm < 1e-10 in reduced units, then the 3N x 3N Hessian in double precision has exactly 6 near-zero modes (|lambda| < 1e-6) and no negative eigenvalue, AND polishing the posted point file gives an energy at least 1e-3 higher (distinct basin).
targets.verification_method: Checker (< 10 min): curl the table page for the variant, parse N and energy; load claim; compute SC energy in float64 and mpmath; polish (analytic gradient), Hessian check; download points/all.tar, polish the posted structure; assert margins. Potential constants (n, m, c) are taken from Doye-Wales 1998 Table 1 (arXiv cond-mat/9711038) and must reproduce posted energies before any claim is evaluated.

angles: Two-level search: enumerate oxygen frameworks (stacked pentagonal/cubic prisms, cages) then solve the proton-arrangement problem exactly over the ice-rule-satisfying orientations of each framework (a constrained discrete optimisation), before rigid-body relaxation.
Import from statistical physics of ice: use Pauling ice-rule graph enumeration (loop moves on the hydrogen-bond digraph) to explore proton disorder exhaustively for N <= 30.
Import from crystallography: carve clusters from clathrate hydrate cages (5^12, 5^12 6^2) for N = 20..40; these are known competitors for TIP4P.
Use the TTM2-F vs TIP4P disagreement at N = 17 and 21 (reported in 2024 work) as a hint of near-degenerate funnels where re-seeding across models may expose missed TIP4P basins.

targets.name: Rigid-water clusters (TIP4P, TIP5P): lower a putative global minimum for (H2O)_N, N <= 21 on the CCD, or beyond against published values

partial_wins.statement: A certified TIP4P or TIP5P minimum for some N in 22..40 lower than a specific fetchable published value (DOI/arXiv plus table reference) for the same model; a literature frontier, not a table record.
A certified improvement on the CCD water-Li+ or water-Ca2+ tables (https://www-wales.ch.cam.ac.uk/~wales/CCD/water_cation/gmin.html; CPL 2005), using exactly the potential defined in that paper.

pitfalls: Model variants (TIP4P vs TIP4P/2005 vs TIP4P-Ew; TIP5P vs TIP5P-E) have different parameters; only the original models are on the CCD.
The CCD notes a published 'new' (H2O)10 minimum (Lee, Suh, Kim 2001) that was an error later retracted; recompute from coordinates.
Flexible-monomer relaxations lower energies artificially; monomers must stay rigid.
Cutoffs or Ewald-style corrections change energies; clusters use the full unscreened sum.

Papers that re-optimise TIP4P candidates with DFT (for example arXiv:2411.00754) report 'lower than CCD' energies in hartree at the DFT level. They are not TIP4P records and are no evidence that the CCD TIP4P table is beaten.
targets.statement: The Cambridge Cluster Database lists putative global minima of (H2O)_N for the rigid TIP4P model (David Wales and Mark Hodges, CPL 1998; N = 2..21) and TIP5P (Tim James, Wales and Javier Hernandez-Rojas, CPL 2005; N = 2..21), with xyz files and energies in kJ/mol (5 and 4 decimals). These small sizes have been confirmed by several independent searches (for example Kabrede and Hentschke, and later graphite-substrate studies that reproduce the same TIP4P minima), so beating N <= 21 is a long shot; the open frontier is N >= 22, where published putative minima exist only in papers (no live table). Hydrogen-bond topology (proton disorder) makes the landscape combinatorial on top of the geometric one.
targets.success_criterion: Success means rigid-molecule coordinates for N waters (N <= 21) such that E* under the exact TIP4P (Jorgensen 1983) or TIP5P (Mahoney-Jorgensen 2000) parameters, no cutoff, rigid monomer geometry preserved to 1e-6 A, computed by a checker calibrated on ten posted xyz files (reproduce to 1e-4 kJ/mol), is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) by at least 1e-3 kJ/mol than the live CCD value for (model, N) re-fetched immediately before claiming and than any published value for that N and model; AND it is a certified rigid-body local minimum (gradient < 1e-6 kJ/mol/A in rigid-body coordinates; rigid-body Hessian with 6 zero modes and no negative eigenvalues); AND polishing the posted structure gives an energy at least 1e-3 kJ/mol higher.
targets.verification_method: Checker (< 10 min): curl the live page; parse; rebuild molecules as rigid bodies (check O-H 0.9572 A, HOH 104.52 deg; TIP5P lone-pair sites); evaluate Coulomb + O-O LJ exactly; rigid-body polish and Hessian; polish posted xyz; margins.

targets.name: Lennard-Jones clusters: lower a putative global minimum in the Cambridge Cluster Database / Doye tables (N = 3..150, 310..1000)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: The Cambridge Cluster Database (mirrored on Doye's site) lists putative global minima of LJ_N (energy in units of the pair well depth, 6 decimals) with point files: N = 3..150 (tables.150.html, LJ.tar), N = 310..561 (LJ310-561.html, incorporating Barron 537-548, Takeuchi 506/521/537-541, Huang-Lai-Xu 326/533/536) and N = 562..1000 (LJ562-1000.html, Xiang-Cheng-Cai-Shao 2004 plus 580 by Huang-Lai-Xu). The N = 151..309 and 1001..1610 tables were hosted at Shao's Nankai site, which no longer resolves (2026-10-08). Pages last modified 2025-03-04 (server move); the CCD invites improvements by email. Decades of global-optimization benchmarking make N <= 150 near-certainly optimal, but N = 310..1000 were set by one 2004 lattice-construction method and only a handful of N have been revisited (DLS-TPIO improved 533, 536; Barron 537-548, 664, 813). This repository's merged result (known-knowns/lennard-jones-ccd-doye-table/, pull request #202, merged 2026-10-16) holds N = 662 at -4581.205775329, 8.80e-4 below the table's -4581.204895; merged values count as published values, values in open pull requests do not. Moonshot-ish within a harvest frame: realistic targets are N in 310..1000.
targets.success_criterion: Success means Cartesian coordinates (>= 16 digits) for N atoms, N listed on one of the three live Doye/CCD LJ table pages, such that E* = sum_{i<j} 4(r^-12 - r^-6) computed in mpmath at 30 digits is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than the table energy for N re-fetched live immediately before claiming, by at least 1e-5 (the tables carry 6 decimals; genuine new minima differ by >= 1e-3 historically), AND the configuration is a certified local minimum (mpmath or quad-precision Newton to gradient norm < 1e-15, Hessian positive semidefinite with exactly 6 zero modes), AND polishing the table's own point file for N with the same routine gives E_table_polished - E* >= 1e-5 (distinct basin), AND an arXiv/Google Scholar check finds no published lower value for that N (Barron's page https://academicos.azc.uam.mx/cbr/LennardJones/nw537-548.htm and the 2013 DLS-TPIO paper are known sources already folded into the table), AND E* is at least 1e-5 below every value for that N merged in this repository (known-knowns/lennard-jones-ccd-doye-table/; N = 662: -4581.205775329, pull request #202).

partial_wins.statement: A certified lower energy (same local-minimum and distinct-basin rules) for some N in 151..309 or 1001..1100 than a SPECIFIC published value that the skeptic can fetch (DOI or arXiv id plus page/table reference, the value quoted to the paper's precision); the CCD has no live table for these N (the Shao/Nankai host chinfo.nankai.edu.cn does not resolve, checked 2026-10-08), so this is reported as 'literature frontier', not a table record, and a claim without a fetchable published comparator is not a win.

A certified improvement to an (N, rho) row that exists on the live CCD Morse-cluster table (https://doye.chem.ox.ac.uk/jon/structures/Morse/tables.html), same local-minimum and distinct-basin rules with margin 1e-5, reported together with the best literature value found for that (N, rho) (the CCD Morse table is known to lag the literature).

Reproduction audit: re-polish every table point file for N = 310..1000 in double precision and report any N where the posted coordinates relax to an energy lower than the posted value by > 1e-5 (under-converged table row) or do not match the posted value within 1e-5.

targets.verification_method: Checker (< 15 minutes for N <= 1000): curl the live table page and parse the energy for N (multi-column HTML; pairs 'N energy'); load the claimed coordinates; mpmath mp.dps = 30 (or numpy float128 then mpmath for the final sum) compute E* with E = 4 sum (r^-12 - r^-6); Newton/BFGS polish in high precision and confirm E* stable to 1e-12 and gradient < 1e-15; eigen-decompose the 3N x 3N Hessian in double and assert exactly 6 zero modes and no negative eigenvalues; download the table point file (LJ310-561/<N>.TXT, LJ562-1000/<N>.TXT, or LJ.tar for N <= 150; all checked live 2026-10-08), polish it identically, assert its energy exceeds E* by >= 1e-5. For N = 664 and 813 also assert E* < Barron's -4596.1978 / -5712.2517 by >= 1e-5. For N = 662 also assert E* < -4581.205775329 (merged here, pull request #202) by >= 1e-5. For N = 447 use the lower of the Oxford cell and the Cambridge copy's cell (https://www-wales.ch.cam.ac.uk/~wales/CCD/jon/structures/LJ/LJ310-561.html, -2992.783729, which 447.TXT reproduces): the Oxford page's -2292.783729 is a typo (2026-10-28).
angles: N = 562..1000 came from a single 2004 lattice-construction + GA pipeline (Xiang et al.) and only N = 580, 662 (this repository, pull request #202), 664 and 813 have since been improved; run dynamic lattice searching (DLS) with two-phase local search plus surface-interior operations from the posted structures, focusing on N just below Mackay/anti-Mackay shell completions (e.g. 561, 923) where decahedral or fcc competitors win (as at 38, 75-77, 98, 102-104).

Structural-competition scan: for each N in 310..1000 build the best icosahedral, decahedral (Marks), fcc truncated-octahedral, and Leary-tetrahedral candidates by filling/removing surface sites greedily, relax, and compare; the 2004 table only explored lattice-based icosahedral/decahedral families.
Polish-and-audit first (p3): relaxing all posted point files in double precision is cheap and may reveal under-converged rows (the CCD Thomson tables had such rows); then target those N.

Known table-vs-literature gap (checked 2026-10-08): Barron's 2010 page claims LJ664 = -4596.1978 and LJ813 = -5712.2517, while the live Doye 562-1000 table still shows -4596.197078 and -5712.249964. Reproducing Barron there is NOT novel; the bar for N = 664 and 813 is Barron's value. Use the same trick (icosahedral 'IC no center' and 'ID' variants of the posted structure) on neighbouring N where nobody has looked.
pitfalls: Literature beats the table for N = 664 and 813 (Barron 2010, not folded into the live Doye table). A 'record' at those N that does not also beat Barron's values fails NOVELTY; always compare against the published value, not just the table.

This repository already beats the table at N = 662: known-knowns/lennard-jones-ccd-doye-table/2026-10-16-swimingupstairs-368a33a7/ (pull request #202, merged 2026-10-16) holds a certified local minimum at -4581.205775329, 8.80e-4 below the live cell -4581.204895 (unchanged on 2026-10-28). It is not in TROPHY_CASE.md, so check known-knowns/ too: a 'record' at N = 662 must beat the merged value by 1e-5, not just the table.

Units: energies are in pair well-depth units with sigma = 1 (E = 4 sum (r^-12 - r^-6)); a different reduced form (e.g. epsilon=1 with minimum at r=1, E = sum (r^-12 - 2 r^-6)) gives different numbers for the same structure.
Any 'improvement' under 1e-5 is numerical; historically new LJ minima differ by 1e-3 or more.
A polished posted structure giving a lower number than the posted value is an under-converged row, not a new minimum (distinct-basin test is mandatory).
The 151..309 and 1001+ tables are offline (Shao's site); claims there cannot be table records.
Emailing the CCD maintainers is an outbound message needing explicit permission from the human.

Morse point files (p2): the Morse table on the Oxford mirror (https://doye.chem.ox.ac.uk/jon/structures/Morse/tables.html) links point files by relative paths that return 404 there (points/32D, 32E, 32F and 38A, 2026-10-18); the files are served at https://www-wales.ch.cam.ac.uk/~jon/structures/Morse/points/. There points/32E (sha256 d34c05b2...6681) holds the 32F structure: it is stationary at rho = 6 at -125.126341 (the 32F row; the 32E row is -125.644966) and relaxes to the 32F values -116.415892 (rho = 10) and -115.246208 (rho = 14), while points/32F is 404. For N = 32 at rho 11.40-20.90, where 32E is the listed global minimum (-115.767561 at rho = 14), the table's own point file is therefore not available for the distinct-basin test.

targets.name: Packomania: equal circles in a circle (cci), beat a per-N record radius
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: Packomania's 'circles in a circle' table (cci) lists the best known radius r(N) of N equal circles packed in the unit circle for every N = 1..2600 plus selected larger N up to 5000 (2735 rows). targets.success_criterion: Success means a file of N centers (x_i, y_i) for one N listed in https://packomania.com/cci/txt/radius.txt such that the FEASIBLE radius r* := min( min_{i<j} |c_i - c_j| / 2, 1 - max_i |c_i| ), computed in mpmath at 50 digits directly from the submitted coordinates (no tolerance), is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the 30-decimal radius for that N re-fetched live immediately before claiming, by at least 1e-11, AND the configuration is not isometric to the posted cci<N>.txt one (sorted distance multisets differ), AND N does not appear in a History-of-updates line on the live cci.html newer than the one the scout fetched. QUEUE RULE (Packomania, checked 2026-10-20; cci N = 652..3943 queued since 15-Oct-2026): the N must NOT lie inside any range listed for this category on https://packomania.com/pending-requests.html re-fetched at verification time; a value that is already in Packomania's queue does not count as ours. No submission (email) is ever made; the claim is for the verified construction only.

partial_wins.statement: A configuration for some N in 1..2600 whose feasible radius r* equals the live table value to within 1e-11 but is certified non-isometric to the posted cci<N>.txt (different sorted distance multiset AND different contact graph, mpmath at 50 digits): a second optimum; not a record.
A certified improvement for one of the gap values N > 2600 that the table lists (e.g. N = 4495, 5000), where the record is a lattice-like seed by Specht rather than an optimized packing.

A certified improvement in the sibling regular-hexagon table chx (N <= 1261, 12-decimal https://packomania.com/chx/txt/radius.txt, so margin 1e-10) using the same mpmath feasible-radius rule, for an N not covered by any chx entry on the live pending-requests page (on 2026-10-08 chx N = 55 and 89 are queued).

targets.verification_method: Independent checker (< 2 minutes): (1) curl the live https://packomania.com/cci/txt/radius.txt and parse row N. (2) Load the claimed centers; mpmath mp.dps=50; r* = min(min pair distance / 2, 1 - max |c_i|). (3) Assert r* - r_table >= 1e-11. (4) Download cci/txt/cci<N>.txt, recompute its r (must reproduce the table to 1e-20; parser sanity) and compare sorted distance multisets. (5) Re-fetch cci<N>.html, the cci.html History of updates and pending-requests.html; apply the queue rule. (6) Compare the contact graph against txt/contacts.txt.
angles: Target N in 1000..2600: 2121 of 2735 rows are Specht's own (txt/author.txt), and the 2023-2024 Lai-Hao / Zhou-He / Basurto waves stopped near N = 1000, so the large-N rows have had far less competition. Use the N=1000..2600 coordinates as seeds and run perturb-and-repack (remove k circles, re-insert at largest holes, then re-jam).

Hexagonal-core templates: take the chx (hexagon) hex-number packings, cut a circular window and relax the boundary layer; Cantrell's bound rows ('now meet Cantrell's bound') show where the frontier is already tight, so skip those N.

Monotonic basin-hopping on a smooth penalty (sum of squared overlaps + squared protrusion) with L-BFGS, then an exact jamming step: solve the KKT system of the active contact set with mpmath to polish r to 30+ digits before comparing.
Rattler exploitation: rows with many 'loose' circles (txt/loose.txt) have slack; move rattlers to open up a boundary contact and re-inflate.
pitfalls: Direction and normalization: cci fixes the container radius at 1 and maximizes r; some literature reports the container radius for unit circles (ratio = 1/r). Compare r to r, never ratio to r.
Double-precision 'records' of +1e-13 are noise. The 1e-11 margin on the mpmath feasible radius is mandatory; a configuration with tiny overlaps that 'rounds' to a record is a false positive.

Stale-table trap: Packomania has a queue of over 5,000 pending candidates (2026-10-08). cci was not in the queue on 2026-10-08, but the 17-Oct-2026 list has 193 cci candidates in 652..3943; re-check pending-requests.html and the per-N page immediately before claiming.
Known-literature trap: an improvement may already be published (Lai-Hao 2024, Basurto 2024) but not yet uploaded; search arXiv for the N before claiming.
Submitting to Packomania is by email (an outbound message on the human's behalf) and is asked not to happen in October 2026; claim the verified construction, not a submission.

The queued 26-Sep-2026 'many: 4666 candidates' bundle of Moki & Julio matches their earlier release v2.2, which has no hsp table (see pitfalls).
targets.success_criterion: Success means N centers in R^d (d in {4,5,6}) for one N listed in the live https://packomania.com/hsp<d>/txt/radius.txt such that the FEASIBLE radius r* := min( min_{i<j} |c_i - c_j| / 2, 1 - max_i |c_i| ) (unit container ball centred at the origin), computed in mpmath at 50 digits directly from the submitted coordinates with no tolerance, is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than that file's 12-decimal value for N re-fetched live immediately before claiming, by at least 1e-10 (the table carries 12 decimals; 1e-10 is 200x its rounding), AND, wherever the posted hsp<d>-<N>.txt reproduces its own header radius to 1e-11, the configuration is not isometric to that posted configuration (sorted pairwise-distance multisets differ by more than 1e-8 somewhere) and r* exceeds by at least 1e-9 the highest radius that the verifier's own local polishes of that posted file reach, each run until it stops improving, under several trust-region schedules, AND the configuration is not a relaxed copy of a posted packing, which is a trivial derivation however much it gains (a polish gain is an errata note for the table keeper, as in packomania-scu-spheres-in-cube since #605; the claim names any posted packing it started from), AND (d, N) does not appear in a History-of-updates entry on the live hsp<d>.html newer than the one the scout fetched. COORDINATES UNAVAILABLE (checked 2026-10-28): every hsp4 file reproduces its header radius, but the hsp5 and hsp6 rows carry 4 coordinates and hsp6 N = 251-259 have no file, so among hsp5 and hsp6 only hsp5 N = 7 and 8 can be compared or polished (see pitfalls); for every other hsp5 or hsp6 N the verdict must say 'posted coordinates unavailable', and the N must be re-checked against the posted file once Packomania posts complete coordinates. QUEUE RULE (Packomania, checked 2026-10-08): the N must NOT lie inside any range listed for this category on https://packomania.com/pending-requests.html re-fetched at verification time; a value that is already in Packomania's queue does not count as ours. The 26-Sep-2026 'Moki & Julio *many* 4666 candidates' bundle is category-unspecified and cannot be resolved; the verdict must state this caveat and the N must be re-checked against the live table once that bundle disappears from the pending list. No submission (email) is ever made; the claim is for the verified construction only.

partial_wins.statement: A certified improvement for a row attributed to 'unknown' or 'A. L. Mackay' in txt/author.txt (hsp4), i.e. a row seeded from classical constructions rather than optimized.

An extension row: a certified packing for N = 301..310 (d = 4 or 5) or N = 260..270 (d = 6) that beats the obvious baseline of (best r(N-1) packing plus one ball at the largest cavity, re-jammed), reported with r* to 20 digits; not a record, but new data for an N the table does not list.

A certified contact-graph audit: for every listed N, re-derive r from the coordinates in the tarball and report any N where the posted coordinates do not achieve the posted 12-decimal radius (data-integrity finding). For the archives seen from 2026-10-16 to 2026-10-28 this is already reported (issue #232, see pitfalls): every hsp5 and hsp6 file except hsp5 N = 7 and 8 falls short because its rows carry 4 coordinates, hsp6 N = 251-259 have no file, and every hsp4 file reproduces its radius within 1.7e-12 (12-decimal rounding, not a finding); a new audit needs re-exported files.

targets.verification_method: Checker (minutes, plus the polishes, which take most of the time): curl the live hsp<d>/txt/radius.txt and parse row N; load the claimed centers; mpmath mp.dps=50; r* = min(half the minimum pairwise distance, 1 - maximum norm); assert r* - r_table >= 1e-10. Download txt/hsp<d>_coords.tar.gz (all three exist; hsp6 holds N = 2..250 only, checked 2026-10-28) and read hsp<d>-<N>.txt; count the numbers per row and recompute its r the same way (parser sanity: the hsp4 files must reproduce the table to 1e-11; all 299 do, within 1.7e-12). If the posted file reproduces its header radius to 1e-11, compare sorted distance multisets to rule out an isometric copy, then polish that file from its posted coordinates with your own local optimizer (for example sequential LP on the near contacts with a trust region) under at least three schedules (largest step 1e-2, 1e-3 and 1e-4), each until it stops improving, report every polished radius and assert r* exceeds the highest by at least 1e-9 (posted hsp4 files gain up to 3.3e-6 this way, see pitfalls), and read the claim's stated starting point: a relaxed copy of a posted packing is its derivation unless the claim documents real search beyond a relaxation; if the posted file does not reproduce its radius, or is missing, record 'posted coordinates unavailable' with the archive's sha256 (every hsp5 and hsp6 N except hsp5 N = 7 and 8 on 2026-10-28). Re-fetch hsp<d>.html (History of updates) and pending-requests.html and apply the queue rule. Report r* to 20 digits.
angles: Single-author tables are the softest: run a completely different optimizer than Specht's (event-driven LS compression in d dimensions from random starts, 10 cores x hundreds of restarts per N) over all N = 50..300; expect many small gains in 12-digit tables.

Lattice shells: in 4D the D4 lattice (24-cell kissing) and in 6D the E6 lattice give dense shell structures; take shells around a center, cut to N, and relax; compare with txt/records.txt (density-record N) to find N where the table is NOT already a lattice shell.

Kissing-configuration seeds: a central ball with a 24-ball (4D) or 40-ball (5D) or 72-ball (6D) shell plus a partial second shell is a natural template for N near 25, 41, 73 and N near the second-shell completions; the table's density-record lists hint at which are already found.

Large-neighbourhood search on the posted coordinates: delete the 5 balls with the largest free volume (compute via random probing), re-insert at the deepest holes, re-jam; polish the active-contact KKT system with mpmath.
pitfalls: 12-decimal table: compare against the exact posted value with the criterion's 1e-10 margin; an improvement of 3e-12 is indistinguishable from the table's own rounding.
Container convention: unit container ball (radius 1, centered at origin); the 'ratio' column is 1/r, not the objective.
A new packing isometric to the posted one (rotated/reflected) with the same r is not a record; the checker compares distance multisets.
Email submission needs explicit permission from the human and Packomania asks for no submissions in October 2026; claim the verified configuration only.

Tables are 12-decimal, and the posted hsp4 coordinates certify their rows only to about 1e-12. Some posted hsp4 files are also short of their own local optimum: sequential-LP polishes of hsp4-88, -99, -115 and -117 end 2.0e-8, 8.5e-9, 7.2e-8 and 3.3e-6 above their rows (checked 2026-10-29). The 1e-10 margin covers rounding only, and a polished copy is not isometric to the posted file, so neither stops a polish. The non-isometry test and the criterion's polish floor apply wherever the posted file reproduces its radius (see COORDINATES UNAVAILABLE).

The posted hsp5/hsp6 coordinates cannot serve the parser check or the non-isometry clause. In hsp5_coords.tar.gz (sha256 e3a7316a...20e5) and hsp6_coords.tar.gz (d36917c4...d15d), unchanged from 2026-10-16 to 2026-10-28, every row of all 299 hsp5 and 249 hsp6 files is an index plus 4 numbers; the radius they give is below the header radius in every file except hsp5 N = 7 and 8 (never above), as if the last coordinates were dropped (both N = 2 files put the two centres at the origin). hsp6 N = 251-259 are listed in radius.txt but have no file (HTTP 404), and the hsp6 page itself stops at N = 250 ('complete up to N = 250'). The 299 hsp4 files (hsp4_coords.tar.gz b929acc8...63df) reproduce their header radii within 1.7e-12. A new sha256 means a re-export: count the numbers per row again before using a file.

Spherical-code constructions: an N-point spherical code with largest cosine c gives N balls of radius s/(2+s), s = sqrt(2 - 2c), in the unit ball (centres on the sphere of radius 1 - r), and N - 1 points plus a centre ball give min(1/3, s/(2+s)). With the codes on spherical-codes.org this exceeds the live hsp4, hsp5 and hsp6 tables at 4, 70 and 159 N, by up to 6.1e-6, 1.9e-3 and 2.9e-3 (2026-10-24; Cohn's table changes, so recompute), so compare a claim with these radii before calling it new.

The queued 26-Sep-2026 'Moki & Julio *many* 4666 candidates' bundle (pending-requests.html of 17-Oct-2026) matches their public release v2.2 (github.com/Hashirama1337s/moki-julio-circle-packing, commit 855d8f6838e9, 2026-09-25T22:41Z, '4,666 records in 15 tables'; its RESULTS_TABLE.md sums to 4,666 over the 2-D tables crt, ccq, cpd, cpt, crc_100 to crc_800, csc, csq and cxd). Balls in 4-, 5- and 6-D enter that repo only at v2.4 (commit 3036c50f5da0, 2026-09-26T08:05Z). No free cells (2026-10-20): in hsp4, hsp5 and hsp6 every row is the largest at any N' >= N, so deleting balls from a larger posted packing never beats a row (kit/propagated_bar.py, PR #573).
