targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: Packomania's 'spheres in a cube' table (scu) lists the best known radius r(N) of N equal spheres in the unit cube, complete for N = 1..1000 plus lattice rows up to N = 1024192 (1134 rows; since the 17-Oct-2026 reorganisation txt/radius.txt gives 12 decimals for 1058 rows and 30 for 76; per-N coordinates scu/txt/scu<N>.txt). Proven only for N <= 10 and a few more. The table is being revised right now: 04-Oct-2026 Specht posted 2022 Lai-Hao-Xiao-Glover candidates for ~60 values of N and wrote 'This table needs a revision!'; 05-Oct-2026 Yuan Gao (Harvard) set ~80 records in 202..576; 06-Oct and 08-Oct-2026 Lu Peng set ~185 records across 102..946; 17-Oct-2026 Lu Peng continued (N in 95..883), Vidit Patankar set records for 40 values of N from 101 to 1596, and the table was reorganized. Author file (2026-10-20): Lu Peng 321 rows, Goldberg (1971) 262, Cantrell 231, Specht 173, Vidit Patankar 40, Lai-Hao-Xiao-Glover 39, so hundreds of rows are still 1970s-2012 constructions. scu is NOT in the pending-requests list of 17-Oct-2026, and the 'many: 4666 candidates' bundle from Moki & Julio of 26-Sep-2026 matches their public release v2.2, which has no scu table (see pitfalls).
targets.success_criterion: Success means N centers in R^3 for one N listed in https://packomania.com/scu/txt/radius.txt such that the FEASIBLE radius r* := min( min_{i<j} |c_i - c_j| / 2, 1/2 - max_i max(|x_i|,|y_i|,|z_i|) ) for the cube [-1/2, 1/2]^3, computed in mpmath at 50 digits with no tolerance, is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the live txt/radius.txt value (12 or 30 decimals depending on the row since 17-Oct-2026) for that N re-fetched immediately before claiming, by at least 1e-11, AND beats what the posted files already give with no new search: B(N) := max over listed N' >= N of r(N') by at least 1e-11 (deleting N' - N spheres from the posted scu<N'>.txt keeps its radius), and by at least 1e-9 the highest radius that the verifier's own local polishes, each run until it stops improving, under several trust-region schedules, reach from the posted scu<N>.txt and from the largest-N' posted file attaining B(N) (files that list their centres), AND the configuration is not isometric to the posted scu<N>.txt configuration (sorted distance multisets differ) and is not a trivial derivation of a posted packing: the posted scu<N>.txt, a posted scu<N'>.txt (N' > N) with N' - N spheres deleted, or the posted scu<N-1>.txt with one sphere dropped into a hole, each followed at most by a local relaxation, however much that gains (#264 and #265 were closed as such derivations, and the deletion-plus-relax siblings #236 and #237 were folded into the packing they came from; a polish gain is an errata note for the table keeper; the claim names any posted packing it started from, and an object seeded from a posted packing by real search, for example several spheres inserted and the packing relaxed, counts, with credit, when it clears all of these bars), AND N does not appear in a History-of-updates line on the live scu.html newer than the one the scout fetched (the table was rewritten on 04, 05, 06, 08 and 17 Oct 2026 from private communications outside the public queue, so a same-day re-fetch is mandatory). QUEUE RULE (Packomania, checked 2026-10-20): the N must NOT lie inside any range listed for this category on https://packomania.com/pending-requests.html re-fetched at verification time; a value that is already in Packomania's queue does not count as ours. The 26-Sep-2026 'Moki & Julio *many* 4666 candidates' bundle is category-unspecified and cannot be resolved; the verdict must state this caveat and the N must be re-checked against the live table once that bundle disappears from the pending list. Packomania coordinate files are CENTERED (container centre at the origin: circle/sphere radius 1, square side 1 in [-1/2,1/2]^2, cube edge 1 in [-1/2,1/2]^3). No submission (email) is ever made; the claim is for the verified construction only.

partial_wins.statement: A certified improvement (same rule) for an N whose live author (txt/author.txt) is 'Michael Goldberg' or 'Hugo Pfoertner' or 'Dave Boll' (pre-2000 hand constructions), i.e. a row nobody has optimized by computer; counted as a record if it passes the criterion, else as a near-miss with r* within 1e-6.

A certified improvement to the sibling 'spheres in a sphere' table (ssp, last update 26-Sep-2024, 1156 rows, 12-decimal txt/radius.txt) using the same mpmath feasible-radius rule against https://packomania.com/ssp/txt/radius.txt (container radius 1), margin 1e-10 because that file has only 12 decimals, same queue rule for category ssp. A p2 claim must also clear the full criterion's other bars against the posted ssp files: the deletion bar B(N) (by 1e-10), the polish floor and the derivation rule. Count the centre rows first: the live ssp100.txt, ssp144.txt and ssp155.txt (fetched 2026-10-29, Last-Modified 12 Jul 2026) list only N-1 centres (the row for index N is empty) and those reproduce the header radius to about 1e-12, so where the posted file is incomplete the verdict must say 'posted coordinates incomplete' and the N is re-checked once a complete file is posted.

Reproduction milestone: re-derive from scu<N>.txt the table radius (12 or 30 decimals) for all N <= 1000 and report any N where the posted coordinates do NOT achieve the posted radius (a data-integrity finding, which Deeter-style audits have found in other tables).

targets.verification_method: Checker (about an hour; the polishes take most of it): curl https://packomania.com/scu/txt/radius.txt live; load the claimed N centers; mpmath mp.dps=50; r* = min(half minimum pairwise distance, 1/2 - max_i max(|x_i|,|y_i|,|z_i|)); assert r* - r_table >= 1e-11 and r* - B(N) >= 1e-11, B(N) = max over listed N' >= N of r(N'). Download scu/txt/scu<N>.txt, scu<N-1>.txt and every scu<N'>.txt (N' > N) whose row lies within 1e-5 of B(N) (or the coordinate archive), count their centre rows, recompute their r (each must reproduce its 12-decimal row to about 2e-12; parser sanity) and compare the claim's sorted distance multiset with scu<N>.txt's. Polish scu<N>.txt and the largest-N' file attaining B(N) from their posted coordinates with your own local optimizer (for example sequential LP on the near contacts with a trust region) under at least three schedules (largest step 1e-2, 1e-3 and 1e-4), each until it stops improving; report every polished radius and assert r* exceeds the highest by at least 1e-9 (in a run of equal rows the smaller files are deletions of a larger one: scu886.txt and scu887.txt lie inside scu888.txt, scu740.txt inside scu741.txt). Compare the claim with each downloaded file under the 48 symmetries of the cube and report the share of its centres that lie within 1e-3 of a posted centre: #264 and #265 (scu<N-1>.txt plus one sphere) kept all but the added one, #526 and #527 (scu734.txt and scu741.txt with spheres deleted, then relaxed) kept all of them, our polishes of five Patankar files kept 44 to 98 percent, and the merged N = 884 and 886 objects keep 9 and 27 percent of the posted scu884.txt and scu886.txt. Read the claim's stated starting point and treat a relaxed copy of a posted file as its derivation unless the claim documents real search beyond a relaxation. Re-fetch scu.html History of updates and pending-requests.html and apply the queue rule. Report r* to 25 digits and the contact graph.
angles: Read txt/author.txt live and attack only rows still attributed to Goldberg/Pfoertner/Boll/Schaer (hundreds of N in 100..1000): these are decades-old constructions and the Oct-2026 waves by Gao and Peng show large gains are still routine there.

Lattice-cut plus relax: cut fcc/hcp/bcc and 'layered square' lattices by the cube at many orientations and offsets, pick the best N-subsets, then inflate with an event-driven (Lubachevsky-Stillinger) compression and polish the active contacts with mpmath Newton.
Peng/Gao ran N = 102..946; try the complementary N they did not touch (check the History of updates lists) and the rows between record clusters.

Monotonic basin-hopping with a smooth overlap penalty; perturbation = remove the 3-5 'loosest' spheres (txt/loose.txt gives rattler counts) and re-insert at the largest cavities found by a Delaunay-based hole search.
Rows N = 385..395 (and other runs) share one identical radius with ref [24]: they are a larger packing with spheres removed, so any genuine optimization of the smaller N beats them.
pitfalls: The table is being rewritten daily (04-08 Oct 2026). A value fetched by the scout at 04:20 can be beaten by Packomania's own update before the verifier runs; re-fetch radius.txt immediately before claiming.
Cube convention: coordinates are centered (edge length 1, [-1/2, 1/2]^3); testing against [0,1]^3 produces false protrusion or false feasibility.
Noise in the 30th decimal is not a record; the 1e-11 margin on the mpmath feasible radius is mandatory.

The 'many' bundle (4666 candidates, Moki & Julio, 26-Sep-2026) matches their public release v2.2 (github.com/Hashirama1337s/moki-julio-circle-packing, commit 855d8f6838e9, 2026-09-25T22:41Z, '4,666 records in 15 tables', all 2-D: crt, ccq, cpd, cpt, crc_100 to crc_800, csc, csq, cxd); spheres in a cube enter that repo only at v2.3 (commit ea2a2e66d21c, 2026-09-26T01:29Z). The count and the timing agree, but the queued zip is not public, so the novelty skeptic must still check pending-requests.html and the per-N page, and compare a claim with their later public scu records (455 N at commit fd6316dd, 2026-10-18; none of them in v2.2) (checked 2026-10-19).
Email submission requires explicit permission from the human and is asked to pause in October 2026.

Count the centre rows before trusting a coordinate file. The 17-Oct-2026 exports listed N-1 centres: scu_coords.tar.gz 6c15d5db... (N-1 rows in all 1000 files with N <= 1000, per the maintainer's note on PR #311) and ed1760a3...57c7 (Last-Modified 17 Oct 2026 19:37 GMT), in which every scu<N>.txt for N <= 1000 and 58 of the 134 lattice files leave the row for index N empty while rows 1..N-1 hold the centres that the next export lists as 2..N. The export of 18 Oct 2026 09:05 GMT (sha256 909f98ca...a4d0, radius.txt unchanged 2e2af491...1791, seen 2026-10-18 21:53Z) lists all N centres in all 1000 files with N <= 1000 and in those 58 lattice files; the 76 largest lattice files (N >= 70304) hold only the radius. An N-1 subset still reaches the table radius (998 of 998 files in ed1760a3 within 1e-9; the complete files within 1.5e-12), so a radius match does not show that a file is complete, and the non-isometry clause needs all N centres. Per-N files can change bytes under an unchanged Last-Modified (txt/scu100.txt was fd927c05... at 07:21Z and 4b7ff475... at 21:53Z on 18 Oct, both dated 15 Oct 2026 18:41 GMT), so compare sha256, not dates.

Free cells (2026-10-20): 26 rows, N in 209..807, lie below the row of a larger N by at least 1e-11, among them N = 727..733 below the 17-Oct-2026 N = 734 row (by up to 4.13e-4), N = 738 and 739 below 741, N = 743..746 below 747 and N = 806 and 807 below 808; no scu range is queued. Deleting balls from the posted N' file gives such an N the N' radius with no search (N = 733 from scu734.txt: r* = 0.0589436758646 against the row 0.058531064607); a claim must therefore beat B(N) = max over listed N' >= N of r(N') (kit/propagated_bar.py, PR #573), not only its own row, and should report its margin over B(N). Relaxing after the deletion does not make it new: #526 (scu734.txt minus one sphere) and #527 (scu741.txt minus two) beat B(N) by 7.7e-8 and 5.1e-7 that way. In ssp (partial win p2) 25 rows, N in 917..100000, are free in the same sense (margin 1e-10, largest gap 7.86e-4 at N = 30000 below 30093), all inside the 15-Oct-2026 Vidit Patankar ssp range on pending-requests.html.

Public packings outside the table (checked 2026-10-21): Vidit Patankar's release v1.1 of github.com/vidigoat/optimization-records (published 2026-10-18T05:54:31Z, asset packings-round2.zip, sha256 4d5f70542d8ce68f016c2bf3eed13127f7a6feec1141d90a125c6b33b564f091) holds scu packings for N = 209, 340, 458, 508, 512, 516, 517, 519-521, 727-733, 738, 739, 743-746, 796, 806 and 807, i.e. 25 of the 26 free cells. Each lies above the live row and the deletion bar (floating-point check for all 26; exact for N = 516, 521, 733, 739, 745 and 806, e.g. 733: 0.058947755877729602, 739: 0.058630658894405385). The repository tree's packomania/SUMMARY.tsv covers only release v1.0, so the release asset has to be read separately. Closed PR #264 holds an 806-centre packing with exact r* = 0.057020808306465647: the posted scu805 plus one sphere, closed by the maintainer as a trivial derivation, but public. A novelty check for any of these N must include both sources.

Rows set in October 2026 carry 12 decimals, and so do the posted coordinates, which certify their row only to about 1e-12 (scu734.txt, sha256 99f0f667..., certifies 0.0589436758646 against the row 0.058943675866). Some posted files are also far short of their own local optimum, so a local polish moves the radius far more than the margin with no new structure. Checked 2026-10-28 with sequential-LP polishes (two independent codes on scu101 and scu734), each run until it stopped improving: Vidit Patankar's scu734.txt reaches 0.0589436791633 (3.3e-9 above its row, median centre move 7e-6), scu101.txt (sha256 b48da09c...) 0.110240749048 (1.39e-7 above its row 0.110240609817, within seconds), scu517.txt 8.8e-8 above its row (5.7e-8 above B(517)), scu518.txt 1.5e-7 and scu747.txt 8.7e-7 or 2.2e-6 (largest step 1e-3 or 1e-2), while Lu Peng's scu880.txt and Goldberg's scu250.txt gain only rounding-level amounts (3e-12, 4e-13). Where a polish stops depends on the run: converged runs on scu101.txt ended between 0.1102407305 and 0.1102407490 (1.9e-8 apart; restarts from 1e-4 random kicks of a lower one reached the top), on scu459.txt 4.5e-9 apart and on scu747.txt 1.3e-6 apart. So no margin over the row or over one polish separates a polish from a new packing (1e-10 does not, nor does 1e-9): the criterion takes the highest of several polishes only as a floor and treats a relaxed copy of a posted file as a derivation however much it gains. A polish gain over a posted file is an errata note for the table keeper, not a record (#605).

targets.name: Spherical codes (Tammes problem and higher dimensions): beat an entry in Cohn's spherical-codes.org table
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: Henry Cohn's table at spherical-codes.org lists the best known spherical codes (maximize the minimal angle between N unit vectors) for dimensions 3..32 (plus one entry each in 52 and 64) and N up to 1024: 15,985 entries on the HTML index (checked 2026-10-20; 16,446 on 2026-10-08), each with the cosine of the minimal angle to 12 decimals, a coordinates file /data/<d>/<N> (16-17 digits per coordinate, one point per line), references, a '*' (HTML entity *) after N for proven-optimal cases, and in 4,859 entries (2026-10-20; 11,996 on 2026-10-08) the per-row reference text 'needs more optimization' (dims 3..32; in dim 3 only N = 842, 893, 907 and 952), meaning the posted code has not converged. A plain CSV is at /plain (15,894 rows on 2026-10-20: d,N,cos[,minimal polynomial]; it carries NO star marks and no labels). Dimension 3 is the Tammes problem (/plain lists N = 7..1024; proven only for small N and N = 24). The table is actively maintained (entries dated 'Henry Cohn, 2026', 'Antoine Jay, 2026'; Numaro records cited). On 2026-10-18, 4,160 rows cited Ilmari Vahteristo (arXiv:2610.19988, 'New spherical codes by tuning an annealing solver', dims 3..32) and 3,541 cited Azmi C. Ozgen (2026, dims 22..32); on 2026-10-24 the index had 15,443 entries, 3,299 citing Vahteristo (one found independently by Henry Cohn), 3,247 citing Ozgen and 4,243 marked 'needs more optimization'. Sloane's original tables (neilsloane.com/packings) return HTTP 403 to curl and are superseded. EinsteinArena's Tammes N=50 leaderboard (checked 2026-10-08) tops out at 0.51347176 rad, consistent with the table's cos 0.868173209127 (= 0.5134721 rad); never use that leaderboard as a record source.
targets.success_criterion: Success means N vectors in R^d for a (d, N) row present in the live https://spherical-codes.org/plain, coordinates given to >= 20 digits, such that after normalizing each vector to unit length in mpmath at 50 digits the maximum pairwise inner product c* (cosine of the minimal angle) is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than the table's 12-decimal cosine for (d, N) re-fetched live immediately before claiming, by at least 1e-10, AND on the live HTML index https://spherical-codes.org/ the (d, N) row has NO '*' (proven optimal) mark AND does NOT contain the text 'needs more optimization' (improving an entry the table itself flags as unconverged is partial win p2, never a claim), AND the row is not superseded by a newer arXiv result for the same (d, N) (search arXiv for 'spherical code' / 'Tammes' and N), AND the result is not a kissing-number configuration (if 9 <= d <= 23 and c* <= 0.5 the claim belongs to the bank target kissing-number-low-dim and is not counted here). Uploading to /upload-code is an external submission and is never done without explicit permission from the human; the claim is for the verified code.

partial_wins.statement: A certified improvement (same rule, margin 1e-10, no star, no 'needs more optimization' label) in dimension 3 (Tammes problem) for an N listed in /plain; only four 3D entries (N = 842, 893, 907, 952) carry the 'needs more optimization' label and they do not count here, so this is the hardest sub-case.

A batch of at least 20 certified improvements (margin 1e-10 each) to rows labeled 'needs more optimization' in one dimension d in 4..32, delivered as one file set with the largest improvement reported; these rows are flagged unconverged by the table, so the batch is a partial win, never a claim.

An exact-angle certificate for an unstarred, unlabeled row that has no minimal polynomial listed: a configuration whose minimal-angle cosine is shown (mpmath findpoly/PSLQ at 60 digits, confirmed at 100 digits) to be an algebraic number matching the table value to 1e-12, with the contact structure verified rigid; adds a polynomial the table lacks.

targets.verification_method: Checker (< 5 minutes per entry): curl https://spherical-codes.org/plain and parse the (d,N) row (CSV: d,N,cos). curl https://spherical-codes.org/ and locate the row via its link href="/data/<d>/<N>": assert no '*' follows the link and the row's reference cell does not contain 'needs more optimization'. Load the claimed vectors; mpmath mp.dps=50; normalize; compute all N(N-1)/2 inner products; c* = max. Assert c_table - c* >= 1e-10. Also curl /data/<d>/<N> and compute the posted code's c (must reproduce the table to 1e-11; parser sanity). Report c* to 20 digits and the minimal angle in degrees.
angles: Harvest the 4,859 'needs more optimization' entries (2026-10-20 count; the table is being re-optimized quickly): for each (d, N) download /data/<d>/<N>, run a smooth-max (log-sum-exp of inner products with increasing sharpness) L-BFGS descent followed by an active-set SLSQP on the true min-angle objective, then mpmath polish; 10 cores can sweep thousands of entries in hours. Prioritize dims 5..12 where N is moderate and gains are typically 1e-6..1e-3.

Structured codes: for d = 4..8 use orbits of finite reflection groups (W(F4), W(E6), W(E7), W(E8)) and their subgroups; union-of-orbits codes with one continuous parameter per orbit often beat unstructured numerical codes at N near 100..1024.
Lifting/projection: good codes in dimension d+1 projected or sliced to d, and codes in d lifted by adding a small coordinate, give fresh basins; also antipodal doubling (N -> 2N) of a good code in d.

3D Tammes (p1): seed with Hars' N <= 60 point sets and Deeter-style symmetric (D_n, T, O, I subgroup) starts, run 10^5 restarts per N in 60..150, polish active contacts to 30 digits; the 2025 N = 60 gain (6e-9) shows tiny improvements still exist.
pitfalls: Direction: the table lists the COSINE of the minimal angle; smaller cosine = larger angle = better.
Normalization: vectors must be exactly unit length in mpmath before computing inner products.
Starred (proven optimal) entries cannot be beaten; the star exists ONLY on the HTML index (/plain has none), so the checker must parse the index, not /plain.
'needs more optimization' rows are the table's own admission of an unconverged entry; beating one is p2, not a record.
Kissing-number overlap: configurations with c* <= 0.5 in dims 9..23 belong to kissing-number-low-dim.
EinsteinArena leaderboards have had verifier exploits; never cite a leaderboard without recomputing from coordinates.
Literature scooping: re-fetch /plain and search arXiv immediately before claiming; uploading to /upload-code needs explicit permission from the human.

targets.name: Thomson problem: lower the best known Coulomb energy for some N (Deeter / Cambridge Cluster Database / Riesz s=1 tables)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: Minimize E(N) = sum_{i<j} 1/|x_i - x_j| for N unit-charge points on the unit sphere. Live tables: (1) Wayne Deeter's table (deetour.net/oppp/thomson/, last modified 2026-10-10) with 13-significant-digit energies and point files e.<N>.txt (12 decimals) for N = 4..524, which already corrects several Cambridge entries (e.g. N = 263, 360, 377, 380-382); (2) the Cambridge Cluster Database Thomson tables (Wales-Ulker 2006, N = 10..400 plus magic N up to 972; Wales-McKay-Altschuler 2009, N = 400..4352 step 10 plus magic N) with 7-decimal energies and xyz files (9 significant digits); (3) the CCD 'Riesz energy database' s = 1 (53 configurations, N = 512..9913, updated 2026-09-20, 18-digit point files); (4) Wikipedia's table (N <= 470); (5) EinsteinArena's N = 282 leaderboard (37147.294418, AlphaEvolve = Deeter's value). Tables disagree in places (CCD Riesz N = 512: 124673.9055677 vs Deeter 124673.8412508), so the record for an N is the MINIMUM over all live tables. Lai-Hao (ESWA 2024) improved N = 360; 2025-2026 arXiv work (2506.08398, 2512.12416) maps landscapes without new minima. Only N <= 6 and N = 12 are proven (a 2026 claim for N = 7 is unverified).
targets.success_criterion: Success means N points on the unit sphere (coordinates to >= 20 digits) for some N <= 1500 listed in at least one live table, such that E* computed in mpmath at 30 digits from the normalized coordinates is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than the minimum energy for that N over ALL of: Deeter's table (https://deetour.net/oppp/thomson/, N = 4..524), CCD Thomson/table.html, CCD Thomson2/table.html, the CCD Riesz s=1 table (site/s_1/index.html), the Wikipedia table and (for N = 282) EinsteinArena, each re-fetched live immediately before claiming, by at least 1e-6 in absolute energy, AND the configuration is a certified strict local minimum (mpmath tangent-space Newton to gradient norm < 1e-20, all 2N-3 non-rotational tangent Hessian eigenvalues > 0), AND it is a different basin from every posted table configuration for that N: polishing each table's own point file (Deeter e.<N>.txt, CCD xyz/<N>.xyz, Riesz dat/points_<N>_1.dat) with the same routine must give an energy higher than E* by >= 1e-6. N > 1500 (Riesz rows up to 9913) cannot be Hessian-certified in under an hour and is partial win p3 only.

partial_wins.statement: A table-integrity finding: an N where a live table's posted energy is not reproduced by its own posted coordinates after mpmath polishing by more than 1e-6 (Deeter documents such cases for CCD N = 263, 377, 380, 381), reported with both energies to 12 digits.

A certified improvement for the logarithmic potential (sum of -log|x_i - x_j|) or Riesz s = 2 for some N <= 500 against the Lai-Hao 2024 ESWA values, if the scout can fetch that paper's table; same local-minimum and distinct-basin rules.

A certified improvement in the CCD Riesz s = 1 table (N = 512..9913) for N > 1500 or beating only that table: same mpmath energy, gradient norm < 1e-15 and a Lanczos/ARPACK smallest tangent-Hessian eigenvalue > 0 in double precision instead of the full eigendecomposition; reported as an improvement of that table only.

targets.verification_method: Checker (< 10 minutes for N <= 1500): (1) curl all live tables and take the minimum for N. (2) Normalize the claimed points in mpmath (mp.dps = 30), compute E* exactly. (3) Tangent-space Newton in mpmath until gradient norm < 1e-20; confirm E* changes by < 1e-12; build the 3N x 3N Hessian in double, project out rotations, assert 2N-3 positive eigenvalues. (4) Download every table's point file for N and polish identically; assert each E_table_polished - E* >= 1e-6. (5) Assert E_table_min - E* >= 1e-6. Report all energies to 12 digits.
angles: Attack N = 400..523 where Deeter's table is newest and CCD only has every 10th N: use Deeter's own method (basin hopping with symmetric seeds from his 'roundest polyhedra' lists) plus Lai-Hao-style population crossover of Voronoi-defect patterns (scars). Deeter himself found new minima at 360 and 382 this way.

Defect-motif engineering: for N near icosadeltahedral magic numbers (10h^2+10hk+10k^2+2) move the 12 disclinations into scar chains and re-relax; N = 520..523 and the Riesz rows 532..548 are far from magic and likely under-explored.

CCD Riesz s = 1 rows for N = 512..972 duplicate Deeter/CCD Thomson values in several cases but are HIGHER for N = 512 (124673.9056 vs 124673.8413); check every N in both tables and polish the Riesz point files, since under-converged rows are easy targets for p3.

Use the 2025 landscape result (number of local minima grows exponentially faster than thought) to justify massive restarts: 10 cores x 10^4 L-BFGS descents per N for N = 150..300 with symmetry-seeded starts (C2, C3, D2, D3, D5 orbits), then mpmath polish.
pitfalls: Under-converged table values: a posted energy can exceed the true minimum of its own basin by 1e-7..1e-4 (Deeter's audit of CCD). Polishing the posted coordinates and getting a lower number is NOT a new minimum; the distinct-basin test is mandatory.
Precision: CCD tables carry 7 decimals and xyz files 9 significant digits; always compute from coordinates in mpmath, never trust a printed value to more digits than it has.
Multiple tables: the record is the minimum over all live tables (Deeter, CCD x2, Riesz s=1, Wikipedia, EinsteinArena); beating only the CCD value is not a record.
Saddle points masquerading as minima: an L-BFGS stop with gradient 1e-8 can be a saddle; require positive tangent Hessian.
EinsteinArena shows a verifier-exploit leader on the sibling Tammes page; never take a leaderboard number without recomputing from coordinates.

angles: Numerical search as quantum-state optimisation: minimise sum_S tr(rho_S^2) over unit vectors (purity minimisation reaches 1/D^k exactly at AME states), with symmetric ansatze (permutation-invariant or cyclic in the parties) to shrink 6^7 or 6^8 amplitudes; this is how AME(4,6) was first found numerically.

Import from combinatorial design theory: AME states of minimal support are orthogonal arrays OA(D^k, n, D, k) / MDS codes; for D = 6 search for quantum orthogonal arrays and 'quantum Latin' structures (the AME(4,6) solution is a quantum Latin square of 36 entangled officers).

Import from coding theory: Hermitian self-dual MDS codes over GF(q^2) give AME states for prime powers; group-circulant (automorphism-guided) searches as in arXiv:2608.05781 cut the search to a few kernel entries; target AME(8,9) and AME(13,5)-type cells that codetables does not yet list.
Import from tensor networks: perfect tensors are AME states with even n; build candidate AME(8,6) from contractions of AME(4,6)-like 2-unitaries and test whether gluing preserves multi-unitarity.

Non-existence side: strengthen shadow inequalities with additional moment or SDP (Lasserre-type) constraints, as Huber, Guhne and Siewert did for AME(7,2) (arXiv:1608.06228) and Huber, Eltschka, Siewert and Guhne did with shadow inequalities (arXiv:1708.06298).

targets.name: Absolutely maximally entangled states: settle an open AME(n,D) cell of the Huber-Wyderka table (e.g. AME(8,6), AME(8,4), AME(11,3))

partial_wins.statement: A numerical AME state for a genuinely open cell (e.g. AME(8,6)) with max_k ||rho_S - I/D^k||_F <= 1e-12 over all k-party subsets S (k = floor(n/2)) after high-precision Newton refinement, posted with its amplitudes; this is strong evidence, not existence, and must be reported as such.

A table-maintenance contribution: a complete list of table cells that are blank or 'Unknown' but already settled in the literature or by live codetables.de k=0 cells, each with its citation or code parameters, checked by an independent script.

pitfalls: The table lags: AME(11,4) and AME(11,5) follow from codetables.de [[11,0,6]]_q codes, AME(12,5) from arXiv:2608.05781 (2026), AME(7,d) for every d >= 3 (including AME(7,6) and AME(7,10)) from arXiv:2608.01011 (2026), and AME(2q,q), AME(2q-1,q) and AME(q+3,q) for odd prime powers q from arXiv:2609.11796 (2026); constructing these is NOT new.
Numerical AME states are not existence proofs; numerical residuals of 1e-8 can sit near non-AME local minima. Only exact states or certified proofs settle a cell.
Stabilizer AME(8,4) and AME(11,3) are already ruled out by codetables.de upper bounds; any claimed stabilizer construction there contains a bug.
Purity of the code matters: AME requires every k-party reduction maximally mixed, i.e. a pure code of distance floor(n/2)+1; impure distance claims do not count.
Emailing the table maintainers is outbound contact needing explicit permission from your human.
targets.statement: An AME(n,D) state is a pure state of n qudits of local dimension D whose every reduction to floor(n/2) parties is maximally mixed (equivalently a pure ((n,1,floor(n/2)+1))_D quantum code; for even n a perfect tensor). Felix Huber and Nikolai Wyderka maintain the Table of AME states (n up to 113, D = 2..10; last updated 22.02.2024). On 2026-10-15 the table data have 73 'Yes' cells, 379 excluded by the Scott bound, 30 by shadow inequalities, 1 other 'No', and 2 cells explicitly 'Unknown': AME(8,6) and AME(11,3) (the latter cannot be a stabilizer state, Danielsen). Many small cells are simply blank, e.g. AME(7,6), AME(8,4), AME(8,9), AME(11,4), AME(11,5), AME(12,5). Some blanks are already settled elsewhere: codetables.de lists [[11,0,6]]_4 and [[11,0,6]]_5 stabilizer states (so AME(11,4), AME(11,5) exist), while its upper bounds rule out stabilizer AME(8,4) ([[8,0,5]]_4 has upper bound 4) and stabilizer AME(11,3); and arXiv:2608.05781 (Aug 2026) constructs AME(12,5), AME(17,11), AME(17,13), AME(18,11), AME(18,13). For non-prime-power D = 6 and 10 no stabilizer theory applies; AME(4,6) was only settled in 2022 (Rather, Burchardt, Bruzda, Rajchel-Mieldzioc, Lakshminarayan, Zyczkowski). arXiv:2608.01011 (Aug 2026) proves that AME(7,d) exists for every d >= 3 (cyclic quadratic-phase states for odd d and a coupled binary-odd construction for d = 2 mod 4), so AME(7,6) is settled although the table shows it blank; arXiv:2609.11796 (Sep 2026) constructs stabilizer AME(2q,q) and AME(2q-1,q) states and AME(q+3,q) states for every odd prime power q. Genuinely open cells include AME(8,6), non-stabilizer AME(8,4) and AME(11,3).
targets.success_criterion: Success means, for an (n,D) cell that is blank or 'Unknown' in the live table (https://tp.nt.uni-siegen.de/ame/table.html, re-fetched live immediately before claiming) AND not settled by a codetables.de [[n,0,floor(n/2)+1]]_D lower bound (re-fetched) AND not settled in arXiv:2608.05781 or any other paper found by an arXiv search for 'AME(n,D)' and 'absolutely maximally entangled', EITHER (a) an exact state: amplitudes in an explicit number field (or a stabilizer/Hermitian self-dual MDS code over GF(D^2) given by an exact generator matrix) such that every floor(n/2)-party reduced density matrix equals I/D^{floor(n/2)} exactly, checked symbolically or in exact arithmetic; OR (b) a non-existence proof certificate (exact rational LP/SDP dual certificate for a shadow-type or new inequality) re-checkable in under an hour. Direction: settle an open cell; there is no numeric margin.
targets.verification_method: For a stabilizer claim: verify the stabilizer generators commute (symplectic form over GF(D) or trace-Hermitian form over GF(D^2)), count n independent generators, and compute the minimum weight of all nonidentity stabilizer elements >= floor(n/2)+1 (exhaustive for D^n up to ~10^9, otherwise via the MDS property: every floor(n/2)-column minor of the code matrix nonzero). For a general state (D^n amplitudes, e.g. 6^7 = 279,936): form each reduction by tensor reshapes and compare to I/D^k exactly (sympy/flint over the number field) or numerically for p1. Check the cell against the live AME table JSON and codetables.de QECC.php?q=D^2&n=..&k=0.

angles: Solve the quantum LP in exact rational arithmetic (SoPlex exact mode, or floating LP then rational reconstruction and exact verification of the dual) for every n = 101..256 and k, binary-searching d; this is the obvious first sweep.
Add shadow-enumerator constraints (Rains) and the split weight enumerators for k > 0; impure-code subtleties are handled by the A_i <= B_i structure.

Import from classical coding theory: the Delsarte LP for quaternary additive codes with Schrijver-type SDP strengthening (semidefinite three-point bounds) can beat the LP; feasible for n up to a few dozen, so use it to test whether LP-only results are tight near n = 101.
Import from numerical analysis: Krawtchouk values reach 4^256; use exact integers or scaled orthogonal-polynomial recurrences to avoid catastrophic cancellation.

targets.name: Qubit stabilizer codes n = 101..256: lower a weak UPPER bound in Grassl's codetables.de qubit table with an exact LP/shadow certificate

partial_wins.statement: A monotonicity repair list: every cell where the live upper bounds violate the standard propagation rules, with the corrected implied bound; useful to maintainers but not a new bound (report as audit).
An exact LP certificate lowering an upper bound for some cell with n <= 100 (where Rains' program was used), which would indicate the earlier computation missed constraints.

pitfalls: Floating-point LPs at n > 100 are numerically meaningless because the coefficients span hundreds of orders of magnitude; only an exact certificate counts.
k = 0 cells use a different distance definition (impure, self-dual codes); do not mix the k = 0 LP with k > 0.
Propagation-implied 'improvements' from other live cells are not new bounds.
Lower bounds (new codes) in the qubit table are a different target; this entry is upper bounds only.
Emailing codes@codetables.de is outbound contact needing explicit permission from your human.
targets.statement: Since 24 May 2024 codetables.de lists bounds on the minimum distance of qubit stabilizer codes [[n,k,d]] up to n = 256 (Markus Grassl). The page notes say most upper bounds for n <= 100 come from Eric Rains' MAGMA linear-programming program, while for n > 100 'the upper bounds on qubit codes are weak (and not necessarily monotone in k)'. Spot checks on 2026-10-15: [[101,1]] 23-34, [[150,1]] 33-51, [[200,1]] 39-67, [[256,1]] 50-86, [[200,20]] 34-59, [[256,60]] 35-63; several of these equal or sit near the self-dual shadow bound 2*floor(n/6)+2, suggesting the full quantum LP with shadow constraints (Rains 1999; Ashikhmin-Litsyn) has not been run above n = 100. Lower-bound improvements in the qubit table are covered by another entry's partial win; this target is upper bounds only.
targets.success_criterion: Success means, for some qubit cell (n,k) with 101 <= n <= 256, a proof that no [[n,k,d]] stabilizer code exists for d equal to the live table upper bound (https://codetables.de/QECC.php?q=4&n=<n>&k=<k>, re-fetched live immediately before claiming), thereby lowering it by at least 1 (direction: min upper bound), where the proof is an exact rational infeasibility certificate (Farkas dual) of the quantum weight-enumerator LP (stabilizer and normalizer enumerators linked by the quaternary MacWilliams identity, A_i <= B_i, A_i = B_i for 0 < i < d, nonnegativity, plus shadow-enumerator nonnegativity where used), checked in exact integer arithmetic by an independent script; and the new bound is NOT already implied by applying the standard propagation rules (d(n,k) <= d(n,k-1) for k >= 2, d(n,k) <= d(n+1,k), d(n,k) <= d(n-1,k+1)+1 or as stated by the table) to other live cells.
targets.verification_method: Independent exact checker in Python integers/fractions: build Krawtchouk polynomials K_j(i) for q = 4 and length n (exact big integers), the LP variables A_0..A_n (stabilizer) and B_0..B_n (normalizer) with A_0 = B_0 = 1 and B(x,y) = 2^{-(n-k)} A(x+3y, x-y) (quaternary MacWilliams identity as in Calderbank-Rains-Shor-Sloane, quant-ph/9608006), the constraints for distance d, and verify that the posted dual vector y satisfies y^T M >= 0 componentwise with y^T b < 0 (Farkas). Runs in seconds for n <= 256. Recompute propagation-implied bounds from the live table for the neighbouring cells.

angles: Scale He's method: run (5, 6) and (6, 6) with the sector decomposition processed in parallel across cores, storing nothing of the matrix and streaming matchings; his table shows near-square cross-sections give the best bounds.

From numerical linear algebra: replace the plain Collatz-Wielandt iterate with a Lanczos/Arnoldi-accelerated test vector, then certify it exactly; a better vector at the same (m, n) can already tighten the bound.
From group theory: exploit the full symmetry group of the diagonal layer (translations, reflections, the swap of m and n) to shrink state space further than He's compression.

For the lower bound, look at Csikvari's matching-polynomial / Lower Matching Conjecture machinery and at Friedland-Gurvits; a 2-lift or local-view argument specialised to Z^3 is a separate, proof-shaped route.

targets.name: Dimer constant of the cubic lattice Z^3: a certified upper bound below He's 0.452130 (2026) or a lower bound above Csikvari's 0.441075

partial_wins.statement: Independent reimplementation that reproduces He's 0.452130 at (m, n) = (5, 5) and every smaller entry of his Table 2 to six decimals (rounded upward) with exact arithmetic; reproduction only, but it validates the method for the main attempt.

A certified improvement of either published bound on the 3D monomer-dimer entropy h3 at unit activity: 0.7849602275 <= h3 <= 0.7862023450 (Friedland, Krop, Lundow and Markstrom, arXiv math/0603001 and refs), same certificate rules.

A certified upper bound on the dimer constant of Z^4 from the generalisation He mentions but did not run, that improves the best published Z^4 upper bound the claimant can cite (DOI/arXiv + page); without a citable comparator it does not count.

pitfalls: Floating-point ratios do not certify anything; the bound must come from exact integer arithmetic with outward rounding, as in He's paper.
Non-rigorous estimates (0.4466-0.4499 from series and tensor networks) are not bounds; beating 0.452130 with an estimate is not a win.
He's paper is two months old and from an active author; a newer preprint may already have (5, 6) or (6, 6). Re-check arXiv immediately before claiming.
Torus vs cylinder vs open boundary transfer matrices give eigenvalues that bound l3 in different directions; an inequality used in the wrong direction yields a fake improvement.
targets.statement: The number of perfect matchings (dimer coverings) of large boxes in Z^3 grows like exp(l3 * volume); l3 has no closed form. Estimates: John Nagle 0.446 (1966 series), Butera-Federbush-Pernici 0.449164 (2013 series), Vanderstraeten-Vanhecke-Verstraete 0.44988452 (2018 tensor networks), Otsuka-Akutsu 0.44715 (2022 TRG). Rigorous bounds: lower 0.441075... = (1/2)log(5^5/6^4) + 0.001 by Peter Csikvari (2016-17), the first improvement on Schrijver/Minc's 0.440075842; upper 0.457547 by Per Hakan Lundow (Discrete Math. 231, 2001, Ciucu's transfer-matrix method) stood for 25 years until Qidong He (arXiv 2607.28810, v2 2026-08-11) proved l3 <= 0.452130 with diagonal transfer layers, Csikvari's matching-polynomial inequality and a Collatz-Wielandt bound sequence. He's table goes up to cross-section (m, n) = (5, 5), which took about 16.5 hours on one desktop PC with sectors processed sequentially (Java, Intel i7, 16 GB RAM); larger and more nearly square cross-sections gave sharper bounds and were not computed. Pushing He's method to (5, 6) or (6, 6) with parallel sectors is a laptop-days computation.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a rigorous bound on l3 that is strictly better (direction: upper bound smaller, or lower bound larger) than the best published bound found when re-fetched live immediately before claiming (arXiv listing and citations of 2607.28810 and of Csikvari's lower bound), by at least 1e-6, together with a machine-checkable certificate: the explicit nonnegative integer or rational test vector and transfer-layer definition such that a skeptic's independent program recomputes the Collatz-Wielandt ratio with exact integer arithmetic (cross-multiplication) and obtains the claimed bound rounded outward, plus a written derivation (or exact citation of He's Corollary 3.4 / Lundow's inequalities) of why that ratio bounds l3.
targets.verification_method: Skeptic (< 1 hour for the check, not the search): load the certificate vector (compressed by the stated symmetries), rebuild the transfer layer independently from its definition, compute (T v)_i / v_i for every coordinate in exact integers, take the stated extremum and power/normalisation from the paper's corollary, and compare with the claim; also rerun (m, n) = (3, 3) and (4, 4) to match He's table.

angles: Start from good classical ternary (or GF(9)) linear codes from codetables.de: any [n,k,d]_9 code gives an EAQECC via the Brun-Devetak-Hsieh construction with c set by the rank of its Hermitian hull, so searching for codes with small Hermitian hull is a direct route.
Quasi-cyclic and quasi-twisted searches over GF(9) with hull-dimension control, mirroring the Ezerman-Grassl-Ling methods that filled the qudit tables.
Import from SAT/ILP: encode 'stabilizer with given commutation rank and no low-weight logical' for n <= 12 and search exhaustively for the smallest gap cells.

Propagation: one new code yields neighbours via the table's own rules (subcode, lengthening, puncturing, teleportation [[n-1,k,d;c+1]]); run them to find all cells it improves, but only cells not already implied by existing entries count.

targets.name: Entanglement-assisted qutrit codes [[n,k,d;c]]_3 with c >= 1: raise a lower bound in Grassl's EAQECC qutrit table

partial_wins.statement: Lowering an upper bound d_upper for some qutrit (n,k,c) cell with an exact rational LP certificate (EAQECC linear-programming bound) re-checkable in under an hour.
A new code that matches d_lower but uses strictly fewer entangled pairs c than any listed code with the same (n,k,d), with the c-dependence checked against the live table row.

pitfalls: c = 0 codes are ordinary qutrit stabilizer codes; improvements there belong to the separate qudit-table target.
Getting c wrong: c is determined by the commutation structure of the stabilizer generators, not chosen freely; a code that needs more pairs than claimed is a different cell.
Catalytic vs non-catalytic: the table is non-catalytic; catalytic-setting parameters are explicitly excluded.
Propagation-only 'improvements' from existing table rows are not new.
Emailing codes@codetables.de is outbound contact needing explicit permission from your human.
targets.statement: Entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting codes use c pre-shared maximally entangled pairs. Markus Grassl maintains bounds tables for qubit and qutrit EAQECCs (eaqecc.codetables.de; references: Luo, Ezerman, Grassl and Ling, QIP 2024 and arXiv:2207.05647; Grassl PRA 2021). The qutrit table (last change 10.07.2025) covers n <= 36 with 3,888 parameter cells; on 2026-10-15 3,281 cells show a gap d_lower < d_upper, 184 of them with n <= 15, e.g. [[6,1,4-5;1]]_3, [[8,2,5-6;3]]_3, [[9,1,6-8;1]]_3, [[10,2,6-7;2]]_3, [[11,2,6-8;2]]_3. The qubit EAQECC table and the unassisted qudit (c = 0) tables are covered by other entries; this target is the qutrit table with c >= 1, which has had far less search.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an explicit EAQECC with parameters [[n,k,d;c]]_3, c >= 1, given by an exact generator matrix over GF(3) (symplectic form, 2n columns) or over GF(9) (trace-Hermitian form), for a cell of the live qutrit table (https://eaqecc.codetables.de/qutrit.php, re-fetched live immediately before claiming), such that: with s independent generators on Alice's n qutrits, c = rank(S J S^T)/2 (half the rank of the symplectic commutation matrix) and k = n - s + c; the minimum distance d, computed exactly as the minimum weight of vectors in the symplectic dual of span(S) that are not in the isotropic part span(S) ∩ span(S)^perp (the EAQECC definition used by Grassl), is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the table's d_lower for that (n,k,c), and d <= d_upper. Results for c = 0 are excluded (they belong to the qudit table entry).
targets.verification_method: Independent checker over GF(3): build the 2n-column symplectic matrix S (rows = generators), compute rank s, the commutation matrix S J S^T and its rank 2c, infer k = n - s + c; d = minimum weight of vectors in span(S)^perp (symplectic dual) that are not in span(S) ∩ span(S)^perp. For n <= 20 exhaustive enumeration of 3^(n-r+...) cosets is seconds; otherwise use two independent minimum-weight algorithms that agree. Compare with the live qutrit.php cell.

angles: Numerical-linear-algebra import: Molteni's cost is dominated by the dense Jacobian of the collocation Newton step (O(n^3) multiprecision work); replace it with a Newton-Krylov solve whose preconditioner is the low-precision inverse Jacobian (mixed precision, as in iterative refinement), cutting memory from O(n^2.5) toward O(n^2).
Signal-processing import: evaluate g(g(x/alpha)) at all collocation nodes with fast multipoint evaluation and fast cosine transforms instead of n separate Clenshaw sums.

For the accumulation point (p1), use renormalization theory: c_inf is where the one-parameter family crosses the stable manifold of g, so solve R^n(f_c) - g = 0 projected on the unstable direction h with Newton in c; error contracts like delta^-n per step, and the 10,000-digit g and h are reusable.

Rigorous-numerics import (computer-assisted proof style, Lanford; Eckmann-Wittwer): wrap the final Newton step in interval (arb) arithmetic to turn the agreed digits into enclosures, which also guards against silent precision loss.

Exploit symmetry and analyticity: g is even and analytic in a disc larger than [-1,1]; choose a Chebyshev domain or a conformal map that maximises the convergence rate per coefficient (Mathar's Chebyshev representation, arXiv:1008.4608).

targets.name: Feigenbaum constants and the period-doubling accumulation point: more verified digits than the published records

partial_wins.statement: The period-doubling accumulation point of the logistic map (r_inf) or equivalently the Myrberg point c_inf, to at least 300 correct decimals: two independent methods (for example a renormalization/stable-manifold Newton solve and Richardson-extrapolated superstable parameters c_n of period 2^n) agreeing to D >= 300 decimals, D greater than the digit count of OEIS A098587 and A218453 re-fetched live and of any published value found by a literature search, with the conversion mu = r(r-2)/4 checked.

The z = 4 (quartic maximum) Feigenbaum alpha or delta to at least 1000 decimals, two resolutions agreeing, exceeding the digit count of OEIS A195102 and Thurlby's thesis (about 330 digits) re-fetched live.

pitfalls: Counting digits that agree between two runs at nearly the same resolution overstates accuracy; use resolutions differing by at least 2% and report the agreed prefix only.
Normalisation conventions differ (g(0) = 1 with g(x) = -alpha g(g(-x/alpha)), alpha positive or negative); a residual computed in the wrong convention looks huge or deceptively small.

Beating only the OEIS b-file (about 1019 digits) for delta or alpha is NOT a record; Molteni's 10,000+ decimals are the bar. For the accumulation point and the quartic constants the OEIS counts are only the minimum bar, and a literature search must find no longer published value.
The logistic-map accumulation point r_inf and the Myrberg point c_inf are the same point in two parameterisations; claiming both as separate records is double counting.
Precision loss in the composition g(g(x)) near x = 0 and in eigen-solves at high n can silently cap correct digits below the working precision; check with two working precisions.
targets.statement: The Feigenbaum constants delta = 4.6692016... and alpha = 2.5029078... govern period doubling in unimodal maps with a quadratic maximum and in many physical systems. Andrea Molteni (arXiv:1602.02357, 2016) computed both via Chebyshev collocation of the Feigenbaum-Cvitanovic fixed point g and a Krylov eigensolver, with a 6144-point run checked by a 6160-point run agreeing to 10,026 decimals for alpha and 10,022 for delta (3 days and 7 GB per run on a 2016 desktop). Earlier records: Keith Briggs (1991), David Broadhurst (1999, 1018 decimals). OEIS A006890 and A006891 carry about 1019 digits (b-files checked 2026-10-15; Steven Kotlarz independently re-derived 1019 digits of delta in June 2026). Much weaker records exist for related constants: the location of the period-doubling accumulation point of the logistic map (r_inf = 3.5699456718709449...; OEIS A098587 lists about 95 digits) and of the quadratic map x -> x^2 - c (the Myrberg point c_inf = 1.4011551890920506...; OEIS A218453, about 65 digits), and the quartic-maximum (z = 4) Feigenbaum constants (OEIS A195102 lists 50 digits; Judi Thurlby's 2021 PhD thesis gives about 330). Checked live 2026-10-15: OEIS A006890 HTTP 200.
targets.success_criterion: Main win: a computation of delta (or alpha) to D decimals with D strictly greater (direction: max) than the largest digit count in Molteni 2016 (10,022 for delta, 10,026 for alpha) and in any later publication or OEIS b-file re-fetched live immediately before claiming, where D is the number of decimals on which two independent runs at different resolutions (collocation sizes differing by at least 2%) agree, the leading 10,000 decimals match Molteni's published value where available, and the posted certificate passes the residual checks in the verification method.
targets.verification_method: Certificate: the Chebyshev (or even-power) coefficients of g on [-1,1] and of the leading eigenfunction h of the linearized renormalization map, at the claimed precision, plus the claimed alpha and delta. Checker (< 1 hour at ~10,000 digits): evaluate the fixed-point residual g(x) + alpha g(g(-x/alpha))... in the normalisation of the certificate, at 30 random points in [-1,1] by Clenshaw summation at precision D + 50 digits (mpmath or python-flint arb), and the eigen-equation residual (L h)(x) - delta h(x) at 30 random points; require both residuals below 10^-(D+5) relative; confirm that the leading 10,000 decimals match Molteni's published digits and that a second certificate at a different resolution gives the same D digits. For p1, rerun the published-method cross-check at reduced precision (200 digits) in < 10 minutes.

angles: Minimise a smooth surrogate (p-frame potential or log-sum-exp of overlaps with p rising to infinity) by Riemannian L-BFGS on the product of spheres, then polish the active set of near-maximal overlaps with Newton or an SQP that equalises them.

Import from coding theory: build structured starts from difference sets, Weyl-Heisenberg or Clifford orbits, harmonic frames (rows of DFT matrices) and unions of mutually unbiased bases, then perturb; many optimal rows are group orbits.

Import from physics: treat lines as particles with a repulsive potential on CP^{d-1} and anneal (as in Thomson-problem work), using the Fubini-Study metric; or use the frameopt suite by Roman-Roche as a baseline.
Remove-one-vector trick: the README conjectures that deleting one vector from an ETF or SIC gives optimal (d, n-1) packings; test analogous deletions from good n+1 packings for nearby rows.
Target rows where the gap between best coherence and the lower bound is largest relative to neighbours (e.g. d = 6, 7 with n around 30-49), where fewer methods have been run.

targets.name: Game of Sloanes: a packing of n lines in C^d (d = 3..7) with lower coherence than the live leaderboard

partial_wins.statement: A strict improvement (same rules) for a sporadic (d,n) outside the d <= 7, n <= 49 grid where the leaderboard lists an entry, or for a d = 3..7 row that matches a known lower bound to 1e-10 (a new putatively optimal packing, reported with the bound it meets).
A rigorous optimality certificate (e.g. an exact SDP/LP dual or a computer-assisted proof re-checkable in under an hour) for a row not yet marked provably optimal.

pitfalls: Unnormalised vectors: coherence must be computed after normalising each vector; posted files may carry rounding.
Layout mistakes: reading the file as d-major instead of vector-by-vector gives wildly wrong coherences (0.97 instead of 0.62 for 3x13).
Improvements below 1e-8 are numerical noise by the maintainers' own rule and are not wins.
d = 2 rows are Bloch-sphere (Tammes) packings: an improvement there would contradict long-proven or long-studied spherical codes and is almost surely a bug; and d = 2 is outside this target.
Submitting to the leaderboard is a pull request to someone else's repository; never open one without explicit permission from your human.
targets.statement: Packing n unit vectors in C^d so that the largest overlap |<phi_j,phi_k>| (the coherence) is as small as possible is the complex analogue of Sloane's line-packing tables; optimal packings include SICs (n = d^2) and mutually unbiased bases and are used in quantum state tomography. John Jasper, Emily J. King and Dustin G. Mixon run the 'Game of Sloanes' leaderboard (arXiv:1907.07848), now on GitHub (gnikylime/GameofSloanes, last commit 2026-04-28) with 291 rows for d = 2..7 (n up to 49) plus a few sporadic rows. Each row gives the best coherence (8 decimals), a lower bound, the creator and a downloadable packing; 75 rows are marked provably optimal and 7 conjectured optimal. Recent improvements came from several groups (creator codes hlc, jrr = Roman-Roche and Roca-Jerat via frameopt, bmem = Massion and Massart, oai = ChatGPT Pro prompted by Mixon), so the table is live and contested. Example rows on 2026-10-15: (d,n) = (3,13) 0.62214387 vs lower bound 0.59160798; (3,22) 0.70342497; (4,9) 0.40185012 vs 0.39528471; (4,10) 0.41077812. For d = 2 the problem is equivalent to point packing on the Bloch sphere (the Tammes problem), already covered by spherical-code tables.
targets.success_criterion: Success means n unit vectors in C^d, 3 <= d <= 7, for a (d,n) row of the live leaderboard (https://github.com/gnikylime/GameofSloanes README table, re-fetched live immediately before claiming) whose coherence mu = max_{j<k} |<phi_j,phi_k>|, computed in mpmath at 40 digits after normalising each vector, is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than the listed 'Best Coherence' by at least 1e-8 (the table's resolution and the maintainers' stated acceptance threshold), the row is not marked provably optimal, mu is at least the listed lower bound (a value below it means a bug), and the vectors are given to >= 16 significant digits in the repository's file format (real parts of all vectors vector-by-vector, then imaginary parts).
targets.verification_method: Download the claimed .txt (2dn numbers), reshape as vectors[j] = re[j*d:(j+1)*d] + i*im[j*d:(j+1)*d] (this layout reproduces the posted coherences, checked on 3x13_dgm and 4x9_hlc on 2026-10-15), normalise in mpmath, compute all n(n-1)/2 overlaps, take the max. Parse the live README table row for (d,n) and compare. Also recompute the posted file for that row to make sure the comparison uses the same convention. Under a minute for n <= 49.

angles: Rectangular instances with a small side: choose m1 <= 32 measurement directions for one party (highly symmetric, e.g. icosahedral/600-cell-derived) and many for the other, so the local bound is exhaustively checkable while Frank-Wolfe optimises M.

Import from spherical design theory: use spherical t-designs and good spherical codes on S^2 (Womersley, Hardin-Sloane, Cohn's tables) as measurement sets; the shrinking factor eta of the local-model polytope is a covering-radius quantity, so better coverings give better upper bounds on K_G(3).

Import from combinatorial optimisation: the local bound is a MaxCut-type QUBO; exact solvers with SDP bounds (BiqCrunch, BiqBin-style) plus symmetry reduction may certify larger instances than Gurobi-based runs.
Import from crystallography: orbit-based measurement sets under the full icosahedral group reduce both the QUBO and the LP to orbit variables (cf. the 600-cell instance analysed in 2409.03739).
Run BellPolytopes.jl longer with larger m on the upper-bound (local-model) side, which the 2023 paper ran with m = 406.

targets.name: Grothendieck constant of order 3 / two-qubit Werner nonlocality threshold: improve 1.43670 <= K_G(3) <= 1.4546

partial_wins.statement: A certified improvement of a lower bound on K_G(d) for some d in 4..9 over the values tabulated in arXiv:2409.03739 (Table 2), same certification rules.

A certified local bound for one of the 2409.03739 'heuristic' symmetric instances (d in {4,7,8}) that turns their heuristic value into a proven bound, re-checkable in under an hour by an independent exact method.

pitfalls: Heuristic local bounds: a QUBO value found by a heuristic solver is only a lower estimate of L and gives an INVALID K_G lower bound; L must be certified exact.
Floating-point quantum values: Q/L must be recomputed in exact or interval arithmetic; rounding M can change both Q and L.
Order matters: K_G(3) bounds are not K_G (unbounded order, ~1.78) or the complex constant; papers from 2026 on those do not change the order-3 bar.
Werner conventions: some papers use p vs v, or include POVMs (a different threshold); compare like with like.
Margins below 1e-5 are within rounding of published values and are not wins.
targets.statement: For two-qubit Werner states v|psi-><psi-| + (1-v)I/4 under projective measurements, Acin, Gisin and Toner (2006) showed the locality threshold is v_c = 1/K_G(3), where K_G(3) is Grothendieck's constant of order 3. Sebastien Designolle, Gabriele Iommazzo, Mathieu Besancon, Sebastian Knebel, Patrick Gelss and Sebastian Pokutta (arXiv:2302.04721, PRR 2023) used Frank-Wolfe algorithms (Julia package BellPolytopes.jl) to give analytic bounds 0.6875 <= v_c <= 0.6961, i.e. 1.4367 <= K_G(3) <= 1.4546, improving Hirsch, Quintino, Vertesi, Navascues and Brunner (2017, v_c >= 0.6829) and Diviansky, Bene and Vertesi (2017, v_c <= 0.6964). Designolle, Vertesi and Pokutta (arXiv:2409.03739, v3 Feb 2026) raised the lower bound to K_G(3) >= 1.43670 with a 97 x 97 Bell-type matrix whose local bound they certified by solving a binary quadratic program. Real and complex K_G (unbounded order) are being attacked heavily in 2026 (e.g. arXiv:2610.10477), but order 3 has not moved since. Via the projective-measurement simulation of qubit POVMs, 2302.04721 also derives v_POVM >= (2/3) * 0.6875 ~ 0.4583 for general POVMs.
targets.success_criterion: Success means EITHER (a) a real matrix M (m1 x m2) with unit vectors x_i, y_j in R^3 such that Q = sum M_ij <x_i,y_j> divided by the exact local bound L = max over a in {+-1}^m1, b in {+-1}^m2 of sum M_ij a_i b_j gives Q/L STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the best published lower bound on K_G(3) (1.43670 from arXiv:2409.03739 on 2026-10-15; re-fetched live immediately before claiming, including a search for newer papers) by at least 1e-5, with M rational (or rounded to rationals with Q recomputed in exact or interval arithmetic) and L certified exactly; OR (b) an explicit local hidden-variable model for all projective measurements on the Werner state at visibility v STRICTLY GREATER than 0.6875 by at least 1e-5 (equivalently K_G(3) < 1.4546 - margin), given as an inscribed polyhedron with exactly computed shrinking factor and a rational convex-decomposition certificate that the skeptic checks in exact arithmetic.
targets.verification_method: (a) Recompute Q from the posted vectors in mpmath (or exactly if algebraic); compute L exactly: if min(m1,m2) <= 34, enumerate all sign vectors of the smaller side (Gray code, the other side's optimum is the sum of absolute values) in a few CPU-hours; otherwise require a branch-and-bound certificate re-run with an open exact solver (e.g. SCIP exact or a custom bound with symmetry) that agrees, plus a second independent run. (b) Check the polyhedron's shrinking factor eta exactly (rational/algebraic computation of inradius over circumradius of the vertex set), solve the LP feasibility of the local model in exact rationals (or verify a posted rational weight vector), and recompute v = eta^2 * nu * v0 as in 2302.04721 Eq. 4. Compare with the live arXiv values.

angles: Re-run Baxter's CTM variational equations (cond-mat/9811264, eqs. 9-14) in arbitrary precision with truncation n up to 40-80; at z = 1 the corner-matrix spectrum decays fast, so each extra block of kept states should add digits geometrically.

From quantum many-body physics: treat the row-to-row transfer matrix as a matrix-product operator and find its fixed point with VUMPS or a boundary-MPS power method in high precision; this is a genuinely different algorithm from CTM and gives the second method the criterion needs.

From numerical analysis: exact strip free energies f_L for widths L <= 24 (state count is the Fibonacci number F(L+2), about 1.2e5 at L = 24) converge exponentially to the bulk value; apply Richardson/Levin-type sequence acceleration in mpmath and compare with CTM.

From computational number theory: once 60+ digits exist, run PSLQ/LLL against algebraic and simple transcendental bases (the hard-hexagon constant is algebraic, Baxter's square value is not known to be); a null result at stated height is a free side observation, not a win.

For p1, port the Friedland-Peled inequality (cylinder and torus transfer matrices) to exact arithmetic: the certificates are integer vectors whose Collatz-Wielandt ratios bound the spectral radius from both sides.

targets.name: Hard-core lattice gas at unit activity: more correct digits of the hard-square entropy constant (OEIS A085850) or the honeycomb constant than Baxter's corner-transfer-matrix values

partial_wins.statement: A rigorous enclosure of kappa certifying at least 20 correct decimals (beyond the 15 certified by Friedland, Lundow and Markström), from Calkin-Wilf / Friedland-Peled transfer-matrix inequalities evaluated with exact rational or interval arithmetic, shipped with the eigenvalue certificates (Collatz-Wielandt vectors) so a skeptic can recheck the inequalities exactly.

At least 20 decimals, by two independent methods, of the hard-core (z = 1) entropy constant of the 4-8-8 lattice (Steven Finch, Errata and Addenda to Mathematical Constants, arXiv 2001.00578, Section 5.12, quotes only 1.54956010...) or of the 'triangular Kagome' lattice that Finch reports as still open; the lattice definition must match Finch's cited source.

Independent reproduction of Baxter's 43 decimals of kappa to at least 48 decimals that settles whether his last two or three digits are correct, reported either as confirmation or as a documented correction.

pitfalls: Baxter flagged his last two or three decimals as uncertain; matching them proves nothing and differing from them is not automatically an error. Validate against the first 40 decimals only.
Plateau trap: successive CTM truncations can agree for a few steps before drifting; 'stable digits' must survive several further truncation increases and match an independent method.
Double-precision linear algebra caps agreement at about 15-16 digits; any claim beyond that from float64 eigen-solvers is noise.

Normalisation: kappa is the partition function per site, ln(kappa) is the entropy; the honeycomb constant is per site, not per two-site unit cell. Mixing these produces a different number that can look new.
A085850 carries keyword 'more' and also falls under the bank's generic OEIS 'more' target; a claim belongs here only if it meets this entry's two-method rule.
targets.statement: The hard-square entropy constant kappa (partition function per site of the nearest-neighbour-exclusion lattice gas on the square lattice at activity z = 1; equivalently the growth rate per cell of n x n 0/1 matrices with no two adjacent 1s) was computed by Rodney Baxter (arXiv cond-mat/9811264; Annals of Combinatorics 3 (1999) 191-203) with the corner transfer matrix (CTM) method as kappa = 1.5030480824753322643220663294755536893857810, 43 decimals, with the remark that the last two or three digits should be treated with caution. OEIS A085850 (keyword 'more', last edited 2026-05-30, checked 2026-10-15) still holds only Baxter's digits. In the same paper Baxter gives the honeycomb-lattice constant 1.54644070878756141848902270530472278026 (38 decimals); that constant has no OEIS entry (search checked 2026-10-15). Rigorous digits are far fewer: Friedland, Lundow and Markström certified 15 digits of kappa, and Kai Liang (arXiv 2507.04007, 2025) gives tensor-network bounds agreeing to 26 decimals, partly resting on empirical convergence patterns. At z = 1 the model is far from its critical activity (about 3.796), so CTM and boundary-MPS iterations converge exponentially; Baxter's 1998 runs used small truncations (honeycomb continued to n = 20). Arbitrary-precision CTM on a laptop should reach well past 43 digits. A win adds digits to a numerical constant; it is not a proof of those digits unless the partial-win certificate route is used.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a decimal value of the square-lattice constant kappa (or the honeycomb constant) with D correct-looking decimals where D >= (longest published digit string for that constant, re-fetched live immediately before claiming: OEIS A085850 DATA plus any b-file for kappa; Baxter's 38 decimals for honeycomb) + 5, AND (a) two computations by independent methods (for example CTM at two different truncation sizes run to a fixed point, and a separate transfer-matrix or VUMPS/boundary-MPS calculation with Richardson-type extrapolation) agree on all D decimals, (b) both agree with the first 40 published decimals of kappa (36 for honeycomb), (c) the run logs show the claimed digits stable over at least the last three increases of truncation, and (d) an arXiv/Google Scholar/OEIS search finds no published value with D or more decimals. Direction: more digits. Disagreement with Baxter's flagged last two or three digits is allowed but must be stated explicitly.
targets.verification_method: Skeptic (< 1 hour): run the claimant's CTM code at two truncation sizes in arbitrary precision (mpmath or python-flint arb, working precision at least D + 20 digits) and confirm the digit string is stable; run the second-method code (transfer matrix on strips of width up to ~24 with Fibonacci-sized state space, or VUMPS) and compare; check the first 40 decimals against A085850 fetched live; for p1, recheck each eigenvalue inequality exactly with the supplied integer/rational vectors.

angles: Use sparse, symmetry-reduced transfer matrices (translation and reflection momentum sectors; the ordered phase breaks sublattice symmetry, so use the odd sector for the correlation length) at widths up to the mid-30s.

From conformal field theory: the critical point is Ising-class with known correction exponents (Guo and Blote confirmed Ising corrections); fit with the exactly known irrelevant-operator exponents instead of free parameters.
From quantum chemistry and DMRG: a corner-transfer-matrix or boundary-MPS calculation at fixed bond dimension gives a second, width-free estimator via finite-entanglement scaling.
For z_c-, the Lee-Yang edge exponent is exactly known (sigma = -1/6 in 2D); building it into the fit, as for the hard-hexagon case solved exactly, tightens the extrapolation.

targets.name: Hard-square lattice gas: more digits of the critical activity z_c = 3.7962551739... (Guo-Blote 2002) or of the negative-activity singularity -0.1193388818... (Todo 1999)

partial_wins.statement: Exact-to-30-digits transfer-matrix eigenvalue data for the hard-square model at widths strictly beyond the largest width used by Guo and Blote (or Todo), released as files with the generating code; checkable by recomputing any single width, useful whether or not the extrapolation beats the record.
A reproduction of z_c+ = 3.79625517391234(4) to at least 13 significant digits with an independently written code and estimator, documenting the widths and corrections-to-scaling form needed.

pitfalls: Under-estimated error bars are the classic false win: an extrapolation that ignores a correction term gives a tight but wrong value. Require two estimator families and report fits with one fewer correction term.
Activity vs chemical potential vs fugacity conventions; and the 2x2 hard-square model (kings, critical activity near 97.5) is a different model with the same name in some papers.
Double-precision eigenvalues limit the extrapolation to about 12-13 digits of z_c; multiprecision eigen-solvers are mandatory beyond that.
The Guo-Blote paper is not on arXiv; quote its value from the paper or from Lyu's reference list, not from secondary rounding.
targets.statement: The nearest-neighbour-exclusion lattice gas on the square lattice (hard squares) has an Ising-class order-disorder transition at activity z_c+ and a Lee-Yang-class singularity on the negative axis z_c-, neither known in closed form (contrast hard hexagons, solved by Baxter). Best published values: z_c+ = 3.79625517391234(4) by Wenan Guo and Henk Blote (Phys. Rev. E 66 (2002) 046140, transfer-matrix finite-size scaling), and z_c- = -0.11933888188(1) by Synge Todo (Int. J. Mod. Phys. C 10 (1999) 517; arXiv cond-mat/9703176). Xinliang Lyu's tensor-network RG study (arXiv 2603.25492, v2 2026-07-23) still uses both as reference values and itself reaches about 7e-7 relative accuracy. Those transfer-matrix studies used strip widths that were limited by 1997-2002 memory; the state count grows like the golden ratio to the width, so widths around 30-36 are now within laptop reach, and high-precision eigenvalue solvers plus modern extrapolation should add digits.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an estimate of z_c+ with stated uncertainty at most 4e-16 (ten times smaller than Guo-Blote's 4e-15), or of z_c- with stated uncertainty at most 1e-12, such that (a) it agrees with the published value within the combined uncertainties, (b) two independent finite-size estimators (for example phenomenological renormalisation of correlation lengths at widths L, L+2 and the free-energy/conformal-anomaly or Binder-type crossing method, or a corner-transfer-matrix scaling analysis) agree within their uncertainties, (c) the raw strip data (leading eigenvalues to at least 30 digits for each width and activity) are published so a skeptic can redo the extrapolation, and (d) a literature search re-run immediately before claiming finds no published value with smaller uncertainty. Direction: smaller uncertainty, consistent value.
targets.verification_method: Skeptic (< 1 hour): recompute the leading two eigenvalues for two of the claimed widths at two activities in multiprecision and match the released data; rerun the claimant's extrapolation script on the released data; check the estimator families agree; compare with the published values.

angles: Numerical-analysis import: replace dense generalized eigen-solves with inverse iteration in multiprecision using a low-precision factorisation as preconditioner (mixed-precision iterative refinement), so 24,000+ term bases fit in laptop memory.
Basis design from singularity analysis: include Fock-expansion logarithmic terms (r^2 ln r near the triple-coalescence point) systematically; the slowest convergence comes from that singularity.
Triple and multi-exponent Hylleraas bases (Drake's doubled basis idea) with exponents optimised in low precision and frozen before the high-precision run.
Rigorous-numerics import: certify the Rayleigh quotient and add a Temple or Kato lower bound to bracket the eigenvalue, which also certifies the claimed digits.
Compressed-sensing / sparse-basis import: prune basis functions with negligible coefficients after a low-precision solve to cut the high-precision cost.

targets.name: MOONSHOT - Helium atom nonrelativistic ground-state energy: more correct digits than Schwartz's 2006 record

partial_wins.statement: An independent open-source reproduction of at least 40 significant digits of the helium ground-state energy from an explicit trial function whose Rayleigh quotient the checker evaluates (no new digits; a published reproducible certificate, which Schwartz's paper does not provide).

A variational energy for the H- ground state (same nuclear-mass and nonrelativistic conventions) lower than the best value in the 2024 Canadian Journal of Physics triple-basis paper and in any later paper found by a literature search.

pitfalls: Conventions: infinite nuclear mass and no relativistic or QED terms; finite-mass energies (about -2.90330) or 'total energies' including corrections are different numbers.

Schwartz's last digits are extrapolated; beating the extrapolated E* is impossible for a variational bound unless his extrapolation is wrong. The bar is his printed variational eigenvalue, and new digits need convergence evidence.
Floating-point linear algebra at 100+ digits silently loses precision in near-singular overlap matrices; only ball/interval arithmetic results count.
This is a moonshot: Schwartz needed a 24,099-term basis in high-precision arithmetic; budget laptop-days and stop early if a 40-digit reproduction (p1) is not reached quickly.
targets.statement: The nonrelativistic, infinite-nuclear-mass ground-state energy of helium is the benchmark three-body Coulomb eigenvalue. Charles Schwartz (arXiv:math-ph/0605018, 2006) used a Hylleraas-type basis with negative powers and a logarithmic term, up to order 50 (24,099 terms), obtaining E = -2.90372 43770 34119 59831 11592 45194 40444 66969 25309... hartree (about 46 significant digits, the last ones by extrapolation). Later work (Hiroyuki Nakashima and Hiroshi Nakatsuji 2007, about 40 digits; Alexei Frolov's exponential expansions 2018, 27-35 digits; Hylleraas-B-spline work 2019) has not surpassed it, and a 2024 Canadian Journal of Physics paper on H- basis sets still calls Schwartz's the most accurate three-body calculation. A rigorous variational upper bound with more converged digits is a checkable object: the Rayleigh quotient of an explicit trial function. Checked live 2026-10-15: arXiv abstract HTTP 200.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an explicit trial wavefunction (basis definition and coefficients, published as a file) whose Rayleigh quotient E_var, computed by the checker in exact or interval arithmetic, is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than Schwartz's best variational (not extrapolated) eigenvalue as printed in arXiv:math-ph/0605018 re-fetched immediately before claiming, AND whose value agrees with Schwartz's extrapolated E* on every digit Schwartz reports as converged; the number of new digits claimed is the length of the prefix on which E_var and an extrapolation over at least three basis sizes agree beyond Schwartz's 46th significant digit.
targets.verification_method: Checker (minutes to a few hours depending on basis size): read the basis (Hylleraas powers, exponents, log terms) and coefficients; assemble the overlap and Hamiltonian matrices in python-flint arb ball arithmetic at precision >= (claimed digits + 20) using closed-form integrals; compute the Rayleigh quotient c^T H c / c^T S c with a rigorous error ball; confirm it lies strictly below Schwartz's printed variational value; compare digits with Schwartz's printed sequence.

angles: Train a small linear or nonlinear atomic cluster expansion (ACE) or MTP model; these polynomial-basis potentials are CPU-friendly and were near the top in Zuo et al., but no ACE/MTP entry exists on the JARVIS tasks.
Kernel-methods import: a SOAP-GAP or sparse Gaussian-process force model with careful hyperparameter search; small data favours kernels over deep networks.

Fine-tune an open universal potential (MACE-MP, CHGNet) on the train split only, after checking that its pretraining data do not contain the mlearn test configurations (the mlearn structures are custom DFT runs, not Materials Project relaxations, but this must be verified).

Physics priors from metallurgy: add an embedded-atom (EAM) baseline and fit the ML model to the residual (delta-learning); Mo, the hardest element, has large forces from stiff bcc bonds where a physical baseline helps.
Statistics import: ensemble five seeds and average; report bootstrap confidence intervals on the test MAE to show the 5% margin is not noise.

A single model that is within 10% of the best listed force MAE on all six elements simultaneously while being at least 5x faster at inference than the listed best model (timing script included).

Metric mismatch: the leaderboard 'Multimae' for forces is a component-wise MAE in eV/A; per-atom force-vector norms or RMSE give different numbers.
