Floating-point SDP output is not a proof: the rounding to a feasible exact certificate is the hard part.
Turán's conjecture has many non-isomorphic extremal constructions (Brown, Kostochka, Fon-der-Flaass); a new construction at exactly 5/9 is not a win.

targets.name: Frankl-Füredi K4^- problem: a certified upper bound on pi(K4^-) below 0.286504, or a K4^--free 3-graph denser than 2/7
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (Lidický-Volec ran K4^- with 8-vertex flags: 9,895,719 K4^--free 3-graphs on 8 vertices, a 1,400 GB SDP in dat-s form solved in about 1,100 GB RAM with their lpsdp solver; re-checking the published interval-arithmetic certificates is much cheaper, but the paper does not state its cost)
targets.statement: K4^- is the 3-graph with three edges on four vertices. Its Turán density pi(K4^-) is conjectured to be 2/7 = 0.285714, the density of the recursive construction of Frankl and Füredi (1984), the iterated blow-up of the 10-edge (6,3,2)-design; this is the corrected form of Erdős problem #794 (whose statement as written was disproved by Harris). Upper bounds came from flag algebras: Razborov (0.2978), Baber and Talbot (0.2871), Vaughan's Flagmatic 2.0 (0.28689), and most recently Bernard Lidický and Jan Volec (arXiv:2610.33850, v1 24 Oct 2026), who report 0.286504 from an 8-vertex flag computation solved with their LP/cutting-plane solver lpsdp, with certificates checked in floating-point interval arithmetic (MPFI/MPFR; certificates at lidicky.name/pub/lpsdp/). The same paper gives the codegree-squared (l2-norm) version: lower bound 4/43 = 0.093023 (Balogh-Clemen-Lidický, arXiv:2108.10406), previous upper bound 0.09307 (same authors), new upper bound 0.093058. Both versions are conjectured to have the same unique maximizer. Both gaps are open as of 2026-10-30.
targets.success_criterion: Success means EITHER (a) a certified proof that pi(K4^-) <= U with U STRICTLY LESS (direction: min) than the exact value certified by the published Lidický-Volec K4^- certificate (reported as 0.286504; compare against the certificate's exact value, not the rounded figure) and than any smaller bound found in a fresh check of arXiv:2610.33850 (latest version), arXiv:2108.10406 and papers citing them; the proof must be a flag-algebra certificate with exact rational or rigorous interval PSD verification that an independent checker re-runs, or a compiling Lean 4 proof; OR (b) an explicit K4^--free 3-graph construction (finite pattern with optional recursion, with a written freeness proof) whose limiting density is computed exactly and is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than 2/7, which would refute the Frankl-Füredi conjecture.

partial_wins.statement: Codegree-squared version: a certified upper bound on pi_l2(K4^-) strictly below the exact value certified by Lidický-Volec (reported as 0.093058), or an explicit K4^--free construction whose limiting normalised codegree-squared sum is strictly above 4/43, verified to the same standard as the main criterion.

A complete Lean 4 proof (no sorry, no new axioms) of pi(K4^-) <= U for some U strictly below 0.28689 (the Flagmatic 2.0 value), provided no Lean-formalised bound of that strength is already public at claim time.

targets.verification_method: Enumerate all K4^--free 3-graphs on the certificate's vertex count up to isomorphism independently, recompute flag densities and products, check PSD matrices exactly (rational LDL^T) or with interval Cholesky, and confirm the bound on every graph. For constructions, brute-force K4^--freeness of the pattern under every map of 4 vertices to parts, verify the recursion argument, and compute the density symbolically. For l2, recompute the codegree-squared objective as defined in arXiv:2108.10406. Re-fetch arXiv:2610.33850 for later versions.
angles: The l2 gap (0.093023 vs 0.093058, about 3.5e-5) is far narrower than the plain one (0.285714 vs 0.286504, about 7.9e-4), and Balogh-Clemen-Lidický solved the l2 tetrahedron problem exactly, so the l2 version of K4^- may be the nearer target.

Use the published lpsdp solver (github.com/BLL4/lpsdp) and certificates as warm starts. The K4^- run already used 8-vertex flags (Table 3 of arXiv:2610.33850), so a gain probably needs extra valid constraints (for example degree or stationarity conditions), not a rerun of the same 8-vertex SDP.
pitfalls: erdosproblems.com/794 discusses 2/9 vs 2/7; the conjectured density is 2/7 (Frankl-Füredi). Do not compare against 2/9.
A construction exactly at 2/7 (the Frankl-Füredi iterated blow-up of the (6,3,2)-design, conjectured to be the unique extremal configuration) is not a win.
0.286504 and 0.093058 are rounded figures. A bound between the rounded figure and the certificate's exact value is not an improvement, so read the exact value from the certificate files.

targets.name: Turán's K5^(3) conjecture: a certified upper bound on pi(K5^(3)) below 0.757017, or a K5^(3)-free construction above 3/4
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (7-vertex 3-graph flag-algebra programs; certificate checking is laptop-hours)
targets.statement: pi(K5^(3)) is the Turán density of the complete 3-graph on 5 vertices. Turán conjectured 3/4, attained by Turán's and Sidorenko's constructions; Erdős offered $500 for any pi(K_k^(r)) with k > r > 2 (Erdős problem #712). For over a decade (since Flagmatic 2.0, 2013) the best upper bound was Vaughan's flag-algebra value 0.7696 (stated as 0.769533 in Balogh-Clemen-Lidický, arXiv:2108.10406). Lidický and Volec (arXiv:2610.33850, 24 Oct 2026) lowered it to 0.757017 with a new LP cutting-plane flag-algebra method, certified with MPFI interval arithmetic (certificates at lidicky.name/pub/lpsdp/), and say their runs were stopped before reaching optimality. The gap 0.75 to 0.757017 is open as of 2026-10-30.
targets.success_criterion: Success means EITHER (a) a certified proof that pi(K5^(3)) <= U with U STRICTLY LESS (direction: min) than 0.757017 and than any smaller bound in a fresh check of arXiv:2610.33850 (latest version) and papers citing it, delivered as a flag-algebra certificate with exact rational or rigorous interval PSD verification that an independent checker re-runs, or as a compiling Lean 4 proof; OR (b) an explicit K5^(3)-free construction (finite pattern, optional recursion, written freeness proof) with exactly computed limiting density STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than 3/4.

partial_wins.statement: A complete Lean 4 proof (no sorry, no new axioms) of pi(K5^(3)) <= U for some U strictly below 0.769533 (Flagmatic 2.0, quoted as 0.7696 in arXiv:2610.33850 Table 2), provided no Lean-formalised bound of that strength is already public at claim time.

targets.verification_method: Independently enumerate all K5^(3)-free 3-graphs on n vertices up to isomorphism (for n <= 7), recompute flag densities and products, verify PSD matrices exactly or by interval Cholesky, and check the inequality on every graph. For constructions, brute-force K5^(3)-freeness of the pattern and compute the density symbolically. Re-fetch arXiv:2610.33850.
angles: The bound dropped by 0.0126 in one step, which suggests the 7-vertex program is far from exhausted; resume from the published lpsdp certificates.
pitfalls: Several non-isomorphic constructions at density 3/4 are known (Turán's, Sidorenko's and others); matching 3/4 is not a win.

Bounds from 6-vertex flags are not known to beat 0.7696; the realistic route to any win is 7-vertex flags, starting from the published lpsdp certificates (the Lidický-Volec K5 run used about 350 GB RAM).

targets.name: Tight 5-cycle C5^(3) (Mubayi-Rödl conjecture): a certified upper bound on pi(C5^(3)) below 0.46503, or a C5^(3)-free construction above 2*sqrt(3)-3
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (6- and 7-vertex 3-graph flag-algebra programs; certificate checking is laptop-hours)
targets.statement: C5^(3) is the tight 3-uniform cycle on five vertices (edges 123, 234, 345, 451, 512). Mubayi and Rödl (JCTA 2002) gave a recursive construction of density 2*sqrt(3)-3 = 0.464101 and conjectured it is optimal. Kamčev, Letzter and Pokrovskiy proved that 2*sqrt(3)-3 is the Turán density of the tight cycle C_l^(3) for all sufficiently large l not divisible by 3, but C5 itself remains open. Flagmatic 2.0 (Vaughan) gave 0.46829; Lidický and Volec (arXiv:2610.33850, 24 Oct 2026) improved this to 0.46503 by solving the 7-vertex program with CSDP (pi(C5) <= 0.465031, on a machine with about 2 TB RAM; their LP cutting-plane method alone gives 0.46507), certificates at lidicky.name/pub/lpsdp/. In the codegree-squared (l2) setting the same paper has 0.25194 (lower, Balogh-Clemen-Lidický) against 0.252451 (upper). Open as of 2026-10-30.
targets.success_criterion: Success means EITHER (a) a certified proof that pi(C5^(3)) <= U with U STRICTLY LESS (direction: min) than 0.46503 and than any smaller bound in a fresh check of arXiv:2610.33850 (latest version) and papers citing it, delivered as a flag-algebra certificate with exact rational or rigorous interval PSD verification that an independent checker re-runs, or as a compiling Lean 4 proof; OR (b) an explicit C5^(3)-free construction (finite pattern with optional recursion, written freeness proof) with exactly computed limiting density STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than 2*sqrt(3)-3, refuting the Mubayi-Rödl conjecture.

partial_wins.statement: Codegree-squared version: a certified upper bound on pi_l2(C5^(3)) strictly below 0.252451, or a C5^(3)-free construction with limiting normalised codegree-squared sum strictly above 0.25194, to the main criterion's standard.
A complete Lean 4 proof (no sorry, no new axioms) of pi(C5^(3)) <= U for some U strictly below 0.46829 (Flagmatic 2.0), provided no Lean-formalised bound of that strength is public at claim time.

targets.verification_method: Independently enumerate all C5^(3)-free 3-graphs on the certificate's vertex count up to isomorphism, recompute flag densities and products, verify PSD matrices exactly or by interval Cholesky, and check the inequality on every graph. For constructions, check C5^(3)-freeness of the pattern by brute force over all maps of the 5 cycle vertices, verify the recursive argument, and compute the density symbolically. Re-fetch arXiv:2610.33850.
pitfalls: Do not confuse C5^(3) with C5^- (tight 5-cycle minus an edge), whose density 1/4 is already known (see arXiv:2409.14257 for the related tight-cycle-minus-an-edge results).
The 0.46503 value (0.465031 unrounded) comes from the CSDP computation, whose files are in anc_lpsdp_csdp.tar.gz rather than in the lpsdp certificates; read that archive before quoting it.

targets.name: Small 3-graph Turán and codegree-squared densities: beat a bound in the Lidický-Volec 2026 table (K6, K7, K5^-, K5^=, K5^ < , J4, J5, F4,2, F4^-,2)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days for the lower-bound side (pattern and blow-up searches); upper-bound wins need 7-vertex flag programs, which took 145-440 GB RAM per cell with the Lidický-Volec solver (their Table 3), since 6-vertex programs only reproduce the prior bounds
targets.statement: Table 2 of Lidický and Volec, 'Solving Large SDPs from Flag Algebra Problems' (arXiv:2610.33850, 24 Oct 2026), lists for small 3-graphs F the best lower bound, the previous upper bound and a new certified upper bound for both the Turán density pi(F) and the codegree-squared density pi_l2(F) (the l2 setting of Balogh, Clemen and Lidický, arXiv:2108.10406 v3). Examples: K6 0.84 vs 0.849270 (l2 0.7348 vs 0.735792); K7 0.888888 vs 0.897843; K5^- 0.602673 (Liu-Schülke-Wang-Yang-Zhang, arXiv:2410.08921) vs 0.632498; K5^= 0.58656 vs 0.602768; K5^< 0.555555 vs 0.571371; J4 0.5 vs 0.502135; J5 9/14 vs min(0.64475, 0.652485); F4^-,2 86/175 vs 0.493024; F4,2 0.618782 vs 0.619154. Certificates and code: lidicky.name/pub/lpsdp/, github.com/BLL4/lpsdp. The authors stopped runs before optimality. Cells for K4, K4^-, K5 and C5 are separate bank targets and are excluded here, as are cells already exact (Fano plane, l2 of K4 and K5).
targets.success_criterion: Success means, for some cell (F, pi or pi_l2) of arXiv:2610.33850 Table 2 other than K4, K4^-, K5, C5, the Fano plane and the l2 cells of K4 and K5, EITHER (a) a certified upper bound STRICTLY LESS (direction: min) than the smallest upper bound for that cell among Table 2's prior and new columns, the latest arXiv:2108.10406 version and any later paper found at claim time, delivered as a flag-algebra certificate with exact rational or rigorous interval PSD verification (or a compiling Lean 4 proof); OR (b) an explicit F-free construction (finite pattern, optional recursion with written proof) whose exactly computed limiting density (or normalised codegree-squared sum) is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the cell's lower bound. F must be exactly the 3-graph defined in arXiv:2610.33850 or arXiv:2108.10406.

partial_wins.statement: Two cells: wins under the main criterion in two different cells of the eligible table (counted once per cell).

A complete Lean 4 proof (no sorry, no new axioms) of one of the new Table 2 upper bounds for an eligible cell, formalised from the published Lidický-Volec certificate, provided no Lean formalisation of it is public at claim time.

targets.verification_method: For upper bounds: independently enumerate F-free 3-graphs on n vertices up to isomorphism, recompute densities (or the codegree-squared objective) and flag products, verify PSD matrices exactly or by interval Cholesky, and check the inequality on every graph. For constructions: brute-force F-freeness of the pattern under all vertex maps (a blow-up contains F iff some map of V(F) to parts sends every edge of F to an edge of the pattern), check the recursion argument, and compute the limiting density symbolically or by exact optimisation over part weights. Compare against the live arXiv:2610.33850 and arXiv:2108.10406 tables.
angles: Lower-bound side: K5^- (0.6027 vs 0.6325) and K7 (0.8889 vs 0.8978) have the widest gaps; search weighted blow-ups of small patterns and iterated constructions.
Upper-bound side: rerun the lpsdp cutting-plane solver longer from the published checkpoints.
pitfalls: For J5 the 2026 new bound (0.652485) is weaker than the prior 0.64475; beat the smaller one.
Several cells mix definitions (K5^=, K5^ < , J4): take the exact edge sets from the papers before computing.
Numerical SDP values without rigorous rounding do not count.

targets.name: C4-free subgraphs of the hypercube (Erdős #86): settle ex(Q7,C4) in [304,308], beat 682 for Q8, or certify a bound below Baber's 0.60318
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (SAT/ILP on Q7, which has 448 edges, with hypercube symmetry breaking; flag-algebra work on the hypercube needs more)
targets.statement: Let f(n) = ex(Q_n, C4), the most edges in a C4-free subgraph of the n-cube. Erdős asked whether f(n) <= (1/2 + o(1)) n 2^(n-1) ($100, Erdős problem #86, page edited 2025-12-27). Lower bounds: Brass, Harborth and Nienborg (1995), (1/2 + c/sqrt(n)) n 2^(n-1). Upper bounds on limsup f(n)/(n 2^(n-1)): Chung 0.62284, Thomason and Wagner 0.62256, Balogh, Hu, Lidický and Liu (arXiv:1201.0209) 0.6068, and Baber 0.60318, the best published value, quoted by erdosproblems.com/86. Lidický and Volec (arXiv:2610.33850, Section 7, 24 Oct 2026) add that Layman and Lidický claimed, by private communication, a bound below 0.59143, with no public certificate. Exact values (OEIS A245762): 1, 3, 9, 24, 56, 132 for n = 1..6 (a(6) = 132 by Harborth and Nienborg 1994, recomputed by Scheucher and Tabatabai in 2015 with an ILP whose generator script is linked from the OEIS page, without a checkable certificate). Paweł Kwaczyński (OEIS comment, 2026-08-27) gives 304 <= a(7) <= 308 from a(n) <= floor(2n a(n-1)/(n-1)). Minamo Minamoto (arXiv:2603.29127 v5, 28 Aug 2026) gives explicit sets showing ex(Q7,C4) >= 304 and ex(Q8,C4) >= 682 (the OEIS comment still says 680). a(7), a(8) and the asymptotic constant are open as of 2026-10-30.
targets.success_criterion: Success means EITHER (a) the exact value of ex(Q7,C4): an explicit C4-free edge set of Q7 with e edges (e >= 304) plus a proof that no C4-free subgraph has e+1 edges, with the computational part certified (LRAT/DRAT checked by cake_lpr or drat-trim, VeriPB, or an exact ILP infeasibility certificate re-verified in rational arithmetic) and any symmetry reduction written out; OR (b) a certified proof that limsup f(n)/(n 2^(n-1)) <= c with c STRICTLY LESS (direction: min) than 0.59143 (the value Layman and Lidický claimed, as reported in arXiv:2610.33850 Section 7) and than any smaller published or claimed constant found at claim time. The proof must be a flag-algebra certificate with exact rational or rigorous interval PSD verification that an independent checker re-runs, or a compiling Lean 4 proof. Bounds are compared with OEIS A245762, erdosproblems.com/86, arXiv:2603.29127 and arXiv:2610.33850, all re-fetched at claim time.

partial_wins.statement: A new lower bound: an explicit C4-free subgraph of Q7 with at least 305 edges, or of Q8 with at least 683 edges, strictly above the best values in OEIS A245762 and the latest arXiv:2603.29127 at claim time, checked exhaustively for 4-cycles.
A new certified upper bound ex(Q7,C4) <= 307 (or lower, but at least 304), with the same certificate standard as success part (a).

An independently checkable certificate (LRAT/DRAT, VeriPB or exact ILP) that ex(Q6,C4) <= 132. The value is due to Harborth and Nienborg (1994) and was recomputed by Scheucher and Tabatabai (2015) with an uncertified ILP; Minamoto notes it is not independently verified in his paper. Counts unless such a certificate is already public at claim time.

A publicly released certified bound limsup f(n)/(n 2^(n-1)) <= c with c strictly below 0.60318 (Baber, the best published bound), to the certificate standard of success part (b), even if c is not below the unpublished 0.59143, provided no public certificate of such a bound exists at claim time.

targets.verification_method: Parse the edge set, check every edge joins two vertices of Q_n at Hamming distance 1, and check every 4-cycle of Q_n (each is a 2-dimensional subcube: n(n-1)2^(n-3) of them) misses at least one chosen edge. Count edges. For upper bounds, re-run the certificate through its checker and review the encoding and any symmetry-breaking lemma. For an asymptotic bound, recompute the certificate exactly. Re-fetch OEIS A245762, arXiv:2603.29127 and erdosproblems.com/86.
angles: The 308 upper bound comes from a simple averaging recurrence on a(6); a SAT model of Q7 with the hyperoctahedral symmetry broken should push it down.
Minamoto relates optimal sets to odd-square edge sets and frustrated spin models; that structure suggests where to seed local search on Q8.
pitfalls: OEIS comment (680) and arXiv:2603.29127 v5 (682) disagree for Q8; use the larger.
Erdős's question is asymptotic; finite values settle nothing about it on their own.
The unpublished Layman-Lidický claim (below 0.59143) is the bar for the full asymptotic win; a public bound between 0.59143 and 0.60318 is only partial win p4.
Minamoto's g(n) is the maximum of odd-square edge sets, a restricted class; his optimality results for g(7) and g(8) are not upper bounds on ex(Q_n,C4).

targets.name: Zarankiewicz numbers for K_{3,3} and K_{4,4}: the exact values z(17;3,3) and z(14;4,4) (next terms of OEIS A001198 and A006616)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (SAT with row/column degree-partition splitting as in Tan 2022, who ran one processor per instance and reports a practical limit near z = 100; z(17;3,3) lies above that, so cube-and-conquer parallelism will help)
targets.statement: z(m,n;a) is the largest number of ones in an m x n 0-1 matrix with no a x a all-ones submatrix (OEIS lists k_a(n) = z(n,n;a) + 1). Jeremy Tan ('An attack on Zarankiewicz's problem through SAT solving', arXiv:2203.02283 v2, Apr 2022; code and data at github.com/Parcly-Taxel/Kyoto) corrected Guy's 1969 tables and extended them with Kissat. His Tables 3 and 4 give z3(m,n) for m <= 16 and z4(m,n) for m <= 13; bold entries are exact and the rest are Roman's bound. OEIS A001198 and A350304 (Howroyd, Alekseyev, Tan) know z(n;3,3) for n <= 16, ending with z(16;3,3) = 128 (Tan, 2022). OEIS A006616 and A347474 (Howroyd, Alekseyev) know z(n;4,4) for n <= 13 (z(13;4,4) = 117). Later work moved rectangular cells but no square one. Davies, Gill and Horsley (arXiv:2411.18842, Discrete Math. 2026) improved many Roman upper bounds. Bhan, Nobili and Langer (arXiv:2605.01120), Afrasyab (arXiv:2608.08154), Hou (arXiv:2608.08549) and Saurabh (arXiv:2608.26603) settled or improved (3,3) cells with n = 17..23, and so did two unreviewed GitHub repositories (dfield/finite-zarankiewicz-closures; joaoamaro70/zarankiewicz, e.g. z(13,20;3,3) = 125) and an SSRN preprint by Padhi (abstract 6960039). 132 <= z(16,17;3,3) <= 133 is still open. Tan's matrix for z3(16) is the only known maximal one, but completeness is unproven. The case a = 2 is excluded (partial win p2 of turan-cycle-free-afzaly-mckay).
targets.success_criterion: Success means the EXACT value of z(17;3,3) or z(14;4,4), shown by (i) an explicit n x n 0-1 matrix with z ones and no a x a all-ones submatrix, checked exhaustively, and (ii) a proof that z+1 ones force such a submatrix. The computational part of (ii) must be certified (LRAT/DRAT checked by cake_lpr or drat-trim, VeriPB, or an exact ILP certificate), and its case split (row/column degree partitions) must be written out and re-generated by the verifier. The value must not already appear in OEIS A001198, A350304, A006616 or A347474, or in a paper, preprint or public repository found at claim time (check all papers citing arXiv:2203.02283, including arXiv:2411.18842, 2605.01120, 2608.08154, 2608.08549 and 2608.26603, plus github.com/dfield/finite-zarankiewicz-closures, github.com/joaoamaro70/zarankiewicz and SSRN abstract 6960039).

partial_wins.statement: An exact value, to the same certificate standard, for a cell z3(m,n) or z4(m,n) of Tan's Tables 3-4 (arXiv:2203.02283 v2) that the paper does not mark exact (not bold) and that no later source has settled. Check arXiv:2411.18842, 2605.01120, 2608.08154, 2608.08549, 2608.26603, github.com/dfield/finite-zarankiewicz-closures, github.com/joaoamaro70/zarankiewicz, SSRN abstract 6960039 and any later paper or repository citing Tan; for example, z(13,18;3,3) = 116 and z(13,20;3,3) = 125 are already settled.

A certified proof that the matrix shown by Tan is the unique maximal matrix for z(16;3,3) up to row/column permutation and transposition, or an explicit second non-isomorphic 16 x 16 matrix with 128 ones and no 3 x 3 all-ones submatrix (non-isomorphism checked with nauty on the bipartite graphs).

targets.verification_method: Check the matrix size and count ones; enumerate all choices of a rows and test whether their common ones reach a columns (C(17,3) = 680 triples for a = 3, C(14,4) = 1001 quadruples for a = 4). For the upper bound, regenerate the CNF instances from the written case split with an independent encoder, run the supplied proofs through drat-trim or cake_lpr, and check the partitions cover all degree sequences. Re-fetch OEIS A001198, A006616 and search for papers citing arXiv:2203.02283.
angles: Tan says his run stopped near z = 100 for lack of parallel case splitting; cube-and-conquer over the first two rows and columns is the stated next step.
Most maximal matrices Tan found have symmetry; seed lower bounds by extending the z3(16) matrix or circulant motifs.
pitfalls: OEIS A001198 and A006616 list k_a(n) = z + 1, not z; A350304 lists z(n;3,3) directly.

Non-bold entries of Tan's tables were Roman's upper bounds in 2022; Davies-Gill-Horsley, several 2026 arXiv papers and two GitHub repositories (dfield/finite-zarankiewicz-closures, joaoamaro70/zarankiewicz) have since lowered or settled many (3,3) cells, so check them before claiming p1. Some of these rely on computer proofs not yet peer reviewed.
OEIS A006616 cites Ignatov (FCA4AI 2024); read it before claiming in case it adds values.

targets.name: Ankeny-Artin-Chowla after Reinhart's counterexample: a second prime p = 1 mod 4 with p | y, or an independent check below 3.4e14
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (Reinhart's search of [1e14, 3.4e14] took about 1200 hours on 162 cores); a partial-win interval of 1e12 is laptop-days on 10 cores
targets.statement: For a prime p = 1 mod 4 let K = Q(sqrt p), omega = (1 + sqrt p)/2, and let epsilon = x + y*omega > 1 be the fundamental unit. The Ankeny-Artin-Chowla (AAC) conjecture (1952; restated by Kiselev-Slavutskii 1959 and Mordell 1960) says p does not divide y. It was verified to 2e11 by van der Poorten, te Riele and Williams (Math. Comp. 2001, corrigenda 2003), then to 1.5e12 (2023) and 5.325e13 (2024) by Andreas Reinhart. Reinhart (arXiv 2410.21864, v3 of 15 Dec 2025) then refuted it: p = 331914313984493 is prime and p | y. He found it by searching every p = 1 mod 4 in [1e14, 3.4e14], and stresses that [2e11, 3.4e14] was never checked independently, so he does not claim it is the smallest counterexample. Mordell's Pellian analogue for p = 3 mod 4 was also disproved by Reinhart (Acta Arith. 215, 2024). Under the usual heuristic that y mod p is random, counterexamples have density about 1/p, so a second one is rare but expected to exist. Still open: a second AAC prime, and an independent confirmation that 331914313984493 is the smallest.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED (full win) for a prime p = 1 mod 4, p != 331914313984493, that is absent from Reinhart's papers and any later literature at verification time, with this unconditional certificate: (i) a primality proof (ECPP or Pocklington, or PARI isprime as a second check); (ii) a unit eta of O_K, given in compact representation (a product of explicit elements alpha_i^e_i) or as explicit integers (as with Reinhart's u, v with u^2 - p^3 v^2 = -4 and eta = (u + v p sqrt p)/2), with N(eta) = +-1, integrality checked by valuations, and log|eta| != 0; (iii) the omega-coefficient of eta is 0 mod p, computed exactly in O_K/pO_K (handling valuations at the ramified prime), so eta lies in the order Z + pO_K; (iv) eta is not a p-th power in K, witnessed by a degree-1 prime ideal l with N(l) = 1 mod p and eta^((N(l)-1)/p) != 1 mod l, or by 1 < eta < eps^p as in Reinhart's Lemma 2.2 with an explicit bound. Since [O_K^x : (Z+pO_K)^x] divides p and the unit rank is 1, (ii)-(iv) force p | y for the fundamental unit (Reinhart, Lemma 2.2). A computation that only reports p | y without this certificate counts as PROMISING.

partial_wins.statement: An independent check, with a different algorithm or implementation and reproduced by the verifier, of every prime p = 1 mod 4 in a contiguous interval of length >= 1e12 inside [2e11, 3.4e14]. It reports no AAC counterexample, or exactly 331914313984493 if the interval contains it. Logs must allow random spot checks, and every spot-checked prime comes with a unit eta whose omega-coefficient is nonzero mod p.
The full independent double-check of [2e11, 3.4e14] under the same rules as p1, proving that 331914313984493 is the smallest AAC counterexample.

targets.verification_method: Recompute in PARI/GP (or Sage) from the certificate: prove p prime; rebuild eta from its compact representation and check its norm and integrality; reduce it in F_p[t]/(t^2) (p ramifies) to read off the omega-coefficient mod p; check the p-th-power-residue witness. As an independent check, recompute the fundamental unit with bnfinit(x^2-x-(p-1)/4,1) and bnfcertify, and confirm that its y-coordinate is 0 mod p. For p1 and p2, rerun random sub-intervals with independent code.
angles: Reinhart's large-step (baby-step giant-step on the infrastructure) algorithm decides p | y in roughly O(p^(1/4+e)) time without writing out the unit; an independent reimplementation (for example on GPUs) is the natural route to p1.
Fermat-quotient and Bernoulli-number criteria (p | y iff p | B_((p-1)/2), Ankeny-Artin-Chowla, Mordell) give a second, independent test for each p.
pitfalls: The fundamental unit of a field near 3e14 has millions of digits. Work with compact representations or the infrastructure, never with expanded integers.
For p = 1 mod 4, O_K = Z[(1+sqrt p)/2], not Z[sqrt p]. Using the wrong order flips the meaning of y.
An unchecked GRH-conditional unit can be a power of the true fundamental unit. Witness (iv) is what excludes p-th powers.

targets.name: Cubic Ankeny-Artin-Chowla-Mordell conjecture (Hirakawa-Shimizu): a prime p with p | beta for the fundamental unit of Q(p^(1/3)) or Q((2p)^(1/3)), or a certified verification for all p < 1e7 and beyond
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster for a counterexample search beyond 1e7 (one unit computation per pure cubic field); the p1 certificate file (about 1.3 million fields) is laptop-days on 10 cores
targets.statement: Hirakawa and Shimizu (Proc. AMS 150 (2022) 1821-1835, arXiv 1912.04600, Conjecture 1.2): for a prime p != 3 and P in {p, 2p}, write the fundamental unit of Q(P^(1/3)) as epsilon = (alpha + beta*P^(1/3) + gamma*P^(2/3))/3 with alpha, beta, gamma integers. Then beta != 0 mod p. It is a cubic analogue of the AAC and Mordell conjectures, and it is what their construction of counterexamples to the local-global principle for plane curves of degree divisible by p needs. They verified it in Magma for both P = p and P = 2p and all p < 1e5. Reinhart (arXiv 2410.21864 v3, 15 Dec 2025, Section 4) says it is still open, although its real-quadratic ancestors have both been refuted. His Remark 4.1 lists every squarefree d <= 1e7 with d | b in Q(d^(1/3)): 17 values, none a prime p >= 5 and none of the form 2p. That settles P = p for all primes 5 <= p <= 1e7, from a PARI/GP computation that was not independently checked. For P = 2p it only rules out 2p | b, not p | b, so P = 2p is fully verified only for p < 1e5. A naive 1/p heuristic suggests a counterexample exists: roughly 0.25 expected with P = p for 1e7 < p < 1e9 and roughly 0.6 with P = 2p for 1e5 < p < 1e9.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED (full win) for a prime p >= 5 and P in {p, 2p}, not listed in the literature at verification time, with an unconditional certificate: a unit eta of O_L, L = Q(P^(1/3)), in compact representation, such that (i) N(eta) = +-1 and eta is integral (valuation check); (ii) log|eta| != 0; (iii) writing eta = (a + b*theta + c*theta^2)/3 with theta = P^(1/3), b = 0 mod p, computed in O_L/pO_L = O_L/q^3, where q is the prime above p, which ramifies totally (reducing modulo q alone keeps only a mod p and loses b; track the q-valuations of the factors of the compact representation); (iv) eta is not a p-th power in L, witnessed by a prime ideal l with N(l) = 1 mod p and eta^((N(l)-1)/p) != 1 mod l. The units with b = 0 mod p form a subgroup of index dividing p: it is the unit group of the order {b = 0 mod p}, and (O/pO)^x has order (p-1)p^2. The unit rank is 1, so (i)-(iv) prove that the fundamental unit has beta = 0 mod p.

partial_wins.statement: An unconditional certificate file that verifies the conjecture for every prime 5 <= p < 1e7 and both P = p and 2p: for each P, a unit eta_P in compact representation with N = +-1 and b != 0 mod p. Any such unit proves the conjecture for P (Hirakawa-Shimizu, footnote 1). Every unit is rechecked by the verifier's independent code.
The same unconditional certificate file for every prime 5 <= p < 1e8 (both P), if no larger verified range is in the literature at verification time.

targets.verification_method: Independent PARI/GP or Sage code: rebuild L = Q(P^(1/3)) and its maximal order, expand each compact representation modulo pO_L (that is, modulo q^3 for the totally ramified prime q above p; modulo q alone does not determine b) and modulo the witness prime l, check norms exactly from the factor norms, check integrality from valuations, and read off b mod p. Recompute the fundamental unit with bnfinit for a random sample as a cross-check.
angles: Compute units with PARI bnfinit(x^3-P,1) using compact units (nf flag), then reduce the compact representation modulo pO_L = q^3 at the totally ramified prime q, keeping track of q-valuations of the factors. Never expand the unit.
Use Voronoi's algorithm for units of cubic fields of negative discriminant as an independent unit source.
pitfalls: For P = 2p use theta = (2p)^(1/3) and theta^2 = (4p^2)^(1/3). Mixing the normalisations of Hirakawa-Shimizu and Reinhart only matters by units mod p, but be consistent.
Squarefree d with 3 | d (e.g. 6, 57, 1185) appear in Reinhart's list of d | b. They are not counterexamples, since the conjecture concerns P = p or 2p with p prime, p != 3.
p = 2 and p = 3 are excluded or trivial; start at p = 5.

targets.name: Reinhart's open problem: squarefree d = pq or 2pq with h(d) = 2 and d | y (orders with unusual sets of distances)
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (Reinhart's exhaustive search of squarefree d <= 2.3e14 used well over a million core-hours; new examples are expected only above that)
targets.statement: Let d >= 2 be squarefree, K = Q(sqrt d), omega = sqrt d if d = 2,3 mod 4 and (1+sqrt d)/2 if d = 1 mod 4, and epsilon = x + y*omega the fundamental unit. Andreas Reinhart (Acta Arith. 211 (2023) 61-92, arXiv 2305.09267) characterised orders in real quadratic fields with min Delta(O) = 2 ('unusual' sets of distances), and in Acta Arith. 215 (2024) 85-95 (Prop. 2.4, Thm. 2.5) tied them to the condition d | y. In Section 4 of arXiv 2410.21864 (v3, 15 Dec 2025) he poses this open problem: find squarefree d with (a) d = pq, p = 5 mod 8, q = 3 mod 4, h(d) = 2, y odd, d | y; or (b) d = pq, p != q, p = q = 1 mod 4, d = 5 mod 8, h(d) = 2, N(epsilon) = -1, d | y; or (c) d = pq, p = 1 mod 8, q = 3 mod 4, h(d) = 2, y odd, d | y; or (d) d = 2pq, p != q, p = q = 3 mod 8, h(d) = 2, d | y. He writes that apart from d = 5374184665 he does not know whether any of these situations can occur. His searches covered every squarefree d <= 2.3e14 (not independently double-checked), and only 22 squarefree d with d | y are known in all, so any solution is expected above 2.3e14. The AAC counterexample 331914313984493 (prime) is the first known squarefree d = 5 mod 8 with d | y, and one of only two known with N(epsilon) = -1.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED (full win) for a squarefree d with an explicit factorisation into proven primes that satisfies all the conditions of one of (a), (b), (c) or (d) above, exactly as stated in Section 4 of arXiv 2410.21864. h(d) = 2 must be proven unconditionally (PARI bnfinit + bnfcertify, which also certifies the fundamental unit, or an equivalent proven computation in Magma). x and y of the certified fundamental unit (taken > 1) are computed modulo 2d from its compact representation, and the verifier checks d | y, the parity of y where required, and N(epsilon) where required. The result must not already appear in Reinhart's papers or later literature at verification time.

partial_wins.statement: A composite squarefree d = 5 mod 8 with d | y for the certified fundamental unit of Q(sqrt d), certified as in the full criterion. The only known squarefree d = 5 mod 8 with d | y is the prime 331914313984493.

A composite squarefree d other than 5374184665 with d | y and N(epsilon) = -1, certified as in the full criterion. Reinhart says 5374184665 and 331914313984493 are the only two known squarefree d with these properties.

targets.verification_method: PARI/GP: prove p and q prime; bnf = bnfinit(minpoly of omega, 1); bnfcertify(bnf) == 1; read the class number; reduce the compact fundamental unit modulo 2d in O_K to get x and y mod 2d; check the congruences and the sign of the norm. Cross-check y mod d with an independent continued-fraction or infrastructure computation.
angles: Screen candidates fast: d | y is equivalent to the order Z + dO_K having the same regulator as O_K. Test it with infrastructure arithmetic modulo d before certifying the class number.
Restrict the sieve to d whose genus theory forces the 2-rank of the class group to be exactly 1, so h(d) = 2 is likely.
pitfalls: Use O_K = Z[omega] with the omega given above. For d = 2,3 mod 4, y is the coefficient of sqrt d.
A GRH-conditional class number or unit is not enough; certify it.
d = 5374184665 = 5 * 1074836933 is 1 mod 8, so it does not satisfy (b); check each congruence literally.

targets.name: Kummer-Vandiver conjecture: extend the verified range past 2^31 (Hart-Harvey-Ong, 2016)
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster for the full win (Hart-Harvey-Ong used about 8.6 million core-hours below 2^31); near 2^31 one prime takes about 300-500 s on one core and 8-60 GB of RAM, so the p1 window (about 4,700 primes) is laptop-days on a 10-core, 64 GB machine
targets.statement: The Kummer-Vandiver conjecture says p does not divide the class number of Q(zeta_p + zeta_p^-1). William Hart, David Harvey and Wilson Ong (Irregular primes to two billion, Math. Comp. 86 (2017), arXiv 1605.02398) computed every irregular pair (p, r), r even in {2, ..., p-3} with B_r = 0 mod p, for all 105,097,564 odd primes p < 2^31 = 2147483648. They verified the conjecture for each of them and checked that lambda_p = nu_p = i_p, so the p-part of the class group of Q(zeta_(p^n)) is (Z/p^n)^(i_p). They found four primes with irregularity index 8 and one with index 9 (p = 1767218027); the previous maximum known was 7. The computation took about 8.6 million core-hours. This follows Buhler-Harvey (to 163,577,856, 2011), Buhler-Crandall-Ernvall-Metsankyla-Shokrollahi (to 12 million, 2001) and earlier work back to Kummer. As of 2026-10-30, no later extension past 2^31 turned up. Washington's heuristics suggest that the number of counterexamples below x grows like log log x, so a counterexample is possible but rare. The conjecture remains open.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED (full win): a new verified bound B >= 2^32. For every prime 2^31 < p < B: the complete list of even irregular indices r in {2, 4, ..., p-3} with B_r = 0 mod p; for every irregular pair, the Kummer-Vandiver sufficient criterion passed (the V_(p,r) test of Buhler-Harvey 2011, with the exponent correction c -> c/2 noted in HHO Section 7); and lambda_p = nu_p = i_p certified by the four incongruences of HHO Section 7, or, for pairs with 2r = 1 mod p, by the alternative test HHO use (Criteria 2 and 4 of their reference [7]). The whole range must be run by two independent implementations, or by one implementation plus an independent check of a random sample of at least 1% of the primes, and the bound must exceed any extension in the literature at verification time. A prime where the Vandiver sufficient criterion fails is not a counterexample: report it as PROMISING with its data.

partial_wins.statement: The same verification, under the same independence rules, for every prime p in [2^31, 2^31 + 1e5], with the irregular-pair list published.
The same for every prime p in [2^31, 2^31 + 1e6].

targets.verification_method: Reimplement the Bernoulli-mod-p computation independently (for example Harvey's multimodular approach, or a Voronoi-congruence or power-series method) and rerun random primes from the claimed window. Compare irregular-pair counts with the Poisson(1/2) expectation, rerun the V_(p,r) and Iwasawa congruence checks for every claimed irregular pair, and regression-test the code on primes below 2^31 against HHO's published irregular-pair table.
angles: HHO's Rader-algorithm reduction makes the cost per prime O(p log p) word operations; a GPU number-theoretic-transform implementation is the obvious speedup.
Only irregular pairs (about 0.5 per prime) need the costly V_(p,r) check; regular primes are done after the Bernoulli scan.
pitfalls: The published V_(p,r) formula in Buhler-Harvey and earlier papers has an exponent error (c should be c/2), per HHO Section 7.
Primes just above 2^31 need more than 31-bit modular arithmetic; watch for overflow in 64-bit products.

targets.name: Greenberg's conjecture for p = 3: extend the Mercuri-Paoluzi-Schoof verification for real quadratic fields beyond discriminant 100,000
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (MPS needed about two weeks on one i5 workstation for f < 100,000)
targets.statement: Greenberg's conjecture (1976) says the Iwasawa invariants lambda and mu vanish for every totally real field F and prime p: the p-class groups A_n of the layers of the cyclotomic Z_p-extension stay bounded. Pietro Mercuri, Maurizio Paoluzi and Rene Schoof (arXiv 2503.00819, March 2025) proved it for p = 3 and all 30,394 real quadratic fields of discriminant f < 100,000. For each f they computed a cyclic Lambda-module C(f) = Lambda/J built from cyclotomic units, which is finite iff Greenberg's conjecture holds for F, and showed it is finite. C(f) is nonzero for 3,359 fields (2,118 of them with J = (3, T)). Their method finds elements of J (upper bounds) from cyclotomic units modulo auxiliary primes r, and lower bounds with G. and M.-N. Gras' high-precision method, until J + (omega_n) = J + (omega_(n+1)). Where the lower bound is infeasible for n >= 3, their Lemma 2.1 with m = 2 closes the case. The ideals J and their Magma code are on GitHub (mercuri-pietro/Iwasawa-modules). Earlier computations cited by MPS: Fukuda-Komatsu (1986), Kraft-Schoof (1995), Taya (1996), Ichimura-Sumida (1996-97). Beyond f = 100,000 no complete verification for p = 3 has been published; individual fields there are covered only by classical criteria (for example Iwasawa's theorem when 3 does not split in F and 3 does not divide h(F)).
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED (full win): for every real quadratic field of fundamental discriminant 100,000 <= f < 200,000, a proof (in the MPS framework or an equivalent published criterion) that C(f), equivalently the 3-part of the class groups in the cyclotomic Z_3-tower, is finite. That means the ideal J or an equivalent invariant, with stabilisation J + (omega_n) = J + (omega_(n+1)), backed by both the upper-bound and the lower-bound computation, or by Lemma 2.1 of MPS (or by the upper bound alone when it already gives J + (omega_0) = Lambda). Output one file per residue class of f mod 3 in the PARI/GP list format of the MPS GitHub data, plus the code. The verifier reruns an independent implementation on every claimed f with J != Lambda and on a random sample of at least 300 further discriminants, and requires exact agreement. The range must not already be covered by a published or arXiv computation at verification time.

partial_wins.statement: The same certified computation for every fundamental discriminant 100,000 <= f < 110,000.
The same for every fundamental discriminant 100,000 <= f < 150,000.

targets.verification_method: Regression first: the verifier's implementation (PARI/GP or Sage, independent of the MPS Magma code where possible) must reproduce the MPS ideals for 200 random f < 100,000. Then rerun the sample of claimed f >= 100,000, checking the elements of J found modulo the auxiliary primes r, the Gras lower bounds at the stated precision, and the Nakayama stabilisation step.
angles: About 89% of fields have C(f) = 0, which is settled at layer 0 or 1 with cheap modular computations. Spend the high-precision lower-bound budget only on the rest.
Treat the three cases f = 0, 1, 2 mod 3 separately, as MPS do (Sections 2 and 4); the f = 1 mod 3 case uses the modified module B~_n.
pitfalls: Upper bounds alone (elements found in J) prove finiteness only when they already give J + (omega_0) = Lambda, i.e. C(f) = 0; otherwise the Gras lower bound or Lemma 2.1 of MPS is required.
Use fundamental discriminants f, not squarefree d; MPS count 30,394 fields below 100,000.
For f = 1 mod 3 the module is built from the modified group B~_n (MPS Section 4); do not reuse the f != 1 mod 3 recipe there.

targets.name: Class groups of quadratic fields with record 3-rank: an imaginary quadratic field of 3-rank 9 (record 8, Elkies), or a real one of 3-rank 8
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (Mestre-Nagao or Diaz y Diaz style searches; certificate checking takes seconds)
targets.statement: Large 3-ranks of class groups of quadratic fields are very rare: under Cohen-Lenstra the chance that an imaginary quadratic field has 3-rank r decays like 3^(-r^2), about 3^-64 for r = 8. Quer (1987) found three imaginary quadratic fields of 3-rank 6 from Mordell curves of rank 12, and Bagshaw, Jacobson, Rollick and Scheidler (CMS Winter Meeting 2021) still cite that as the record for fields found by the Diaz y Diaz construction. Noam Elkies (ANTS XVI, 2024, 'Rank of an elliptic curve and 3-rank of a quadratic field via the Burgess bounds') proved unconditionally that Q(sqrt(-3D)), with D = 72513834653847828539450325493 = 41 * 1768630113508483622913422573, has class group of 3-rank 8, 'the current record for the class group of a quadratic number field'. The mirror real field Q(sqrt D) has 3-rank 7, which is unconditional as a lower bound and exact under GRH. Both come from the Mordell curve y^2 = x^3 + 16D of rank 16. Elkies also reports the record rank 17 for Mordell curves y^2 = x^3 + k, with k = -908800736629952526116772283648363 (announced 2016, exhibited on MathOverflow in 2023), whose fields again have 3-ranks 8 and 7 under GRH.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED (full win) for a fundamental discriminant Delta < 0, proven fundamental by factorisation, together with nine primitive positive-definite binary quadratic forms f_1..f_9 of discriminant Delta. Each f_i^3 must reduce to the principal form, and every product f_1^e_1 ... f_9^e_9 with e in {0,1,2}^9 \ {0} (19,682 products) must reduce to a non-principal reduced form. This proves 3-rank >= 9 > 8 (direction: max). The verifier composes and reduces the forms with independent code (exact integer arithmetic; PARI qfbcomp/qfbred as a cross-check). The field must not appear with 3-rank >= 9 in the literature at verification time.

partial_wins.statement: A real quadratic field Q(sqrt D), D > 0 fundamental, with 3-rank of the class group >= 8 (record 7). Certificate: (3^8 - 1)/2 = 3280 cubic polynomials whose fields all have discriminant exactly D (by Hasse, these are the unramified cyclic cubic extensions), proven pairwise non-isomorphic by Frobenius cycle types at small primes or nfisisom, and each field's discriminant proven equal to D (nfdisc with complete factorisation).
A Mordell curve y^2 = x^3 + k over Q with 18 or more points whose Neron-Tate height matrix has positive determinant (computed at 100 and at 200 digits, agreeing), beating Elkies' rank 17.

targets.verification_method: Full win: check that Delta is fundamental, check the discriminant of every form, cube each form and reduce, then enumerate all 3^9 - 1 exponent vectors with independent composition code. p1: nfdisc on each cubic, pairwise isomorphism tests, and confirmation that the count 3280 is reached. p2: PARI ellinit, ellisoncurve and ellheightmatrix at two precisions.
angles: Follow Elkies: rank(E_k) is at most 1 plus the 3-ranks of Q(sqrt k) and Q(sqrt(-3k)), so Mordell curves of rank >= 18 force large 3-ranks. Search with Mestre-Nagao sieves over k.
Diaz y Diaz / Quer / Bagshaw-Jacobson-Rollick-Scheidler: build discriminants as norms from cubic fields with many small cubic units, then sieve by 3-rank heuristics.
pitfalls: The forms must be primitive and of the exact discriminant Delta; a non-fundamental Delta describes an order, not the field.
Rank 17 for Mordell curves is a lower bound from explicit points; only explicit independent points count for p2, never analytic rank.

targets.name: Elliptic curves over Q of rank r = 5..11 with smaller conductor than the Elkies-Watkins records
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (searches for curves with many small integral points, then 2-descent and conductor computation)
targets.statement: The smallest conductors of elliptic curves over Q of rank 0..4 are 11, 37, 389, 5077 and 234446 (OEIS A052432; minimality comes from Cremona's complete tables). For higher ranks only upper bounds are known. Noam Elkies and Mark Watkins (ANTS VI, 2004, arXiv math/0403374, Table 2) list the smallest conductors they found: rank 5: 19047851 ([0,0,1,-79,342], previously known); rank 6: 5187563742; rank 7: 382623908456; rank 8: 249649566346838; rank 9: 32107342006814614; rank 10: 10189285026863130793; rank 11: 18031737725935636520843. They credit Tom Womack's earlier compilations (2000). Cremona's 'Best known conductors' table (originally Womack's, updated April 2012, https://johncremona.github.io/conductors.htm) still lists exactly these records on 2026-10-30. OEIS A052432, whose data stops at rank 4, quotes the rank 5, 6, 7 and 11 values in a comment as 'just upper bounds'. The authors were fairly certain about ranks 5-8 but expected that gains remain at ranks 9-11: their rank-11 record has prime conductor, and their searches were not exhaustive. Their Table 4 gives the matching records for smallest minimal |discriminant|, for ranks 5-10.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED (full win) for an elliptic curve E/Q, given by its global minimal model, with r in {5, ..., 11} independent rational points (Neron-Tate height matrix determinant > 0 at 100 and at 200 digits, agreeing), whose conductor N (PARI ellglobalred, with complete factorisation of the discriminant) is STRICTLY BELOW (direction: min) the Elkies-Watkins Table 2 value for that r. N must also be below any smaller value for that r on OEIS A052432, on Cremona's 'Best known conductors' table (https://johncremona.github.io/conductors.htm, originally Womack's), or in later literature, checked at verification time. Rank must be shown by explicit points; analytic rank does not count. The curve may have rank greater than r; it is then compared in every row it qualifies for.

partial_wins.statement: For r in {9, 10, 11}, a curve with r independent points, not isomorphic to any curve in Elkies-Watkins Table 2, whose conductor is below the fifth (largest) Table 2 value for that r: 77211251506212554 for r=9, 39432942782223365758 for r=10, 252948166615918192888894 for r=11.

For r in {7, 8, 9, 10}, a curve with r independent points whose minimal discriminant has |Delta| STRICTLY BELOW the first entry of Elkies-Watkins Table 4 for that r: 1829517077483, 409086620841461, 95276302704064331 and 50881111474471687972.

targets.verification_method: PARI/GP: E = ellinit(a); ellminimalmodel; ellglobalred gives the conductor (factor the discriminant completely); check ellisoncurve for each point; ellheightmatrix at \p100 and \p200 with determinant agreement. Compare against the Elkies-Watkins tables and a fresh check of OEIS A052432, Cremona's best-known-conductors table and the literature.
angles: Elkies-Watkins search lattices of curves with many integral points with |x| <= h^2. Extending to larger h and smaller U-parameters, which they suggest for rank 9, is the most direct route.
Bias the search toward curves whose discriminant has large |Delta|/N, i.e. squarefull factors; the authors note their rank-11 record has prime conductor, so there is room.
pitfalls: OEIS links Cremona's 'Best known conductors' page at an old Warwick URL that no longer resolves; the live copy is https://johncremona.github.io/conductors.htm (still the Elkies-Watkins records for ranks 6-11 on 2026-10-30). Check it, OEIS and the literature before claiming.
Do not compare a non-minimal model's discriminant; use the minimal model and the true conductor, including wild primes 2 and 3.
Ranks 5-8 are believed optimal by the authors; expect wins at r = 9-11.

targets.name: Are the pure quartic fields Q(13^(1/4)), Q(61^(1/4)) and Q(116^(1/4)) norm-Euclidean? (last open cases of Lemmermeyer's classification)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (Cerri-Lezowski Euclidean-minimum algorithm for a mixed-signature quartic field, unit rank 2)
targets.statement: Egami (Tokyo J. Math. 2 (1979)) proved, for m not of the form 2p^2, that only finitely many pure quartic fields Q(m^(1/4)) are norm-Euclidean. Lemmermeyer gave an elementary proof with the Behrbohm-Redei technique and showed that m must lie in {2, 3, 5, 7, 12, 13, 20, 28, 52, 61, 116, 436}. His survey 'The Euclidean algorithm in algebraic number fields' (update of Expo. Math. 13 (1995)) records m = 2, 5, 12, 20 as norm-Euclidean and m = 7, 28, 52, 436 as not, which 'leaves the open cases m = 3, 13, 61 and 116'. Since then, Pierre Lezowski's table of Euclidean minima (Bordeaux; algorithm in Math. Comp. 83 (2014) 1397-1426) gives Q(3^(1/4)) (discriminant -6912) as norm-Euclidean with M = 11/12. On 2026-10-30 the table's search page serves unexecuted PHP, but its SQLite file tables/table_euc.db downloads. The other three fields all have class number 1 in the LMFDB: Q(13^(1/4)) = 4.2.35152.1, Q(61^(1/4)) = 4.2.3631696.1, Q(116^(1/4)) = 4.2.1560896.1. None of them appears in Lezowski's table: its signature-(2,1) quartic part stops at |d| = 42591 and has no entry of discriminant -35152. Nothing deciding them was found on 2026-10-30. OEIS A187774 lists all twelve candidates as 'norm-Euclidean', which conflicts with Lemmermeyer's survey for m = 7, 28, 52 and 436.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED (full win) when norm-Euclideanity of Q(m^(1/4)) is decided for every m in {13, 61, 116}, each by one of two certificates. (i) Norm-Euclidean: a finite cover of a fundamental domain of K tensor R modulo O_K (coordinates in a stated Z-basis of the maximal order) by rational boxes, each paired with gamma in O_K, such that an interval-arithmetic upper bound of |N(x - gamma)| over the box is < 1; or an output of Lezowski's 2014 algorithm (critical points plus a covering) proving M(K) < 1. (ii) Not norm-Euclidean: an explicit xi in K with a finite certificate, in the Cerri-Lezowski framework (critical orbit under units plus a covering of its complement), proving |N(xi - gamma)| >= 1 for all gamma in O_K. For unit rank > 1, M(K) is attained at a point of K and is rational (Lezowski, Theorem 1.6), so one of the two certificates always exists. The verifier rechecks each certificate with independent interval-arithmetic code. Each field must still be undecided in the literature at verification time.

partial_wins.statement: A certificate as in (i) or (ii) for one of the three fields.
Certificates as in (i) or (ii) for two of the three fields, or a certified exact Euclidean minimum M(K), with its critical points, for one of them, independently recomputed.

targets.verification_method: Rebuild the maximal order (PARI nfinit(x^4-m)) and confirm the discriminants -35152, -3631696 and -1560896. Parse the boxes or critical points and verify the covering of the fundamental parallelotope exactly over Q. Bound |N(x - gamma)| on each box with arb/mpmath interval arithmetic, and recheck unit-orbit claims with exact arithmetic.
angles: Implement Cerri's algorithm for unit rank >= 2: unit actions shrink the search to a compact set, and local covering by boxes then terminates.

Look first for small-denominator candidate points xi (denominators dividing small prime ideals) with |N(xi - gamma)| >= 1; Egami's and Lemmermeyer's non-Euclidean proofs for m = 7, 28, 52, 436 work this way.
pitfalls: Z[m^(1/4)] is not always the maximal order; use O_K.
Lemmermeyer's survey predates Lezowski's table: m = 3 is settled there (M = 11/12). m = 13 is NOT settled: its class number is 1, not 2.

Lezowski's HTML table served raw PHP on 2026-10-30; query table_euc.db (table euc, column euclidean < 0 means norm-Euclidean) with sqlite3 instead, by discriminant (disc is stored as text, e.g. '-35152').
Floating-point norm bounds near 1 are not certificates; use interval arithmetic.

targets.name: Norm-Euclidean cyclotomic rings Z[zeta_m]: decide one of the open class-number-one cases (m = 17, 19, 25, 27, 28, 33, 35, 36, 40, 44, 45, 48, 60, 84)
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (box coverings in degree 12 to 24); the degree-9 and degree-10 real subfields in the partial wins are laptop-days
targets.statement: Z[zeta_m] (m != 2 mod 4) has class number 1 exactly for m = 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 19, 20, 21, 24, 25, 27, 28, 32, 33, 35, 36, 40, 44, 45, 48, 60, 84 (Masley-Montgomery). Lemmermeyer's survey records these as norm-Euclidean: m = 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 20, 21, 24. This is the work of Gauss, Kummer, Eisenstein, Ojala, Lenstra (1975-78, including m = 11 and 24) and McKenzie (m = 13). Lenstra showed Q(zeta_32) is not norm-Euclidean. Kummer conjectured, in a letter to Kronecker, that m = 17 and 19 are Euclidean; the survey says this 'has not been verified so far'. Lezowski (Math. Comp. 83 (2014)) computed the exact Euclidean minimum of Q(zeta_n) for every n with phi(n) <= 8, but nothing higher. So m = 17, 19, 25, 27, 28, 33, 35, 36, 40, 44, 45, 48, 60, 84 remain undecided, with degrees 12 (m = 28, 36) up to 24. No later decision was found on 2026-10-30.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED (full win) for one m in {17, 19, 25, 27, 28, 33, 35, 36, 40, 44, 45, 48, 60, 84}, deciding whether Z[zeta_m] is norm-Euclidean. Either (i) a finite cover of the fundamental domain of R^phi(m)/Z[zeta_m] (power-basis coordinates) by rational boxes, each with an assigned gamma in Z[zeta_m] and an interval-arithmetic proof that |N(x - gamma)| < 1 on the whole box (or an equivalent certificate from Lezowski's 2014 algorithm proving M < 1); or (ii) an explicit xi in Q(zeta_m) with a finite certificate (Lenstra-style or Cerri-Lezowski critical-orbit certificate) proving |N(xi - gamma)| >= 1 for every gamma in Z[zeta_m]. The verifier rechecks the certificate with independent code. The case must still be undecided in the literature at verification time.

partial_wins.statement: A certificate as in (i) or (ii), for the ring of integers, deciding norm-Euclideanity of the maximal real subfield Q(zeta_m)^+ for one m in {19, 25, 27} (degrees 9, 10, 9), provided it is not decided in the literature or in Lezowski's table at verification time. Q(zeta_17)^+ (discriminant 17^7 = 410338673) is excluded: Lezowski's table (table_euc.db) lists it as norm-Euclidean, without an exact minimum.
The same for all three m in {19, 25, 27}.

targets.verification_method: Build the power basis; parse the cover and check exactly over Q that the boxes tile the unit cube modulo the lattice. Bound prod |sigma_i(x - gamma)| over each box with arb interval arithmetic. For (ii), verify the critical-orbit argument and every finite check with independent code; reject any argument that relies on floating point near |N| = 1.
angles: Lenstra's norm-Euclidean proofs pick a finite set of gamma that are differences of units ('exceptional sequences') and a Minkowski-type covering. Reuse that for m = 28 and 36.
Adaptive box subdivision guided by the Galois action (the group (Z/m)^x permutes coordinates) cuts the covering size by phi(m).
pitfalls: Being Euclidean is weaker than being norm-Euclidean; only the norm counts here.
The plain box cover grows exponentially with degree; for phi(m) >= 16 a naive cover is hopeless, and unit-based reductions are needed.
Upper bounds of Bayer-Fluckiger-Maciak type that are >= 1 decide nothing.

Lezowski's table (https://www.math.u-bordeaux.fr/~plezowsk/tables/table_euc.db; its HTML page served raw PHP on 2026-10-30) marks a field norm-Euclidean with euclidean < 0 even when the M1 column is empty; check it before claiming a real-subfield partial win.

targets.name: MaxSAT Evaluation benchmarks: beat the best known cost of an instance whose optimum is unknown
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours per instance (anytime MaxSAT solvers, SAT-based local search, LNS); instance archives are large (2-5 GB zips per 2026 track)
targets.statement: The MaxSAT Evaluations (20th edition MSE 2026 at SAT 2026; Zenodo record authors Dieter Vandesande, Christoph Jabs, Jeremias Berg, Johannes Fichte, George Katsirelos, Ruben Martins, Andre Schidler, Dominik Schreiber) keep a benchmark metadata database, meta.db in github.com/maxsat-evaluations/data (updated with the 2026 results in July 2026, repository pushed 2026-10-07), with fields optimal_cost and best_known_cost ('found during a MSE') per standardised WCNF instance, keyed by GBD hash. On 2026-10-30 it lists 798 non-disqualified instances with optimal_cost 'unknown' and a numeric best_known_cost, from families such as logistics-routing (43), decision-trees (89), interpretable-rule-based-classifiers (77), RBAC maintenance, inconsistency-measurement, optimizing-bdds, correlation-clustering, generalized-hypertree-width, Ramsey and Steiner-triple encodings. Five of them (families aes and aes-key-recovery, cipher key-recovery encodings) are outside this target, leaving 793. 247 of those were in the 2026 exact tracks, where no exact solver finished any of them in the time limit, and in the 2026 anytime tracks (300 s and 1707 s) no solver went below the stored best_known_cost. Lower it.
targets.success_criterion: For one instance whose meta.db row (re-fetched from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maxsat-evaluations/data/main/meta.db at claim time) has disqualified 'no', optimal_cost 'unknown', numeric best_known_cost B and a family other than aes or aes-key-recovery (cipher encodings are not eligible): a complete assignment to the standardised WCNF (std_wcnf output as the data README defines, GBD hash equal to the row's hash) that satisfies every hard clause and whose total weight of falsified soft clauses is strictly less than B, recomputed by an independent checker. The instance must not have a published optimum or lower cost elsewhere (MSE proceedings, solver papers). A cost on a preprocessed or re-encoded instance does not count.

partial_wins.statement: A proof of optimality of the current best_known_cost for one such instance (same family exclusion), as a VeriPB proof accepted by the VeriPB checker (or CakePB) for the PB translation of that exact WCNF.

A first feasible solution (all hard clauses satisfied, cost recomputed) for one of the 11 2026 exact-track instances whose row has best_known_cost and optimal_cost both 'unknown' and unsat not 'yes' (overcommitted-scheduling, bnn-verification, traveling-salesman, judgment-aggregation, minimum-weight-dominating-set).

targets.verification_method: Load meta.db (an SQL dump; sqlite3 meta.sqlite < meta.db) and query the row by hash. Obtain the instance from the MSE Zenodo archive (2026: record 21358014) or the year's benchmark archive, run std_wcnf, and confirm the GBD hash. A 30-line script parses the WCNF (new format: 'h' hard lines, weighted soft lines) and the v-line assignment, checks every hard clause and sums weights of falsified soft clauses. Seconds.
angles: Run 2026 anytime entrants (NuWLS-c-2026, SGAT-NuWLS-c, SPB-NIM-c, Loandra, Aperture variants, BouMS) for hours instead of 1707 s, seeded with each other's best solutions.
Instances from structured applications (logistics-routing, decision-trees, BDD optimisation) admit domain heuristics: decode the assignment, improve in the original domain, re-encode and check.
LNS with an exact MaxSAT or CP-SAT solver on a freed neighbourhood around the best-known assignment.
pitfalls: Hashes refer to std_wcnf-standardised files; an older WCNF file of the same name can hash differently and have different variable numbering.
optimal_cost 'unknown' can mean only that no MSE run proved it; check the family's proceedings description and later papers for a published optimum.

Families that encode public library instances (miplib, capacitated-vehicle-routing, steiner-triple-systems, ramsey-numbers) may have an optimum or a better solution already known in the source library (MIPLIB, CVRPLIB, covering-design or Ramsey tables); such a cell is not eligible, and a better MaxSAT cost is a benchmark result, not a new record of the source problem.

targets.name: SMT-LIB nonlinear integer arithmetic (QF_NIA): a checked answer for an unknown-status benchmark no SMT-COMP solver ever decided
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours per benchmark (cvc5, z3, Yices, local search for NIA, bit-blasting with bounds); certificate checks seconds to hours
targets.statement: The SMT-COMP 2026 benchmark metadata (benchmarks-2026.json.gz, SMT-COMP/smt-comp.github.io) gives SMT-LIB status 'unknown' to 5,270 QF_NIA files. Of those run in the 2026 single-query track, 287 never received a sat or unsat answer in any SMT-COMP single-query log 2018-2026, in the 2024-2026 model-validation, parallel and unsat-core logs, or in the 2024 cloud log (no 2025 or 2026 cloud log is published) (checked 2026-10-30): 243 VeryMax ITS and 23 VeryMax CInteger termination-proof constraint problems (Borralleras, Larraz, Oliveras, Rodriguez-Carbonell, Rubio, 2017), 14 mcm multiple-constant-multiplication instances (Lopes, Aksoy, Manquinho, Monteiro), 5 MathProblems (Jia, Liu, Huang, Ma, Zhang 2022: MF_04 and MF_12 magic squares of fifth powers, SF_12 semi-magic of fifth powers, SQ_05 and SQ_10 semi-magic squares of fourth powers) and 2 Ultimate Automizer ps6.c files (Heizmann). SQ_10 is already satisfied by Nicolas Rouanet's 2018 10x10 semi-magic square of 4th powers on Christian Boyer's multimagie.com (checked against all 5,070 assertions), so it is excluded, leaving 286 eligible files. QF_NRA has 26 such files (hycomp, zankl matrix interpretations, Sturm MBO), QF_IDL 31 (synthetic job-shop, ASP graph colouring, knight tour, labyrinth, solitaire), QF_LIA 2 and QF_LRA 3. The files are in the SMT-LIB 2025 release (Zenodo 16740866).
targets.success_criterion: For one of the 286 eligible QF_NIA files (the 287 above minus 20220315-MathProblems/SQ_10.smt2; path under non-incremental/QF_NIA/ and SHA-256 of the unmodified file from QF_NIA.tar.zst of Zenodo record 16740866), still 'unknown' in the current SMT-COMP benchmark metadata, with no sat/unsat result in any SMT-COMP log at claim time, and with no model or proof already public (for the MathProblems files check Christian Boyer's multimagie.com tables): (a) sat, an integer assignment to every declared constant under which every assertion evaluates to true with exact big-integer arithmetic in a script independent of the solver; or (b) unsat, a proof with no trusted or hole steps accepted by an independent checker (a cvc5 CPC proof checked by Ethos, an Alethe proof that Carcara reports valid, not holey), or a self-contained mathematical certificate checked mechanically (for example a modulus m with an exhaustive check that the constraints have no solution mod m, or verified bounds plus a checked bit-blasted DRAT/LRAT proof). A file whose name matches a file decided under another family (all 14 mcm files share names with decided 20170427-VeryMax/SAT14 files) counts only if its SHA-256 differs from that file's.

partial_wins.statement: The same certificate standard for one of the 26 QF_NRA files never decided in SMT-COMP 2018-2026 (rational or real-algebraic model checked exactly, or a checked proof).

The same certificate standard for one of the 36 QF_IDL / QF_LIA / QF_LRA files (31 + 2 + 3) never decided in SMT-COMP 2018-2026 (Farkas/negative-cycle based proofs checked by Carcara count for unsat). A file whose name matches a file decided under another family (six 20220214-jobshop-BohanLi files match decided job_shop files) counts only if its SHA-256 differs from that file's.

The same certificate standard for one of the 23 QF_UFNIA files (mostly Certora verification conditions) that are unknown-status and never decided in SMT-COMP 2018-2026, with the same same-name hash check.

targets.verification_method: Download benchmarks-2026.json.gz, all results-sq-2018..2026, results-mv/parallel/uc-2024..2026 and results-cloud-2024 files from SMT-COMP/smt-comp.github.io/data; recompute that the file is unknown and never decided (match on logic, family and name, and hash-check any same-name file decided under another family). Extract the file from the SMT-LIB 2025 archive and hash it. For sat, evaluate every assertion under the model with Python integers (or exact rationals for QF_NRA). For unsat, run Ethos or Carcara on the proof against the original file and confirm there are no trust or hole steps. Minutes.
angles: VeryMax ITS/CInteger files ask for template ranking functions; most should be sat. Try NIA local search, incremental linearisation and bounded bit-blasting (a model found under bounds is still a model).
For the magic-square files, modular arithmetic (fifth powers mod 11, mod 25 and so on) gives cheap necessary conditions and possible unsat certificates.
mcm instances are adder-graph problems: a constructive adder graph from the MCM literature can be translated into a model.
pitfalls: MF_04, MF_12 and SF_12 are open number-theory questions: Christian Boyer's multimagie.com lists 4x4 and 12x12 magic squares of fifth powers as unknown, and the smallest known semi-magic square of fifth powers is 16x16. A sat model there would be a major result and needs extra scrutiny, and unsat may be very hard.
SQ_10 already has a published model (Rouanet 2018) and is excluded; check SQ_05 (5x5 semi-magic of fourth powers) against multimagie.com before claiming.
A bounded search that finds no model is not an unsat proof.
cvc5 NIA proofs may contain trusted steps; they do not count.
Status fields change between SMT-LIB releases: re-check the latest release and SMT-COMP results before claiming.

targets.name: SMT-LIB quantified UF and UFLIA: a checked refutation or model for an unknown-status benchmark never decided at SMT-COMP
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours per benchmark (cvc5/z3 quantifier instantiation, Vampire SMT-LIB mode); proof checking minutes
targets.statement: SMT-COMP 2026 metadata marks 3,395 UF and 2,379 UFLIA files as status 'unknown'. Of those run in the 2026 single-query track, 501 UF and 378 UFLIA files never received a sat or unsat answer in any SMT-COMP single-query log 2018-2026 nor in the 2025-2026 model-validation, parallel and unsat-core logs (checked 2026-10-30). The largest families are Isabelle Sledgehammer exports (sledgehammer/Fundamental_Theorem_Algebra, QEpres, TypeSafe, FFT, NS_Shared, Hoare, StrongNorm), Barrett/Reynolds/Blanchette cdt-cade2015 codatatype problems (UF part), and Boogie verification conditions (UFLIA). Further never-decided quantified files: UFNIA 383, UFDT 389, ALIA 257, AUFBVDTLIA 281. Contributors are named in each file's :source field; SMT-LIB is co-ordinated by Clark Barrett, Pascal Fontaine and Cesare Tinelli.
targets.success_criterion: For one of the 501 UF or 378 UFLIA files (unmodified from the SMT-LIB 2025 release, Zenodo 16740866, path and SHA-256 recorded), still 'unknown' in the current SMT-COMP metadata and never decided in any SMT-COMP log at claim time: (a) unsat, an Alethe proof of the original file that `carcara check` reports as valid (not holey), run without --ignore-unknown-rules or --allowed-rules, or a cvc5 CPC proof accepted by Ethos with no trusted steps; or (b) sat, for a UF file only, a finite model (a finite universe for every uninterpreted sort and a table for every function and predicate) under which a script independent of the solver evaluates every assertion, quantifiers included, to true by exhaustive enumeration. For a UFLIA file, sat counts only if every uninterpreted function is given as a closed LIA term over its arguments (with finite tables for uninterpreted sorts) and an Alethe or CPC proof, checked as in (a), shows that the negation of the original assertions with these definitions substituted is unsatisfiable. Neither a bare solver answer nor a proof of a preprocessed or premise-selected variant counts. A file whose name matches a file decided under another family (3 UFLIA files on 2026-10-30) counts only if its SHA-256 differs from that file's.

partial_wins.statement: The same certificate standard for one never-decided unknown-status file in UFNIA, UFDT, UFDTLIA, ALIA or AUFLIA. A file whose name matches a file decided under another family (239 of the 383 UFNIA files, 32 UFDT and 16 UFDTLIA files on 2026-10-30) counts only if its SHA-256 differs from that file's.
An unsat proof of the original file reconstructed and checked in Isabelle/HOL or Lean from a solver's output, for one of the 879 UF/UFLIA files, where Carcara does not support a rule used.

targets.verification_method: Recompute eligibility from benchmarks-2026.json.gz and all results-*.json.gz files in SMT-COMP/smt-comp.github.io/data (match on logic, family and name, and hash-check any same-name file decided under another family). Hash the file. Run `carcara check <proof> <original.smt2 > ` and accept only a 'valid' result (not 'holey'; no --ignore-unknown-rules or --allowed-rules), or Ethos on a CPC proof with no trust steps. For a UF sat claim, run an independent evaluator on the finite model; for a UFLIA sat claim, check the substituted formula's proof the same way. Minutes.
angles: Sledgehammer exports carry hundreds of facts; relevance filtering finds a small unsat core whose refutation is then replayed on the full file (extra assertions do not break an unsat proof).
Run Vampire and E on a TPTP translation for the proof search, then produce the checkable Alethe proof with cvc5 restricted to the found instances.
Model finders (cvc5 finite-model-finding, Paradox-style) for the problems that look satisfiable.
pitfalls: Many Sledgehammer goals were proved in Isabelle by other means; that is not a certificate for the SMT file, and the file may differ from the original goal.
Carcara does not yet support every cvc5 rule; check rule coverage before a long run.
Some of these problems also exist in TPTP; a TPTP proof does not count unless replayed on the SMT-LIB file.

targets.name: Confluence Competition: certified YES/NO for a first-order TRS in ARI-COPS that no CoCo tool has answered since 2019
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (CSI, Hakusan, CONFident, ACP-style decomposition, critical-pair analysis); CeTA checks seconds
targets.statement: The Confluence Competition (CoCo 2026, 15th edition, run live at IWC 2026 / FLoC 2026, Lisbon, 24 July 2026; steering committee Naoki Nishida, Teppei Saito, Rene Thiemann, Sarah Winkler, assisted by Nao Hirokawa for ARI-COPS) runs all tools on the ARI-COPS problem database. In the 2026 TRS full run (444 problems; AProVE, CO3, CONFident, CSI, CSI2025, CSI+CeTA, CeTA-Prover+CeTA, FORT-h, FORT-h+FORTify, Hakusan, Hakusan+CeTA) 32 problems got no YES or NO. Cross-checking the 2019-2025 full runs (2019-2023 tables use COPS numbers, 2024-2026 ARI numbers, mapped by each ARI file's @cops tag) leaves 18 that no tool has ever answered: ARI 51, 53, 55, 56, 57 (Aoto-Yoshida-Toyama extensions of combinatory logic S, K, I: a conditional B, Dh z z -> z, Dk z z -> E z, Klop's Ds z z -> E, and surjective pairing D, D0, D1), 108 (relation-algebra rules), 124 (one rule f(f(x,y),z) -> f(f(x,z),f(y,z)), a self-distributivity variation), 239 (Suzuki-Aoto-Toyama), 448 and 449 (Middeldorp: binary arithmetic with associativity, and max with associativity and commutativity), 465 (van Oostrom 2016), 507 (Aoto), 987 (Shintani, secret 2019), 1014 (Ogawa: d x x -> x, f x -> d x (f x), a -> f a), 1133, 1135, 1136 (Zantema braid-like systems) and 1621 (Felicissimo-Jouannaud, secret 2025). Klop showed by hand that CL with Ds z z -> E and CL with surjective pairing are not confluent, so 56 and 57 are known NO yet have no automated or certified proof.
targets.success_criterion: For one of ARI-COPS problems 51, 53, 55, 56, 57, 108, 124, 239, 448, 449, 465, 507, 987, 1014, 1133, 1135, 1136, 1621 (file from https://ari-cops.uibk.ac.at/ARI/, hashed), still without a YES or NO in the latest CoCo full run of the TRS category at claim time: a confluence (YES) or non-confluence (NO) proof in CPF format accepted by the current CeTA release. For NO, an explicit peak t ->* s1, t ->* s2 with every rewrite step listed and a CeTA-checked argument that s1 and s2 have no common reduct also counts. A tool's bare YES/NO, or a hand proof, does not win.

partial_wins.statement: An uncertified YES/NO for one of the 18 problems from a tool whose proof is written out step by step and independently re-checked by a second tool or a short script (for NO: the peak and a non-joinability argument by tree automata or by distinct normal forms of a terminating sub-system), labelled uncertified.

A CeTA-certified YES/NO for one of the 13 other TRS problems unanswered in the CoCo 2026 full run that have never had a certified answer: ARI 27, 88, 158, 166, 167, 169, 223, 394, 395, 397, 418, 444 (answered without certification, mostly by ACP, in 2019-2025) and 1134 (answered NO without certification by ACP in 2022 only). ARI 246 already has an ACP+CeTA certified NO and does not count.

targets.verification_method: Fetch https://ari-cops.uibk.ac.at/CoCo/2026/full-run/TRS/ and the older full-run pages (/CoCo/ < year > /full-run/TRS/). For 2024-2026, look up the ARI number; for 2019-2023, look up the COPS number given by the @cops line of the ARI file. Confirm that no row has a YES or NO cell. Run CeTA (cl-informatik.uibk.ac.at/software/ceta) on the ARI problem and the CPF proof; accept only CERTIFIED. Seconds.
angles: For 56 and 57, formalise Klop's counterexample term for CL with Ds / surjective pairing as an explicit peak and look for a certifiable non-joinability argument (for example an ordering or interpretation showing the two reducts lie in disjoint closed sets).
Non-left-linear systems (51, 53, 55, 448, 449, 987, 1014, 1621) defeat critical-pair methods; try decreasing diagrams with relative termination, or layer-preserving decomposition.
For 1133, 1135 and 1136 (braid-like rules, some with p -> a p), the word problem view may give a direct confluence modulo argument or a counterexample peak.
pitfalls: Problem numbers are ARI ids, which differ from the old COPS numbers (problem 56 is COPS 57, 1134 is COPS 1282); the 2019-2023 full-run tables are indexed by COPS number, so compare via the @cops tag.
The other 14 problems unanswered in 2026 were answered by earlier tools (mostly ACP); they count only under p2, with a certificate, and 246 is already certified.
A hand proof in the literature is not a certified answer.

targets.name: Termination Competition: a CeTA-certified termination or nontermination proof for a TPDB rewriting benchmark never solved at termCOMP 2023-2026
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (matrix/arctic interpretations by SAT search, dependency pairs, loop and nonloop search); CeTA checks seconds to minutes
targets.statement: The Termination Competition (termCOMP 2026, results at termcomp.github.io/Y2026) runs AProVE, matchbox, MnM, MU-TERM, Mint, NaTT, NaTT++ and NTI on the Termination Problem Database (TPDB 11.6); AProVE and matchbox also ran certified (CeTA) configurations. In the 2026 SRS Standard category, 61 of 1,921 string rewriting systems got no YES or NO from the virtual best solver, and in TRS Standard 86 of 1,528; none of these 147 got a YES or NO in the 2023, 2024 or 2025 tables either (the 29 CirponsMitchellSmith_25 files first appear in 2025). The SRS set includes the 29 CirponsMitchellSmith_25 files contributed by Reinis Cirpons, James D. Mitchell and Finn L. Smith (Adian rewriting systems of about 30 rules each, encoding one-relation monoid presentations such as <a,b | abaabaabaa = baaaba > ), 7 Waldmann_07_size12, 6 Waldmann_23, 3 Waldmann_19, 3 Gebhardt_06, Trafo_06/un16, Zantema_04/z079 and the one-rule system Wenzel_16 ababbbabbab -> abbabbbababbba (termination of one-rule string rewriting is a long-standing open area); the TRS set includes Transformed_CSR_04 (26), Applicative_05 (7), EEG_IJCAR_12 nonloop examples (7), Secret_05/06_TRS tpa*, Hydras (hydra_buchholz, lepper_0/1), Kaliszyk_19, Paulson_20/ackermann_iterative and Zantema_05/15.
