The set6 (25,120) and set8 (7,077) instance pages returned HTTP 500 on 2026-10-30, but their solution files (e.g. set6_128.sol, set8_74.sol) are listed in OptHub's public storage container. Earlier records came from Bykov and Petrovic and from Battistutta, Schaerf and Urli's single-stage simulated annealing. As far as the vetters found, no ITC-2007 exam instance has a published lower bound matching its best known value. Find a feasible solution with a strictly lower penalty than OptHub's best for one of set1-set12.
targets.success_criterion: A solution in the ITC-2007 exam .sol format (one line 'period, room' per exam, in exam order) for one of set1-set12, that an independent checker written from the ITC-2007 examination track specification reports as hard-feasible with total soft penalty (using the instance's own institutional weightings) strictly below the 'Best solution' for that instance on https://opthub.uniud.it/problems/timetabling/edutt/ett/itc-2007-ett, re-fetched live immediately before claiming. The checker must first reproduce the OptHub objective of that instance's posted best file (e.g. 3,085 for set1_443.sol, 5,095 for set12.sol). For set6 and set8, whose instance pages returned HTTP 500 on 2026-10-30, the checker must instead reproduce the problem-page best (25,120 and 7,077) as the minimum over the files listed at https://opthubstorage.blob.core.windows.net/opthub-data?restype=container&comp=list&prefix=timetabling/edutt/ett/itc-2007-ett/solutions/ < set > / ; an instance whose best value cannot be reproduced that way does not count. Nothing is uploaded by the agent.

partial_wins.statement: A strictly better solution for set12 (5,095, unchanged since Bykov) or set11 (22,186), verified by the checker.
A strictly better solution for any other set1-set10 instance, verified by the checker.
A strictly better solution for one of the eight Yeditepe instances on the same OptHub page (yue20011-6-450 ... yue20032-6-550), verified by the checker.

targets.verification_method: Instances: https://opthubstorage.blob.core.windows.net/opthub-data/timetabling/edutt/ett/itc-2007-ett/instances/exam/ < set > .exam; best solutions: linked from each instance page (e.g. .../solutions/set12/set12.sol). The checker parses exams with student lists, periods, rooms, period and room hard constraints and institutional weightings, verifies hard constraints, computes the seven soft components, reproduces the posted best value, then evaluates the claim. Seconds.
angles: Start from the posted best files and apply long simulated annealing or late-acceptance hill climbing with Kempe-chain moves. set12 still has Bykov's 2021 file and is the obvious first test.
Period-assignment as graph colouring plus room assignment as a matching; re-optimise one period block at a time with CP-SAT.
pitfalls: Papers sometimes report lower values without posting files. Only the OptHub value can be checked, but a claim below OptHub that is above a published (unverified) value should be reported as such.
The Yeditepe instances (Parkes and Ozcan's conversion) are scored separately; compare them only against their own OptHub rows.
Institutional weightings differ per instance and are read from the file header; hard-coding them breaks the checker.

OptHub's instance pages sometimes return a server error (set6 and set8 on 2026-10-30); the best value is still on the problem page, and the solution files can be listed from the storage container (https://opthubstorage.blob.core.windows.net/opthub-data?restype=container&comp=list&prefix=timetabling/edutt/ett/itc-2007-ett/solutions/set6/), which on 2026-10-30 held exam6.sol, set6.sol, set6_20.sol, set6_128.sol for set6 and exam8.sol, set8.sol, sol8-7312.sol, sol-8-7280.sol, set8_74.sol for set8.

targets.name: Flexible job shop with worker flexibility (FJSSP-W benchmark, 402 instances): lower a best known makespan
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: FJSSP-W extends the flexible job shop: each operation needs one eligible machine and one eligible worker at the same time, its duration depends on the (machine, worker) pair, and machines and workers each process one operation at a time; minimise makespan. The benchmarking environment of the Josef Ressel Centre (jrc-rodec/FJSSP-W-Benchmarking; Hutter, Steinberger and Hellwig, arXiv 2501.16159, revised May 2026) publishes 402 FJSSP-W instances derived from the classic FJSP sets (Behnke-Geiger, Brandimarte, Chambers-Barnes, Dauzere-Peres-Paulli, Fattahi, Hurink, Kacem) and a best_known.csv of UB and LB per instance, last committed 2026-04-27. The README states the values come from 20-minute runs of state-of-the-art solvers and the genetic algorithm of Hutter, Hellwig and Steinberger (CEC 2024). On 2026-10-30, 371 of the 402 instances have UB > LB, with a median gap of about 37% of the UB. Find a feasible FJSSP-W schedule with makespan strictly below the listed UB for any instance.
targets.success_criterion: For one of the 402 instances in instances/Example_Instances_FJSSP-WF, an assignment of each operation to an eligible (machine, worker) pair with start times such that an independent checker written from the repository's instance format confirms job precedence, machine and worker no-overlap and the pair-specific durations, and computes a makespan strictly below that instance's UB in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jrc-rodec/FJSSP-W-Benchmarking/main/instances/InstanceData/FJSSP-W/best_known.csv, re-fetched live immediately before claiming, with the instance-to-row mapping (e.g. Behnke10.fjs <-> behnkegeiger10) confirmed from the repository's data.csv. Nothing is submitted by the agent.

partial_wins.statement: A strictly better makespan on any Brandimarte- or Behnke-derived FJSSP-W instance with UB > LB, verified by the checker.
Strict improvements on at least 10 distinct FJSSP-W instances, each verified by the checker.
A strictly better makespan on any Hurink-, Dauzere-Peres-Paulli- or Chambers-Barnes-derived FJSSP-W instance with UB > LB, verified by the checker.

targets.verification_method: Instance file https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jrc-rodec/FJSSP-W-Benchmarking/main/instances/Example_Instances_FJSSP-WF/ < name > .fjs: first line 'jobs machines workers'; per job the number of operations, then per operation the number of machine choices and, for each machine, the number of worker choices and (worker, duration) pairs (1-based). A ~80-line Python checker validates and recomputes the makespan; test it on a hand-built schedule for a small Kacem-derived instance. Compare with best_known.csv (semicolon-separated Instance;UB;LB). Seconds.
angles: CP-SAT with optional intervals per (operation, machine, worker) triple, no-overlap per machine and per worker, run longer than 20 minutes with 10 workers; the reference values are short-run, so long runs should already improve many.
Decompose: fix machine choice from the FJSP best schedule of the parent instance, then assign workers by a min-cost matching per time slice and repair.
pitfalls: The FJSSP-W instances are randomly generated from FJSP instances; regenerating them with the repository's translator gives different instances that are not comparable to best_known.csv.
Names differ between files (Behnke10.fjs) and the CSV (behnkegeiger10); a claim on the wrong row is void.
The CSV header was 'Instance;LB;UB' with the UB in the first column until 2026-04-27, when it was corrected to 'Instance;UB;LB'. Read columns by header and check UB >= LB on every row.

Some UB and LB values carry floating-point noise (e.g. fattahi12 UB 414.99999995839994 means 415, hurinkrdata1 LB 42.99999999999994 means 43); durations are integers, so round each value to the nearest integer when within 1e-3 before comparing, and a claim must be at least 1 below the rounded UB.
Some listed LBs are trivial (8 open rows have LB 0), so the gap overstates how much room there is; only UB improvements count.
This table is newer and less studied than FJSPLib; UB improvements are expected to be easier, so tractability is high but each single win is modest.

targets.name: EarthquakeNPP: beat the ETAS benchmark's per-event test log-likelihood on a real California catalog
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (catalogs of 10^4 to 10^5 events ship pre-processed in the repo; ETAS inversion with the etas package and small NPPs both train on CPU)
targets.statement: EarthquakeNPP (Samuel Stockman, Daniel Lawson, Maximilian Werner, Univ. Bristol; TMLR 2026, arXiv 2410.08226v3) standardises earthquake forecasting as spatio-temporal point-process modelling on 7 real California catalogs with fixed chronological burn-in/train/val/test periods: ComCat_25 (M2.5+), SCEDC_20/25/30, QTM SanJac_10 and SaltonSea_10 (Ross et al. 2019 template-matching catalog) and WHITE_06 (White et al. 2019). Its ETAS baseline (Leila Mizrahi's etas package, fitted on train+val) gives these mean per-event test log-likelihoods (temporal + spatial = total = -nll, nats/event; Experiments/ETAS/output_data_*/ll_scores.json): ComCat_25 1.4343 + -8.6898 = -7.2554; SCEDC_20 2.5410 + -7.5342 = -4.9932; SCEDC_25 2.1394 + -7.5380 = -5.3986; SCEDC_30 1.8403 + -7.6206 = -5.7803; SanJac_10 1.1325 + -5.3981 = -4.2656; SaltonSea_10 2.3320 + -2.3151 = +0.0170; WHITE_06 2.0211 + -4.2611 = -2.2400. The paper finds that none of the five NPPs it tested beats ETAS. Of the three with a likelihood (NSTPP, DeepSTPP, AutoSTPP; SMASH and DSTPP are generative and were scored by CSEP consistency tests, which also favour ETAS), the best mean total per dataset in Experiments/out_metrics.csv is AutoSTPP's, 1.06 to 1.41 nats/event below ETAS, mostly in the spatial term (e.g. WHITE_06 -3.391, SaltonSea_10 -1.286). One DeepSTPP seed edges ETAS's temporal term on SaltonSea_10 (2.340 vs 2.332), so temporal-only gains are not wins. Open task: any model, neural or a better classical one, with a higher total test log-likelihood than ETAS on a real dataset.
targets.success_criterion: Saved, runnable code (fixed seeds, weights or fitted parameters) that, for one of the 7 real datasets (not the synthetic ETAS_25 or ETAS_incomplete_25, where ETAS is the generating model), is fitted only on events before the dataset's test start (burn-in, train and validation periods as defined in the repo's dataset notebooks) and evaluated on the official test period with the paper's metric: mean log-likelihood per test event of the temporal plus spatial terms, each event conditioned on the full history including auxiliary events, with the temporal integral term included. The total must be strictly greater (direction: max) than the ETAS total for that dataset in Experiments/ETAS/output_data_ < dataset > /ll_scores.json at https://github.com/ss15859/EarthquakeNPP re-fetched live immediately before claiming, by at least 0.02 nats/event, for the mean over 3 seeds with every seed above ETAS; and greater than any total test log-likelihood for the same dataset and split reported in a paper from the last 24 months (search 'EarthquakeNPP'). The spatial density must integrate to 1 over the dataset's region (checked numerically to within 1e-3).

partial_wins.statement: Re-run the repo's ETAS (invert_etas.py, predict_etas.py) and reproduce ll_scores.json totals to within 0.005 on 3 datasets, then beat the best NPP total in out_metrics.csv (AutoSTPP 3-seed mean) by at least 0.3 nats/event on those 3 datasets.
A higher spatial test log-likelihood than ETAS (by at least 0.02 nats/event, 3-seed mean) on any real dataset, with a temporal term no more than 0.05 below ETAS's.

A model that beats ETAS's total test log-likelihood on any real dataset by at least 0.02 nats/event for the 3-seed mean, with every seed above ETAS, meeting every rule of the success criterion except the 24-month literature condition.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic clones the repo, runs the claimed code from the repo's pre-processed CSVs with the documented splits, recomputes per-event temporal and spatial log-likelihoods with an independent script (numerical integration of the intensity over the test window and of the spatial density over the region polygon), reruns the ETAS scripts for the comparator, and checks that no test-period event enters fitting (code reading plus refitting with test events deleted gives identical parameters). About 1-3 hours on CPU.
angles: Conventional: better ETAS variants: anisotropic or finite-fault spatial kernels for large events, spatially varying background from smoothed seismicity, magnitude-dependent productivity fitted per region.
Conventional: hybrid ETAS + neural background (ETAS triggering kept, NPP models only the non-stationary background, where the paper finds NPPs help).
Cross-domain import (epidemiology): Hawkes models with covariate-driven reproduction numbers, as in COVID-19 nowcasting.
Cross-domain import (crime forecasting): self-exciting point processes with learned anisotropic kernels (Mohler et al.) carried over to fault-aligned aftershock zones.
pitfalls: Temporal-only gains do not count: DeepSTPP already edges ETAS's temporal term on SaltonSea_10 in one seed while losing more than 1.8 nats/event spatially.
The synthetic ETAS datasets are generated by ETAS; beating it there is not possible in expectation and is excluded. Japan_Deprecated is not one of the 7 real datasets.
Leakage: fitting the background rate or kernels on the full catalog (including the test period) inflates the score; refit with test events deleted.
Spatial densities that do not integrate to 1 over the region (truncated flows, unnormalised kernels) produce spuriously high spatial log-likelihoods.
ETAS was fitted on train+val in the repo; Appendix C shows train-only fitting changes little, so compare against the published file, not a weaker re-fit.

No 2024-2026 literature search could be run when this entry was drafted or audited (search budget exhausted on 2026-10-30); before claiming, look for papers citing arXiv 2410.08226 that report EarthquakeNPP test log-likelihoods.

targets.name: NASA CCMC CME Scoreboard: CME arrival-time forecasts for 2023-2024 with a lower mean absolute error than every scoreboard method
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (scoreboard JSON via REST in seconds; DONKI CME analyses, OMNI solar wind and LASCO/STEREO coronagraph summaries are small; drag-based or ML models run on CPU)
targets.statement: The NASA CCMC Earth CME Scoreboard (M. Leila Mays and the CCMC team; validation by Riley et al. 2018 and Kay et al. 2024, Space Weather) archives real-time CME shock-arrival predictions from about 30 methods (WSA-ENLIL+Cone run by NASA M2M, NOAA/SWPC, Met Office, BoM and KSWC, Cone+HAF, EAM, SARM, CMEFM, ELEvo, SIDC and others) together with the observed arrival, served by a public REST API. For CMEs with cmeID dated 2023-01-01..2024-12-31 the API returns 164 closed-out CMEs with an observed arrival. 153 of them (set S) have a pre-arrival WSA-ENLIL+Cone (NASA M2M) prediction (median lead 57.8 h). Taking each method's earliest pre-arrival prediction per CME, the mean absolute arrival-time errors on S (computed 2026-10-30) are: NOAA/SWPC ENLIL 9.93 h (44 CMEs), Ensemble ENLIL (M2M) 10.18 h (51), Cone+HAF 10.20 h (42), Met Office ENLIL 10.45 h (87), M2M ENLIL 10.74 h (153), BoM 11.57 h (39), CMEFM 11.59 h (70), EAM 11.93 h (57), SARM 12.07 h (70), SIDC 15.33 h (72). In 2025 the scoreboard's 'Median of all Methods' scored 9.63 h on 50 CMEs. Errors of about 10 h have hardly moved in a decade (Riley et al. 2018 reported a similar figure). Open task: an issue-time-honest method that beats every one of these on its own CMEs.
targets.success_criterion: A saved file with one predicted shock-arrival time for every CME in S, plus code that regenerates it using only data timestamped before T_c, the submission time of that CME's earliest WSA-ENLIL + Cone (NASA M2M) prediction (DONKI CME analyses, coronagraph images or catalogs, OMNI/real-time solar wind, magnetograms), with any training or tuning on CMEs before 2023-01-01 only, such that the skeptic, recomputing from https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/CMESB-Earth/WS/get/predictions (queried per year, 2023 and 2024, re-fetched live immediately before claiming), finds (a) the method's MAE over S strictly below (direction: min) the M2M ENLIL MAE on S; (b) for every scoreboard method with at least 39 CMEs in S, the method's MAE on that method's CMEs strictly below that method's MAE on the same CMEs, using each method's earliest pre-arrival prediction; and (c) a 95% paired bootstrap (resampling CMEs, 10,000 draws) interval of the MAE difference against M2M ENLIL on S whose lower bound is above 0. The MAE must also be lower than any MAE reported for the same 2023-2024 scoreboard CMEs in a paper from the last 24 months.

partial_wins.statement: MAE over S strictly below the M2M ENLIL value (10.74 h as of 2026-10-30) under the same data-cutoff and training rules, without the bootstrap condition.
Beat the NOAA/SWPC ENLIL MAE (9.93 h) on its 44 CMEs in S under the same rules.

For the 2025 CMEs, an MAE strictly below the scoreboard's 'Median of all Methods' (9.63 h on its 50 CMEs), with T_c set to the median-of-methods entry's submission time and training on CMEs before 2025-01-01.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the 2023 and 2024 predictions JSON, recomputes per-method MAEs with a 30-line script (earliest pre-arrival prediction per method per CME), regenerates the claimed predictions from code through a harness that refuses any input timestamped at or after T_c, and runs the paired bootstrap. About 1 hour.
angles: Conventional: drag-based model (DBM) ensembles driven by DONKI speed/width, with ambient wind speed from WSA or 27-day recurrence of OMNI speed.
Conventional: gradient boosting on CME speed, width, direction, source location and pre-event solar-wind state, trained on 2013-2022 scoreboard CMEs (CAT-PUMA style).
Cross-domain import (forecast combination): a trimmed-mean or stacked combination of physics models whose weights are fitted on pre-2023 events only.
Cross-domain import (travel-time estimation in logistics): quantile regression of transit time with heteroscedastic noise, then predicting the median.
pitfalls: The scoreboard scores only CMEs that arrived (the API skips no-arrival CMEs by default); the challenger must predict all of S and cannot skip hard events.
Using DONKI analyses revised after T_c, or science-quality coronagraph products, leaks hindsight; keep the analysis version available before T_c.
Methods cover different CME subsets; compare on each method's own CMEs, not pooled averages.
Arrival times are shock arrivals at L1 as recorded by the scoreboard; do not substitute ICME-catalog leading-edge times.
Small subsets (39-51 CMEs) make sub-hour gains statistically weak; the bootstrap condition is against M2M on all of S.

targets.name: NOAA SWPC 3-day forecast 2025: beat SWPC's Heidke skill for G1+ (Kp >= 5-) 3-hour slots at 1-3 day lead
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (363 archived forecast text files, the GFZ Kp file and OMNI/DONKI inputs are a few MB; models train on CPU)
targets.statement: NOAA SWPC issues a 3-day forecast twice daily with predicted Kp for every 3-hour slot over 3 UT days; NCEI archives the texts (daily_reports/3day_forecast; 363 of the 365 00:30 UTC issues of 2025 are present, 2025-07-17 and 2025-12-17 missing). Scoring those 363 issues against GFZ Potsdam's definitive Kp (Matzka et al.; all 2025 values definitive), on slots whose UT date falls in 2025, with the G1 threshold SWPC itself uses in the forecast (Kp >= 4.67, i.e. 5-, labelled '(G1)'), SWPC's day-2 forecasts (lead 23.5-47.5 h) give Heidke skill score HSS = 0.1462 (41 hits, 128 false alarms, 192 misses, 2,896 slots) and day-3 forecasts 0.1313 (30, 79, 202; 2,888 slots). Trivial baselines are far lower: 27-day recurrence 0.073, recurrence with +/-3 h tolerance 0.098, last-slot persistence 0.077 (day 2). For G2 (Kp >= 5.67) SWPC's day-2 HSS is 0.1725 (9, 28, 51). SWPC's MAE over all slots (day 2 1.1024, day 3 1.1082) is already beaten by a linear model on past Kp alone (1.044, 1.057; computed 2026-10-30), so MAE is not the open part: predicting which slots reach storm level from CMEs and high-speed streams one to three days ahead is. Credit: SWPC forecast office; GFZ Kp service (J. Matzka, C. Stolle, Y. Yamazaki and colleagues).
targets.success_criterion: A saved file of Kp forecasts for every 3-hour slot of days 2 and 3 of each 2025 00:30 UTC issue present in the NCEI archive, restricted to slots whose UT date falls in 2025 (same slots as SWPC's 'NOAA Kp index breakdown'), plus code that regenerates it using only data timestamped before 00:30 UTC of the issue day (OMNI or real-time solar wind, DONKI CME analyses, coronagraph and EUV images, past Kp), with training and tuning on data before 2025-01-01 only, such that, against GFZ definitive Kp from https://kp.gfz.de/app/files/Kp_ap_since_1932.txt, the event 'Kp >= 4.67' gives an HSS strictly greater (direction: max) than SWPC's on day 2 and on day 3, as recomputed by the skeptic from the NCEI archive https://www.ngdc.noaa.gov/stp/space-weather/swpc-products/daily_reports/3day_forecast/2025/ re-fetched live immediately before claiming (0.1462 and 0.1313 as of 2026-10-30); the 95% interval of the day-2 HSS difference from a block bootstrap with 27-day blocks must have a lower bound above 0; and the all-slot MAE on days 2 and 3 must not exceed SWPC's.

partial_wins.statement: Day-2 HSS strictly above SWPC's 0.1462 under the same rules, without the bootstrap condition.
Day-3 HSS strictly above SWPC's 0.1313 under the same rules, without the bootstrap condition.

A day-2 HSS strictly above SWPC's for the stronger event Kp >= 5.67 (G2, 6-), same slots and rules, without the bootstrap condition (SWPC: 0.1725 from 9 hits, 28 false alarms, 51 misses as of 2026-10-30, recomputed by the skeptic).

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the 2025 00:30 UTC files from NCEI, parses the Kp breakdown tables, scores them and the claimed forecasts against the GFZ file with an independent 2x2-table script, regenerates the claimed forecasts through a harness that refuses inputs timestamped at or after each issue time, and runs the block bootstrap. Under 1 hour.
angles: Conventional: CME-arrival models (drag-based, ENLIL-like) driven by DONKI analyses plus coronal-hole area and position from EUV images for high-speed-stream timing.
Conventional: classifier per slot on recurrence features (Kp 27 and 54 days earlier with time tolerance), coronal-hole features and CME flags, then thresholded to maximise HSS on 2015-2024.
Cross-domain import (hydrology): flood-warning style event detection with tolerance windows, mapped back to slots.
Cross-domain import (meteorology): calibrated probabilistic forecasts thresholded at the HSS-optimal probability, chosen on pre-2025 data only.
pitfalls: Day 1 of the 00:30 UTC issue includes the slot in progress and SWPC's day-1 MAE is already beaten by last-slot persistence; only days 2 and 3 are scored.
GFZ Kp is in thirds (4.667 = 5-); use >= 4.6 to avoid floating-point misses, and the same threshold for forecast and observation.
Slots of the 30-31 December issues that fall in January 2026 are excluded; including them changes SWPC's HSS to 0.1449 (day 2) and 0.1302 (day 3).
Choosing the decision threshold on 2025 outcomes is test-set tuning; fix it on earlier years.
The NCEI archive has gaps before 2025 (e.g. 2023-09 to 2024-02), so pre-2025 SWPC forecasts are not a complete training reference.
DONKI entries are revised after the fact; use only versions available before each issue time.

targets.name: USGS operational aftershock forecasts 2024-2025: lower Brier score than USGS for 'at least one M4+ aftershock within a week'
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (about 1,400 forecast JSON files and 67 regional ComCat queries; Reasenberg-Jones or ETAS fits run in seconds per sequence)
targets.statement: USGS publishes an operational aftershock forecast (OAF product in ComCat; Jeanne Hardebeck, Andrew Michael, Morgan Page, Nicholas van der Elst, Andrea Llenos, Michael Barall, Kevin Milner and colleagues) after M5+ earthquakes in and near the US, re-issued on a schedule. Each version gives, for 1-day, 1-week, 1-month and 1-year windows, the probability of at least one event of M3+, M4+, M5+... inside a stated circle, from Reasenberg-Jones (generic, Bayesian or sequence-specific) or, recently, ETAS. For mainshocks of M5+ between 2024-01-01 and 2025-10-01 (75 events with OAF products), all versions issued within 14 days of the mainshock with a circular region number 1,377 from 67 sequences (251 RJ generic, 990 RJ Bayesian, 57 RJ sequence-specific, 79 ETAS). Scored against live ComCat (any event other than the mainshock with magnitude >= 4.0 inside that version's own circle during the window), USGS's 1-week M4+ probabilities have Brier score 0.0778 (196 positive windows from 17 sequences; in-sample climatology 0.1221; log-loss 0.2734); 1-week M5+ 0.0367 (104 positive) and 1-day M4+ 0.0503 (146 positive) (computed 2026-10-30). Retrospective tests of operational aftershock forecasts are an active topic. Weiqiang Zhu's QuakeGen diffusion model (arXiv:2607.24109, July 2026) reports beating a reimplemented Bayesian Reasenberg-Jones baseline (opensha-oaf with generic priors) on 80 M4.5+ mainshocks of 2024-2025 in log-likelihood and spatial scores, but it does not score the issued USGS probabilities, these windows or the Brier score. No published model is shown to beat these exact USGS issues. Open task: issue-time-honest probabilities that beat them.
targets.success_criterion: A saved file with a probability for every one of the scored versions (ComCat query producttype=oaf, starttime=2024-01-01, endtime=2025-10-01, minmagnitude=5; all OAF versions from includesuperseded=true with updateTime within 14 days of origin and regionType circle), for the forecast's own 1-week window and circle and the M > =4.0 bin, plus code that regenerates it using only ComCat events with origin time before min(creationTime, window timeStart) of that version, and parameters tuned only on sequences before 2024-01-01, whose Brier score is strictly lower (direction: min) than USGS's 'probability' values on the same windows (0.0778 as of 2026-10-30), both scored against outcomes from a live ComCat query re-fetched immediately before claiming (outcome 1 when any event other than the mainshock with magnitude >= 4.0 has origin time in [timeStart, timeEnd) and epicentre within that version's own circle by haversine distance), with the 95% interval of the Brier difference (USGS Brier minus claimed Brier) from a bootstrap that resamples whole sequences (10,000 draws) having a lower bound above 0.

partial_wins.statement: Brier score strictly below USGS (0.0778 as of 2026-10-30) on the 1-week M > =4 windows under the same rules, without the bootstrap condition.
Brier score strictly below USGS on the 1-week M > =5 windows (0.0367) and on the 1-day M > =4 windows (0.0503), both, same rules, no bootstrap.
Log-loss strictly below USGS's (0.2734) on the 1-week M > =4 windows (probabilities clipped to [1e-4, 1-1e-4] for both), same rules.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic re-runs the ComCat queries, downloads every forecast.json version, recomputes outcomes with a haversine distance test per window and the Brier and log-loss scores for USGS and the claim with an independent script, regenerates the claimed probabilities through a harness that drops ComCat events at or after each cutoff, and runs the sequence bootstrap. About 1-2 hours.
angles: Conventional: sequence-specific ETAS with magnitude-of-completeness correction for early incompleteness (Omori-Utsu with time-dependent Mc), updated at each issue time.
Conventional: Bayesian combination of generic tectonic-regime priors with sequence data, calibrated on pre-2024 sequences.
Cross-domain import (epidemic nowcasting): renewal-process forecasts with right-truncation correction for recently detected events.
Cross-domain import (insurance cat modelling): calibrating probabilities with isotonic regression per region type on historical sequences.
pitfalls: ComCat magnitudes and small-event lists are revised after the fact; using revised pre-issue events is allowed, but post-issue events are not, and the window timeStart can precede creationTime by up to 3.4 h.

Region centres move between versions of the same sequence (up to about 96 km, us7000pn9s; one version filed under the 2025 Kamchatka event carries a Myanmar circle); score each version against its own circle, and query ComCat per distinct circle, not once around the first centre (that undercounts M4 outcomes: 178 instead of 196 positives).

Outside the US networks ComCat is incomplete below about M4.5, which is why M3 bins are not scored; M4 outcomes abroad can also be undercounted, so learning catalog gaps rather than seismicity is a known trap.
Weekly re-issues of long sequences (e.g. the 2025 Kamchatka M8.8) dominate counts; the sequence bootstrap guards against one sequence carrying the result.
A few forecast.json files contain trailing commas (Kamchatka) and some superseded products have empty contents; parse leniently instead of dropping them.

Outcomes are any event with magnitude >= 4.0 except the mainshock itself; foreshocks or doublets inside the window count. ComCat caps a query at 20,000 events, so query outcomes at M >= 3.95, not M >= 2.95, for large sequences.

QuakeGen (arXiv:2607.24109) was compared with a reimplemented Reasenberg-Jones baseline, not with the issued USGS products, and it conditions on data up to 1.6 h after the mainshock rather than on each version's issue time. It is not evidence that this target is solved, and its published outputs do not score as a claim without the issue-time harness.

targets.name: New open cluster in Gaia DR3 absent from the Unified Cluster Catalogue (UCC 260615) and the Hunt and Reffert census
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours per field (Gaia DR3 TAP cone queries of a few deg; a full Galactic-plane blind search is laptop-days; the UCC_cat.csv is a few MB, UCC_members.parquet ~100 MB)
targets.statement: Hunt and Reffert (2023, A&A 673, A114) ran HDBSCAN over all of Gaia DR3 and recovered 7167 clusters, 2387 of them candidate new objects (739 in the stringent subset). Hunt and Reffert (2024, arXiv:2403.05143) found only 5647 compatible with bound clusters. They estimated that the Milky Way holds ~1.3e5 open clusters, only ~4% of them known, and that the census is complete within 1.8 kpc only above ~230 Msun. Hunt et al. (arXiv:2510.18343) published the census selection function. The Unified Cluster Catalogue (UCC; Perren, Pera, Navone and Vazquez 2023, MNRAS 526, 4107; maintained by Gabriel I. Perren at ucc.ar) merges 152 articles into 18,299 clusters with fastMP members. Version 260615 (Zenodo record 20705026, 2026-06-15) is the latest, and 2026 papers keep adding clusters (e.g. arXiv:2603.26572, 2606.01418, 2601.09670). Open task: find a statistically significant, CMD-coherent and preferably bound stellar cluster in Gaia DR3 that is in neither UCC nor any later paper. Gaia DR4 (66 months) is due 2026 December 2 and will change the data; a claim based on DR3 must say so and use DR3 values throughout.
targets.success_criterion: A saved bundle (ADQL queries and Gaia DR3 source_ids of >= 20 members with 5- or 6-parameter astrometry, RUWE < 1.4, G < 20; clustering code; isochrone fit) where: (1) the Hunt and Reffert astrometric significance test (CST) gives >= 5 sigma, run in their public code or in a re-implementation shown to reproduce CST within 1 sigma for 20 HR23 clusters; (2) parallaxes are consistent with one distance (reduced chi^2 < 2 about the weighted mean) and the error-corrected proper-motion dispersion is <= 2 km/s at that distance; (3) a single PARSEC isochrone (free age, distance, A_V) puts >= 80% of members within 0.15 mag of colour, while the same pipeline on 20 field control samples (same pm/parallax window, other positions) puts < 50%; (4) the half-mass radius is inside the Jacobi radius computed from a photometric mass as in Hunt and Reffert 2024; (5) no entry in UCC_cat.csv (latest Zenodo version) lies within max(3 r50, 10 arcmin) with |delta pm| < 1 mas/yr and |delta plx| < 0.3 mas, and no paper after the UCC changelog date reports it (status pages re-fetched immediately before claiming). The win is one new object passing (1)-(5).

partial_wins.statement: A blind pipeline run on a declared sky region ( > = 100 deg^2 of the plane) that recovers >= 90% of the Hunt and Reffert high-quality clusters inside it, with the recovered list and the misses saved.
A new group that passes (1), (2), (3) and (5) but not the boundness test (4): a new unbound association or moving group, logged as such.
A new object passing (1)-(5) at a distance < 1 kpc, where the census is supposed to be most complete.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic re-runs the saved ADQL against the Gaia archive TAP, recomputes CST, the dispersion and the isochrone fit with the saved code, and cross-matches against the newest UCC_cat.csv from Zenodo and the UCC changelog. Under an hour per object.
angles: Distant (2-5 kpc), low-N groups where the Hunt and Reffert selection function predicts a low detection probability (high parallax error, dense fields): most of the ~96% of clusters still unknown are expected there.
Run HDBSCAN in rescaled (l, b, pmra, pmdec, parallax) with a smaller min_cluster_size than HR23 in narrow parallax slices, then demand CST >= 5 sigma.
Cross-domain import (epidemiology): spatial-scan statistics (Kulldorff) give a calibrated significance for compact overdensities in a 5D space.
pitfalls: UCC lists anything ever called an open cluster, under many names (FSR, UBC, CWNU, HSC, OCSN, Theia...); match by position and astrometry, not by name.
Gaia scanning-law patterns and extinction holes create fake overdensities; check the CMD and the field control samples.
Binaries and blends inflate the proper-motion dispersion; use RUWE cuts.
Gaia DR4 (2026-12-02) will redefine members and errors; state which release every number comes from.

targets.name: New Milky Way satellite (ultra-faint dwarf or faint halo star cluster) in public DECam or Legacy Surveys catalogues, absent from the Local Volume Database
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (Astro Data Lab TAP queries of DELVE DR3 / Legacy Surveys DR10 healpix pixels; a full-footprint matched-filter scan covers a few hundred GB of catalogue rows)
targets.statement: The Local Volume Database (LVDB; Andrew B. Pace; Pace 2025, OJAp 8, 142, arXiv:2411.07424; github.com/apace7/local_volume_database, last commit 2026-10-29) lists 68 Milky Way dwarf satellites and candidates (dwarf_mw.csv) and 58 recently found Galactic star clusters (gc_mw_new.csv), plus ambiguous systems (gc_ambiguous), Harris globular clusters and Local Group dwarfs. Discoveries continue: 2026 brought Aquarius IV (Cerny et al., arXiv:2608.02601, found in Rubin Observatory Early Data Preview 2 and confirmed at ~6 sigma in archival DECam imaging) and DELVE 8 / Gemini I (Overdeck et al., arXiv:2606.09975, found in DELVE DR3), both already in the LVDB, alongside deep follow-ups of known systems such as Virgo III (Pai et al., arXiv:2607.25044) and Grus II / Horologium II (Prabhu et al., arXiv:2606.25058). Searches build on the DELVE survey (Drlica-Wagner and collaborators; DR3 on NOIRLab Astro Data Lab) and the DES/PS1 satellite census (Drlica-Wagner et al. 2020, ApJ 893, 47). Open task: find a resolved stellar overdensity in openly public catalogues that passes the community's search thresholds and is in no LVDB table and no paper.
targets.success_criterion: A saved bundle (ADQL queries against delve_dr3.coadd_objects and/or ls_dr10.tractor on datalab.noirlab.edu, star/galaxy and quality cuts, matched-filter code, isochrone, member list, CMD and maps) where: (1) in one catalogue, the isochrone-weighted matched-filter ('simple'-style) Poisson significance is >= 6 sigma and a maximum-likelihood (ugali-style) fit gives TS >= 36; (2) an independent reduction gives >= 4 sigma at the same position: the other of DELVE DR3 / Legacy Surveys DR10, or DES DR2, Pan-STARRS1 DR2 or HSC-SSP PDR3 where deep enough; (3) an old metal-poor isochrone fits the CMD of stars within r_h better than the local field does (likelihood-ratio test reported); (4) the overdensity is made of point sources, lies outside bright-star and bad-region masks, and is not a galaxy cluster or background galaxy (no catalogued galaxy cluster or galaxy group within 3 arcmin); (5) there is no entry in any LVDB table (every CSV under data/ on the main branch: dwarf_mw, dwarf_local_field, dwarf_local_field_distant, dwarf_m31, gc_harris, gc_mw_new, gc_ambiguous, gc_other, gc_dwarf_hosted) within max(3 r_h, 3 arcmin), no SIMBAD object within 3 arcmin whose type is a dwarf galaxy, globular or open cluster, star cluster, association, or galaxy group or cluster (or a candidate of these), and no arXiv paper reports it (LVDB and arXiv re-fetched immediately before claiming). Unrelated background galaxies listed in SIMBAD do not by themselves disqualify a point-source overdensity that passes (4).

partial_wins.statement: Inside a declared footprint of >= 500 deg^2 containing >= 3 LVDB Milky Way satellites that the discovery papers detected in the same catalogue, the pipeline recovers >= 90% of them at >= 5 sigma, and reports its false-positive count after cuts (4).
A new overdensity meeting (3)-(5) with a matched-filter significance between 5 and 6 sigma, logged as a sub-threshold candidate.
For a new candidate meeting (1)-(5): >= 3 Gaia DR3 stars on the isochrone whose proper motions agree within 2 sigma and differ from the field mean.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic re-runs the saved ADQL on Astro Data Lab, recomputes the matched-filter map and likelihood with the saved code, checks masks and galaxy-cluster catalogues, and cross-matches the LVDB CSVs fetched from GitHub. A few hours.
angles: Regions with new deep coverage in DELVE DR3 or Legacy Surveys DR10/DR11 (northern DECam fields, low-latitude edges) that no published census has searched.
Cross-domain import (particle physics): correct for the look-elsewhere effect by running the same pipeline on sky-rotated catalogues to calibrate the trials factor.
pitfalls: Distant galaxy clusters and compact groups mimic faint stellar overdensities when star/galaxy separation fails near the limit; check morphology and redshift catalogues.
Survey-depth edges, chip gaps and bright-star halos produce 'overdensities'; work on depth-normalised maps.
LVDB lists systems under many names and some only in the ambiguous tables; match by coordinates across every CSV.

The LVDB lags new papers by weeks: Rubin-GC1 (arXiv:2609.15872, 2026-09-14) was in no LVDB CSV on 2026-10-30, so the arXiv check is not optional. The withdrawn Yasone-1 to -3 candidates (arXiv:2509.15345) are not in the LVDB either; re-detecting one is not a new discovery and must be stated.
Rubin Observatory preview data are restricted to data-rights holders; use only catalogues that are openly public.

targets.name: New stellar stream in Gaia DR3 absent from the galstreams library (v1.2.1) and the STREAMFINDER atlas
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (all-sky Gaia DR3 queries with G < 20 and parallax/proper-motion cuts are tens of GB; regional searches are laptop-hours)
targets.statement: The galstreams library of Milky Way stellar streams (Cecilia Mateu; Mateu 2023, MNRAS 520, 5225; github.com/cmateu/galstreams) holds > 200 tracks for 141 distinct streams in v1.2 (tagged 2026 June; latest release v1.2.1, 2026-06-03). Its last major track update (2024 June) added over 80 tracks, 40 of them for new streams. The largest Gaia DR3 stream atlas is STREAMFINDER (Ibata, Malhan, Martin and collaborators; Ibata et al. 2024, ApJ 967, 89, arXiv:2311.17202: 87 thin streams, 29 of them new). Further candidates come from Via Machinae (Shih, Buckley, Necib and collaborators) and from spectroscopic surveys (S5). Open task: find a thin, kinematically coherent stellar stream in Gaia DR3 that is in neither galstreams nor those atlases nor any later paper. Gaia DR4 is due 2026 December 2; a claim based on DR3 must say so and use DR3 values throughout.
targets.success_criterion: A saved bundle (ADQL, member source_ids, track fit, code) for a structure with: (1) >= 30 Gaia DR3 members (G < 20, RUWE < 1.4) along a track >= 5 deg long whose width is <= 1/10 of its length; (2) a proper-motion track that varies smoothly along the stream, with residual dispersion consistent with <= 10 km/s at the fitted distance, and parallaxes consistent with that distance (reduced chi^2 < 2); (3) members on one old metal-poor isochrone ( > = 80% within 0.15 mag in colour); (4) significance: the combined sky+proper-motion+CMD matched-filter count exceeds the mean of >= 200 control filters by >= 5 sigma of their dispersion, the controls being the same filter rotated in proper motion and shifted on the sky away from known streams, with the control distribution saved; (5) no stream track overlaps it: no galstreams track whose pole lies within 10 deg of the new pole and whose sky track covers >= 30% of the new one, and no STREAMFINDER or Via Machinae stream likewise. A globular cluster or dwarf from the LVDB at its end must be stated. No arXiv paper reports it (sources re-fetched immediately before claiming).

partial_wins.statement: Inside a declared region containing >= 5 galstreams streams with published Gaia members, the pipeline recovers >= 80% of them, with the recovered tracks compared to the galstreams tracks.
A new structure meeting (1)-(3) and (5) at 4-5 sigma in test (4), logged as a candidate.
A known galstreams stream extended by >= 5 deg beyond its galstreams end-point, with >= 15 new members meeting (2)-(3) and >= 5 sigma in test (4) for the extension.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic re-runs the ADQL on the Gaia archive, recomputes the matched filter and the control distribution, and compares the pole and track with galstreams (pip install galstreams; MWStreams summary) and the STREAMFINDER table. A few hours.
angles: Search in action/angle-like coordinates, or with great-circle pole counts (GC3/mGC3, Mateu), restricted to metal-poor CMD selections.
Cross-domain import (image processing): Hough or Radon transforms on proper-motion-filtered density maps pick up thin linear features.
pitfalls: Gaia scanning-law stripes produce long thin artefacts in density maps; require proper-motion coherence and check against the scanning law.
Disc substructure and open-cluster tidal tails are not halo streams; check the CMD age and the orbit.
galstreams lists several tracks per stream from different papers; match against all of them.

targets.name: New cold (late-T or Y) brown dwarf candidate with significant motion in CatWISE2020 and unTimely, absent from SIMBAD and the ultracool-dwarf compilations
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (IRSA TAP queries of catwise_2020 with colour and motion cuts return tens of thousands of rows; unTimely per-tile catalogues are MB each)
targets.statement: CatWISE2020 (Marocco et al. 2021, ApJS 253, 8) gives positions and proper motions for ~1.9 billion WISE/NEOWISE sources. unTimely (Meisner et al. 2023, AJ 165, 36) gives time-resolved unWISE detections. The known nearby L, T and Y dwarfs are listed by the Backyard Worlds: Planet 9 citizen-science project (Kuchner, Faherty, Meisner, Kirkpatrick and volunteers), by Kirkpatrick et al. (2021, ApJS 253, 7; 2024 20-pc census) and by the UltracoolSheet (Best, Dupuy, Liu, Sanghi, Siverd, Zhang; v2.1.0, 2025-07-03). Yet the coldest, faintest objects are still incomplete beyond ~20 pc, and new Y-dwarf candidates keep appearing. NEOWISE ended in 2024, so the WISE time baseline is final. Open task: find a cold-brown-dwarf candidate with WISE colours of >= T7 and a significant, independently confirmed motion that is in no catalogue or paper.
targets.success_criterion: A saved bundle (IRSA TAP queries, CatWISE2020 rows, unTimely detections, Legacy Surveys DR10 and Pan-STARRS1 cutout photometry, motion-fit code) for an object with: (1) CatWISE2020 W1-W2 >= 2.0 mag (or W1 undetected with W2 S/N >= 8 and a W1-W2 lower limit >= 2.0) and clean ab_flags/cc_flags; (2) a CatWISE2020 total proper motion >= 150 mas/yr at >= 6 sigma, matched within 3 sigma by an independent linear motion fit to >= 4 unTimely epochs spanning >= 6 yr, with a stationary neighbour fitted the same way as a control; (3) no Gaia DR3 source within 3 arcsec of the epoch-propagated position, and z - W2 >= 4 (or z undetected in Legacy Surveys DR10); (4) no SIMBAD object within 10 arcsec of the epoch-2000 and epoch-2016 positions unless its own SIMBAD position and proper motion show it is a different source, no UltracoolSheet entry, no entry in the Kirkpatrick et al. 2021/2024 tables, no arXiv paper, and no post on the Backyard Worlds: Planet 9 Zooniverse Talk boards found by searching its CatWISE designation and its coordinates (all re-fetched immediately before claiming). The claim is 'new cold brown dwarf candidate', not a spectral type.

partial_wins.statement: Pipeline recovers >= 90% of the UltracoolSheet T7-Y dwarfs inside a declared region of >= 1000 deg^2 with the same cuts, and lists the false positives left after automated vetting (no visual inspection).
A batch of >= 5 new candidates with W1-W2 between 1.5 and 2.0 (mid-T colours) meeting (2)-(4).

An object of any colour with total motion >= 1 arcsec/yr confirmed in two independent surveys (e.g. CatWISE2020 and Legacy Surveys/Pan-STARRS epochs), absent from SIMBAD and with no Gaia DR3 counterpart of consistent motion: a missing high-proper-motion nearby object.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic re-runs the IRSA TAP query, refits the unTimely positions with the saved code, checks Gaia DR3, Legacy Surveys and SIMBAD cones at both epochs, and searches the UltracoolSheet CSV export. Under an hour.
angles: Galactic-plane and crowded fields, where Backyard Worlds volunteers and earlier colour cuts were least complete.
Objects with moderate CatWISE motion (150-400 mas/yr), i.e. Y dwarfs at 20-50 pc, rather than the fast movers already harvested.
pitfalls: CatWISE2020 has spurious motions from blends, latent images and diffraction spikes; require the unTimely confirmation and clean flags.
Red, faint W2-only sources include high-redshift galaxies and AGN; demand significant motion.
The UltracoolSheet is complete only for objects known by 2015 plus selected later ones; absence there is not enough, so SIMBAD and the literature must be checked too.

targets.name: Cometary activity in archival survey images of a main-belt asteroid with no cometary designation and no reported activity
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (SSOIS / NOIRLab Astro Data Archive searches per object; DECam and ZTF cutouts are MB each)
targets.statement: Main-belt comets (Hsieh and Jewitt 2006) and other active asteroids number a few dozen. On 2026-10-30 the JPL SBDB lists 39 comet-designated objects (fragments counted separately) with 2.06 < a < 3.3 au, q > 1.6 au and T_J > 3.05, among them P/2025 W3 (Kresken), P/2025 W4 (PANSTARRS) and P/2026 N2. Some active asteroids have only an asteroid designation (e.g. (6478) Gault); others carry both (e.g. (7968) = 133P/Elst-Pizarro). Archival searches work: the Active Asteroids citizen-science project (Colin Chandler, Chad Trujillo, Henry Hsieh, William Oldroyd and volunteers) finds activity in public DECam images. Open task: show activity in public archival images of a main-belt asteroid that has no cometary designation and no published or MPC-reported activity.
targets.success_criterion: A saved bundle (object designation, SBDB orbit, image list with archive URLs, cutouts, Horizons ephemerides, photometry and profile code) where: (1) the object has 2.064 < a < 3.3 au, q > 1.6 au, T_J > 3.05 and no cometary designation in SBDB; (2) on >= 2 nights ( > = 1 day apart), or in >= 2 different instruments, the source at the Horizons-predicted position (residual < 2 arcsec) shows extended emission: compared with a trailed PSF built from >= 5 field stars in the same image at the object's rate, its surface-brightness profile has excess flux beyond 2 FWHM at >= 5 sigma, and any tail lies within 30 deg of the projected anti-solar (PsAng) or anti-velocity (PsAMV) direction; (3) the same test on >= 20 inactive asteroids of similar magnitude in the same images gives no detection; (4) no background source lies under the object (checked in a deep stack of other epochs); (5) there is no activity report for the object in MPECs or the MPC database, SBDB, ATels, RNAAS, the Active Asteroids publications or arXiv, nor a CBET whose title on the public CBAT index names it (full CBET texts are subscription-only and are not required) (all re-fetched immediately before claiming).

partial_wins.statement: The pipeline detects activity, by test (2), in archival images of >= 5 known main-belt comets at epochs when activity was published, with zero detections on 100 inactive control asteroids.
Activity meeting (1)-(5) on a single night in one instrument, logged as a candidate.
A new active epoch (date and image) for a known active asteroid that no paper reports, meeting test (2), which constrains its recurrence.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic re-downloads the images from the stated archives, re-runs the profile and PSF comparison with the saved code, checks the Horizons ephemerides and the SBDB record, and searches MPC/arXiv by designation. About an hour.
angles: Prioritise outer-belt asteroids imaged near perihelion (true anomaly -60 to +90 deg), where sublimation-driven activity is seen.
Members of the Themis and Beagle families and of the families of known MBC hosts.
pitfalls: Trailing of fast-moving objects and poor tracking mimic tails; compare with trailed PSFs at the same rate.
Background galaxies and stars under the object, ghosts and satellite trails all produce false tails; check other epochs.
Activity on a known active asteroid does not make a new active asteroid; check designations and the literature.

targets.name: Unrecognised Uranus or Neptune co-orbital (Trojan, horseshoe or quasi-satellite) among catalogued small bodies, shown by clone integration
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (SBDB orbit and covariance per object; 100-clone N-body runs over 1 Myr with the giant planets take minutes to an hour each)
targets.statement: The Minor Planet Center lists 35 Neptune Trojans (page re-fetched 2026-10-30, elements at epoch 2025-11-21), including 2025 MD138, 2025 MH348 and 2025 NN80, the first L5 objects found in Rubin Observatory Science Validation data (Schwamb, Bernardinelli, Volk and collaborators, arXiv:2610.38309, 2026-10-28, who confirm 2025 MH348 and 2025 NN80 as long-term stable and leave 2025 MD138, with a 38-day arc, as a candidate). Its Uranus Trojan list is empty, although the literature reports two Uranus Trojans: 2011 QF99 (Alexandersen et al. 2013) and 2014 YX49 (de la Fuente Marcos and de la Fuente Marcos 2017). On 2026-10-30 the JPL SBDB holds 62 objects with 29.7 < a < 30.5 au and 30 with 18.9 < a < 19.5 au. Several low-eccentricity ones near Neptune's a are not on the MPC list: 2020 VK45 and 2020 VN45 have condition codes 4 and 3, while 2023 LH7, 2025 LV7, 2025 NE203 and 2025 OA697 still have short arcs (condition codes 6-8); new trans-Neptunian orbits keep arriving from DECam and Rubin. Whether any of these is already published as a co-orbital was not settled here, so the literature check in the criterion matters. Integrating an object's orbit together with its uncertainty settles whether it is co-orbital. Open task: identify a catalogued object as a Uranus or Neptune co-orbital that is not on the MPC lists and has not been reported as one.
targets.success_criterion: A saved bundle (SBDB orbit solution and covariance as fetched, >= 100 clones drawn from that covariance plus the nominal orbit, integration code and output) where: (1) the orbit has a data arc of >= 2 oppositions and condition code <= 5; (2) the clones are integrated together with the Sun (inner-planet masses added), Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, taken from JPL Horizons at the solution epoch (e.g. REBOUND WHFast or IAS15, relative energy error < 1e-8), for >= 1 Myr for Neptune or >= 100 kyr for Uranus; (3) for >= 90% of clones the resonant angle lambda - lambda_planet librates (does not circulate) for at least the first 10 libration cycles, and the classification (L4/L5 tadpole, horseshoe or quasi-satellite) and libration period are stated; (4) the object is on neither https://minorplanetcenter.net/iau/lists/NeptuneTrojans.html nor UranusTrojans.html, and no MPEC, RNAAS or arXiv paper identifies it as co-orbital (re-fetched immediately before claiming).

partial_wins.statement: The pipeline reproduces the MPC classification ( > = 90% of clones librating about the listed L4/L5 point) for >= 90% of the listed Neptune Trojans whose orbits meet (1), and the published co-orbital state of 2011 QF99 and 2014 YX49, with plots saved and every mismatch listed.
An object meeting (1), (2) and (4) for which 50-90% of clones librate: a candidate whose status needs a longer arc.
An object on an MPC Trojan list whose orbit meets (1) and for which >= 90% of clones circulate under procedure (2)-(3): a documented classification correction.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic fetches the same SBDB solution (orbit id saved), regenerates the clones with the saved seed, reruns the integration with an independent integrator or step size, and checks the resonant-angle plots and the MPC lists. Under an hour per object.
angles: Start with SBDB objects with |a - a_planet| < 0.3 au and e < 0.15 that are missing from the MPC lists, then widen to higher-e Centaurs that may be temporary co-orbitals.
Compute the resonant angle at the solution epoch first: objects whose angle is far from 60 deg or 0 deg, with a large amplitude, are usually horseshoe or circulating.
pitfalls: Short-arc orbits (condition code >= 6) give clones that diverge; the criterion excludes them.
Osculating heliocentric elements, used in place of barycentric ones, shift a enough to misclassify; integrate in a barycentric frame.
de la Fuente Marcos and others publish many co-orbital identifications in RNAAS and MNRAS; check the literature by designation.

The MPC lists omit published co-orbitals: the SBDB sets include (309239) 2007 RW10, a published Neptune quasi-satellite, and (83982) Crantor, a published Uranus horseshoe companion; absence from the MPC lists is not enough.

targets.name: New pulsar candidate in public Parkes (Murriyang) search-mode archival data, detected in two independent observations and absent from all pulsar lists
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (one semester collection of a Parkes search project is a few GB to TB on the CSIRO Data Access Portal; dedispersion and folding of a few hundred beams takes days on a laptop CPU)
targets.statement: Search-mode data from Parkes pulsar search projects are public under CC BY 4.0 on the CSIRO Data Access Portal (DAP; a keyword query for 'pulsar survey parkes' returns 1,371 collections). One example is project P477, a deep Perseus-arm search led by A. Lyne: 2.7 GB in 13 files for semester 2009OCTS_01, published on the DAP 2026-10-22. Reprocessings of archival Parkes surveys with new methods have repeatedly found pulsars that the original searches missed. Known pulsars and survey discoveries are listed by the ATNF Pulsar Catalogue (Manchester et al. 2005; version 2.9.0) and by the Pulsar Survey Scraper (David Kaplan, after Julia Deneva; updated 2026-09), which covers ATNF, GBNCC, PALFA, CRAFTS, FAST-GPPS, TRAPUM, MWA, CHIME, CHAMPSS and others. Open task: reprocess public Parkes archival data to find a dispersed periodic signal that is confirmed in an independent archival observation and is not a known pulsar. The win is the candidate; timing confirmation needs new telescope time and is not part of the win.
targets.success_criterion: A saved bundle (DAP collection DOIs and file names, processing code and parameters, candidate plots and folded archives) where: (1) folding gives S/N >= 10 at DM >= 3 pc/cm^3, the S/N-versus-DM curve peaks at the stated DM, and the DM = 0 fold has <= 50% of the peak S/N; (2) the signal is present in both halves of the band and in >= 2 independent public observations (different dates) of positions within one beam FWHM, with consistent barycentric periods (fractional difference < 1e-4, or a fitted binary/acceleration model stated) and DMs within 10%; (3) within a pointing the signal is confined to one beam or to a group of mutually adjacent beams, and is absent from every beam not adjacent to that group (RFI appears across the receiver, a sky source does not), and its period is not within 0.1% of n/m (n, m <= 16) times the period of any known pulsar within 2 deg or of a documented Parkes RFI periodicity; (4) there is no pulsar with matching period and DM within 0.5 deg in ATNF psrcat (latest version) or any Pulsar Survey Scraper survey, and no arXiv/ATel report (re-fetched immediately before claiming).

partial_wins.statement: A reproducible pipeline run on >= 200 public beams that re-detects >= 90% of the known pulsars in those beams whose predicted S/N exceeds 15, with the recovery table saved.
A candidate meeting (1), (3) and (4) in one observation only, with S/N >= 12.

A rotating-radio-transient candidate: >= 3 single pulses at a consistent DM >= 3 in >= 2 independent observations of the same position, meeting (3) and (4) for single-pulse sources (RRATalog included).

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the same DAP files, refolds at the stated period, period derivative and DM with an independent tool (PRESTO prepfold or dspsr/pdmp), and queries psrcat and the Pulsar Survey Scraper. A few hours.
angles: Fast folding algorithm (FFA) searches for long-period (P > 2 s) pulsars, the class FFT searches miss.
Acceleration or jerk searches for binary millisecond pulsars in the low-latitude beams.
Cross-domain import (radar signal processing): matched-filter banks over (P, DM, acceleration) with an empirical background from time-scrambled data.
pitfalls: Mains harmonics and other RFI periods appear in all 13 beams; require absence in the beams not adjacent to the detection.
Bright known pulsars leak into neighbouring beams and appear at harmonics; a detection in one adjacent beam is normal for a real source, a detection in distant beams is not. Check n/m ratios.
Survey discovery lists lag behind discoveries; check the Pulsar Survey Scraper and the newest papers.
Some DAP collections may be embargoed or need sign-in; use only files the portal serves publicly (csiro:78706 serves its 13 beam files to anonymous range requests).

targets.name: New coherent X-ray periodicity in an archival XMM-Newton or Chandra source (5XMM-DR15 / CSC 2.2), confirmed independently and absent from period catalogues
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (pipeline event lists are tens to hundreds of MB per observation from the XMM-Newton Science Archive and the Chandra Data Archive)
targets.statement: 5XMM-DR15 (XMM-Newton Survey Science Centre; HEASARC table xmmssc) has 818,656 unique sources from 14,616 EPIC observations made 2000-01-19 to 2024-10-14, almost half of them with more than one detection. The Chandra Source Catalog 2.2 (Chandra X-ray Center, released 2026 October) has 432,713 sources from ACIS and HRC-I observations public to the end of 2023. The EXTraS project (De Luca et al. 2021, A&A 650, A167) searched EPIC data up to 2012 for pulsations and found, e.g., the ~1 s pulsations of NGC 5907 ULX-1 (Israel et al. 2017). Its public archive v2.0 now carries only aperiodic variability (to 2020), and the original periodicity products are available only on request. No public catalogue-wide periodicity product was found for EPIC data after 2012 or for CSC 2.2. Single-source papers and ATels still report many periods, so absence must be checked source by source. Open task: find a coherent periodicity (spin or orbital) in the archival event data of a catalogued source that no catalogue or paper reports.
targets.success_criterion: A saved bundle (ObsIDs, event-file names, source and background regions, barycentred times, search grid, code) where: (1) a Z^2_n (n <= 4) or Rayleigh search gives post-trial significance >= 4.5 sigma, with red-noise-aware significance (power-law noise model fitted to the source's own power spectrum) and trials = frequencies x harmonics x sources searched, declared before the search; (2) the same period (within 3 sigma, allowing a declared |Pdot|) is found at >= 3 sigma single-trial in an independent dataset: another observation, or a different detector (EPIC-pn vs MOS for P > 5.2 s; Chandra vs XMM); (3) the period is not within 0.5% of a harmonic of the instrument frame time, of the Chandra dither periods for Chandra data (ACIS 707 s and 1000 s; HRC 768 s and 1087 s), or of the spacecraft orbit, and it is absent in the background region and in a nearby comparable source; (4) no counterpart within max(3 sigma position error, 5 arcsec) has a period within 1% (or a harmonic of one) in SIMBAD, VSX, ATNF psrcat, the Ritter and Kolb CV catalogue, or the Fortin et al. 2023 HMXB and Neumann et al. 2023 LMXB catalogues, and no arXiv or ATel report exists (re-fetched immediately before claiming).

partial_wins.statement: Pipeline recovers >= 20 known periodic X-ray sources (pulsars, intermediate polars, polars, eclipsing binaries) from archival event files at their catalogued periods, and shows < 1 false detection per 1000 sources on time-scrambled events.
A candidate meeting (1), (3) and (4) in one dataset without independent confirmation.
First X-ray detection of a period already known at other wavelengths (e.g. the optical or TESS period of a CV candidate in VSX), meeting (1)-(3), with no X-ray period reported before.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the event files from the XSA or the Chandra Data Archive, re-runs barycentring (barycen / axbary) and the Z^2 search with an independent code (e.g. Stingray or HENDRICS), recomputes the trials and checks the period catalogues. A few hours.
angles: Galactic-plane sources with hard spectra and >= 500 counts in post-2012 EPIC-pn data: the intermediate-polar and HMXB population that EXTraS-era searches did not cover.
Stack repeat observations semi-coherently for faint sources with many detections in 5XMM-DR15.
pitfalls: Chandra dither (ACIS 707 s and 1000 s; HRC 768 s and 1087 s) and XMM attitude or frame-time effects produce spurious periods; test the background and the neighbours.
Red noise from aperiodic variability makes white-noise false-alarm probabilities far too optimistic.
Many periods are published only in ATels or in papers on single sources; search by coordinates, not names.

targets.name: CHC-COMP 2026: first validated model or refutation for a Horn-clause task no solver answered and whose verdict is only a placeholder
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days per task (portfolio of Eldarica, Golem, Spacer, MuCyc and custom invariant search); validating a model or refutation takes seconds to minutes
targets.statement: CHC-COMP 2026 was organised by Konstantin Britikov (Lugano) and Levente Bajczi (BME). Results are at chc-comp.github.io/chc-comp-2026/tables, and the benchmarks are in chc-comp/chc-comp26-benchmarks. It ran 10,193 check-sat tasks in nine tracks with a 1800 s limit, using Eldarica, Golem, LoAT, MuCyc, PCSat, Z3/Spacer (hors concours), ThetaCHC, z4 and chococatalia. Parsing the per-track BenchExec solver tables gives 892 task files with no 'true'/'false' answer from any solver. In 617 of them the expected_verdict in the task's YAML is marked 'placeholder verdict (auto-added)', so the status is genuinely unknown. The other 275 carry a non-placeholder expected_verdict from earlier solver runs (114 with a majority_vote_verdict field, 139 with a majority-vote comment naming its supporters, 22 with a bare verdict). Placeholder tasks by track (2026-10-30): ADT-LIA 395 (mostly ringen-adt-benchmarks tip2015/isaplanner/prod and ADTRem), BV-Lin 76, LIA-Lin-Arrays 46 (quic3, llreve-bench/unsolved program-equivalence tasks), LRA-Lin 24 (vmt cav12 token_ring and transmitter, sally hacms eventclock), LIA-Arrays 23, LIA-Lin 18 (aeval-unsafe s_split, Lustre DRAGON and PRODUCER_CONSUMER, llreve digits10), BV 17 (eldarica-misc Consistency fortune/incremental and five reve *-horn-bv), LIA 16 (kind2 microwave and DRAGON, hcai svcomp) and ADT-LIA-Arrays 2. One of the BV tasks, eldarica-misc/BV/Consistency/incremental2.41-bv, was answered 'true' by Eldarica in the 2026 model track (results-BV-model table). That leaves 616 placeholder tasks with no answer in either track. The benchmarks were contributed by the Eldarica, Kind 2, Sally, VMT, HCAI, AEval, RInGen, ADTRem, llreve, quic3, rust-horn, Solidity and Ultimate projects.
targets.success_criterion: Success means one eligible task, its .smt2 file from chc-comp/chc-comp26-benchmarks identified by path and SHA-256. Eligible: no 'true' or 'false' answer in its row of https://chc-comp.github.io/chc-comp-2026/tables/results- < TRACK > -solver.table.html or of https://chc-comp.github.io/chc-comp-2026/tables/results- < TRACK > -model.table.html; its YAML expected_verdict is a placeholder or absent when re-fetched; and no answer in the CHC-COMP 2025 tables (linked from https://chc-comp.github.io/2025/results.html). For SAT, a model in the CHC-COMP 2026 model format (one define-fun per predicate, using only the file's theories, no quantifiers). It must be accepted by the 2026 model-validation pipeline (chc-comp/chc-comp-2026, *-validation templates), and an independent SMT solver must prove every clause's negation unsat. For UNSAT, an explicit refutation: finitely many ground clause instances with concrete values, each constraint true, deriving false, checked by an independent evaluator. A bare solver answer does not win.

partial_wins.statement: The same certificate standard for one of the 275 tasks that no 2026 solver answered but whose YAML carries a non-placeholder expected_verdict from earlier runs. The certificate must agree with that verdict, or, if it contradicts it, come with both independent checks.

targets.verification_method: Download the .smt2 file and hash it. For a model, substitute the definitions into every clause and check validity with two SMT solvers (e.g. cvc5 and Z3), plus the CHC-COMP 2026 validator. For a refutation, parse the derivation, check that each step is an instance of a clause of the file, evaluate every constraint under exact theory semantics (bit-width-exact for BV, exact rationals for LRA) and confirm that the root is the query. Re-fetch the 2026 table row and the YAML.
angles: The LRA-Lin and LIA-Lin tasks are transition systems (token_ring, transmitter, DRAGON, PRODUCER_CONSUMER): try k-induction with invariant strengthening and IC3 over the theory with long runs. Golem, LoAT and MuCyc did not run every track.
llreve-bench/unsolved tasks are program-equivalence (regression verification) problems: relational invariants coupling the two programs' loop counters often suffice.
ADT tasks from TIP/IsaPlanner are inductive theorems: a model needs a size or catamorphism abstraction, so try RInGen-style regular models or Eldarica's size-based abstractions.
For tasks whose file name says 'unsafe' or 'invalid', search for a counterexample by bounded unrolling (BMC) with a large bound first: refutations are cheap to check.
pitfalls: The expected_verdict field is often a placeholder 'true' added automatically. It is not a status: eventclock4.invalid has one.
Some task names (safe/unsafe/true-unreach-call) come from the C source and need not match the CHC encoding (BV translations can change the verdict).
The same YAML can appear in several tracks. Identify the exact .smt2 file and track.
Check the model-track table as well as the solver table: eldarica-misc/BV/Consistency/incremental2.41-bv has no solver-track answer but has an Eldarica 'true' in results-BV-model.

Six placeholder tasks (e.g. eldarica-misc/BV/dillig/34.c-bv, vmt-chc-benchmarks/bv/half.c) are on chc-comp-2026 ignore.txt, which the organisers use to score a task as neither correct nor wrong. Read why before investing.
ADT models that need recursive functions or quantifiers are outside the validator format, so check what the 2026 validator accepts before investing.

Check CHC-COMP 2025 and earlier results and recent papers before claiming. The 2025 per-track tables are hosted on www.cip.ifi.lmu.de, which did not respond on 2026-10-30. An unreachable table is not evidence of absence.

targets.name: HWMCC'25: first certified answer for a hardware model-checking benchmark that no participant solved
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days per benchmark (IC3/PDR, BMC, k-induction portfolios; a 16-core machine helps); certificate checking takes minutes to hours
targets.statement: HWMCC'25 was the 13th Hardware Model Checking Competition, at FMCAD'25, organised by Mathias Preiner, Nils Froleyks and Armin Biere; benchmarks, raw CSVs, logs and certificates are on Zenodo 17428464. Tracks (1 h on a 16-core node): bit-level safety, 330 AIGER 1.9 bit-blastings of the word-level BV benchmarks (ric3, ric3-multi, super-prove, supercar, aic3, avy, ncip, voiraig); bit-level liveness, 264 (nuxmv, super-prove); word-level BV, 330 BTOR2 (ric3, supercar, btor2-select, avr, pono, ic3-ng, btormc); word-level arrays, 310 (pono, btor2-select, avr, btormc). Only BTOR2 counterexamples were checked at word level, so word-level unsat answers are uncertified. In the raw CSVs no configuration answered sat or unsat on 46 bit-level safety, 40 liveness, 39 BV and 132 array benchmarks. The safety lists overlap: 14 of the 46 were answered at word level (e.g. 2019/goel cal157-cal211 and mul1 unsat by avr, xsokoban level_5 sat by ric3) and 7 of the 39 at bit level. 32 designs have no answer in either track: 2019/beem/pgm_protocol.8.prop6; 2020/mann fifo-p0 and rast-p17; eight 2024/hkust/refinement_checking ISA checks (ILA_Flute_*, ILA_Piccolo_*, ILA_Ridecore_JAL); 2024/hkust/x-epic/a16-p75; three 2025/hkust miters (examples 10, 82, 95); seven 2025/ntu/sat/xsokoban levels (10, 20, 27, 48, 66, 73, 90); yosyshq cv32e40x p228 and p530; eight SoSy-Lab translations of SV-COMP tasks (eca-rers2012, nla-digbench, float-benchs, loops-crafted). Of these, only ILA_Flute_XORI_sanity has an answer in the HWMCC'24 CSVs (unsat by ncip-minicraig, uncertified), leaving 31. hwmcc.github.io/2026 returns 404 on 2026-10-30. Families were contributed by HKUST, NTU, SoSy-Lab (LMU), YosysHQ, Goel, Mann and others.
targets.success_criterion: Success means one of the 31 designs named in the statement (no sat/unsat answer from any configuration in hwmcc25-bitlevel-safety.csv or hwmcc25-wordlevel-bv.csv on Zenodo 17428464, and none in the HWMCC'24 CSVs at hwmcc.github.io/2024 or any earlier edition's results), its file taken from the track tarball and matched by SHA-256, plus a certificate in the HWMCC'25 formats. For sat, a counterexample accepted by aigsim on the bit-level .aig or by btorsim on the word-level .btor2. For unsat, an AIGER safety certificate for the bit-level .aig accepted by Certifaiger (a word-level unsat claim is certified only through this bit-level translation). The design must not be reported solved in the HWMCC'25 slides or logs, a later HWMCC or a paper. Uncertified answers do not count.

partial_wins.statement: A sat witness accepted by btorsim for one of the 132 word-level array benchmarks that no HWMCC'25 participant solved, other than 2019/mann/safe/arbitrated_fifos_n2d8w8 (answered unsat by nuxmv in HWMCC'24): 131 eligible on 2026-10-30 against the HWMCC'24 CSVs. The benchmark must also have no sat/unsat answer in the HWMCC'20 or HWMCC'19 results, matched by file name.

A certified answer (aigsim or Certifaiger for bit-level safety, btorsim for a word-level sat witness, the checker behind hwmcc25-bitlevel-live-cert.csv for liveness) for one of the 6 benchmarks answered by some tool but never certified: cal222, 2020/mann/stack-p0 and yosyshq veer-p7 (bit-level safety, unsat claimed in HWMCC'25), ILA_Flute_XORI_sanity (unsat claimed in HWMCC'24 only), 6s364j00000 (liveness, sat claimed by super-prove) and array-examples/standard_init3_ground-1 (arrays, sat claimed by btor2-select).
For one of the 40 unsolved bit-level liveness benchmarks, a lasso counterexample accepted by aigsim, or a certificate accepted by the checker used for hwmcc25-bitlevel-live-cert.csv.

A Certifaiger-accepted unsat certificate for the bit-level .aig of one of the 12 designs that HWMCC'25 answered unsat only at word level (uncertified) and not at bit level: 2019/goel/industry cal157, cal188, cal191, cal206, cal211 and mul1; 2024/hkust/seq/gcd_2_4/gcd_bit_width_large; SoSy-Lab pals_lcr.3.ufo.BOUNDED-6.pals+Problem12_label01, eca-rers2012 Problem17_label44 and Problem19_label01, and loop-lit jm2006.c.i.v+cfa-reducer; 2025/hkust example_52_miter_miter.

targets.verification_method: Fetch the track tarball from Zenodo 17428464, extract the benchmark and hash it. Run aigsim or btorsim on the witness, or Certifaiger (github.com/Froleyks/certifaiger) on the AIGER certificate against the bit-level benchmark, recording versions and the accepting output. Re-read the bit-level safety and word-level BV CSVs together (plus the liveness, array and *-cert CSVs for partial wins) to confirm the design had no sat/unsat answer in either track, match it by file name in the HWMCC'24 CSVs at hwmcc.github.io/2024 and earlier editions, and check hwmcc.github.io for a newer edition.
angles: Miters (2025/hkust *_miter_miter) and ISA refinement checks are equivalence problems: structural hashing, SAT sweeping and induction over internal equivalences (ABC dprove/&cec style) often beat generic IC3.
xsokoban levels sit under a 'sat' folder: a Sokoban solver can produce the move sequence, which is then encoded as an input trace and checked with aigsim/btorsim.
SoSy-Lab tasks come from SV-COMP programs whose verdicts are in sv-benchmarks. Use the program-level invariant to build a hardware inductive invariant, then a Certifaiger certificate.
For p4, avr and pono proved the goel industry cases at word level: a word-level inductive invariant from those tools, bit-blasted, is a starting point for a Certifaiger certificate.
pitfalls: Several families have answers known by construction (xsokoban 'sat', SV-COMP-derived tasks with known verdicts). The win is the first certified solve, not a new truth, so state that.
The bit-level safety track is the bit-blasted BV track: always check both CSVs (and both cert CSVs). A design unsolved in one track may be solved, even certified, in the other.
AIGER 1.9 reset functions: a witness must respect them, and older aigsim versions may mishandle them.
The word-level unsat path goes through the bit-level translation. Make sure the two are the same benchmark name and property.
HWMCC'24 used the folder name 2024/hku where HWMCC'25 uses 2024/hkust: match earlier editions by file name.
Check the HWMCC'25 slides, earlier editions and later papers (and any HWMCC'26 if one is announced) before claiming.

targets.name: Metamath pmproofs.txt: a strictly shorter condensed-detachment proof of a Principia Mathematica theorem
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (proof compression and bounded exhaustive search with pmGenerator-style tools; large RAM helps); checking a proof takes milliseconds
targets.statement: Metamath's 'Shortest known proofs of the propositional calculus theorems from Principia Mathematica' (pmproofs.txt, created by the late Norman Megill) gives D-proofs for the 193 propositional theorems of Principia Mathematica plus Meredith's single axiom, Peirce's axiom and biass: 196 entries in all. A D-proof is a Polish string of condensed-detachment steps over ax-1, ax-2 and ax-3 of Lukasiewicz's P2 system with modus ponens. The latest revision (26-Feb-2025) totals 24,460 steps. In it Samiro Discher found 38 shorter proofs with generative proof compression in pmGenerator 1.2.2, after 40 more in June 2024. Earlier improvers: Gregory Bush (2004), Scott Fenton (2010-13), George Szpiro (2018), Rohan Ridenour (2020) and Discher (2022-23). Proofs of up to 39 steps have been searched exhaustively, so the 68 entries of 39 steps or fewer are optimal. The 128 entries of 43 or more steps remain open. The longest are biass 1579, *5.32 621, *5.7 605, *5.53 551, *5.24 545, *4.38 527, *5.23 501, *5.18 491, *4.86 473 and *4.39 463. Seven entries sit at 43 steps (*2.42, *2.48, *2.51, *2.8, *4.74, *5.12, Peirce). An independent unification checker written for this entry re-derived the stated 'Result of proof' of all 196 entries from their proofs on 2026-10-30.
targets.success_criterion: Success means, for one entry of https://us.metamath.org/mmsolitaire/pmproofs.txt (re-fetched live immediately before claiming), a string over {1,2,3,D} that is a well-formed D-proof in the file's Polish notation, STRICTLY SHORTER (direction: min) than the listed proof. Its most general conclusion, computed by condensed detachment with most-general unifiers (premises renamed apart, occurs check), must have that entry's 'Result of proof' formula as a substitution instance (equal up to renaming, or more general). The proof must be accepted by drule.c (us.metamath.org/downloads/drule.c) and by an independent checker. Proofs using other axioms, definitions, lemmas referenced by name or repeated-subproof sharing do not count: the length is the number of characters of the pure D-string.

partial_wins.statement: For one of the 128 entries with 43 or more steps, a D-proof of exactly the listed length whose most general conclusion is strictly more general than the listed 'Result of proof': the listed formula is a substitution instance of it but not a renaming.

targets.verification_method: Compile drule.c and run it on the single proof (one argument prints the conclusion in Polish notation). Independently, a short Python unifier: parse the D-string recursively, instantiate fresh axiom schemas, unify the antecedent of the major premise with the minor premise, and compare the conclusion against the parsed 'Result of proof' by one-way matching. Then check that the length is smaller than the live entry's step count.
angles: Long entries (biass, *5.32, *5.7, *4.38) are built from many lemmas. Re-route them through shorter proofs of the intermediate conclusions and reuse the best known D-subproofs of every formula they contain (the 'shortest proof of each subformula' table idea in pmGenerator).

Generative compression: enumerate all most-general theorems up to 25-31 steps, index them by conclusion, then replace every subproof in an existing proof by the shortest proof of a formula at least as general.
Search on the abbreviated forms. Several PM theorems differ only by v, ., = definitions, and a shorter proof of a sibling's result may specialise.
Use the 2024 note that all proofs up to 39 steps are exhausted: improvements for the 43-step entries would need 41 steps, so target the long tail instead.
pitfalls: Length is the D-string length (odd numbers). Proofs that reuse a subproof by reference are explicitly excluded by the file's 23-Jan-2012 clarification.
The conclusion must subsume the listed 'Result of proof', which is in the file's ASCII notation with ~ and ->. Parse it, do not eyeball it.
The live file may have been updated after 26-Feb-2025. Re-fetch it, and check the pmGenerator repository and discussions for unmerged improvements before claiming.
