More than a third of residues are still predicted wrongly given the backbone, and the splits, data pipelines and evaluation (per-chain recovery over the test chains) are public in the ProteinInvBench / PiFold repositories, so the benchmark runs on one GPU or a patient CPU.
targets.success_criterion: Designed sequences for every chain of the CATH 4.2 test split exactly as distributed by the public pipeline used in the published table (PiFold / ProteinInvBench data loaders; the split file hash must be stated), one sequence per chain from a single frozen model with declared sampling temperature, such that the recovery computed by the skeptic with that repository's evaluation code (same aggregation as the published table) is STRICTLY HIGHER (direction: max) than 63.5 percent - above Refold (Joint)'s reported 0.63 on CATH 4.2 (arXiv:2603.14350, re-fetched live immediately before claiming) with its two-decimal rounding absorbed - and higher than any later recovery for the same split found by the novelty check, with the short-subset recovery also reported; training must respect the CATH 4.2 split and every pretraining corpus must be declared and filtered so that no test chain (and no chain above a stated sequence-identity threshold to a test chain) appears in it. A full-test recovery above 60.77 but at or below 63.5 percent counts only as partial win p4.

partial_wins.statement: Short-subset recovery strictly above 51.5 percent (absorbing the rounding on Refold (Joint)'s reported 0.51) with the full-test recovery also reported from the same frozen model and the same corpus audit.

With the same frozen model, TS50 recovery strictly above 62.79 percent or TS500 strictly above 69.19 percent (Knowledge-Design) by at least 0.5 points, with the CATH 4.2 numbers reported alongside, provided the novelty check finds no higher published value for those sets.
Matching the published 60.77 percent within 1 point using a model of at most 10M parameters trained from scratch on the CATH 4.2 training split alone, with training logs and the harness published.

Full-test recovery strictly above 60.77 percent (Knowledge-Design) by at least 0.5 points under the same split, frozen-model and corpus-audit rules, reported as beating the Knowledge-Design row and not as the record.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic obtains the CATH 4.2 split through the public loaders, checks the split hash and that the submission covers each test chain exactly once, recomputes recovery with the repository's evaluation code (and independently as per-chain identity, median and mean both reported), reruns the attacker's inference from the released checkpoint and seed, and audits the declared training and pretraining corpora for test chains and near-identical homologues. An hour or two plus the attacker's training cost.
angles: Most of the remaining error is in loops and surface positions; a model with an explicit burial/secondary-structure prior, or a two-stage core-then-surface decoder, attacks exactly where the gap is.

Cross-domain import (sequence modelling): recovery is a per-position classification with strong neighbourhood structure, so iterative refinement decoding (mask-predict, as in non-autoregressive translation) fits better than one-shot decoding.
Pair a structure encoder with a protein language model as a prior, but freeze the language model and declare its corpus, since that is where leakage hides.
Report designability (self-consistency TM-score) alongside recovery: a recovery gain that lowers designability is not progress, and the extra number costs little.
Check the easy wins first: ensembling several public models and voting per position often moves recovery by a point, which calibrates how much a new architecture is really worth.
pitfalls: Several CATH splits circulate (4.2 vs 4.3, different chain lists); numbers are only comparable within one split, so the split file hash must be stated.
Protein language models pretrained on recent UniRef or PDB snapshots may have seen the test chains; without a declared and filtered corpus the number is unverifiable.
Recovery is reported as median or mean over chains in different papers, and sampling temperature changes it; pin both and report both.
Sequence recovery is not a measure of whether a designed protein works; a win is a benchmark result only.
TS50 and TS500 are small sets with their own conventions; a TS50 number quoted against the CATH bar is a category error.

targets.name: ProteinBench (ATLAS): beat the best published conformational-ensemble distribution metrics for proteins
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (GPU; 250 conformations for each of 82 proteins, plus metric computation)
targets.statement: ProteinBench (Fei Ye, Zaixiang Zheng, Dongyu Xue, Yuning Shen, Lihao Wang, Yiming Ma, Yan Wang, Xinyou Wang, Xiangxin Zhou, Quanquan Gu and co-authors, arXiv:2409.06744) includes a distribution-prediction task: predict the conformational ensemble of a protein and compare it with the ATLAS molecular-dynamics ensembles, 82 proteins with 250 sampled conformations per protein, scored by pairwise-RMSD correlation, per-target RMSF correlation, root-mean Wasserstein distance (RMWD), MD-PCA and joint-PCA Wasserstein-2 distances, plus validity checks (CA clash percentage, peptide-bond breaks); the metric suite and the 82-protein test split are those of AlphaFlow (Bowen Jing, Bonnie Berger and Tommi Jaakkola, arXiv:2402.04845). Published medians (Table 15): among the sequence-only rows ConfDiff-Open-MD leads with pairwise-RMSD r 0.59, per-target RMSF r 0.85, RMWD 2.75, MD-PCA W2 1.41 and joint-PCA W2 2.27, with CA clash 0.5 percent and peptide-bond breaks 6.5 percent; AlphaFlow-MD is close (0.53 / 0.85 / 2.64 / 1.55 / 2.29) but breaks 22.2 percent of peptide bonds, while MSA-subsampling reaches only r 0.25 and EigenFold -0.03. Two facts bound what counts as a record. First, re-evaluations of the same sequence-only models disagree with ProteinBench: BBFlow (Nicolas Wolf, Leif Seute, Vsevolod Viliuga, Simon Wagner, Jan Stuehmer and Frauke Graeter, arXiv:2503.05738) reports ConfDiff at r 0.62, RMWD 2.56 and joint-PCA W2 2.19 on the same test set, so the better of the two published numbers is the bar. Second, methods that are handed the test protein's experimental structure score far better and are a different input regime, not a bar for prediction from sequence: AlphaFlow-MD+Templates reaches r 0.94, per-target RMSF r 0.90, RMWD 1.95, MD-PCA W2 1.25 and joint-PCA W2 1.58, and backbone-conditioned BBFlow reaches 0.83 / 2.07 / 1.90. The reference rows show how much room is left in the sequence-only regime: independent MD samples score r 0.96 and joint-PCA W2 0.71, and even a short 2.5 ns MD run scores r 0.89 and joint-PCA W2 1.89, which no sequence-only learned method approaches. Data and metric code are public (ATLAS ensembles and the benchmark repository).
targets.success_criterion: An ensemble of 250 conformations per protein for every protein of the ProteinBench ATLAS distribution-prediction test set (the 82-protein AlphaFlow split), generated from sequence - optionally from a declared static structure prediction of that sequence, but with no experimental structure, template or backbone of a test protein as input at any stage, and no ATLAS trajectory for a test protein used in training or selection - such that the skeptic, recomputing the benchmark's metrics with its released code, obtains on a declared metric a value STRICTLY BETTER than the better of the two published sequence-only evaluations: joint-PCA W2 below 2.19 by at least 0.05 (direction: min), or pairwise-RMSD correlation above 0.62 by at least 0.03 (direction: max), or RMWD below 2.56 by at least 0.05 (direction: min) (arXiv:2409.06744 Table 15 and arXiv:2503.05738 Table A.1, both re-fetched live immediately before claiming), and better than any later published sequence-only value for the same task found by the novelty check, while the CA clash percentage stays at or below 1.0 and peptide-bond breaks at or below 7.0 (the ConfDiff-Open-MD row's values, which several published rows fail) and the other listed metrics are all reported. Template-conditioned and backbone-conditioned rows (for example AlphaFlow-MD+Templates or BBFlow) are a different regime: they are neither the bar nor a win here, and a submission that takes any such input does not qualify. Ensembles, configs, seeds and the per-protein metric table must be published.

partial_wins.statement: Per-target RMSF correlation median strictly above 0.88 - the best published sequence-only value, ConfDiff as re-evaluated in arXiv:2503.05738 - by at least 0.02, with the validity bounds met and all other metrics reported from the same frozen model.

On a declared metric, a value strictly better than the 2.5 ns MD reference row (pairwise-RMSD r above 0.89, or joint-PCA W2 below 1.89, or RMWD below 2.22) on at least a pre-registered half of the 82 proteins, in the sequence-only regime, with the full-set numbers also reported.

A reproduction artefact: reproducing a published method's row (for example AlphaFlow-MD or ConfDiff-Open-MD) within 0.05 on joint-PCA W2 and 0.03 on pairwise-RMSD correlation with public weights and the public metric code, with runtime published.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the ATLAS test ensembles and the ProteinBench metric code, checks the submission has the required number of conformations for every test protein with correct sequences and no duplicated frames, recomputes every listed metric and the validity checks, verifies from the configs that no ATLAS trajectory of a test protein was used in training or selection (and that MD-trained variants declare their training trajectories), and re-fetches the published table. Hours of compute for scoring.
angles: The MD-trained variants win on distributional metrics while PDB-trained ones win on static accuracy; a two-stage model (PDB pretraining, then MD fine-tuning on non-test proteins) targets the actual metric.

Cross-domain import (generative evaluation): the metrics are Wasserstein distances between point clouds in PCA space, so explicitly matching low-order moments of the ensemble (variance along the top MD-PCA modes) is more direct than hoping a sampler covers them.

Cheap physics in the loop: relax sampled conformations with a short energy minimisation to fix clashes and broken peptide bonds, which protects the validity constraint that several published methods violate.
Spend samples where the ensemble is wide: estimate flexibility first (RMSF proxy) and allocate the 250 conformations per protein non-uniformly along the predicted flexible modes.
Report per-protein metrics, since medians over 82 proteins hide collapse on the most flexible targets.
pitfalls: Several published rows are trained on MD data; a method trained on ATLAS trajectories of test proteins is leaking, and the training trajectory list must be declared.

Template-conditioned and backbone-conditioned models (AlphaFlow-MD+Templates, BBFlow) see the test protein's experimental structure and score far better; feeding such an input, or quoting their rows as the bar, puts a claim outside this target's regime.

The same model scores differently in different evaluations (ProteinBench and BBFlow differ by 0.03 in pairwise-RMSD r and 0.08 in joint-PCA W2 for ConfDiff), so a claim must clear the better published number and state the metric script and version used.
Validity metrics must be reported with the distributional ones: an ensemble that scores well while breaking 20 percent of peptide bonds is not a win, even though a published row does exactly that.
Medians across 82 proteins are reported; mixing means and medians, or scoring a subset, breaks comparability.
Metric values depend on the number of sampled conformations; 250 per protein is the published protocol and must be matched.
The ATLAS ensembles are themselves finite MD samples, so the reference rows are a ceiling in practice, not ground truth; claims must stay inside the benchmark.

targets.name: ProteinBench apo-holo: beat TMens 0.873 for predicting both states of 91 conformational-change proteins
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (GPU; 20 conformations for each of 91 proteins)
targets.statement: ProteinBench (Fei Ye, Zaixiang Zheng, Dongyu Xue and co-authors; ICLR 2025, arXiv:2409.06744) includes a multiple-state prediction task built on 91 apo-holo protein pairs curated by Saldaño et al. (Bioinformatics 2022). The task is to sample 20 conformations per protein from the apo sequence and score how well the ensemble covers both experimental states. apo-TM and holo-TM are the best TM-score of any sample to each state, and TMens is their arithmetic mean; all three are averaged over the 91 proteins. Pairwise TM measures diversity, and CA-clash and peptide-bond-break percentages check validity. Published values (Table 14; the same rows are on the ProteinBench Hugging Face leaderboard, last changed 2024-12-10): AlphaFlow-PDB leads with TMens 0.873 (apo-TM 0.855, holo-TM 0.891). It is followed by MSA-depth256 and ConfDiff-Open-PDB at 0.867 and ESMFlow-PDB at 0.866, with AlphaFlow-MD best on apo-TM at 0.857; Str2Str variants fall to 0.68-0.77. The row that makes this a real open problem is the trivial reference: submitting the experimental apo structure as the only prediction scores TMens 0.895 (apo 1.000, holo 0.790). That is above every method, so no sampler yet covers the holo state well enough to beat a one-state baseline that models no change at all. Later papers that use 90 of these pairs with 5 samples per protein stay below 0.873: ConfDiff (arXiv:2403.14088) and the structure-language-model/ESMDiff paper (arXiv:2410.18403, AlphaFlow 0.864 mean). ProteinBench has no evaluation repository of its own. The 91-target list (revision1_86_plus_5.csv, from Saldaño et al. via EigenFold) and an apo-holo scoring script are public in the same group's ConfDiff repository (github.com/bytedance/ConfDiff, datasets/apo), and all structures are in the PDB.
targets.success_criterion: At least 20 sampled conformations for each of the 91 apo-holo targets of revision1_86_plus_5.csv. They must be generated from the apo sequence alone, using sequence databases or MSAs only. No experimental apo or holo coordinates of a test protein may be used as input, template, starting conformation or selection signal, and no ligand identity taken from the holo entry may be used as input. The skeptic recomputes the metrics with the apo-holo evaluation in github.com/bytedance/ConfDiff (datasets/apo, src/analysis/apo.py, TMscore binary, 20 samples) and must obtain a TMens (mean over the 91 proteins, as the published table reports) STRICTLY HIGHER (direction: max) than 0.873 by at least 0.005. 0.873 is AlphaFlow-PDB, arXiv:2409.06744 Table 14, re-fetched live immediately before claiming. The TMens must also be higher than any later published TMens for the same task found by the novelty check. apo-TM, holo-TM, pairwise TM, CA clash percentage and peptide-bond-break percentage must all be reported, and validity must stay within the published range (CA clash at most 1.0 percent, peptide-bond breaks at most 10.0 percent). Conformations, configs and seeds must be published so the metrics recompute. Passing the 0.895 apo-structure reference row is the standing goal and should be stated when reached.

partial_wins.statement: A holo-TM strictly above 0.891 (AlphaFlow-PDB) by at least 0.005 with TMens at or above 0.867, under the same no-experimental-input rule.
TMens strictly above 0.873 by at least 0.005 while using at most 5 sampled conformations per protein instead of 20, with the sampling budget and compute reported.
A reproduction artefact: reproducing a published row (method, apo-TM, holo-TM, TMens) within 0.005 with public weights and the public metric code, with runtime and hardware published.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic builds the 91 apo and holo reference structures from revision1_86_plus_5.csv with the ConfDiff datasets/apo pipeline (make_csv.py from RCSB mmCIF files). The skeptic checks that the submission covers every protein with the required number of conformations and correct apo sequences, then recomputes apo-TM, holo-TM, TMens, pairwise TM and the validity metrics with the ConfDiff apo evaluation and the TMscore binary. The skeptic inspects configs and logs to confirm that no experimental structure of a test protein entered generation or model selection (including as a template or a starting conformation) and that no holo ligand was given as input, and re-fetches the published table. Hours of compute.
angles: MSA subsampling at depth 256 nearly matches the best flow models while being far cheaper; sweep depth jointly with a diversity-aware selection rule before training anything new.

The metric rewards covering two specific states, not broad diversity: sample a few well-separated modes (for example by clustering a large cheap ensemble and keeping cluster centres) rather than 20 random draws.

Cross-domain import (coverage/recall in generative models): optimise an explicit two-mode coverage objective, since TMens is a max-over-samples quantity per state and is dominated by the single best sample for each state.
Ligand-free holo prediction is the hard half: test whether a pocket-closure prior (predicted cavity volume) helps steer samples toward the holo state.
Watch validity: several methods trade peptide-bond integrity for diversity, and a short relaxation step recovers it cheaply.
pitfalls: The 'apo model' row uses the experimental apo structure and is a reference, not a competitor; using any experimental coordinates of a test protein makes a result inadmissible.
Co-folding with the bound ligand copies information from the holo experiment; ligand-conditioned runs may be reported as a separate row but do not count toward the bar.
AlphaFlow/ESMFlow/ConfDiff variants trained on MD or PDB snapshots may have seen the holo states; training data and cutoffs must be declared.
TMens, apo-TM and holo-TM move together; reporting only the one that improved hides a regression, so all are required.
Sampling budget changes the max-over-samples metrics; 20 conformations per protein is the published protocol. Papers using 5 samples or EigenFold's 90-pair splits/apo.csv are not on the same footing.
There is no official ProteinBench evaluation repo (github.com/bytedance/ProteinBench returns 404 as of 2026-10-30); use the ConfDiff apo scorer and state its commit.
A benchmark gain on 91 pairs is not evidence about any particular protein's mechanism; claims must stop at the benchmark.

targets.name: Automated cryo-EM model building: raise completeness above ModelAngelo's 77% on its 177-map held-out set
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (GPU; 177 maps, hundreds of GB of EMDB downloads)
targets.statement: ModelAngelo (Kiarash Jamali, Lukas Käll, Rui Zhang, Alan Brown, Dari Kimanius and Sjors Scheres; Nature 628:450-457, 2024, open access as PMC11006616) set the current bar for automated model building into cryo-EM maps. Its held-out test set is 177 protein-containing structures at 4 A resolution or better, released between the 1 April 2022 training cut-off and 9 February 2023. Structures above 30,000 residues and icosahedral viruses were excluded, as were structures with a chain above 10 percent identity to a training chain. The EMDB/PDB list is published as Supplementary Information, and ModelAngelo's built models are on Figshare (10.6084/m9.figshare.25218434). After one standard Servalcat refinement cycle, ModelAngelo built 77 percent of the 410,585 residues, or 85 percent after excluding the 51,446 residues whose deposited Q-score is below 0.4. Completeness here means the fraction of deposited residues whose Ca lies within 3 A of the built model with the correct amino acid. On a 27-structure subset, DeepTracer, the best alternative, reaches about 80 percent only at 2.5-3 A local resolution, against ModelAngelo's roughly 80 percent at 3.5-4 A; Phenix, Buccaneer and Demo-EM are considerably lower. Nucleic acids are much weaker: on ribosomes at 1.98-3.80 A, completeness with correct base identity falls from about 80 percent in the best regions to roughly 20 percent in the worst, and the paper gives no aggregate figure. Maps and depositions are public in EMDB and the PDB. Later preprints claim improvements: CryFold (B. Su, K. Huang, Z. Peng, A. Amunts and J. Yang; bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.11.13.623164, several versions) benchmarks on the same 177 maps and reports more complete models than ModelAngelo. EM3DFold (bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.09.16.752067) and CryoZeta (2026) use other benchmark sets. Any of these may already move the bar, so the novelty check must settle their figures on this list before any claim.
targets.success_criterion: An automated pipeline that, given only the released map and the sequences of the chains present, builds models for every entry of the 177-structure test list in the ModelAngelo supplementary information. The skeptic computes completeness with a published script implementing the paper's definition: the fraction of all deposited protein residues whose Ca lies within 3 A of the built model with the correct residue identity, pooled over residues, with failed entries counted as zero. That completeness must be STRICTLY HIGHER (direction: max) by at least 2 percentage points than the published value: 77 percent over all 410,585 residues, or 85 percent on the Q-score >= 0.4 subset (Nature 628:450-457, re-fetched live immediately before claiming). It must also be higher than any later published value on the same list and definition found by the novelty check, including CryFold's. The run must have no human intervention per map (one fixed configuration for the whole list, published) and must not use the deposited coordinates of a test entry at any stage. Declared training data must exclude every test entry and every chain above 10 percent sequence identity to a test chain. Built models, configs, the per-entry completeness table and runtimes must be published.

partial_wins.statement: On the 177-structure list, completeness strictly above 77 percent by at least 2 points on the full residue count, or strictly above 85 percent by at least 2 points on the Q-score >= 0.4 subset, with both numbers reported.

On a list of at least 10 EMDB ribosome maps at 1.9-4.0 A released after 1 April 2022 (ModelAngelo's training cut-off), declared and published before any building, nucleotide completeness with correct base identity must be strictly higher by at least 5 percentage points than the attacker's own re-run of the released ModelAngelo weights on the same maps under one fixed configuration. Completeness is computed over all deposited nucleotides as the fraction whose P atom lies within 3 A of a built nucleotide with the correct base, as in the paper's Extended Data Table 2. Both per-map tables and both sets of built models must be published.

A reproduction artefact: reproducing ModelAngelo's published completeness within 2 points on at least 30 entries of the test list with the released weights, publishing the end-to-end harness (map download, build, refinement, score) and the per-entry table.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic takes the test list from the paper's supplementary information, downloads the maps from EMDB and the deposited models from the PDB, runs a published completeness script on the attacker's built models (Ca/C1' within 3 A plus identity match), checks every entry of the list is covered with failures counted as zero completeness, verifies one fixed configuration was used for all entries and that no deposited coordinates of a test entry were inputs, and audits declared training data against the test list with a 10 percent identity search. Days of download and compute; the model building is the attacker's cost.
angles: The residues ModelAngelo misses concentrate at low local resolution and low Q-score; an explicit local-resolution-aware decision rule (build, or build backbone-only, or abstain) targets the reported 51,446 low-Q residues.
Nucleic acids are the open flank: base identity is where completeness collapses, and a dedicated base-type classifier conditioned on sugar-phosphate geometry is a narrow, checkable improvement.

Cross-domain import (sequence alignment): treat built fragments as noisy reads and assign them to sequences with a profile HMM over fragment-derived residue posteriors, the trick that makes identification work, then re-thread using the assignment.
Iterate build-refine-rebuild with an open refinement program rather than one forward pass; refinement improves local map agreement and lets a second pass extend chains.
Report completeness per local-resolution bin, since a gain limited to the best bins is not a gain on the headline number.
pitfalls: The deposited models are public, so pipelines that read them (even for masking, chain assignment or stopping) are leaking; the per-entry audit must show map and sequence inputs only.
Per-map manual intervention is not an automated result: one fixed configuration must run the whole list, which is also what makes the comparison fair.

Completeness definitions differ (Ca within 3 A with or without identity, residue vs atom counts, per-map mean vs pooled residues); the paper's definition and the exact test list must be used, with the script published.
ModelAngelo's 77 percent is after one Servalcat refinement cycle; compare refined with refined, or report both.
CryFold's figures on the same 177 maps could not be read on 2026-10-30 (bioRxiv rate-limit block); a claim that has not settled CryFold's number on this list and definition is not a claim.

The paper's alternative-tool numbers come from Extended Data tables that are images in the full text, so the published comparison values must be read from the article's tables or supplementary files before any head-to-head claim.
Averaging over entries instead of over residues changes the number; the published 77 percent is over all 410,585 residues.

targets.name: Quantum-corrected Lennard-Jones clusters (Xe, Ar, Ne with harmonic zero-point energy): lower a global minimum in the Calvo-Doye-Wales table (N < 100)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: The Cambridge Cluster Database hosts the table of Florent Calvo, Jonathan Doye and David Wales (J. Chem. Phys. 114, 7312, 2001; page dated 12/12/2000) for the 36 sizes N in 17..98 where quantum delocalisation changes the global minimum of LJ_N. Each row is a classical LJ minimum with its energy E_LJ and E_Xe, E_Ar, E_Ne (5 decimals, reduced units): the classical energy plus the harmonic zero-point energy at that minimum (no re-optimisation). A check on 2026-10-30 found that, on 27 posted point files that match their rows, E_sp = E_LJ + (q/2) * sum_i sqrt(lambda_i) reproduces all four columns to 1.1e-4 or better (to 3e-5 for every row except 44B). Here E_LJ = 4 sum (r^-12 - r^-6), the lambda_i are the 3N-6 nonzero eigenvalues of the analytic Hessian of that E_LJ (unit masses), and q is the de Boer parameter hbar/(sigma sqrt(m epsilon)): 0.01 (Xe), 0.03 (Ar) or 0.095 (Ne). Examples of the bar: N = 38 Ne -107.42431 (38B, C1, beating the classical Oh 38A at -106.47765); N = 98 Ne -349.46688 (98B, Cs). The candidate sets were drawn from low-lying LJ minima known in 2000. For Ne, open low-frequency structures win, and no later re-search of this table with a ZPE-aware objective is posted on the CCD. The classical LJ global minima are a separate entry (lennard-jones-ccd-doye-table).
targets.success_criterion: Coordinates ( > = 12 digits) of N atoms, for an N with rows on the live table (https://www-wales.ch.cam.ac.uk/~florent/LJZPE/table.html, re-fetched immediately before claiming), that form a certified local minimum of the classical E_LJ = 4 sum (r^-12 - r^-6): gradient norm < 1e-9, analytic Hessian of that E_LJ with exactly 6 eigenvalues of magnitude < 1e-6 and none below -1e-6. In addition, E_sp = E_LJ + (q/2) sum sqrt(lambda_i) over the 3N-6 nonzero eigenvalues, with q = 0.01 (Xe), 0.03 (Ar) or 0.095 (Ne), must be STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) by at least 5e-4 than the lowest tabulated value in that species' column for that N (minimum over the A/B/C rows), and lower by at least 5e-4 than any published harmonic-ZPE value for the same N and q that the skeptic finds. The checker must first reproduce the table rows 17A, 31B, 38A and 38B from their posted point files to 5e-5 with the same code. Structures re-optimised on the quantum-corrected surface do not count: the convention is a classical minimum plus its harmonic ZPE.

partial_wins.statement: For a size N in 13..99 that has no rows in the table (the table implies the classical global minimum stays lowest for all three species), a certified classical LJ local minimum whose E_Ne (q = 0.095) is lower by at least 5e-4 than E_Ne of the CCD/Doye classical global-minimum point file for that N evaluated with the same rule.

For a size N in 100..150, beyond the table, a certified classical LJ local minimum whose E_Ne (q = 0.095) is lower by at least 5e-4 than E_Ne of the CCD classical global-minimum point file for that N (a literature frontier, not a table record).

targets.verification_method: Python checker (minutes): parse the live table; evaluate E_LJ, the analytic gradient and the Hessian in double precision (mpmath for the final energy); polish with BFGS or Newton; take the eigenvalues; drop the 6 zero modes; apply the ZPE rule; calibrate on rows 17A, 31B, 38A and 38B (http://www-wales.ch.cam.ac.uk/~florent/LJZPE/points/ < label > ); compare with the minimum of the tabulated column for N; for p1 and p2, evaluate the classical GM point file from https://doye.chem.ox.ac.uk/jon/structures/LJ.html (LJ.tar) or the LJ310+ pages the same way.
angles: Ne at q = 0.095 rewards low-frequency, less compact minima: enumerate many low-lying LJ_N minima (basin-hopping or a disconnectivity database) and rank them by E_LJ + ZPE, not by E_LJ alone.
Run basin-hopping on the objective E_LJ + ZPE(local minimum), quenching on the classical surface at each step, so the search is ZPE-aware while the convention is kept.
For p1, scan sizes next to listed ones (e.g. 39-43, 58-64, 94-97), where the table's authors may have stopped.
pitfalls: Several posted point files do not match their rows (checked 2026-10-30): 67B, 75B, 77C, 78B, 82B, 83B, 84B and 86B evaluate to E_LJ values other than the tabulated ones (e.g. 82B gives -439.48103 against the row's -440.04139). The tabulated number, not the file, is the bar.
Point files for 65A-C, 69A-B, 79A-B, 85A-B and 87A to 93B return 404 (2026-10-30); the tabulated values still stand.

Factor-of-sqrt-2 trap: the rule is (q/2) sum sqrt(lambda) with the Hessian of 4 sum (r^-12 - r^-6). A gradient or Hessian that double-counts pairs is twice too large and then seems to need q/(2 sqrt 2); an earlier draft of this entry made exactly that error. Always calibrate on 17A, 31B, 38A and 38B first.
Row 44B is reproduced only to 1.1e-4 even with an analytic Hessian; use rows that reproduce to 5e-5 for calibration.
Emailing the CCD maintainers is an outbound message for the human, never for the agent.

targets.name: Fullerene isomer counts: the number of fullerenes (OEIS A007894) or IPR fullerenes (A046880) with 402 carbon atoms or more
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days via the published oriented-count formula plus a symmetry-restricted count of the (under a million) achiral C402 fullerenes; needs cluster for brute-force generation (about 1.3e11 fullerenes, 2.6e11 oriented, at C400 alone)
targets.statement: A fullerene C_2n is a cubic plane graph whose faces are pentagons and hexagons; IPR fullerenes have no two adjacent pentagons. In A007894 and A046880 enantiomers are counted once. Gunnar Brinkmann, Jan Goedgebeur and Brendan McKay counted all fullerenes up to 400 vertices with buckygen (J. Chem. Inf. Model. 52, 2910, 2012; arXiv:1207.7010). Goedgebeur and McKay counted all IPR fullerenes up to 400 vertices with a recursive IPR generator (J. Math. Chem. 53, 1702, 2015; arXiv:1501.02680). Goedgebeur's OEIS b-files end at n = 200 (C400): A007894(200) = 132,247,999,328 and A046880(200) = 40,286,153,024. The A007894 page notes that a(10)..a(190) were confirmed independently by buckygen and fullgen, while a(191)..a(200) come from buckygen only. The counting picture changed with Philip Engel and Peter Smillie, with an appendix by Goedgebeur (Exact enumeration of fullerenes, Duke Math. J. 174, 575-613, 2025; arXiv:2304.01655). Building on Thurston's Eisenstein-lattice parametrisation, they give an exact formula, a linear combination of Eisenstein series, for the number of ORIENTED fullerenes (mirror images counted separately, OEIS A057210) at every n; for example, there are 1,203,397,779,055,806,181,762,759 oriented fullerenes with 10,000 vertices. The coefficients were fixed by solving a linear system with the first 200 oriented counts from a buckygen run (about 3 CPU years). The authors leave unoriented counts to future work, and the formula does not cover IPR fullerenes. Since A007894(n) = (A057210(n) + achiral(n))/2, where achiral(n) is the number of fullerenes with an orientation-reversing automorphism (839,622 at C400, from the two b-files), A007894(201) now reduces to two steps: evaluate the published formula at n = 201 and count under a million achiral C402 fullerenes. That replaces generating about 1.3e11 fullerenes. No term beyond 400 vertices appears on A007894 (last edited 2026-06-28), A046880 (2025-11-05), A057210 (b-file to n = 200, edited 2026-08-08) or the buckygen page (last updated 2012), checked 2026-10-30.
targets.success_criterion: The exact value A007894(201) (fullerenes C402) or A046880(201) (IPR fullerenes C402), or a later term, with released code and per-size counts for every n from the sequence offset up to the claimed index. The released counts must equal the live b-file exactly for every n <= 200, re-fetched immediately before claiming; the generation or counting run must reproduce them, not copy them. The new term must be confirmed by an independent computation: either a second implementation of a different algorithm, or a skeptic re-run of the same code split into residue classes on separate machines, agreeing exactly. A claim that uses the Engel-Goedgebeur-Smillie oriented-count formula has three further requirements. The skeptic must evaluate that formula independently from the published paper at every n used. The formula values must reproduce the A057210 b-file for n <= 200. The achiral count at the new size must be confirmed as above. A value of A057210 alone is not a win, since the published formula already determines it. The term must be absent from the live OEIS entry and from the literature the skeptic finds (direction: first to report).

partial_wins.statement: Independent confirmation of A007894(191)..A007894(200) (all ten values, exactly matching the b-file) by a program that does not share code with buckygen and does not rely on buckygen-derived counts. The oriented-count formula was fitted to buckygen output, so formula-based values do not count as independent here.

The exact number of achiral fullerenes (those with an orientation-reversing automorphism, equal to 2*A007894(n) - A057210(n)) for every n from 10 to 200. It must be computed by a released method that does not generate all fullerenes, must match the two b-files exactly, and must finish within 24 hours when the skeptic re-runs it on one laptop.

targets.verification_method: Diff the claimed per-size table against https://oeis.org/A007894/b007894.txt and https://oeis.org/A046880/b046880.txt; rerun the released code on a few sizes (n <= 60) and on a random subset of residue classes at the new size; for a generation-based claim, check canonical-form deduplication on a sample with an independent graph-isomorphism tool (e.g. nauty) and check face sizes (12 pentagons) and the IPR condition.
pitfalls: Index n is half the vertex count (A007894 offset 10 means C20); A046880 starts at n = 30 (C60).
Enantiomorphic pairs count as one in A007894 and A046880; the Engel-Goedgebeur-Smillie formula counts them twice (A057210), so it must be combined with an achiral count, not used directly.
fullgen had a programming error for 136 vertices and more (found by the buckygen authors, since fixed); old fullgen output is not an independent check there.
The oriented-count formula's coefficients were solved from buckygen counts up to C400 (152 unknowns, 200 equations); it is strong evidence but not independent of buckygen for n <= 200.

An achiral-only generator must catch every orientation-reversing symmetry (mirror planes, inversion and improper rotations S4, S6, ...), not only mirror planes; check it against 2*A007894(n) - A057210(n) for all n <= 200 first.
A046880(191..200) may already have been checked by the 2015 IPR generator, which is a different algorithm; that is why p1 names A007894 only.

targets.name: JARVIS-Leaderboard QM9 (qm9_std_jctc, 130,829 molecules): beat ALIGNN's test MAE on one of 11 quantum-chemical properties (R2 excluded)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (CPU training of a graph network on about 100k small molecules; a GPU shortens this to hours)
targets.statement: JARVIS-Leaderboard (Kamal Choudhary and many co-authors, npj Comput. Mater. 10, 93, 2024) scores models on the QM9 set as the JARVIS dataset qm9_std_jctc. QM9 is from Raghunathan Ramakrishnan, Pavlo Dral, Matthias Rupp and Anatole von Lilienfeld (Sci. Data 1, 140022, 2014; DFT B3LYP/6-31G(2df,p) properties of 134k small organic molecules). Each property has a fixed 110,000/10,000/10,829 train/val/test id split inside the benchmark file. The benchmark targets are standardised: on 2026-10-30 the U0, R2, ZPVE, gap and mu train targets each had mean about 0 and standard deviation about 1. The MAEs below are therefore in units of each property's standard deviation, not eV; a constant predictor scores about 0.71-0.83 on the test set. On 2026-10-30 each of the 12 pages had a single entry, alignn_model (ALIGNN; Choudhary and Brian DeCost, npj Comput. Mater. 7, 185, 2021; submitted 01-14-2023). Its test MAEs: U0 0.0146, U 0.0138, H 0.0140, G 0.0133, HOMO 0.0187, LUMO 0.0175, gap 0.0345, ZPVE 0.0019, mu 0.0248, alpha 0.0557, R2 0.6523, Cv 0.0239. The R2 row (0.6523, against 0.713 for a constant train-median predictor) is a failed run rather than a bar, so R2 is excluded. QM9 records in the literature (a few meV for U0) were obtained on other splits and in physical units and are not comparable: the bar is this fixed split in the benchmark's own standardised units.
targets.success_criterion: For one property other than R2 (U0, U, H, G, HOMO, LUMO, gap, ZPVE, mu, alpha or Cv): predictions for every test id of the official benchmark (jarvis_leaderboard/benchmarks/AI/SinglePropertyPrediction/qm9_std_jctc_ < prop > .json.zip) from a model fitted only on that benchmark's train ids, with the val ids used only for early stopping and tuning. The test MAE recomputed by the skeptic against the benchmark targets must be STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) by at least 2% relative than the best entry on the live page for that property (re-fetched immediately before claiming). It must also be lower than any published MAE on the same JARVIS split that the skeptic finds. No pretraining or distillation on QM9 or on any dataset containing QM9 labels (for example models pretrained on QM9-derived sets). A skeptic retraining from the released script and seed must land within 3% of the claimed MAE and still below the bar.

partial_wins.statement: A full-win-quality result on one property from a model trained in at most 12 CPU-hours (no GPU), with the wall-clock log released.
One fixed architecture and hyperparameter set that meets the full-win criterion on all four thermochemical energies U0, U, H and G at once.
A re-run of the posted ALIGNN contribution (its run.sh and metadata.json) whose test MAE differs from the posted value by more than 10%, with all outputs saved (a reproduction audit).

targets.verification_method: pip install jarvis-leaderboard; load the benchmark json; check that the submitted csv covers exactly the test ids; recompute the MAE with the package's scoring; audit the training script for use of test ids or QM9-pretrained weights; retrain once from the seed. Hours on CPU.
pitfalls: Do not compare with QM9 numbers from other splits (e.g. 110k/10k/rest); only this benchmark's test ids count.
Unit conventions differ between QM9 releases (hartree vs eV, U0 with or without atomisation reference); fit to the benchmark file's targets, not to a re-downloaded QM9.
R2 is excluded: alignn_model's 0.6523 is barely below the 0.713 test MAE of predicting the train median for every molecule, so beating it says nothing.
The posted ALIGNN rows are single runs from one 2023 sweep and are far from QM9 state of the art, so the bars are soft; the 2% margin and the retrain check are what keep a win honest.
Submitting to the leaderboard is a GitHub pull request, an action for the human; the agent claims the verified local result only.

targets.name: JARVIS-Leaderboard catalysis adsorption energies (AGRA O, OH, CO, CHO, COOH and TinNet O, OH, N): beat the best listed test MAE
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: JARVIS-Leaderboard hosts eight DFT adsorption-energy tasks for heterogeneous catalysts. Five come from the AGRA dataset (Automatic Graph Representation Algorithm; Zachary Gariepy, ZhiWen Chen, Isaac Tamblyn, Chandra Veer Singh and Conrard Giresse Tetsassi Feugmo, APL Mach. Learn. 1, 036103, 2023; github.com/Feugmo-Group/AGRA). Three come from the TinNet dataset (Hongliang Xin group). Each task has a fixed split in its benchmark file (e.g. AGRA_O 800/100/100, AGRA_CO 155/19/19, tinnet_N 263/32/32). The best listed test MAEs (eV) on 2026-10-30 were: AGRA_O 0.0319 (dataset size 1,000), AGRA_OH 0.0241 (875), AGRA_CO 0.1082 (193), AGRA_CHO 0.0953 (214), AGRA_COOH 0.0383 (280), tinnet_O 0.2657 (745), tinnet_N 0.0871 (327, the plain alignn_model) and tinnet_OH 0.0843 (746). All but tinnet_N are by the problem-specific ALIGNN-atomwise models of the transferability study on Special/catalysis_mat. That study is Shih-Han Wang, Hongliang Xin, Luke Achenie and Kamal Choudhary, 'Examining generalizability of AI models for catalysis', J. Catal. 450, 116171 (2025); preprint chemRxiv 10.26434/chemrxiv-2024-hj733, posted 2024-09-25. The pages also list 'Out-...' rows, models trained on one dataset and scored on another, and zero-shot universal potentials (CHGNet, MACE, MATGL, ALIGNN-FF) with MAEs of about 2 to 44 eV. Neither kind is the bar to beat.
targets.success_criterion: For one of the eight tasks: predictions for every test id of the official benchmark json (AI/SinglePropertyPrediction/ < task > .json.zip) from a model fitted only on that task's train ids, with val ids used only for tuning. The test MAE recomputed by the skeptic must be STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than the lowest MAE on the live task page (re-fetched immediately before claiming) by at least 5% relative, because the test sets are small. The mean over 5 training seeds must also be below the bar. No pretraining on data that contains the task's source adsorption energies (e.g. Catalysis-Hub or OC20 records of the same systems) unless those systems are removed and the removal is shown. The result must also beat any published MAE on the same JARVIS split that the skeptic finds.

partial_wins.statement: One fixed architecture and hyperparameter set that meets the full-win criterion on three of the eight tasks.
A model trained on the union of the five AGRA train sets that meets the full-win criterion on two AGRA tasks (a multi-adsorbate model).

targets.verification_method: Install jarvis-leaderboard, load the task json, recompute the MAE from the submitted csv over the test ids, run the 5 seeds, and audit pretraining data for overlap. Minutes to an hour on CPU.
pitfalls: The page rows named 'Out-AI-SinglePropertyPrediction-ead- < other task > -test-mae' are cross-dataset transfer scores; the bar is the row trained on the same task (or alignn_model if lower).

The same-task 'Out-' rows (ALIGNN-atomwise, trained on the task's own split per their config.json) score exactly the benchmark test ids. They are 1.05 to 3.6 times lower than alignn_model on the same split (tinnet_OH 0.0843 vs 0.0882; AGRA_O 0.0319 vs 0.1134), except tinnet_N, where alignn_model is lower. Their protocol is described in J. Catal. 450, 116171 (2025) (not read on 2026-10-30). The bar is still the lowest row.
The 'Dataset size' column is the whole dataset; test sets are 19 to 100 structures, so read the split from the benchmark json.
Universal MLIP rows predict total energies, hence MAEs of several eV; do not mistake them for weak adsorption-energy baselines.
Submitting to the leaderboard is a GitHub pull request, an action for the human.

targets.name: SSUB experimental formation enthalpies on JARVIS-Leaderboard (1,726 compounds, composition only): beat ElemNet2-TL's test MAE of 0.0924
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: The JARVIS-Leaderboard task ssub_formula_energy asks for the experimental formation enthalpy of a compound from its formula alone. The data are 1,726 compounds from the SGTE substance database (SSUB, Scientific Group Thermodata Europe), with a fixed 1,381/345 train/test split in the benchmark file (no validation ids). On 2026-10-30 the page listed 11 entries (test MAE, eV/atom): ElemNet2_TL 0.0924 (Northwestern University; the ElemNet transfer-learning line of Dipendra Jha, Vishu Gupta, Ankit Agrawal and Alok Choudhary, pretrained on DFT formation energies), BRNet 0.1143, matminer_xgboost 0.1244 (UofT; the robustness study of Kangming Li, Brian DeCost, Kamal Choudhary, Michael Greenwood and Jason Hattrick-Simpers), BNet 0.1286, IRNet_EF 0.1319, matminer_lgbm 0.1441, matminer_rf 0.1468 (UofT), cfid_chem 0.1694 (JARVIS), ElemNet2_SC 0.2064, ElemNet1 0.2068 and element_fraction_desc 0.3807. The leader has stood since 01-14-2023. Experimental thermochemistry is the regime where DFT-trained models carry systematic errors, so modest data and careful transfer can matter more than model size.
targets.success_criterion: Predictions for every test id of the official benchmark (AI/SinglePropertyPrediction/ssub_formula_energy.json.zip) from a model fitted only on its train ids. The benchmark has no val ids, so all tuning and early stopping must use splits of the train ids only. Pretraining on DFT formation energies (OQMD, Materials Project, JARVIS-DFT, Alexandria) is allowed. Training on any other experimental formation-enthalpy compilation is allowed only after every test formula is removed from it. The test MAE recomputed by the skeptic must be STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than the best entry on the live page (re-fetched immediately before claiming) by at least 3% relative (at most 0.0896 against today's 0.0924). It must also be below every published MAE on this split that the skeptic finds, and the mean over 5 seeds must stay below the bar.

partial_wins.statement: Beat ElemNet2_TL under the full-win protocol using no external data at all (train ids only, no pretraining).
A closed-form or symbolic model with at most 50 fitted parameters whose test MAE beats matminer_xgboost (0.1244) under the same split and leakage rules.

targets.verification_method: Install jarvis-leaderboard; recompute the MAE from the csv over the test ids; grep the training pipeline for external experimental datasets and check formula overlap with the test set; rerun 5 seeds. Under an hour on CPU.
pitfalls: Formulas repeat across experimental compilations (and across polymorphs); dedupe by reduced formula before any external fine-tuning.
The page gives no units; the targets in the benchmark file are the reference, so check them before mixing in kJ/mol data.
Submitting to the leaderboard is a GitHub pull request, an action for the human.

targets.name: JARVIS-Leaderboard single-entry materials tasks: halide perovskites (5 properties), MXene formation energy and phonon DOS spectra: beat the only listed model
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: Seven JARVIS-Leaderboard materials tasks had exactly one entry on 2026-10-30. Five use the halide perovskite dataset of Arun Mannodi-Kanakkithodi (Purdue) and Maria Chan (Energy Environ. Sci. 2022, doi 10.1039/D1EE02971A): 229 compounds, split 183/46 train/test with no val ids, each scored by alignn_model (01-14-2023) on test MAE. The five values are HSE06 band gap 0.1615, PBE band gap 0.1223, HSE decomposition energy 0.0512, PBE decomposition energy 0.0477 and refractive index 0.0233. The sixth is mxene275_formation_energy, a 2D MXene set of 274 structures split 220/27/27; the page cites the C2DB update of Morten Gjerding and co-authors, 2D Mater. 2021, doi 10.1088/2053-1583/ac1059. Its only entry is mxene_alignn at 0.0561 (team MXene_ALIGNN, 06-12-2023). The seventh is edos_pdos_ph_dos, the total phonon density of states for 14,243 JARVIS-DFT materials (split 11,395/1,424/1,424; Ramya Gurunathan, Kamal Choudhary and Francesca Tavazza, Phys. Rev. Mater. 7, 023803, 2023), scored by multi-MAE, with alignn_model at 0.05773. Single-entry tasks have soft bars, but small test sets make noise a real risk, hence the seed and margin rules.
targets.success_criterion: For one of the seven tasks: predictions for every test id of the official benchmark json from a model fitted only on that task's train ids. Val ids, where the benchmark has them, are for tuning only; where it has none (the perovskite tasks), all tuning must use splits of the train ids. The metric (MAE, or multi-MAE for the phonon DOS, computed with the jarvis_leaderboard scoring code on the benchmark's test spectra) must be STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than the only entry on the live page (re-fetched immediately before claiming). The margin is at least 5% relative for the perovskite and MXene tasks and at least 2% for the phonon DOS. The mean over 5 seeds must also be below the bar. No pretraining on data containing the same compounds' labels at the same level of theory (for example the Mannodi perovskite set itself, C2DB labels of the MXenes, or JARVIS-DFT phonon DOS for the phonon task). The result must also beat any published value on the same split that the skeptic finds.

partial_wins.statement: One fixed model and hyperparameter set that meets the full-win criterion on three of the five halide perovskite tasks.
A composition-only model (no structure input) that meets the full-win criterion on the HSE06 band gap task.

targets.verification_method: Install jarvis-leaderboard; load each benchmark json; recompute the metric from the submitted csv with the package scorer; rerun 5 seeds; audit pretraining data. Minutes to hours on CPU.
pitfalls: The task slugs spell 'peroskites'; use the slug exactly when fetching the benchmark file.

The halide_peroskites_PBE_gap page description says 'decomposition energy' (copied from the decomp page), but its benchmark targets are PBE band gaps (0.53-5.25 eV on the test ids). Trust the benchmark json, not the page text.
The 'Dataset size' column is the whole set; perovskite and MXene test sets are only a few dozen compounds, so one outlier can move the MAE by more than 5%.
Phonon DOS multi-MAE depends on the binning and normalisation in the benchmark file; do not re-bin.
Submitting to the leaderboard is a GitHub pull request, an action for the human.

targets.name: Matbench v0.1 large tasks (mp_e_form, mp_gap, mp_is_metal): beat the best published Matbench-protocol score (JMP-L's 0.0101 eV/atom and 0.091 eV, CGCNN's 0.9520 balanced accuracy)
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (fine-tuning a pretrained model like JMP-L over 5 nested folds of 106k-133k structures takes GPU-days); the partial wins fit laptop-days on one GPU
targets.statement: Matbench v0.1 (Alexander Dunn, Qi Wang, Alex Ganose, Daniel Dopp and Anubhav Jain, npj Comput. Mater. 6, 138, 2020) has three large Materials Project tasks, each with fixed 5-fold nested cross-validation. The per-task leaderboards on 2026-10-30 read: matbench_mp_e_form (132,752 structures, formation energy), MAE 0.0170 +- 0.0003 eV/atom by coGN, then coNGN 0.0178, ALIGNN 0.0215 and SchNet (kgcnn) 0.0218; matbench_mp_gap (106,113 structures, PBE band gap), MAE 0.1559 +- 0.0017 eV by coGN, then DeeperGATGNN 0.1694, coNGN 0.1697 and ALIGNN 0.1861; matbench_mp_is_metal (106,113 structures), 0.9520 +- 0.0074 by CGCNN v2019 in the column labelled rocauc (which equals balanced accuracy, as the matbench pages note for thresholded predictions), then ALIGNN 0.9128 and coGN 0.9124. coGN and coNGN are the connectivity-optimised nested graph networks of Robin Ruff, Patrick Reiser, Jan Stuehmer and Pascal Friederich (kgcnn); CGCNN is by Tian Xie and Jeffrey Grossman. Lower Matbench-protocol scores have been published off the leaderboard. JMP (Nima Shoghi, Adeesh Kolluru, John Kitchin, Zachary Ulissi, Larry Zitnick and Brandon Wood, Meta FAIR and CMU, ICLR 2024, arXiv:2310.16802 Table 4) pretrains a GemNet-OC model on OC20, OC22, ANI-1x and Transition-1x (no Materials Project data) and fine-tunes it on each fold. JMP-L (235M parameters) reports 5-fold means of 10.1 meV/atom (0.0101 eV/atom) on mp_e_form and 0.091 eV on mp_gap; JMP-S reports 0.0133 and 0.121. CrysToGraph (Hongyi Wang, Sheng Gong and co-authors, arXiv:2407.16131 v2, Table 3) reports 0.0168 and 0.1522. Some lower scores build on potentials trained on MPtrj and fall under the leakage rule, so they do not set the bar: fine-tuned MatterSim (0.12 eV) and fine-tuned ORB (about 0.10 eV) on mp_gap, both quoted in HackNIP (arXiv:2506.18497), and DenseGNN-CHGNet (arXiv:2509.05712). No published non-leaking mp_is_metal score above CGCNN's was found (CrysToGraph 0.9146). The small and medium Matbench tasks are separate entries (matbench-small-data-tasks, matbench-medium-structure-tasks-cpu).
targets.success_criterion: For one of the three tasks: saved code and per-fold predictions that the skeptic re-runs with the official matbench package (MatbenchBenchmark v0.1, fixed folds, hyperparameters chosen only inside training folds). The mean score must be STRICTLY BETTER than both (a) the best entry on the live per-task leaderboard (re-fetched immediately before claiming) and (b) the best published Matbench-protocol score for that task from a model that obeys the leakage rule below. Today the binding bars are 0.0101 eV/atom for mp_e_form and 0.091 eV for mp_gap, both 5-fold means by JMP-L (arXiv:2310.16802 Table 4), lower mean MAE (direction: min). For mp_is_metal the bar is higher mean balanced accuracy of predictions thresholded at 0.5 (direction: max), which is the quantity the page's existing 'rocauc' values actually report (CGCNN v2019 0.9520). The margin must exceed the larger of 1% relative and a fold standard deviation: the bar-holder's where one is published, otherwise the claim's own. No model or pretraining whose training data includes Materials Project calculations of the test structures. That rules out off-the-shelf universal potentials trained on MPtrj, MP-ALOE, Alexandria or OMat24 unless test structures are provably excluded. The claim must also beat every other non-leaking Matbench-protocol score for that task that the skeptic finds published.

partial_wins.statement: Beat ALIGNN's per-task score on mp_gap (0.1861) or mp_e_form (0.0215) under the full protocol with a model trained on CPU only, with wall-clock logs.
Beat ALIGNN, the second-best entry on mp_is_metal (mean balanced accuracy 0.9128 at a 0.5 threshold), under the full protocol with any structure-based model, a step towards CGCNN's 0.9520.
Beat coGN's leaderboard score on mp_e_form (0.0170) or mp_gap (0.1559) by the full-win margin under the full protocol with a model that uses no pretraining and no external data of any kind.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic installs matbench, reruns the saved script for one fold to confirm the score, recomputes the task metric from all saved per-fold predictions, compares with the live per-task page and audits the training data for MP leakage. GPU-hours.
pitfalls: Universal interatomic potentials and foundation models trained on MP-derived data have seen the test labels; such scores do not count.
The binding bars for mp_e_form and mp_gap are published scores (JMP-L) that are not on the per-task page. Search papers citing JMP and Matbench for newer non-leaking scores before claiming.

For mp_is_metal the page's existing 'rocauc' values are balanced accuracy of 0.5-thresholded predictions. The page says scoring is fixed for future submissions, so a new leaderboard score may be a true ROC-AUC that is not comparable; compare balanced accuracy only.
Submitting to the leaderboard is a GitHub pull request, an action for the human.

targets.name: CHIPS-FF on JARVIS-Leaderboard: a universal force field with lower MAE than all 16 listed for vacancy energy, surface energy, C11, bulk modulus or formation energy (104 materials)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to evaluate an existing open model; needs cluster to train a new one
targets.statement: CHIPS-FF (Daniel Wines and Kamal Choudhary, ACS Materials Lett. 2025, doi 10.1021/acsmaterialslett.5c00093; github.com/usnistgov/chipsff) evaluates universal machine-learning force fields with fixed workflows (relaxation, vacancy and surface energies, elastic constants) against JARVIS-DFT OptB88vdW values for 104 materials common in semiconductor devices. The JARVIS-Leaderboard pages (16 models each, all dated 3-11-2025) list these best MAEs: vacancy formation energy 0.357 eV (eqV2_31M_omat_mp_salex; 48 entries); surface energy 0.1564 J/m^2 (eqV2_31M_omat_mp_salex; 85); C11 31.81 GPa (MatterSim); bulk modulus Kv 77.99 GPa (mace-alexandria); formation energy 0.0756 eV/atom (eqV2_86M_omat). Lattice constant a (0.0111) and volume (0.4171) are led by alignn_ff, which is trained on JARVIS-DFT itself. Other evaluated models include orb-v2, orb-d3-v2, mace-mpa, mace, sevennet, chgnet and matgl. Models released after March 2025 do not appear yet.
targets.success_criterion: For one of vac_en, surf_en, c11, kv or form_en: per-material predictions for the benchmark's full material list, produced by the chipsff workflow with default settings and an openly released force field (weights public). The MAE recomputed by the skeptic against the benchmark json must be STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than the best entry on the live task page (re-fetched immediately before claiming) by at least 5% relative. The force field must not be trained or fine-tuned on JARVIS-DFT calculations of any of the 104 benchmark materials, or of their vacancy or surface supercells. The result must beat any CHIPS-FF value for that property that the skeptic finds published. A new model trained by the agent, rather than a newer third-party model, should be stated as such.

partial_wins.statement: Any openly released force field that is not yet on the leaderboard and meets the full-win criterion on one property (credit goes to the model's authors; the claim is the verified evaluation).

An analysis of the Kv task showing, with per-material outputs, that a stated subset of at most 5 materials accounts for more than half of the best listed model's MAE, plus a corrected workflow setting that lowers that model's MAE by 20% or more without changing its weights.

targets.verification_method: Install chipsff and jarvis-leaderboard; rerun the workflow for the claimed property with the named weights; recompute the MAE from the per-material csv against the benchmark json; check the model card's training data for JARVIS-DFT. Hours on CPU.
pitfalls: JARVIS-DFT uses OptB88vdW while most universal potentials are trained on PBE(+U) data: part of the error is a functional mismatch, so a model trained on PBE has a floor.
Kv MAEs of 78-136 GPa for every model suggest a few failed relaxations or fits dominate; inspect per-material outputs before tuning.
The task lists hold different numbers of materials (e.g. 48 for vacancies, 85 for surfaces); score the benchmark's list, not all 104.

Several leading checkpoints (fairchem eqV2 OMat24 models, UMA) are gated on Hugging Face behind a licence agreement. Accepting it is an action for the human, and the claim should say whether the weights it used need such a step.
Submitting to the leaderboard is a GitHub pull request, an action for the human.

targets.name: On Cloud N (Sentinel-2 cloud cover challenge): beat the winning 0.8974 Jaccard on the released private test split
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (about 11.7k training and 11k test 512x512 four-band Sentinel-2 chips, tens of GB; U-Net/SegFormer training on one GPU or Apple-silicon for 1-3 days)
targets.statement: The 'On Cloud N: Cloud Cover Detection Challenge' (DrivenData competition 83, Dec 2021-Feb 2022, 848 participants; Radiant Earth Foundation with Microsoft AI for Earth) asked for a per-pixel cloud mask for each 512x512 Sentinel-2 L2A chip (bands B02, B03, B04, B08; extra bands from the Planetary Computer allowed). The score is the Jaccard index summed over all pixels in the scoring set (total intersection / total union, not a per-chip mean). Final private scores: 0.8974 (adityakumarsinha), 0.8972 (Team IG NB: XCZhou, cloud_killer, Sunyueming, mymoon, windandcloud), 0.8961 (Victor). Their public scores were 0.8988, 0.8986 and 0.83975. Radiant Earth released the full dataset under CC-BY-4.0 on Source Cooperative (radiantearth/cloud-cover-detection-challenge/final). It includes private/test_features and private/test_labels for all 10,980 test chips, plus private/pub_sub_idx.csv, which marks each chip as public (5,490) or private (5,490). So the official private score can be recomputed offline. Labels went through expert validation before release; label value 255 means nodata. The 1st-place code (U-Net EfficientNet-B1 and SegFormer-B1 fold ensembles) is public in drivendataorg/cloud-cover-winners, and its 1st-place README links the final weights in a public Google Drive folder (reachable on 2026-10-30). Open task: a private-split Jaccard strictly above 0.8974.
targets.success_criterion: Binary masks (uint8, 0/1, 512x512) for all 5,490 chips that private/pub_sub_idx.csv marks public == FALSE. They come from a model trained only on final/public/train_features and train_labels (11,748 chips), optionally with other Sentinel-2 bands of the same chips and dates from the Planetary Computer as the challenge rules allowed. Openly available pretrained backbones with no cloud labels (ImageNet or ADE20k weights, as the winners used) are allowed. No other cloud-labelled data that overlaps the test chips may be used, and the model and threshold are frozen before any test label is read. The skeptic computes the aggregate Jaccard on those chips (total intersection / total union over all pixels, excluding pixels whose label is 255). It must be STRICTLY HIGHER (direction: max), by at least 0.002, than the larger of (a) 0.8974, the 1st-place private score in the README at https://github.com/drivendataorg/cloud-cover-winners, re-fetched immediately before claiming, and (b) the skeptic's rescoring, with the same script and chips, of the 1st-place released ensemble (weights linked from that repository's 1st-place README), if those weights can still be downloaded. The released labels were expert-validated and may differ from those scored in 2022. It must also beat any private-split Jaccard on this dataset published since.

partial_wins.statement: Re-run the 1st-place released code and weights (linked from its README) on the 5,490 private chips. Publish the standalone scoring script, the 255 handling used, the per-chip intersection and union counts, and the resulting private-split Jaccard, so that the skeptic can reproduce that number to within 0.0005.
Private-split Jaccard >= 0.8961 (3rd place) with a single model (no ensemble), trained in under 24 hours on one laptop or consumer GPU.
Whole-test (all 10,980 chips) Jaccard strictly above the skeptic's whole-test rescoring of the 1st-place released ensemble.

targets.verification_method: The skeptic downloads test_labels and pub_sub_idx.csv by plain GET from data.source.coop/radiantearth/cloud-cover-detection-challenge/final/private/ and scores the claimed masks with a standalone numpy script (total I/U over private chips, 255 excluded). As a calibration, the skeptic re-scores the 1st-place released weights the same way, and audits the training code for any read of test_labels. Scoring takes minutes; re-running the 1st-place inference takes about an hour on a GPU.
angles: Conventional: larger modern encoders (ConvNeXt, EfficientNetV2, SegFormer-B3+) with multi-fold ensembling and flip/rotate test-time augmentation. The top three are separated by only 0.0013, so variance reduction matters.
Use the extra bands the rules allowed (B01, B05-B07, B8A, B09-B12 from the Planetary Computer). Cirrus-sensitive and SWIR bands separate thin cloud from bright ground better than RGB-NIR.
Cross-domain import (noisy-label learning): labels were crowd-drawn then expert-corrected. Use loss reweighting by label confidence, or co-teaching, and check fold-level disagreement maps.
Cross-domain import (medical image segmentation): boundary-aware losses (Lovasz-hinge, which directly optimises the Jaccard metric) and nnU-Net-style automatic configuration.
pitfalls: Score only the 5,490 private chips (pub_sub_idx public == FALSE) when comparing with 0.8974. Public-split or whole-test numbers are not like for like.
The metric is aggregate over pixels, not a per-chip mean. Per-chip mean IoU numbers in papers are a different metric.

Label value 255 is nodata in the released labels. The competition page says missing label values were set to 0 during scoring, so verify via p1 that your nodata handling reproduces the winner's score.
Tuning thresholds or choosing checkpoints on the released test labels is leakage. Use folds of the training set.
Margins between the top entries are around 0.001. Report several seeds.

targets.name: BioMassters (Finnish forest biomass from Sentinel-1/2 time series): beat the best published whole-test average RMSE (27.43, TESSERA) on the released test labels
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (about 216 GB of training and 73 GB of test features; the winning model trained 8 days on 2 A100 GPUs, though smaller models fit one GPU workstation)
targets.statement: The BioMassters challenge (DrivenData competition 99, Nov 2022-Jan 2023, 976 participants; Nascetti, Yadav, Brodt, Qu, Fan, Shendryk, Shah, Chung and Lipstein, NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks) asks for yearly peak above-ground biomass (AGB, Mg/ha) on a 10 m grid for each 2,560 m chip in Finnish forests. Inputs are 12 monthly Sentinel-1 (4 bands) and Sentinel-2 (11 bands including cloud probability) images. Labels are LiDAR-derived AGB maps calibrated with field plots (Finnish Forest Centre). The metric is per-chip RMSE averaged over the 2,773 test chips, with zero pixels included. Private scores: 27.628 (kbrodt: tf_efficientnetv2_l U-Net encoder shared over months, self-attention aggregation), 27.68 (Team Just4Fun: qqggg, HongweiFan; SWIN UNETR), 28.04 (yurithefury; UNet++ ensemble), 31.08 (MATLAB bonus, Team D_R_K_A: kaveh9877, AZK90). The full dataset, including test_agbm.tar (730 MB of test labels), is on Hugging Face (nascetti-a/BioMassters, CC-BY-4.0, not gated). The public/private split is not published, so the honest comparison is on the whole test set. The BioMassters paper (Table 2) gives whole-test scores for the top three: 27.49 (1st place, described there as a U-TAE adaptation), 27.53 (Swin UNETR) and 27.92 (U-Net++ ensemble). The Prithvi-EO-2.0 paper (Szwarcman et al., arXiv:2412.02732 v3, Table XIII) quotes the same 27.49; its own best (Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M, 12 Sentinel-2 frames, LoRA) is 33.40. The lowest whole-test value found is 27.43 by TESSERA (Zhengpeng Feng, Srinivasan Keshav, Anil Madhavapeddy and co-authors, Cambridge, arXiv:2506.20380 v7, Table 1c): a UNet on frozen TESSERA embeddings, which are computed from the authors' own Sentinel-1/2 retrieval at the chip coordinates rather than from the official features, scored as average per-patch RMSE on the 2,773 test patches. The BioMassters cells in PANGAEA and GEO-Bench-2 use reduced protocols and are not comparable. Open task: whole-test average RMSE strictly below 27.43.
targets.success_criterion: Predicted AGB GeoTIFFs (256x256, float) for all 2,773 test chips, with code and weights. The model is trained only on the official training features and train_agbm, with no test AGB used in training or model selection, and frozen before scoring. The skeptic computes RMSE per chip against test_agbm (all pixels, zeros included, as in the challenge metric) and averages over chips. The result must be STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than every one of: 27.43, TESSERA's whole-test average per-patch RMSE (arXiv:2506.20380 v7, Table 1c); 27.49, the winning model's whole-test RMSE in the BioMassters paper (NeurIPS 2023, Table 2) and in Prithvi-EO-2.0 (arXiv:2412.02732 v3, Table XIII); and 27.628, the 1st-place private score in the 1st-place README of https://github.com/drivendataorg/the-biomassters, re-fetched before claiming. It must also be lower than any whole-test value published since, on unclipped labels. If the 1st-place released weights (linked from its README) can still be downloaded, it must also be lower than the skeptic's whole-test rescoring of them.

partial_wins.statement: Whole-test average RMSE strictly below 27.92 (the 3rd-place U-Net++ ensemble's whole-test score in the BioMassters paper, Table 2) with a model trained in under 72 hours on a single consumer GPU.
Whole-test average RMSE strictly below 31.08 (MATLAB bonus winner) with no neural network, e.g. per-pixel gradient boosting on temporal composites.

targets.verification_method: The skeptic downloads test_agbm.tar from huggingface.co/datasets/nascetti-a/BioMassters, scores the claimed GeoTIFFs with a standalone numpy script implementing per-chip RMSE averaged over chips, and checks the file count (2,773) and shape. They audit the data loader for any test_agbm read, and re-run inference on a sample of chips from the released weights. Scoring takes minutes; inference takes hours, mostly I/O.
angles: Conventional: the winner's shared-encoder U-Net with month dropout. Swap in modern encoders, and add a temporal-attention decoder and test-time augmentation.
Use fewer, better inputs: cloud-free S2 median composites plus S1 statistics shrink 12x15 bands to a laptop-sized tensor (the 3rd-place team used 6 composites per year).
Cross-domain import (forestry allometry): predict canopy height first, then biomass through a learned allometric head. LiDAR-derived AGB is itself height-driven.
Cross-domain import (super-resolution): treat 10 m AGB as dense regression, with losses that penalise blur (gradient losses), since RMSE is dominated by high-biomass pixels.
pitfalls: The metric averages per-chip RMSE; it is not a pooled pixel RMSE. These differ substantially.
The challenge counts zero pixels whether they are true zero biomass or missing data. Do not mask them.

Private-split scores (27.628) and whole-test scores are not identical. The winner's whole-test figure is 27.49 (BioMassters paper, Table 2), and the best whole-test figure found is TESSERA's 27.43. Compare whole-test with whole-test.
TESSERA also reports figures with labels clipped at 500 t/ha (26.61, against 25.90 for the released winner weights). Clipped-label numbers are a different target and are not comparable.
RMSE numbers from PANGAEA, GEO-Bench-2 or Atomizer-style benchmarks use subsets, crops or normalised targets and are not comparable.
The data are very large (about 290 GB). Check the archive checksums, and do not let an incomplete download silently drop months.

targets.name: NASA/IBM HLS multi-temporal crop segmentation (US, CDL 2022): beat 55.1 mIoU (InstaGeo's fine-tuned Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M) on the official validation split
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (3,854 chips of 224x224x18 at 30 m; about 10.6 GB training and 1.2 GB validation archives)
targets.statement: The Multi-Temporal Crop Classification dataset (Cecil, Kordi, Li, Khallaghi and Alemohammad, 2023; NASA IMPACT, IBM and Clark University; Hugging Face ibm-nasa-geospatial/multi-temporal-crop-classification, CC-BY-4.0) has 3,854 Harmonized Landsat-Sentinel S30 chips from across the contiguous US in 2022. Each chip has three growing-season observations of 6 bands (18 channels). Labels are 13 USDA Cropland Data Layer classes (natural vegetation, forest, corn, soybeans, wetlands, developed/barren, open water, winter wheat, alfalfa, fallow/idle, cotton, sorghum, other), with 0 meaning no data. Chips are randomly split 80/20 into training (3,083) and validation (771), as listed in training_data.txt and validation_data.txt. The validation split is the evaluation split used to benchmark the Prithvi foundation models. The Prithvi-EO-2.0 paper (Szwarcman et al., arXiv:2412.02732 v3, Mar 2026, Table IX) reports mIoU: U-Net 42.6, Prithvi-EO-1.0-100M 42.7, Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M 48.6, Prithvi-EO-2.0-600M 50.7. InstaGeo (Yusuf, Houndayi, Oualha, Cherif, Panford-Quainoo and colleagues, InstaDeep; arXiv 2510.05617, Oct 2025) retrains on this benchmark with its own pipeline. Prithvi-EO-1.0-100M trained on the original chips reaches 48.07 (Table 1). Vanilla fine-tuned Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M reaches 55.10 (Table 2, from the replica experiments; InstaGeo's replica of this dataset reproduces the original within 0.2 points). Its headline 60.65 comes from an expanded 14,061-chip dataset with its own test split and is a different task. A better training recipe for a public encoder therefore already clears 50.7, so the bar that counts is 55.1. The small size makes this a laptop-scale crop-type mapping benchmark. Open task: strictly above 55.1 mIoU on the official validation chips.
targets.success_criterion: A trained model (code, config, weights, at least 3 seeds), trained only on the chips in training_data.txt, with any model selection done on a held-out subset of the training chips. No validation chip is used for training, early stopping or hyperparameter choice. The skeptic computes mIoU on all chips in validation_data.txt: per-class IoU from the dataset-level confusion matrix over the 13 classes, ignoring label 0, then the unweighted mean. The mean over seeds must be STRICTLY HIGHER (direction: max) than 55.1 (InstaGeo's vanilla fine-tuned Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M, arXiv 2510.05617 Table 2) by at least 0.5. It is then also above the 50.7 of Prithvi-EO-2.0-600M on this split. It must also beat any mIoU on this split published since (Prithvi-EO-2.0 v3 and InstaGeo checked on 2026-10-30; search papers using this dataset before claiming). Pretrained encoders are allowed if declared.

partial_wins.statement: Mean mIoU over 3 seeds strictly above 48.6 (Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M) with a model of under 50M parameters trained in under 12 laptop-hours.
Mean mIoU over 3 seeds strictly above 48.6 with no pretrained weights at all (from-scratch model), against the 42.6 U-Net baseline.
Mean mIoU over 3 seeds strictly above 51.2 (the 50.7 of Prithvi-EO-2.0-600M, the best value published on the official chips themselves, plus 0.5), under the same no-validation-tuning rule.

targets.verification_method: The skeptic downloads validation_chips.tgz and validation_data.txt from Hugging Face, re-runs inference from the released weights, and scores with a standalone confusion-matrix script (label 0 ignored), reporting per-class IoU. They also check the training file list against validation_data.txt for overlap. Under an hour.
angles: Conventional: temporal-attention segmentation (U-TAE or TSViT-style) that treats the 18 channels as 3 dates x 6 bands rather than one stacked image.
Fine-tune Prithvi-EO-2.0-600M or TerraMind with stronger decoders (UPerNet) and test-time augmentation. Freezing versus fine-tuning matters here.
Cross-domain import (agronomy): add crop-calendar features (NDVI and NDWI trajectories, phenology metrics) as extra channels. Corn, soybean and sorghum separate mainly by timing.
Cross-domain import (long-tail classification): logit adjustment or class-balanced losses for rare classes (sorghum, cotton, fallow), which dominate the mIoU gap.
pitfalls: There is no separate test split. The validation split is the benchmark, so any tuning on it invalidates the claim.

mIoU conventions differ (including or excluding class 0, per-image versus dataset-level IoU). State and use the convention above, and when comparing with 50.7, note any difference in the Prithvi config.
CDL labels are themselves model outputs with class-dependent errors. Small gains on noisy classes may be label noise.
Random 80/20 chip splits leave spatial autocorrelation between train and validation. Report results honestly, but do not claim generalisation beyond this split.

targets.name: iWildCam2020-WILDS camera-trap species ID: beat the leaderboard's best out-of-distribution test macro F1 (52.0, AutoFT)
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (one GPU for 1-3 days per replicate; ~11 GB of camera-trap images via the wilds package)
targets.statement: iWildCam2020-WILDS (Beery et al.; packaged by the WILDS team, Koh, Sagawa, Liang and colleagues) asks for species labels for camera-trap images. Models train on one set of camera locations and are tested on held-out locations (the OOD test split, released with labels in the wilds package). The official metric is macro F1 over classes on the OOD test split, averaged over random replicates, with model selection on the OOD validation split. The WILDS leaderboard (re-fetched 2026-10-30) lists these entries without unlabeled data: AutoFT, CLIP ViT-L/14@336 (Caroline Choi, Yoonho Lee, Annie Chen, Allan Zhou, Aditi Raghunathan, Chelsea Finn; 2024-01-28) 52.0 (0.4); FLYP (Sankalp Garg) 46.0; Model Soups (Mitchell Wortsman) 43.3; ERM CLIP ViT-L 41.4. The best entry that follows the default-model guidelines (no asterisk) is ABSGD, ResNet-50 (Qi Qi), at 33.0. With unlabeled data the top entry is Connect Later, ResNet-50 (Helen Qu), at 36.8. The newest entry is COSMO (2025-02-28, 32.3). In the literature, Dual Risk Minimization (Kaican Li, Weiyan Xie and colleagues, arXiv 2411.19757) reports 51.8 with CLIP ViT-L/14@336, just under AutoFT. No 2024-2026 arXiv abstract found on 2026-10-30 claims more than 52.0. Rare classes dominate macro F1, which is why macro F1 stays far below accuracy.
targets.success_criterion: Mean OOD test macro F1 (WILDS evaluator, dataset.eval on the iwildcam v2.0 'test' split) over at least 3 replicates with different seeds, each replicate selected by OOD validation macro F1 only. The mean must be STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the top 'without unlabeled data' iWildCam entry on https://wilds.stanford.edu/leaderboard/, re-fetched live immediately before claiming (52.0, AutoFT, on 2026-10-30), by at least 0.5 points. It must also beat any OOD test macro F1 for iWildCam2020-WILDS that the NOVELTY skeptic finds in a 2024-2026 paper (the highest known on 2026-10-30 is DRM's 51.8). Training uses only the iWildCam train split labels. Unlabeled WILDS splits are allowed, but such a claim is then compared against both tables. Pretrained weights are allowed if declared with their training corpora, but no corpus documented to contain WCS Camera Traps or iWildCam images may be used (LILA collections, MegaDetector and other detectors trained on LILA, biology foundation-model corpora that ingested them). Web-scale corpora without a public manifest, such as OpenAI CLIP's, are allowed, as they are for the leaderboard entries.
