Deliverables: code, configs, seeds, per-replicate saved test predictions and the WILDS eval output.

partial_wins.statement: With an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 and no extra pretraining data or auxiliary models, mean OOD test macro F1 over 3 replicates above 36.5. That is the best known such number: ERM w/ targeted augmentation (Irena Gao, asterisked) at 36.5, with DRM's ERM+LP-FT ResNet-50 baseline at 36.4 (arXiv 2411.19757 Table 12). ABSGD's 33.0 is the best entry that follows the guidelines, but it is already beaten.
With WILDS unlabeled data and a ResNet-50 backbone, mean OOD test macro F1 over 3 replicates above 36.8 (Connect Later).
With a CLIP ViT-B/16 or smaller backbone, mean OOD test macro F1 over 3 replicates above 46.0 (FLYP's ViT-L/14@336 entry).

targets.verification_method: The skeptic installs the pinned wilds version and downloads iwildcam v2.0. They load each replicate's saved OOD test predictions, recompute macro F1 with dataset.eval and check that the predictions cover every OOD test image. They re-train one replicate from the released config and confirm its score lands within 2 standard deviations. They audit that checkpoint selection used OOD validation only and that no declared pretraining corpus or auxiliary model (such as a camera-trap detector) is documented to contain iWildCam or WCS images. Finally they re-fetch the leaderboard and do the literature check.
angles: Robust fine-tuning of large vision-language models (WiSE-FT style weight interpolation, FLYP contrastive fine-tuning, learned objectives as in AutoFT, LLM-described core features as in DRM) with class-balanced losses aimed at macro F1.
Cross-domain import (long-tail recognition): logit adjustment and decoupled classifier re-training on frozen features, since macro F1 rewards rare classes.

Camera-trap specific: use the WILDS location and sequence metadata at train time only (sequence-consistent pseudo-labels, location-balanced sampling). MegaDetector crops are out: MegaDetector was trained on LILA camera-trap images, which the corpus rule excludes.
pitfalls: Using the ID validation split or the OOD test split for checkpoint or hyperparameter selection is leakage; WILDS prescribes OOD validation.
Asterisked entries deviate from the guidelines; a claim must state which deviations it uses.
Single-seed results are not comparable: the replicate std of iWildCam macro F1 is about 1 point.
Pretraining corpora scraped from LILA or GBIF can contain the WCS camera-trap images used for the test locations.

targets.name: NCEAS/disdat species distribution benchmark: beat the best published presence-absence AUC for presence-only models in six regions
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (disdat point data a few MB; optional OSF raster grids for spatial-context models)
targets.statement: The NCEAS benchmark (Elith et al. 2006) was released as the disdat R package and OSF node kwc4v by Elith, Graham, Valavi, Hijmans and the NCEAS working group (Biodiversity Informatics 15:69-80, 2020). It gives presence-only training records and background points for 225 anonymised species (birds, plants, bats, reptiles) in six regions (AWT, CAN, NSW, NZ, SA, SWI), plus independent presence-absence (PA) survey sites for evaluation. The standard score is AUC-ROC per species on the PA sites, averaged within each region and then across the six regions. Table 2 of the DeepMaxent paper (fetched 2026-10-30) collects the published values: Valavi et al. 2022 single-species models up to 0.723 (RF down-sampled, ensemble), Maxent with target-group background (Phillips et al. 2009) 0.760, the Zbinden et al. 2024 multi-species model 0.755. DeepMaxent with target-group background (Ryckewaert, Marcos, Botella, Servajean, Bonnet, Joly; arXiv 2412.19217v4, Jan 2026; Methods in Ecology and Evolution 2026, doi 10.1111/2041-210x.70262) has the best average, 0.768. The best region means in that table are AWT 0.732 (Maxent TGB), CAN 0.732, NSW 0.752, NZ 0.753 and SWI 0.850 (DeepMaxent TGB), and SA 0.815 (Zbinden). Doi, Osawa and Tsutsumida (tabfm-distribution repository, Oct 2026, paper submitted) benchmark TabPFN and TabICL under the Valavi protocol and release per-species result tables. Their best six-region average is 0.736 and their best median over the 217-species subset is 0.758. Their Table S2 leave-one-region-out fine-tuning arms, which use no PA data, reach NZ 0.759 and SA 0.820, so those are now the best known region means. Anand, Deneu and Radeloff (PNAS 2026) report a median per-species AUC of 0.774 for a CNN with augmentation on the environmental grids, over the 217 species with fewer than 1,000 presence records (ensemble 0.744 on that subset, 0.749 over all 225). A Google heterogeneous GNN (Harrell et al., arXiv 2503.11900) reports per-region values only in a figure. The Valavi paper page on Wiley returned 403 (BLOCKED) on 2026-10-30, so its numbers are taken from the DeepMaxent table.
targets.success_criterion: Saved per-species predictions at every disdat PA evaluation site for all 225 species, from models fitted only on the disdat presence-only and background data (and, optionally, the OSF environmental grids). Two conditions must both hold. First, the AUC-ROC averaged within each region and then across the six regions is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than 0.768 by at least 0.005. Second, the median per-species AUC-ROC over the 217 species with fewer than 1,000 presence records (the Anand et al. subset; the claim lists the species) is strictly greater than 0.774. Both values must also exceed any value for the same aggregation that the NOVELTY skeptic finds in a paper or released result table from the last 24 months. That includes the HGNN figure where it can be read and the tabfm-distribution results tables (checked 2026-10-30: 0.736 average, 0.758 median). The PA data must not be used for fitting, tuning, variable selection or model selection; tuning uses cross-validation within the presence-only data. NSW species are scored only on the evaluation sites of their own group, as disdat defines them.

partial_wins.statement: Average of the six region-mean AUCs strictly above 0.768 (DeepMaxent, target-group background), under the same no-PA-tuning rule, without the median condition.

One fixed configuration that beats the best known region mean in at least three of the six regions (AWT 0.732, CAN 0.732, NSW 0.752, NZ 0.759, SA 0.820, SWI 0.850; NZ and SA from the tabfm-distribution Table S2 fine-tuning arms), under the same no-PA-tuning rule.
A model using only the point covariates shipped in disdat (no rasters) whose median per-species AUC over the same 217-species subset is strictly above 0.774.

targets.verification_method: The skeptic installs disdat from CRAN and recomputes every per-species AUC from the saved predictions against the PA files (pROC or sklearn), then recomputes both aggregations. They re-run the fitting script for one region and check that the predictions agree. They read the code to confirm that the PA data are loaded only in the scoring step.
angles: Multi-species neural models with target-group background and Maxent-style losses (DeepMaxent), ensembled with down-sampled random forests.
Cross-domain import (survey statistics): treat presence-only data as a biased sample and model observer effort explicitly (thinned point processes) before predicting.
Spatial context from the OSF grids (patch CNNs, multi-scale summaries) for the median-AUC condition.
pitfalls: Several published ablation tables choose hyperparameters by PA test AUC; such numbers are not a fair bar, and such tuning disqualifies a claim.
Mean versus median per-species AUC, and region-average versus pooled average, give different numbers; the criterion fixes both.
Species counts differ between papers (225 vs 226; one NSW species with two records is usually dropped); state the species list.

targets.name: SAGE global species distribution benchmark: beat the best overall test AUROC (85.9, random forest) on sPlotOpen presence-absence plots
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (3.8 GB benchmark tar plus 10 GB of GBIF presence-only records; the paper's multi-species DeepSDM trains in about 17 GPU-minutes)
targets.statement: SAGE (Arens, van Tiel, Zbinden, Robert and colleagues; arXiv 2609.31082, Sept 2026; data on Zenodo 21297133, code at github.com/earens/sage-sdm-benchmark) is a sampling-aware global benchmark. Models are trained on GBIF presence-only records for 5,771 plant species and evaluated on sPlotOpen presence-absence vegetation plots. The plots are split 20% validation and 80% test, stratified so that each species keeps at least 20 test occurrences. The headline score is the mean per-species AUROC on the test plots, also reported in four quadrants of sampling effort (sparse/dense) by relative prevalence (infrequent/frequent). The paper's Table 2, mirrored on the SAGE results page (fetched 2026-10-30), lists overall AUROC as a mean over 5 seeds: RF 85.9, the tuned multi-species DeepSDM (+loss) 85.8, BRT 85.2, MaxEnt 84.5, GLM 84.0, GAM 83.8. The quadrant bests are sparse-infrequent 86.6 (RF), sparse-frequent 84.3 (RF), dense-infrequent 87.9 (DeepSDM) and dense-frequent 85.0 (RF). AUPRG values are in the paper's Appendix D.2. The maintainers add new models to the public table on request; the bank never submits.
targets.success_criterion: Per-species predictions on every SAGE test plot from a model trained only on the released SAGE training data (GBIF presence-only records, pseudo-absences and predictors from the Zenodo record), scored with the official SAGE evaluation code. Validation plots may be used for model selection; test plots never. The overall mean per-species test AUROC over 5 seeds must be STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the best overall AUROC on https://earens.github.io/sage/results.html, re-fetched live immediately before claiming (85.9 on 2026-10-30), by at least 0.2 points. No quadrant may fall more than 0.5 points below its best listed value. The score must also beat any overall SAGE test AUROC that the NOVELTY skeptic finds in a later paper. Deliverables: code, seeds, predictions and the species_metrics.csv that the official code writes.

partial_wins.statement: Beat the best listed value in any one of the four sampling-effort/prevalence quadrants by at least 0.3 points (5-seed mean) while keeping overall test AUROC at or above 85.5.

Overall test AUPRG strictly above 86.9 (Random Forest, the best overall value in the paper's Appendix D.2 Table 10), aggregated as SAGE does (median over species within each seed, then mean over 5 seeds, official code), with overall AUROC at or above 85.5.

targets.verification_method: The skeptic downloads the Zenodo record and checks SHA256SUMS. They recompute species_metrics.csv from the saved predictions with the official evaluation code, then recompute the overall and quadrant means. They re-run one seed and confirm from the code that test plots enter only the scoring step.
angles: Ensembles of the RF and the tuned DeepSDM, which win different quadrants.
Cross-domain import (recommender systems): treat species-by-site as an implicit-feedback matrix with exposure (sampling effort) modelling.
Effort-aware pseudo-absence weighting learned on the validation plots.
pitfalls: The validation and test plots come from the same sPlotOpen pool; tuning on test, or reporting the validation split as test, is invalid.
Using sPlotOpen plots (any split) as training presences or absences leaks the evaluation data.
GBIF snapshots change over time; train on the released record, not a fresh GBIF download.

targets.name: AnuraSet neotropical frog calls: beat the best published test macro F1 (60.8, Mixture of Mixups) for 42-species multi-label classification
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (11.4 GB zip of 93k 3-second clips; a 3M-parameter MobileNetV3 trains from scratch)
targets.statement: AnuraSet (Canas, Toro-Gomez, Sugai and colleagues, Scientific Data 10:771, 2023; Zenodo record 8342596, code at github.com/soundclim/anuraset) is 27 hours of passive-acoustic recordings from four Brazilian sites, annotated by herpetologists. The recordings are cut into 93,378 three-second windows, each labelled with the presence of any of 42 anuran species, and split into fixed train and test sets at recording level (about 2/3 and 1/3). The metric is macro F1 over the classes at threshold 0.5. The paper's best baseline is ResNet152 with macro F1 37.8 (frequent 68.4, common 56.8, rare 15.7). Moummad, Farrugia, Serizel, Froidevaux and Lostanlen (Mixture of Mixups, arXiv 2403.09598, EUSIPCO 2024; code at github.com/ilyassmoummad/Mix2) report 60.8 +/- 0.3 on the full 42-class task with a MobileNetV3-Large trained from scratch for 100 epochs (frequent 89.2, common 77.1, rare 51.8). Having no validation set, they did model validation on the test set, as the paper states, so 60.8 is an optimistic bar. Their reduced variants AnuraSet-36N (70.4) and AnuraSet-36 (74.2) drop classes and are separate tasks. An arXiv query on 2026-10-30 found no later paper reporting a higher full-task score. The iNatSounds paper reports AnuraSet mAP and mF1 (best mF1 37.0) only on the 25 species shared with iNatSounds, a different task.
targets.success_criterion: A model trained only on the official AnuraSet training split, evaluated on the official test split of the full 42-class task with the F1 computation behind the 60.8 figure: per-class F1 at threshold 0.5 (torchmetrics MultilabelF1Score, average=None), macro-averaged as in Mix2's val.py, which follows the AnuraSet baseline evaluate.py. Any validation set must be carved from training recordings, never from test. The mean over at least 3 seeds must be STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than 60.8 by at least 0.6 points (twice the reported std). It must also beat any full-task macro F1 that the NOVELTY skeptic finds in a paper from the last 24 months. External pretraining is allowed if declared and if its corpus excludes the AnuraSet source recordings. Deliverables: code, seeds, per-seed saved test predictions and evaluation output.

partial_wins.statement: Mean macro F1 over 3 seeds above 51.8 on the rare-species group (fewer than 5k samples) of the full task, with overall macro F1 of at least 60.0.
Full-task macro F1 above 60.8 (3-seed mean) with a model of at most 1M parameters.

targets.verification_method: The skeptic downloads the Zenodo zip and checks the split column. They recompute macro F1 from the saved per-window test probabilities with Mix2's val.py logic: torchmetrics MultilabelF1Score(num_labels=42, average=None, threshold=0.5), then the plain mean of all 42 per-class values, so classes with no test positives score 0. They re-train one seed and confirm the score lands within 1 point. They audit that no test recording was used for selection or pretraining.
angles: Pretrained bioacoustic encoders (Perch 2.0, BirdMAE, BEATs variants) fine-tuned with Mix2-style mixing.
Cross-domain import (multi-label text classification): per-class threshold calibration learned on a hold-out of training recordings, and asymmetric losses for rare labels.
pitfalls: The paper reports results without a validation set; picking the epoch or the threshold on test inflates scores.
Overlapping 3-second windows (1-second hop) mean a random window-level split leaks; split by recording.

Four classes occur only in train and two only in test. Mix2's val.py averages over all 42 classes, so the train-only classes score 0 and cap the attainable macro F1. Use the same rule, not a 38- or 36-class average.

Per-class thresholds tuned on held-out data can roughly double macro F1 (one public Perch-embedding repo reports 0.317 at 0.5 and 0.628 with tuned thresholds); such numbers are not comparable with the fixed-0.5 bar.

targets.name: iNatSounds 2024: beat the best published test mAP (65.4) for file-level species ID across 1,212 species of birds, frogs, insects and mammals
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (one GPU for 1-3 days; 133 GB of audio: 81 GB train, 25 GB val, 27 GB test on AWS Open Data)
targets.statement: The iNaturalist Sounds Dataset (Chasmai, Shepard, Maji, Van Horn; arXiv 2506.00343; data at github.com/visipedia/inat_sounds) has 230k recordings of 5,569 species from 27k recordists. It has fixed train (137,012 files), validation (45,698) and test (49,527 files, 1,212 evaluation species) splits, and the test labels are released. Evaluation is at file level. The primary metric is class-averaged mAP; class-averaged top-1, top-5 and mF1 are also reported. The paper's best test results are mAP 65.4 +/- 0.1 and mF1 67.9 (ViT-B/16, multi-label loss plus mean teacher). The best class-averaged top-1 is 53.6 without location (ViT-B/16) and 60.7 with a geo prior (ResNet-50). A later paper from the same group (Liu, Chasmai, Maji, Van Horn, arXiv 2605.14031, May 2026) reports test top-1 62.76 and top-5 82.58 by fine-tuning BirdMAE, but no mAP. An arXiv query on 2026-10-30 returned no other paper with iNatSounds test numbers.
targets.success_criterion: A model trained on the iNatSounds train split (validation split for selection only) that outputs one score per evaluation species for every test file, from audio alone (no location or date). Its class-averaged test mAP, computed with the authors' evaluation code (github.com/cvl-umass/iNatSounds) as a mean over at least 3 seeds, must be STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than 65.4 by at least 0.5 points. It must also beat any iNatSounds test mAP that the NOVELTY skeptic finds in a paper from the last 24 months. Pretrained weights are allowed if declared, but their training corpus must exclude iNaturalist audio observations (the source of the test files), or the claim must show by file hash or observation id that no test recording was seen. Deliverables: code, seeds, saved per-file test scores and the evaluation output.

partial_wins.statement: Audio-only class-averaged test top-1 above 62.76 and top-5 above 82.58 (3-seed mean), under the same leakage rules.
Test mF1 (per-class best threshold, as the paper defines it) above 67.9 with mAP of at least 65.0 (3-seed mean).

targets.verification_method: The skeptic downloads the test annotations (md5 5482f112f05db4ba8576ba425d95d6a7) and recomputes mAP, top-1/top-5 and mF1 from the saved per-file scores with the authors' code. They re-run inference for one seed on a random 2,000-file test subset and audit the pretraining corpora for iNaturalist audio.
angles: Fine-tune BirdMAE or other large bioacoustic encoders with the multi-label plus mean-teacher recipe that gave the best mAP.
Cross-domain import (fine-grained vision): hierarchical taxonomic losses and test-time augmentation over crops of long recordings.
pitfalls: Perch 2.0, AVEX, NatureLM-audio and similar encoders were trained on iNaturalist audio, which can include test recordings.
Geo-prior results are a separate track; do not mix them with audio-only numbers.
mF1 here picks the best threshold per species on test (optimistic); it is not a deployable threshold.

targets.name: BirdSet soundscapes: beat the best published class-mean AP (mean 0.440 over seven test sites) for multi-label bird detection
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (GPU days to train on Xeno-canto XCM/XCL; the seven test_5s splits total about 320k five-second segments)
targets.statement: BirdSet (Rauch, Schwinger, Wirth, Heinrich, Huseljic, Herde, Lange, Kahl, Sick, Tomforde and colleagues; ICLR 2025; HF dataset DBD-research-group/BirdSet) trains on focal Xeno-canto recordings and tests on strongly labelled passive-acoustic soundscapes from eight sites: POW (validation) and the test sites PER, NES, UHH, HSN, NBP, SSW and SNE. The metrics are class-mean average precision (cmAP), AUROC and top-1 on each test_5s split. The HF leaderboard results dataset was last updated 2024-09-30 (best mean cmAP 0.37). Perch 2.0 (van Merrienboer, Dumoulin, Hamer, Harrell, Burns, Denton; arXiv 2508.04665) tabulates the strongest published means, verified from the paper HTML on 2026-10-30: BirdMAE-L fine-tuned (Rauch, Heinrich, Moummad, Joly, Sick, Scholz; TMLR 2025) 0.440, Perch 2.0 0.431, Audio ProtoPNet-5 0.424 (0.423 in its Table 3). Audio-only per-site cmAP bests: PER 0.350 (BirdMAE-L FT as rounded in Perch 2.0; 34.64 in the Bird-MAE paper), NES 0.415 (BirdMAE-L FT, 41.50 in the Bird-MAE paper's Table 6; Perch 2.0 rounds it to 0.41), NBP 0.720 (BirdMAE-L FT as rounded in Perch 2.0; 71.69 in the Bird-MAE paper); HSN 0.555 (AudioProtoPNet-20 in Schwinger, McEwen, Kather, Heinrich, Rauch, Tomforde, arXiv 2511.08261, a class-frequency-weighted figure kept as a conservative bar; BirdMAE-L FT has 0.55 but was tuned on HSN); UHH 0.380 and SSW 0.469 (Perch 2.0 random); SNE 0.351 (Perch 2.0 phase I). The best mean AUROC is 0.908 and the best mean top-1 is 0.665 (both Perch 2.0 random). Adversarial training of AudioProtoPNet and ConvNeXt (arXiv 2507.13727) reaches mean cmAP 0.42 at best. FINCH (Ovanger, Harris, Keitt; arXiv 2602.03817) adds a metadata prior and reports UHH cmAP 0.536 on four sites only; this target is audio-only. AVEX (Miron et al., arXiv 2508.11845) and the 2026 attentive-probing study (arXiv 2605.10494) report lower BirdSet scores under probe protocols.
targets.success_criterion: Predictions on the seven BirdSet test_5s splits (PER, NES, UHH, HSN, NBP, SSW, SNE), computed from the audio alone (no recording location, date or other metadata at inference), scored with the birdset package's cmAP. The model's training data must contain none of the BirdSet test soundscape recordings or their source collections. The mean cmAP over the seven sites must be STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than 0.440 by at least 0.005. It must also beat any audio-only mean cmAP on the same seven splits that the NOVELTY skeptic finds in a paper or on the BirdSet leaderboard. Training data must be declared (BirdSet DT/MT/LT or other public focal recordings). POW may be used for selection. Deliverables: code, weights, per-segment test scores and the metric output.

partial_wins.statement: Beat the audio-only per-site cmAP best on at least one site by 0.01 or more (PER 0.350, NES 0.415, UHH 0.380, HSN 0.555, NBP 0.720, SSW 0.469, SNE 0.351), under the same data rules.
Audio-only mean AUROC over the seven sites above 0.908, or mean top-1 above 0.665, under the same data rules.

targets.verification_method: The skeptic loads the HF test_5s splits with the pinned birdset version and recomputes cmAP, AUROC and top-1 from the saved scores. They re-run inference on two sites and audit the training manifest against the test soundscape sources.
angles: Ensemble BirdMAE fine-tuning with Perch 2.0 prototype heads; they win different sites.
Cross-domain import (speech): soundscape-style augmentation that mixes focal clips with real background noise, plus pseudo-labelling of unlabelled passive-acoustic audio.
pitfalls: AVEX's training mix lists Sapsucker Woods soundscapes, the source of the SSW test site; models trained on such data are contaminated for that site.
cmAP ignores classes absent from a split; compare only against the package's implementation.
The HF leaderboard numbers are rounded to two decimals and older than the paper tables.

targets.name: BEANS animal-sound benchmark: beat the best published test score on one of seven freely downloadable animal classification or detection datasets
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days per dataset (about 300 GB for all BEANS data; frozen-encoder probes run on CPU)
targets.statement: BEANS (Hagiwara, Hoffman, Liu, Cusimano, Effenberger, Zacarian; arXiv 2210.12300; github.com/earthspecies/beans) fixes train/validation/test splits and metrics over public animal-sound datasets: accuracy for classification, mAP for detection. Best published test values, collected on 2026-10-30 from the Perch 2.0 tables (arXiv 2508.04665, which also tabulate AVES-Bio and BioLingual fine-tuning), the AVEX study (Miron, Robinson, Alizadeh and colleagues, arXiv 2508.11845), the OpenBEATs full fine-tuning table (Bharadwaj, Cornell, Choi, Fukayama, Shim, Deshmukh, Watanabe; arXiv 2507.14129, Table 6) and the BioMamba comparison (Tang and Baskiyar, arXiv 2512.03563). Classification accuracy: watkins 0.935 (AVEX sl-BEATS-bio probe), bats 0.815 (Perch 2.0 peak-select prototype probe), dogs 0.971 (BioLingual fine-tuned; BEATs iter 1 and Dasheng 1.2B fine-tuned tie in OpenBEATs). Detection mAP: dcase 0.495 (OpenBEATs-Large iter 1 fine-tuned), enabirds 0.764 (Perch 2.0 peak-select PP), hiceas 0.713 (BEATs iter 1 fine-tuned, as run in the OpenBEATs paper; AVES fine-tuned 0.683 in the BioMamba paper), gibbons 0.516 (Perch 2.0 peak-select PP). The best mean over these four detection sets is 0.581 (Perch 2.0 peak-select PP: 0.457, 0.764, 0.585, 0.516; the best OpenBEATs row has 0.549). NatureLM-audio and BioMamba's own model report lower values. The 2026 attentive-probing paper (arXiv 2605.10494) gives its results only in figures, and BEANS-Next (arXiv 2610.10663) uses new tasks. Some papers compute mAP differently from the BEANS repository, so every claim is recomputed with the repository code. cbi and rfcx are left out because their download needs a human to accept Kaggle competition terms; ESC-50, Speech Commands and HumBugDB are left out too.
targets.success_criterion: Pick one dataset D among watkins, bats, dogs, dcase, enabirds, hiceas and gibbons. The claim is a model trained only on D's BEANS train split (validation split for selection; declared pretraining allowed). Its test metric, computed with the BEANS repository's evaluation code as the mean over at least 3 seeds, must be STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the value listed above for D by at least 0.005. It must also beat any test value for D in the BEANS paper, AVES, BioLingual, NatureLM-audio, Perch 2.0, AVEX, OpenBEATs, BioMamba, or any other paper from the last 24 months that the NOVELTY skeptic finds. Pretraining corpora must not contain D's test recordings (for example Watkins or Xeno-canto items reused by BEANS). Deliverables: code, seeds, saved test predictions and evaluation logs.

partial_wins.statement: With a frozen public encoder and only a linear or prototype probe, beat the best frozen-probe value for some dataset D (the Perch 2.0 LP/PP or AVEX probe columns), even if a fine-tuned model holds the overall record.
One model whose mean mAP over the four detection datasets dcase, enabirds, hiceas and gibbons exceeds 0.581 (Perch 2.0 peak-select PP), recomputed with the BEANS code.

targets.verification_method: The skeptic runs the BEANS download and preprocessing scripts (MD5 checked) and recomputes D's metric from the saved predictions with the repository code. They re-train one seed and check the pretraining corpora against D's source recordings.
angles: Multi-layer probing of several frozen encoders, then stacking their predictions.
Cross-domain import (speaker verification): margin losses designed for individual identity, for the bats and dogs tasks (both identify individual animals).
pitfalls: AVEX's pretraining mix lists Watkins; a pretrained model that saw Watkins test recordings cannot make a watkins claim.
mAP implementations differ between papers; only the BEANS repository's computation counts.
Single-seed differences of 0.01 on small test sets (dogs, bats) are noise.

targets.name: FASD13 few-shot animal sound detection: beat DRASDIC's 5-shot event F1 averaged over the twelve animal datasets
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (about 16 GB of audio on Zenodo; inference-only methods run on CPU, larger models want a GPU)
targets.statement: FASD13 (Hoffman, Robinson, Miron, Baglione, Canestrari, Elias, Trapote, Effenberger, Cusimano, Hagiwara, Pietquin; arXiv 2503.00296; Zenodo 15843741; github.com/earthspecies/drasdic_api) is a public evaluation set for few-shot bioacoustic event detection: 13 datasets of 2-12 recordings each. A system sees the audio up to the 5th positive event and must predict the onsets and offsets of the remaining positive events. Scoring is F1 at IoU 0.3, following the DCASE few-shot protocol (Nolasco et al. 2023). Eleven datasets come from earlier studies (AnuraSet, Hawaiian birds, Hainan gibbon, humpback and right whales, katydids, marmosets, Powdermill birds, ruffed grouse, Rana sierrae) and two are new (carrion crow, jumping spider). The paper's per-dataset table (verified from the HTML on 2026-10-30) gives DRASDIC (116M parameters, trained on 8.8k hours of synthetic scenes) an average of 0.445 over all 13. This target uses the 12 animal datasets, leaving out GS (a gunshot set). Over those 12, DRASDIC's mean is 0.433, and the per-dataset bests over all listed models are AS 0.645, CC 0.341, HA 0.587, HG 0.242, HW 0.453, JS 0.302, KD 0.673, MS 0.831, PM 0.474, RG 0.732, RS 0.352 and RW 0.764. The ablation rows report only 13-dataset averages, the best being 0.457 (DRASDIC without pitch/time shifting), with no per-dataset breakdown, so their 12-dataset means are unknown but at most 0.4575 x 13 / 12 = 0.496. No later paper reporting FASD13 was found on arXiv on 2026-10-30.
targets.success_criterion: Predicted event lists for every file of the 12 animal datasets of FASD13 (AS, CC, HA, HG, HW, JS, KD, MS, PM, RG, RS, RW), produced under the 5-shot protocol: for each file, only audio and labels up to the end of its 5th positive event may be used. Scored with the DCASE few-shot evaluation code at IoU 0.3, the unweighted mean of per-dataset F1 must be STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than 0.496, the largest 12-dataset mean any published DRASDIC variant can have. It must also beat the 12-dataset mean of any model with published per-dataset FASD13 scores that the NOVELTY skeptic finds. No FASD13 audio may be used for training or tuning. Deliverables: code, weights, the prediction files for each of the 12 datasets and the scorer output.

partial_wins.statement: Beat the per-dataset best listed above on any one of the 12 datasets by at least 0.02 F1, under the same 5-shot rules.
A system with at most 10M parameters whose 12-dataset mean exceeds 0.395 (AVES+linear, 90M parameters).
A 12-dataset mean strictly above 0.443 (DRASDIC's 0.433 plus 0.01), under the same rules.

targets.verification_method: The skeptic downloads the Zenodo zips and runs the claimant's inference on a fresh copy, checking that no labelled support is read beyond the end of each file's 5th positive event. They rescore with the DCASE evaluation code and recompute the 12-dataset mean.
angles: Prompted foundation models (DRASDIC) combined with per-file transductive refinement on the query audio.
Cross-domain import (keyword spotting): query-by-example with dynamic time warping on learned embeddings, tuned only on the DCASE training/validation sets.
pitfalls: Unlabelled query audio may be used; ground-truth labels after the 5th positive event may not, so test-time label propagation that reads them is leakage.
The DCASE validation sets share species with some FASD13 sources; declare all training data.
Several FASD13 datasets have only 2-4 files, so per-dataset F1 is noisy.

targets.name: SatBird USA-summer bird encounter rates: one model that beats every published test metric (top-10, top-30, top-k, MAE, MSE)
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (GPU days for Sentinel-2 patch models; tabular or embedding models run on a laptop)
targets.statement: SatBird (Teng, Elmustafa, Akera, Bengio, Radi Abdelwahed, Larochelle, Rolnick; NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks; data at satbird.github.io, code at github.com/RolnickLab/SatBird) asks for encounter rates of 670 bird species at eBird hotspots in the USA, predicted from Sentinel-2 imagery and environmental rasters. It has fixed train/validation/test splits for USA-summer, USA-winter and Kenya. The metrics are MAE, MSE, top-10, top-30 and adaptive top-k accuracy. On USA-summer test, the best published values (checked 2026-10-30) are split between two models. MiTREE (Theresa Chen and Yao-Yi Chiang, arXiv 2412.18995) has top-10 47.38%, top-30 66.61%, top-k 67.82%, MAE 2.070e-2 and MSE 0.630e-2. An MLP on AlphaEarth embeddings (Tijunaityte, van der Plas, Belaid, Knapen, Soja, Athanasiadis; arXiv 2610.23110, Oct 2026) has top-10 49.7%, top-30 61.5%, MSE 0.58e-2 and MAE 1.93e-2. MIAM reports MAE 1.94e-2. On USA-winter, MiTREE reports top-10 51.77%, top-30 70.01%, top-k 71.40%, MAE 1.621e-2 and MSE 0.430e-2. CISO (arXiv 2508.06704) uses a songbird/non-songbird split and is not comparable.
targets.success_criterion: Predicted encounter-rate vectors for every USA-summer test hotspot from one model trained on the SatBird USA-summer train split (validation for selection), scored with the SatBird repository's metric code. As means over 3 seeds, the model must SIMULTANEOUSLY beat all five current bests: top-10 > 49.7%, top-30 > 66.61% and top-k > 67.82% (direction: max), and MAE < 1.93e-2 and MSE < 0.58e-2 (direction: min). It must also beat any value for the same split and metric that the NOVELTY skeptic finds in a paper from the last 24 months. Extra public inputs (for example satellite embeddings) are allowed if declared and if they carry no eBird checklist information from test hotspots. Deliverables: code, seeds, predictions and metric output.

partial_wins.statement: On USA-summer test, top-30 above 66.61% and top-k above 67.82%, with MAE no worse than 2.070e-2 (3-seed mean).

On USA-winter test, one model that beats MiTREE's top-10 51.77%, top-30 70.01%, top-k 71.40% and MAE 1.621e-2, with MSE no worse than 0.430e-2 (3-seed mean). The SatBird paper's ResNet-18 winter rows report MSE only as 0.4e-2 (rounded), so MSE is not part of this win.

targets.verification_method: The skeptic downloads the SatBird release and recomputes the five metrics from the saved predictions with the repository code. They re-run one seed and check that no test-hotspot target vector, and no eBird data from test hotspots, entered training or feature construction.
angles: Fuse AlphaEarth-style embeddings (strong on MAE, MSE and top-10) with MiTREE-style image encoders (strong on top-30 and top-k).
Cross-domain import (recommender systems): species co-occurrence priors and ranking losses that target top-k directly.
pitfalls: Spatial autocorrelation: features built from neighbouring hotspots' eBird data can leak test targets.
Papers quote MiTREE slightly differently (47.3/66.5 vs 47.38/66.61); use the higher values.
MSE and MAE are reported in units of 1e-2; mixing units creates false records.

targets.name: ARPA-E GO Competition Challenge 3 (multi-period AC unit commitment): beat the best Event 4 score on a public synthetic scenario
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (73- and 617-bus scenarios; the 4,000- to 23,643-bus ones need laptop-days and 16+ GB RAM)
targets.statement: Challenge 3 of the ARPA-E Grid Optimization (GO) Competition (2022-2023) posed a multi-period security-constrained AC unit commitment and market-clearing problem: commit and dispatch generators, loads and storage over 1-8 hour horizons with AC power flow, reserves, ramping, contingencies and optional line switching, maximising market surplus z. The organisers (Jesse Holzer, Stephen Elbert, Arun Veeramany and colleagues at PNNL, with Richard O'Neill, Hans Mittelmann, Carleton Coffrin and others) released the 591 synthetic Event 4 scenarios (73 to 23,643 buses; industry scenarios withheld), the official evaluator C3DataUtilities, and the full Event 4 results workbook E4LB_Master_20240506.xlsx on OEDI (DOI 10.25984/2426334, May 2024). Its per-network tabs (73, 617, 1576, 2000, 4224, 6049, 6717, 8316, 23643) give the Best Score and Best Team for every (division, model, scenario, switching) row; the 'data' tab lists every team's objective and feasibility. Best scores came from YongOptimization (most rows), GravityX, TIM-GO, The Blackouts, GOT-BSI-OPF and Artelys_Columbia, with a few rows from Occams razor, Gatorgar, LLGoMax and the ARPA-e Benchmark, all under event wall-clock limits of 600 s (D1), 7,200 s (D2) and 14,400 s (D3). Nobody has published a later best-known table, so offline computation can beat these scores; Brun, Lee, Lauinger, Chen and Sun (arXiv 2505.06211, 2025) report second-order-cone dual bounds and a 1.33% average gap for their own solutions on Challenge 3 cases, but no per-scenario objectives above the Event 4 bests. On C3E4N23643 D2 and D3 scenario 4 every team scored 0: the best feasible objectives listed are -690,443,352.45 (ARPA-e Benchmark, D2) and -2,623,296,182.38 (quasiGrad, D3).
targets.success_criterion: A solution JSON for one public synthetic Event 4 scenario (a scenario_ < n > .json in one of the C3E4N*_20231002.zip files on https://data.openei.org/submissions/5997; the 6708-bus industry network is excluded) that the C3DataUtilities evaluator (https://github.com/GOCompetition/C3DataUtilities, main branch; check_data.py --problem scenario_ < n > .json --solution sol.json, with the four *_switch_*_allowed parameters set to false when the row's SW is 0) reports as feasible, with objective z strictly greater than both the Best Score in that row of the network's tab of E4LB_Master_20240506.xlsx and the largest objective of any row with feas = 1 for the same model, scenario and SW in the 'data' tab, by more than 1e-6 * max(1, |best|). Division matters only through the scenario file; time limits do not apply offline and must be reported. The evaluator must first reproduce the objective of the scenario_ < n > .json.pop_solution.json shipped with that scenario.

partial_wins.statement: An evaluator-feasible solution for C3E4N23643D2 or C3E4N23643D3 scenario 4 whose objective is greater than every feasible team objective listed for it in the 'data' tab (-690,443,352.45 for D2, -2,623,296,182.38 for D3).

A strict improvement, by the full-win rule, on a scenario of an earlier event (E1, E2.1 or E3.1 on the same OEDI page) over the best team objective in that event's results workbook (E1LB, E2LB or E3LB master xlsx). The Sandbox sets have no results workbook and do not count.

An evaluator-feasible solution within 1e-4 relative of the Best Score on 10 different Event 4 scenarios of at least 617 buses, produced by one documented pipeline (reproduction of the competition state).

targets.verification_method: Download the scenario zip and E4LB_Master_20240506.xlsx (sha256 8ae933e17368428ffdb822b3fd3b28ea2969b65a8446e4d1f35e7f8b45654ff1 on 2026-10-30) from OEDI submission 5997. pip-install C3DataUtilities and GO-3-data-model in a clean venv, run check_data.py on the shipped pop_solution.json to confirm the evaluator works, then on the claimed solution with the right switching parameters, and read feasibility and z from its summary output. Read the Best Score cell with openpyxl (data_only=True) and the 'data' tab rows for that scenario. Minutes to an hour.
angles: Start from the shipped pop_solution.json and the formulation PDF; the 73- and 617-bus D1 scenarios had only 600 s in the event, so a slow exact MIP (commitment) plus AC-OPF polishing per period can plausibly beat them.

Decompose: solve a DC or copper-plate unit commitment MILP with HiGHS or SCIP, fix commitments, then solve the multi-period AC dispatch with Ipopt, and repair with the evaluator's own penalty terms in mind.
Rows where the best and second-best teams differ by more than 0.1% signal slack.
pitfalls: Score is not objective: infeasible or negative-objective solutions were scored 0, so the Best Score cell can be 0 while the real bar (feasible objective) is negative; compare with both, as the criterion says.
Switching: SW = 1 rows allow line and transformer switching, SW = 0 rows forbid it; evaluating an SW = 0 claim with default parameters lets switching in.
Use the 20231002 Event 4 files; Event 2 2000- and 6717-bus files were replaced (C3E2.1) and the old ones fail the data checker.
gocompetition.energy.gov served an expired TLS certificate on 2026-10-30; use OEDI and GitHub.

targets.name: ARPA-E GO Competition Challenge 2 (SCOPF with switching): beat a Monarch of the Mountain best-known objective
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (617- to 31,777-bus networks with hundreds of contingencies; 16+ GB RAM for the largest)
targets.statement: Challenge 2 of the ARPA-E GO Competition (2020-2021) is a single-period security-constrained AC optimal power flow with transformer taps, phase shifters, switched shunts, price-responsive loads, ramp limits, fast-start unit commitment and optional line switching, maximising economic surplus over the base case and all post-contingency cases. After the Final Event, ARPA-E ran 'Monarch of the Mountain' (MotM, 2022), inviting anyone to improve the best known solutions of the 84 public synthetic Final Event scenarios (16 networks, 617 to 31,777 buses). The results workbook Challenge_2_Monarch_of_the_Mountain_Results.xlsx on OEDI (DOI 10.25984/2448433) records, in tab 'Ch2', the best Challenge 2 objective and the current best MotM objective per scenario; the last improvements are dated 26 Oct 2022. GravityX (Hassan Hijazi and colleagues) holds 74 of the 84 records, GOT-BSI-OPF 8 and Gordian Knot 2. Every record improves on the Final Event best, which GravityX held on 59 scenarios, GO-SNIP on 10, NU_Columbia_Artelys on 8, magos and Monday Mornings on 3 each and GMI-GO on 1. MotM is closed and no later table exists. Example records: C2FEN00617 scenario 5, 1,350,775.92643542 (GravityX); C2FEN03970 scenario 23, 257,435.110836647 (GOT-BSI-OPF); C2FEN31777 scenario 11, 129,394,052.138728 (GravityX).
targets.success_criterion: Solution files (solution_BASECASE.txt and one solution_ < label > .txt per contingency, in the Challenge 2 output format) for one scenario listed in tab 'Ch2' of https://data.openei.org/files/6197/Challenge_2_Monarch_of_the_Mountain_Results.xlsx, using that scenario's case.raw, case.json and case.con from 'Challenge_2 _Final_Event_4_Synthetic_Data_Scenarios.zip' on https://data.openei.org/submissions/6197, that the C2DataUtilities evaluator (https://github.com/GOCompetition/C2DataUtilities, data_utilities.evaluation, line and transformer switching allowed) reports as feasible (no hard-constraint violation beyond its tolerances), with objective strictly greater than that scenario's 'Current Best data Objective' cell by more than 1e-7 * |best| (consecutive records differ by as little as 1.3e-6 relative). As a smoke test the verifier first runs the evaluator on the infeasibility solution that the repository's construct_infeasibility_solution builds for the same scenario; it must run to completion and report feasibility and an objective.

partial_wins.statement: An evaluator-feasible solution for a MotM scenario whose objective beats that scenario's 'Best Ch2 Objective' (the original competition best) but not the MotM record.
A documented pipeline that reaches within 1e-4 relative of the MotM record on 5 scenarios of different networks, each evaluator-feasible.

targets.verification_method: Download the Final Event synthetic zip (71.7 MB) and the MotM workbook (sha256 db04c3e5e68d27537f8d37d01c00eef4cc55659cc6a18f6f53036a972b04c579 on 2026-10-30) from OEDI submission 6197; pip-install C2DataUtilities in a clean venv; run its evaluation (switching allowed) on the claimed solution_BASECASE.txt and solution_ < label > .txt files against the scenario's case.raw, case.json and case.con; read feasibility and objective; read the record with openpyxl (data_only=True). Minutes to hours for the largest networks.
angles: The records are near-converged on base-case dispatch; remaining gains are likely in discrete choices (switching, taps, shunts, fast-start commitment) and in contingency responses, so local search over discrete settings with an AC-OPF inner solve is the natural attack.
Small-relative-gap records (617, 2020 buses) are cheapest to attack; start from the posted best solution if the MotM submission archives are reachable, else from GravityX-style Ipopt solves.
pitfalls: The objective depends on the contingency solutions (solution2); a better base case with poor contingency responses can lower the score.
MotM rows are the 84 public synthetic scenarios; industry scenarios were never released.
The 'Previous' and 'old' tabs hold superseded records; use 'Ch2' column 'Current Best data Objective'.

targets.name: ARPA-E GO Competition Challenge 1 (continuous SCOPF): beat the best Final Event score on a public synthetic scenario
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (networks of a few hundred to tens of thousands of buses; contingency evaluation dominates)
targets.statement: Challenge 1 of the ARPA-E GO Competition (2018-2019) is the single-period security-constrained AC optimal power flow with generator response after contingencies: choose a base-case operating point (code 1, under a strict wall-clock limit) and post-contingency responses (code 2) minimising generation cost plus soft-constraint penalties. The Final Event (late 2019) scored 25 teams and the ARPA-E Benchmark on 352 scenarios in each of Division 1 (real-time data) and Division 2 (offline data), mostly 20 per network. The results workbook C1_E4_scenario_results_20200106.xlsx on OEDI (DOI 10.25984/2437761) lists, per scenario, every entrant's score and a 'best score' / 'by team' column: Division 1's 352 rows are led by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (226 best scores), BAT (43), Lehigh University (31), Georgia Tech (Sun) (25) and gravityx (21); Division 2's 352 rows by LLNL (182), Lehigh (110) and BAT (41). The synthetic scenarios (340 real-time and 340 offline, 17 networks) are public; the industry networks 40, 41 and 42 are not. The official Python evaluator is GOCompetition/Evaluation. The bests were obtained under event time limits and no later best-known table exists. Example: Network_02R-173 scenario 1, best score 280,109.889140951 (BAT).
targets.success_criterion: Solution files (solution1.txt and solution2.txt in the Challenge 1 format) for one scenario row of the 'Division 1' or 'Division 2' tab of https://data.openei.org/files/6153/C1_E4_scenario_results_20200106.xlsx whose data (case.raw, case.rop, case.con, case.inl) is in Challenge_1_Final_Event_Real-Time_Synthetic_Scenarios.zip (Division 1) or Challenge_1_Final_Event_Offline_Synthetic_Scenarios.zip (Division 2) on https://data.openei.org/submissions/6153, that the evaluator https://github.com/GOCompetition/Evaluation (evaluation.py) scores with zero hard-constraint infeasibility and an objective strictly lower than the row's 'best score' cell by more than 1e-6 * |best|. As a smoke test the verifier first runs the evaluator on the repository's examples/case2 (sol1.txt, sol2.txt), since no team solutions are published.

partial_wins.statement: A strict improvement, by the full-win rule (evaluator-feasible, objective lower by more than 1e-6 relative), on a synthetic Trial Event 2 or 3 scenario whose data is in Challenge_1_Trial_Event_2_Used_Scenarios.zip or Challenge_1_Trial_Event_3_Scenarios.zip on OEDI 6153. The bar is the lowest team 'Score' cell for that network and scenario across the 'Division 1' to 'Division 4' tabs, and any team revision tab, of Challenge_1_Event_2_Results_Summary.xlsx or Challenge_1_Event_3_Results_Summary.xlsx; these workbooks have no 'best score' column.
Evaluator-feasible solutions within 1e-4 relative of the best score on 10 Final Event scenarios from at least 3 networks, from one documented pipeline.

targets.verification_method: Download the synthetic zip and the results workbook (sha256 cff10169df2cefa8d25447c6deb495ba4973e0f7038a890e363f5b5b355cf086 on 2026-10-30) from OEDI submission 6153; clone GOCompetition/Evaluation, run evaluation.py on the scenario files and the claimed solution pair in a clean venv, read infeasibility and objective; read the 'best score' cell with openpyxl (data_only=True). Minutes.
pitfalls: Minimisation: lower is better here, unlike Challenges 2 and 3.
Some workbook rows are industry networks or geomean summary rows ('Network 02 Geomean'); only rows whose scenario folder is in the public synthetic zips count.
Teams whose solutions were infeasible were scored with a slack solution ('# slacks', 'slack score' columns); the 'best score' column already takes the minimum over team scores.

targets.name: PGLib-OPF v23.07: an AC-feasible dispatch cheaper than the published baseline on a large case with an open relaxation gap
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (1,803- to 78,484-bus cases; multistart Ipopt or global-solver heuristics)
targets.statement: The Power Grid Library for AC optimal power flow (PGLib-OPF, IEEE PES Task Force on Benchmarks; curated by Carleton Coffrin, LANL) is the standard AC-OPF benchmark: 66 networks in typical (TYP), congested (API) and small-angle-difference (SAD) conditions. Its BASELINE.md for the current release v23.07 (unchanged since 24 Jul 2023) lists, per case, the AC objective from PowerModels.jl v0.19.9 + Ipopt (a local optimum) and the SOC and QC relaxation gaps. Global optimality is unknown for most large cases. On v21.07, Gopinath and Hijazi (LANL, arXiv 2203.11328, 2022) closed the gap below 1% on 85% of the open cases (SOC gap above 1%) up to 3,000 buses with SDP-RLT and bound tightening. Wang, Magron and Lasserre (EPSR 2022) certified 1% optimality on 58 of 115 hard cases (29 at first order, 29 more at order 1.5). Certified optimal-value intervals posted in Oct 2026 (pglib-opf issue #49) cover only cases up to 600 buses. In scope are the 82 cases with at least 1,000 buses and BASELINE SOC gap at least 1.00%, excluding the five networks MINLPLib also carries (case1354_pegase, case6468_rte, case6515_rte, case9241_pegase, case13659_pegase: bank target minlplib-open-primal-bound). Examples: case8387_pegase 2.7714e+06 $/h (SOC gap 64.11%), case6495_rte 3.0678e+06 (15.11%), case2742_goc__api 6.0996e+05 (22.67%), case3970_goc__api 1.7494e+06 (38.79%). A cheaper AC-feasible point would show that the published baseline is not globally optimal for that case.
targets.success_criterion: For one in-scope case (listed in https://github.com/power-grid-lib/pglib-opf/blob/master/BASELINE.md for v23.07 with Nodes >= 1000 and SOC Gap >= 1.00, network not one of the five excluded), give a full AC operating point (bus voltage magnitudes and angles, generator P and Q) for the unmodified v23.07 .m file. Use the standard polar AC power-flow model with MATPOWER conventions: branch pi-model with taps and shifts, and bus shunts. Only in-service elements count, as in PowerModels: generators and branches with status 0 carry no power and stay off, and type-4 buses are dropped. The point must satisfy all of the following: every bus P and Q balance holds within 1e-6 p.u. on baseMVA; all voltage, generator and branch angle-difference bounds hold within 1e-6; every branch apparent-power flow at both ends is at most rate_a * (1 + 1e-6); and the polynomial gencost objective summed over in-service generators is below the BASELINE.md AC value times (1 - 1e-4) (the listed value has 5 significant figures). The checker must first reproduce the BASELINE AC objective within 1e-4 relative from an Ipopt solve of the same case.

partial_wins.statement: An independent AC-feasibility and cost checker (not PowerModels or MATPOWER code) that, given points from PowerModels + Ipopt solves, reproduces the BASELINE.md AC objective within 1e-4 relative and reports all residuals below 1e-6 on 20 in-scope cases.

For an in-scope case, two AC-feasible local optima (by the full-win checks) whose objectives differ by more than 1e-3 relative, showing a non-trivial local-optimum structure; the lower one need not beat the baseline.

targets.verification_method: Download the case from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/power-grid-lib/pglib-opf/master/ (api/ and sad/ subfolders for those conditions) at tag v23.07, parse the MATPOWER struct, recompute all injections and branch flows from the claimed voltages with a short numpy script, check every bound and the cost, and compare with the BASELINE.md row (sha256 of BASELINE.md 0634196fbf73cc0e19f6d19fa04032a26a218e42779e08e9265bc11b89dca62c on 2026-10-30). Seconds.
angles: Multistart Ipopt from randomised voltage profiles and from SOC/QC-relaxation solutions; congested (API) cases with large gaps are the likeliest to hide better local optima.
Fix the generator commitment pattern implied by an SDP or QC relaxation solution and re-solve AC; try spatial branch-and-bound on a reduced network around binding lines.
pitfalls: Most baseline points are probably near-global; a large relaxation gap usually reflects a weak relaxation, not a bad local optimum, hence the low tractability.
Tolerance games: loosening balance or line-limit tolerances lowers cost; the checks are absolute at 1e-6 p.u.

Out-of-service units: most in-scope cases have many status-0 generators (e.g. 782 of 1,349 in case4917_goc, 692 of 1,372 in case6495_rte) and some status-0 branches. Switching them on gives a cheaper but invalid dispatch, so they must stay off.
rate_a = 0 would mean unlimited in MATPOWER (no in-service branch of an in-scope case uses it); angmin/angmax and gencost model 2 coefficient order must be read exactly.

pglib-opf issue #48: the rte6xxx cases (including in-scope case6470_rte and case6495_rte) have a phase shifter in parallel with a line, probably a data error. Deleting it lowers case6495_rte's cost by about 57 $/h, but the case must be used unmodified.
MINLPLib's acopf_* instances use a different scaling; those five networks are excluded here.

targets.name: OptiWindNet RouteSets: a shorter offshore wind-farm array-cable network than the best stored for a real site
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (16-210 turbines per site; MILP or HGS/LKH-style heuristics)
targets.statement: OptiWindNet RouteSets (Mauricio Souza de Alencar, Tuhfe Gocmen and Nicolaos A. Cutululis, DTU Wind; preprint wes-2026-124, in review at Wind Energy Science) is an open benchmark for the wind-farm cable-routing problem: connect every turbine to an offshore substation with cables of a given capacity (2-12 turbines per string), radial (paths) or branched (trees), without crossings, routing around site borders and obstacles, minimising total cable length. Release 26.10-v4 (Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23537067, 21 Oct 2026, CC-BY-4.0) holds 49,204 route sets for 13,954 (location, capacity) instances from CPLEX 22.1.1 and Gurobi 12 MILP runs (with bounds) and HGS-CVRP and LKH-3 heuristics. Recomputed from the SQLite file on 2026-10-30, comparing each instance's shortest stored length (detours included; radial counts for branched) with its best branched MILP bound (a bound on the model's straight-line objective, so these are indicative gaps, not certified ones): 2,431 instances are at 1-2%, 2,502 at 2-5% and 514 at 5% or more; 1,252 instances whose nodeset name has no '!' prefix (built farms, literature sites and their '.1_OSS' or '.solid' variants) carry a branched bound. Largest: London Array capacity 12, 138,963.85 m vs bound 132,040.61 (stored relgap 3.7%); Belwind capacity 10, 35,115.17 m vs 33,449.99 (4.3%); Hornsea One.1_OSS capacity 8, 380,296.05 m (a radial set) vs branched bound 362,862.42. Shorter route sets on these instances are open.
targets.success_criterion: For one (nodeset, capacity) instance of release r26.10-v4 whose nodeset name does not start with '!', and topology X (radial or branched), a route set of topology X with strictly smaller total length than every stored route set for that instance of topology X or more restrictive (radial counts for branched), by more than 1e-6 relative, using at each substation no more feeders than the shortest such stored route set (feeders_per_root), and carrying the same nodeset (all turbines, substations, borders and obstacles from its VertexC blob). It must pass optiwindnet.validating.validate_routeset with no violations (topology, capacity, loads, crossings), every route segment must stay inside the site border and outside every obstacle polygon (checked separately, since the validator does not test this), and its length, recomputed as the sum of Euclidean segment lengths in metres, must be the value compared.

partial_wins.statement: A strict improvement, by the full-win rule, on an augmented instance (nodeset name starting with '!') whose stored best has a certified gap of at least 2%.
A radial route set, by the full-win rule, beating the best stored radial route set on a real-site instance whose radial best has no MILP bound in the release.

targets.verification_method: Download optiwindnet-routesets-r26.10-v4.sqlite.xz (sha256 c78c8f3c0543468a48c24d02a08a9a71f9b385389b1e82b6af6bd5bbfdd05e3a on 2026-10-30) from Zenodo; with sqlite3 read the nodeset row and all routeset rows for the instance (length, feeders_per_root, misc.topology). pip-install optiwindnet in a clean venv, load the claim, run validate_routeset; check segment containment in the border and obstacles with shapely; recompute length. Minutes.
angles: Warm-start the package's own MILP (HiGHS or SCIP) from the stored best and run longer, or with the feeder-limit and segmented feeder-route options the release used; many gaps come from 6-hour CPLEX limits.
Branched instances at high capacity (8-12) on 150-200 turbines have the largest gaps; capacitated minimum spanning tree heuristics (Esau-Williams, ruin-and-recreate) plus crossing repair are natural.
pitfalls: Feeder limits differ between stored runs (min_plus1, min_plus2, unlimited); the criterion caps feeders at the shortest stored route set's count so that relaxing the feeder limit does not count.
Stored 'length' includes detours computed by PathFinder; 'misc.objective' is the model's straight-line objective. Compare lengths.
A newer Zenodo version may change the table; re-read the latest version before claiming.

targets.name: Erdos #1033 (Bollobas-Erdos): a construction below 1.463877226961 n, or a certified lower bound of at least 1.453 n, for the forced triangle degree sum
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (blow-up optimisation in exact or interval arithmetic); laptop-days for a flag-algebra SDP with exact rounding
targets.statement: Let h(n) be the largest value such that every graph on n vertices with more than n^2/4 edges has a triangle whose three vertex degrees sum to at least h(n). Bollobas and Erdos conjectured h(n) >= (2(sqrt3-1)-o(1))n, which matches the Erdos-Laskar/Fan construction (about 1.46410n). That conjecture is now false. rickyc, working with GPT-5.5 Pro, posted a blow-up of the butterfly graph (two triangles sharing a vertex) reaching about 1.46393n (forum, 27 Jun 2026). Wouter CvB optimised the part weights and partial densities (note dated 27 Jul 2026). This gives c+ = y0 = 1.463877226961..., the smallest positive root of P(y) = 384y^7 + 1744y^6 - 832y^5 - 86712y^4 + 379016y^3 - 697963y^2 + 617212y - 215708. Blow-ups of all graphs on at most 8 vertices did not beat it. The published lower bound is Fan's 21/16 = 1.3125 (1988). On the forum RealBelgian reports flag-algebra lower bounds of about 1.45016 (1 Aug 2026) and then about 1.4525 (7 Aug 2026), with no paper or certificate public yet. So 1.4525 <= liminf h(n)/n <= y0, with the lower value claimed and not yet verified. The problem page is open; the question is to estimate h(n).
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED by either of two routes. (A) Construction. Give a template: a graph H with independent parts V_1..V_t, rational or algebraic weights x_i > 0 summing to 1, and pair densities f_ij in [0,1] on the edges of H, each realised by near-regular bipartite graphs. In exact or rigorous interval arithmetic, the edge density sum_{ij in E(H)} f_ij x_i x_j must be strictly greater than 1/4, and the largest degree sum d_i + d_j + d_k over triangles ijk of H, where d_i = sum_j f_ij x_j, must be c < 1.463877226961 (strictly less than y0, and below any smaller construction posted on the forum thread at verification time). Any equivalent explicit graph family with a proof of the same two limits also counts. (B) Lower bound. An exact flag-algebra or other machine-checkable certificate (rational SDP with exact rounding, checked by independent code) proving h(n) >= (c - o(1))n with c >= 1.453, and c strictly greater than every lower bound posted on the forum thread or in a paper at verification time. The 1.453 threshold sits clearly above RealBelgian's approximate 1.4525 claim.

partial_wins.statement: A publicly released exact certificate proving liminf h(n)/n >= 1.40, provided no public certificate or paper with c >= 1.40 exists at verification time.
A publicly released exact certificate proving liminf h(n)/n >= 1.45, provided no public certificate or paper with c >= 1.45 exists at verification time.

targets.verification_method: (A) Recompute the edge density and every triangle degree sum of H from the stated weights. Use exact algebraic arithmetic (sympy/flint) or interval arithmetic with outward rounding. Confirm the parts are independent, so every triangle of the blow-up comes from a triangle of H. Then build G_N for N = 10^4 with near-regular bipartite realisations, count edges and scan all triangles as a sanity check. (B) Re-run the SDP certificate check in exact rational arithmetic with code written independently of the prover: positive semidefiniteness via exact LDL^T, and the flag identities recomputed from scratch.
angles: Leave the butterfly support. rickyc reports (forum, 1 Aug 2026, GPT-assisted, unverified) that Wouter CvB's point is optimal among all graphons with the butterfly support pattern, even with arbitrary measurable structure in its two partial blocks. Wouter CvB found nothing better among constant-density blow-ups of graphs on <= 8 vertices. A gain probably needs a different support graph: 9+ vertices, three or more partial pairs, or non-constant density on a pair of a new template.
Flag algebras on 3-graphs of the pair (G, degree-class labelling), or on graphs with vertex weights encoding degree. For the lower bound, start from Fan's 21/16 argument and add degree-type flags.
pitfalls: Edge density must be strictly above 1/4. A template at exactly 1/4 needs the perturbation argument written out.
Degree sums are over triangles of the whole graph. Non-independent parts create extra triangles.
RealBelgian's ~1.4525 is an approximate forum claim with no public certificate. Do not cite it as proven, and do not claim p1/p2 if a certificate or paper has appeared in the meantime.

Floating-point optimisation near y0 is not a proof; certify the strict inequality. Even y0 itself needs exact arithmetic: a naive double-precision root finder returns 1.4638772262, while the true root is 1.463877226961326.
The problem page (last edited 3 Apr 2026) still lists 2(sqrt3-1) and 21/16 as the bounds; the current state is in the forum thread and Wouter CvB's note.

targets.name: Erdos #628 (Erdos-Lovasz Tihany, a = 2 branch): a noncomplete double-critical graph, or the order-14 census
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days for order 14 with k >= 8; needs cluster for (k,n) = (6,14) (estimated about 10^4 core-hours)
targets.statement: Erdos-Lovasz Tihany conjecture (Erdos 1968): a K_k-free graph with chromatic number k is (a,b)-splittable for all a,b >= 2 with a+b = k+1. The case a=b=3 was proved by Brown and Jung. The a=2 case reduces to the Double-Critical Graph Conjecture: every connected double-critical k-chromatic graph (chi(G - x - y) = k-2 for every edge xy) is K_k. It is known for k <= 5 at every order (Stiebitz 1987). Kawarabayashi-Pedersen-Toft (EJC 2010, Prop. 9) show that a noncomplete connected example with k >= 6 has minimum degree >= k+1, hence at least k+2 vertices, and that no two vertices of degree k+1 are adjacent. Orders <= 12 are excluded (A. S. Pedersen's 2012 note, cited in Kriesell-Pedersen 2015). An unrefereed 2008 UBC undergraduate report by Edward Lui already claims at least 14 vertices, and minimum degree >= 8 for k = 6; only its abstract is online. Order 13 is now closed by computation: the erdosproblemaday.com report (Jul 2026) did k = 8..11, and BitterLemma (forum, 17 Aug 2026, github.com/bitterlemma/erdos-628) did k = 6 and 7. The (6,13) cell held 12,371,706,156 generated graphs (geng -c -d7 13), 2,468,617,015 of them 6-chromatic, with 0 survivors. Order 14 was not attempted. Z. Song's survey records many special cases; the conjecture is open.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED: an explicit graph (edge list) that is connected and noncomplete, has chromatic number k >= 6 (exact), and is double-critical: chi(G - {x,y}) = k-2 for every edge xy, checked exactly. This is a counterexample to the Double-Critical Graph Conjecture and so to Erdos-Lovasz Tihany at (2, k-1). Also accepted: any K_k-free graph with chi = k and some a,b >= 2, a+b = k+1, that is provably not (a,b)-splittable, with an exhaustive certificate.

partial_wins.statement: Complete order-14 census for every k in {8,...,12}: all connected graphs on 14 vertices with minimum degree >= k+1, zero noncomplete double-critical k-chromatic survivors. Per-cell counts (generated, K_k-free, chi = k, survivors) must be reproduced by two independent runs with different shard splits.
The same order-14 census for k = 7 (connected graphs on 14 vertices with minimum degree >= 8).
The same order-14 census for k = 6 (connected graphs on 14 vertices with minimum degree >= 7).

targets.verification_method: For a counterexample: compute chi(G) and chi(G - x - y) for every edge with two unrelated exact colouring codes (DSATUR branch and bound, and a SAT encoding). For a census: regenerate the candidate stream with nauty geng (-c -d(k+1) 14 res/mod) and check that shard totals agree across two different moduli. Re-decide a random sample plus every chi = k graph with a second chromatic-number implementation, and check that chi = k equals the splittable count plus survivors in every cell.
angles: Use the KPT structure (delta >= k+1, no two vertices of degree k+1 adjacent, no K_k, every edge in many (k-1)-cliques of G-x-y) to prune geng output early. Augmentation from 13-vertex near-misses may beat plain generation.
For p1 the minimum degree is >= 9 on 14 vertices, so the complements have maximum degree <= 4. Generate complements instead, which is far cheaper.
pitfalls: geng res/mod is 0-based. The degree flag is -d(k+1), not -dk; the wrong flag gives a plausible wrong universe.
Connectedness matters: K_k plus an isolated vertex is double-critical.
A census is finite evidence only; it does not prove the conjecture.
Survivors must be re-checked with an independent chromatic-number code before any claim.
Lui's 2008 claim of delta >= 8 for k = 6 is unrefereed and its proof is not public. A p3 census must still cover the full delta >= 7 universe; a delta >= 8 run alone does not count.

targets.name: Erdos #583 (Gallai path decomposition): a connected graph needing more than ceil(n/2) paths, or the exhaustive n = 12 check
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (n = 12 sweep reported to need about 15 h on 9 cores with the improved decider); needs cluster for n = 13
targets.statement: Gallai's conjecture (Erdos-Gallai): every connected graph on n vertices can be partitioned into at most ceil(n/2) edge-disjoint simple paths. Known partial results include Lovasz (paths and cycles), Pyber (even-degree vertices induce a forest), Bonamy-Perrett (maximum degree <= 5), Blanche-Bonamy-Bonichon (planar), Anto-Basavaraju (2-degenerate) and Chu-Fan-Zhou (2026), plus the Dean-Kouider/Yan bound of ceil(2n/3). Exhaustive verification: Botler, Cano and Sambinelli (On computing the path number of a graph, ENTCS 346 (2019) 185-197) used an integer-programming model to verify the conjecture for all graphs on at most 11 vertices, bipartite graphs on at most 16 vertices and regular graphs on at most 14 vertices. Independently, sallerk (forum, 31 Aug 2026, github.com/sallerk/erdos-notes) did all connected graphs with n <= 11 (1,006,700,565 at n = 11). herong / Darrenus (17 Sep 2026, github.com/Darrenus/erdos583-gallai) reproduced n <= 11 with a much faster decider that uses ceil(Delta/2) and sums bounds over components. They announced an n = 12 sweep (164,059,830,476 graphs, about 15 h) as running, but no result has been posted on the forum or in the repository (last push 17 Sep 2026). sallerk's own n = 12 attempt left 35,633,639 graphs undecided.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED: an explicit connected graph G on n vertices (edge list) such that E(G) cannot be partitioned into ceil(n/2) edge-disjoint simple paths. The certificate is an exhaustive search that two independently written deciders (no shared code) both report as undecomposable. Decomposability into trails, or with repeated vertices, does not count.

partial_wins.statement: Exhaustive verification of every connected graph on 12 vertices: the shard counts sum to A001349(12) = 164,059,830,476, nothing is left undecided, and every 'yes' is witnessed by an explicit path family. A second decider must independently re-decide all graphs that the fast filters did not settle trivially, or a uniformly random sample of at least 10^6 of them. This counts only if no complete n = 12 verification has been published (paper or preprint) or posted on the forum thread, in github.com/Darrenus/erdos583-gallai or in github.com/sallerk/erdos-notes by verification time.
The same exhaustive verification for n = 13 (A001349(13) = 50,502,031,367,952 connected graphs).

targets.verification_method: Check a decomposition claim by confirming each path is simple, the paths are edge-disjoint and cover E(G), and their number is <= ceil(n/2). Check a counterexample by running two independent exact deciders (one written from the definition) to exhaustion. Check a census by re-running geng shards, confirming the totals equal A001349(n), and spot-checking witnesses.
angles: Apply the published sufficient conditions (Pyber forest condition, max degree <= 5, 2-degenerate, planar) as a cheap pre-filter. Only graphs outside all of them need the decider; per sallerk that is a majority already at n = 10.
Search for counterexamples among dense graphs whose even-degree vertices induce a dense subgraph, since those are the cases the theorems miss.
pitfalls: Simple paths, not trails: a decider that lets a path revisit a vertex reports success on everything.
Memoisation by hash can only prune. A false 'no' must be re-checked by hand, and a hash must never produce a 'yes'.
herong's n = 12 run may finish and be posted at any time; re-check the thread and the repository before claiming p1.

targets.name: Erdos #1204 (Elliott): a narrower admissible k-tuple than Sutherland's table for some 343 <= k <= 5000, or exact minimal sums B(k) beyond k = 147
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (local search over sieved tuples; exact branch and bound for p1)
targets.statement: A sequence 0 <= a_1 < ... < a_k is admissible if it misses at least one residue class modulo every prime. Erdos #1204 (attributed to Elliott) asks for A(k) = min a_k (the minimal diameter, OEIS A008407) and B(k) = min (a_1+...+a_k)/k. It is known that (1/2+o(1)) k log k <= A(k) <= (1+o(1)) k log k. The best known admissible tuples for k <= 5000 are in Andrew Sutherland's table 'Narrow admissible tuples' (math.mit.edu/~primegaps, Polymath8). Entries are by Engelsma, Sutherland and Xiao-Feng Xie; the last updates are from 2016 and 2019. Optimality is proven only for k <= 342 (Engelsma). Sample entries: k=343: 2340; k=500: 3594; k=1000: 7802; k=2000: 16978; k=3000: 26606; k=5000: 46806. The page says submissions are no longer taken there and directs improvements to Sutherland by email; that is a human action, not part of the win. For B(k), Leandre Jack (forum, 5 Sep 2026) computed exact S(k) = k*B(k) for all k <= 147 by two independent searches; for example S(93) = 22474, and the greedy sequence stops being optimal at k = 93.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED: an explicit integer k-tuple, for some 343 <= k <= 5000, that is admissible and has diameter a_k - a_1 strictly smaller than the Sutherland table entry for that k at verification time.

partial_wins.statement: Exact S(k) = min sum over admissible k-tuples, with an optimal tuple, for every k from 148 up to some K >= 160. Values come from two independent exact searches, and the k <= 147 values must reproduce Leandre Jack's table.
A reproducible exhaustive proof that the k = 343 table entry (diameter 2340) is optimal, or an admissible 343-tuple of smaller diameter (which is then the full win).

targets.verification_method: Admissibility: for every prime p <= k, compute the set of residues a_i mod p and confirm it is not all of Z/pZ; primes p > k are automatic. Diameter: a_k - a_1. Compare with the table row fetched from math.mit.edu/~primegaps on the day. For p1/p2, re-run the exact searches with an independent implementation.
angles: Polymath8 methods: Schinzel sieve and shifted greedy sieve, then local 'adjustment' search that swaps elements while keeping admissibility. xfxie's 2016/2019 improvements came from long runs of this kind.

Most rows still date from June-July 2013. The only later improvements are scattered 2014 rows, xfxie/Engelsma rows of Aug-Sep 2016 spread over k = 1573..4957, and k = 1976-1979 (Feb 2019). Rows untouched since 2013, especially between the improved clusters, may still be soft.
pitfalls: Ties do not count: the diameter must be strictly smaller.
Do not email or submit anything; record the improvement for the human operator.
Rows for k <= 342 are proven optimal and cannot be beaten.

targets.name: Erdos #1055 (Erdos-Selfridge prime classes): determine a(20) of OEIS A005113, or find a class-20 prime below 764276710625653
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (recursive enumeration of high-class primes up to about 8e14 by p+1 = m*q with q of the previous class)
targets.statement: Erdos-Selfridge classification (Guy A18; Erdos #1055). A prime p is in class 1 if p+1 has no prime factor other than 2 and 3. Otherwise p's class is one more than the largest class of the prime factors of p+1 (the OEIS A005113 convention). Erdos asks how p_r^(1/r) behaves, where p_r is the least prime of class r. OEIS A005113 lists p_1..p_19 = 2, 13, 37, 73, 1021, ..., 3666349256113, 65994286610033. a(17)-a(19) are from Jud McCranie (May 2026). M. F. Hasler (2007) gave a(20) <= 764276710625653, and Alper Ferudun confirmed in the OEIS discussion (18 Oct 2026) that this number is a prime of class 20. A b-file for n = 1..396 by Sascha Fürstenberg (Oct 2026) was found to list non-minimal values, e.g. a(20) = 1055908585760527. The data line was cut back to a(19), so a(20) is open. Lower bound: a(20) >= 2*a(19) - 1.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED by either (A) an explicit prime p < 764276710625653 of class 20, with a recursive certificate: the full factorisation of p+1 and of q+1 for every prime q in the chain, with primality proofs, so an independent checker recomputes the class; or (B) the exact value of a(20), proved minimal by an exhaustive enumeration that two independently written programs reproduce. They must agree on the full list of class-19 primes below a(20)/2 used in the search.

partial_wins.statement: An explicit prime of class 21 smaller than 2111817171521053 (the non-minimal a(21) value in the withdrawn Oct 2026 b-file), with a recursive class certificate.
An explicit prime of class 22 smaller than 105590858576052649 (the withdrawn b-file value), with a recursive class certificate.

targets.verification_method: Recompute the class recursively from the supplied factorisations, checking every factorisation by multiplication and every prime with a deterministic test (BPSW plus an ECPP or Pocklington certificate for numbers above 2^64). For (B), rerun both enumerations and diff the class-19 prime lists and the final minimum.
angles: Any class-20 prime p < 7.65e14 has p+1 = m*q with q of class 19, q >= a(19) = 65994286610033 and m even, so m <= 11. Enumerate the class-19 primes below 3.83e14 recursively from class-18 primes below 1.92e14, and so on, rather than classifying all primes.
Hasler's PARI 'someofnextclass' routine in the OEIS entry is a useful starting point, but rewrite it so minimality is exhaustive.
pitfalls: The OEIS b-file b005113.txt (n = 1..396) contains non-minimal values. Use the data line and the history page, not the b-file.
The class of a prime depends on the classes of all prime factors of p+1, not only the largest.
The site and OEIS phrase the class-1 convention slightly differently; use the OEIS convention stated above and say so.

targets.name: Erdos #1063 (Erdos-Selfridge): n_k for k >= 76 (OEIS A389360 beyond the forum's k = 75)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (progression sweeps; 89e9 candidates covered k = 60..75)
targets.statement: n_k is the least n >= 2k such that n-i divides C(n,k) for all but exactly one i in 0 <= i < k (Erdos-Selfridge 1983; Guy B31; OEIS A389360). Values start n_2..n_5 = 4, 6, 9, 12; Monier gave n_k <= k! and Cambie n_k <= k*lcm(2..k-1). rickyc (forum, Jun-Jul 2026) proved n_k >= prod over p^a || k of p^(a + floor(log_p(k-1))), and has two AI-assisted proof claims on the site (Jul-Aug 2026) for asymptotic bounds on log n_k. The OEIS b-file (Chai Wah Wu) ends at k = 59 (a(59) = 4967281530). On the forum, jbell31 (28 Jul 2026, github.com/Jaybell31/dreamwalk/tree/master/erdos1063) extended it to k = 75 (e.g. n_75 = 32639932074432). That work uses rickyc's structural results: the failing index is n mod k, and solutions lie on explicit progressions. Each value was checked by an independent exact-binomial verifier and declared minimal after a sweep of 89,015,468,839 candidates; the repository states that minimality rests on that single sweep implementation. Minimality is also conditional on rickyc's lemmas, which have forum proofs but are not formalised.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED: the exact value of n_76: an n with exactly one 0 <= i < 76 such that (n-i) does not divide C(n,76), verified with exact big-integer arithmetic, plus an exhaustive minimality sweep reproduced by two independent implementations. Larger k extend the record.

partial_wins.statement: A Lean 4 proof (no sorry, standard axioms only) of rickyc's structural lemma used to restrict the search: the unique failing index satisfies e = n mod k, together with the prime-power divisibility conditions. This makes the published minimality claims for k = 60..75 unconditional.
An independent re-derivation of n_60..n_75 by code sharing nothing with jbell31's searcher or verifier, matching all 16 forum values or exhibiting a smaller solution.
Exact n_k for every 76 <= k <= 85 with minimality as in the success criterion.

targets.verification_method: Compute C(n,k) exactly (Python integers) and test each n-i for divisibility, expecting exactly one failure. Re-run the minimality sweep with independent code over the progressions n = r mod D(k,r), and check the predicted candidate count against the number enumerated.
angles: Use the progression structure: for each residue r, solutions satisfy n = r mod D(k,r). Sweep candidates in increasing order across all r in parallel.
Use 128-bit arithmetic: n_k already reaches 3.3e13 at k = 75 and may pass 2^63 soon after.
pitfalls: Take the minimum over all residues r, not the first hit in r-order (a real bug jbell31 reported).
Respect the n >= 2k floor.
Values above the OEIS b-file are forum claims; re-derive before relying on them.

targets.name: Erdos #580 (Erdos-Furedi-Loebl-Sos n/2-n/2-n/2 conjecture): a counterexample, or certified verification for n = 20
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (SAT with DRUP/LRAT proofs over the trees on 10 vertices)
targets.statement: Conjecture of Erdos, Furedi, Loebl and Sos (Erdos #580): if at least n/2 vertices of an n-vertex graph G have degree at least n/2, then G contains every tree on at most n/2 vertices.
