pitfalls: Geometry definition: R is measured from the H2 nuclear centre of mass (the midpoint), not from the nearer proton. Ferenc and Matyus show that the 2009 Pavanello et al. value belongs to the nearer-proton convention (7.142 vs 6.442 bohr).
At R = 6.442 and 7.142 the paper prints different values in Tables 1 and 3 (Table 1: -1.674561687 and -1.674547750; Table 3: -1.674561676 and -1.674547764). The bar is the lower of the two.

The extrapolated CBS value -1.67456175(3) is not variational and is not the bar. Beating the raw value by 1e-9 is required. A value below the extrapolated limit should trigger extra scrutiny of linear dependence and precision.

Ferenc and Matyus deposited their optimised basis parameters in the Chem. Phys. Lett. Supplementary Material, so refining that basis is the cheapest route. For the Table 2 point, the text says 5 Powell cycles (4 hours) while footnote d says 1000 cycles. Either way it is less refined than the 3000-cycle point at 6.442 bohr.

Literature status: the 9 works citing the paper (OpenAlex, checked 2026-10-30) report no lower energy. Ferenc-Matyus 2023 (arXiv:2208.03033) reuses -1.674561687. Repeat the search before claiming; it is part of the criterion.

targets.name: DeepVariant case-study accuracy: beat DeepVariant 1.10's documented F1 on its own public held-out inputs, above all ONT R10.4.1 indels (0.9302) and RNA-seq
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours for a chr20 cell (5.9 GB ONT chr20 BAM); a large cloud VM or cluster for whole-genome cells (the HG003 ONT BAM is 131 GB)
targets.statement: Google's DeepVariant team (Pi-Chuan Chang, Andrew Carroll, Kishwar Shafin and colleagues) keeps a public accuracy table for each release: docs/metrics.md and docs/pangenome-aware-metrics.md on branch r1.10 (release v1.10.0, 2026-03-05, still the newest on 2026-10-30). They are whole-genome hap.py (vcfeval) runs against the NIST/GIAB v4.2.1 benchmarks maintained by Justin Zook and Nathan Olson. HG003 has been left out of training since v1.1 and chr20-22 have never been used; HG005 is held out of the RNA-seq model. Current HG003 F1: Illumina WGS 35x, INDEL 0.99598, SNP 0.996136; pangenome-aware WGS (vg Giraffe BAM of the same reads), INDEL 0.996976, SNP 0.998139; WES, INDEL 0.98328, SNP 0.992926 (pangenome-aware SNP 0.993544); PacBio Revio SPRQ, INDEL 0.994173, SNP 0.99852; ONT R10.4.1, INDEL 0.930243 (recall 0.912496, precision 0.948695), SNP 0.998451; hybrid PacBio+Illumina, INDEL 0.996838. HG005 poly-A RNA-seq, GENCODE CDS at 3x or more: SNP 0.951595, INDEL 0.806842. The ONT case-study page adds a chr20 cell (80x ultra-long simplex): INDEL 0.897772, SNP 0.999031. ONT indels (mostly homopolymer length) and RNA-seq calls are where a strong open caller is still well below 0.99. Input BAMs (named in scripts/inference_deepvariant.sh r1.10), truth files and DeepVariant outputs are public over HTTPS on storage.googleapis.com/deepvariant.
targets.success_criterion: A VCF for one cell (a row of the r1.10 metrics pages, or the chr20 ONT case study), called only from that cell's reads (the BAM named in inference_deepvariant.sh r1.10 or the case-study page; realigning those same reads is allowed) on GRCh38 no-alt, with no other data from HG002, HG003, HG004 or HG005, including pangenomes or panels that contain them. The skeptic scores it with hap.py v0.3.12 --engine=vcfeval --pass-only against that preset's truth VCF and BED (HG003: v4.2.1 benchmark_noinconsistent.bed). For RNA-seq the region is the case study's protocol extended to chr1-22 (GENCODE v41 basic CDS, 3x or more coverage, intersected with the HG005 v4.2.1 BED), and the comparator is the higher of the listed value and DeepVariant 1.10 RNASEQ rerun by the skeptic on that region. F1 for the stated variant type must be STRICTLY HIGHER (direction: max) than the best DeepVariant value for that sample and technology on the live pages (for Illumina WGS and WES, the higher of the standard and pangenome-aware rows): by at least 0.005 absolute where that value is below 0.99, otherwise by at least a 10% relative cut in (1 - F1). The other variant type may not fall more than 0.0005 below its best listed F1. The same margins must hold against Clair3 (newest release, matching model; Clair3-RNA for RNA-seq) on the same input; for the hybrid PacBio+Illumina cell, which has no matching Clair3 model, only the DeepVariant comparator applies. The method is released and uses no HG003 or HG005 truth and no chr20-22 truth of any GIAB sample in training or tuning.

partial_wins.statement: On the chr20 ONT R10.4.1 case study (HG003_R104_sup_merged.80x.chr20.bam, scored with the case-study hap.py command, -l chr20): INDEL F1 of at least 0.907772 (0.897772 plus 0.01) with SNP F1 of at least 0.998531, and INDEL F1 above Clair3 (newest release, matching R10.4.1 model) on the same BAM by at least 0.01.

On the HG005 RNA-seq cell under the genome-wide region of the success criterion: SNP F1 above the comparator by at least 0.005, INDEL F1 no lower than the comparator's, and SNP F1 above Clair3-RNA (newest release) on the same BAM and region.

On the HG003 WES cell (HG003.novaseq.wes_idt.100x.dedup.bam with the script's capture BED): INDEL F1 of at least 0.98828 (0.98328 plus 0.005) with SNP F1 of at least 0.993044, and INDEL F1 above Clair3 (newest release, Illumina model) on the same BAM.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the cell's input BAM, reference, truth VCF and BED over plain HTTPS from storage.googleapis.com/deepvariant and the GIAB FTP, reruns the claimant's released pipeline (or checks the VCF's provenance against a rerun on chr20), and runs hap.py --engine vcfeval with the same flags as the r1.10 case-study script. The skeptic compares the PASS rows with the live metrics.md, reruns Clair3 on chr20 as a spot check, and greps the training configuration for HG003, HG005 and chr20-22 truth.
angles: ONT indel errors are dominated by homopolymer length calls; a model that reads per-read base qualities and move tables (or that is phasing-aware within homopolymers) attacks exactly the missing 44,146 false negatives.

Cross-domain import (speech recognition): homopolymer length is a duration-estimation problem, so duration models from speech (explicit length distributions rather than per-frame labels) may beat pileup classification.
Combine DeepVariant and Clair3 candidates with a learned arbiter trained only on HG002/HG004 non-chr20-22 regions; disagreement sites are where both are weakest.
For RNA-seq, model allele-specific expression and RNA editing (A-to-I) explicitly: many RNA false positives are editing sites, not DNA variants.
pitfalls: Training or tuning on HG003 truth (or on chr20-22 of any GIAB sample) is leakage; DeepVariant itself excludes them, so a fair comparison must too.
HG002 is the son of HG003 and HG004 and carries one haplotype of each parent; a pangenome, panel or model input containing HG002 leaks HG003 genotypes. Use HPRC graphs with HG002 removed.
Use the same BED as the table (for HG003 that is v4.2.1 benchmark_noinconsistent.bed); the plain benchmark BED gives different numbers.
hap.py with its default xcmp engine and with vcfeval can disagree on complex indels; the table used vcfeval through the case-study script.
For Illumina WGS the standard row (0.99598 INDEL) is already beaten by DeepVariant's own pangenome-aware mode on the same reads; the comparator is the better of the two rows.
The sample_sheet.tsv linked from metrics.md returns NoSuchKey; the whole-genome input BAM names are in inference_deepvariant.sh r1.10.
Re-basecalling raw signal or adding HiFi reads changes the input and is not a win for a single-technology cell.

The chr20 case-study cells and the whole-genome metrics rows are different cells; never compare a chr20 F1 with a whole-genome F1. The RNA-seq case-study page scores only chr20 (SNP 0.968421 on 287 truth SNPs), not the 11,349-SNP metrics row.

targets.name: DeepSomatic on held-out HCC1395 chr1: beat DeepSomatic 1.10's somatic F1, especially ONT (SNV 0.858, indel 0.737) and tumor-only modes
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours per cell (the tumor and normal chr1 BAMs are 8-10 GB each); a GPU helps but is not required
targets.statement: DeepSomatic (Jimin Park, Daniel Cook, Alexey Kolesnikov, Andrew Carroll, Pi-Chuan Chang and colleagues at Google with Benedict Paten's group at UCSC; Nature Biotechnology 2026, doi 10.1038/s41587-025-02839-x, preprint bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.08.16.608331) calls somatic SNVs and indels from tumor-normal or tumor-only reads. Its case-study pages on github.com/google/deepsomatic, branch r1.10 (DeepSomatic 1.10.0, the newest release on 2026-10-30), score chr1 of HCC1395/HCC1395BL, which is held out during training, with som.py against the SEQC2 high-confidence truth v1.2.1 (Li Tai Fang, Wenming Xiao and the SEQC2 Somatic Mutation Working Group, Nat Biotech 2021). From recall and precision, the chr1 F1 values are (3,440 truth SNVs, 133 truth indels): Illumina WGS, SNV 0.9761 and indel 0.9091; PacBio, SNV 0.9489 and indel 0.8188; ONT, SNV 0.8576 (recall 0.7608) and indel 0.7373; FFPE WGS, SNV 0.8817 and indel 0.7766; tumor-only Illumina WGS, SNV 0.7480 and indel 0.3741; PacBio tumor-only, SNV 0.7751 and indel 0.5178; ONT tumor-only, SNV 0.6705 and indel 0.3653. The metrics.md table reports whole-genome numbers that include training chromosomes. The chr1 BAMs (1-15 GB each), truth VCF and BED are public over HTTPS, so each cell is a self-contained, laptop-scale record.
targets.success_criterion: A somatic VCF for HCC1395 chr1, for one stated mode (tumor-normal or tumor-only) and one technology, called only from that mode's case-study chr1 BAMs, plus declared public population resources (for example gnomAD or a 1000 Genomes panel of normals) that contain no HCC1395 data. It is scored by the skeptic with som.py exactly as in the case-study page: truth high-confidence_sINDEL_sSNV_in_HC_regions_v1.2.1.merged.vcf.gz, -R High-Confidence_Regions_v1.2.bed, -l chr1, --feature-table generic. Its F1 = 2PR/(P+R) for SNVs or indels must be STRICTLY HIGHER (direction: max) than the DeepSomatic value on the newest case-study page for that mode, re-fetched live: by at least 0.01 for SNVs or 0.03 for indels, with the other type no more than 0.005 below its listed F1. It must also beat ClairS (tumor-normal) or ClairS-TO (tumor-only), newest release with the matching model, run on the same BAMs and scored the same way, by the same margin. No HCC1395 chr1 truth, and no SEQC2 callset used to build the truth, may be used in training, tuning or filtering. The method is released.

partial_wins.statement: ONT tumor-normal chr1: SNV recall of at least 0.810756 (0.760756 plus 0.05) with SNV precision of at least 0.97, and SNV F1 above ClairS (newest release, matching ONT model) on the same BAMs.
Illumina WGS tumor-only chr1: SNV F1 of at least 0.7780 (0.7480 plus 0.03) and above ClairS-TO (newest release) on the same BAM, using only declared public germline resources for germline filtering.
FFPE WGS tumor-normal chr1: SNV F1 of at least 0.9017 (0.8817 plus 0.02) and above ClairS (newest release, Illumina model) on the same BAMs.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the chr1 BAMs and reference from storage.googleapis.com/deepvariant/deepsomatic-case-studies/deepsomatic-chr1-case-studies and the truth from .../SEQC2-S1395-truth over plain HTTPS, reruns the claimant's released caller, runs the case-study som.py command in the pkrusche/hap.py container, reruns ClairS or ClairS-TO on the same BAMs, and compares with the live case-study page. One to a few hours per cell.
angles: ONT tumor-normal loses mostly recall (823 of 3,440 SNVs missed), so the gap is in low-VAF candidate generation, not in classification; haplotype-aware candidate rescue (somatic variants sit on one haplotype) is the obvious lever.
Cross-domain import (radio astronomy stacking): pool weak evidence across reads on the same haplotype block before thresholding, rather than deciding per site.
In tumor-only mode the false positives are mostly germline; phase-aware germline/somatic separation using allele fraction relative to local copy number can cut them without a panel of normals.
pitfalls: The whole-genome numbers in metrics.md include chromosomes DeepSomatic was trained on; only chr1 is held out, so only chr1 counts here.
ClairS's README reports HCC1395 numbers against HighConf plus MedConf truth at VAF 0.05 or more, a different truth subset; never compare them with the som.py numbers here.
With 133 truth indels, one or two variants move F1 by about 0.01, which is why the indel margin is 0.03.
SEQC2 consensus callsets were built from the same cell line's data; using them as features or filters leaks the truth.

targets.name: precisionFDA Truth Challenge V2 (finished, answers released): beat the best submission's F1 in difficult-to-map regions or the MHC for HG003/HG004 from the challenge reads
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days per sample for the Illumina 35x cells (alignment plus calling); needs cluster for the 85x ONT and the multi-technology cells
targets.statement: The precisionFDA Truth Challenge V2 (May-June 2020; Olson, Wagner, McDaniel, Zook and colleagues at NIST GIAB with the precisionFDA team, Cell Genomics 2022) gave participants about 35x Illumina NovaSeq, 35x PacBio HiFi (Sequel II) and about 85x ONT R9.4.1 (Guppy 3.6) FASTQs for the then semi-blinded parents HG003 and HG004, with HG002 as the unblinded training sample. Winners were chosen on F1 in all benchmark regions, in difficult-to-map regions (low mappability plus segmental duplications, v2.0 stratifications) and in the MHC. The challenge is over: NIST record mds2-2336 holds the FASTQs, all 64 submitted callsets (192 VCFs, one each for HG002, HG003 and HG004) and their hap.py results, and the v4.2.1 truth for both parents is on the GIAB FTP. Winning F1 values (challenge_winners.tsv): difficult-to-map, Illumina 0.9693 (DRAGEN), PacBio 0.9929 (Sentieon), ONT 0.9825 (PEPPER-DeepVariant), multi-technology 0.9944 (Roche); MHC, Illumina 0.9923 (Seven Bridges GRAF), PacBio 0.9949 (Sentieon), ONT 0.9717 (NanoCaller/Clair/Medaka ensemble), multi-technology 0.9979 (Sentieon). The all-regions Illumina cell (0.9971) is already passed on the same HG003 reads by pangenome-aware DeepVariant 1.10 (SNP 0.998139, INDEL 0.996976), so only the difficult-to-map and MHC cells are offered here, each checked against current tools.
targets.success_criterion: For one technology (ILLUMINA, PACBIO, ONT or MULTI) and one stratum (difficult-to-map = v2.0 union/GRCh38_alllowmapandsegdupregions.bed.gz, or MHC = v2.0 OtherDifficult/GRCh38_MHC.bed.gz): VCFs for HG003 and HG004 made only from that technology's challenge FASTQs in mds2-2336, with HG002 data used only as the challenge allowed and no HG003 or HG004 truth in training or tuning. Besides GRCh38, public graphs, panels or haplotype catalogues may be used only if they contain no sequence or genotypes from HG002, HG003 or HG004 (for example an HPRC graph with HG002 removed). The skeptic scores them with hap.py --engine=vcfeval against each parent's v4.2.1 benchmark (HG00x_GRCh38_1_22_v4.2.1_benchmark.vcf.gz with its benchmark_noinconsistent.bed) restricted to the stratum and takes the harmonic mean of the two parents' combined SNV+INDEL F1. The result must be STRICTLY HIGHER (direction: max), by at least a 10% relative cut in (1 - F1), than (a) the best 2020 submission in that technology category, every one rescored by the skeptic with the identical pipeline, and (b) on HG003 alone, a current caller run on the same HG003 reads with its official preset: DeepVariant 1.10 (the better of WGS and WGS_PANGENOME) for Illumina, PACBIO for PacBio, HYBRID_PACBIO_ILLUMINA for MULTI, and Clair3 (newest release, r941_prom_hac_g360+g422 model) for ONT R9.4.1, for which DeepVariant has no preset. The method is released.

partial_wins.statement: MHC, Illumina only: harmonic-mean parental F1 above the best Illumina submission rescored under the identical pipeline (the GRAF winner was listed at 0.9923), by a 10% relative cut in (1 - F1), with no HG003 or HG004 truth used.

MHC, ONT R9.4.1 only: harmonic-mean parental F1 above the best ONT submission rescored under the identical pipeline (the winning ensemble was listed at 0.9717), by at least 0.005, with no HG003 or HG004 truth used.

A published, reproducible rescoring of every 2020 submission in the eight difficult-to-map and MHC cells with hap.py vcfeval, v4.2.1 and the v2.0 stratifications, giving each cell's best rescored value and any change from challenge_winners.tsv, which fixes comparator (a) for this target.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the claimant's VCFs, the winner's VCFs from mds2-2336 (data.nist.gov, plain HTTPS), the v4.2.1 truth and the v2.0 stratification BEDs, runs hap.py with vcfeval on both, aggregates per the challenge README, and for (b) runs the newest DeepVariant on the HG003 reads or a stated chromosome subset. Hours on a workstation for scoring; the DeepVariant rerun needs a cloud VM.
angles: The MHC is about 4 Mb of extreme polymorphism: local diploid assembly of reads recruited to the MHC, followed by assembly-to-reference calling, sidesteps reference bias in a way read-pileup callers cannot.

Cross-domain import (population genetics): HLA haplotypes are well catalogued, so a graph built from public HLA/MHC haplotypes (IPD-IMGT/HLA, HPRC assemblies with HG002 removed) gives short reads somewhere to map; first confirm that no HG002, HG003 or HG004 haplotype is in the catalogue.
In segmental duplications, paralog-specific variants decide mappability; modelling copy number per duplicated block before calling turns false positives into informative sites.
pitfalls: The data README describes the results table as a geometric mean of the parents' F1, the paper's main text as a harmonic mean (its Methods equation uses the geometric mean); the criterion fixes the harmonic mean and compares rescored VCFs, never printed numbers.
Under rescoring the best submission in a cell may not be the 2020 winner; comparator (a) is the best rescored submission.
Current DeepVariant and Clair3 models train on HG004 (only HG003 is excluded), so they cannot be components of a claim, and comparator (b) is taken on HG003 only.
The all-regions cells are not offered: on the Illumina reads they are already passed by public tools.
Using HiFi or ONT reads for an Illumina-only cell, or any other HG003/HG004 data, breaks the single-technology rule.

targets.name: HG002 vs the Q100 genome benchmark: an automated diploid assembly with fewer GQC errors than the best listed non-curated assembly (38,072)
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (a diploid human assembly takes hundreds of CPU-hours and over 100 GB of RAM; GQC takes about 64 GB and 4 hours per assembly)
targets.statement: The T2T, HPRC and GIAB consortia's HG002 Q100 assembly (marbl/hg002; Hansen, Dwarshuis, Rhie, Koren, Phillippy and colleagues, Cell 2026, doi 10.1016/j.cell.2026.06.016) is a near-perfect diploid genome. Its GQC tool aligns a test assembly to it and counts every substitution and indel discrepancy, along with phase switches, coverage and mononucleotide-run accuracy. The consortium publishes GQC results against hg002v1.1 for many public HG002 assemblies under T2T/HG002/assemblies/benchmarking/analyses/assembly_comparison on the human-pangenomics S3 bucket. The best total outside the curated Q100 lineage (hg002v0.x and v1.x) is verkko_thic_assignedcontigs (v3 exclusion run, Aug 2025): 38,072 errors (6,174 substitutions, 31,898 indels), QV 53 without wrong-haplotype errors, 5,959,494,470 benchmark bases covered (99.3%), 5.51 switches per Mb, NGA50 115.5/115.9 Mb. Next come hifi_q28_trio_hic and verkko_asm_thic at 41,207, the HPRC release 2 assembly hprc_year2 (= hprc_year2_polished) at 42,963 (QV 53, NGA50 about 71 Mb), v2_trio at 48,276, hprc_year2_v2_thic at 51,089 and lc24_medaka_6b4 at 52,842. Every assembly run under both the v3 and the v4 (Feb 2026) exclusion configs has the same total in both. For scale, the curated hg002v1.0.1 has 3,370 errors, so automated pipelines still make about 11 times more. A v1.2 benchmark was released in August 2026, but every listed run is against v1.1. Inputs (HiFi, ONT ultra-long, Hi-C, trio short reads) are public on S3, and the score is a mechanical count.
targets.success_criterion: A diploid HG002 assembly FASTA produced end to end by a released, deterministic pipeline (no manual edits) from public HG002 read data, and optionally public parental reads. It may not use the Q100 assemblies, their patches, the HG002-issues lists, any assembly in the GQC tables, or any reference genome as input. GQC (commit 1fe404c, as in the February 2026 runs, or newer) is run with the hg002v1.1 resources tarball and the v4 exclusion BED (or v3 for a like-for-like check). Total errors must be STRICTLY FEWER (direction: min) than the smallest non-Q100-lineage total in the live assembly_comparison tables (38,072 as of 2026-10-30) by at least 5%, that is at most 36,168. Total v1.1 bases covered must be at least 5,959,494,470, and the switch rate at most 5.5079 per Mb.

partial_wins.statement: An assembly from ONT reads only (no HiFi, Illumina, Element or Hi-C) with fewer total GQC errors than 52,842 (lc24_medaka_6b4's total), with at least 5,964,776,254 v1.1 bases covered.

Polishing: starting from the public HPRC release 2 HG002 assembly (hprc_year2, 42,963 errors), a released polisher using only public reads cuts its total GQC errors by at least 30% (to at most 30,074) without lowering bases covered or raising the switch rate.

Mononucleotide-run accuracy (runs of 10 bp or longer) above the best non-curated listed value (99.308%, hprc_year2_v2_thic) by at least 0.1 percentage point, with at least 5,953,357,669 v1.1 bases covered.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic checks the pipeline's inputs (read accessions only, with no Q100 or assembly files), reruns it or a chromosome-level subset if needed, runs GQC assemblybench against hg002v1.1 with the resources tarball and the exclusion config of the compared run set, and compares the generalstats totals with the live S3 tables. About 4 hours and 64 GB per GQC run.
angles: In hprc_year2 errors split roughly evenly between substitutions and indels and about a quarter match the other haplotype, so better haplotype assignment in low-heterozygosity stretches is worth as much as better consensus; in the Verkko assemblies indels dominate.
Polishing with a k-mer database built from accurate short reads (Element or Illumina) is how the Q100 lineage got from QV 53 to the 70s, and it can be automated.
Cross-domain import (error-correcting codes): treat the HiFi, ONT and short-read layers as independent noisy channels and decode the consensus jointly, rather than polishing in sequence.
pitfalls: The hg002v0.x and v1.x entries are the curated benchmark lineage and are excluded from the comparison.
Use the exclusion BED of a listed run set; adding further exclusions (as the hprc_year2_polished_nodiffregions run does, 2,108 errors) is not comparable.
Listed runs use the v1.1 benchmark; a GQC run against the newer v1.2 resources (the GQC README default since August 2026) is not comparable with them.
Anything derived from the Q100 effort (patch VCFs, HG002-issues, reads aligned to Q100 and used to filter) is leakage, even when used only for filtering.
GQC QV and coverage percentages are rounded; the criterion uses total error counts and covered-base counts.

targets.name: HG002 nanopore read correction scored against the Q100 genome: corrected ONT reads with fewer errors per megabase than HERRO's 88 (GQC readbench)
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster or a GPU workstation for the full about 115 Gb read set; laptop-days for a single-chromosome partial
targets.statement: Correcting ONT reads before assembly is what made ONT-based telomere-to-telomere assembly practical. The HERRO corrector (Dominik Stanojević, Mile Šikić and colleagues) is the reference method used with Verkko and hifiasm. The Q100 team (Nancy Hansen and colleagues; Hansen et al., Cell 2026, supplementary Table S14) aligns read sets to the diploid HG002 benchmark and counts every discrepancy with GQC readbench, publishing the results under T2T/HG002/assemblies/benchmarking/analyses/read_evaluation on the human-pangenomics S3 bucket. Current values (gqc_sep2025 runs): ONT Q28 HERRO-corrected reads, 10,193,695 errors in 115,022,133,633 aligned bases, or 88.62 errors per Mb (3 substitutions and 84 indels per Mb, 277,178,935 clipped bases). Its BAM header shows the input was HG002.experimentalUL.corrected.fasta.gz, aligned with Winnowmap 2.03 (--MD -W repetitive_k15.txt -ax map-pb -I12g -y) and filtered with samtools view -F0x104. The HERRO README publishes that file (Zenodo record 13252378) as HERRO-corrected reads of ONT's experimental high-accuracy ultra-long GM24385 release (EPI2ME gm24385_ncm23_preview, s3://ont-open-data/gm24385_2023.12/, 125 Gbp at Q10 or more, read N50 91 kbp), so the raw input is public. Uncorrected ONT Epi2Me Q28 reads have 3,055 per Mb, ONT R10 ultra-long Dorado v0.3.4 reads 26,113 per Mb, PacBio Revio SPRQ HiFi 1,060 per Mb and the best short reads (Onso) 470 per Mb. Corrected reads already beat HiFi, but nearly all remaining errors are indels, mostly in homopolymers and short tandem repeats. Raw ONT reads and the scored BAMs are public, so a better corrector shows up as a mechanical error count when compared with HERRO on the same input.
targets.success_criterion: A corrected read set derived only from public HG002 ONT reads, with the source accessions stated. Correction may not use HiFi, Illumina, Element or Onso reads, any assembly, or any reference genome. The reads are aligned to the hg002v1.1 diploid benchmark with Winnowmap 2.03 using the listed run's options (--MD -W repetitive_k15.txt -ax map-pb -I12g -y), unmapped and secondary alignments are removed with samtools view -F0x104 (as in the listed BAM), and they are scored with GQC readbench (no downsampling) with the hg002v1.1 resources. Errors per Mb of aligned bases must be STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min), by at least 10% relative, than both (a) the HERRO-corrected row in the live read_evaluation results (88.62 per Mb as of 2026-10-30, so at most 79.76) and (b) HERRO (newest release) run by the skeptic on the same raw input reads, aligned and scored identically. Aligned bases must be at least 115.0 Gb and at least those of (b), and clipped bases no more than 0.25% of aligned bases. The corrector is released.

partial_wins.statement: Restricted to reads whose primary alignment is to chr20 (either haplotype): errors per Mb at least 10% lower than HERRO run by the skeptic on the same raw input and scored the same way, with aligned bases on chr20 no lower than HERRO's.

Indel errors per Mb at least 15% lower than HERRO's on the same raw input (and below the listed row's 84.96 per Mb), at equal or greater aligned yield, even if substitutions rise, provided total errors per Mb stay at most 88.62.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic confirms that the corrector's inputs are ONT reads only, runs HERRO on the same raw reads (or a stated chromosome subset), aligns both corrected sets to hg002v1.1 with Winnowmap 2.03 -ax map-pb, runs GQC readbench on both with the same resources, and compares errors per Mb, aligned bases and clipped bases with each other and with the live read_evaluation generalstats file. GPU hours for HERRO, then hours to a day per readbench run.
angles: Indels are 84 of the 88 errors per Mb, so the target is homopolymer and short-tandem-repeat length; correcting run lengths jointly across overlapping reads from the same haplotype is the direct attack.
Cross-domain import (speech and duration modelling): estimate homopolymer length as a duration with an explicit length distribution conditioned on context, rather than a per-base vote.
Use the raw signal or the move tables where they are public: run length is better resolved in signal space than in called bases, and this stays ONT-only.
pitfalls: Dropping hard reads or clipping hard regions lowers the error rate trivially; hence the aligned-yield and clipping constraints.
Newer or deeper raw ONT data alone lowers the error rate; that is why the claim must also beat HERRO run on the same raw input.
Correction toward GRCh38, CHM13, HPRC assemblies or the Q100 genome is not ONT-only correction and is forbidden, even indirectly as k-mer filters.
The Q100 v1.1 benchmark was itself polished using HG002 reads, which may include the ONT data being corrected; report which read set you used.
Aligner choice changes clipping and error counts; use the listed run's aligner and settings.
Downsampling in readbench changes counts; the listed rows use full alignments.

targets.name: Connected maximum-density still lifes: close a gap in Mahajan's n = 26..50 table (OEIS A398723), starting with 349 <= a(26) <= 352
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (CP-SAT / MaxSAT on 26x26..50x50 boards for lower bounds; certified upper bounds may take laptop-days)
targets.statement: Place live cells in an n x n square so that the whole plane, with every cell outside the square dead, is a still life under Conway's Life (B3/S23). Every live cell has 2 or 3 live neighbours, and no dead cell (inside the square or in the ring just outside it) has exactly 3. All live cells must also form one component under king-move (8-neighbour) adjacency. Maximise the population. This is the Connected Maximum-density Still Life benchmark of the Fourth ASP Competition (2013). Chu and Stuckey (2012) solved the unconnected version (A055397) for all n. Siddhartha Mahajan (2026, OEIS A398723, GitHub release v1.0.1) proved exact values for n = 1..25 and n = 31, 32, 33, 39, each with a witness and an upper-bound proof (row-DP enumeration, Chu-Stuckey's unconnected maxima, or his bound C(n) <= floor((4n^2+5n-d[n mod 8])/8) for n >= 14). The problem was also used in the CAISc 2026 verifiable-problems track, which ended in July 2026. His live table docs/RESULTS.md (repository last updated 2026-10-28; unchanged on 2026-10-30) gives these open bounds as (lower, upper): 26 (349,352), 27 (375,378), 28 (406,407), 29 (433,435), 30 (462,465), 34 (594,597), 35 (625,631), 36 (665,668), 37 (701,704), 38 (738,742), 40 (815,821), 41 (858,863), 42 (902,906), 43 (940,948), 44 (989,993), 45 (1034,1037), 46 (1077,1083), 47 (1126,1132), 48 (1174,1178), 49 (1223,1228), 50 (1276,1279). a(26) is the first unresolved OEIS term.
targets.success_criterion: Full win: the exact value of a(26). This needs (1) a 26 x 26 board that passes the checks below, with population P, and (2) a proof that no connected still life in the 26 x 26 square has population P+1 or more. The proof is either (a) a DRAT/LRAT UNSAT certificate checked by drat-trim or cake_lpr, or a VeriPB certificate checked by veripb, or (b) an exhaustive enumeration or dynamic-programming bound. Either way it must be produced by two independently written programs or encodings that agree. Board checks: run one Life step on the (n+4) x (n+4) zero-padded board and get the identical board back; confirm by BFS that the live cells form one 8-connected component; count the cells. Before claiming, re-fetch the live RESULTS.md and OEIS A398723 and confirm the value is still open there. A solver's 'optimal' status without a checked certificate or independent reproduction is not a proof.

partial_wins.statement: For any open n in 26..50, a board that passes the checks, with population STRICTLY greater than the Lower value in the live RESULTS.md at verification time.

For any open n in 26..50, a proof meeting the full-win proof standard that no connected still life in the n x n square has population U or more, where U is at most the live Upper value, so the table's upper bound drops. The same encoding or program must reproduce the known exact values for n = 10..16 (feasible at the optimum, infeasible at optimum+1).
Any other open n in 26..50 closed exactly (a matching board and an upper bound to the same standard).

targets.verification_method: Write an independent numpy Life stepper and an 8-connectivity BFS, and run them on the claimed board JSON or RLE. For upper bounds, check the proof file with drat-trim / cake_lpr (or veripb), and inspect the encoding: cells outside the square must be forced dead and must stay dead, and connectivity must be encoded soundly (e.g. flow or spanning-tree constraints). Re-run the encoder on n <= 25 against Mahajan's proof index. Fetch RESULTS.md and A398723 live.
angles: Seed from Mahajan's own n26..n50 constructions and from Chu-Stuckey optimal unconnected patterns. Then run large-neighbourhood search with CP-SAT: free a window, re-solve it, and keep connectivity with a flow formulation.
Upper bounds: adapt Chu-Stuckey's relaxation (per-cell wastage accounting over 3x3 windows) and add connectivity cuts. The gaps of 1-3 at n = 26..30 are the natural first attacks.
Sizes with gap 1 (n = 28) are the cheapest exact closures.
pitfalls: A055397 values are for unconnected still lifes. Several of Mahajan's upper bounds (e.g. n = 28, 36, 44, 47) already equal them, so they are not new upper bounds you can claim.
Connectivity is by king moves (8-neighbour), not rook moves.
Births in the ring just outside the square are forbidden; a board that is stable only on a bounded grid fails.
The table moves (repository last updated 2026-10-28). Re-fetch it before claiming.

CAISc 2026 accepted several connected-still-life papers: V. P. T. Menta (cited in A055397), A. S. Jaswal ('... up to n = 32'), T. Sodha, P. Sridhar, A. A. Rushdi, Collier-Derfer and Reddy et al. The track's accepted sizes were 8-21 (subset), 31 and 32, and Menta's public repo (github.com/praxelhq/connected-still-life) is below Mahajan's values (n = 31: 485, n = 32: 515). OpenReview showed a bot check here (BLOCKED), so check those papers, especially Jaswal's, for n = 26..30 values before any claim.

targets.name: Game of Life still-life enumeration: the number of strict and pseudo still lifes with 35 cells (A019473, A056613), or quasi still lifes with 23 cells (A330283)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (counting, not listing: a(34) is 3.5e10 strict still lifes, and a(35) is expected to be about 2.5 times larger; the quasi count at n = 23 is laptop-hours)
targets.statement: Count finite still lifes in Conway's Life (B3/S23) with exactly n live cells, up to rotation and reflection. A strict still life cannot be split into two or more smaller still lifes (A019473). A pseudo still life can be split that way (A056613, using the 'two or more' definition). A quasi still life is made of two or more strict still lifes that share dead neighbour cells which stay dead for the same reason as when the parts are separated (A330283). Current state: A019473 and A056613 are known through n = 34 (strict a(34) = 35,422,864,104; pseudo a(34) = 41,058,173,683). The terms beyond 30 were computed by Nathaniel Johnston with Simon Ekström's still-life enumeration program, with a(34) added in January 2020. Earlier terms came from Robert Munafo, Mark Niemiec, Ekström and others. A330283 (Johnston, Dec 2019) is known through n = 22 (26,943,317). Wikipedia's still-life table is documented only up to 34 cells. Strictness can be decided in polynomial time (Cook 2003).
targets.success_criterion: An exact value of A019473(35) or A056613(35), computed by two independent programs that agree. At least one program must not be derived from Ekström's code. Both programs must reproduce every listed term for n <= 30 exactly, and at least one must reproduce n = 31..34. At claim time the value must be in neither the live OEIS entry nor the enumeration table of Wikipedia's 'Still life (cellular automaton)' article. Report the run logs, the per-n counts and the symmetry-class breakdown (counts by symmetry group), so a skeptic can re-run any slice.

partial_wins.statement: The exact value of A330283(23) (quasi still lifes with 23 cells), from two independent programs that also reproduce A330283(8..22) exactly, and not already in the live OEIS entry.

An independent confirmation of A019473(34) and A056613(34): a program not derived from Ekström's code reproduces both 34-cell counts exactly, with logs and per-symmetry-class counts. A discrepancy counts instead only if two independent programs agree on the new value and it is backed by explicit lists of the disputed objects.

targets.verification_method: Run both programs. Spot-check samples of enumerated objects with lifelib (apgcode, still-life test, strict/pseudo classification) and with an independent numpy stepper. Compare the small-n counts with OEIS, and check that the strict and pseudo totals at each n agree with a single combined enumeration of all still lifes. Fetch the OEIS entries live.
pitfalls: Strict, pseudo and quasi have different definitions. A056605 is a known incorrect version of the strict count, so do not reproduce it.
Counting is up to the 8 symmetries of the square, so orbit counting must handle the symmetric objects correctly.
Strict still lifes need not be 8-connected (several islands can stabilise each other), so a pure polyplet enumeration misses objects.
Use 64-bit (or wider) counters.

The OEIS 2026-10-27 edit (A019473 rev. 73) added a MathWorld link, not a new term. Wikipedia (edited 2026-09-19) and search snippets of LifeWiki's Still life page stop at 34 cells (strict, pseudo) and 22 cells (quasi). LifeWiki and the conwaylife.com forums were Cloudflare-blocked here (BLOCKED), so check them by any route that is not blocked before claiming.

targets.name: MOONSHOT - Firing squad synchronization: a 5-state minimal-time solution, or a certified proof that none exists (Mazoyer's 6 states have stood since 1987)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (SAT on joint space-time diagrams for all lengths n = 2..N with an unknown transition table)
targets.statement: The firing squad synchronization problem (Myhill 1957) concerns a line of n identical finite automata with a boundary marker * beyond each end. At time 0 the leftmost cell is the general G and all others are quiescent Q. Each cell updates from (left, self, right) by one shared table. Q must be stable: (Q,Q,Q) -> Q and (Q,Q,*) -> Q. All n cells must enter the firing state F for the first time simultaneously. Minimal time is 2n-2. Mazoyer (1987) gave a 6-state minimal-time solution, the smallest known (states counted including F). Balzer (1967) claimed, and Sanders (1994) confirmed with a corrected exhaustive search, that no 4-state minimal-time solution exists. Wikipedia still says it is unknown whether a five-state solution exists. The Correa-Gustavo-Lemos-Settle survey (arXiv 2017) calls the existence of a complete 5-state solution (minimal-time or not) the most significant open problem in the area. Only partial 5-state solutions are known: e.g. Umeo-Yanagihara (2007, 2009) synchronize lengths n = 2^k in 3n-3 steps, which is neither all lengths nor minimal time. Clergue, Verel and Formenti (2018) found 718 further 6-state minimal-time solutions, and Nguyen and Maignan (2020) generated millions more, but none with 5 states. A minimal-time solution must synchronize every n, so nonexistence follows from the unsatisfiability of the finite family n = 2..N for some N.
targets.success_criterion: Either (A) or (B), under the stated conventions (left-end general, n >= 2, boundary symbol *, F never appears before time 2n-2, all cells F at exactly time 2n-2; the mirror-image right-end convention is equivalent). (A) A 5-state transition table with a machine-checked proof (Lean, Coq or Isabelle) that it is a minimal-time solution for every n >= 2. (B) A DRAT/LRAT UNSAT certificate, checked by drat-trim or cake_lpr, showing that no 5-state table synchronizes all lengths n = 2..N in exactly 2n-2 steps, for an explicitly stated N. Two independently written encodings must both be UNSAT. Sanity checks on the same encoders: SAT, with Mazoyer's table (or another verified 6-state solution) found or accepted, when 6 states are allowed; UNSAT when 4 states are allowed.

partial_wins.statement: A 5-state table, with Q, G, F and two further states under the conventions above, that a simulator verifies synchronizes every length n = 2..200 in exactly 2n-2 steps, with no F before then. No proof for all n is needed.

A DRAT/LRAT-certified machine proof of the Balzer-Sanders theorem (no 4-state minimal-time solution), by UNSAT of n = 2..N with two independent encodings that pass the 6-state SAT sanity check. It counts only if the verifier's literature check finds no earlier formal or certified proof.

targets.verification_method: For tables: simulate every n in the claimed range with an independent 30-line simulator, checking that F first appears at time 2n-2 in all cells simultaneously. For (A): build the proof assistant file and check that the statement matches the conventions. For (B) and p2: check the certificates, read both encodings (variables for table entries delta(l,c,r) over the non-F centre states, and space-time cell variables for every n), and re-run the 6-state SAT and 4-state UNSAT sanity checks.
angles: Incremental SAT: add the lengths n = 2, 3, 4, ... as constraints on one shared table, break the symmetry between the two free states, and watch whether the solution count collapses.
Seed the table structure from the 6-state families (Clergue-Verel-Formenti, Nguyen-Maignan local simulations): try to merge two states of a known solution and repair with SAT.
pitfalls: Convention drift. Sanders states the restriction with the initiator at the right end (the mirror image). Some papers allow the general anywhere (the generalized problem, which is a different open question) or use rings.
A table that works for n <= N but whose UNSAT or SAT status depends on an encoding bug. Run the 4-state and 6-state sanity checks.
Non-minimal-time 5-state solutions do not count toward (A) or (B), although a complete one would settle the survey's broader open question.
Hybrid (non-uniform) CA 'solutions', e.g. arXiv 1212.3069's 4-state rule 60/102 hybrid, are a different model and do not count.

An audit on 2026-10-30 found no 2021-2026 arXiv paper or web result on 5-state minimal-time solutions, and Wikipedia (edited 2026-10-22) still calls the question open. Journal papers off arXiv (Umeo, Yunes, Kobayashi) were not searched exhaustively, so re-check them before claiming.

targets.name: Counting n x n Life configurations: still lifes in the 16 x 16 square (A136278 a(16)) and patterns that vanish in one step in the 15 x 15 square (A134963 a(15))
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (cell-by-cell transfer-matrix or BDD counting; the naive frontier is 2n+2 cells, i.e. 2^32-2^34 states at n = 15-16, so sparse or hashed state storage, or splitting the frontier, is needed; 128-bit or multi-modular arithmetic)
targets.statement: Count configurations confined to an n x n square, with all cells outside dead, evolving under Conway's Life (B3/S23) on the infinite plane. A136278(n) counts those that are unchanged after one step, including that no birth happens just outside the square. A134963(n) counts those whose successor is empty. Counts are not reduced by symmetry. Don Knuth introduced both (OEIS 2008, TAOCP Vol. 4A, Sec. 7.1.4). Tomas Rokicki corrected A136278 and extended it to n = 15 in 2010: a(15) = 1,327,574,905,899,625,395,329,686. A134963 is known through n = 14 (a(14) = 4,080,967,796,136,376,032,811,105,207,453, last edit 2015). Neither sequence has been extended since. A small brute force written for this check reproduced a(1..4) of both (1, 2, 12, 83 and 2, 11, 51, 860), which confirms the dead-exterior convention.
targets.success_criterion: The exact value of A136278(16) or A134963(15), computed by two independent methods that agree. For example, a transfer-matrix count in exact big integers, plus a second implementation (another frontier order, or the same algorithm run modulo several 64-bit primes and recombined by the CRT, with a code base written separately). Both methods must reproduce every listed term of the sequence exactly. The value must not already be in the live OEIS entry at claim time.

partial_wins.statement: The exact value of the other sequence's next term, under the same two-method rule. Both terms together count as one full win, and the second term as this partial.

The counts of rotation- and reflection-inequivalent configurations for A136278 n = 1..15 (a new companion table), computed via Burnside's lemma with two independent implementations whose fixed-point counts for the identity element reproduce A136278.

targets.verification_method: Run both programs. Check them against the brute force for n <= 5 and against every OEIS term. For modular runs, check the CRT reconstruction across disjoint prime sets. Fetch OEIS live.
pitfalls: Cells just outside the square must stay dead (births outside are forbidden). A count on a bounded board with a 'no neighbours outside' convention gives different numbers.
Counts are not symmetry-reduced.

The terms overflow 64 bits (a(14) of A134963 is about 4e30). Unsigned 128-bit integers suffice for A136278(16) (about 4e27) and A134963(15) (about 1e35), or use big integers or several primes with the CRT.

A134963's extension line reads 'a(12)-a(15) from Tomas Rokicki, Oct 31 2010', but only a(12)..a(14) were entered (history revision #2). A value of a(15) may exist in Rokicki's or Knuth's notes, so check before claiming.
The A134963 growth ratio jumps between n = 13 and 14. An independent counter reproduced a(13) mod 2^64 and a(14) mod 2^32, so this is real, not a typo.

targets.name: Still-life counts in other Life-like rules: HighLife a(14) (A175000), 2x2 a(11) (A166476), Move a(11) (A175001), Maze a(10) (A175002)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: OEIS lists the number of strict still lifes with n live cells, up to rotation and reflection, for several Life-like rules. Christian Schroeder (2010) and Nathaniel Johnston (2009) computed short initial runs that have not been extended since: HighLife B36/S23 (A175000) through n = 13 (218), 2x2 B36/S125 (A166476) through n = 10 (126), Move/Morley B368/S245 (A175001) through n = 10 (3), and Maze B3/S12345 (A175002) through n = 9 (669). Strict means the pattern is stable under the rule and cannot be split into two or more still lifes of that rule. Pseudo still lifes are excluded. HighLife and Life share S23, so a HighLife still life is a Life still life in which no dead cell has exactly 6 live neighbours. Strictness must still be re-decided under the HighLife rule.
targets.success_criterion: A new exact term for any of the four sequences: A175000(14), A166476(11), A175001(11) or A175002(10). It must come from two independent enumerators that agree. Each must reproduce every listed term of that sequence, and one must be a general Life-like-rule enumerator, not a filter of a Life still-life list. Report the objects as RLE or apgcodes so a skeptic can re-check stability and strictness one by one. The term must not already be in the live OEIS entry at claim time.

partial_wins.statement: Any one new term as above (each sequence's next term counts once).
Three or more further consecutive terms of one sequence (e.g. A175000(14..16)), each meeting the same two-enumerator rule.

targets.verification_method: Re-step every reported object under the stated rule with an independent stepper (lifelib supports arbitrary outer-totalistic rules) and check stability. Check strictness by testing every partition of the live cells into still-life parts (or with Cook's skew-symmetric-graph method adapted to the rule). Canonicalise under the 8 symmetries and count. Compare small n with OEIS.
pitfalls: Strictness depends on the rule. A Life-strict object can be pseudo in another rule, and the reverse.

Births can only happen in the one-cell ring around the pattern (no rule here has B0), but that ring must be checked under the rule's own birth set: B6 and B8 kill many Life still lifes in HighLife, 2x2 and Move.
LifeWiki pages for these rules (Cloudflare-blocked here) may already list longer counts. A term already published there is a re-derivation, not a new result, so check before claiming.

targets.name: Elementary CA on rings: the maximum cycle length of Rule 30 (A334497) and Rule 110 (A204371) on a cyclic width of 37
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (exhaustive over 2^37 states, reduced by rotation, the only symmetry that commutes with Rules 30 and 110; bitset memory of order 16 GB, or a disk-backed variant)
targets.statement: Run an elementary cellular automaton on a cyclic universe of n cells. Every start eventually enters a cycle. A334497(n) is the longest eventual period over all starts for Rule 30, and A204371(n) the same for Rule 110. Both are listed for n = 1..36. A334497(36) = 2,237,472. Credits for A334497: a(1..7) Bradley Klee, a(8..12) Jinyuan Wang, a(13..22) Pontus von Brömssen, and a(23..36) transcribed by Paolo Xausa in 2023 from Table 2 of Gage, Laub and McGarry (2005). That paper's full state-space census (its Table 1) covers widths 5..24 only, and it lists larger widths as further research, so a(25..36) may not come from an exhaustive search. Wolfram (1986, 'Random sequence generation by cellular automata') published maximum-cycle values for widths up to 54. Gage et al. found larger cycles than Wolfram at widths 22, 27 and 30 (the bold rows of their Table 2), so those 1986 values are not exhaustive and serve only as lower bounds; OEIS lists no term beyond 36. A204371(36) = 1584 (Ben Branman 2012, extended by Lars Blomberg 2015), and A204371(n) >= A180001(n), the eventual period of a single live cell, so A204371(37) >= 4403. Small brute-force checkers written for this check reproduced both sequences for n <= 18.
targets.success_criterion: The exact value of A334497(37) or A204371(37) (or any later term), from an exhaustive search over all 2^n states, or over all rotation orbits with the rotation factor accounted for. It must be run by two independent implementations that agree. Both must reproduce A334497(1..24) and A204371(1..30) exactly, and both must report their values for A334497(25..30). Where these differ from the listed terms, the claim must also meet partial p1's correction rule. A value below a listed term means a bug, because every listed term comes from an observed cycle. A witness state on the maximal cycle must be given, so a skeptic can confirm the cycle length by direct iteration. Bit order must follow the Wolfram rule-number convention, which the small-n reproduction checks. The term must not already be in the live OEIS entry at claim time.

partial_wins.statement: An independent exhaustive recomputation of A334497(25..36). OEIS took a(23..36) from a 2005 conference table whose full census stopped at width 24. The recomputation either confirms every term or corrects one, and a correction must exhibit a cycle longer than the listed value, verified by iteration.
An independent exhaustive recomputation of A204371(31..36) by a second implementation, with the same confirm-or-correct rule.

targets.verification_method: Re-iterate the witness state for the claimed number of steps and check that it returns to itself with no shorter period, by testing the divisors of the claimed length. Re-run one implementation on a held-out width. Inspect the exhaustive code: it should mark visited states or orbits, take the eventual image, and walk each cycle once.
pitfalls: A cycle found by random sampling is only a lower bound; the term needs exhaustive coverage. Wolfram's 1986 sampled values for widths 37..54 are lower bounds of this kind: a new term must be at least as large as Wolfram's value for that width, or the discrepancy must be explained. For Rule 110, A180001(37) = 4403 is a further floor.
Rotation-orbit methods must convert an orbit cycle into the true period of the state (orbit length times the rotation offset needed to return).
Reflection does not commute with Rule 30 or Rule 110 (their mirror images are Rules 86 and 124). Do not reduce by reflection.
A334497 is the maximum eventual period, not the maximum transient or the number of cycles.
A334497(25..36) may come from a non-exhaustive search (see statement), so a mismatch there is not by itself evidence of a bug in your exhaustive code. Resolve it with a witness cycle.

targets.name: Cellular automata on graphs: the next maximum period for Life on simple graphs (A384209) and for totalistic or outer-totalistic rules on connected graphs (A357951-A357953)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (nauty geng enumerates the 12,005,168 graphs on 10 vertices for A384209(10), the 11,117 connected graphs on 8 vertices for A357951(8), or the 261,080 connected graphs on 9 vertices for A357952(9) and A357953(9); each graph needs all 2^n states, times all rules for the totalistic variants)
targets.statement: Put two-state automata on the vertices of a finite graph. A384209(n) (Pontus von Brömssen, 2025) is the longest cycle period of Conway's Life rule (a live vertex survives with 2 or 3 live neighbours; a dead vertex is born with exactly 3) over all simple graphs on n vertices and all starting states. It is known for n = 1..9: 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 4, 8, 14, 27. Von Brömssen's 2022 sequences take the maximum over connected graphs on n nodes, all rules of a class and all starts: outer-totalistic rules A357951 (n <= 7, a(7) = 66), totalistic rules counting the node itself A357952 (n <= 8, a(8) = 112), and totalistic rules not counting the node A357953 (n <= 8, a(8) = 96). The OEIS entries give optimal examples: graph6 graphs for A384209, and graphs, rules and starts for the A35795x sequences. A checker written for this check reproduced A384209(1..7) from the networkx graph atlas.
targets.success_criterion: A new exact term of any of the four sequences: A384209(10), A357951(8), A357952(9) or A357953(9), or a later term. It must come from exhaustive enumeration of all graphs of the class (nauty geng, connected graphs where required), all rules of the class and all 2^n states. Two independent implementations must agree and reproduce every listed term. The result must include a witness (graph6 string, rule, start state) whose cycle length equals the claimed value under direct simulation. The term must not already be in the live OEIS entry at claim time.

partial_wins.statement: Any one new term as above (each sequence's next term counts once).

Two or more further consecutive terms of one sequence (e.g. A384209(10) and A384209(11)), each meeting the full-win rules: exhaustive enumeration, two agreeing implementations and a simulated witness.

targets.verification_method: Simulate the witness from its graph6 string with an independent stepper and confirm the minimal period. Confirm the geng graph counts per n (OEIS A000088 for all graphs, A001349 for connected graphs). Re-run the enumerators on n <= 7 against the OEIS data.
pitfalls: A384209 ranges over all simple graphs, including disconnected ones, where the period is the lcm of the component periods. The A35795x sequences use connected graphs only.
A357952 counts the node itself in the totalistic sum, and A357953 does not.
For outer-totalistic rules, the birth and survival sets range over 0..n-1 neighbours. Pruning rules by the graph's actual degree set is allowed only if the pruning is shown to be complete.

targets.name: CAMI II genome binning: recover more near-complete genomes from the gold-standard co-assembly than any binner on the CAMI Benchmarking Portal (marine, strain-madness, plant-associated)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (pooled gold-standard assemblies of a few Gbp plus 10, 100 or 21 short-read samples of about 5 Gbp each to map for coverage; 32-64 GB RAM advisable, GPU optional)
targets.statement: Genome binning groups assembled contigs into per-genome bins. The second CAMI challenge (Fernando Meyer, Alice McHardy, Alexander Sczyrba and about 100 co-authors, Nature Methods 2022) released three simulated metagenomes with full gold standards: marine (10 samples, 976 bins in the binning gold standard), strain-madness (100 samples, 408 bins, many strains above 95% ANI) and plant-associated (21 samples, 831 bins). The CAMI Benchmarking Portal (Meyer, Robertson et al., NAR 2025) scores every public upload with AMBER against the gold standard and keeps a live table. On 2026-10-30, the best counts for binning the pooled short-read gold-standard assembly (GSA) at >90% completeness and <5% contamination were as follows. Marine: 351 (CompleteBin 1.1.0.2; 354 at <10%), then COMEBin 1.0.4 base (316), COMEBin 1.0.3 (313), COMEBERT-2 and COMEBERT-S (307 each), SemiBin 2.1.0 and Vamb fa045c0 (264) and UltraBinner (261). Strain-madness: 77 (CONCOCT 0.4.1; 82 at <10%). Plant-associated: 118 (VAMB 3.0.1; 119 at <10%). The COMEBin paper (Wang et al., Nat Commun 2024) reports 337 near-complete marine GSA bins under its own settings. The Briefings in Bioinformatics 2025 benchmark by Yazhini, Morice, Jochheim, Lieser and Söding finds SemiBin2 and COMEBin best overall. All three datasets remain far from their gold standards, strain-madness most of all.
targets.success_criterion: A genome binning (CAMI binning format) of the pooled short-read gold-standard assembly of the CAMI II marine dataset, produced by released deterministic code with the seed stated, that AMBER (the version the portal uses, with the portal's default options and no filter or exclusion that the record row does not use) scores at STRICTLY MORE than 351 genomes recovered with >90% completeness and <5% contamination (direction: max). It must also beat the largest such count for the same assembly in the live portal table at https://cami-challenge.org/datasets/marine/marmgCAMI2_short_read_pooled_gold_standard_assembly/genome_binning/ (re-fetched immediately before claiming) and in any paper found by a novelty search that uses the same AMBER definition. No reference database, marker set or pretrained model may contain the CAMI II source genomes; anything taxonomy-based must use references frozen at or before 2019-01-08, the CAMI II cutoff.

partial_wins.statement: Strain-madness pooled GSA: STRICTLY MORE than 77 genomes at >90% completeness and <5% contamination by AMBER, beating the live portal maximum for that assembly, under the same rules.
Plant-associated pooled short-read GSA: STRICTLY MORE than 118 genomes at >90% completeness and <5% contamination by AMBER, beating the live portal maximum for that assembly, under the same rules.

Marine pooled GSA: one binning with adjusted Rand index (bp) STRICTLY GREATER than 0.887 and at least 300 genomes at >90% completeness and <5% contamination. No portal row on 2026-10-30 has both: the rows with 300 or more such genomes have ARI (bp) of at most 0.854 (CompleteBin 1.1.0.2; COMEBin 1.0.3 has 0.841), and the rows at or above 0.887 (MetaWRAP 1.3.2 at 0.990, SemiBin 2.1.0 at 0.887) recover at most 264.

Reproduce a portal row from scratch (for example COMEBin 1.0.3 at 313, or CompleteBin 1.1.0.2 at 351 genomes at <5% contamination) within 2% using released commands, confirming that the record is reproducible.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the CAMI II GSA and the genome-binning gold-standard mapping (frl.publisso.de/data/frl:6425521), runs AMBER (github.com/CAMI-challenge/AMBER) on the claimed binning file with the same options as the record row, reads the ' > 90% completeness, <5% contamination' count, and compares it with the live portal table. Optionally reruns the released binner to check that it reproduces the file. Minutes to evaluate, hours to rerun.
angles: Ensemble refinement: the Nat Commun 2026 binning benchmark (PMC13079874) reports more than 30% more high-quality genomes from refining the top three binners' outputs together; no such ensemble row is on the portal yet.
Exploit the multi-sample coverage (10 marine samples) with per-sample embedding splits, which the Briefings 2025 benchmark found helps.
Strain-madness: cluster on coverage alone first (the COMEBin paper's no-k-mer variant beat full COMEBin there), then split strains by variant-aware coverage.
pitfalls: The portal shows separate <10% and <5% contamination columns. The headline here is <5%, so compare like with like.
Pooled GSA, per-sample GSA and MEGAHIT assemblies are different tables. A count on one is not a record on another.
The 'Filter out circular element' option changes completeness but barely moves the recovered-genome counts (CompleteBin shows 351 either way). State the option you use and match the record row.
Most CAMI II genomes were newly sequenced for the challenge, but they have since become public. Newer GTDB/RefSeq releases and models pretrained on large genome sets can therefore leak the answer.
Paper-reported counts (for example COMEBin's 337) come from different AMBER settings and are not directly comparable with portal rows.

targets.name: CAMI II metagenome assembly: beat MetaHipMer 2.2.0's strain F1 on the marine short-read co-assembly in the CAMI Benchmarking Portal
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (co-assembling 10 marine samples of about 5 Gbp short reads each needs roughly 100-500 GB RAM; MetaQUAST against 977 reference genomes takes hours)
targets.statement: CAMI II (Meyer et al., Nature Methods 2022) released the reads and source genomes of its simulated marine metagenome. The CAMI Benchmarking Portal (Meyer, Robertson et al., NAR 2025) evaluates assemblies with MetaQUAST. It ranks them on strain recall (the fraction of genomes assembled at >=90% completeness and <=5 mismatches per 100 kb), strain precision, their F1, auNGA, IDY and genome fraction. On 2026-10-30 the live table for the marine Illumina pooled co-assembly was led by MetaHipMer 2.2.0, with strain F1 29.27% (recall 17.21%, precision 97.67%, genome fraction 38.49%). Next by F1 were HipMer 1.0 (20.59%), metaSPAdes 4.0.0 (17.09%), Ray Meta 2.3.1 (16.71%), MEGAHIT 1.2.7 (15.06%) and GATB 1.0 (13.54%). The gold-standard assembly reaches 63.32% strain recall and 76.98% genome fraction. On plant-associated short reads, MetaHipMer 2.0.0 leads with strain F1 13.21%. Strain-madness remains the hardest: the best strain recall is 3.92% (HipMer 1.0), against 90.2% for the gold standard. Assembling closely related strains from short reads is the open core of the problem.
targets.success_criterion: A co-assembly (FASTA) of the 10 CAMI II marine short-read samples, produced by released code from the reads alone (no reference genomes, no CAMI gold-standard contigs, no long reads). Its F1 strain score must be STRICTLY GREATER than 29.27% (MetaHipMer 2.2.0; direction: max) and greater than every row in the live table at https://cami-challenge.org/datasets/marine/marmgCAMI2_short_read_pooled_assembly/assembly/, re-fetched immediately before claiming. The score is computed with the portal's MetaQUAST settings (min identity 95%, the record row's options) against the same marine reference sequence set the portal uses. The assembly must also have IDY of at least 99.0%.

partial_wins.statement: Plant-associated short-read pooled co-assembly: F1 strain score STRICTLY GREATER than 13.21% (MetaHipMer 2.0.0) under the same rules and the portal's evaluation.
Strain-madness short-read pooled co-assembly: strain recall STRICTLY GREATER than 3.92% (HipMer 1.0) with strain precision of at least 90%.
Plant-associated Oxford Nanopore pooled assembly from the ONT reads alone: strain recall STRICTLY GREATER than 3.02% (metaFlye 2.8) with strain precision of at least 77.14%.
Marine short-read pooled co-assembly: genome fraction above 46.58% (A-STAR, the table's highest) with strain precision of at least 90%.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic reruns the released assembler on the public reads (or takes the released FASTA plus its command log), runs MetaQUAST with the portal's options against the marine genome set from frl.publisso.de/data/frl:6425521, computes strain recall and precision as the NAR 2025 portal paper defines them, and compares with the live table. Hours of compute.
angles: Strain recall needs genomes assembled at >=90% completeness with <=5 mismatches per 100 kb, so polishing and strain-aware graph resolution may pay more than raw contiguity.
Start from MetaHipMer 2.2.0's iterative k-mer scheme and add coverage-aware bubble resolution across the 10 samples.
pitfalls: Do not mix the hybrid, long-read and short-read tables: they are separate assemblies with separate records.
The F1 strain score is missing ('-') for strain-madness rows on the portal, so p2 uses recall and precision explicitly.
The marine long-read pooled table has no tool submissions, only the gold standard, so a first entry there is not a record.

targets.name: CAMI II taxonomic profiling at species rank: beat ganon2's F1 on the plant-associated samples in the CAMI Benchmarking Portal
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (21 plant-associated samples of about 5 Gbp each; building an index over the 2019-01-08 NCBI RefSeq snapshot is the heavy step, 64 GB RAM helps)
targets.statement: Taxonomic profilers estimate which taxa are present and in what relative abundance. CAMI II (Meyer et al., Nature Methods 2022) evaluated profilers with OPAL against gold-standard profiles. The CAMI Benchmarking Portal (Meyer, Robertson et al., NAR 2025) now ranks uploaded profiles, sample-averaged, rank by rank. Genus level on marine is close to saturated (mOTUs 3.1: genus L1 error 0.10); species level is not. The best species-rank presence/absence F1 scores on 2026-10-30 were as follows. Plant-associated: 0.436 (ganon2 2.1.0, completeness 0.512, purity 0.381, L1 norm error 0.803), then sourmash gather 3.3.2 at 0.394 and MetaPhlAn 2.9.21 at 0.387. Strain-madness: 0.610 (ganon2 2.1.0, L1 0.294), then MetaPhlAn 2.9.22 at 0.568. Marine: 0.875 (Sylph 0.8.0), then mOTUs 3.1.0 at 0.869. The gold standards are public, as is the reference snapshot given to participants (NCBI RefSeq, nt, nr and taxonomy of 2019-01-08).
targets.success_criterion: A set of CAMI-format profiles for all 21 plant-associated short-read samples, produced by released deterministic code using only references frozen at or before 2019-01-08 (the CAMI II snapshot or an earlier NCBI release; no database containing the CAMI II source genomes), whose sample-averaged species-rank F1, computed by OPAL with the portal's options and the same 'filter out plasmid, circular element, virus' setting as the record row, is STRICTLY GREATER than 0.436 (ganon2 2.1.0, direction: max) and greater than every row of the live table at https://cami-challenge.org/datasets/plant-associated/avg/group_4/taxonomic_profiling/species/ (re-fetched immediately before claiming), with a species L1 norm error no worse than 0.803.

partial_wins.statement: Strain-madness (100 samples, averaged): species-rank F1 STRICTLY GREATER than 0.610 (ganon2 2.1.0) with species L1 norm error no worse than 0.294, under the same rules.
Marine (10 samples, averaged): species-rank F1 STRICTLY GREATER than 0.875 (Sylph 0.8.0) using only 2019-01-08 references.
Plant-associated: species-rank L1 norm error below 0.169 (sourmash gather 3.3.2, the lowest listed) with F1 of at least 0.394.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the plant-associated gold-standard profiles (frl.publisso.de/data/frl:6425521/plant_associated/), runs OPAL (github.com/CAMI-challenge/OPAL) on the claimed profiles with the record row's filter option, averages over the 21 samples as the portal does, and checks the reference database build date and contents in the released code. Minutes to evaluate.
angles: Plant-associated purity is the weak side (0.381): most errors are false-positive species, so calibrated abundance thresholds or containment-based filtering may lift F1 without losing completeness.
Combine a k-mer containment profiler (sylph/sourmash style) with a marker-gene profiler and keep only species that both support.
pitfalls: Newer databases (GTDB, RefSeq after 2019) can contain the CAMI II source genomes, which were deposited after the challenge; some portal rows may use them, but a claim here must not.
Rows differ in the 'Filter out' option; match the record row's setting.
Do not filter the rarest taxa to inflate purity unless the same filter percentage is reported and the record is compared with that filter.

targets.name: CAMI II taxonomic binning of reads at species rank: beat ganon2's per-bin F1 on the plant-associated samples without losing accuracy
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (classify 21 short-read samples of about 5 Gbp each against an index of the 2019-01-08 RefSeq snapshot; 64 GB RAM helps)
targets.statement: Taxonomic binners label each read or contig with a taxon, which is a different output from an abundance profile. CAMI II (Meyer et al., Nature Methods 2022) scored taxonomic binning with AMBER, and the CAMI Benchmarking Portal (Meyer, Robertson, Deng et al., NAR 2025) keeps per-rank, sample-averaged tables. At species rank on short reads the per-bin scores are poor because many small false-positive species bins drag down average purity. On 2026-10-30 the live tables showed: plant-associated (21 samples), ganon2 2.1.0 with F1 (bp) 0.055 (average purity 0.029, average completeness 0.460) and accuracy (bp) 0.712, ahead of Ganon 0.3.1 (F1 0.051, accuracy 0.700) and Kraken 2.0.8 beta (0.011, 0.320); marine (10 samples), Metabuli 1.0.8 with the best F1 (bp) 0.279 at accuracy 0.390, and ganon2 2.1.0 with the best accuracy 0.901 at F1 0.221; strain-madness (100 samples), Ganon 0.1.4 at F1 0.033 and ganon2 2.1.0 at accuracy 0.850. No listed method combines high per-bin purity with high accuracy.
targets.success_criterion: Read-level taxonomic binning files (CAMI binning format) for all 21 plant-associated short-read samples, produced by released deterministic code using only references frozen at or before 2019-01-08 (no database containing the CAMI II source genomes), whose sample-averaged species-rank scores, computed by AMBER with no filter and no minimum length as in the record row, have F1 score (bp) STRICTLY GREATER than 0.055 AND accuracy (bp) of at least 0.712 (both from ganon2 2.1.0; direction: max), beating every row of the live table at https://cami-challenge.org/datasets/plant-associated/avg/group_4/taxonomic_binning/species/ (re-fetched immediately before claiming) on F1 (bp). A minimum bin size, read-count or abundance cut that unassigns reads at species rank is a filter: a claim whose pipeline applies one must also report ganon2 2.1.0, rerun by the claimant on the same 2019-01-08 references with released commands and scored after the same cut, and must beat that rerun on F1 (bp) while keeping accuracy (bp) of at least 0.712.

partial_wins.statement: Marine (10 samples, averaged, species rank, unfiltered): F1 score (bp) STRICTLY GREATER than 0.279 (Metabuli 1.0.8) with accuracy (bp) of at least 0.901 (ganon2 2.1.0), dominating both leaders, under the same rules (including the ganon2-rerun rule for any size or abundance cut).

Strain-madness (100 samples, averaged, species rank, unfiltered): F1 score (bp) STRICTLY GREATER than 0.033 with accuracy (bp) of at least 0.850, under the same rules (including the ganon2-rerun rule for any size or abundance cut).

Plant-associated: F1 score (bp) of at least 0.10 at accuracy (bp) of at least 0.60, nearly doubling the listed F1 while giving up little accuracy, under the same rules (including the ganon2-rerun rule for any size or abundance cut).

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the read-level gold-standard mappings for the plant-associated samples, runs AMBER in taxonomic mode on the claimed files with no filter, averages over samples as the portal does, compares F1 (bp) and accuracy (bp) with the live table, and checks the reference build date in the released code. Minutes per sample.
angles: Average purity is a per-bin mean dominated by many tiny false-positive species bins. A principled fix (calibrated per-read confidence, LCA on ambiguous hits, pushing doubtful reads up to genus) has to beat what a plain size cut already gives ganon2, as the criterion requires.
Use profile-informed binning: first estimate which species are present, then restrict read assignment to that set.
pitfalls: The portal's 'Filter %' option removes small bins and inflates F1; the criterion is unfiltered.

A minimum-bin-size or abundance cut built into the pipeline is the same filter by another name. It likely lifts average purity a lot at little accuracy cost, so it counts only against a ganon2 2.1.0 rerun given the same cut.
Accuracy (bp) and F1 (bp) trade off; a claim must meet both bounds at once.
Read-level and gold-standard-contig tables are different; this target is the read-level sample average.

targets.name: HomFam multiple sequence alignment: beat learnMSA2's best 66.92% mean total-column score over the 94 HomFam families
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (94 families of 93 to 93,681 sequences; protein-language-model embeddings need a GPU or many CPU hours)
targets.statement: HomFam (Sievers et al., Clustal Omega, Mol Syst Biol 2011) embeds a structure-based reference subset of each of 94 Pfam families in up to 93,681 homologs. An aligner is scored only on how it aligns the reference sequences inside the full set: SP (correctly aligned residue pairs), TC (fully correct reference columns) and column score, computed with T-Coffee aln_compare. learnMSA2 (Felix Becker and Mario Stanke, Bioinformatics 2024) is a profile-HMM aligner fed with protein-language-model embeddings. The authors' public benchmark pipeline (github.com/felbecker/snakeMSA, one line per family) holds two sets of learnMSA2 runs. The main comparison (results/*.out) gives these means over the 94 HomFam families: learnMSA2 with language model 65.90 TC / 87.31 SP / 72.98 column; learnMSA without embeddings 63.12; FAMSA 60.07; MUSCLE5 59.09; MAFFT-sparsecore 58.70; Clustal Omega 58.20; MAGUS 56.77; regressive T-Coffee 56.57. The paper's hyperparameter search (lm_experiments/results, 54 runs over three language models, r, activation and C; ProtT5 runs average 66.00 TC / 87.30 SP as the paper reports) reaches the best HomFam mean: 66.92 TC / 87.65 SP / 73.67 column for ProtT5 with r = 32, softmax, C = 10. The paper's default (r = 16, sigmoid, C = 32) scores 66.70. On the largest extHomFam set ('huge', 62 families) the best TC is 44.17 (learnMSA2). FAMSA2 (Gudys, Zielezinski, Notredame and Deorowicz, Nature Biotechnology 2026) benchmarks on a new extHomFam v37.0 set rather than HomFam. ARIES (Hoang, Armour-Garb and Singh, Princeton, 2026), a protein-language-model aligner, reports results on BAliBASE, HOMSTRAD and QuanTest2 but not on HomFam.
targets.success_criterion: Alignments of all 94 HomFam families, each aligning the full family (reference plus homologs) and produced by released deterministic code, whose mean TC score over the 94 reference subsets, computed with T-Coffee aln_compare exactly as in the snakeMSA pipeline, is STRICTLY GREATER than 66.92 (learnMSA2, ProtT5, r = 32, softmax, C = 10; direction: max), with mean SP of at least 87.65. The claim must also beat the best mean HomFam TC in both https://github.com/felbecker/snakeMSA/tree/main/results and https://github.com/felbecker/snakeMSA/tree/main/lm_experiments/results (re-fetched immediately before claiming) and any HomFam TC found by a novelty search. The method must not use the HomFam or Pfam-seed reference alignments, or structures of the reference sequences, as input, and its hyperparameters must be fixed before scoring, not selected on HomFam.

partial_wins.statement: extHomFam 'huge' (62 families): mean TC STRICTLY GREATER than 44.17 (learnMSA2) under the same scoring.
extHomFam 'large' (83 families): mean TC STRICTLY GREATER than 59.74 (learnMSA2) under the same scoring.
extHomFam 'xlarge' (67 families): mean TC STRICTLY GREATER than 52.51 (learnMSA2, the best in snakeMSA results) under the same scoring.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic extracts the reference sequences' rows from each claimed alignment, scores them against the HomFam references with T-Coffee aln_compare (SP, TC, column) as the snakeMSA Snakefile does, averages over the 94 families, and compares with the best mean in results/ and lm_experiments/results/. Minutes once the alignments exist.
angles: The language-model gain is largest at low identity and on large families, so ensemble or consensus approaches (for example learnMSA2 plus an embedding-similarity aligner) may add TC where the two disagree.
ARIES's reciprocal embedding similarity could replace the HMM's emission signal for the hardest families.
pitfalls: Scores must come from aligning the full family; aligning only the reference subset is a different and easier task.
learnMSA_paper.out in snakeMSA is an older learnMSA run (57.29 TC) and not the record.

results/learnMSA_language2.out (65.90 TC) is not the best learnMSA2 run either: the hyperparameter grid in lm_experiments/results reaches 66.92 TC, and the paper's default configuration scores 66.70 there. Picking the best of many configurations on HomFam itself is how that bar was reached; a claim must fix its settings in advance.
HOMSTRAD in the same pipeline is not a valid record to cite: ARIES 2026 claims to beat the listed tools there.

targets.name: Quest for Orthologs 2022 SwissTree benchmark: ortholog predictions that beat every public method on recall and precision at once
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (orthology inference on the 78 QfO 2022_02 reference proteomes; the QfO benchmark pipeline runs in Docker/Nextflow)
targets.statement: The Quest for Orthologs benchmark service (Nevers, Jones, Jyothi et al., NAR 2022; maintained by the Dessimoz lab with OpenEBench) scores ortholog predictions on fixed reference proteomes. It checks them against curated gene phylogenies, species-tree discordance and function conservation. SwissTree is an expert-curated set of reference gene trees. On it, the public 2022 results list 20 methods by true positive rate (recall) and positive predictive value (precision) of ortholog pairs. On 2026-10-30 the highest recall was pbDOOD (midpoint) at TPR 0.854 / PPV 0.950, then pbDOOD (eggnog v7) 0.847 / 0.952, OrthoFinder 0.825 / 0.917 and PANTHER v18 (all) 0.811 / 0.943. The highest precision was FastOMA v0.1.4 at PPV 0.953 (TPR 0.699). No listed method has both. OrthoFinder v3 (Emms, Liu, Belcher, Holmes and Kelly, Nature Methods 2026) reports the highest SwissTree recall among the methods it plots, which leave out pbDOOD. Its points (Fig. 5e: OrthoFinder3 about 0.83 / 0.93, OrthoFinder3_Linear about 0.845 / 0.92) lie below pbDOOD's recall and FastOMA's precision. On TreeFam-A the maxima are TPR 0.7367 (OrthoFinder) and PPV 0.9566 (PANTHER v18 LDO).
targets.success_criterion: Ortholog pair predictions on the QfO 2022_02 reference proteomes, produced by released deterministic code that does not use SwissTree, TreeFam-A or any curated reference tree as input, whose SwissTree evaluation by the official QfO benchmark pipeline (2022 release) gives TPR STRICTLY GREATER than 0.854 AND PPV STRICTLY GREATER than 0.953 (direction: max on both), exceeding every method on the public results page https://orthology.benchmarkservice.org/proxy/results/2022/ (re-fetched immediately before claiming) on both axes, and not dominated on SwissTree by either OrthoFinder v3 point published in Emms et al. 2026, Fig. 5e (OrthoFinder3 about 0.83 / 0.93, OrthoFinder3_Linear about 0.845 / 0.92; the paper's Supplementary Data hold no QfO values).

partial_wins.statement: TreeFam-A (2022): TPR STRICTLY GREATER than 0.7367 together with PPV of at least 0.9300, beating every listed method's recall while keeping precision at Hieranoid 2's level.
