Nicolas Rouanet's best order-13 square has 13 trimagic rows, 11 trimagic columns and 1 trimagic diagonal. Tetramagic: smallest known 243 (Pan Fengchu, February 2004). Orders up to 23, and 25 and 26, are proven impossible, so the smallest is 24 or lies in 27..243. Pentamagic: smallest known 729 (Li Wen, June 2003). Hexamagic: smallest known 4096 (Pan Fengchu, December 2003). Cubes: the smallest known bimagic cube has order 16 (Christian Boyer, January 2003; below 8 is impossible). Boyer's order-32 perfect bimagic cube (2003) was superseded in April 2015 by Zhong Ming's perfect bimagic cubes of orders 16 and 25, so the smallest known perfect bimagic cube also has order 16. The Records, Unsolved problems, Smallest tetramagic and Multimagic cubes pages were re-fetched on 2026-10-30 and give these values. A web search found no smaller construction, though its coverage of recent preprints may be incomplete. Boyer's prize Enigmas, such as the 5x5 bimagic square in distinct integers and small add-mult squares, are separate live prize challenges and are not part of this target.
targets.success_criterion: Any one of the following, built from consecutive integers (normal), strictly smaller than the record on multimagie.com at verification time: a tetramagic square of order < 243; a pentamagic square of order < 729; a hexamagic square of order < 4096; a trimagic square of order 13 or 15; or a bimagic cube of order < 16 (all rows, columns, pillars and the four space diagonals bimagic; a perfect bimagic cube of order < 16 also qualifies, since it is a bimagic cube). The object must be given in full.

partial_wins.statement: A normal 13 x 13 magic square (entries 1..169, all 28 lines summing to 1105) in which strictly more than 25 of the 28 lines (rows, columns, two diagonals) are also bimagic and trimagic, beating Rouanet's 13 rows + 11 columns + 1 diagonal.

targets.verification_method: Big-integer check of the entry set (exactly 1..n^2, or 1..n^3 for cubes), then the power sums for j = 1..k along every required line, compared with the magic sums S_j = (sum of i^j over the entries) / n. The check takes seconds even for order 242.
pitfalls: Normal means consecutive integers 1..n^2. Squares in arbitrary distinct integers are a different (and partly prize-carrying) problem.
Wikipedia's multimagic page still gives 256 as the smallest tetramagic order and omits Pan Fengchu's 243. Use multimagie.com.

The top table on multimagie.com's Cube.htm still lists 32 as the smallest perfect bimagic cube. The Zhong Ming section further down the same page, and the Problems page, show that orders 16 and 25 were built in April 2015. A perfect bimagic cube of order 16 to 31 is not a new record.

targets.name: Conway's Topswops: the maximum number of steps for 22 cards (next term of OEIS A000375 after Chaffin's f(21) = 282), or longer 22- and 23-card decks
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster for the exact f(22) (f(21) took about 181,000 CPU-days); finding a longer deck is laptop-days of local search
targets.statement: Topswops (John Conway; Martin Gardner; Knuth, TAOCP 4A, section 7.2.1.2, exercise 107): shuffle cards 1..n. While the top card m is not 1, reverse the top m cards. f(n), OEIS A000375, is the largest number of steps over all decks. Known values: f(1..17) through Knuth's and later exhaustive searches; f(18) = 191 and f(19) = 221 (Kimura, Takahashi, Araki and Amano, arXiv:2103.08346, 2021); f(20) = 249 with a unique deck, and f(21) = 282 with five decks (Ben Chaffin, April 2026). Chaffin's searches took about 7,200 and 181,000 CPU-days. This lane re-checked Chaffin's 20-card and 21-card decks with its own simulator: they take 249 and 282 steps. The OEIS gives lower bounds f(22) >= 335 and f(23) >= 382 (Hugo Pfoertner, updated 2016), which come from optimisation searches, including Al Zimmermann's 2010-11 Topswops contest (winner Jarek Wroblewski, second Tomas Rokicki). That contest used prime deck sizes only, from 2 to 97. Its final report (azspcs.com/Contest/Cards/FinalReport, loaded 2026-10-30) gives 382 as the best 23-card score, first reached on 6 December 2010 and matched by about a dozen entrants, and it had no 22-card problem. Known bounds: a quadratic lower bound (Morales and Sudborough, 2010) and a Fibonacci upper bound.
targets.success_criterion: The exact value of f(22), the first unknown term of OEIS A000375 at verification time. It must come with a complete, re-runnable exhaustive search (for example Knuth's forward algorithm with Chaffin-style pruning). The search must be independently re-run or cross-checked (for example by splitting the search tree and re-running a random sample of sub-trees with independent code), and the same code must reproduce f(n) for n <= 19.

partial_wins.statement: A 22-card deck taking at least 336 steps, or a 23-card deck taking at least 383 steps, strictly above the OEIS lower bounds f(22) >= 335 and f(23) >= 382, provided those bounds are unchanged on A000375 at verification time.

targets.verification_method: Simulate the deck: repeatedly reverse the top m cards, where m is the top card, until the top card is 1, and count the reversals. This takes microseconds. For an exact value, rerun the search on independent hardware, or audit it by re-running randomly chosen sub-trees with an independent implementation, and require exact agreement on the per-subtree maxima.
pitfalls: The game stops when the top card is 1, not when the deck is sorted.

The AZsPCs Topswops final report (azspcs.com/Contest/Cards/FinalReport) lists only prime sizes. Its best 23-card deck takes exactly 382 steps, the same as the OEIS bound, and it has no 22-card entry, so it does not raise either p1 bar. Its 23-card bar has resisted many strong entrants since 2010.

targets.name: MOONSHOT - Tower of Hanoi with five or more pegs: a move sequence shorter than Frame-Stewart, or an extension of the exhaustive verification beyond Hinz-Petr's frontier
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (Hinz and Petr ran their Hanoi-graph BFS on SuperMUC-NG; checking a claimed short sequence is laptop-minutes)
targets.statement: Move a tower of n discs from one peg to another with p pegs, never placing a larger disc on a smaller one. The Frame-Stewart algorithm (1941) uses FS_p(n) = min over m of 2*FS_p(m) + FS_{p-1}(n-m), with FS_3(n) = 2^n - 1 (OEIS A007664 for 4 pegs, A007665 for 5, A182058 for 6). Frame-Stewart is proven optimal for 4 pegs (Thierry Bousch, 2014). For p >= 5 its optimality is the open Frame-Stewart conjecture. Exhaustive breadth-first search on Hanoi graphs has confirmed it for p = 5 and n <= 20, p = 6 and n <= 16, and p = 7 and n <= 21, as reported by Andreas M. Hinz and Ciril Petr at the SuperMUC-NG Status and Results Workshop on 2023-05-10 (LRZ project pr87mo). Earlier large exhaustive searches (Korf 2004; Korf and Felner 2007; Houston and Masum 2004) concerned four pegs. This lane recomputed the next unverified values from the recurrence: FS_5(21) = 127, FS_6(17) = 65, FS_7(22) = 79.
targets.success_criterion: For some p >= 5 and n, an explicit legal move sequence that transfers a perfect tower of n discs from peg 0 to peg 1 in strictly fewer than FS_p(n) moves, where FS_p(n) is computed from the recurrence. That would disprove the Frame-Stewart conjecture. By Hinz-Petr, such an n must exceed 20 for p = 5, 16 for p = 6 and 21 for p = 7.

partial_wins.statement: A complete, re-runnable exhaustive search, with released code and per-layer (or per-distance) state counts, that confirms d_p(0^n, 1^n) = FS_p(n) for a case beyond Hinz-Petr's frontier: (p, n) = (5, 21) with value 127, (6, 17) with value 65, or (7, 22) with value 79. It must be independently re-run, at least on a reduced instance and on a random sample of the search.

targets.verification_method: For a move sequence: simulate on p stacks, check that every move takes the top disc and places it on an empty peg or a larger disc, check the final state, and count the moves. Compare with FS_p(n) from the recurrence in exact integers. For a verification claim: rerun the search over all legal states (a breadth-first search on the Hanoi graph, as Hinz and Petr ran it, or a Korf-Felner-style search that exploits the symmetry of the 0^n to 1^n problem), reproduce the published smaller cases and per-layer counts, and check that the code computes the true distance and not a restricted subtower distance.
pitfalls: Searching only Frame-Stewart-style (subtower) strategies cannot disprove the conjecture. The search must range over all legal states.
The four-peg case is settled (Bousch 2014). A shorter four-peg sequence is impossible.

targets.name: Water retention of magic squares (Knecht): a normal magic square of order 10-15 retaining more water than the OEIS A201126 lower bounds, or better order 16-28, semi-magic and associative records
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: Craig Knecht's topographical model treats a magic square as a height map. Pour water on it: a cell's water level is the minimum, over all orthogonal paths from the cell to the outer boundary, of the maximum height on the path, and water drains off the edge. Retention is the sum over cells of (level - height). OEIS A201126 gives the maximum retention of a normal magic square of order n: 0, 15, 69, 192, 418, 797, 1408 for n = 3..9. It lists the lower bounds a(10) >= 2267, a(11) >= 3492, a(12) >= 5185, a(13) >= 7445, a(14) >= 10397 and a(15) >= 14154. These come mostly from Al Zimmermann's spring 2010 Retaining Water contest (winner Walter Trump, second Hermann Jurksch), which set the known values for orders 4 to 28. Its final report (azspcs.com/Contest/MagicWater/FinalReport, loaded 2026-10-30) publishes the best square for each order. It gives 7442 for order 13, three below the OEIS bound, and for orders 16 to 28 it gives 18887, 24730, 31871, 40473, 50754, 62877, 77098, 93623, 112710, 134598, 159565, 187880 and 219822. This audit recomputed all 25 published squares (orders 4 to 28): each is a normal magic square whose retention equals its listed score. Related records: the semi-magic analogue A201127 (a(10) >= 2280, Hugo Pfoertner 2012); and the associative analogue A261798 (a(7) = 361, a(8) = 704, a(9) = 1247; a(11) >= 3226, a(12) >= 4840, a(13) >= 6972). For associative squares, OEIS states that no value above order 5 is proven maximal. See also Knecht, Trump, ben-Avraham and Ziff, PRL 108 (2012) 045703. This lane brute-forced all 7,040 normal 4 x 4 magic squares with orthogonal drainage and got a maximum of 15, which matches a(4) and confirms the drainage model.
targets.success_criterion: A normal magic square of order n, for some 10 <= n <= 15 (entries 1..n^2, all rows, columns and both main diagonals summing to n(n^2+1)/2), whose water retention under the orthogonal-drainage model is strictly greater than the A201126 lower bound for that n at verification time.

partial_wins.statement: A normal semi-magic square of order 10 (rows and columns only) retaining at least 2281 units, beating A201127's a(10) >= 2280.

A normal associative magic square (a(i,j) + a(n+1-i, n+1-j) = n^2 + 1) of order 7, 8, 9, 11, 12 or 13 retaining strictly more than the A261798 value or lower bound for that order (361, 704, 1247, 3226, 4840, 6972).

A normal magic square of order n, 16 <= n <= 28, retaining strictly more water than the best score in the AZsPCs Retaining Water final report for that order (16: 18887, 17: 24730, 18: 31871, 19: 40473, 20: 50754, 21: 62877, 22: 77098, 23: 93623, 24: 112710, 25: 134598, 26: 159565, 27: 187880, 28: 219822), and strictly more than any larger value published for that order (OEIS or elsewhere) at verification time.

targets.verification_method: Check the entry set and the magic, semi-magic or associative conditions in exact integers. Compute retention with a priority-flood (Dijkstra-style) algorithm: seed the boundary cells at their own heights, propagate level = max(height, neighbour level) through the 4 orthogonal neighbours, and sum (level - height). Validate the implementation on all 4 x 4 magic squares (maximum 15) and on the best squares published in the AZsPCs Retaining Water final report, orders 4 to 28, each of which must reproduce its listed score exactly.
pitfalls: Drainage is orthogonal only. With 8-neighbour drainage the 4 x 4 maximum drops to 5. Boundary cells hold no water.

For order 13 the contest final report's 7442 is below OEIS's a(13) >= 7445. Always use the larger of the two published values for an order. For orders 16 to 28 only the 2010 contest values were found. Later improvements may exist unpublished or elsewhere, so recheck before claiming p3.

targets.name: SV-COMP 2026: a doubly validated witness for a verification task that no participating verifier answered correctly
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours per task (validators run 15 min to a few hours each; ldv and coreutils tasks are large preprocessed C files)
targets.statement: SV-COMP, the International Competition on Software Verification (organiser Dirk Beyer, LMU Munich; sv-benchmarks contributors; verifier and validator teams), runs every participating verifier on the sv-benchmarks tasks and confirms answers by witness validation. Its 2026 edition (15th, TACAS 2026) published 52 C and Java results-verified category tables (BenchExec 3.34; 24 to 37 verifiers per C category, 11 for Java). Parsing every row on 2026-10-30 gives 1,748 task/property pairs where no verifier's result is correct or correct-unconfirmed. Two subsets are left out because other bank entries cover the same problems: c/neural-networks (441, VNN-COMP-style networks) and c/hardware-verification-bv (288, btor2c translations of HWMCC circuits). Of the other 1,019, 173 were never scored in 2026: every verifier's result there is 'invalid task' (category missing), and in 130 of them at least one verifier gave the labelled answer, so they are left out too. This removes almost all no-data-race pairs (pthread-race-challenges) and the unsolved array-fpi, argv-tasks and coreutils-v9.5-units rows. Re-reading the .yml of the remaining 846 scored pairs at sv-benchmarks main 813a819f (2026-10-29): 6 lost the property and 1 flipped its expected verdict, leaving 839 pairs, 771 in C and 68 in Java. C: unreach-call 441 expected true (95 in combinations, 80 in intel-tdx-module) and 11 false; valid-memsafety 113/105 (false mostly coreutils-v8.31, ldv-linux and memsafety-cve); no-overflow 46/23; termination 16/14; no-data-race 2 true (libvsync). Small classics include nla-digbench dijkstra-u, egcd3-ll and hard-ll, the knuth and prodbin-ll unwindbound variants, insertion_sort-2-2, recursive gcd02 and 17 recursified_nla-digbench tasks. Java: valid-assert 7/37, no-runtime-exception 23/1. The labels are known: the open part is an answer validators or a replay accept. SV-COMP 2026 validated correctness witnesses only for unreach-call, no-overflow and (demo) termination, so expected-true memsafety, data-race and Java pairs carry no win here.
targets.success_criterion: Pick a task/property pair from the 2026 results-verified tables (https://sv-comp.sosy-lab.org/2026/results/results-verified/) where at least one verifier's result was scored (the row is not 'invalid task' / category missing for every verifier) and no verifier's result is in category correct or correct-unconfirmed, not under c/neural-networks/ or c/hardware-verification-bv/, whose .yml on current sv-benchmarks main (re-fetched before claiming) still carries that property with the same expected_verdict (for valid-memsafety, the same subproperty). (a) C, expected false: a violation witness (format 2.0, or 1.0 where only v1 validators handle the property, as for no-data-race) that two distinct validators from the 2026 witness-validation tables (https://sv-comp.sosy-lab.org/2026/results/results-validated/, v2 or v1) confirm in their 2026 configuration. A deterministic execution replay (CPA-witness2test, ConcurrentWitness2Test, or a Test-Comp test vector that reaches the violation when compiled with the sv-benchmarks harness) may stand in for one of the two. (b) C, expected true, property unreach-call, no-overflow or termination only: a format-2.0 correctness witness that two distinct validators from the 2026 correctness-witness v2 table confirm. Each validator run: at most 4 h CPU, 15 GB. (c) Java, expected false: a list of Verifier.nondet* return values that, returned in order by a replay version of org.sosy_lab.sv_benchmarks.Verifier with every other class unmodified, makes the program fail an assertion under java -ea or throw the uncaught runtime exception. A result contradicting the label is a label bug, not a win.

partial_wins.statement: A format-2.0 correctness witness for an in-scope expected-true C pair (unreach-call, no-overflow or termination) that exactly one SV-COMP 2026 correctness validator confirms within 4 h CPU and 15 GB, and that no other 2026 correctness validator rejects (the others time out or answer unknown).

A violation witness for an in-scope expected-false C pair that exactly one SV-COMP 2026 violation validator confirms, or that only a deterministic execution replay (criterion a) confirms, and that no 2026 violation validator rejects.

For one of the in-scope expected-true tasks nla-digbench dijkstra-u, egcd3-ll or hard-ll, or nla-digbench-scaling knuth_unwindbound5/10/50 or prodbin-ll_unwindbound50/100: a published SMT-LIB script that encodes the program's loops with the task's C integer semantics (QF_BV, or integer arithmetic with explicit range constraints for the ILP32/LP64 data model) and states loop invariants, on which z3 and cvc5 both return unsat for every initiation, consecution and assertion-implication query within 1 h each, even if no validator accepts a witness built from those invariants.

targets.verification_method: The skeptic downloads the task at the current sv-benchmarks commit and checks the property, expected verdict and (for memsafety) subproperty in the .yml. They confirm on the 2026 results-verified table that the row was scored (not 'invalid task' for every verifier) and has no correct or correct-unconfirmed entry, then run the named validators (archived 2026 versions from fm-tools / Zenodo, with the competition's BenchExec benchmark definitions and the task's data model) or the replay harness on the submitted witness or test vector. For Java they compile the task with the replay Verifier class and run it with java -ea. For p3 they read the SMT encoding against the C source and run it in z3 and cvc5. 1 to 8 hours per claim.
angles: Small nonlinear-arithmetic loops (nla-digbench): invariant synthesis with polynomial templates or Gröbner-basis equalities, emitted as witness 2.0 invariants.
intel-tdx-module and combinations expected-true unreach-call tasks: compositional invariants per component, exported as witness 2.0 and cross-validated.
coreutils and memsafety-cve false tasks: run a sanitiser-guided fuzzer on the harness to find the bad input, then turn the trace into a violation witness.
Java expected-false tasks: concolic testing (JDart/GDart style) with the Verifier stub to get concrete nondet sequences.
pitfalls: The unsolved list was computed from the 2026 tables; SV-COMP 2027 (spring 2027) may solve tasks, so re-check its tables when they appear.

Rows where every verifier's result reads 'invalid task' (category missing) were never scored in 2026 and are out of scope: 173 of the 1,019 candidates, and in 130 of them some verifier already gave the labelled answer. Filter on the category, not only on the absence of 'correct'.

Between the svcomp26 tag and main 813a819f, 6 of the 846 scored pairs lost the property and 1 flipped verdict (over all 1,019 candidates: 1 task file removed, 28 lost, 6 flipped), usually because a label was wrong. Always re-check the current .yml, and note that task files use two YAML layouts (property_file first or expected_verdict first) and both lower-case and capitalised verdicts when scripting the check.
Validators accept witnesses under specific data-model and property options (ILP32 vs LP64, subproperty for memsafety); a mismatch gives a spurious reject.
No SV-COMP 2026 correctness-witness validation track covered valid-memsafety or no-data-race, so expected-true pairs for those properties cannot meet criterion (b).
The sv-benchmarks Java Verifier stub draws values from java.util.Random, so criterion (c) needs a replay stub; Java assertions only fire with -ea.
The c/neural-networks and c/hardware-verification-bv subsets are excluded on purpose (overlap with VNN-COMP and HWMCC entries).

targets.name: Freek Wiedijk's 100 theorems: fill a gap in Isabelle, HOL Light, Rocq, Metamath or Mizar (Lean is complete)
targets.compute_profile: pure thought plus laptop-hours of proof-assistant builds
targets.statement: Freek Wiedijk (Radboud University) maintains 'Formalizing 100 Theorems'. The page (last modified 2026-10-29) shows 100% formalised overall: Lean has all 100 (the four colour theorem as a Lean port of Gonthier's proof by Chris Emery and Robert D. Barish, Fermat's Last Theorem by Anthropic). Its other counts are HOL Light 95, Isabelle 95, Rocq 80, Metamath 74 (the Metamath 100 page of David A. Wheeler and Norman Megill says 75) and Mizar 71. John Harrison's HOL Light repository is ahead of the page: commit d30e823 (2026-10-20) added Claude-autoformalised Puiseux's theorem, independence of CH and AC from ZF, and a port of the four colour theorem, leaving only #16 (Abel-Ruffini, insolvability of the general quintic) and #33 (FLT) open in HOL Light. Isabelle lacks #16, #28 Pascal's hexagon theorem, #32 four colour, #33 FLT and #43 the isoperimetric theorem, and no AFP entry proves any of them. Larry Paulson's New_Algebra development in the Isabelle repository (since 2026-09-06) already proves the finite Galois correspondence and the non-solvability half of Abel-Ruffini; the radical-extension half is only begun. Rocq lacks 20, among them PNT, trisection, the area of a circle, the parallel postulate, Green, Brouwer, Pell, Minkowski, isoperimetric, partitions, CLT, Dirichlet, Platonic solids, Fourier series, Pick, Buffon and Descartes' rule of signs. Metamath's own to-do list has 25 items (including Goedel's incompleteness, the polyhedron formula, Brouwer, CLT, pi transcendental, Morley, Pick and Buffon). Mizar lacks 29. Every gap is a fixed, famous statement whose proof one system's kernel can check.
targets.success_criterion: A complete formalisation, in the target system, of a theorem from the list for which neither Freek's page nor that system's own sources show a formalisation at claim time. The sources are: the HOL Light repository (100/, Autoformalization/, 4CT/), the Isabelle distribution and its development repository and the AFP, Rocq's opam/contrib ecosystem, set.mm, and the MML. The full win is a cell in HOL Light (#16 or #33) or Isabelle/HOL (#16, #28, #32, #33 or #43). The statement must be at least as strong as the Lean, HOL Light or Rocq statement linked from Freek's page for that theorem, using the system's standard library notions; no new axioms. The development must be checked by the system's kernel, with no sorry/oops (Isabelle), no cheat or new_axiom and axioms() unchanged (HOL Light), no Admitted/Axiom (Rocq), and no ? steps (Metamath). A Rocq, Metamath or Mizar cell counts as a partial win (below).

partial_wins.statement: A Rocq (Coq) formalisation, with Print Assumptions showing only the standard library's classical axioms if any, of one of the 20 theorems Freek's page lists without a Rocq entry, where no Rocq development of it is already public.
A set.mm proof of one of the 25 theorems on the Metamath 100 to-do list, accepted by metamath-exe 'verify proof *' and by one other verifier (metamath-knife or checkmm).
A Mizar article proving one of the 29 theorems with no Mizar entry on Freek's page, accepted by the current Mizar verifier against the current MML.

targets.verification_method: The skeptic builds the development with the stated system version (isabelle build -D; a HOL Light loads run followed by axioms() showing only the three standard axioms; coqc plus Print Assumptions; metamath-exe plus a second verifier; or the Mizar verifier). They grep for sorry, oops, cheat, Admitted and new_axiom, and compare the final statement with the Lean, HOL Light or Rocq statement linked from Freek's page. They also re-check Freek's page, the system's repository and library (for Isabelle, the development repository as well as the AFP) that the cell was still empty. 1 to 4 hours.
angles: Pascal and the isoperimetric theorem in Isabelle can be ported from HOL Light's 100/pascal.ml and 100/isoperimetric.ml; Isabelle HOL-Analysis shares much of HOL Light's multivariate library.
Rocq gaps such as Descartes' rule of signs, Pick's theorem and the number of Platonic solids rest on mathcomp and mathcomp-analysis; translate the Isabelle or HOL Light proofs.
Abel-Ruffini: follow Lean's AbelRuffini.exists_not_solvable_by_rad (Thomas Browning) or Rocq's Bernard-Cohen-Mahboubi-Strub development.
pitfalls: Freek's page lags the systems (HOL Light's 2026-10-20 additions of Puiseux, CH independence and 4CT were not on it on 2026-10-29); check the system's repository and AFP before starting.

Isabelle #16 is in active development: Paulson's src/HOL/New_Algebra (Abel_Ruffini.thy, Radical_Extension.thy, Galois_Finite_Correspondence.thy) may finish it in the Isabelle repository before the next release; check it right before claiming.

The AFP's Projective_Geometry/Pascal_Property.thy (Anthony Bordg) proves that Pascal's property of an abstract projective plane is equivalent to Pappus's property; that is not Pascal's hexagon theorem for conics and does not fill #28.
AI-assisted autoformalisation is filling cells fast in 2026; re-check right before claiming.
A weaker statement (special cases, extra hypotheses, a different notion of solvability by radicals) does not count.

targets.name: Oberwolfach problem: solve every instance OP(F) of order 61 to 64 (verified so far for all orders up to 60)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (order 59 took about 29 CPU-hours with the published method)
targets.statement: OP(F), posed by Gerhard Ringel in 1967, asks for a decomposition of K_v (v odd) or K_v minus a perfect matching (v even) into copies of a given 2-regular graph F of order v. The only known non-solvable instances are [3,3], [4,5], [3,3,5] and [3,3,3,3]. Deza, Franek, Hua, Meszka and Rosa (JCMCC 2010) solved all orders up to 40; Salassa, Dragotto, Traetta, Buratti and Della Croce (Australasian J. Combin. 79, 2021; arXiv 1903.12112) solved every instance with at least three cycles for orders 41 to 60 (239,444 instances by their Table 1; their text quotes 241,200, which includes order 40) with 1- and 2-rotational models on a desktop PC, releasing their code (TheOberSolver). Theorems cover uniform F, bipartite F, two-table F (Traetta 2013) and all sufficiently large v (Glock, Joos, Kim, Kuhn and Osthus, JEMS 2021, with an inexplicit bound). Wikipedia's Oberwolfach problem page and the 2023 survey of Burgess, Danziger and Traetta (arXiv 2308.04307) still give the verification for v <= 60. Counting 2-regular graphs with at least three cycles (partitions into at least three parts >= 3; this reproduces the paper's 33,552 at order 60), the next orders have 38,409 (v = 61), 43,974 (62), 50,275 (63) and 57,449 (64) instances. Credit: Ringel; Deza et al.; Salassa et al.; Traetta; Glock et al.
targets.success_criterion: Success means, for every 2-regular graph F with at least three cycles and order v in {61, 62, 63, 64}, an explicit solution of OP(F): either the full list of 2-factors, or base 2-factor(s) plus the 1- or 2-rotational group action that the checker expands, such that every expanded factor is isomorphic to F (same multiset of cycle lengths, each a simple cycle), the factors are pairwise edge-disjoint, and together they cover every edge of K_v (v odd) or of K_v minus one perfect matching that is itself checked (v even). The number of instances solved must equal 38,409 / 43,974 / 50,275 / 57,449. Before claiming, re-check the literature for a newer computational extension beyond order 60; orders already published do not count.

partial_wins.statement: A complete, checked solution set for all instances of one order v in {61, 62, 63, 64}.
Complete, checked solution sets for both orders 61 and 62, extending the verification to all orders up to 62.

targets.verification_method: For each instance expand the stored base factors under the stated group (Z_{v-1} plus a fixed point, or a 2-rotational action), check each factor is a 2-factor with the right cycle type, check pairwise edge-disjointness and full coverage of K_v or K_v - I with a bitset over the C(v,2) edges, and enumerate the partitions independently to confirm coverage. Minutes per order.
angles: Reimplement Salassa et al.'s 1-rotational (orders 4t+1, giving 4t+2) and 2-rotational (orders 4t+3, giving 4t) labeling models with an open solver (OR-tools CP-SAT or HiGHS) instead of CPLEX.
Handle instances without 1-rotational solutions (their Proposition 3.4) with the 2-rotational model for even n.
Cache sub-labelings: many partitions share all but one or two cycles.
pitfalls: Instances with one or two cycles are settled by theorems and are not part of the count; do not omit any instance with three or more cycles.
For even v the target graph is K_v minus a perfect matching, not K_v.
Derived solutions (4t+2 from 4t+1, 4t from 4t-1) must still be expanded and checked explicitly.
The published code uses IBM CPLEX; a licence is not needed if the models are reimplemented.
Salassa et al. state 241,200 instances for orders 41-60 although their Table 1 rows for 41-60 sum to 239,444 (the 241,200 includes order 40's 1,756); use your own partition count per order.
The 2023 survey of Burgess, Danziger and Traetta (arXiv 2308.04307) still gives v <= 60 as the computational bound; re-check for a newer extension before attacking.

targets.name: Graham-Sloane windmill conjecture: is K_8^(2) (two K_8 sharing a vertex) harmonious? (first open case of 'K_n^(2) harmonious iff n = 4')
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: A graph with q edges is harmonious (Graham and Sloane 1980) if its vertices get distinct labels in Z_q so that the edge sums f(u)+f(v) mod q are all distinct. The windmill K_n^(2) is two copies of K_n sharing one vertex: 2n-1 vertices and q = n(n-1) edges. Equivalently: two n-subsets A, B of Z_q meeting in exactly one element, each with all C(n,2) pairwise sums distinct mod q, whose 2*C(n,2) = q sums together cover Z_q exactly once. Ron Graham and Neil Sloane conjectured that K_n^(2) is harmonious if and only if n = 4 and verified it for n odd and n = 6; B. Liu (1994) proved non-harmonious when n is even and has a prime factor p = 3 mod 4 with odd exponent. Gallian's Dynamic Survey DS6 (28th ed., 30 Oct 2025, Section 2.4 and Table 2) still lists the conjecture as open. By our reading of Liu's condition the open n up to 50 are 8, 10, 16, 18, 20, 26, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50; the smallest is n = 8 (15 vertices, q = 56). Our own small checker reproduces the known facts (n = 4 harmonious, n = 3, 5, 6 not). Credit: Graham, Sloane; Liu; Gallian.
targets.success_criterion: Success means, for n = 8, EITHER (a) an explicit assignment of 15 distinct residues mod 56 to the vertices of K_8^(2) such that the 56 edge sums are pairwise distinct mod 56 (refuting the conjecture), OR (b) a certified proof that no such labeling exists: an exhaustive search by two independent programs, or a SAT/CP encoding whose UNSAT result carries a DRAT/LRAT proof checked by drat-trim or cake_lpr plus an independent second method, with every symmetry reduction used (translation f -> f+t, multiplication by a unit mod 56) justified in the write-up. Before claiming, re-check the latest DS6 edition (Table 2, 'windmills') and the literature for a published decision of K_8^(2).

partial_wins.statement: The same (a) or (b) decision for n = 10 (19 vertices, q = 90).
A decision, (a) or (b), for any other n in {16, 18, 20, 26, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50} that DS6 and the literature do not already settle.

targets.verification_method: For (a): check the 15 labels are distinct mod 56 and that the 28 + 28 pair sums of the two cliques (both containing the shared vertex) are 56 distinct residues; milliseconds. For (b): check the proof certificate, rebuild the CNF or the search independently, and confirm the symmetry-breaking lemmas (translation by t shifts every sum by 2t; multiplication by a unit u permutes Z_56).
angles: Enumerate all n-subsets of Z_q containing 0 with distinct pair sums, up to multiplication by units, then pair them with bitset tests for disjoint sum sets.
Necessary congruence: summing all edge sums gives 7(sum of the 14 non-central labels) + 14c = 28 mod 56; use such sum and sum-of-squares identities to prune.
Exact-cover formulation over the 56 residues, solved with DLX or a SAT solver with symmetry breaking.
pitfalls: The shared vertex's label belongs to both cliques; both sum sets include its sums.
For graphs that are not trees the labels must be injective (no repeated label).
Multiplying by a non-unit mod 56 is not a symmetry.
The list of open n is derived from Liu's theorem as quoted in DS6 (Math. Practice Theory 1994); re-check Liu's exact hypotheses before claiming a case other than n = 8.
The Graham-Sloane paper's ResearchGate copy returned 403 and the SIAM version may be paywalled; the status rests on DS6 Section 2.4.

targets.name: Knuth's cubic graceful conjecture: extend the verification past 14 vertices (16, 18, 20, 22), or a connected cubic graph that is not graceful
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (16-20 vertices); laptop-days for the 7,319,447 graphs on 22 vertices
targets.statement: A graph with q edges is graceful if its vertices can be given distinct labels from {0,...,q} so that the edge differences |f(u)-f(v)| are exactly 1,...,q. Donald Knuth (The Art of Computer Programming, Vol. 4B) proved by computer search that every cubic graph on 4, 6, ..., 14 vertices is graceful except the disconnected 2K4 and 3K4 (Kotzig), and conjectured that every connected cubic graph is graceful. Joseph Gallian's Dynamic Survey of Graph Labeling (DS6, 28th edition, 30 October 2025, Section 2) still reports the verification only up to 14 vertices. The next orders are small by enumeration standards: 4,060 connected cubic graphs on 16 vertices, 41,301 on 18, 510,489 on 20 and 7,319,447 on 22 (OEIS A002851), each with q = 3n/2 edges, and modern backtracking finds graceful labelings of cubic graphs such as generalized Petersen graphs P(n,k) with n <= 75 in seconds (Shao, Deng, Li and Vese, cited in DS6). Credit: Knuth (conjecture and verification to 14), Kotzig (2K4, 3K4), Gallian (survey).
targets.success_criterion: Success means EITHER (a) a certificate that every connected cubic graph on 16, 18, 20 and 22 vertices is graceful: one file per order giving each graph (graph6, as produced by nauty geng -c -d3 -D3 n or genreg) with a graceful labeling, where an independent checker regenerates the complete list, confirms the counts 4,060 / 41,301 / 510,489 / 7,319,447 (A002851), matches every generated graph to a certificate entry by canonical form, and checks that the labels are distinct integers in [0, 3n/2] and the edge differences are exactly {1,...,3n/2}; OR (b) a connected cubic graph with no graceful labeling, certified by two independent exhaustive methods (for example a SAT/CP encoding with a DRAT/LRAT proof checked by drat-trim or cake_lpr, plus an independent backtracking search). Before claiming, re-read the latest DS6 edition and Knuth's TAOCP errata/pre-fascicles for a newer verification bound; orders already covered there do not count.

partial_wins.statement: Certificate (as in (a)) that every connected cubic graph on 16 vertices (4,060 graphs) is graceful.
Certificate that every connected cubic graph on at most 18 vertices is graceful (adds the 41,301 graphs on 18 vertices).
Certificate that every connected cubic graph on at most 20 vertices is graceful (adds the 510,489 graphs on 20 vertices).

targets.verification_method: Regenerate the graphs with nauty (geng -c -d3 -D3, or genreg) and compare the count with A002851. Canonically label each certificate graph (pynauty or nauty) and check one-to-one coverage. For each labeling assert injectivity, range [0, q], and that the multiset of |f(u)-f(v)| over edges equals {1..q}. Seconds to minutes. For a counterexample, check the DRAT/LRAT proof and re-derive the CNF independently.
angles: Edge-driven backtracking: the edge with difference q must join labels 0 and q, then place differences q-1, q-2, ... (Knuth-style dancing links / exact cover over edge differences).
CP-SAT model with AllDifferent on vertex labels and on edge differences, warm-started from a labeling of a neighbouring graph under a single edge switch.
Run order 16 first as a pipeline test; most graphs should fall in milliseconds, so time goes into the rare hard graphs, which are worth reporting.
pitfalls: Disconnected cubic graphs are excluded: 2K4 and 3K4 are not graceful.
Labels come from {0..q} with q = 3n/2 edges, not from {1..n}.
A file of labelings is not a certificate unless the checker proves it covers every isomorphism class (count must match A002851).

The 14-vertex bound is taken from Gallian's survey (DS6, 28th ed.), which cites TAOCP 4B. Knuth's later Volume 4 Fascicle 7 (Constraint Satisfaction, 2025, section 7.2.2.3, exercise 93 and answer) treats graceful labelings of regular graphs; read it and the TAOCP errata for a newer cubic bound before claiming (Knuth's site refused connections when this entry was checked).

targets.name: MOONSHOT - Graceful tree (Ringel-Kotzig) conjecture: a tree with no graceful labeling, a formal proof, or the first verification past Fang's 35 vertices
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (about 6.2e12 trees on 36 vertices)
targets.statement: The graceful tree conjecture (Ringel, Kotzig, Rosa 1960s): every tree with q edges has an injective vertex labeling into {0..q} whose edge differences are exactly 1..q. It implies Ringel's conjecture that K_{2n+1} decomposes into copies of any tree with n edges (proved only for large n by Montgomery, Pokrovskiy and Sudakov and by Keevash and Staden) and Kotzig's cyclic-decomposition conjecture. Wenjie Fang (arXiv 1003.3045, 2010) verified it for every tree with at most 35 vertices (2,262,366,343,746 trees at n = 35). Brinkmann, Crevals, Melot, Rylands and Steffen (DMTCS 14, 2012) computed alpha-deficits of all trees with maximum degree 3 up to 36 vertices: none on 36 vertices is deficitary, so all of them have alpha-labelings and are graceful; most, not all, trees on 37 vertices were tested. Gallian's Dynamic Survey DS6 (28th ed., 30 Oct 2025, Section 2.1) says the conjecture 'remains open even for trees with maximum degree 3' and records no verification beyond 35. Claimed proofs by Edinah Gnang (arXiv 1811.07614; arXiv 2202.03178, v3 31 Jan 2025) and J. Keen (Zenodo 2026, abstract redacted) are unrefereed and not accepted; a July 2026 ResearchGate preprint by P. Pajo titled as a verification at n = 36 could not be read (403) and is unconfirmed. Credit: Ringel, Kotzig, Rosa; Fang; Brinkmann et al.; Gallian.
targets.success_criterion: Success means EITHER (a) a tree T with no graceful labeling, certified by two independent exhaustive methods (for example a SAT encoding with an UNSAT proof in DRAT/LRAT checked by drat-trim or cake_lpr, plus an independent backtracking search); necessarily T has at least 36 vertices; OR (b) a complete machine-checked proof (Lean 4 with Mathlib, Isabelle or Coq) of 'every finite tree has a graceful labeling', with the formal statement reviewed to match the standard definition and no sorry or extra axioms. Gnang's arguments count only if formalised as in (b).

partial_wins.statement: Verification that every tree on 36 vertices (6,226,306,037,178 trees, OEIS A000055) is graceful: released deterministic code that generates all trees (count checked against A000055) and passes each emitted labeling through an independent checker, with logs, reproduced by a skeptic on a random sample of at least 1% of the generation shards plus the shard totals, and no earlier complete, checkable verification of n = 36 found at claim time.

The same standard of verification for every tree with maximum degree at most 3 on 37 and on 38 vertices (59,574,334,817 and 138,533,927,938 trees, OEIS A000672); n = 36 and below is already covered by Brinkmann et al. (2012) and Fang (2010).

targets.verification_method: (a) Check the proof certificate and rebuild the CNF independently; confirm T is a tree. (b) Compile the formal proof, print axioms, review the statement. Partial wins: rerun the released generator and checker on random shards, compare shard counts and the total with A000055 (or A000672), and validate each sampled labeling with an independent checker.
angles: Fang's probabilistic backtracking plus Horton's ideas; most trees fall instantly, so the cost is generation (WROM / gentreeg) and the rare hard trees.
Use known theorems (caterpillars, lobsters with perfect matchings, trees with alpha-labelings) only as a filter whose correctness is proven, never as an unchecked skip.
For a counterexample hunt, search trees with few graceful labelings (Anick's statistics point to particular caterpillar-like families).
pitfalls: Gnang's and Keen's proofs are unrefereed claims; citing them is not a win.
Proving a tree has no graceful labeling needs a certified exhaustive search, not a timeout.
Ringel's packing conjecture and Kotzig's rho-labeling conjecture are weaker consequences; a verification of those alone is not a win here.
Trees with maximum degree 3 on at most 36 vertices are already done (Brinkmann et al. 2012 via alpha-labelings); do not claim them.
Pajo's 2026 ResearchGate preprint on n = 36 returned 403 when this entry was checked; read it honestly if accessible before claiming p1.

targets.name: Super edge-magic tree conjecture (Enomoto-Llado-Nakamigawa-Ringel): extend the verification past 17 vertices, or a tree that is not super edge-magic
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (18-22 vertices); laptop-days to 25 vertices
targets.statement: An edge-magic total labeling of a graph with p vertices and q edges is a bijection from V and E to {1..p+q} with f(u)+f(uv)+f(v) constant over all edges; it is super edge-magic if the vertices get {1..p}. Equivalently (Figueroa-Centeno, Ichishima and Muntaner-Batle) a graph is super edge-magic iff there is a bijection f: V -> {1..p} whose edge sums f(u)+f(v) form q consecutive integers. Enomoto, Llado, Nakamigawa and Ringel (SUT J. Math. 34, 1998) conjectured that every tree is super edge-magic (which implies the Kotzig-Rosa conjecture that every tree is edge-magic total). S. M. Lee and Q. X. Shan verified it by computer for all trees with at most 17 vertices (MCCCC 2002); Fukuchi and Oshima proved it for trees of order n with diameter at least n-5. Gallian's Dynamic Survey DS6 (28th ed., 30 Oct 2025, Section 5.2) still gives 17 vertices as the verification bound. Tree counts (OEIS A000055): 123,867 on 18 vertices, 823,065 on 20, 5,623,756 on 22, 104,636,890 on 25. Credit: Enomoto, Llado, Nakamigawa, Ringel; Lee and Shan; Fukuchi and Oshima; Gallian.
targets.success_criterion: Success means EITHER (a) a certificate that every tree on at most 25 vertices is super edge-magic: for each n in 18..25, a file giving every unlabeled tree on n vertices (as from nauty gentreeg) with a bijection to {1..n} whose n-1 edge sums are consecutive integers, where an independent checker regenerates the trees, confirms the counts equal A000055(n), matches every tree by canonical form and checks each labeling; OR (b) a tree with no super edge-magic labeling, certified by two independent exhaustive methods (for example SAT with a DRAT/LRAT UNSAT proof plus an independent search). Before claiming, re-check the latest DS6 edition and the literature for a higher verification bound; orders already covered do not count.

partial_wins.statement: Certificate (as in (a)) that every tree on at most 20 vertices is super edge-magic.
Certificate that every tree on at most 22 vertices is super edge-magic.

targets.verification_method: Regenerate trees with gentreeg n, compare counts with A000055, canonically label and match certificate entries, and for each labeling check it is a bijection onto {1..n} and that the sorted edge sums are consecutive. Minutes per order up to 22; about an hour at 25.
angles: Use the consecutive-edge-sum reformulation: a much smaller search than total labelings.

Every tree with an alpha-labeling is super edge-magic (DS6 Section 5.2; with threshold k, map lower labels l to k+1-l and upper labels u to u+1). Brinkmann, Crevals, Melot, Rylands and Steffen (DMTCS 14, 2012, https://dmtcs.episciences.org/569/pdf) tabulate the alpha-deficit of all trees up to 26 vertices, so label every tree via a fast alpha-labeling search and spend exact search only on the deficitary residue.
Caterpillars are super edge-magic by construction; label everything else with CP-SAT or randomized backtracking seeded from a caterpillar spine.
Record the hardest trees per order; they are the natural place to look for a counterexample.
pitfalls: Super edge-magic requires vertex labels exactly {1..p}; an edge-magic total labeling with other vertex labels does not count.
The 17-vertex bound comes from a 2002 conference talk cited in DS6; a later unpublished extension may exist, so search before claiming.
Certificates must cover every isomorphism class; check the count against A000055.

targets.name: Odd-graceful tree conjecture (Gnanajothi): extend the verification past 12 vertices, or a tree that is not odd-graceful
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: A graph with q edges is odd-graceful (Gnanajothi 1991) if its vertices get distinct labels from {0,1,...,2q-1} so that the edge differences |f(u)-f(v)| are exactly the odd numbers 1, 3, ..., 2q-1. Every graph with an alpha-labeling is odd-graceful and no graph with an odd cycle is. R. B. Gnanajothi conjectured that every tree is odd-graceful and proved it for trees of order up to 10; Christian Barrientos extended this to trees of order up to 12 (unpublished, cited in DS6) and proved it for caterpillar forests and trees of diameter at most five. Gallian's Dynamic Survey DS6 (28th ed., 30 Oct 2025, Section 3.6) still gives order 12 as the bound. The next orders are tiny: 1,301 trees on 13 vertices, 19,320 on 16, 823,065 on 20 and 5,623,756 on 22 (OEIS A000055). Credit: Gnanajothi; Barrientos; Gallian.
targets.success_criterion: Success means EITHER (a) a certificate that every tree on at most 22 vertices is odd-graceful: for each n in 13..22, a file giving every unlabeled tree on n vertices (as from nauty gentreeg) with an odd-graceful labeling, where an independent checker regenerates the trees, confirms the counts equal A000055(n), matches every tree by canonical form, and checks the labels are distinct in [0, 2n-3] with edge differences exactly {1, 3, ..., 2n-3}; OR (b) a tree with no odd-graceful labeling, certified by two independent exhaustive methods. Before claiming, re-check the latest DS6 edition and the literature for a higher verification bound.

partial_wins.statement: Certificate (as in (a)) that every tree on at most 16 vertices is odd-graceful.
Certificate that every tree on at most 20 vertices is odd-graceful.

targets.verification_method: Regenerate trees with gentreeg, compare counts with A000055, match certificate entries by canonical form, check each labeling's range, injectivity and the set of edge differences. Minutes.
angles: Trees with an alpha-labeling are odd-graceful (double the labels on one side and shift), so start from alpha-labelings and search directly only for the rest. Brinkmann, Crevals, Melot, Rylands and Steffen (DMTCS 14, 2012, https://dmtcs.episciences.org/569/pdf) computed the alpha-deficit of every tree up to 26 vertices and give the number of trees with nonzero deficit for each order (Appendix A: counts, not lists). That residue, which you must regenerate yourself, is the only part needing a direct search.
Backtracking by largest odd difference first, as for graceful labelings.
pitfalls: Labels range over {0..2q-1}; edge differences must be exactly the q odd numbers below 2q.
Barrientos's order-12 result is unpublished; DS6 is the source of the bound, and a later extension may exist, so search before claiming.

targets.name: MOONSHOT - Graham-Sloane harmonious tree conjecture: a tree that is not harmonious, a formal proof, or the first verification past Fang's 31 vertices
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (about 4.7e13 trees on 38 vertices)
targets.statement: Graham and Sloane (SIAM J. Alg. Discrete Methods 1, 1980) conjectured that every tree is harmonious: for a tree with q edges (q+1 vertices) there is a labeling f: V -> Z_q, injective except that exactly one label is used twice, such that the edge sums f(u)+f(v) mod q are pairwise distinct. Aldred and McKay verified it for trees with at most 26 vertices; Wenjie Fang (arXiv 1106.3490, v2 2012) published a verification for all trees with at most 31 vertices (40,330,829,030 trees at n = 31). Fang's code then ran on the volunteer project yoyo@home, whose Harmonious Trees status page (fetched 2026-10-30) shows the series for 32 to 37 nodes as completed, with no published write-up or certificates. Montgomery, Pokrovskiy and Sudakov proved every tree is almost-harmonious (any abelian group of order n + o(n)); Muyesser and Pokrovskiy (arXiv 2509.05280, v2 6 Oct 2025) confirm the Graham-Sloane conjecture for bounded-degree trees on sufficiently many vertices (their Theorem 1.5: for each maximum degree Delta, all n at least an inexplicit n0(Delta)). Gallian's Dynamic Survey DS6 (28th ed., 30 Oct 2025) still lists the conjecture as open; Gnang and Williams posted a claimed proof (arXiv 2201.02240, v1 only, no journal reference). Credit: Graham, Sloane; Aldred, McKay; Fang and the yoyo@home volunteers; Montgomery, Pokrovskiy, Sudakov; Muyesser, Pokrovskiy; Gallian.
targets.success_criterion: Success means EITHER (a) a tree with no harmonious labeling, certified by two independent exhaustive methods (for example SAT with a DRAT/LRAT UNSAT proof checked by drat-trim or cake_lpr plus an independent search); by Fang's published result it has at least 32 vertices (very likely at least 38, given the completed yoyo@home series), and by Muyesser-Pokrovskiy a tree of maximum degree Delta can be a counterexample only below their inexplicit threshold n0(Delta), so their theorem rules out no specific small tree; OR (b) a complete machine-checked proof (Lean 4/Mathlib, Isabelle or Coq) that every finite tree with at least 2 vertices is harmonious, with the formal statement reviewed and no sorry or extra axioms.

partial_wins.statement: Verification that every tree on 38 vertices (47,436,313,524,262 trees, OEIS A000055) is harmonious: released generator and labeler, independent checker on every emitted labeling, total checked against A000055, and a skeptic rerun of at least 1% of shards. Orders 32 to 37 do not count (yoyo@home series completed).

targets.verification_method: (a) Check the certificate and re-derive the encoding; (b) compile and audit the formal statement and axioms. Partial win: rerun random shards, compare counts with A000055(38), and check sampled labelings (one repeated label, all q sums distinct mod q) with an independent program.
angles: Fang's hybrid of probabilistic backtracking, tabu search and constraint programming; reuse labelings across trees that differ by moving one leaf.
Caterpillars are harmonious (Graham-Sloane); filter only with proven theorems.
A counterexample search should focus on trees whose harmonious labelings are rare in exhaustive counts for small n.
pitfalls: The tree definition allows exactly one repeated vertex label; injective labelings are impossible for trees since there are q+1 vertices and q residues.
The Gnang-Williams arXiv proof is an unrefereed claim.
Do not confuse harmonious with graceful labelings or with the 'almost-harmonious' theorem.
Every tree with an alpha-labeling is harmonious, so a counterexample must have no alpha-labeling.
The yoyo@home page shows completed workunits for 32-37 nodes but no stated outcome; treat those orders as done, not as open.

targets.name: Automatic decipherment on known scripts: beat CSA_OptMatcher's mean cognate-matching accuracy on the seven Tamburini 2025 benchmarks (Ugaritic, Linear B, Cypriot, Phoenician, Luvian)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (seven lexicon files of 136 to 4,442 lines; CSA_OptMatcher itself runs 16 parallel annealers)
targets.statement: Decipherment methods are validated on scripts that are already read: given an unpaired word list in the 'lost' script and one in a known related language, match each lost word to its cognate. Snyder, Barzilay and Knight (ACL 2010) introduced Ugaritic/Old Hebrew; Berg-Kirkpatrick and Klein (2011) reached 90.4% noiseless; Luo, Cao and Barzilay (NeuroDecipher, ACL 2019) added Linear B/Mycenaean Greek (919 pairs) and its names-only variant. Fabio Tamburini (Frontiers in AI 8, 2025, doi 10.3389/frai.2025.1581129; CAWL 2023 version) released all seven benchmarks in github.com/ftamburin/CSA_OptMatcher (GPL-3.0, last commit c2cb1626ca, 2025-09-15): U/OH noiseless (2,214 pairs), U/OH noisy (2,214 pairs plus 1,119 and 1,108 unpaired words), Ph/Ug (105 pairs, StarlingDB), LB/MG (919), LB/MG-names (455 pairs, 919 Linear B words), CS/AG Cypriot Syllabary/Arcadocypriot (693), Luv/Hit (59 gold rows in the file; the paper says 60). Table 3 gives mean (max) accuracy over four runs for CSA_OptMatcher: 95.5 (96.3), 74.7 (75.8), 80.5 (82.9), 89.4 (91.0), 83.4 (87.0), 86.3 (87.9), 47.5 (48.3); and for NeuroDecipher rerun by Tamburini without cognate counts: 90.4, 87.6 (88.26) on U/OH noisy, the best there, 71.2, 75.8, 67.9, 75.9, and 18.2 on Luv/Hit (that run was given the number of cognates). Luo 2019's own figures (93.5, 84.7, 67.3; 65.9 on a different noisy set) are below these bests; Born, Monroe, Kelley and Sarkar (CAWL 2024) report 46% top-1 on noisy U/OH. Status 2026-10-30: no later result on these files found (citations of Luo 2019 and Tamburini 2025 checked).
targets.success_criterion: For a benchmark D among the seven .cog files at commit c2cb1626ca (sha256: uga-heb.no_speNL.cog 048eb1eab6921f6594fa2ba1035dd96ee3a95fb99ca6beb6b52e60480f0fdfb7; uga-heb.no_speNoisy.cog 0f73045a2d9e44ba6212c22fb21e15e98f16dacfe66bcc6d35590121881a2e65; StarlingDB_Ph-Ug.cog ff5b915afecfe844cc6cd278d64bfe64c1b494fa687708f0342a99b431219033; linear_b-greek.cog 270ff077e1300baf5e0b383a91cf3ab9fc84a981f6f08c780f3e7fa0fdfa9cff; linear_b-greek.names.cog ec09bb5d840051965e8d849f8fa643aecaa2d2a140177195d623c08540d035c6; csyl-greek.cog 60fd1818341dcc45bcf97a6cea0ba441c0d6488992a07a22e48c7955a6bc4b58; RWT2002_Luv-Hit.cog 4de4b31a7f487739a32653b210284d93df9645b140376172786ed5d577ae6523), the verifier splits D into a lost list (non-'_' cells of column 1) and a known list (non-'_' cells of column 2), shuffles each with a published seed, relabels every lost-side symbol by a random bijection to opaque codes, and gives the claimant only these two lists. The claimant's published code outputs a one-to-one partial matching (each lost entry to at most one known entry, each known entry used at most once). Accuracy = matched gold rows (both cells non-'_', lost and known entry from the same row; '|' variants belong to their entry) / number of gold rows. A full win: one fixed configuration, run with at least 4 seeds fixed in advance, all runs reported and none selected using gold, whose mean accuracy is strictly above the best published mean on at least two benchmarks, one of them noisy (U/OH noisy, Ph/Ug, LB/MG-names, Luv/Hit). Bars: 95.5, 87.6, 80.5, 89.4, 83.4, 86.3, 47.5 (Table 3, re-read before claiming). No gold pairs, cognate counts, sign values, external lexica or pretrained language models may be used; the verifier reruns at least one seed under a fresh shuffle and relabelling.

partial_wins.statement: Same protocol, mean accuracy over at least 4 seeds strictly above the best published mean on one of the seven benchmarks.
Same protocol, on LB/MG-names or Ph/Ug, the claimant's mean over at least 4 seeds is strictly above CSA_OptMatcher's best single run (87.0 and 82.9 respectively), not only its mean.
Same protocol, Luv/Hit (same script, different languages): mean accuracy of at least 55.0% (32.45 of 59 gold rows on average) without being told the number of cognates.

targets.verification_method: The verifier downloads the .cog files from the pinned commit and checks their sha256, builds the shuffled and relabelled lists with its own seed, runs the claimant's code (CPU, hours at most) for at least one seed and checks the output is a one-to-one matching, recomputes accuracy with its own scorer and compares with the claimed runs; it reads the code to confirm that no gold pairing, cognate count or external resource is used.
angles: Combine CSA's sign-mapping search with NeuroDecipher's neural edit model: anneal over mappings, score with a learned character alignment.
Exploit frequency and positional statistics of sign n-grams to prune the mapping space before annealing.
For noisy sets, add an explicit null-match option with a calibrated threshold so unpaired words are not forced into pairs.
pitfalls: The .cog rows are aligned pairs: reading both columns together is reading the answer. Only the verifier's shuffled, relabelled lists are legitimate input.

Ugaritic and Hebrew are both transliterated in Latin letters in these files, so a system that trusts identical symbols gets a free prior; the relabelling removes it, and a claim that depends on it fails.
Pretrained LLMs know Linear B sign values and Greek words; any use of them, or of a Linear B or Cypriot sign table, voids the claim.
Tamburini scored with his EvalModel (any variant pair in the matching counts); this entry scores one-to-one entry matches, which can be slightly stricter. Report both.
Tamburini and Luo note that NeuroDecipher needed restarts to converge; restarts chosen by gold accuracy are selection, and all runs count in the mean.

targets.name: Cognate reflex prediction (SIGTYP 2022 surprise data): beat FeVeT and CogTran on normalized edit distance and B-Cubed F at the 0.10, 0.30 and 0.50 test proportions
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (10 Lexibank wordlists, a few MB; small transformers train on CPU)
targets.statement: In the SIGTYP 2022 shared task (List, Vylomova, Forkel, Hill and Cotterell, 2022.sigtyp-1.7; github.com/sigtyp/ST2022, release v1.4) systems predict withheld words in cognate sets from their reflexes in related languages, on 10 surprise datasets (bremerberta, wangbai, beidazihui, hillburmish, deepadungpalaung, luangthongkumkaren, bodtkhobwa, birchallchapacuran, kesslersignificance, bantubvd) at five test proportions (0.10 to 0.50). Official scores (st2022 --evaluate): per dataset the mean over languages, then the mean over the 10 datasets, of edit distance (ED), normalized edit distance (NED), B-Cubed F (BCFS) and BLEU. Task winner Mockingbird-I1 (Kirov, Sproat and Gutkin): NED 0.2431 / 0.2648 / 0.2899 / 0.3162 / 0.3518 and BCFS 0.7673 / 0.7120 / 0.6717 / 0.6428 / 0.6050 at 0.10 to 0.50. Akavarapu and Bhattacharya's Cognate Transformer (EMNLP 2023) report CogTran-small NED 0.2421 / 0.2919 / 0.3332 and BCFS 0.7823 / 0.6954 / 0.6477 at 0.10 / 0.30 / 0.50 (their appendix per-family BCFS average to only 0.7628 / 0.6752 / 0.6257). Wientzek's FeVeT (Open Research Europe 2025, doi 10.12688/openreseurope.20647.1, v1 under review; github.com/TGH-2020/FeVeT) reports fine-tuned ED 0.7836 / 0.9589 / 1.1111, NED 0.205 / 0.2397 / 0.2825, BCFS 0.8041 / 0.7232 / 0.673, but these are means over 99 languages; its own per-dataset files average, in the official way, to ED 0.9064 / 1.1128 / 1.2725, NED 0.2289 / 0.2705 / 0.3111 and BCFS 0.7811 / 0.6941 / 0.6418. Bars used here: NED 0.2289, 0.2705, 0.3111 (FeVeT, official-style); BCFS 0.7823, 0.6954, 0.6477 (CogTran headline, the highest reported, kept as the conservative bar). Status 2026-10-30: no later result found (citations of the task paper, CogTran and FeVeT checked).
targets.success_criterion: Frozen prediction files (hash committed before scoring) for all 10 surprise datasets at proportions 0.10, 0.30 and 0.50, each produced by published code that reads only that proportion's training-{P}.tsv and test-{P}.tsv from ST2022 tag v1.4 (other datasets' training partitions and generic phonetic feature tables such as CLTS are allowed; no Lexibank or CLDF source of the surprise languages, no solutions file, no other proportion's files of the same dataset). Scored with the ST2022 definitions as the mean over the 10 datasets, the claim must, at every one of the three proportions, have NED strictly below the bar (0.2289, 0.2705, 0.3111) and BCFS strictly above the bar (0.7823, 0.6954, 0.6477). Bars are re-read from the FeVeT family-result files and the CogTran paper before claiming, and any credible published official-style value found by the skeptic replaces them if better.

partial_wins.statement: Same rules, NED and BCFS both beat the bars at one of the three proportions 0.10, 0.30, 0.50.

Same rules at proportion 0.20 or 0.40 (where only shared-task runs are published): beat Mockingbird-I1 on all four official metrics (0.20: ED 1.0413, NED 0.2648, BCFS 0.7120, BLEU 0.6326; 0.40: ED 1.2725, NED 0.3162, BCFS 0.6428, BLEU 0.5724).
Same rules, NED strictly below FeVeT's headline averages (0.205, 0.2397, 0.2825) at all three proportions under the official mean over datasets.

targets.verification_method: The verifier fetches the v1.4 training, test and solutions files, checks the prediction files' hashes, scores them with its own implementation of the ST2022 metrics (cross-checked on the released Mockingbird-I1 outputs, which must reproduce the results/*.md values), and reads the code to confirm the data restrictions; one dataset and proportion may be re-run.
angles: Ensemble FeVeT-style feature-vector decoding with correspondence-pattern SVM predictions (the ST2022 baseline-SVM) and pick per cognate set by agreement.
Pretrain on the other datasets' training partitions with language embeddings, then fine-tune per dataset as FeVeT does.
pitfalls: FeVeT's headline averages (s2s_reflex_finetuned_avg.txt) are means over languages, not the official mean over datasets: its own family files give NED 0.2289 at 0.10, not 0.205. Compare like with like.

Proportions are separate splits of the same wordlists: training-0.10.tsv contains most of the words withheld in test-0.50.tsv. Using any other proportion's files of the same dataset leaks the answers.
Each data-surprise/ < dataset> folder of ST2022 also holds cognates.tsv, wordlist.tsv and solutions-{P}.tsv, which contain every withheld word; only training-{P}.tsv and test-{P}.tsv may be read.
The full Lexibank CLDF datasets behind the surprise data are public and contain every withheld word.

targets.name: Middle Chinese protoform reconstruction (WikiHan, WikiHan-aug, Hóu): beat the Lu-Wang-Mortensen 2024 reranked systems on accuracy and token edit distance
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (5,165 cognate sets; GRU and Transformer models train on CPU or a small GPU)
targets.statement: Supervised protoform reconstruction predicts the ancestral form of a cognate set from its daughter reflexes. WikiHan (Chang, Cui, Kim and Mortensen, COLING 2022, github.com/cmu-llab/wikihan, CC0) pairs Baxter-Sagart Middle Chinese with reflexes in 8 Sinitic varieties; with Chang et al.'s split it has 3,615 / 517 / 1,033 train / dev / test cognate sets. Lu, Wang and Mortensen (LREC-COLING 2024, arXiv 2403.18769; github.com/cmu-llab/reranked-reconstruction, last commit 2024-04-30) rerank beam-search reconstructions with a reflex prediction model and report, as means of 20 runs on the test sets (Table 3): WikiHan, GRU-BS + Transformer reranker, ACC 57.26%, token edit distance (TED) 0.7029, TER 0.1646, FER 0.0658, BCFS 0.7520; WikiHan-aug (Cui et al. 2022, training augmented with Mockingbird-I1 predictions, same test set) 58.58% and 0.6822 (GRU reranker); Hóu 2004 (39 varieties, Kim et al. 2023 split, 562 / 81 / 161) 42.08% and 0.9503 (Transformer reranker). Baselines: Meloni et al. 2021 GRU and Kim et al. 2023 Transformer (WikiHan 55.58% and 54.62%). The repository ships all three Sinitic splits (data/chinese_wikihan2022, chinese_wikihan2022_augmented, chinese_baxter). Status 2026-10-30: searches found no later supervised result above these on the same splits; the ACL 2024 semisupervised paper (arXiv 2406.05930) keeps only 5-30% of the training labels (main experiments at 10%), and the repository marks the Romance sets as unavailable.
targets.success_criterion: On the WikiHan test split shipped in cmu-llab/reranked-reconstruction data/chinese_wikihan2022/test.pickle (sha256 b8d4e577bfc5c85f208f841b9d49c352607fec5f44499f0ce6782bf4a829898d; 1,033 cognate sets), a system trained only on the matching train.pickle (dev.pickle for tuning) produces frozen predictions (hash committed before scoring) from at least 10 independent seeds fixed in advance, all scored; a deterministic system may submit one run. The mean exact-match accuracy over runs (whole phoneme sequence including tone equals the gold Baxter protoform) must be strictly above 57.26% AND the mean token edit distance (Levenshtein over phoneme tokens, averaged over test sets) strictly below 0.7029. Inputs are the daughter reflexes and language labels only: the character keys of the pickles, any Middle Chinese or Old Chinese dictionary, WikiHan's full TSVs and any pretrained model that saw Chinese character readings are excluded.

partial_wins.statement: Same rules on WikiHan-aug (train from chinese_wikihan2022_augmented, same test set): mean ACC strictly above 58.58% and mean TED strictly below 0.6822.
Same rules on Hóu (chinese_baxter split, 161 test sets): mean ACC strictly above 42.08% and mean TED strictly below 0.9503.
Same rules on WikiHan: mean ACC strictly above 57.26% alone, with mean TED no worse than 0.7360 (the Meloni GRU baseline).

targets.verification_method: The verifier fetches the pickles, checks sha256, loads them with an unpickler that refuses all classes (each file is a tuple of a language list and a dict of cognate sets holding only dicts, lists and strings), checks the prediction hashes, and recomputes ACC and TED with its own code; it reads the training code for the input restrictions and may retrain one seed.
angles: Rerank larger beams with an ensemble of reflex predictors, as Lu et al. did, but score with PanPhon feature distance rather than exact reflex match.
Cognate Transformer (Akavarapu and Bhattacharya 2023) style MSA encoders over aligned reflexes.
pitfalls: The splits are Python pickles: never load them with a plain pickle.load; a class-refusing unpickler is enough.
The pickle keys are Chinese characters with an index (e.g. 梆1), and a Middle Chinese reading is a dictionary lookup away; any use of the key, or of a model that knows character readings, is leakage.
Lu et al.'s values are means of 20 runs: one lucky seed above 57.26% is not a win.

targets.name: Historical handwriting (READ 2016 Ratsprotokolle, line level): beat HTR-ConvText's 3.6% CER and 15.7% WER on the 1,138 test lines without external data
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (about 550 MB of page images; a GPU helps); scoring needs only text files
targets.statement: The ICFHR 2016 READ competition dataset (Sánchez, Romero, Toselli and Vidal, ICFHR 2016; Zenodo record 1297399, CC BY 4.0, 2018) holds pages of the Ratsprotokolle council minutes (1470 to 1805, Early Modern German) with line-level PAGE ground truth: the test archive Test-ICFHR-2016.tgz (md5 894063b8abbe2f671dbb07a144738300) has 50 pages with 1,138 transcribed lines, matching the 8,349 / 1,040 / 1,138 line split used in the line-level literature. Lowest published line-level test CER without external data, pretraining or language models: HTR-ConvText (arXiv 2512.05021v1, December 2025, code and checkpoints at github.com/DAIR-Group/HTR-ConvText) 3.6% CER / 15.7% WER; before it HTR-VT (Li et al., Pattern Recognition 2024) 3.9 / 16.5, VAN and DAN (Coquenet et al.) 4.1, and Spike-HTR (arXiv 2608.01646, August 2026) 3.9. With external resources, HAND (arXiv 2412.18981, github.com/MHHamdan/HAND) reports 2.71 / 10.98 after pretraining on synthetic lines rendered from 103 fonts and 1.65 / 4.95 with an mT5 post-corrector. Page-level results (DAN 3.43) are a different task. Status 2026-10-30: searches found no closed-setting line-level result below 3.6.
targets.success_criterion: A frozen transcription file (one line of text per test line id, hash committed before scoring) for all 1,138 transcribed lines of Test-ICFHR-2016.tgz, with line images cut by a published deterministic rule from the PAGE coordinates. CER = total character Levenshtein distance / total gold characters, WER the same over whitespace-separated words, both on the gold Unicode text with only a published whitespace normalisation, must be strictly below 3.6% CER AND 15.7% WER. Training and model selection use only the Train-And-Val-ICFHR-2016 images and transcriptions: no other handwriting or printed data, no synthetic text images, no pretrained weights, no language model built from outside text. Control: the claimant scores the released HTR-ConvText READ2016 checkpoint through the same line extraction and scorer; it must land within 0.3 CER of 3.6, otherwise the pipeline is not comparable, and the claim must also beat this reproduced score.

partial_wins.statement: Same rules and control: CER strictly below 3.6% with WER at most 16.5% (HTR-VT).
Synthetic text images allowed (rendered from fonts with text drawn only from the training transcriptions), otherwise the same rules and control: CER strictly below HAND's 2.71%.

targets.verification_method: The verifier downloads both Zenodo archives (md5 checked), regenerates the line images and gold strings with the published rule, checks the frozen file's hash, recomputes CER and WER with its own Levenshtein code, reruns the HTR-ConvText control, and reads the training code for the data restrictions.
angles: Heavy geometric and elastic augmentation plus test-time augmentation with CTC posterior averaging.
A character n-gram language model trained only on the training transcriptions, decoded with beam search, is allowed and untried by the closed-setting leaders.
pitfalls: Line extraction (polygon mask vs bounding box) and Unicode normalisation of the gold text move CER by tenths; the reproduced-checkpoint control is what makes a comparison fair.
Two test lines carry no text and are not scored.
The Ratsprotokolle collection is online in Transkribus and elsewhere; any of its transcriptions outside the training archive may contain test pages.

The control checkpoint (read.pth on the DAIR-Group/HTR-ConvText Hugging Face repo) is a PyTorch pickle: load it with torch.load(..., weights_only=True) and review the repository code before running any of it.

targets.name: Latin dependency parsing (EvaLatin 2026): beat the best CLAS on Seneca's Phoenissae (74.03) and Aquinas's Summa (83.14) under the official scorer
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (two CoNLL-U files of about 4,150 words each; UD Latin treebanks for training)
targets.statement: EvaLatin 2026 (LT4HALA 2026 at LREC; parsing task run by Federica Iurescia, Marco Passarotti and Rachele Sprugnoli of CIRCSE, Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore) set Universal Dependencies parsing of two unseen Latin texts with gold tokenisation, lemmas, POS and features given: poetry, Seneca's Phoenissae (308 sentences, 4,156 syntactic words plus 86 multiword tokens, from LASLA's Opera Latina, converted, pre-parsed and revised by an expert) and prose, a portion of Thomas Aquinas's Summa Theologiae from the Index Thomisticus (203 sentences, 4,151 words). No training set was imposed: any data or model could be used. Gold files (uploaded 2026-02-20), scorers, all submitted runs (EvaLatin_2026_runs) and ranking are in github.com/CIRCSE/LT4HALA, 2026/data_and_doc. Best CLAS with subtypes: poetry THIVLVC_2 (Pommeret, Wagret and Deret) 74.03, prose UppsalaNLP_1 (Sara Stymne) 83.14 (UDPipe baseline 56.94 and 79.41); CLAS without subtypes 76.08 (THIVLVC_2) and 86.88 (UppsalaNLP_1); LAS with subtypes 72.88 and 84.41; LAS without subtypes 77.60 and 87.93 (both THIVLVC_2). The proceedings (11 May 2026) add contrastive runs (Uppsala ITTB-only prose CLAS+s 82.77, LAS+s 84.43) that do not move the CLAS-with-subtypes records. Since then UD_Latin-CIRCSE has added the whole of Phoenissae (new text added April 2026, merged to master 6 May 2026): all 308 poetry test sentences, 306 of them with the same HEAD and DEPREL as the EvaLatin gold (our check, 2026-10-30). Status 2026-10-30: no later result on these files was found.
targets.success_criterion: Frozen CoNLL-U outputs (HEAD and DEPREL filled, all other columns as in the released test files EvaLatin_2026_poetry_test_data.conllu, sha256 b9fe2d95717976e4bcd5617edc71449890d032621fd6de841e55cf4cf3aeba4f, and EvaLatin_2026_prose_test_data.conllu, sha256 29cef94d9afca54ea488b1875d983465e3dc712f9f5e9afd124283e7902d533d; output hashes committed before scoring), scored against EvaLatin_2026_poetry_gold.conllu (sha256 0584cc804f6fd0cae200cd0640f0f391af2099bae5f450edc5239d0aadfb3842) and EvaLatin_2026_prose_gold.conllu (sha256 59ac041f12d9d30da5cc1f20122ea6a0c87748722caaf714383112cf71811f60) with the official scorer, meaning data_and_doc/conll18_ud_eval_with_subtypes-EvaLatin2026.py run with --subtypes (not the _modified version), which counts a word for CLAS only when its full DEPREL is in the plain UD content list and reproduces 74.03 on the released THIVLVC_2 poetry run and 83.14 on the released UppsalaNLP_1 prose run, must reach CLAS with subtypes strictly above 74.03 on poetry AND strictly above 83.14 on prose. The gold files, the released runs and any copy of these test sentences are excluded from training and tuning. That includes the Seneca Phoenissae sentences in UD_Latin-CIRCSE (all 308 poetry test sentences are there since the May 2026 release; drop every Phoenissae sentence from every split) and any UD Latin-ITTB or Opera Latina sentence that matches a test sentence (verifier checks overlap). Language models may be used only if their training data predate 2026-02-01 (documented release) or were trained locally on stated data. One system and configuration covers both files.

partial_wins.statement: Same rules, CLAS with subtypes strictly above the record on one of the two files.
Same rules, LAS without subtypes strictly above 77.60 (poetry) and 87.93 (prose).

targets.verification_method: The verifier fetches the gold and test files, both scorer versions and the released runs from CIRCSE/LT4HALA and checks hashes. It confirms that conll18_ud_eval_with_subtypes-EvaLatin2026.py --subtypes reproduces 74.03 (THIVLVC_2 poetry) and 83.14 (UppsalaNLP_1 prose) on the released runs, or its own reimplementation of that rule does. It checks that the outputs keep the given tokenisation and annotation, then rescores them with that scorer and with its own CLAS code. It checks the training data for overlap with the test sentences (exact and near-duplicate sentence match), in particular that no Phoenissae sentence from UD_Latin-CIRCSE and no matching ITTB or Opera Latina sentence was used.
angles: Train on a harmonised mix of the UD Latin treebanks (Perseus, and UD_Latin-CIRCSE's other Seneca tragedies Hercules Furens, Agamemnon and Oedipus for poetry, with every Phoenissae sentence removed; ITTB for Aquinas) with treebank embeddings, as the guidelines suggest.
Use the gold morphology in the input: feature-rich biaffine parsers gain most from it on poetry.
pitfalls: UD_Latin-CIRCSE (master since 6 May 2026, UD release of May 2026) contains Seneca's Phoenissae in its train, dev and test splits: all 308 poetry test sentences, 306 with gold-identical trees. Any model trained on a UD_Latin-CIRCSE release from 2026 or later, or a pretrained Latin parser whose training set includes it, has seen the answer key. Filter by sent_id (SenPhoen-P-17-* or Latin_SenecaYounger_Phoen_poetry-*) and by text match.
UD Latin-ITTB is built from Aquinas and may contain the Summa test passage; remove any overlap before training (our check found 1 exact sentence match and 2 sentences sharing an 8-gram).
The gold has been public since February 2026: a language model trained on later web data may have seen it. Models with training data after 2026-02-01 are excluded.

Rankings with and without subtypes differ; this entry's bar is CLAS with subtypes, under the unmodified scorer. The _modified scorer in the same folder counts subtyped relations as content words and gives different numbers.

targets.name: Latin named entity recognition (EvaLatin 2026, Ovid, Pliny, Tacitus): beat uOttawa's strict micro-F1 (0.908 coarse, 0.865 fine)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (26,308 test tokens in HIPE IOB format)
targets.statement: The EvaLatin 2026 named entity task (LT4HALA 2026 at LREC; task organisers Valeria Irene Boano, Eleonora Litta and Matteo Romanello, within the CIRCSE-run EvaLatin campaign of Passarotti and Sprugnoli) asks for proper names in Classical Latin, typed coarse (person, place, collective, creature, ...) and fine, in the HIPE IOB format, scored with the CLEF HIPE scorer as micro precision, recall and F1, strict (exact type and boundaries) and fuzzy. The test file evalatin2026-ner-v0.1-test.tsv (26,308 tokens; Ovid Metamorphoses 4 and 14, Pliny the Elder Naturalis Historia IV 1-85, Tacitus Germania; 2,665 scored coarse mentions, CC BY; gold uploaded 2026-02-27) and a small training sample are in github.com/CIRCSE/LT4HALA, 2026/data_and_doc, with the official results (EvaLatin_NERC_results.pdf, 27 February 2026). Best runs, both by Callum Chan (uOttawa) with few-shot prompting of commercial LLMs: NERC coarse strict uOttawa_nerc-coarse_2 (claude-sonnet-4-5) P 0.899 R 0.917 F1 0.908 (KULeuven 0.714, argo-navis 0.534); coarse fuzzy 0.941; NERC fine strict uOttawa_nerc-fine_1 (gemini-2.5-pro) 0.865; fine fuzzy 0.887. Any resource was allowed. The proceedings (11 May 2026) add only weaker post-campaign runs (uOttawa fine-tuned LaBERTa, coarse strict 0.749). Status 2026-10-30: no later result on this file was found.
targets.success_criterion: A frozen prediction file in the HIPE IOB format of evalatin2026-ner-v0.1-test-masked.tsv (sha256 487a1c9e5fec675931f10582143a0ec185b4d8b56fa588d5964821e97f9f56af; output hash committed before scoring), scored against evalatin2026-ner-v0.1-test.tsv (sha256 e92227d40f2f4b7080a68091d99c34055c41602444684ae8bbb5ed89e6f96a26) with the HIPE scorer's micro F1, must reach NERC coarse strict F1 strictly above 0.908 AND NERC fine strict F1 strictly above 0.865. The gold file and any annotated copy of these four texts are excluded from training, prompting and tuning. Annotated means any token-level annotation, not only named entities: the Tacitus Germania portion of UD_Latin-CIRCSE (gold UPOS, PROPN) and the LASLA Opera Latina lemmatised files for these texts count. Language models may be used only if their training data predate 2026-02-01 (documented) or were trained locally on stated data; the training sample and other public NER data are allowed.

partial_wins.statement: Same rules, NERC coarse strict micro-F1 strictly above 0.908 alone.
Same rules, NERC fine strict micro-F1 strictly above 0.865 alone.
