targets.verification_method: Write an independent checker (numpy or C, no claimant code). For each agent, compute MMS_i by enumerating all n^m labelled partitions, or by an exact DP over bundle sums, and check that the claimed partition attains it. Then enumerate all n^m complete allocations and compute the exact max-min ratio with fractions.Fraction; for chores compute the min-max ratio. Negative controls: the Ezra-Garbuz goods instance (v1 = 1 17 3 10 1 10 7 7 7 3 18 and v2 = 1 14 5 10 1 9 6 7 7 5 19, two agents of each type) must give MMS = 21 and best min value 20. Their chores instance must give MMS 90 and best max cost 93, and the FST instance must give 39/40. Compare strictly with the bars.
angles: Ezra and Garbuz report that their small instances were explored with an LLM. Their structure is two valuation types, every agent's MMS equal to her proportional share, and two disjoint exact partitions. Generalise it to three types, five agents or 12-14 items, and search integer perturbations with an exact inner oracle.
Treat the search as a game: fix target partitions (one per type), then maximise the number of allocations violated, and repair them with ILP.
pitfalls: Instances with m <= n + 5 goods always have MMS allocations (FST), and so do four agents with at most 10 goods (Hummel IJCAI 2023). Search above those sizes.
Rounding MMS values or ratios in floating point can turn a tie into a false record; use exact arithmetic.
Partial allocations (goods left unallocated) are not allowed. Every item must go to some agent.

targets.name: Pairwise maximin share (PMMS): an additive instance whose best PMMS factor is below Gölz's 78/79 (goods) or above 1.102065 (chores)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-minutes to laptop-hours; a 3-agent, 9-good instance checks in under a second (3^9 allocations), and 4-5 agents with 10-12 items check in minutes
targets.statement: An allocation X of indivisible goods is PMMS if, for every pair of agents i and j, v_i(X_i) >= mu_i(2, X_i u X_j), the best worst bundle agent i can get by splitting the pair's pooled goods in two. Its PMMS factor is the min over pairs of v_i(X_i)/mu_i(2, X_i u X_j) (pairs with mu = 0 skipped). alpha*(I) is the best factor over all allocations; chores are defined dually with rho*(I). Whether PMMS always exists for additive goods was open from Caragiannis et al. (2016) until September 2026, when three groups answered it negatively: Aziz (arXiv:2609.06282, four agents), Gölz (arXiv:2609.08954, three agents and nine goods) and Bei, Lin, Liu, Luan and Tao (arXiv:2609.10493). Gölz also gave a 3-agent, 9-good instance with alpha* = 78/79, checked by exhaustive enumeration. Bei et al. give goods 226/227 and a five-agent, twelve-chore instance with rho* = 220413/200000 = 1.102065, prove every additive chores instance has a 4/3-PMMS allocation, and pose closing 0.7808 <= alpha_PMMS <= 78/79 and 1.102065 <= rho_PMMS <= 4/3 as open problems. Kurokawa's (sqrt 17 - 1)/4 ~ 0.781 is the best goods guarantee. This lane checker reproduced 78/79 exactly on Gölz's instance.
targets.success_criterion: An explicit additive instance with nonnegative integer values (or costs) such that either (goods) alpha*(I) < 78/79, or (chores) rho*(I) > 220413/200000, both strictly (direction: goods lower, chores higher). The definitions follow Section 2 of arXiv:2609.10493: two-way maximin share mu_i(2,S), and the factor is the min over ordered pairs i != j with mu_i(2, X_i u X_j) > 0 (dually for chores). The claim gives the exact optimal factor as a fraction, an allocation attaining it, and an exhaustive exact certificate checkable in laptop-hours. Bars are re-checked at claim time against the latest versions of arXiv:2609.08954 and 2609.10493 and any newer paper.

partial_wins.statement: A strictly positive additive goods instance with n = 3 and at most 8 goods that has no exact PMMS allocation (alpha* < 1). Gölz found none and believes 9 is minimal or nearly so; PMMS exists when m <= n + 2 (Amanatidis et al.).
An additive chores instance with exactly three agents and no exact PMMS allocation (rho* > 1), provided no published three-agent chores PMMS counterexample exists at claim time.

targets.verification_method: Independent exact checker: precompute mu_i(2,T) for every subset T by subset-sum reachability, enumerate all n^m complete allocations, and compute each allocation's factor with fractions.Fraction. Negative control: Gölz's instance (u1 = 1 3 4 5 8 14 16 18 23, u2 = 10 2 15 6 8 22 31 30 32, u3 = 14 2 22 13 15 27 42 38 48) must return exactly 78/79, attained at allocation (2,0,2,0,2,2,1,1,0). Bei et al.'s Table 2 instance must return 226/227. Re-fetch the status source before claiming.
angles: Bei et al.'s chores-to-goods reduction (their Lemma 1) preserves PMMS existence. A strong chores instance may transfer to goods with a computable factor.
Gölz's instances have three large goods plus small goods and a makeweight. Use them as seeds for local search with the exact factor as objective; 4-agent seeds include Aziz's instance.
pitfalls: For n = 2, PMMS coincides with MMS and always exists for additive goods (cut and choose). Use at least 3 agents.
Several conventions exist for pairs with mu = 0 and for empty bundles. Use the convention in Section 2 of arXiv:2609.10493 and state it.
Exact PMMS non-existence alone is already published; a new instance must beat the quantitative bar.

targets.name: Schwartz's conjecture: a tournament on at most 23 alternatives with two minimal TEQ-retentive sets (the smallest known has 24)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days for structured search; computing TEQ exactly with memoisation over dominator subsets takes about 0.1 s on Brandt-Seedig's 24-vertex tournament in plain Python
targets.statement: For a tournament T = (A, >), let D(x) be the set of alternatives that dominate x. A nonempty X subset of A is TEQ-retentive if TEQ(T[D(x)]) is contained in X for every x in X with D(x) nonempty. Schwartz (1990) defined the tournament equilibrium set TEQ recursively as the union of the inclusion-minimal TEQ-retentive sets, and conjectured that every tournament has exactly one minimal TEQ-retentive set. The conjecture is equivalent to TEQ being monotonic and satisfying independence of unchosen alternatives and the weak and strong superset properties. Brandt, Chudnovsky, Kim, Liu, Norin, Scott, Seymour and Thomassé (Soc. Choice Welf. 40, 2013) disproved it non-constructively, with about 10^136 alternatives. Brandt and Seedig (arXiv:1302.5592) gave an explicit 24-alternative tournament with two disjoint isomorphic minimal TEQ-retentive sets of order 12, and wrote 12 <= n_TEQ <= 23. Brandt, Fischer, Harrenstein and Mair (2010) had checked all tournaments up to order 12. Yang (arXiv:1611.03991) proved the conjecture for all tournaments of order <= 14, and posed Conjecture 1: a minimal TEQ-retentive set of size 3 is always the unique one. So the smallest counterexample has 15 to 24 alternatives. This lane's own checker reproduced the 24-vertex example.
targets.success_criterion: An explicit tournament (adjacency matrix) on n <= 23 alternatives together with two distinct inclusion-minimal TEQ-retentive sets X != Y, both recomputed by the verifier with an exact TEQ recursion. Direction: smaller n is better; any n <= 23 is a full win, because no counterexample on fewer than 24 alternatives is published and Yang (arXiv:1611.03991) proved there is none on 14 or fewer. Counterexamples to other TEQ-related statements (for example Brandt's weakening of the conjecture, which the 24-vertex example does not refute) are not this target unless they also exhibit two minimal TEQ-retentive sets on at most 23 alternatives.

partial_wins.statement: A tournament of any order with two minimal TEQ-retentive sets whose orders (|X|, |Y|) differ from (12, 12), a pair outside Yang's Figure 1 non-existence region and different from Brandt-Seedig's.
A counterexample to Yang's Conjecture 1: a tournament with a minimal TEQ-retentive set of size 3 that is not its unique minimal TEQ-retentive set.

targets.verification_method: Write an independent memoised recursion on vertex bitmasks: TEQ(S) = S if |S| = 1. Otherwise compute T_x = TEQ(D_S(x)) for each x in S. The least retentive superset C(x) of {x} is the closure under adding T_y for y already in the set. The minimal TEQ-retentive sets are the inclusion-minimal sets among the C(x), and TEQ(S) is their union. Check that the matrix is a tournament (exactly one arc per pair). Negative control: rebuild the Brandt-Seedig tournament (dominator lists in arXiv:1302.5592; X1 > Y2, X2 > Y1, Y1 > X1, Y2 > X2) and confirm the twelve TEQ(D(x_i)) sets printed there and exactly two minimal retentive sets. Also confirm uniqueness on random tournaments of order <= 12. Cross-check with a second, independently written implementation.
angles: The 24-vertex example joins two copies of a 12-vertex tournament with a block pattern. Search the same two-block construction with smaller or unequal blocks (sizes 7-11), keeping the cross pattern and searching the internal tournaments.
TEQ evaluation is cheap at these sizes, so a simulated-annealing search on arc flips with 'number of minimal retentive sets' and 'size of the second-best closure' as objectives is practical.
Yang's Figure 1 lists which (|H1|,|H2|) pairs are ruled out; use it to prune.
pitfalls: TEQ(empty set) and alternatives with no dominators (Condorcet winners) need explicit handling; a Condorcet winner makes the minimal retentive set unique.
Do not use a heuristic TEQ. The recursion must be exact on every dominator subtournament.
Yang proved there are no (T3, Tk)-retentive tournaments for k <= 12, so a p2 witness needs a second minimal set of size at least 13.

targets.name: Five voters: a tournament on at most 21 alternatives that no five voters can induce by majority (13 <= N(5) <= 22, Chindelevitch-Harutyunyan Question 1)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days per candidate (symmetry-broken SAT/cube-and-conquer over five linear orders of 21 alternatives); certificates are LRAT proofs
targets.statement: A tournament is k-inducible if k voters with linear orders produce it by pairwise majority. N(k) is the least number of alternatives on which some tournament is not k-inducible. McGarvey, Stearns and Erdős-Moser fix the asymptotics. N(3) = 8 (Shepardson-Tovey 2009; Eggermont, Hurkens and Woeginger 2013). Bachmeier et al. (2019) left the 23-vertex Paley tournament P23 undecided. Chindelevitch and Harutyunyan (arXiv:2607.26690, v2 22 Oct 2026) proved 12 <= N(5) <= 38. Their 'Tournaments not inducible by five voters' (arXiv:2609.13924, v2 22 Oct 2026) narrows this to 13 <= N(5) <= 22. The upper bound comes from nine 22-vertex obstructions: eight one-vertex deletions of doubly regular 23-vertex tournaments, plus one arc reversal. The lower bound comes from a census showing every 12-vertex tournament is 5-inducible. Four negative results come with machine-checked proofs (code at github.com/Leonardini/TournamentsBeyond5Voters). Of 4,108 21-vertex classes obtained by deleting two vertices of a doubly regular 23-vertex tournament, 2,916 are still undecided (Appendix G). Section 4.2 asks Question 1 (is N(5) = 22, i.e. is every 21-vertex tournament 5-inducible?). It also lists Conjecture 2 (P_q is not 5-inducible for every prime q >= 23 with q = 3 mod 4; P23, P31 and P43 are settled), Open problem 1 (P31 or P43 minus two vertices), Open problem 2 (a tournament 5-inducible but not with margin <= 3) and Conjecture 3 (k-inducible implies (k+2)-inducible with unit margin).
targets.success_criterion: An explicit tournament on n <= 21 vertices (adjacency matrix) with a certificate that it is NOT 5-inducible: an LRAT (or DRAT) refutation, checked by an independent checker, of a CNF that the verifier regenerates with their own encoder. The CNF encodes five linear orders (transitivity), with each arc u -> v carried by at least three of the five orders. This sets N(5) <= n < 22 (direction: lower is better) and answers Question 1 of arXiv:2609.13924 negatively. Cube-and-conquer is fine if the cube partition is itself checked to be exhaustive. A symmetry-breaking step must be justified (the paper's Theorem 2.1 style) and re-derived by the verifier.

partial_wins.statement: Open problem 2 of arXiv:2609.13924: a tournament that is 5-inducible, shown by five explicit orders, but not 5-inducible with margin <= 3 (every arc carried 3-2 or 4-1), certified by a checked refutation.
Open problem 1: decide whether P31 or P43 minus two vertices is 5-inducible, by an explicit witness or a checked refutation.

Conjecture 2 at a new prime: for a specific prime q with 47 <= q <= 103 and q = 3 mod 4, either a checked LRAT/DRAT refutation (of a CNF the verifier regenerates) showing P_q is not 5-inducible, or an explicit five-voter witness refuting the conjecture.

A counterexample to Conjecture 3 for some odd k: a tournament that is k-inducible (explicit witness) but not (k+2)-inducible with unit margin (checked refutation). For k = 3 it needs at least 13 vertices.

targets.verification_method: Positive claims (witnesses) take seconds: check that the orders are permutations, recompute every pairwise majority and margin, and compare with the tournament. Negative claims: regenerate the CNF independently, with order variables per voter and pair, transitivity clauses and a cardinality encoding of 'at least 3 of 5' per arc. Add only symmetry breaking the verifier can justify. Check the solver's LRAT with lrat-trim or cake_lpr. Negative controls: one of the paper's nine 22-vertex obstructions must give UNSAT with a checked proof; P19 must be SAT (5-inducible) but UNSAT at unit margin; random 12-vertex tournaments must be SAT.
angles: The authors searched only classes near doubly regular tournaments (their Appendix G). Low-predictability tournaments far from that family, such as quadratic-residue-like constructions on 21 vertices, circulants or products, are unexplored.
Use the paper's necessary condition: tournaments whose maximum acyclic subgraph fraction is below 3/5 are not 5-inducible with no search. Look for 21-vertex tournaments just above that threshold.
pitfalls: Unit-margin obstructions at n = 19 and 21 are known and do not move N(5); the full win needs plain majority.
Deleting vertices from the 22-vertex obstructions gives 5-inducible tournaments; the paper checked all of them.
A solver timeout or an unchecked UNSAT is not a certificate.

targets.name: Randomized metric distortion: certify a lower bound above Charikar-Ramakrishnan's 2.11264 (current window [2.11264, 2.13713])
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (LP over candidate distributions, with metrics found by column generation over consistent metrics); exact rational checking of a certificate takes seconds to minutes
targets.statement: In metric voting, voters and candidates lie in an unknown (pseudo)metric, and each voter ranks candidates by distance. A randomized rule sees only the rankings. Its distortion is the worst ratio of expected social cost (sum of voter-to-winner distances) to the optimal social cost, over all elections and all consistent metrics. Deterministic rules have optimal distortion 3 (Gkatzelis, Halpern and Shah 2020). For randomized rules, Charikar and Ramakrishnan ('Metric Distortion Bounds for Randomized Social Choice', SODA 2022, arXiv:2111.03694) and, independently, Pulyassary and Swamy (arXiv:2111.08698, 2021) disproved the conjectured value 2; Charikar and Ramakrishnan's (0,1,2,3)-metrics give the current bounds. Their Table 1 gives 2.02613 for m = 3 (tight), 2.04957 for m = 4, 2.06323 for m = 5, 2.07206 for 6, 2.07822 for 7, 2.08276 for 8, 2.08625 for 9, 2.08900 for 10, and 2.11264 as m tends to infinity. Their Conjecture 1 says these lower bounds are optimal. The upper bounds fell quickly in 2026: 2.753 (Charikar, Ramakrishnan, Wang and Wu, J. ACM 2024), then 5/2 (Frank arXiv:2608.17863, Ye arXiv:2608.21202), 2.1441 (Shah arXiv:2608.29308 v2), and 2.13713 (Cai, Charikar, Hastings, Ramakrishnan, Wang and Ye arXiv:2609.08259, 8 Sep 2026), which quotes 2.11264 as the lower bound. MathWorld's Metric Voting Distortion page reports no lower-bound improvement since 2022.
targets.success_criterion: A finite certificate: (i) an election with m candidates and voter types with positive rational weights and strict rankings; (ii) K explicit rational pseudometrics d_1..d_K on voters plus candidates. Each must satisfy symmetry, d(x,x) = 0, nonnegativity and every triangle inequality, and be consistent with the rankings (d(v,a) <= d(v,b) whenever v ranks a above b). (iii) Rational weights lambda_k >= 0 summing to 1 such that D = min over candidates c of sum_k lambda_k SC_k(c)/OPT_k, with OPT_k = min_c SC_k(c) > 0. Every randomized rule then has distortion >= D on this election. Full win: D >= 2.1127, strictly above Charikar-Ramakrishnan's limit 2.11264 (direction: higher). Any certificate with D > 2.13713 contradicts the published upper bound of arXiv:2609.08259 and must be treated as a checker bug until three independently written exact checkers agree. Re-check arXiv for newer lower bounds before claiming.

partial_wins.statement: For a fixed m in 4..10, a certificate with exactly m candidates and D >= (Table 1 value for that m) + 0.00001, refuting Charikar-Ramakrishnan's Conjecture 1 at that m. m = 3 is excluded because 2.02613 is proven tight.

targets.verification_method: Python with fractions.Fraction. Check that the weights are positive and the rankings are permutations. Check each metric: symmetric, zero diagonal, nonnegative, all O(N^3) triangle inequalities, and ranking consistency for every voter and candidate pair. Compute SC_k(c) and OPT_k exactly, check lambda, and compute D exactly. Compare with the bar using exact rationals. Negative control: rebuild CR's m = 3 construction from arXiv:2111.03694 (Appendix A or Section 4 with Table 1 parameters) and get a certificate close to 2.02613 from below, never above. By the weak-duality argument, no valid certificate for m = 3 may exceed 2.02613.
angles: CR restricted to (0,1,2,3)-metrics and a particular matrix structure; they note numerically that freeing more rows of M did not help within that family. Column generation over general biased metrics (their Proposition 4) is the natural next step.
Mine the worst-case elections of the new upper-bound analyses (stable lotteries, Integrated Veto mixtures): where their proofs are tight, a lower-bound election may hide.
pitfalls: Using different elections for different metrics is invalid: the certificate must fix one election, because the rule's output is fixed per election.
Floating-point LP optima are not certificates; rationalise lambda and recheck exactly.
Consistency uses each voter's own ranking; ties in distance are allowed but must not reverse a strict preference.

Family-specific lower bounds do not move the bar: Shah's v2 proves 2.136 only for rules in his random-size stable-lottery family, and Cai et al. give matching lower bounds only for stable k-lotteries. A win must bind every randomized rule, which the single-election certificate above does.

targets.name: Square-lattice site percolation threshold: settle the 5-sigma clash between Yang-Zhou's 0.5927460507896(1) and Jacobsen's 0.59274605079016(1) (2024)
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (exact transfer matrices with state counts growing like ~2.6-2.75^n; n >= 25 needs 100+ GB RAM big-memory nodes)
targets.statement: Site percolation on the square lattice has no exact threshold. Jesper Jacobsen (J. Phys. A 48 (2015) 454003, arXiv 1507.03027) located p_c from eigenvalue identities in the periodic Temperley-Lieb algebra on semi-infinite cylinders of circumference n <= 21 and quoted 0.59274605079210(2). Stephan Mertens (J. Phys. A 55 (2022) 334002, arXiv 2109.12102) computed the exact spanning probability R_n(p) of n x n squares up to n = 24 (complexity ~2.6^n) and got 0.592746050786(3). Yi Yang and Shuigeng Zhou (Comment, J. Phys. A 57 (2024) 258001) computed the exact critical probability h(n) of n x infinity helical lattices up to n = 24 (complexity O(n^2 c^n), c = 2.7459...). They found its extrapolation inconsistent with Jacobsen's value, extended exact cylinder critical points p_c(n) to n = 24, and concluded that the 2015 value is incorrect, giving 0.5927460507896(1). Jacobsen's Reply (J. Phys. A 57 (2024) 258002; full text paywalled) appears in the Wikipedia 'Percolation threshold' square-lattice row (maintained by Robert Ziff, last edited 2026-10-23) with 0.59274605079016(1). The two 2024 values differ by 5.6e-13 with stated errors of 1e-13 (Yang-Zhou) and 1e-14 (Reply), a gap of about 5.6 combined sigma, so at least one error bar is badly underestimated. Both lie within 1.5 sigma of Mertens's 3e-12-wide value. No later value is listed. Settling the 12th-13th digit needs larger exact cylinders, helices or squares (n = 25-28) or an independent extrapolation scheme with honest corrections to scaling.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an estimate of the square-lattice site threshold with stated one-sigma uncertainty at most 5e-14, so that the 5.6e-13 gap between the two 2024 values exceeds 10 of its sigma. The estimate must meet five conditions. (a) It is obtained with code written independently of Jacobsen's and Yang-Zhou's, from finite-size data at sizes that include at least one n beyond the largest published for that geometry (n >= 25 for cylinders, helices or squares). (b) Two different estimator families agree within their combined uncertainties, for example Jacobsen's two-sector eigenvalue identity on cylinders and Mertens/Yang-Zhou exact crossing or cylinder critical points. (c) The claim states its distance, in combined sigma, to both 0.5927460507896(1) and 0.59274605079016(1); no particular outcome is required. (d) All finite-size numbers are released to at least 25 digits with the extrapolation script. (e) A re-check of the live Wikipedia row and a literature search immediately before claiming show no third published determination (beyond the 2015 and 2024 values above) with uncertainty at most 5e-14. Direction: a decisive independent value at uncertainty <= 5e-14.

partial_wins.statement: Exact spanning polynomial R_n(p) of the n x n square (Mertens's definition) for n = 25 or larger, as integer coefficients, with the same code reproducing Mertens's published n <= 24 data (or its root crossings) exactly.

Jacobsen-type two-sector eigenvalue-identity estimates p_c(n) for site percolation on cylinders of circumference n beyond the largest n published by Jacobsen (2015 paper or 2024 Reply), to at least 25 digits, with the code reproducing his published n <= 21 values.
Exact cylinder critical points p_c(n) or helical h(n) in Yang-Zhou's sense for some n >= 25, to at least 25 digits, reproducing their n <= 24 values where published.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic (< 1 hour for checks, not the search): rerun the claimant's code at small n (n <= 12) and compare with published R_n(p) and p_c(n) values exactly; recompute one large-n eigenvalue identity or polynomial root with an independent multiprecision solver; rerun the extrapolation on the released data and refit with one correction term fewer; confirm the stated sigma and the distance to both 2024 values.
angles: Mertens's R_n(p) algorithm is O(2.6^n) in time and memory; frontier-compression tricks from Jensen's SAW/polygon codes and modular arithmetic with CRT reconstruction can push n by 2-4.

Use the exact cylinder p_c(n) sequence with the known correction exponents for 2D percolation (leading irrelevant exponent and analytic terms) rather than free power laws; the clash is probably about which corrections are included.
Cross-check the method on bond percolation on the kagome lattice, where Scullard and Jacobsen give 0.52440499916744820(1), before trusting it on the square site problem.
pitfalls: The Reply's full text is behind a paywall (IOP); quote its value from the Wikipedia row or a legitimate copy, and do not assume what its argument says.
Error bars from the spread of the last few extrapolants are the classic false precision; both 2024 values cannot be right as stated.
Spanning (open boundaries), wrapping (torus) and cylinder quantities converge at different rates and from different sides; do not mix them in one fit without the right correction terms.
Double precision is useless here; work in exact rationals or >= 40-digit arithmetic.

targets.name: Twin-lattice percolation: are the hcp and fcc bond thresholds equal (both 0.120164 within 1e-6), and how far apart are ice Ih and diamond?
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days for the partials (3D Newman-Ziff or wrapping-probability Monte Carlo on L up to 128-256; ice-Ih p1 is laptop-hours); needs cluster (or a GPU union-find code for weeks) for the full Delta win, which needs each threshold to <= 6e-8, beyond Xu et al.'s L <= 128, ~1e8-sample fcc runs
targets.statement: The hcp and fcc lattices, and ice Ih vs diamond (hexagonal vs cubic diamond), differ only in layer stacking, so their percolation thresholds agree to many digits. Robert Ziff's Wikipedia 'Percolation threshold' page (3D table, last edited 2026-10-23) asks this explicitly. Are the hcp and fcc bond thresholds identical? If not, how far apart are they and which is bigger? The same question is asked for ice and diamond, citing M. F. Sykes, J. J. Rehr and Maureen Glen, 'A note on the percolation probabilities of pairs of closely similar lattices'. Current values: hcp bond 0.1201640(10) and site 0.1992555(10) (Christian Lorenz, Raechelle May and Robert Ziff, J. Stat. Phys. 98 (2000) 961, arXiv cond-mat/9908034). They found the site thresholds different but the bond thresholds equal within errors. fcc bond 0.12016377(15) and site 0.19923517(20) (Xiao Xu, Junfeng Wang, Jian-Ping Lv and Youjin Deng, Front. Phys. 9 (2014) 113, arXiv 1310.5399, Table V). Diamond bond 0.3895892(5) and site 0.4299870(4) (same paper). Ice Ih still carries only the 1961 values 0.433(11) site (Frisch et al.) and 0.388(10) bond (Vyssotsky et al.). So the fcc-hcp bond difference, 2.3e-7 +- 1.0e-6, is consistent with zero at the 1e-6 level and its sign is unknown, and ice Ih has no modern threshold at all.
targets.success_criterion: Success means either (A) or (B). (A) A determination of Delta = p_c^bond(hcp) - p_c^bond(fcc) with one-sigma uncertainty at most 3e-8, from simulations of both lattices with the same code, estimator and fit form, with each individual threshold to uncertainty <= 6e-8. The fcc value must be within 3 sigma of Xu et al.'s 0.12016377(15), or the discrepancy must be analysed and shown by both estimators. (B) The same for the ice-Ih / diamond pair, with Delta uncertainty at most 1e-7 for bond or site and the diamond value within 3 sigma of Xu et al. (or the discrepancy analysed). In both cases a second estimator (for example two different wrapping probabilities, or wrapping plus cluster-size ratios) must give a consistent Delta, raw data and code are released, and a literature check immediately before claiming finds no published Delta of that precision. Direction: smaller uncertainty on the difference; a nonzero Delta at >= 5 sigma and a null result at the stated precision both count.

partial_wins.statement: First modern ice-Ih (hexagonal diamond, z = 4) site and bond thresholds, each with one-sigma uncertainty <= 2e-6, with the same code reproducing Xu et al.'s diamond site 0.4299870(4) and bond 0.3895892(5) within 3 sigma, and a literature search immediately before claiming finding no published ice-Ih value with uncertainty <= 2e-6.
hcp site and bond thresholds each with uncertainty <= 3e-7 (more than 3 times better than Lorenz-May-Ziff), with the same code reproducing the fcc values of Xu et al. within 3 sigma.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic (< 1 hour): build both lattices from their stacking sequences and check coordination 12 (hcp, fcc) or 4 (ice Ih, diamond) and the site counts per periodic cell; rerun short simulations at two sizes with fresh seeds and check consistency with the released data; refit Delta from the released wrapping probabilities with and without the leading correction term; confirm the reproduction tests.
angles: Correlated sampling: run hcp and fcc with the same random numbers on bonds that map to each other layer by layer, so most noise cancels in Delta; this is the whole trick for a difference far below the individual errors.

Series view: Sykes-Rehr-Glen and Lorenz-May-Ziff note the low-density series of the twins first differ at high order; an exact enumeration of where they first differ gives the sign expectation to test.

Periodic cells: hcp needs an even number of layers and ice Ih needs cells compatible with its hexagonal stacking; use tori whose wrapping probabilities have the same universal limit as for the cubic twins, or compare at matched aspect ratio.
pitfalls: Wikipedia lists a third fcc bond value, 0.120169(2) (Hu and Charbonneau 2021, invasion percolation), 2.6 sigma from Xu et al.; use matched-method comparisons, not mixed literature values, for Delta.

Wrapping probabilities on tori of different shape (hexagonal vs cubic cells) have different universal limits; the threshold is found from size crossings, not from a universal-value equation, unless the cell shapes match.
The fcc-hcp difference may be far below 1e-8; a null result is a legitimate full win under (A) only at the stated precision.

targets.name: Simple cubic, bcc, fcc and diamond percolation thresholds: beat the Xu-Wang-Lv-Deng (2014) precision, e.g. sc site 0.31160768(15), sc bond 0.24881185(10)
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (or laptop-days with a GPU union-find code); L up to 1024 and 1e8+ samples per size
targets.statement: The basic 3D thresholds are known only numerically. Best values (Xiao Xu, Junfeng Wang, Jian-Ping Lv and Youjin Deng, Front. Phys. 9 (2014) 113, arXiv 1310.5399, Table V, from simultaneous fits of wrapping probabilities sharing universal parameters): simple cubic bond 0.24881185(10) and site 0.31160768(15); bcc bond 0.18028762(20) and site 0.2459615(2); fcc bond 0.12016377(15) and site 0.19923517(20); diamond bond 0.3895892(5) and site 0.4299870(4). The simple cubic values rest on Junfeng Wang, Zongzheng Zhou, Wei Zhang, Timothy Garoni and Youjin Deng (Phys. Rev. E 87 (2013) 052107, arXiv 1302.0421; sc bond 0.24881182(10), site 0.3116077(2), L <= 512). The Wikipedia 'Percolation threshold' 3D table (edited 2026-10-23 by Robert Ziff) lists no later improvement for these lattices; for bcc it still shows Lorenz-Ziff 1998 values 0.2459615(10) and 0.1802875(10), and for fcc bond it adds Hu-Charbonneau 2021 0.120169(2), which sits 2.6 sigma from Xu et al. In 4D and above Mertens and Moore (2018) reached 1e-8 to 1e-11, so 3D is now the least precise of the hypercubic family.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a threshold for at least one of the eight (lattice, site/bond) pairs above with stated one-sigma uncertainty at most one third of the Xu et al. 2014 Table V uncertainty for that pair (for example <= 5e-8 for sc site, <= 3e-8 for sc bond), such that (a) two estimators (for example two wrapping probabilities, or wrapping probability and a cluster-size ratio) agree within 3 combined sigma, (b) the value is within 3 sigma of Xu et al. or the discrepancy is analysed, (c) the fit includes at least two correction-to-scaling terms and is stable when the smallest sizes are dropped, (d) raw per-size data and code are released, and (e) a literature search immediately before claiming finds no published value for that pair with smaller uncertainty. Direction: smaller uncertainty.

partial_wins.statement: Independent reproduction, with own code, of all eight Xu et al. Table V thresholds to uncertainty <= 3 times theirs and agreement within 3 sigma, with released data; reproduction only.
One of the eight pairs with uncertainty at most one half of Xu et al.'s, under the same rules (a)-(e).

targets.verification_method: Skeptic (< 1 hour): rerun the claimant's code at two small sizes with fresh seeds and compare wrapping probabilities with the released data; refit the released data with the claimant's and one alternative correction ansatz; check the reproduction of the Wang et al. 2013 sc values at L <= 128.
angles: Simultaneous fits across lattices sharing the universal wrapping limits and y_t = 1/nu (Xu et al.'s trick) gain a factor of 2-3; feeding in nu from the most precise percolation exponent studies gains more.
GPU union-find with path compression (or Hoshen-Kopelman on slabs) makes L = 1024-2048 sweeps cheap; microcanonical Newman-Ziff gives all p at once.
pitfalls: Several Xu et al. Table V values (sc bond 0.24881185(10), bcc site 0.2459615(2) and bond 0.18028762(20), fcc bond 0.12016377(15)) are not in the Wikipedia rows; compare against Table V of arXiv 1310.5399, not only the wiki row.
Correlated estimators from the same samples are not independent methods; their agreement does not validate the error bar.
Random-number quality matters at this precision; use a modern generator and report it.

targets.name: Percolation thresholds still at 3-4 digits: stacked 2D lattices, van der Marck duals, d-dimensional bcc/diamond (d = 4-6) and extended neighbourhoods in Wikipedia's 3D and higher-d tables
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours per lattice (Newman-Ziff on 3D-6D tori)
targets.statement: Robert Ziff's Wikipedia 'Percolation threshold' page (checked 2026-10-30, last edited 2026-10-23) still lists many periodic lattices with only 3-4 significant digits. Most come from Steven C. van der Marck's 1997-98 studies (Phys. Rev. E 55 (1997) 1514 and 6593; Int. J. Mod. Phys. C 9 (1998) 529; J. Phys. A 31 (1998) 3449) and from Krzysztof Malarz's extended-neighbourhood work (with Kurzawski 2012; Phys. Rev. E 91 (2015) 043301). 3D table examples: kagome stack site 0.3346(4) and bond 0.2563(2), honeycomb stack 0.3701(2)/0.3093(2), dice stack 0.2998(4)/0.2378(4), bow-tie stack 0.2822(6)/0.2092(4), octagonal (union-jack) stack 0.2524(6)/0.1752(2), pentagonal stack 0.3394(4)/0.2793(4), bow-tie stack dual 0.3480(4)/0.2853(4), octagonal stack dual 0.3840(4)/0.3168(4), fcc dual 0.3341(5)/0.2703(3), hcp dual 0.3101(5)/0.2573(3), bcc dual 0.4560(6)/0.4031(6), diamond dual 0.3904(5)/0.2350(5) and 3D kagome bond 0.2709(6). Also site columns for sc neighbourhoods such as NN+3NN 0.1420(1), 2NN+3NN 0.1036(1), NN+2NN+4NN 0.11440(12), NN+3NN+4NN 0.11920(12) and 2NN+3NN+4NN 0.11330(12). Higher-d table: 4D diamond 0.2978(2)/0.2715(3), 4D kagome bond 0.177(1), 4D bcc site 0.1037(3), 4D hypercubic 3NN, NN+3NN and 2NN+3NN site 0.04540(23), 0.04000(23), 0.03310(23), 5D diamond 0.2252(3)/0.2084(4), 5D bcc 0.0446(4)/0.033(1), 5D kagome bond 0.130(2), 6D diamond 0.1799(5)/0.1677(7) and 6D bcc site 0.0199(5). Zhipeng Xun, Robert Ziff and co-authors (2020-22) redid the bond columns of the neighbourhood rows and some site cells to 7 digits. Where they overlap, Malarz's 2015 4NN site values disagree strongly with equivalent lattices (sc-2NN+4NN = fcc NN+2NN, 0.1361408(8) vs 0.15950(12); sc-3NN+4NN = bcc NN+2NN, 0.1759432(8) vs 0.20490(12); sc-1..4, 0.0801171(9) vs 0.10000(12)), so his remaining 4NN cells are suspect.
targets.success_criterion: Success means, for at least one cell of the live Wikipedia 3D or 'other higher-dimensional lattices' table whose best listed value has uncertainty >= 1e-4 (re-fetched immediately before claiming), a threshold with stated one-sigma uncertainty at most 1e-6. Five conditions apply. (a) Two estimators agree within 3 combined sigma, for example two wrapping probabilities with finite-size fits, or wrapping plus a cluster-size ratio. (b) The value is within 3 sigma of the listed one, or the discrepancy is explained. (c) The same code reproduces the simple cubic site 0.31160768(15) and bond 0.24881185(10) (Xu et al. 2014) to at least 6 digits. (d) The lattice is defined explicitly (basis, neighbour vectors) and matches the table's z and the cited paper's construction. (e) A literature search finds no published value below 1e-6 for that lattice or any lattice equivalent to it. Three kinds of cell are excluded: cells fixed by an exact identity (3D and d-dimensional kagome site = diamond bond), cells equivalent to a lattice already known to 1e-6 (sc-2NN+4NN = fcc NN+2NN; sc-3NN+4NN = bcc NN+2NN; sc-3NN = bcc), and the ice Ih row, which is covered by the separate hcp-fcc / ice-diamond twins entry. Direction: smaller uncertainty.

partial_wins.statement: Five or more such cells, each to uncertainty <= 1e-6 under the same rules, published as one table with code.
A cell improved to uncertainty <= 1e-5 (10 times or more better than listed) under rules (a)-(e), for a lattice whose construction is fully specified.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic (< 1 hour): rebuild the lattice from the stated basis and neighbour list and check z and site counts against the table; rerun the claimant's simulation at two sizes with fresh seeds; refit the released data; check the sc reproduction.
angles: Stacked lattices are a 2D Archimedean or Laves lattice times Z with vertical bonds; build them from the 2D tilings already used for the 2-uniform entry.
For the high-d bcc and diamond rows, Mertens-Moore's hypercubic code (wrapping on hypertori, L up to 64 in 4D) is the template.
pitfalls: 'Dual' here means van der Marck's construction in PRE 55, 6593; a different dual gives a different, wrong lattice. Check z-bar.

Some cells (e.g. sc NN+4NN site) already have a 7-digit value in the same row; only the best value in a cell counts, and a lattice equivalent to another row (sublattice decompositions of extended sc neighbourhoods) inherits that row's value.

Malarz 2015's sc 4NN site values (0.11440, 0.11920, 0.11330, 0.15950, 0.20490, 0.10000, all (12)) disagree by 15-25% with equivalent-lattice values where checkable; expect discrepancies on the remaining 4NN cells, check your neighbour shells against the equivalences first, and explain any discrepancy under rule (b).
This is the 3D/high-d analogue of the 2-uniform entry; one cell is one partial harvest, not a separate target.

targets.name: Continuum percolation of overlapping hyperspheres in d = 6-11: beat the Torquato-Jiao (2012) thresholds, still the most precise published values
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (union-find on cell lists in d-dimensional tori; memory, not CPU, limits d >= 9)
targets.statement: For the Poisson Boolean model of equal overlapping hyperspheres, the critical reduced density eta_c (expected number of sphere centres per sphere volume) has no closed form. In d = 3 the best values are Christian Lorenz and Robert Ziff's 0.341889(3) (J. Chem. Phys. 2001) and Piotr Brzeski and Grzegorz Kondrat's critical volume fraction 0.2895693(26), i.e. eta about 0.341884 (J. Stat. Mech. 2022, 053202), with an outlier 0.341935(8) (Gori-Trombettoni 2015). Brzeski and Kondrat also improved d = 4 and 5 by factors of about 230 and 10. For d = 6..11 the Wikipedia 'Percolation threshold' page (higher-dimension continuum table, checked 2026-10-30) lists only Salvatore Torquato and Yang Jiao (J. Chem. Phys. 137 (2012) 074106, arXiv 1208.3720, rescaled-particle method): eta_c = 0.02339(5) (d = 6), 0.01051(3) (7), 0.004904(6) (8), 0.002353(4) (9), 0.001138(3) (10), 0.0005530(3) (11), plus older Dall-Christensen values for d <= 8. These are 3-4 digit numbers from a single method, while hypercubic lattice thresholds in the same dimensions are known to 8-11 digits (Mertens-Moore 2018).
targets.success_criterion: Success means, for at least one d in 6..11, a value of eta_c for overlapping equal hyperspheres with stated one-sigma uncertainty at most one tenth of Torquato-Jiao's (d = 6: 5e-6; 7: 3e-6; 8: 6e-7; 9: 4e-7; 10: 3e-7; 11: 3e-8), such that (a) two estimators or methods agree within 3 combined sigma (for example wrapping-probability crossings on hypertori, and spanning or largest-cluster scaling, or a discrete-to-continuum extrapolation in the Brzeski-Kondrat manner), (b) the same code reproduces eta_c(3) = 0.34189 to within 1e-5, (c) data and code are released, and (d) a literature search immediately before claiming finds no published value for that d with smaller uncertainty. Agreement with Torquato-Jiao is not required, but a discrepancy above 3 sigma must be reported. Direction: smaller uncertainty.

partial_wins.statement: d = 3: eta_c with uncertainty <= 1e-6 under rules (a), (c) and (d), better than both Lorenz-Ziff and Brzeski-Kondrat, and resolving the 0.341889 vs 0.341935 disagreement.
Any d in 6..11 with uncertainty at most one third of Torquato-Jiao's, same rules.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic (< 1 hour): rerun the claimant's code at two system sizes in the claimed d with fresh seeds; check the overlap test (distance < diameter) and periodic wrapping in a toy configuration; refit the released crossing data; confirm the d = 3 reproduction.
angles: In high d, nearly all overlaps are between pairs; tree-like expansions (Torquato-Jiao's lower bound) give a control variate for the Monte Carlo.
Cell lists in d >= 8 waste memory; use a k-d tree or random-shift hashing on coordinates.
pitfalls: The Wikipedia 4D/5D Brzeski-Kondrat numbers sit in the eta column but look like volume fractions; read the paper before comparing.
eta_c, phi_c = 1 - exp(-eta_c) and the mean number of overlaps 2^d eta_c are different quantities; state which one is measured.
Finite-size corrections in high d are large because the torus side is only a few diameters at feasible N; report the side length in diameters.

targets.name: Penetrable disks in the plane: settle the 3-sigma clash between Mertens-Moore's eta_c = 1.12808737(6) and the critical-polynomial 1.12808706(8)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (microcanonical union-find on tori with 1e8-1e9 disks)
targets.statement: The critical filling factor eta_c of equal fully penetrable disks (2D Poisson Boolean model; critical density n_c = 4 eta_c / pi) is a benchmark of continuum percolation. Stephan Mertens and Cristopher Moore (Phys. Rev. E 86 (2012) 061109, arXiv 1209.4936) used wrapping probabilities with the exactly known universal torus values and found eta_c = 1.12808737(6), n_c = 1.43632545(8). Wenhui Xu, Junfeng Wang, Hao Hu and Youjin Deng (Phys. Rev. E 103 (2021) 022127, arXiv 2010.02887) used critical polynomials and found n_c = 1.43632505(10) (eta_c = 1.12808706(8)), which they describe as slightly below Mertens-Moore's. Zbigniew Koza, Piotr Brzeski and Grzegorz Kondrat (J. Phys. A 56 (2023) 165001, three-leg cluster method) found 1.1280867(5), closer to the critical-polynomial value but too coarse to decide. The gap, about 3.1e-7 in eta, is about 3 combined sigma; Wikipedia's 2D continuum table (checked 2026-10-30) lists no resolution.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an estimate of eta_c for equal fully penetrable disks with stated one-sigma uncertainty at most 2e-8 (3 times smaller than Mertens-Moore's), such that (a) two methods agree within their combined uncertainties (for example wrapping probabilities on tori with and without the universal-value constraint, critical polynomials on growing bases, or the three-leg method), (b) the claim states its distance, in combined sigma, to both 1.12808737(6) and 1.12808706(8) (no particular outcome is required), (c) finite-size data, fits and code are released, and (d) a literature search immediately before claiming finds no published value with uncertainty below 2e-8. Direction: smaller uncertainty.

partial_wins.statement: An independent eta_c with uncertainty <= 6e-8 (matching Mertens-Moore's) from a method different from both wrapping-with-universal-value and critical polynomials (for example crossing-only wrapping fits or the three-leg method), under rules (c) and (d), stating its distance to both values.

Using one of the two published methods on the claimant's own released data, reproduce that method's published estimate within its stated error. Then show that including one specific, named systematic effect (a neglected correction term, aspect-ratio effect or base-size trend) shifts the estimate by at least 2e-7 in eta, with the shift stable under dropping the smallest sizes.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic (< 1 hour): rerun the claimant's simulation at two system sizes with fresh seeds; check the universal wrapping values used against the exact torus formulas; refit the released data with an extra correction term and with the correction exponent left free; if critical polynomials are used, re-estimate P_B at two densities from the released samples and refit its zero crossing.
angles: Mertens-Moore fix the threshold from the universal wrapping value; repeating it with a crossing-only fit (no universal input) separates a universal-value bias from statistics.

Xu et al. simulate the continuum disks directly (tori of side L = 3 to 128, disk diameter 1), assume P_B = 0 at criticality as on planar lattices, and fit with yt = 3/4 and the correction exponent fixed at -2. Freeing the correction exponent, or measuring P_B at the Mertens-Moore density on large L, tests whether the bias sits in that ansatz.
pitfalls: eta_c vs n_c vs phi_c = 1 - exp(-eta_c): convert consistently before comparing (n_c = 4 eta_c / pi for unit-radius disks).
Wikipedia's row also lists several 2019-21 powder-technology values with no error bars; they do not count as comparators.

targets.name: Directed percolation on the square lattice: more digits of p_c than Jensen's series values 0.644700185(5) (bond) and 0.70548522(4) (site)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (Jensen-type transfer-matrix series; memory-bound, each doubling of RAM adds terms)
targets.statement: Directed percolation in 1+1 dimensions has no exact threshold (it is not conformally invariant). The record values are still Iwan Jensen's low-density series results (J. Phys. A 32 (1999) 5233, doi 10.1088/0305-4470/32/28/304, arXiv cond-mat/9906036). With a new transfer-matrix algorithm he extended the bond series to order 171 and the site series to order 158 using about 5.5 GB, and estimated p_c(bond) = 0.644700185(5) and p_c(site) = 0.70548522(4); an earlier analysis in the same paper gave 0.70548515(20). Monte Carlo values are less precise: Wikipedia lists 0.6447001(2) and 0.7054852(3) from Junfeng Wang, Zongzheng Zhou, Qingquan Liu, Timothy Garoni and Youjin Deng (Phys. Rev. E 88 (2013) 042102, arXiv 1201.3006). The Wikipedia 'Percolation threshold' directed-percolation table (checked 2026-10-30) lists nothing more precise for the (1+1)-d square lattice. Jensen's algorithm has a growth factor below 2^(1/8), so each doubling of memory adds about 8 terms; a machine with 100 times his memory should add about 50 terms. The same applies to the triangular, honeycomb and kagome cases of his 2004 paper.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an estimate of the directed square-lattice threshold with stated uncertainty at most 1e-9 for bond (5 times smaller than 5e-9) or at most 1e-8 for site (4 times smaller than 4e-8), such that (a) it comes from exact series longer than Jensen's (bond > 171 or site > 158 terms) or from an independent method, (b) the series coefficients are released as exact integers and the first 100 agree exactly with an independent recomputation (and with Jensen's where available), (c) at least two series (for example mean cluster size and moments of the cluster length) analysed with differential approximants give consistent p_c, (d) the value agrees with Jensen's within 3 combined sigma or the discrepancy is analysed, and (e) a literature search before claiming finds no better published value. Direction: smaller uncertainty.

partial_wins.statement: Exact low-density series for bond directed percolation on the square lattice to at least 190 terms (or site to at least 175), released as exact integers, with the first 100 terms independently recomputed by a second program.
An independent Monte Carlo or transfer-matrix estimate of p_c(bond) with uncertainty <= 2e-8, ten times better than Wang et al. 2013 and consistent with Jensen within 3 sigma.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic (< 1 hour): recompute the first 40-60 series terms with a simple brute-force or row-transfer program and compare exactly; rerun the claimant's differential-approximant analysis on the released series and vary the approximant orders; check the stated uncertainty against the spread.
angles: Jensen computed modulo primes and reconstructed by CRT; the same trick plus 64-bit hashing of boundary states and disk-backed sorting now fits much longer series.
Biased differential approximants with the DP exponents fixed from the best Monte Carlo (beta, nu_par, nu_perp) sharpen p_c from the same series.
pitfalls: Jensen's university series page returns 403 today; do not use mirrors of uncertain provenance, recompute instead.
Series analysis error bars are judgement calls; require the spread over many approximant orders, not the best few.
Site vs bond and diagonal vs nearest-neighbour conventions differ between papers; the table row is the (1+1)-d square lattice, diagonal.

targets.name: MOONSHOT - Percolation threshold of Z^d in powers of 1/(2d-1): the first coefficient beyond Mertens-Moore's 119077/96 (site) and 4855/12 (bond)
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (classical route: Mertens-Moore Table 9 puts the missing bond enumerations at 9 years for (d, e) = (6, 14) up to 133,800 years for (11, 14) on 368 cores, so a full win needs new closed formulas; the Pade route for p1 is months to years)
targets.statement: With sigma = 2d - 1, the percolation thresholds of the d-dimensional hypercubic lattice have asymptotic expansions p_c^site = 1/sigma + (3/2)sigma^-2 + (15/4)sigma^-3 + (83/4)sigma^-4 + (6577/48)sigma^-5 + (119077/96)sigma^-6 + O(sigma^-7) and p_c^bond = 1/sigma + (5/2)sigma^-3 + (15/2)sigma^-4 + 57 sigma^-5 + (4855/12)sigma^-6 + O(sigma^-7). The first terms are from David Gaunt, Michael Sykes and Heather Ruskin (J. Phys. A 9 (1976) 1899; Gaunt-Ruskin J. Phys. A 11 (1978) 1369). Stephan Mertens and Cristopher Moore (J. Phys. A 51 (2018) 475001, arXiv 1805.02701) added terms after about 40 years. Enumerating proper lattice animals with perimeter and vertex counts on a 368-core cluster, and proving formulas for the top binomial coefficients of bond perimeter polynomials (Theorems 4-6), they obtained 6577/48 and 4855/12 by the classical procedure. Each came from fitting the minimum number of points (for 4855/12 a quadratic in r through r = 10, 11, 12), checked by the cancellation of higher powers of r in ln b_r. The site term 119077/96 comes from their observation that (l-1,1) Pade approximants of the mean-cluster-size series stabilise one coefficient per two terms. Their Theorem 7 shows that this stabilisation is equivalent to the classical one (coefficients of ln b_r linear in r for r >= 2j), so neither route is a proof; the classical route needs more data and so carries more internal checks. For the next bond term the classical route needs b_r for r = 12..15, and their Table 9 estimates the missing enumerations at (d, e) = (6, 14) about 9 years, (7, 14) 116 years and (11, 14) about 133,800 years. The Pade route needs only b_13: about 57 days at (7, 12), 387 days at (8, 12) and 4.5 years at (9, 12). One more site coefficient b_13, which they put at months on a small cluster, would conjecturally give the sigma^-7 site term. The Wikipedia 'Percolation threshold' page (checked 2026-10-30) still shows both series ending at sigma^-6.
targets.success_criterion: Success means the exact rational coefficient of sigma^-7 in p_c^site(d) or p_c^bond(d), obtained by the classical Gaunt-Sykes-Ruskin procedure as Mertens-Moore used it for 4855/12, and not from the Pade stabilisation alone. That procedure uses exact perimeter polynomials as functions of d (from enumeration or from proven closed formulas) and fits the sigma^-k coefficients of b_r / sigma^r as polynomials in r through at least the minimum number of points, with the higher powers of r cancelling in ln b_r as the consistency check. Four conditions apply. (a) All enumeration data are released and reproducible by an independent program on at least the smaller (d, size) cases. (b) The same pipeline reproduces every known coefficient obtained classically (site through sigma^-5, bond through sigma^-6). (c) The new series agrees with Mertens-Moore's numerical thresholds for d = 10..13 better than the old series does. (d) A literature check before claiming shows no published sigma^-7 coefficient. Direction: one more exact term.

partial_wins.statement: The coefficient b_13 of the site (or bond) mean-cluster-size series in Mertens-Moore's sense, as an exact polynomial in d, with the resulting Pade-stabilised (conjectural) sigma^-7 coefficient, both reproducible by a second program.

A proven closed formula for the next coefficient family of the bond perimeter polynomial D_e (the binom(d, e-3) coefficient, extending Mertens-Moore's Theorems 4-6 for binom(d, e), binom(d, e-1), binom(d, e-2)), or the analogous site formula with perimeter. It must remove one of the enumeration tasks in their Table 9 and be checked by computer against brute-force counts for small e and d.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic: recompute the claimed animal counts with perimeter data for small (d, e) by brute force and match exactly; rerun the series derivation script from the released data to reproduce all known coefficients and the new one; compare the extended series with the numerical thresholds for d = 10..13 on the Wikipedia hypercubic table.
angles: Exploit that only the dependence on d up to fixed degree matters: count animals as polynomials in d via their 'dimension-reduced' shapes (animals spanning k dimensions times binomial(d, k)), which is how the top coefficients were proven.
Lace-expansion work (Hara-Slade) gives rigorous 1/d expansions to low order; matching to it is a check on any new term.
pitfalls: Pade stabilisation is an observed pattern, not a proof; it gives p1, not the full win.
Lattice-animal counts alone (OEIS A151830-type sequences, a separate bank entry) do not suffice; perimeter and vertex counts are needed.

targets.name: Random sequential adsorption on the square lattice: more digits of the NN-exclusion jamming coverage 0.3641323(1), and the dimer value (0.906820 vs 0.906823)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (exact time-series expansions by depth-first enumeration, plus event-driven Monte Carlo)
targets.statement: In random sequential adsorption (RSA) particles land irreversibly at random and stick if allowed, until a jammed state. With nearest-neighbour exclusion on the square lattice (equivalently the density of a random greedy maximal independent set of Z^2), the jamming coverage has no closed form, unlike Flory's 1D result. Chee Kwan Gan and Jian-Sheng Wang (J. Chem. Phys. 108 (1998) 3010, doi 10.1063/1.475687, arXiv cond-mat/9710340) computed exact time-series coefficients: 21 terms for NN-exclusion and 18 for dimers on the square lattice, 24 and 22 on the honeycomb lattice. Their depth-first algorithm ran in under 60 MB per machine, up to 120 hours each; the older algorithm needed 706 MB already at order 14. Pade analysis gave 0.3641323(1) (square NN-exclusion), 0.37913944(1) (honeycomb NN-exclusion) and 0.906823(2) for dimers on the square lattice. For dimers this compares with the Monte Carlo 0.906820(2) of Jian-Sheng Wang and Ras Pandey (PRL 77 (1996) 1773) and a biased earlier estimate 0.9068088(4). Asher Baram and Marshall Fixman gave 0.3641330(5) (J. Chem. Phys. 103 (1995) 1929). The Wikipedia 'Random sequential adsorption' tables (checked 2026-10-30) list nothing more precise. The 1998 series were limited by 1998 compute; today's multicore machines allow many more exact terms.
targets.success_criterion: Success means either (A) the square-lattice NN-exclusion jamming coverage with stated uncertainty at most 2e-8 (5 times smaller than Gan-Wang's 1e-7), or (B) the square-lattice dimer jamming coverage with uncertainty at most 5e-7, such that (a) two methods agree within combined uncertainty (exact series longer than Gan-Wang's analysed with Pade or differential approximants, and event-driven Monte Carlo on large tori with finite-size checks), (b) the series coefficients are released as exact integers and reproduce all Gan-Wang Table I coefficients exactly, (c) for (B) the claim states its distance in combined sigma to both 0.906820(2) and 0.906823(2), and (d) a literature search before claiming (physics and probability literature on random greedy independent sets) finds no better published value. Direction: smaller uncertainty.

partial_wins.statement: Exact series for the vacancy probability of NN-exclusion RSA on the square lattice beyond order 21 (at least 26 terms), reproducing Gan-Wang's 21 coefficients exactly, checked by a second program.
Exact series for dimer RSA on the square lattice beyond order 18 (at least 23 terms), reproducing Gan-Wang's coefficients exactly.
A Monte Carlo jamming coverage for NN-exclusion RSA on the square lattice with uncertainty <= 5e-8 and an explicit finite-size study, consistent or inconsistent with 0.3641323(1) at 3 sigma.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic (< 1 hour): recompute the first 10-12 series coefficients by brute-force enumeration of local histories and compare exactly with the released list; rerun the approximant analysis; rerun the Monte Carlo at two sizes with fresh seeds.
angles: NN-exclusion RSA jamming is a local function of i.i.d. arrival times (a site is occupied iff no earlier-arriving neighbour is occupied), so the coverage is an exact integral over decreasing paths; this gives an independent expansion and a fast Monte Carlo with no time stepping.
Modular arithmetic and memoised local configurations (Gan-Wang's depth-first tree) parallelise well across cores.
pitfalls: The Wikipedia RSA page has had no content edits since 2023; probability papers on greedy independent sets of Z^2 may hold newer numbers not listed there. Search them before claiming.
Series are in t, in y = 1 - e^-t or in u = e^-t - 1 depending on the paper; convert before comparing coefficients.
Continuum RSA of disks (0.547...) is a different problem and not covered here.

targets.name: New compact-binary merger candidate in public O4a/O4b LIGO-Virgo strain that GWTC-4.1, GWTC-5.0 and the community catalogs do not list
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days for one month of data to needs cluster for a whole run (H1+L1 4 kHz strain is roughly 100 GB per month, our estimate from 4096-s HDF5 files; a broad BBH template bank over all of O4a and O4b is cluster-scale; re-ranking the released sub-threshold triggers needs only data around each one and takes laptop-hours)
targets.statement: The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) collaborations have released the strain from the first two parts of their fourth observing run through GWOSC: O4a (2023 May 24 to 2024 January 16, H1 and L1; open-data paper arXiv:2508.18079) and O4b (2024 April 10 to 2025 January 28, H1, L1 and V1; released 2026 May 26; open-data paper arXiv:2605.27090). GWTC-4.0 (arXiv:2508.18082) reported 128 new O4a candidates with p_astro >= 0.5; GWTC-4.1 updated the O4a results; and GWTC-5.0 (arXiv:2605.27225) added 161 O4b candidates, bringing the cumulative catalog to 390 candidates (391 rows in the GWOSC event-portal snapshot of 2026-05-27, Zenodo 20418856, still the latest snapshot version when checked). The LVK candidate data releases list every trigger with FAR < 2/day from GstLAL, MBTA, PyCBC and cWB, with p_astro and BAYESTAR skymaps: 1,456 for O4a (GWTC-4.1, Zenodo 20276095; 139 have p_terrestrial < 0.5 in at least one pipeline and no data-quality veto) and 1,886 for O4b (GWTC-5.0, Zenodo 20348004; 161 such). In O1-O3, independent searches of the same public strain found mergers the LVK had not listed: the IAS pipeline (Olsen et al. 2022; Mehta et al. 2025; Wadekar et al., arXiv:2312.06631), 4-OGC (Nitz et al. 2023) and AresGW (Koloniari et al. 2025). Malz, Russell, Ashton and Colombo (arXiv:2607.07272) re-rank the released sub-threshold candidates across the catalog and name the O4a and O4b candidates they up-rank. As of 2026-10-28 no independent catalog of new O4a or O4b mergers had appeared on arXiv, and the live GWOSC event list matched the 2026-05-27 snapshot event for event (671 entries). Open task: a two-detector compact-binary candidate in public O4a or O4b strain, found at FAR <= 1/yr by a search with its own time-slide background, that no LVK or community catalog lists.
targets.success_criterion: A saved candidate package (GPS merger time to 0.01 s, detectors, best-fit template masses and aligned spins, SNR and reduced chi-squared per detector, the search code and configuration, the analysed segment list, the trigger and time-slide background files, and the excess-power scan of criterion (2)) such that: (1) the search covers a pre-declared span of at least 30 days of GWOSC O4a or O4b strain, and the candidate has FAR <= 1 per year from an inclusive background (the candidate's own single-detector triggers kept in the slides) built from at least 100 non-zero time slides, with background livetime at least 10 times the inverse of the claimed FAR, after multiplying by the number of searches, template banks and spans tried; (2) two detectors (H1 and L1, or two of H1, L1 and V1 in O4b) each have SNR >= 4.5 at the candidate with reduced chi-squared <= 2, the time lies inside the GWOSC data segments and passes the release's CBC_CAT1 data-quality bit in each detector used, no hardware injection is listed for that time, and, apart from the candidate's own chirp track, an Omicron or GWpy Q-transform scan of the GWOSC strain run by the claimant shows no excess-power trigger with SNR > 8 within 1 s in either detector (the O4a and O4b open-data papers describe no public Omicron or Gravity Spy trigger list); (3) Bayesian parameter estimation on the GWOSC strain (bilby or equivalent, with IMRPhenomXPHM or a newer model) gives a network matched-filter SNR posterior median >= 8; and (4) nothing lies within 1 s of it in the live GWOSC allevents list (https://gwosc.org/eventapi/json/allevents/, every catalog including marginal, discovery-paper and community lists), among the GWTC-4.1 and GWTC-5.0 candidate-release entries with p_terrestrial < 0.5 in any pipeline, or in any arXiv paper reporting O4 candidates (including the up-ranked candidates of arXiv:2607.07272), all re-fetched live immediately before claiming. A candidate listed in a candidate release with p_terrestrial >= 0.5 in every pipeline counts (a promotion), and the claim must say so.

partial_wins.statement: A candidate meeting criteria (2)-(4) with 1/yr < FAR <= 12/yr (once a month) in the claimant's search, the FAR coming from a background built by the rules of criterion (1), that is absent from all four LVK pipelines' FAR < 2/day candidate tables (a trigger every LVK search missed).

A new O3a or O3b candidate meeting criteria (1)-(4) on GWOSC O3 strain (with the O3 data-quality bits and hardware-injection lists in place of the O4 ones, and the glitch check also run against the Gravity Spy O1-O3 classifications, Zenodo 5649212), absent from GWOSC allevents, GWTC-2.1, GWTC-3 and their candidate releases, the IAS O3a, O3b and higher-harmonics catalogs (arXiv:2201.02252, 2311.06061, 2312.06631), 4-OGC (arXiv:2112.06878, including its sub-threshold list), AresGW (arXiv:2407.07820) and any other arXiv paper reporting O3 candidates (for example Kumar and Dent, arXiv:2403.10439), all re-fetched live immediately before claiming.

A saved, re-runnable search over at least 30 days of O4a or O4b strain that recovers at least 90% of the GWTC-4.1 or GWTC-5.0 candidates with FAR < 1/yr in that span at FAR <= 1/yr from its own time-slide background (method validation).

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads 4096 s of GWOSC 4 kHz strain around the candidate for each detector, re-filters it with the saved template (PyCBC or equivalent) to reproduce the per-detector SNR, chi-squared and time offset, reruns the saved pipeline's background on at least one week of the declared span with different slide offsets to check the FAR, checks the GWOSC segments, data-quality bits and hardware-injection list, reruns the excess-power scan around the time, reruns a short PE, and compares against the live GWOSC event list, both candidate releases and arXiv. Hours for the candidate checks; days for a full background rerun.
angles: Conventional: a PyCBC-style matched-filter search with a bank aimed where LVK banks are coarse (high-mass, precessing or higher-mode BBHs), with time slides for background: the route by which the IAS pipeline found new O3 events.
Re-rank the 3,342 released sub-threshold triggers (1,456 O4a + 1,886 O4b) with a coherent multi-detector statistic or a PE-based Bayes factor; a promotion needs only data around each trigger.
Cross-domain import (radar CFAR detection): set thresholds per data-quality epoch from the local background instead of one global ranking statistic.
Cross-domain import (ML ensembles, as in AresGW): an ML front end proposes triggers, matched filtering re-scores them, and time slides run on the combined statistic.
pitfalls: Use the inclusive background: removing the candidate's own triggers from the time slides inflates the significance of a loud trigger.
Scattered-light and blip glitches mimic high-mass BBHs; check Gravity Spy/Omicron near the time and the shape of the SNR time series.
In O4a, CAT2 flags were applied only to burst searches (arXiv:2508.18079); CBC_CAT1 is the release-defined bar for CBC times.
gwosc.org did not resolve or answer from our network on 2026-10-29 (it answered about ten hours earlier); the Zenodo event-portal snapshots mirror the event list but lag updates by about a day.
Do not post to GraceDB, GCN or social media; the result is a candidate in a run report only.

targets.name: First significant sub-solar-mass compact-binary candidate in public LIGO-Virgo strain (O1-O4b)
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster for a full search (sub-solar templates stay in band for minutes; Kacanja et al. needed about 25 million templates for O4a); laptop-hours to re-analyse the published outliers; laptop-days for a reduced bank over one month
targets.statement: Stellar evolution is not expected to make neutron stars or black holes below about 1 Msun, so a sub-solar-mass (SSM) merger would point to primordial black holes or dark-matter black holes. Searches of public strain have produced only marginal outliers. SSM200308 in O3b had search SNR 8.90 and FAR about 1 per 5 years (Prunier et al., arXiv:2311.16085). In O4a, the LVK (arXiv:2605.05444) and Kacanja, Soni, Akyuz and Nitz (arXiv:2602.12115, a public-data search with about 25 million templates) found no significant candidate. In O4b, the LVK search (arXiv:2610.20276, 2026-10-14; secondary 0.2-1 Msun, primary 0.2-10 Msun) reports two outliers that it judges consistent with noise. S240422ed (2024-04-22 21:35:13.42 UTC) has GstLAL SSM FAR 0.015/yr and was not confirmed by MBTA or PyCBC. S241229bq (2024-12-29 13:52:36.83 UTC) has MBTA FAR 0.0043/yr, about 2.8 sigma before trials, against 34/yr in GstLAL and 7.7/yr in PyCBC, and its SNR fell when the low-frequency cutoff was lowered. Table 1 of that paper also lists a third MBTA candidate (2025-01-02 09:44:02.30 UTC, FAR 1.3/yr, network SNR 10.6, a two-detector coincidence that includes Virgo) that the LVK judges consistent with noise. Christensen, Cornish, Kuhnel, Sakellariadou and Villares Guanga (arXiv:2607.23119) ran Bayesian PE on the seven most significant LVK O4a SSM triggers and on four triggers reported by other groups; several may contain a sub-solar component, but none is significant in its search. Kacanja, Soni and Nitz searched O4a+O4b public data (arXiv:2610.19329, 2026-10-14; primary 0.1-2 Msun, secondary 0.1-1 Msun, tidal deformabilities up to 7e5) and found no significant candidate (their most significant has FAR 0.6 per year). Miller (arXiv:2609.16238) found none for chirp masses 0.01-0.1 Msun in O4a+O4b. O4c strain is not public; it holds the SSM public alert S251112cm (MBTA SSM online FAR about 1 in 6 years, revised to about 1 in 4 years; GCN Circulars 42650 and 42690) and the sub-threshold SSM candidate S250818k. Open task: a sub-solar-mass candidate in public strain that stays significant after trials and that an independent second search recovers.
targets.success_criterion: A saved candidate package (GPS time, detectors, template parameters, search code and configuration, trigger and time-slide background files, PE samples, and the excess-power scan of criterion (4)) for a candidate in GWOSC strain from any public run (O1 to O4b) such that: (1) the claimant's search, over a pre-declared span and template bank, gives FAR <= 1e-3 per year (IFAR >= 1000 yr) from an inclusive time-slide background with livetime at least 10 times that IFAR, after multiplying by the number of banks, spans and searches tried; (2) a second, independently implemented search of a different pipeline family (for example PyCBC-style vs GstLAL-style vs MBTA-style) recovers it within 0.05 s at FAR <= 1 per year; (3) Bayesian PE on the GWOSC strain gives a 90% upper bound on the secondary source-frame mass below 1.0 Msun, with a network SNR posterior median >= 8; (4) the time passes the GWOSC CBC_CAT1 bit in each detector used, no hardware injection is listed near it, no glitch with SNR > 8 lies in band within the template's last 10 s in either detector (checked with an Omicron or GWpy Q-transform scan of the GWOSC strain run by the claimant, and for O1-O3 times also against the Gravity Spy O1-O3 classifications, Zenodo 5649212; the O4a and O4b open-data papers describe no public O4 glitch list), and in each detector the SNR, as the low-frequency cutoff is lowered, follows the template's expected accumulation within 1 sigma (the check that weakened S241229bq); and (5) the claim states its relation to SSM200308, S240422ed, S241229bq, the other candidates in Table 1 of arXiv:2610.20276, the candidates in Table 1 of arXiv:2610.19329 and the O4a triggers analysed in arXiv:2607.23119, and exceeds every published significance for the same time, with arXiv:2610.20276, arXiv:2610.19329 and later SSM papers re-fetched live immediately before claiming.

partial_wins.statement: A candidate meeting criteria (2)-(5) with 100 yr <= IFAR < 1000 yr after trials in the claimant's search; once trials are counted, this already exceeds both LVK O4b outliers.

An independent re-analysis of public O4b strain that recovers both LVK O4b outliers (S240422ed and S241229bq) within 0.05 s, with network SNR within 10% of the Table 1 values of arXiv:2610.20276, and reports their FAR from its own inclusive background (a reproducibility check).

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the GWOSC strain around the candidate (several minutes, since SSM templates are long), re-filters it with the saved template to reproduce SNR, chi-squared and the SNR-versus-cutoff behaviour, reruns the second search near the time, spot-checks the background by rerunning a subset of time slides with new offsets, reruns PE (relative binning or a reduced-order likelihood keeps this to hours), and compares with the LVK and Nitz-group tables. Hours to days.
angles: Conventional: a reduced SSM bank aimed at the region the LVK banks under-cover, for example the high aligned spins of S240422ed (the GstLAL low-latency SSM bank limits |chi| to 0.3), run with PyCBC and time slides.
Hierarchical or ratio-filter de-chirping methods (Soni and Nitz, arXiv:2409.11317) make long templates affordable on one machine.
Cross-domain import (sonar and radar long-pulse detection): stack-slide semi-coherent statistics over minutes-long chirps before a full coherent follow-up.
Cross-domain import (particle physics look-elsewhere corrections): pre-register the bank and trials count, then compute a global p-value from toy backgrounds.
pitfalls: SSM templates stay in band for minutes, so non-stationary noise over that time drives the background; a short-segment PSD estimate inflates significance.

S240422ed was first a stellar-mass candidate (chirp mass about 1.7 Msun, chi_eff above 0.75); a high-spin stellar-mass signal can land in an SSM bank with biased masses, and criterion (3) is what makes a candidate sub-solar.
The LVK notes that an outlier's false-alarm probability rises by about an order of magnitude once several pipelines are considered; count every search and bank you ran.
O4c alerts such as S251112cm cannot be analysed yet: O4c strain is not public (the GWOSC data-sets page lists O4a and O4b only).
Do not post to GraceDB, GCN or social media; the result is a candidate in a run report only.

targets.name: Gravity Spy v1.0 LIGO glitch classification: beat the best published test accuracy on the official 22-class split
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (the v1.0 image arrays are one 3.3 GB HDF5 file; a small CNN, or a fine-tuned pretrained model, trains on CPU or an Apple GPU)
targets.statement: Gravity Spy (Zevin et al. 2017; Bahaadini et al. 2018, Information Sciences 444:172-186) combines citizen-science labels with machine learning to classify transient noise (glitches) in LIGO data. The v1.0 training set released with Bahaadini, Noroozi, Rohani, Coughlin, Zevin, Smith, Kalogera and Katsaggelos (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.1476156) holds 8,583 O1/O2 glitches in 22 classes, each as four Omega-scan images (0.5, 1, 2 and 4 s). An official split is given in trainingset_v1d0_metadata.csv (md5 6b99210289d508696fb3feccfa7c79fc): 6,008 train, 1,288 validation and 1,287 test. Published test accuracies on this split are 97.67% (merged-view CNN) and 98.21% (four-CNN hard-fusion ensemble), both from Bahaadini et al. 2018, and 98.68% with macro-F1 97.18% for a ResNet18 trained from scratch (Fernandes, Vieira, Onofre, Calderon Bustillo, Torres-Forne and Font, arXiv:2303.13917, Table I). George, Shen and Huerta (PRD 97, 101501) report 98.84%, but on a different split with no validation set. A search of arXiv and the web on 2026-10-28 found no higher test accuracy on the official v1.0 split; later work uses other datasets (the v1d1 release of 7,966 glitches, or O3 data with more classes). Open task: a model trained only on the official training split that beats 98.68% on the official test set by a clear margin.
targets.success_criterion: A saved model (code, fixed seeds, weights) trained only on the 6,008 'train' samples of Gravity Spy v1.0 (Zenodo record 1476156; labels and split from trainingset_v1d0_metadata.csv, md5 6b99210289d508696fb3feccfa7c79fc), with hyperparameters and early stopping chosen on the 1,288 'validation' samples only. No other Gravity Spy-labelled data may be used for training or pre-training: v1d1, the O1-O3 machine-learning and volunteer classification releases and the Zooniverse data contain the same glitches. Generic pretrained weights such as ImageNet are allowed. The model must satisfy: (1) top-1 accuracy on the 1,287 'test' samples (all 22 classes, every image kept, labels as released) of at least 1,273/1,287 (98.91%), strictly above (direction: max) the 98.68% of Fernandes et al. (arXiv:2303.13917) and the 98.84% of George et al. (different split); (2) macro-averaged F1 on the test set of at least 97.18%; (3) retraining from scratch with 3 further seeds gives mean test accuracy of at least 98.76% (1,271/1,287); and (4) the accuracy exceeds any test accuracy on the official v1.0 split reported in a paper up to the claim date (search arXiv and the web for Gravity Spy classification, re-fetched live immediately before claiming).

partial_wins.statement: Test accuracy above 98.21% (the Bahaadini et al. four-CNN ensemble) from a single network that sees only one time-window view (0.5, 1, 2 or 4 s), under the same training rules.
Test accuracy of at least 98.68% (1,270/1,287) from a model trained on CPU in under 2 hours wall-clock, under the same training rules, with a 3-seed mean of at least 98.5%.

Macro-F1 of at least 98.0% on the test set with accuracy of at least 98.68%, under the same training rules (the minority classes Paired_Doves, Wandering_Line, Air_Compressor and Chirp drive macro-F1).

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads trainingsetv1d0.h5 and the metadata CSV from Zenodo record 1476156 (checking the md5 values on the record), runs the saved inference on the 1,287 test samples, recomputes accuracy and macro-F1 with an independent 20-line script, retrains one seed from scratch to confirm the recipe reaches the reported validation accuracy, and confirms the training script never reads test samples: two deterministic CPU reruns with the same seed, one with the test images replaced by noise, must give identical weights (GPU training is often not bitwise reproducible, so this check runs on CPU). A few hours.
angles: Conventional: fine-tune a modern pretrained image model (ConvNeXt, EfficientNet, ViT) on the four views, stacked as channels or fused late; the ResNet18 baseline of Fernandes et al. is a strong start.
Label smoothing for noisy citizen-science labels (Wu et al., CQG 42, 165015, found it helps on Gravity Spy O3 data).
Cross-domain import (audio tagging): treat the Omega scans as spectrograms and fine-tune an audio-pretrained transformer (Deshmukh et al., arXiv:2601.20034, used AST on O3/O4 glitches).
Cross-domain import (medical imaging): multi-scale view fusion with test-time augmentation limited to time shifts that keep the frequency axis fixed.
pitfalls: The test labels are public; using test images or labels for model selection, threshold tuning or pseudo-labelling voids the claim.

v1d1 (Zenodo 1476551, 7,966 glitches) keeps 5,726 v1.0 ids with the same train/validation/test assignment and adds 2,240 new ones; its test split holds 853 of the 1,287 v1.0 test glitches, so training on all of v1d1 leaks them, and even its training split is Gravity Spy-labelled data the rules exclude.

Some released spectrograms are blank (Yan et al., arXiv:2207.04001, removed them before making their own split); keep all 1,287 test samples, because dropping images changes the denominator and the comparison.
George et al.'s 98.84% used a different split and is not directly comparable; the main bar is set above it anyway.
Differences of 1-2 test samples are within seed noise; criterion (3)'s 3-seed mean guards against a lucky seed.

targets.name: First continuous gravitational-wave signal: a candidate in public LIGO data confirmed in an independent observing run
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster for broad all-sky searches (Einstein@Home scale); laptop-hours to days for targeted searches of known pulsars and for following a candidate up in narrow bands of GWOSC strain
targets.statement: Continuous gravitational waves (CWs) from spinning, deformed neutron stars have never been detected. In O4a data, the LVK targeted 45 known pulsars with three methods and found no signal (Abac et al., ApJ 983, 99, arXiv:2501.01495). Its upper limits beat the spin-down limit for 29 pulsars, and the lowest h0 limit, 6.4e-27, is for J0537-6910. An LVK narrowband search of 34 known pulsars in O4a+O4b data (arXiv:2603.25938) also found no signal; its tightest limit is about 2% of the Crab spin-down limit. LVK O4a searches toward 15 supernova remnants (arXiv:2603.25808), all-sky for isolated neutron stars from 20 to 2000 Hz (arXiv:2603.14168), all-sky for neutron stars in binaries (arXiv:2511.16863) and toward Scorpius X-1 (arXiv:2607.07765, whose outliers were ruled out with later O4 data) also found none. McGloughlin et al. (arXiv:2607.18219) searched public O4a data for J0435+3233 and set h0 < 5.8e-27.
