One Einstein@Home candidate survived the multi-stage follow-up of an O3a search with O3b and O4a data, O4a giving weaker evidence: the G347.3-0.5 outlier of Ming, Papa and collaborators (arXiv:2512.15672). Three pipelines then followed it up with the newly released O4b data and found no related standard CW signal in O4a or O4b (Mirasola et al., arXiv:2608.07662). Knee, Riles and Sun (arXiv:2608.07312) followed up 562 O4a radiometer candidates; none of their 21 outliers was recovered in O4b. GWOSC O4a and O4b data contain CW hardware injections for 18 simulated pulsars. Open task: a CW candidate in public data that is significant after trials in one run and predicted and recovered in an independent run.
targets.success_criterion: A saved candidate (target: a known pulsar with its ephemeris, or a sky position; f0, f1 and any higher derivatives or binary parameters at a stated reference time; amplitude parameters) with the full search and follow-up code, such that: (1) in a pre-declared discovery data set from GWOSC (any of O3a, O3b, O4a or O4b), the candidate's detection statistic has false-alarm probability <= 1e-3 after the full trials factor of the declared search, with the noise distribution measured by running the identical pipeline on at least 1,000 off-source trials of the same data (bands shifted by at least 1 Hz, or sky positions at least 10 degrees away, avoiding instrumental lines); (2) in a later run not used for discovery (for example O4b after an O4a discovery), a coherent or semi-coherent follow-up at the parameters predicted from the discovery solution, with the prediction frozen before the data are analysed, recovers it with single-trial false-alarm probability <= 1e-3 against at least 1,000 off-source trials, and h0 agrees with the discovery value within 2 sigma; (3) H1-only and L1-only analyses each show the signal, with a ratio of detector SNRs within a factor 2 of the antenna-pattern expectation; (4) its frequency is not within 1 frequency bin of any line in the published LIGO line lists for those runs, and it matches none of the GWOSC hardware injections; and (5) it is not the G347.3-0.5 outlier or one of the 21 O4a radiometer outliers unless criterion (2) holds for it, and no published search has reported the same signal, with arXiv re-fetched live immediately before claiming.

partial_wins.statement: An outlier passing (1), (3) and (4) at post-trials false-alarm probability <= 1e-2 in one run, with the pre-registered follow-up in the second run reported whatever it shows.

For one of the 45 known pulsars of arXiv:2501.01495, a 95% upper limit on h0 from public O4a+O4b data that is lower (direction: min) than every published limit for that pulsar (the O4a targeted limit of arXiv:2501.01495 and, where one exists, the O4a+O4b narrowband limit of arXiv:2603.25938), calibrated with at least 200 software injections and checked by recovering the O4a hardware injection nearest in frequency.
Independent recovery of at least 15 of the 18 O4a CW hardware injections at their documented parameters from GWOSC strain, with a saved, re-runnable pipeline (method validation).

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads narrow bands of GWOSC strain around the candidate frequency for both runs (or builds SFTs from them with lalpulsar or PyFstat), reruns the saved coherent follow-up at the stated parameters with fresh off-source trials, checks the line lists and the hardware-injection table, and repeats the single-detector analyses. Hours for a follow-up; the discovery search itself is spot-checked, not rerun.
angles: Conventional: targeted Bayesian, 5-vector or F-statistic searches on O4a+O4b together for pulsars with recent radio or X-ray timing that were not in the 45-pulsar O4a list.
Follow up published outlier lists (Knee et al. 2026; Einstein@Home papers) in O4b with an independent pipeline.
Cross-domain import (radio pulsar searching): acceleration searches and fast-folding ideas for CW sources in binaries.
Cross-domain import (sonar narrowband tracking): hidden-Markov-model (Viterbi) tracking of spin wandering across long coherent segments.
pitfalls: CW hardware injections are present in almost all O4a data (18 simulated pulsars); check the injection table first.
Instrumental lines and combs dominate outlier lists; check the run's line list and single-detector consistency before anything else.
The trials factor of a broad search is enormous; draw the off-source trials exactly as the search draws its templates, not from a quieter band.
O4c strain is not public; a confirmation in O4b only counts if it was predicted from the O4a solution before the O4b data were analysed.
Do not announce or post; the result is a candidate in a run report only.

targets.name: Decisive stacked evidence for the (l=2, m=0) memory-carrying mode across all GWTC-4.0 and GWTC-5.0 binary black holes
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (about 190 events x 2 waveform models x 2 seeds of bilby/dynesty nested sampling with a time-domain waveform; each run takes hours to a day on many cores) or laptop-weeks; inputs are GWOSC strain and the LVK PE releases (PSDs, calibration envelopes)
targets.statement: Gravitational-wave memory, the permanent displacement left after a burst of radiation, is a nonlinear prediction of general relativity that has not been detected. It lives mainly in the (l=2, m=0) spherical-harmonic mode, which also has an oscillatory ringdown part. Rossello-Sastre, Husa, Xu, Valencia, Llobera-Querol and Ramos-Buades (arXiv:2607.04909, 2026-07-06) compared IMRPhenomTHM_20 (with the full (2,0) mode) against IMRPhenomTHM (without it) for the 84 GWTC-4.0 binary black holes plus 6 GWTC-5.0 events chosen for high SNR or spin. They used bilby/dynesty with nlive 1000, naccept 60, dlogz 0.05 and two seeds. The stacked sum of log10 Bayes factors over GWTC-4.0 is 1.38 +/- 0.79: strong on Jeffreys' scale but not decisive. The best single event is GW230814_230901 at 0.63 +/- 0.09. They estimate that decisive evidence needs about 166 (+82/-55) events, and they left the O4b events out of the stack because those were not chosen in an unbiased way. Mitman, Isi and Farr (arXiv:2605.27500) use hierarchical inference on GWTC-5.0 to constrain the memory enhancement factor to 0.26 (+4.09/-4.08), and warn that naively multiplying Bayes factors across events can mislead. GWTC-5.0 (arXiv:2605.27225) adds 104 O4b candidates with FAR < 1/yr and full PE releases. Open task: decisive (log10 B >= 2) evidence for the (2,0) mode from a complete, unbiased GWTC-4.0 + GWTC-5.0 stack, robust to waveform choice and calibrated against simulated memory-free data.
targets.success_criterion: Saved per-event results (configuration files, priors, the PSDs and calibration envelopes used, evidences with sampling errors for both models and both seeds, and the code) for a pre-registered, complete event list: every binary black hole candidate with FAR < 1/yr and an LVK PE release from O4a (the 84 GWTC-4.0 BBHs analysed in arXiv:2607.04909; PE release Zenodo 17602505) and from O4b (the 104 GWTC-5.0 candidates; PE releases Zenodo 20348005 and 20348006), 188 events; O1-O3 events are not part of the list. No selection by SNR, spin or Bayes factor is allowed; an event may be dropped only by a data rule declared before any (2,0)-mode result is seen (for example, events the LVK analysed with glitch-mitigated data, Table 3 of arXiv:2508.18079 and Table 4 of arXiv:2605.27090, when that data is not public). The events are analysed on GWOSC strain with IMRPhenomTHM_20 vs IMRPhenomTHM (or a newer model pair that differs only by the (2,0) mode), at settings no looser than those of arXiv:2607.04909 (dynesty, nlive 1000, naccept 60, dlogz 0.05, two seeds), such that: (1) the stacked sum of per-event log10 B is at least 2.0 (direction: max), and its 1-sigma lower bound (the sum minus the quadrature sum of per-event errors) is at least 1.5; (2) for the 10 events contributing most, a second waveform family that contains the (2,0) mode, run with and without it (for example an NR surrogate or an effective-one-body model with m = 0 modes), gives a summed log10 B at least half of the first family's sum for those events; (3) null calibration: for each of the 5 largest contributors, at least 20 injections of the memory-free model at that event's maximum-likelihood parameters into GWOSC noise from nearby times, analysed identically, give log10 B values whose 95th percentile lies below that event's observed value; and (4) the stacked value exceeds every published stacked (2,0)-mode or memory Bayes factor for LVK data, with arXiv re-fetched live immediately before claiming.

partial_wins.statement: The complete, unbiased GWTC-4.0 + GWTC-5.0 stack (event-list and settings rules met) with stacked log10 B of at least 1.0 and null calibration (3) passed, published as a per-event table: the first unbiased stack to include O4b.
A single event with log10 B >= 1.0 for the (2,0) mode under both waveform families and null calibration (3) for that event; the current best single event is at 0.63 +/- 0.09.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic reruns the per-event analyses from the saved configurations with new seeds for 10 randomly chosen events plus the 5 largest contributors, checks each log10 B lies within 2 sigma of the saved value, recomputes the stacked sum from the saved table, checks the event list against the GWTC-4.0 and GWTC-5.0 tables and the pre-registration, and reruns 5 of the null injections. Days on a cluster or a large workstation.
angles: Conventional: rerun the published bilby setup on every O4b BBH with FAR < 1/yr, add the results to the 84 GWTC-4.0 runs, and reuse the LVK PSDs and calibration envelopes.

Importance-reweight the released LVK posterior samples to the (2,0) model, as Hubner et al. did for memory in GWTC-1 and GWTC-2, to get cheap Bayes factors, and rerun full sampling only where the reweighting efficiency is low.
Cross-domain import (medical meta-analysis): random-effects stacking and leave-one-out influence checks to show the evidence is not driven by one or two events.
Hierarchical alternative (Mitman, Isi and Farr): report the memory-enhancement-factor posterior alongside the stacked Bayes factor.
pitfalls: Selecting events by SNR, spin or a first-pass Bayes factor biases the stack; freeze the event list before seeing any (2,0)-mode result.
Waveform systematics in the dominant modes can masquerade as (2,0)-mode evidence at high SNR (GW250114_082203 has network SNR 76.9); criterion (2) exists for this.
Nested-sampling evidence errors are often underestimated; use two seeds and the tighter dlogz, and report per-event errors.
Mitman, Isi and Farr show that naive products of Bayes factors can favour wrong conclusions; the stacked number is one line of evidence, and the null calibration is the guard.

targets.name: Gamma-ray counterpart candidate in public Fermi-GBM data for an O4a/O4b gravitational-wave candidate, sub-threshold ones included
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (GBM CTIME and CSPEC daily files are tens of MB per day for about 600 days; continuous TTE is larger and needed only near candidates; each LVK candidate release with skymaps is about 1-1.5 GB)
targets.statement: GW170817 with GRB 170817A remains the only confirmed gravitational-wave/gamma-ray pair. The weak Fermi-GBM transient 0.4 s after GW150914 (Connaughton et al., arXiv:1602.03920, false-alarm probability 0.0022, 2.9 sigma) is contested. The LVK candidate data releases list every O4 trigger with FAR < 2/day, with times, p_astro and BAYESTAR skymaps: 1,456 for O4a (GWTC-4.1, Zenodo 20276095) and 1,886 for O4b (GWTC-5.0, Zenodo 20348004). Fermi-GBM daily CTIME, CSPEC, continuous TTE and position-history files are public at HEASARC (the O4b day 2024-12-29 was checked). For O1-O3, the GBM team ran its targeted and untargeted sub-threshold searches on the catalog events, including the GWTC-1 low-significance candidates, and found no confident counterpart other than GRB 170817A (Hamburg et al. 2020, arXiv:2001.00923; Fletcher et al. 2024, arXiv:2308.13666, jointly with Swift-BAT). Pillas, Dal Canton and collaborators (arXiv:2306.04373) cross-matched every O2 PyCBC trigger with a reanalysis of all public GBM data from that run. Perera, Zackay and Venumadhav (arXiv:2507.05739) built a time-slide sGRB search of archival GBM data that finds about 50% more short bursts than the on-board trigger, but it does not cross-match O4 GW candidates. Other published work: single-event studies such as GW230529 (Ronchini et al., arXiv:2405.10752, no detection by Swift-BAT or Fermi-GBM), a 4-OGC cross-match with GBM/BAT long GRBs (Wang, Nitz et al., arXiv:2208.03279, consistent with a null result), and a match of 13 O4-era sub-threshold short GRBs against the significant O4 public alerts (Cai et al., arXiv:2509.02995, no coincidence). As of 2026-10-28, no paper reports a systematic search of the O4 (GWTC-4.1 and GWTC-5.0) sub-threshold candidate lists against untriggered GBM data. Open task: a gamma-ray transient in public GBM data, coincident in time and sky with an O4 gravitational-wave candidate, whose association survives the full trials factor.
targets.success_criterion: A saved pair, consisting of a GW candidate from the GWTC-4.1 or GWTC-5.0 candidate release (gw_name, GPS time) and a gamma-ray transient found in public Fermi-GBM data (HEASARC daily CTIME or continuous TTE files), with the search code and a pre-registered list of every GW candidate searched, such that: (1) the transient begins within [-1 s, +5 s] of the GW merger time; (2) its single-candidate false-alarm probability p, from the claimant's targeted-search statistic evaluated identically on off-source windows of the same GBM data within 3 days of the event (excluding SAA passages and known triggers; overlapping windows and inter-detector time slides are allowed), is <= 1e-4, and the off-source set holds at least 100,000 windows and at least 10/p windows, so that p is counted rather than extrapolated; (3) the GW candidate's 90% credible region from the release skymap is not entirely Earth-occulted for Fermi at that time and overlaps the transient's 90% GBM localisation, including systematic error; (4) the false-association probability, p multiplied by the number of GW candidates searched and by every timescale, spectral template and window tried, is <= 1e-3 (so the off-source set of (2) must be large enough to count a p that small); and (5) the transient is not a catalogued GBM trigger of another origin (terrestrial gamma-ray flash, magnetar burst, solar flare, particle event), and the pair is absent from GCN Circulars (https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars) and from published GW-GRB papers, all re-fetched live immediately before claiming.

partial_wins.statement: A pair meeting every criterion except (4), with post-trials false-association probability between 1e-3 and 1e-2.

Method validation: run blind on public data, the same pipeline recovers GRB 170817A for GW170817 with single-candidate false-alarm probability <= 1e-4, and the GW150914 GBM transient with a false-alarm probability within a factor 3 of the published 0.0022.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the GBM CTIME/TTE and position-history files for the day, reruns the saved targeted search on the on-source window and on 10,000 freshly drawn off-source windows, recomputes the Earth occultation and the overlap with the release skymap, recounts the trials from the pre-registration, and searches the GBM trigger catalog and the GCN archive. A few hours.
angles: Conventional: a GBM targeted-search approach (a coherent Poisson likelihood across the detectors with spectral templates) run on CTIME data around every candidate.
Joint-mission detection (Perera, Zackay and Venumadhav, arXiv:2609.25672): combine GBM with Swift-BAT rates to reach fainter short bursts.
Rank GW candidates by p_BNS + p_NSBH and distance before searching, and pre-register the ranking so the trials factor stays honest.
Cross-domain import (neutrino astronomy): unbinned stacking likelihoods over many weak candidates, for a population-level signal.
pitfalls: Most of the 3,342 candidates are noise; the trials factor over candidates, windows and templates dominates.
Terrestrial gamma-ray flashes, magnetospheric particle events and solar activity make short GBM excesses; check the GBM trigger catalog and the spacecraft's geomagnetic position.
Earth occultation and SAA passages remove large parts of the sky and of the time; a counterpart must be geometrically possible.
Do not post GCN Circulars or contact the GBM or LVK teams; the result is a candidate in a run report only.

targets.name: Greek inscriptions: beat Stoicheia v2 (CER 15.5, top-1 74.5) on the frozen 3,000-gap file cut from Ithaca's PHI-digit-3 test split
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (a GPU helps; fine-tuning or reranking with a ~400M-parameter character model); test file 2.9 MB, public Greek corpora a few GB
targets.statement: Ithaca (Assael, Sommerschield, Shillingford, Bordbar, Pavlopoulos, Chatzipanagiotou, Androutsopoulos, Prag and de Freitas, Nature 2022) fixed the standard split for Greek epigraphic restoration: I.PHI inscriptions whose PHI id ends in 3 are test, 4 validation. Its masked test set was never released (Locaputo, Brunello, Saccomanno, Platanou and Serra, 'Ithaca Revisited', LREC 2026, aclanthology 2026.lrec-1.82, recompute Ithaca on their own masks for that reason), so CERs printed in different papers are not comparable. Cullhed and Thorn Cleland (Stoicheia, arXiv 2608.07249v1, 7 Aug 2026; code github.com/ericu9500/stoicheia, Apache-2.0, HEAD 1870b871 of 2026-08-03) ship a frozen sample file, insc/eval/frozen/strict_test_fold3_samples.json (2,936,335 bytes, git blob 54062823f79f, sha256 4373df905922785094688153462dd524cab2e8216a33a0673cbf0b5b35a1004a): 3,000 artificial gaps, 300 at each length L = 1..10, cut from 375 decontaminated digit-3 inscriptions; each record is {phi_id, L, start, gold, text}, the whole inscription is context with its real lacunae left as '-' runs, and spaces count inside the gap (1,896 of the 3,000 golds contain a space). On this file, beam 20, Levenshtein CER over the gap string (insc/eval/restore_strict.py), their Table 2 reports CER / top-1 / top-20 (%): Ithaca 24.6 / 63.0 / 74.9; the 2025 Aeneas-framework Greek release 23.5 / 64.0 / 75.5; Stoicheia v1 17.0 / 72.0 / 80.8; Stoicheia v2 15.5 / 74.5 / 81.7 (a 405M-parameter character-level masked-diffusion encoder; the digit-3 checkpoint Ericu950/Stoicheia-restoration-test3 is public on Hugging Face). Apollo Restore (McGovern, Dolganov, Belkadi, Kunsch, Vlitas and Smith, arXiv 2609.22455v4, 7 Oct 2026; 24B, fill-in-the-middle) reports large top-20 gains on its own IG / DDB / DCLP benchmarks, but has not released weights or benchmark ('We will release the weights, data, and evaluation code') and does not report on this file. Status 2026-10-28: no result on the frozen file other than Stoicheia's Table 2 was found; arXiv 2608.07249 is still at v1 and the repository is unchanged since 2026-08-03. Ithaca's beam search was fixed upstream on 2026-10-27 (google-deepmind/ithaca cd4e47bc: deduplication kept the lower-scoring copy of a duplicate hypothesis, and punctuation could fill a gap), and predictingthepast's on 2026-10-21 (c8889e9c), so the Ithaca and Aeneas rows of Table 2 were produced before those fixes.
targets.success_criterion: A frozen prediction file covering all 3,000 records of strict_test_fold3_samples.json (git blob 54062823f79f), with up to 20 ranked candidate strings per record, each exactly L characters long over the characters that occur in the file (the 24 unaccented lower-case Greek letters with sigma merged, space, '.' and '0'), whose hash is committed before scoring, must score CER strictly below 15.5 AND top-1 strictly above 74.5 (percent; Stoicheia v2, Table 2 of arXiv 2608.07249, re-read immediately before claiming). CER = mean over records of Levenshtein(candidate 1, gold) / L, which equals the mean of the per-length means because every length has 300 records; top-1 = exact match of candidate 1 with gold, spaces included. Conditions: (a) for each record the model reads only that record's text with text[start:start+L] hidden; no other record, metadata or id lookup; (b) no training, tuning or retrieval material contains a test inscription (phi_id in the file) or a near-duplicate of one: same normalised text, Jaccard similarity of normalised character 5-gram sets of at least 0.5, or a shared run of 100 or more consecutive normalised characters; (c) every source of training and pretraining text is public and listed with hashes so that (b) can be checked; material inherited from a released Stoicheia checkpoint counts as decontaminated by its authors' fold manifests, everything the claimant adds is scanned; models whose pretraining data is undisclosed cannot claim the full win.

partial_wins.statement: Same file and conditions: CER strictly below 15.5 or top-1 strictly above 74.5 (only one of the two), with the other metric no worse than Stoicheia v1 (17.0 CER, 72.0 top-1).

Long gaps: on the 1,500 records with L = 6..10, mean CER and top-1 both strictly better than Stoicheia v2 on the same records, where the Stoicheia v2 predictions are regenerated by the claimant from the released Ericu950/Stoicheia-restoration-test3 checkpoint with the repository harness (beam 20, INSC_TEST_DIGIT=3) and published as a frozen file (hash committed before scoring); the verifier re-runs a random 100 of those records to confirm them.

targets.verification_method: The verifier fetches the frozen file at commit 1870b871 and checks its blob id and sha256, checks the prediction file's hash against the pre-scoring commitment, and rescores CER, top-1 and top-20 both with independent code (Levenshtein over the L-character gap strings, sigma folded, spaces counted) and with the scoring loop of insc/eval/restore_strict.py. It then scans the published training manifest for the 375 test phi_ids and for near-duplicates of their texts (identical text, 5-gram Jaccard at least 0.5, shared runs of 100 characters) with a rolling-hash pass. Rescoring takes seconds and the scan under an hour; the verifier never retrains.
angles: Rerank Stoicheia v2's 20-best: its top-20 (81.7) is 7.2 points above its top-1 (74.5), so a second scorer (a right-to-left or fill-in-the-middle character model trained on the same decontaminated public corpora) can win top-1 without a better generator.

Retrieval of formulae from the training digits (not 3 or 4): decrees, dedications and epitaphs repeat long phrases, and a parallel passage often fixes a whole gap; keep the near-duplicate filter on the retrieval index too.
Length-exact, segmentation-aware decoding: the gold is exactly L characters including spaces, so enumerate word divisions inside the gap rather than letters alone, as Stoicheia's boundary plane does.
Report the letters-only CER that the harness also computes (spaces stripped from both strings); about 15% of gap characters are spaces, which are easier than letters.
If you report Ithaca or Aeneas baselines, re-run them with decoders at or after google-deepmind/ithaca cd4e47bc and predictingthepast c8889e9c and record the commits.
pitfalls: The gold is embedded in each record's text (text[start:start+L] == gold for all 3,000 records): mask it before any model sees the text, and never let a model read the raw file.
The 3,000 gaps come from only 375 inscriptions (about 8 per inscription), so gaps are not independent; use paired tests that resample inscriptions, not gaps.

The file covers only the decontaminated part of the digit-3 split (the harness excludes test inscriptions flagged as contaminated), so its numbers are not comparable with Ithaca's printed 26.3 CER (Nature 2022, Table 1) or with Apollo Restore's IG numbers.
Table 2's Ithaca and Aeneas rows predate the upstream beam-search fixes of 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-27; re-runs with current code can give different baselines.
PHI texts are on the open web: a model with undisclosed pretraining may have read the test inscriptions and their editors' restorations, which is why such models cannot claim the full win.
PHI can hold several editions of one stone under different ids, so a split by id alone leaks; the near-duplicate rule in (b) is part of the criterion.

Candidates must be exactly L characters: generators that do not know the length (Ithaca's no-count mode, FIM decoders without a hint) must be truncated or filtered consistently, or they lose exact matches.

55 of the 3,000 golds contain '.' (48) or the numeral placeholder '0' (7); decoders that emit only letters and spaces (Stoicheia's renderer, Ithaca after cd4e47bc) can never match those exactly, so a system that can emit them has a small built-in edge.
Released checkpoints are Python pickles or remote-code model classes; load them only in a sandbox.

targets.name: Latin inscriptions (LED): beat Aeneas on dating (13.4 years) and province attribution (72.3% top-1) on the id-digit-3 test split
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (180,205 inscriptions in a 62 MB JSON; released Aeneas checkpoint 146 MB; a GPU helps)
targets.statement: Aeneas (Assael, Sommerschield, Cooley, Shillingford, Pavlopoulos, Suresh, Herms, Grayston, Maynard, Dietrich, Wulgaert, Prag, Mullen and Mohamed, Nature 645, 141-147, 2025, published online 23 July 2025, doi 10.1038/s41586-025-09292-5) introduced the Latin Epigraphic Dataset (LED: EDR, EDH and EDCS_ETL inscriptions merged by Trismegistos id; 176,861 inscriptions in the paper) and split it by the last digit of the inscription id: 3 test, 4 validation, the rest training (predictingthepast dataloader, should_process_sample). Table 2 (LED test set): province attribution over 62 provinces top-1 72.3% / top-3 83.9% (the 'Province (Vision)' column: images used where available, about 5% of inscriptions); date distance 13.4 years (distance from the predictive mean date to the ground-truth range); restoration of up to 20 characters CER 40.5% / top-20 46.5% with the length given and 66.1% / 32.7% without; Ithaca retrained on LED 61.3% / 75.3%, 14.1 years, 43.5% / 44.2%; onomastics baseline 17.9% / 30.9%, 51.3 years. The released file led.json (storage.googleapis.com/ithaca-resources/models/led.json, 62,464,288 bytes, md5 e1be05c28b7c97490065486c8f82e3af equal to the GCS etag, last modified 2025-06-16) holds 180,205 records (id, text, date_min, date_max, region_main, region_sub, ...), 17,990 of them with id % 10 == 3. The Latin checkpoint aeneas_117149994_2.pkl (145,662,103 bytes, etag 0cdebf373bf3694ef413b00e2e830e8c) and the code (github.com/google-deepmind/predictingthepast, Apache-2.0 code, CC BY / CC BY-SA data, HEAD f2d17de7 of 2026-10-27, beam-search fix c8889e9c of 2026-10-21) are public. Status 2026-10-28: no published system beating Aeneas on LED was found; the closest 2026 work (arXiv 2608.28170, Zhang, Caraffa, Zuffrano, Modesti and Colavizza) restores unpublished Bolognese notarial documents, not LED.
targets.success_criterion: On led.json (md5 e1be05c28b7c97490065486c8f82e3af), the test list T is every record with int(id) % 10 == 3 whose text, after deleting whitespace and the characters '-', '#' and '_', has at least 25 characters (15,381 records); the province list T_p is the records of T whose region_sub, mapped by region_name_filter of predictingthepast/util/region_names.py at a recorded commit, is one of the 62 names of train/data/led-region-sub.txt mapped the same way (15,192 records); the dating list T_d is the records of T with numeric date_min <= date_max, both inside [-800, 800] (8,164 records). The verifier recomputes all three lists. A frozen predictions file, whose hash is committed before scoring and which is made from each record's text alone (no images, metadata or id lookups), ranks the 62 provinces for every record of T_p and gives one point date (a year) for every record of T_d. Full win: province top-1 accuracy on T_p strictly above 72.3% AND mean date error on T_d strictly below 13.4 years (date error is 0 when the point date lies in [date_min, date_max], else the distance to the nearer bound; both paper values re-read from Table 2 immediately before claiming), AND both strictly better than the released checkpoint aeneas_117149994_2.pkl on the same lists, whose frozen predictions the claimant also publishes (hash committed before scoring), made with predictingthepast at a recorded commit no older than c8889e9c as follows: each record's text is prepared as the dataloader prepares it (LatinAlphabet.filter, which deletes '!,;?·', then lower-casing) and passed to attribute() text-only (vision_img=None); a prepared text of 768 or more characters (91 records of T), which attribute() rejects, is cut to its first 767 characters; the checkpoint's point date is its predictive mean (date_pred_avg of predicted_dates in predictingthepast/util/eval.py), the quantity the paper scores. Training uses only LED records with id % 10 not in {3, 4} (digit 4 for model selection) plus public non-epigraphic Latin text, all listed with hashes; none of that material may be a test record or a near-duplicate of one (same normalised text, or a shared run of 60 or more consecutive normalised characters with a record of T; normalised means lower-cased, with whitespace and the characters '-', '#' and '_' deleted), so a model initialised from aeneas_117149994_2.pkl, which was trained on such records, cannot claim the full win; models whose pretraining data is undisclosed cannot claim the full win.

partial_wins.statement: One attribution task only, same lists and rules: province top-1 strictly above 72.3% with top-3 strictly above 83.9%, or mean date error strictly below 13.4 years, beating both the Table 2 value(s) and the released checkpoint on the same records.

Restoration with the length given: on a sample file built from T by a published deterministic rule (for example 200 gaps per length L = 1..20 with a fixed seed, gaps placed only in text free of '-', '#' and '_'), frozen and hashed before any model is run, CER strictly below 40.5% and top-20 strictly above 46.5%, and both strictly better than the released Aeneas checkpoint's frozen predictions on the same file (beam 20, predictingthepast at a recorded commit no older than c8889e9c).

targets.verification_method: The verifier downloads led.json (md5 check) and, at the recorded predictingthepast commit, led-region-sub.txt and region_names.py; it regenerates T, T_p and T_d from the stated rule, checks both prediction files' hashes against the pre-scoring commitments, and rescores top-1, top-3 and mean date error with independent code. It re-runs the released Aeneas checkpoint on a random 300 records of T in a sandbox, with the stated preparation, 767-character cut and predictive-mean date, to confirm the baseline file (CPU, under an hour), and scans the published training manifest for test ids and near-duplicates (identical normalised text, shared 60-character runs). No retraining.
angles: Retrieval-augmented attribution: the nearest training inscriptions by character n-gram TF-IDF carry province and date labels; ensemble a k-NN vote with a fine-tuned character transformer.

Onomastics, tribes, military units and formula variants (D M, h s e, stipendia) carry place and date; a model with explicit name and formula features may beat a pure character model on short epitaphs.
For dating, predict a distribution over ten-year bins and output the year minimising expected distance to the true range, rather than the predictive mean.
Hierarchical labels: LED's region_main (2,068 places, present for 75,032 records) nests in the 62 provinces and is a useful auxiliary training target.
Text-only inference is required, but object_type, inscription_type and monument_type (at least one of them present for 75,613 records) can serve as auxiliary losses during training.
pitfalls: 73 inscription texts of 40 or more characters occur verbatim both in the test digit and in other digits of the pinned led.json (counted 2026-10-29), 64 of them in a training digit that the released checkpoint was trained on; 96 records of T have an exact textual twin under an id of another digit (100 counting twins inside digit 3). Report results with and without those records.

The near-duplicate rule removes training material: 1,252 training-digit records (0.9%) share a run of 60 or more normalised characters (lower-cased; whitespace, '-', '_' and '#' deleted) with a record of T, and 1,366 in all are dropped once records with the same normalised text as a record of T are added (recounted 2026-10-30).
Table 2's 72.3% uses images where available (images are not in led.json); comparing a text-only system against it is conservative, and the released checkpoint is scored text-only.
The paper's numbers come from Aeneas's own filtered test set; the lists here are defined by rule and differ, which is why the released checkpoint must be scored on the same lists.

Province names in led.json and in led-region-sub.txt differ for about 5,800 records ('Samnium' and 'Sabina et Samnium', 'Thrace' and 'Thracia'); apply region_name_filter to both, or those records are silently dropped or miscounted.

predictingthepast's attribute() does not apply LatinAlphabet.filter (raw ',' or '·' raises a KeyError) and rejects inputs of 768 or more characters; prepare texts as the dataloader does and apply the fixed 767-character cut, or the baseline file cannot be reproduced. The claimant's own system may read whole texts.
Restoration beam search changed on 2026-10-21 (predictingthepast c8889e9c, 'Fix active beam deduplication and nucleus filtering'); record the commit used for every restoration baseline.

Inscriptions, their dates and their provinces are on the open web (EDH, EDR, EDCS, Wikipedia; the Res Gestae is also in literary corpora), so near-duplicate scanning must cover any added non-epigraphic text.
Dates outside [-800, 800] fall outside Aeneas's 160 ten-year bins and are excluded from T_d.
The released checkpoint is a Python pickle; load it only in a sandbox.

targets.name: Bamboo-slip fragment rejoining: beat WisePanda's Top-10 and Top-50 on the released Bamboo1350 fracture-curve benchmark without using real pairs
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (fracture curves of 64 points; benchmark arrays under 20 MB)
targets.statement: Zhu, Zhao, Lei, Wang, Lu, Li, Tang, Shen, Xia, Du and Xu (Nature Communications 17, article 3550, published 2026-03-06, doi 10.1038/s41467-026-70361-y; arXiv 2505.08601v2) rejoin transversely broken Western Han bamboo slips (Tomb 77, Shuihudi, Yunmeng, 179-157 BCE, not yet published) by ranking fracture-curve matches. Their WisePanda network is trained only on physics-simulated fracture curves, never on real pairs. The benchmark data are public at github.com/zhujinchi/wisepanda (HEAD af79b052 of 2026-09-30; the README licenses the code under Apache 2.0 and names no data licence, and the repository has no LICENSE file; the notebook loads the arrays from algorithm/ as dataset/...): algorithm/dataset/vector_real_118_patch.npy (118 expert-verified pairs, float64 118x4x64, sha256 94a4ffbc1f0a75b1417f85e0a67ac234e28ce5e1ec0caa138a31b3ae605feaab; the evaluation uses channels 2:4 as top and bottom curves), algorithm/dataset/interference_data_bamboo.npy (1,114 unrelated real curves, 1114x64, sha256 9f32f60c1f0f398cc21fee4c0956c782f1d186467463531094375b2be2c8b17a), algorithm/dataset/wood/vector_real_335_patch.npy (335 wooden-slip pairs, sha256 45173a322e802bfd3ed3052a929001d8fa89dce2ef9259cf15afbd7f5456a03f), algorithm/dataset/wood/interference_data_wood.npy (2,259 curves, sha256 b0eeb885f282f51ae1b01bbf1110b1844302e5e7ec0f426a8c5c51e6d48ee7e3), the synthetic training set algorithm/dataset/vector_reallike_6000.npy, cropped edge images of Bamboo236 (real-world_dataset/Bamboo236), and three trained weight pairs per method (algorithm/models/normal). Scoring (algorithm/method_comparison.ipynb, get_topk_accuracy_with_extend): every real top curve ranks all bottom candidates and every real bottom ranks all top candidates, and Top-k = hits / 236. Table 1, mean of 3 runs (%), Top-1 / 5 / 10 / 20 / 50 / 100: Bamboo236 (118 pairs) WisePanda 13.42 / 37.15 / 50.85 / 66.81 / 91.81 / 100.00; Bamboo1350 (118 pairs plus 1,114 interference curves) WisePanda 5.37 / 16.53 / 25.42 / 37.57 / 52.54 / 64.40, best Top-1 SIS 7.34, next-best Top-50 seriesGAN 38.28; Wood670 (335 pairs) WisePanda 1.89 / 10.14 / 17.25 / 24.31 / 31.24 / 35.61, best Top-1 Event-DTW 2.84. Eleven curve-matching and generative baselines are compared (DTW, FMM, SIS, Event-DTW, Drop-DTW, Modified COW, two-stage DTW, GAN, seriesGAN, DDPM, Diffusion-TS). Status 2026-10-28: no later result on these sets was found; the bamboo-slip papers of Sept-Oct 2026 work on other material (ordering of excavated Chu slips, point-cloud registration).
targets.success_criterion: On Bamboo1350 built exactly as get_topk_accuracy_with_extend in algorithm/method_comparison.ipynb at commit af79b052 but with extend_number = 1114 for every method (all 1,114 interference curves, so 1,232 candidates on each side), a frozen 1,232 x 1,232 distance matrix D, whose hash is committed before scoring, in the notebook's order (row i is top candidate i: the 118 real top curves, channel 2 of vector_real_118_patch.npy, then the 1,114 rows of interference_data_bamboo.npy; column j is bottom candidate j: the 118 real bottom curves, channel 3, then the same 1,114 curves; a smaller D[i][j] means a better match, as in the notebook's ascending sort), must give two-direction Top-10 strictly above 25.42% AND Top-50 strictly above 52.54% (WisePanda, Nat. Commun. 2026, Table 1, re-read before claiming), with ties broken pessimistically (a true mate tied with other candidates is ranked after all of them), AND both strictly above the verifier's pessimistic-tie re-score of the three released WisePanda weight pairs (algorithm/models/normal/f_model_wisepanda{1,2,3}.pth with c_model_wisepanda{1,2,3}.pth) at extend_number = 1114, averaged over the three. The method never uses the real pairing: no training, tuning, threshold choice or model selection may use any information about which real top curve belongs to which real bottom curve (vector_real_118_patch.npy, vector_real_335_patch.npy, the Bamboo236 images and file names). Real curves may be used without pair information, synthetic data (vector_reallike_6000.npy or the claimant's own generator) freely.

partial_wins.statement: Wood670 (vector_real_335_patch.npy, no interference curves, 670 two-direction queries): Top-10 strictly above 17.25% and Top-50 strictly above 31.24%, same no-pairing rule and pessimistic ties.
Bamboo1350 at extend_number = 1114: Top-1 strictly above 7.34% (SIS, the best Top-1 in Table 1) and Top-5 strictly above 16.53% (WisePanda), same rules.
Bamboo236 (no interference curves): Top-20 strictly above 66.81% and Top-50 strictly above 91.81%, same rules.

targets.verification_method: The verifier clones github.com/zhujinchi/wisepanda at the recorded commit, checks the sha256 of the .npy files, rebuilds the candidate pools from the notebook's recipe (channels 2:4 of the real array, interference curves appended to both sides), checks the matrix hash against the commitment, and recomputes two-direction Top-k with pessimistic tie-breaking with independent code. It re-scores the released WisePanda weights the same way (torch.load with weights_only=True, in a sandbox) and reads the claimant's code to confirm no pair information enters training or selection. Minutes on a laptop.
angles: Ensemble the learned similarity with classical curve matchers: SIS has the best Top-1 on Bamboo1350 and Modified COW the best classical Top-50 on Bamboo236, so their errors differ from WisePanda's.

Global assignment: each real top has at most one bottom, so a bipartite matching (Hungarian or Sinkhorn) over the score matrix, re-ranked by its marginals, can suppress interference curves that attract many queries.
Hubness reduction (CSLS or mutual-nearest-neighbour scaling) on the distance matrix is cheap and often lifts Top-k in large candidate pools.
Improve the synthetic generator: fit the fracture-model parameters to real curve statistics without pair information (allowed), as the paper's genetic_param module does.
pitfalls: The notebook's ranking is optimistic on ties (the true distance's index in the sorted list): a constant matrix scores 100%. The criterion uses pessimistic ties; re-score every baseline that way.

In the released notebook the WisePanda cell builds 'Bamboo1350' with extend_number = 1000 while every other method uses 1114; the stored WisePanda numbers (52.54 Top-50) may therefore come from a 1,118-candidate pool (the notebook keeps no execution counts to tell). The criterion uses 1114 for all methods and re-scores the released WisePanda weights at 1114.
Wood3833 cannot be rebuilt from the repository: it ships 2,259 wood interference curves, while the paper uses 3,163.
Pair identity is encoded in the array index (row i top matches row i bottom) and in the Bamboo236 file names (N_1.png, N_2.png); any training or selection on those rows is label use.
Orientation (upper or lower part) is given by the archaeologists; no other metadata may be used.
There are only 118 bamboo pairs: one extra hit moves two-direction Top-k by 0.42 points, so report bootstrap intervals over pairs.
The .pth weights are pickles; load them with weights_only=True in a sandbox.

targets.name: Medieval manuscript dating (ICDAR 2017 CLaMM tasks 3 and 4): beat 59.0% and 49.9% date-class accuracy on the released test sets
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (about 12 GB of TIFF and JPEG page images; a GPU helps); scoring needs only two CSV files
targets.statement: The ICDAR 2017 Competition on the Classification of Medieval Handwritings in Latin Script (CLaMM; Cloppet, Eglin, Helias-Baron, Kieu, Stutzmann and Vincent, ICDAR 2017, pp. 1371-1376, doi 10.1109/ICDAR.2017.224) set four tasks on a 3,540-image training set: script class (tasks 1 and 2) and date class (15 classes from 500 to 1600 CE; task 3 on 2,000 clean 300-dpi greyscale TIFFs, task 4 on 1,000 images of varied formats and resolutions). Best published accuracies, tasks 1 to 4: 85.2% (Tensmeyer, T-DeepCNN), 76.5% (Christlein and Kestemont, method 2), 59.0% (T-DeepCNN) and 49.9% (Christlein and Kestemont, method 2), as tabulated in the survey of Nikolaidou, Seuret, Mokayed and Liwicki (arXiv 2203.08504v3). The full dataset, with the test ground truth and all competitors' output matrices, is on Zenodo (record 5527690, doi 10.5281/zenodo.5527690, CC BY 4.0, deposited 2021-09-25 by Stutzmann and Helias-Baron). Re-scored on 2026-10-29 from those files (argmax of each belonging matrix, columns in header order where the file has a header): task 3, Tensmeyer's T-DeepCNN (a residual CNN on 227x227 patches averaged per image) 1,181 of 2,000 = 0.5905, adjacent-class 0.8865; Christlein and Kestemont method 2 0.5485 (method 1 0.5415, method 3 0.5255); Pondenkandath 0.4980. Task 4: Christlein and Kestemont method 2 499 of 1,000 = 0.499 (its matrix orders columns DATE_TYPE1, DATE_TYPE10, ..., DATE_TYPE9, as its header says), Tensmeyer 0.480. One task-3 ground-truth row names IRHT_P_009783.tif, but the zip ships that image as IRHT_P_009793.tif, the name all four task-3 output files use; Tensmeyer's prediction for it is wrong, so its 1,181 stands either way. Status 2026-10-28: no later result on the official task 3 or task 4 test sets was found. Later dating work on CLaMM data uses other splits or metrics (the 2024 'deep-dating' models on Hugging Face use 5-fold cross-validation; a 2023 DenseNet study by Boudraa and Bennour reports cumulative score and MAE; Studer et al., ICDAR 2019, reach at best 37.9% dating accuracy), and the ICDAR 2021 HDC dating task has its own test set scored by mean absolute error in years. The original site clamm.irht.cnrs.fr did not respond on 2026-10-29.
targets.success_criterion: Frozen prediction files (one date class from 1 to 15 per test image, hashes committed before scoring) for all 2,000 images of ICDAR2017_CLaMM_task1_task3 and all 1,000 images of ICDAR2017_CLaMM_task2_task4, scored against the DATE_ICDAR column of the zips' own @ICDAR2017_CLaMM_task1_task3.csv (sha256 adf733bf867b61820c89cb37b0318b21e4edfecffd783277886d0af503081d55) and @ICDAR2017_CLaMM_task2_task4.csv (sha256 25e4d61e1d90d76953f5fb9c311c09c8b1b020874902647a45683816e85343ad), with file names matched on the lower-cased stem and the ground-truth row IRHT_P_009783.tif scored as the image IRHT_P_009793.tif, must reach plain per-image accuracy strictly above 0.5905 on task 3 (at least 1,182 of 2,000 correct; the record, Tensmeyer's T-DeepCNN, printed as 59.0%, re-scores to 1,181) AND strictly above 0.499 on task 4 (at least 500 of 1,000; Christlein and Kestemont method 2 re-scores to 499), both record values re-read from the competition paper or arXiv 2203.08504 and re-scored from the Zenodo output matrices before claiming. Training and model selection use only the ICDAR2017_CLaMM_Training images and labels; generic image models pretrained without any manuscript script or date labels are allowed and must be named; no test image is used for training or adaptation, and no other dated-manuscript collection (ICFHR 2016 CLaMM, ICDAR 2021 HDC, e-codices, IRHT or BnF metadata) may be used.

partial_wins.statement: Task 3 only: accuracy of at least 0.600 (1,200 of 2,000) on the 2,000 clean test images, same rules.
Task 4 only: accuracy of at least 0.510 (510 of 1,000) on the 1,000 varied test images, same rules.

Task 3: exact accuracy strictly above 0.5905 (at least 1,182 of 2,000) together with adjacent-class accuracy (prediction within one date class of the truth) strictly above 0.8865 (at least 1,774 of 2,000; Tensmeyer's re-scored value with the file-name mapping is 1,773), same rules.

targets.verification_method: The verifier fetches only the two ground-truth CSVs from the Zenodo zips by ranged GET (the central directory at the end of each zip gives the offsets; a few hundred kilobytes in all, no images), checks their sha256, checks the prediction files' hashes against the commitments, and recomputes exact and adjacent-class accuracy with independent code, matching file names on the lower-cased stem and scoring the ground-truth row IRHT_P_009783 as image IRHT_P_009793. It re-scores the competitors' matrices from ICDAR2017_CLaMM_outputs.zip (argmax per row, column order from each file's header where present) to confirm the record counts (task 3: 1,181 of 2,000; task 4: 499 of 1,000). Minutes.
angles: Modern self-supervised vision backbones on text-region patches with per-image aggregation; the 2017 winner trained a residual CNN from scratch on 227x227 patches.
Date classes are ordinal: train with ordinal losses or soft labels over neighbouring classes. Adjacent-class accuracy is already 0.886 on task 3, so most errors are one class off.
Use the script labels in the same CSVs as an auxiliary task; script and date are strongly correlated.
Task 4 images vary in format and colour: normalise resolution (estimate x-height) and convert to greyscale to match the training conditions.
pitfalls: File names differ in case and extension between ground truth and some outputs (.tif, .TIF, .jpg, .JPG): match on the lower-cased stem. One task-3 ground-truth row (IRHT_P_009783.tif) has no image of that name; the zip ships it as IRHT_P_009793.tif, which has no ground-truth row and which every 2017 task-3 output uses. Score the two as one image.

The output matrices do not share a column order: Christlein and Kestemont's method 2 and 3 files carry a header in lexicographic class order. Read headers, or re-scored records come out wrong (method 2 on task 4 scores 0.105 read in natural order and 0.499 read by its header).
Class sizes are uneven: class 10 has 352 of the 2,000 task-3 images, class 15 only 6 (4 in task 4).

The competition paper speaks of accuracy 'per date'; plain per-image accuracy reproduces 59.0% for task 3 from the released matrix (1,181 of 2,000 = 0.5905), while mean per-class recall is 0.494. The criterion is plain accuracy, with thresholds at the re-scored counts: 1,181 correct on task 3 or 499 on task 4 only ties the record.

Generic backbones pretrained on web images may have seen digitised pages of the same manuscripts, but never their labels; any model trained with manuscript date or script labels from outside the CLaMM 2017 training set is excluded.
The task 3 and task 4 zips are 3.1 and 3.3 GB and the training zip 5.5 GB; scoring needs only the CSVs inside.

ieeexplore.ieee.org (the competition paper) and link.springer.com answer plain fetches with an empty 202 or a JavaScript challenge; read the results in arXiv 2203.08504 or re-score the Zenodo matrices instead of getting around them. Two Springer chapters that cite the competition and date manuscript images could not be read for that reason: Boudraa and Bennour (ISPR 2023, reported elsewhere as cumulative score and MAE) and Sakout, Nait-Hamoud, Gahmousse, Djeddi and Ennaji ('Accurate Dating of Ancient Manuscripts with SIFT-CNN', 2025). Have a human check their protocols before claiming.

targets.name: Cuneiform language and dialect identification (VarDial 2019 CLI): beat NRC-CNRC's macro-F1 0.7695 on the released test set, closed track
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (about 5 MB of Unicode cuneiform lines)
targets.statement: The Cuneiform Language Identification shared task (VarDial 2019; organiser Tommi Jauhiainen, dataset by Jauhiainen, Jauhiainen, Alstola and Linden, W19-1409; campaign report Zampieri et al., W19-1401) asks which of seven varieties a line of Unicode cuneiform belongs to: Sumerian or one of six Akkadian dialects (Old Babylonian, Middle Babylonian peripheral, Standard Babylonian, Neo-Babylonian, Late Babylonian, Neo-Assyrian), built from Oracc transliterations. The data (github.com/tosaja/CLI2019, commit 2f82d58b of 2019-07-08; CLIdata.zip git blob ce86e5a4, sha256 9fe02f82e76a53c51638079291406b9e24fb5977f03aad55ba678c45ee32b7e1; CC BY-SA 3.0) hold 139,421 training lines, 4,676 development lines and a balanced test set of 6,895 lines (985 per variety) with gold labels (gold.txt, gold.labels). Official metric: macro-averaged F1 over the seven classes. Record: NRC-CNRC (Bernier-Colborne, Goutte and Leger, W19-1402; code github.com/gbcolborne/lang_id), a character-level BERT pretrained on the task data with a second unsupervised pretraining phase on the unlabelled test lines, macro-F1 0.7695 (accuracy 0.7711); runner-up tearsofjoy (linear SVM with language-model adaptation) 0.7632; best non-adaptive run 0.7511. Status 2026-10-28: no closed-track result above 0.7695 on the official test set was found; SharifCL's 2020 write-up (arXiv 2009.10794) reports 0.7210, and an IJICT 2024 paper's 96% is on its own oversampled random re-split, not on the official test set.
targets.success_criterion: A frozen label file for all 6,895 lines of CLIdata/test.txt (order preserved, hash committed before scoring) with macro-F1 strictly above 0.7695 against CLIdata/gold.labels (sklearn f1_score with average='macro' over the seven labels), under the 2019 closed-track rules: training and tuning use only CLIdata train.txt and dev.txt; the unlabelled test lines may be used for unsupervised adaptation, as the 2019 winner did, but no gold label is read before the file is frozen; no external data of any kind, including Oracc, CDLI, eBL or ePSD texts (the test lines come from Oracc) and any pretrained model trained on anything other than CLIdata. Code and seeds are published.

partial_wins.statement: Non-transductive: macro-F1 strictly above 0.7632 (the runner-up's test-adapted SVM) without using the test lines in any way before the label file is frozen, same closed-track rules.

Hardest classes: F1 strictly above NRC-CNRC's class-wise F1 on both Standard Babylonian (0.5705) and Neo-Babylonian (0.6500) (Table 3 of W19-1402), with overall macro-F1 of at least 0.7600, same rules.

targets.verification_method: The verifier fetches CLIdata.zip from github.com/tosaja/CLI2019 (checks the blob id and sha256), checks the label file's hash against the commitment, and recomputes macro-F1 and per-class F1 with sklearn and with independent code. It reads the published code to confirm that only CLIdata train and dev (and, for the full win, unlabelled test text) are used, and may re-train once (laptop-hours) to confirm the frozen file comes from the stated system. Scoring takes seconds.
angles: Character n-gram SVM and naive Bayes ensembles with test-set language-model adaptation (tearsofjoy, 0.7632) are within 0.007 of the record; combine them with a small character transformer and calibrate the ensemble on dev.
Deduplicate the training lines first (NRC did): many lines repeat across varieties, so keep label distributions for duplicates rather than one label.
Short lines dominate the error: 1,922 test lines have 5 signs or fewer; back off to dev-tuned class priors for very short lines.
Unsupervised adaptation on the unlabelled test lines (allowed for the full win) gave NRC most of its margin over non-adaptive runs.
pitfalls: 638 of the 6,895 test lines occur verbatim in train or dev, and 104 of those carry a different or additional label there; 12 distinct test texts occur twice in the test set with different gold labels, so 100% is unreachable.
External cuneiform corpora contain the test lines (all from Oracc); using them, or a pretrained model that saw them, breaks the closed track and leaks labels.

Dev and test contain no line shorter than 3 signs while train has 31,706 such lines, and dev is balanced while train is not (38% Sumerian); NRC found cross-validation on train plus dev, with folds built to match, more reliable than the official dev set alone.
Random re-splits with oversampling inflate scores (IJICT 2024 reports 96%); only the official test labels count.
The criterion is macro-F1 over seven balanced classes, not accuracy.

targets.name: Greek inscriptions (I.PHI): beat Ithaca's region (70.8% top-1) and date (29.3 years) attribution on the PHI-digit-3 test split
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (178,551 inscriptions in a 217 MB JSON; released checkpoints about 0.2 GB each; a GPU helps)
targets.statement: Ithaca (Assael, Sommerschield, Shillingford, Bordbar, Pavlopoulos, Chatzipanagiotou, Androutsopoulos, Prag and de Freitas, Nature 603, 2022, doi 10.1038/s41586-022-04448-z) attributes Greek inscriptions to region and date. Table 1 (I.PHI test set, n = 7,811 inscriptions, PHI ids ending in 3): region top-1 70.8% / top-3 82.1% over 84 regions, date distance 29.3 years; onomastics baseline 21.2% / 26.5% and 144.4 years. No later system has beaten these on a shared protocol: Cullhed (arXiv 2409.13870v3; Digital Scholarship in the Humanities 41(1), 2026) reports 75.0% / 83.7% and 37.1 years on his own 95/5 split but lower attribution than Ithaca on a shared test set; Locaputo, Brunello, Saccomanno, Platanou and Serra ('Ithaca Revisited', LREC 2026) recompute Ithaca at 71.11% / 81.70% and 33.98 years on inputs with artificial gaps, against 59.02% / 69.66% and 44.78 years for GPT-5 with retrieval-augmented prompting; Stoicheia (arXiv 2608.07249) and Apollo Restore (arXiv 2609.22455) do restoration only. The current I.PHI release (storage.googleapis.com/ithaca-resources/models/iphi.json, 216,735,767 bytes, md5 7876f27fe7881bd5c1962e54f83cee1b, last modified 2025-06-24) holds 178,551 records, 17,789 with id % 10 == 3; it is not the 2022 snapshot (78,608 inscriptions), so Table 1's test set cannot be rebuilt exactly. Released checkpoints: Ithaca's checkpoint_v1.pkl (202,256,537 bytes, 2022-01-19) for github.com/google-deepmind/ithaca, and the Greek Aeneas-framework model ithaca_153143996_2.pkl (142,485,416 bytes, 2025-06-24) for predictingthepast, with no published attribution numbers. Status 2026-10-28: open; google-deepmind/ithaca last changed on 2026-10-27 (inference now lower-cases its input; the beam-search fix concerns restoration only).
targets.success_criterion: On iphi.json (md5 7876f27fe7881bd5c1962e54f83cee1b), the test list T is every record with int(id) % 10 == 3 whose text, after deleting whitespace and the characters '-', '#' and '_', has at least 50 characters (7,684 records); the region list T_r is the records of T whose region_sub, mapped by region_name_filter of predictingthepast/util/region_names.py at a recorded commit, is one of the 82 names of train/data/iphi-region-sub.txt mapped the same way (7,464 records); the dating list T_d is the records of T with numeric date_min <= date_max, both inside [-800, 800] (4,682 records). The verifier recomputes all three lists. Every system reads only the record's text, in one of two preparations named before scoring: (G) as google-deepmind/ithaca train/dataloader.py prepares a record with char_use_guess=True, the setting behind Table 1: '[' and ']' deleted and the editorial supplements between them kept as letters; or (M) as predictingthepast train/dataloader.py prepares a test record: each [...] replaced by '-' of the same length, any remaining '[' or ']' deleted, then GreekAlphabet.filter. A frozen predictions file, whose hash is committed before scoring, ranks the 82 regions for every record of T_r and gives one point date for every record of T_d. Full win: region top-1 strictly above 70.8% AND mean date error strictly below 29.3 years (Ithaca, Nature 2022, Table 1, re-read before claiming; date error is 0 inside [date_min, date_max], else the distance to the nearer bound), AND, on each of the two metrics, strictly better than the better of the two released checkpoints on that metric. The claimant publishes the checkpoints' frozen predictions on the same lists (hashes committed before scoring), made as follows: checkpoint_v1.pkl with google-deepmind/ithaca on (G) and ithaca_153143996_2.pkl with predictingthepast on (M), commits recorded; a prepared text of 768 or more characters is cut to its first 767 characters, and one shorter than Ithaca's 50-character minimum is right-padded with '-' to 50 characters; predicted regions are mapped to the 82 names with region_name_filter, and unmappable predictions never count as correct; a checkpoint's point date is its predictive mean (date_pred_avg of predicted_dates in the repository's util/eval.py), the quantity Table 1 scores. Training uses only I.PHI records with id % 10 not in {3, 4} (digit 4 for model selection) plus public non-epigraphic Greek text, all listed with hashes; none of it may be a test record or a near-duplicate of one (same normalised text, or a shared run of 60 or more consecutive normalised characters with a record of T; normalised means the raw iphi.json text lower-cased, with whitespace and the characters '-', '#', '_', '[' and ']' deleted), so a model initialised from either released checkpoint cannot claim the full win; models whose pretraining data is undisclosed cannot claim the full win.

partial_wins.statement: One task only, same lists, preparations and baseline rules: region top-1 strictly above 70.8% with top-3 strictly above 82.1%, or mean date error strictly below 29.3 years, each named metric also strictly better than the better of the two released checkpoints on that metric on the same records.

Region top-1 at least 2 points above, or mean date error at least 2 years below, the better of the two released checkpoints on that metric on the same lists, with a paired bootstrap over inscriptions giving p < 0.01, same rules (the Table 1 value need not be beaten).

targets.verification_method: The verifier downloads iphi.json (md5 check) and, at the recorded predictingthepast commit, iphi-region-sub.txt and region_names.py; it regenerates T, T_r and T_d, checks the prediction files' hashes against the commitments, rescores region top-1 and top-3 and mean date error with independent code, re-runs both released checkpoints on a random 300 records in a sandbox, each with its stated preparation, the 767-character cut, the '-' padding and the predictive-mean date, to confirm the baseline files (CPU, under an hour), reads the claimant's code to confirm which preparation its system reads, and scans the published training manifest for test ids and near-duplicates. No retraining.
angles: Fine-tune a public Greek character model with region and date heads; the documentary-clean Stoicheia backbone (Ericu950/Stoicheia-doc_clean) never saw documentary texts and is open.

Dialect spellings, letter forms transcribed as spellings, formulae and personal names localise inscriptions; nearest-neighbour retrieval over the training digits by character n-grams is a strong baseline to ensemble with.
For dating, predict a distribution over ten-year bins and output the year minimising expected distance to the true range.
Use region_main (15 macro-regions) as an auxiliary target.
pitfalls: iphi.json (2025) is not the 2022 I.PHI: Table 1's n = 7,811 cannot be rebuilt, so only checkpoints re-scored on the same lists make a beat meaningful.

6,131 of the 7,684 T texts carry editorial supplements in square brackets (27% of their non-space characters). Ithaca read them as letters (train/config.py char_use_guess=True, the setting behind Table 1); predictingthepast replaces them with '-'. A system that reads supplements set beside a baseline that masks them is not a like-for-like comparison, hence the fixed preparations (G) and (M). 210 T texts have unbalanced brackets, so apply each dataloader's steps literally.

Both inference codes reject inputs of 768 or more characters ('Input text too long'): 662 T texts under (G), 663 under (M). Ithaca's also rejects inputs under 50 characters: 40 T texts under (G). The criterion fixes a 767-character cut and '-' padding so the baseline files are reproducible; the claimant's own system may read whole texts.

checkpoint_v1.pkl predicts the 2022 subregions (84 regions in the paper; 88 entries in google-deepmind/ithaca train/data/iphi-region-sub.txt) while predictingthepast's iphi-region-sub.txt lists 82; map by name with region_name_filter and count unmappable predictions as misses, for the claimant too.
Dates in the test digit run from -750 to 1881; records outside [-800, 800] are excluded from T_d.

One stone can carry several PHI ids (re-editions): 201 T records have an exact textual twin under an id of another digit (172 in a training digit; 223 counting twins inside digit 3), which the released checkpoints may have been trained on (predictingthepast drops repeated texts, keeping the lowest id). Report results with and without them. Under the near-duplicate rule, with '[' and ']' deleted as the criterion's normalisation says, 5,577 training-digit records (3.9%) share a 60-character run with a record of T and 5,687 must be dropped in all (recounted 2026-10-30); keeping the brackets finds only 2,167, so normalise exactly as stated.
PHI texts and their dates are on the open web; models with undisclosed pretraining may have memorised them.
Ithaca Revisited's 71.11% and 33.98 years were measured on inputs with artificial gaps, not on full texts; don't mix protocols.
Released checkpoints are Python pickles; load them only in a sandbox.

targets.name: Herculaneum 9 µm ink detection on a never-seen scroll: beat every public 9 µm model's AUC on the three human-labelled PHerc. 0841 segments (9.366 µm / 113 keV) with a model that never saw PHerc. 0841
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (one consumer GPU with 12-16 GB: a 40k-78k-iteration run of the ink_9um architecture takes about 3-10 GPU-hours; streams tens of GB of public surface volumes from S3; scoring the three segments is laptop-minutes)
targets.statement: Most still-unread prize volumes only have native 8.6-9.4 µm scans (the Reader v2 README counts 20 of 22 First Letters scrolls without a 2.4 µm scan). That makes the team's 9 µm surface-render ink models the working tool for First Letters searches. Cross-scroll generalization is a named bottleneck on scrollprize.org/2026_open_problems (updated 2026-10-14): 'Ink models may work on one scroll but not another'. The released models (huggingface.co/scrollprize/ink_9um, MIT, 14 checkpoints = 2 seeds x 7 steps, 2026-08-14) were trained on aligned labels from PHerc. 0139, 1667, Paris 4 and 0814 plus 5 native 0139 segments. They ship no metrics, and the model card calls them 'far from optimized'. TEST SET (S3 listings fetched 2026-10-29, HTTP 200): PHerc0841 is on neither the Grand Prize list nor the First Letters list. It has a 9.366 µm / 113 keV scan (volumes/20250821151531-9.366um-1.2m-113keV-masked.zarr) and a 2.403 µm / 77 keV scan (20260319124803). Its three official segments are 20260220213127-w00, 20260220214732-auto_grown_20260220144552896 ('ag144') and 20260221022814-auto_grown_20260220174252405 ('ag174'). Each has tifxyz meshes on both scans, a 9.366 µm surface volume (surface-volumes/9.366um-1.2m-113keV-volume-20250821151531.zarr), the team's 2.4 µm ink map (ink-detection/...new_canon_autoresearch_recipe-tile256-stride128.tif) and human ink labels version 20260918. The labels are ink-labels/2.403um-volume-20260319124803/20260918/{inklabels,supervision,validation}.zarr: uint8 OME-Zarr 0.5 on the 2.403 µm render canvas, 16460 x 18560 px for w00, uploaded 2026-09-22. CURRENT STATE on these three segments (none of the models below trained on PHerc0841, except possibly Hecate; the TRACE checkpoints were selected on it). khj1222/vesuvius-challenge docs/32 (2026-10-28; AUC against the human labels inside the supervision mask, forward layer order): ink_9um seed43 step-075000 scores 0.772 / 0.681 / 0.756 (w00 / ag144 / ag174) and Reader V3 0.916 / 0.834 / 0.853 (mean 0.868). The Reader V3 repo's own suite (results/suite_*.json, 2026-10-20): Reader V3 0.8805 / 0.8258 / 0.8372 (w00 / ag1 / ag2, mean 0.8478); Hecate 9.6 µm 0.8774 / 0.7976 / 0.8962 (mean 0.8571); Reader v2 0.8192 / 0.8581 / 0.8145 (mean 0.8306); the v8-in-style 'base21' mean 0.8042. Background marked as ink at 80% human-label recall on ag1 / ag2 / w00 is 32.3 / 22.7 / 18.8% for V3 and 39.4 / 14.8 / 17.8% for Hecate. The Reader v2 README (2026-09-27) gives 3-segment AUC against the human labels: v2 0.824, Hecate 0.855, Nieuwlaar dense-native 0.800, ink9um-dense 0.771, best of the 14 ink_9um checkpoints 0.733, and 0.866 for its 'with Hecate' mean of v2 and Hecate. Against the team's 2.4 µm map: v2 0.858, Hecate 0.848. The two harnesses differ by about 0.04 AUC on the same model (V3 on w00: 0.916 vs 0.881). TRACE (github.com/Jashann/vesuvius-scrolling, release v1.0 of 2026-09-29, weights CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) fine-tunes ink_9um seed42 step-075000 on native 9.362 µm PHerc0139/0814 renders with the team's 2.4 µm maps as soft targets (v3 adds PHerc0009B, PHerc0343P and PHerc0500P2). Its MODEL_CARD gives AUC against the human labels on w00 / ag144 / ag174 of 0.868 / 0.862 / 0.837 for v3B (v3A 0.866 / 0.860 / 0.832, sB 0.857 / 0.839 / 0.817) and discloses that every TRACE checkpoint was selected on these three segments plus PHerc0139 w043, so PHerc0841 is 'never trained on', not 'never looked at'. A-hn (huggingface.co/Prodigle/pherc0306b-ink-ahn, 2026-10-28, three fine-tunes of v8-in) reports AUC 0.845 on PHerc0841 known text, and its product with TRACE v3B (two networks) 0.874. These figures are therefore context only; the bar is re-measured under one pinned protocol. Hecate's card names the scrollprize/datasets bucket and 'existing ink annotations' as its supervision, and that bucket's ink/ tree holds an 841/ folder (these three segments, with v2 supervision and validation masks), so Hecate may have seen PHerc0841. CAMERA TRUTH (p1): DomRusso2/ir-truth-9um (2026-10-21, commit 7e96b96) placed the team's 1050 nm infrared photo of PHerc0343P and the team-traced letters (dl.ash2txt.org/fragments/PHerc0343P/paths/2um_front_surface/) onto the 8.64 µm / 116 keV surface volume of segment 20250511003658 (canvas 3440 x 2060, 31 layers). Its results/scores.json gives AUC against the camera: team 2.2 µm model map 0.909, Reader v2 0.834 (trained on PHerc0343P), Reader V3 0.774 (trained on this segment), v8-in 0.744 (never trained on the fragment), Hecate 9.6 µm 0.721. The best of 2000 random placements reaches 0.65-0.71, p = 0.0005. LEAVE-ONE-SCROLL-OUT (p2): khj1222 docs/15 and docs/26 retrained the ink_9um recipe without PHerc1667 (about 3 h per seed on an RTX 5090). With the threshold calibrated on pherc1667-w013 and then frozen, mean F1 on w023 / w028 / w029 / w031 is 0.5306 (both seeds). Fine-tuning on one annotated 1667 segment (w018) reaches 0.6293. CREDITS: the Vesuvius Challenge team (scans, segments, labels, ink_9um, Hecate, the canonical 2.4 µm model); Domenico Russo / KLAVIS (Reader v2, Reader V3, ink9um-dense, ir-truth-9um); the khj1222 repository (validation harness, LOSO arms, docs/32; its work matches the progress prizes credited to Hyojun Kwon on scrollprize.org/winners); Youssef Nader (v8-in); Erwin Nieuwlaar (dense-native); Jashanjot Singh Gill and Nhat Nam Tran (TRACE); Liam Warner and Nicola Bodill (A-hn). DATA: CC BY-NC 4.0 plus the dl.ash2txt.org/LICENSE.txt terms (no redistribution, no publicising hidden text). A human must accept these terms before any download.
targets.success_criterion: PROTOCOL '0841-9um' (pinned). score_0841.py is written by the scout on day 1 and frozen by sha256 in a hash-locked METRIC.sha256 before any model is scored. Input: one ink map per segment on the 9.366 µm canvas, computed only from the official surface-volumes/9.366um-1.2m-113keV-volume-20250821151531.zarr; depth window, layer order and flip-TTA are declared in the attempt manifest. Mapping: label-canvas pixels go to the map canvas by the ratio of the two published tifxyz grid scales (meta.json 'scale'), with bilinear sampling. One integer offset per segment is fixed before any scoring by phase correlation of the two official surface volumes' middle layers, never by a model score. Metrics: (1) ROC AUC (ties averaged) of the map against inklabels > 0 over pixels with supervision > 0 (primary); (2) the same AUC over validation > 0 pixels (robustness); (3) FA80 = fraction of label-0 supervised pixels at or above the threshold that recalls 80% of ink pixels, averaged over the three segments. GATE A (baselines). In a hash-locked BASELINES.json the scout scores, under this exact protocol and in both layer orders (each model keeps its better order per segment, which favours the baselines): Reader V3 (domenicor046/reader-v3 @ aee1d64), Reader v2 step-040000, Hecate 9.6 µm (renders resampled to 9.6 µm as its card requires), v8-in (YoussefMoNader/ink-8um-v8in), all 14 ink_9um checkpoints, ink9um-dense w016excluded step075000, Nieuwlaar dense-native, TRACE sA, sB, v3A and v3B (Jashann/vesuvius-scrolling release v1.0, sha256 as in its MODEL_CARD), A-hn seeds 0-2 (Prodigle/pherc0306b-ink-ahn) and any other public single-network 9 µm ink checkpoint the scout finds on the day BASELINES.json is frozen. Definitions: B_s = best baseline AUC on segment s; B_mean = best baseline 3-segment mean; F_min = lowest baseline FA80; V_s = best baseline validation-region AUC. GATE B (leakage). leak_audit.py over the training manifest and the whole initialisation and teacher chain must find: no PHerc0841 path or hash (CT, renders, meshes, labels, team ink maps, predictions, pseudo-labels); no initialisation from Hecate or ink_canonical_2um (their documented supervision is the ink bucket that holds 841/) or from anything fine-tuned from them, from any TRACE checkpoint (selected on PHerc0841 labels), or from any other network whose training read PHerc0841 bytes or whose checkpoint, layer order or depth window was chosen on PHerc0841 scores; networks trained only on other scrolls' renders and team 2.4 µm maps (ink9um-dense, Reader v2, Reader V3) are allowed starts; teacher outputs used only on other scrolls. GATE C (selection). One network, no ensemble of separately trained networks. Its checkpoint sha256, layer order and TTA are declared before the first PHerc0841 inference. Every PHerc0841 scoring is appended to EVALS_0841.log, and the count is reported. GATE D (nulls). The same weights, with the declared TTA, on the reversed layer order and on a seeded z-shuffled layer order give AUC <= 0.65 on every segment (a network trained on, or averaged over, both layer orders therefore fails this gate). SUCCESS requires all of: mean AUC >= B_mean + 0.03; AUC >= B_s on at least two of the three segments and >= B_s - 0.01 on the third; FA80 <= F_min; validation-region AUC >= V_s - 0.01 on every segment. This is an internal benchmark. It is credited officially only if scrollprize.org/winners credits a Progress Prize submission made by the human.

partial_wins.statement: Camera truth at 116 keV. A single network obeying Gates B-C, extended to PHerc0343 and PHerc0343P: no CT, render, label or map bytes of either, and no initialisation from Reader v2, Reader V3 or any other weights whose training names PHerc0343P. Run on the official 8.64 µm / 116 keV surface volume of PHerc0343P segment 20250511003658 (3440 x 2060 map, declared layer order), it must score AUC >= 0.83 against the camera masks of DomRusso2/ir-truth-9um @ 7e96b96 (data/truth_ink.png against data/truth_noink.png inside data/valid.png; sha256 recorded by the scout), with the 2000-random-placement control at p <= 0.001. The skeptic recomputes this with a numpy re-implementation of scripts/score_map.py. For context: the best fragment-naive model, v8-in, scores 0.744 and the team's 2.2 µm map 0.909.

Leave-1667-out at a frozen threshold. A single network trained with zero PHerc1667 bytes: the ink_9um labels minus the six 1667 representations, plus any non-1667 data, with initialisation only from weights whose documented training excludes PHerc1667 (every released ink_9um, Reader and Hecate checkpoint saw 1667). Its 8-bit maps on the aligned 1667 segments are thresholded at the lowest exact maximiser of pooled F1 on pherc1667-w013 (integers 0-255, positive = score >= threshold, unique-pixel counting as in khj1222 docs/26). Mean F1 over pherc1667-w023, w028, w029 and w031 must be >= 0.5806 (= the docs/26 LOSO base 0.5306 + 0.05). Gate: the scout first reproduces the docs/26 base 0.5306 within 0.005 with the same scorer, from khj1222's archived predictions or a retrained LOSO arm.

targets.verification_method: After the human has accepted the data terms, the skeptic fetches the three segments' 20260918 label zarrs (about 1 MB) and checks their sha256 against the scout's record. The skeptic then: (1) checks METRIC.sha256 and BASELINES.json; (2) recomputes AUC, validation AUC and FA80 for the frozen claimed maps and for two baselines' stored maps, requiring |difference| < 1e-6; (3) re-runs the claimed checkpoint on one seeded segment at the declared settings (minutes on a consumer GPU, about an hour on CPU or MPS) and requires Pearson r > 0.99 with the frozen map; (4) recomputes the reversed and z-shuffled nulls on that segment; (5) runs leak_audit.py over the training manifest and initialisation chain; (6) before any claim, re-reads the S3 PHerc0841 listings, the HF ink bucket, scrollprize.org/prizes and /winners, khj1222 docs/32, the Reader V3 repo, the Jashann/vesuvius-scrolling releases and the Hugging Face ink-model listings for newer models. For p1 the skeptic recomputes the AUC and the random-placement p from the frozen map. For p2 the skeptic recomputes the w013 threshold and the four F1 values from the frozen 8-bit maps.
angles: Start from Reader V3, whose train_config names no PHerc0841 data, or from Reader v2 (both allowed by Gate B; TRACE checkpoints are not). Train further with larger tiles and stronger 113 keV augmentation in one declared layer order: training on both orders, or averaging both at inference, fails Gate D. p1 needs a start free of 0343P, such as ink_9um or v8-in.
Distil an ensemble into one network on non-0841 renders: Reader V3, v8-in and ink_9um checkpoint averages. In the KLAVIS suite, the mean of v2 and Hecate beats either model alone.

Build dense native-scan labels from the team's 2.4 µm maps on objects scanned at both resolutions (Reader v2 used six), and add them to the ink_9um corpus. Add scan-protocol randomisation: blur, contrast, decohesion and noise.
Fix a label-free layer-order rule on non-0841 data before scoring, for example taking the order whose output is more spread out, as reported for ink_9um on the project Discord.
For p2, follow the docs/26 calibration rule exactly and report seeds separately.
pitfalls: Never compare with the published AUCs: two harnesses on the native 9.366 µm renders disagree by about 0.04 on the same map (Reader V3 on w00: 0.881 in its own suite, 0.916 in khj1222 docs/32), and khj1222 docs/33 and docs/35 (2026-10-29/30) report Reader V3 at 0.930 / 0.859 / 0.862 and ink_9um seed43 at 0.891 / 0.800 / 0.820 on level-2 renders of the 2.403 µm scan, which is not this protocol's input. Only BASELINES.json under the frozen script counts.
The 2.4 µm and 9 µm canvases are not a pure rescale: DomRusso2 and the khj1222 notes on villa #2243 report an extra 6-8 px shift. Fix the offset once from CT-to-CT alignment, never per model.
Reversed layer order collapses AUC to about 0.54-0.62 for every model. Declare the order rule before any 0841 inference.

Hecate and ink_canonical_2um were trained on the ink bucket that holds 841/, the TRACE checkpoints were selected on PHerc0841, and Reader v2, Reader V3 and TRACE v3A/v3B were trained on PHerc0343P. Using Hecate, ink_canonical_2um or TRACE as initialisation voids the main claim; using Reader v2, Reader V3 or TRACE v3 voids p1.
Choosing checkpoints, thresholds, directions or depth windows by 0841 scores is test-set selection. EVALS_0841.log is reported with every claim.
The human labels were drawn on CT renders and the team's 2.4 µm maps, so AUC measures agreement with annotators. That is why p1 adds a camera truth.
Label smoothing 0.5 puts outputs at about 0.25-0.75. AUC is unaffected, but FA80 thresholds must be recomputed for each model.

Data terms: a human accepts the Vesuvius Challenge terms (CC BY-NC 4.0; dl.ash2txt.org/LICENSE.txt) before any download. Agents never accept terms, never redistribute labels or renders, and never post ink images of unread scrolls.

targets.name: Scroll CT compression with random access: beat volcomp's rate-distortion on its 54 held-out PHerc. Paris 4 2.4 µm 128³ chunks while every chunk stays independently decodable
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (CPU only; the held-out set is 54 raw uint8 128³ chunks, 108 MiB, read directly from the public S3 zarr)
targets.statement: Data scale is a named bottleneck on scrollprize.org/2026_open_problems: large scroll volumes reach dozens of terabytes. At level 0 the PHercParis4 2.4 µm masked volume alone is 75784 x 32693 x 32693 uint8 voxels, stored as raw uncompressed 128³ zarr v2 chunks (.zarray fetched 2026-10-29). volcomp (Forrest McDonald; github.com/SuperOptimizer/volume-compressor, MIT; the README introduces the C library as version 1.3.0, format revision 4, while head 81f6519 of 2026-10-13 also documents format revision 5 / volcomp 1.4.0 typed chunks for non-u8 data, with the u8 tANS tables unchanged) won a September 2026 Progress Prize as 'a chunked compressor for scroll CT and model predictions, now supported in VC3D'. It codes 16³ blocks with a 3-D DCT, a dead-zone quantiser and tANS into independently decodable 128³ chunks inside zarr v3 shards, and its mirror of all 39 samples is at dl.ash2txt.org/community-uploads/forrest/volcomp/. Its docs/BENCHMARKS.md (lossy 2026-09-01, lossless 2026-09-07; unchanged at head commit 81f6519, fetched 2026-10-29) uses two sets of 54 chunks. A tune set serves every design choice.
