A held-out set (corpus/manifest_heldout.tsv: 41 chunks at level 0, 9 at level 1, 4 at level 2, including one contiguous 2x2x2 octet) is touched only for the published numbers. Held-out ratio / PSNR / SSIM at q 2, 4, 8, 16, 32: 17.56 / 41.33 dB / .9840; 30.05 / 38.04 / .9700; 52.92 / 35.00 / .9463; 95.58 / 32.22 / .9088; 176.5 / 29.67 / .8532 (one thread, AVX2; decode 702-2484 MB/s). The optional volcomp_deblock() post-filter adds up to 0.42 dB (q8: 35.17 dB / .9494). The predecessor codec c5d is 0.6-6.9% larger at the same q. The open part comes from the interim comparison in docs/SUBMISSION_2026-09.md section 5 (four 512³ cubes, contended timings). Inter-frame video codecs need fewer bits at 35 dB: SVT-AV1 0.53-0.86x volcomp's bits (0.69x on the 2.40 µm cube), x265 0.71-0.99x, aom 0.75-0.90x. They get there only by giving up 128³ random access: reading one chunk means reading a 128-frame GOP, with 6-21x more bytes and 14-179x slower decoding. Every random-access codec tested needs 1.5-31x more bits than volcomp: SZ3, ZFP, JPEG 2000, JPEG XL, AVIF, WebP and all-intra video. On those four cubes no tested codec beats volcomp while keeping chunk random access (docs/bench/README.md is still marked interim: sizes and quality final, timings contended). No third-party codec has been run on the 54 held-out chunks; Gate A measures only volcomp there. CREDITS: Forrest McDonald (volcomp, c5d, the benchmark and the mirror); the Vesuvius Challenge team and ESRF (PHercParis4 2.4 µm / 78 keV scan 20260411134726). DATA: CC BY-NC 4.0 open data plus the dl.ash2txt.org terms. A human must accept the terms before any download; chunks are never redistributed.
targets.success_criterion: SCORER (pinned). score_codec.py is written by the scout and frozen by sha256 in METRIC.sha256 before the baseline run. (1) Fetch: the 54 held-out chunks listed in manifest_heldout.tsv @ 81f6519, from https://vesuvius-challenge-open-data.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/PHercParis4/volumes/20260411134726-2.400um-0.2m-78keV-masked.zarr/ < level > / < cz > / < cy > / < cx> (2,097,152 bytes each). Their sha256 is recorded on first fetch, and any later mismatch aborts. (2) Decode: each submitted chunk stream is decoded in its own fresh process, in a seeded random order, from that stream plus the codec's static side data only. (3) Report: total bytes (the sum of the 54 streams plus all static side data such as tables, dictionaries or weights, counted once in full); pooled PSNR = 10 log10(255^2 / MSE over all 54 x 128^3 voxels); mean SSIM (2-D, 7 x 7 Gaussian window, data_range 255, averaged over all z-planes of all chunks); max absolute error; single-thread CPU decode throughput (decoded bytes per wall second, in-memory stream to uint8 output, median of 3 runs). GATE A. The scout builds volcomp @ 81f6519 and stores in a hash-locked BASELINE.json its bytes, PSNR, SSIM and decode throughput at q 2, 8 and 32, both plain and with volcomp_deblock(). At each q the baseline variant is the one with the higher pooled PSNR (ties: higher mean SSIM); its bytes, PSNR, SSIM and single-thread decode throughput (decode plus filter for the deblock variant) are the reference values. The run should reproduce the BENCHMARKS.md ratios within 0.5% and PSNR within 0.02 dB; otherwise the measured values stand and the discrepancy is reported. GATE B. Codec design, parameters and any learned weights use no byte of the 54 held-out chunks and no byte of any chunk at another level that covers the same voxels (the level-1 and level-2 chunks containing a held-out level-0 chunk, and the level-0 and level-1 chunks inside a held-out level-1 or level-2 chunk); leak audit over training and tuning logs and hashes. The tune set and any other data are allowed. SUCCESS requires all of the following, at each of three operating points matched to volcomp q2, q8 and q32: pooled PSNR >= the baseline's; mean SSIM >= the baseline's; total bytes <= 0.85 x the baseline's at q8 and <= 0.90 x at q2 and q32; every chunk decodes independently and bit-exactly across two runs; single-thread decode throughput >= 0.25 x the baseline variant's throughput measured at the same point on the same machine; decoder source supplied and built by the verifier. This is an internal benchmark. It is credited officially only if scrollprize.org/winners credits a Progress Prize submission made by the human.

partial_wins.statement: One operating point. At q8-matched quality (pooled PSNR and mean SSIM >= volcomp q8's, taking the better of plain decode and deblock), total bytes <= 0.85 x the baseline's. The same independence, decode-speed and leakage rules apply.

Lossless. Byte-exact, independently decodable chunks whose total bytes are <= 0.90 x the smallest of three codecs on the same 54 chunks: volcomp q = 0, per-chunk zstd -19 and per-chunk blosc-zstd level 5, all measured by the scout in Gate A. Single-thread decode must reach >= 0.25 x the fastest of those three.

Speed at equal size. Total bytes <= 1.01 x the q8 baseline variant's (Gate A), pooled PSNR and mean SSIM at least that variant's, and single-thread decode throughput >= 2 x that variant's measured q8 throughput on the same machine. The same independence and leakage rules apply.

targets.verification_method: The verifier: (1) fetches the 54 chunks (108 MiB) and checks them against the scout's sha256 list; (2) builds the claimant's decoder from source, with static side data supplied separately and counted; (3) decodes every chunk in its own process in a seeded random order (a chunk that needs another chunk's bytes fails); (4) recomputes bytes, PSNR, SSIM and max error with score_codec.py, which takes seconds; (5) rebuilds volcomp @ 81f6519 and re-encodes 5 seeded chunks at q8 to confirm the BASELINE.json byte counts exactly; (6) times both decoders on the same machine (median of 3); (7) re-reads volcomp's BENCHMARKS.md and docs/bench tables, and villa's VC3D codec support, for newer records.
angles: Chunk-closed inter-slice prediction: treat each 128³ chunk as its own 128-frame sequence, with motion or affine prediction between z-slices as inter-frame video codecs do across a 512² GOP. Random access then survives at chunk granularity.
Adaptive context modelling with arithmetic or rANS coding across blocks inside a chunk, trellis or rate-distortion-optimised quantisation, and in-format deblocking.
Learned transforms or priors fitted on the tune set and other scroll data, shipped as counted static side data.
Exploit the masked-air fill value and the near-periodic sheet structure (winding pitch) for prediction.
Report results per chunk class (dense interior, smooth papyrus, boundary, air), as volcomp does.
pitfalls: Inter-frame video codecs already beat volcomp on bits at 35 dB by giving up random access. A stream that needs neighbouring chunks or a 512-wide GOP does not count.
PSNR alone rewards smoothing that erases ink-scale texture. The success needs both PSNR and SSIM, and max-error tails should be reported.
Never tune on the held-out chunks; the tune manifest exists for that. Held-out chunk hashes appearing in tuning logs void the attempt.
Static side data (dictionaries, weights, tables) counts in full. Amortising it over a larger corpus is not allowed.
Timing noise is about +-10% under WSL2. Compare decoders on the same machine and use medians.
Data terms: chunks come straight from the public bucket, only after the human has accepted the terms, and they are never redistributed.

targets.name: Papyrus fiber tracing on Scroll 1 (PHerc. Paris 4, 2.4 µm): beat the published automated fiber volume on precision against dense hand tracing with no loss of recall in the held-out band
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days at best (one consumer GPU; tracing covers five cube regions and every 512³ block of the held-out band z 45,000-48,500: about 11,000 blocks inside the mask, roughly 1.3-1.4 TB of level-0 uint8 CT to stream for a level-0 tracer (estimate from the S3 listing of z-chunk 360: 165 stored chunk rows of up to 167 chunks) and 8x (level 1) to 64x (level 2) less for a tracer that reads a coarser level; the 11.1 GB published AFV is read by HTTP range requests; the p1/p2/p3 filters and all scoring take laptop-minutes to laptop-hours)
targets.statement: Fibers give the spiral fitter its connectivity. scrollprize.org/2026_open_problems (updated 2026-10-14) asks for robust fiber tracing with an explicit preference: 'a tracer that confidently follows fewer fibers correctly is more useful than one that follows more fibers with a higher error rate.' BASELINE: the automated fiber volume fibers.afv (SQLite with rtree, 11,127,046,144 bytes, 2026-10-19) in the team's Scroll 1 spiral dataset PHercParis4/representations/spiral/20260411134726-spiral-dataset-20261019084150/. The same dataset holds eval_fibers/: 645 human-annotated fiber files, 299 MB. According to the afv-audit report, the AFV holds 931,104 fibers from the neural fiber follower checkpoint polar_tokens_a3_ms_slim_dagger_b32x2_50k/ckpt_050000.pt, traced over z 28,000-68,000 base voxels; the tracer code is in villa under vesuvius/neural_tracing/tracers/fibers. The same report says every fiber-follower config holds z 45,000-48,500 out of training (data/fibers.py training_state_allowed). Related community AFVs sit in dl.ash2txt.org/community-uploads/qual/AutomatedFiberVolumes/: Paris4_v1.afv (2026-10-05), Paris4_1mm_v2.afv and Paris4_all_v2.afv (2026-10-25/26). Judging by the handle, they come from Samir Lerognon (@qualzz), who won the September 2026 $20,000 Progress Prize for automated fiber extraction. His fiber models (huggingface.co/Qualzz20/afv_fiber_9um and _v2) are fine-tuned from scrollprize/fiber_hz_vt, which the open-problems page describes as trained on the fibers hand-traced in WebKnossos on the older 7.91 µm scans, and the lasagna-fiber card says SD2 was 'trained on S1A NML fibers registered to the PHercParis4 2.400 µm, 78 keV volume' (SD1 is a separate 's1a' run). These models descend from the fiber-skeletons NMLs that include the five cubes used below as the precision judge (SD1 presumably), so the community AFVs' in-cube precision is presumed contaminated. villa's fiber dataset config paris50.json holds out val_z [45000, 48500] and also samples two qualzz AFVs of other scrolls (0175A_5mm_v1, 1447_5mm_v1). MEASUREMENT: github.com/Rano200/afv-audit (MIT, commit e0710d2, 2026-10-21) scores an AFV two ways. (i) Precision against the five Scroll 1 cubes of the 2025 fiber-skeletons dataset: WEBKNOSSOS NMLs fibers_s1a_00497z_01497y_03997x_256_v00, fibers_s1a_00497z_02497y_02997x_256_v00, fibers_s1a_00997z_02497y_02997x_256_v00, fibers_s1a_08997z_02997y_02497x_256_v00 and fibers_s1a_10997z_02997y_02997x_256_v00, with every fiber traced (550 fibers), mapped into the 2026 frame with the volume's transform.json. AFV fibers are cut into 200-voxel windows, labelled GOOD ( > = 80% of points within tol of a hand fiber) or BAD (<= 20%). (ii) Recall on the eval_fibers stretches inside the held-out band: 375 stretches from 314 fibers, scored on windows of <= 600 voxels. RESULTS.md for the official AFV: 1,052 windows. At tol 10: GOOD 34.8%, BAD 37.9% (null 0.3% / 92.5%). At tol 20: GOOD 71.5%, BAD 17.4% (null 4.6% / 69.6%). Recall at tol 10: single-fiber median 0.94, union median 0.96, single >= 0.7 on 252/375; at tol 20, 288/375. REPORT.md adds: 110 of 138 scorable links (79.7%) join pieces of one hand fiber; following links needs 0.22 chains per 1,000 voxels of held-out human fiber (0.45 pieces without links); an in-sample length filter (L = 3,000) cut the BAD share from 18.1% to 12.2% while removing 15.7% of GOOD windows; two learned window scorers missed the pre-registered AUROC of 0.645 (0.637 and 0.599). A BAD window is an AFV fiber with no hand fiber nearby, so it is either an error or an annotator omission. CREDITS: the Vesuvius Challenge team (2.4 µm ESRF scan, spiral dataset, fiber follower, eval_fibers annotators); the 2025 fiber-skeletons annotators (cubes traced on the EduceLab-Scrolls DLS scan of Scroll 1); Samir Lerognon (automated fiber volumes); Rano200 (afv-audit). DATA: CC BY-NC 4.0, plus the dl.ash2txt.org terms and the EduceLab-Scrolls citation terms. A human must accept them before any download.
targets.success_criterion: SCORER: afv-audit @ e0710d2958d792c8424b39c1058acecdaefc15f3, or the scout's re-implementation frozen in METRIC.sha256 that reproduces RESULTS.md for the official AFV exactly (1,052 windows and identical percentages and counts). SUBMISSION: one AFV in the same SQLite schema, produced by a single deterministic tracer run with identical settings over (i) the five cube regions (each cube's 2026-frame bounding box plus a 64-voxel margin) and (ii) every block in BLOCKS.json. BLOCKS.json is the scout's frozen list of 512³ level-0 blocks with z in [45,000, 48,500) that intersect the scroll mask, and each listed block is traced in full. GATE A. BASELINES.json holds afv-audit results for the official fibers.afv and for each community Paris4 AFV (Paris4_v1, Paris4_1mm_v2, Paris4_all_v2). B = the scored AFV with the largest GOOD@10 - BAD@10 among those with single >= 0.7 at tol 10 on at least 252/375 stretches whose fiber model never read the fiber-skeletons NMLs, directly or through an initialisation (today the official fibers.afv; the qualzz AFVs descend from fiber_hz_vt and are scored and reported as contaminated references, not as B). GATE B (leakage). leak_audit.py over manifests and the initialisation chain must show that the tracer's training, tuning and filtering never read the five cube NMLs or their voxelised labels, any eval_fibers file, or any CT or label with base z in [45,000, 48,500). No initialisation from, and no use on PHercParis4 data (as features, probability volumes or teacher labels) of, fiber_hz_vt, lasagna-fiber SD1/SD2, Qualzz20/afv_fiber_9um or _v2, or any other model trained, directly or through a parent checkpoint, on the fiber-skeletons dataset that includes these cubes; their outputs on other scrolls may serve as training data, as in villa's paris50.json. SUCCESS requires all of: window count inside the cubes >= 0.75 x B's; at tol 10, GOOD >= B + 12 points and BAD <= B - 10 points; at tol 20, GOOD >= B + 6 points and BAD <= B - 5 points; recall single >= 0.7 at tol 10 on at least B's count of stretches, and union median at tol 10 >= B's; nulls: shifted-hand-fiber GOOD@20 <= 10%, and shifted-stretch recall single >= 0.7 at tol 20 on <= 5/375. With the official AFV as B, the bars are GOOD@10 >= 46.8%, BAD@10 <= 27.9%, GOOD@20 >= 77.5%, BAD@20 <= 12.4% and >= 252/375 stretches. This is an internal benchmark. Official credit comes only through a Progress Prize awarded to the human.

partial_wins.statement: Filter only, no new tracing. A deterministic filter of B's fibers (CT, geometry and AFV metadata allowed), with every parameter chosen leave-one-cube-out so the held-out cube's windows are never used for its own fold. It must bring pooled out-of-fold BAD@20 to <= 12.0% while removing <= 10% of GOOD@20 windows, and keep single >= 0.7 at tol 10 on >= 240/375 held-out-band stretches.

Window scorer. A scorer of B's 200-voxel cube windows reaching leave-one-cube-out AUROC >= 0.70 for BAD vs GOOD at tol 20, with a block-bootstrap 95% lower bound > 0.60. afv-audit's pre-registered bar was 0.645; its two learned scorers reached 0.637 and 0.599.

Links. Fiber-to-fiber links, on the claimant's fibers or on B's, of which >= 90% join pieces of the same hand fiber, on >= 130 scorable links in the five cubes (B: 110/138 = 79.7%). The linked chains must not exceed 0.22 per 1,000 voxels of held-out-band human fiber.

targets.verification_method: The skeptic: (1) fetches the five NMLs (about 4.6 MB), the 2026 volume's transform.json and eval_fibers (299 MB); (2) reads the claimant's AFV and the baseline AFVs, locally or by range requests; (3) runs the pinned scorer, about 11 minutes for precision, recall and links on 4 workers; (4) checks BASELINES.json by re-scoring the official AFV, which must give identical numbers; (5) checks that every BLOCKS.json block and every cube region contains traced output; (6) re-runs the tracer on two seeded blocks and one cube region and requires >= 95% of its fiber points to lie within 2 voxels of the submitted ones; (7) runs leak_audit.py; (8) before any claim, re-lists the S3 spiral datasets and the qual uploads for newer AFVs.
angles: Conservative stopping: stop or branch-check at H x V weave crossings instead of tracing through them. The masfocl-spec fiber-reconnect study found that about two thirds of real breaks sit at such crossings.

Fit splines to H/V fiber probability volumes from a model that never saw the fiber-skeletons NMLs (not lasagna-fiber SD1/SD2, fiber_hz_vt or the Qualzz afv_fiber_9um models, which all descend from them; train one on data outside the band and the cubes), then prune short or low-contrast pieces. afv-audit notes that BAD windows sit on short fibers with lower tube contrast.
DAgger-style training of a follower on data outside the band and the cubes, with confidence-calibrated termination at each step.
Verify links by CT continuity along the join rather than by end angles: afv-audit found AUROC 0.66 for the angle and 0.55 for the gap.
Report numbers per cube: for the official AFV, BAD ranges from 7.1% to 29.4% across the five cubes.
pitfalls: BAD means 'unconfirmed by hand tracing', not proven false. The cubes were traced on the 2023 7.91 µm DLS grid, and per-cube offsets are 2-5 base voxels, so tol 10 is tight; report both tolerances.
Fewer, shorter windows can inflate precision. The 0.75 x window-count rule and the band recall guard stop coverage being traded for precision.
eval_fibers and the cube NMLs are public. Any read of them by the tracer, its training or its filter voids the attempt.

fiber_hz_vt, lasagna-fiber SD1/SD2 ('trained on S1A NML fibers registered to the PHercParis4 2.400 µm volume') and the Qualzz afv_fiber_9um models (fine-tuned from fiber_hz_vt) all descend from these cubes' labels. They are not clean initialisations, nor clean teachers or feature extractors on PHercParis4, and Paris4 AFVs made with them are contaminated in the cubes.
Base voxels are level-0 voxels of the 2026 2.4 µm volume (z up to 75,784). The cubes live in the 2023 frame and must go through transform.json (matrix inverted), as afv-audit does.
Data terms: a human accepts the Vesuvius Challenge terms and the EduceLab-Scrolls citation terms before any download. AFVs and NMLs are never redistributed.

targets.name: Herculaneum 9 µm ink detection within a scroll: beat every public model's average precision on the three official ink_9um validation masks (384 px buffer rule)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (one consumer GPU: the official aligned21_hybrid_3d2d recipe trains in about 3 h on an RTX 5090 and 9.5 h on an RTX 5070 Ti; full-canvas inference on the three segments takes minutes; pooled inputs are 1-2 GB per segment, streamed from S3)
targets.statement: The team defines its within-scroll held-out test itself. The ink_9um labels README (HF bucket scrollprize/datasets, ink_9um/, fetched 2026-10-29) states that 'the three _validation_mask.zarr segments (pherc0139-w016, pherc0814-46527, pherc1667-w029) are the online-validation cases the released checkpoints report metrics on'. The ink tutorial (scrollprize.org/tutorial5) says 'Validation regions are held out, so you can measure whether the model generalizes'. The ink_9um card publishes no metrics and still expects 'substantial gains'. LABELS: 24 aligned segments (2.399 µm volumes pooled to about 9.6 µm, 21 slices, annotated at Z=10) and 5 native 9.362 µm PHerc0139 segments. The aligned label directories were re-uploaded on 2026-08-18 after a seam-masking fix (reported in DomRusso2/ink9um-dense). PUBLISHED HELD-OUT NUMBERS. Domenico Russo's ink9um-dense (August 2026 Progress Prize for ink checkpoint benchmarking) scored all 14 released checkpoints with the team's BalancedAccuracy at threshold 0.5 and with AUC. Best released per region: w016 0.8194 / 0.9366, 0814 0.8129 / 0.8970, w029 0.8434 / 0.9334. The spread across the 14 reaches 0.14, and a dense pseudo-label model reaches 0.8539 / 0.9350 on 0814. Alex Clark's inkbench (commit a0ff572, 2026-09-07; September 2026 Progress Prize for ink ensembling) reports full-canvas average precision on the held-out pixels (0814 / w029 / w016): recommended seed42 step-075000 0.839 / 0.901 / 0.622; seed-42 10k-30k weight soup 0.841 / 0.902 / 0.808; output average of all 14 checkpoints 0.860 / 0.927 / 0.808 (mean 0.865). Some public models saw these masks' pixels through another representation of the same papyrus: TRACE (github.com/Jashann/vesuvius-scrolling, runs/trace_manifest_v3.json) trained on the native 9.362 µm renders of 20250108000004-w029 (the physical segment behind pherc0139-w016) and 20260226000000-46527_2um_try2 (behind pherc0814-46527) with the team's whole-segment 2.4 µm maps as soft targets, and for 46527_2um_try2 also with its human ink labels (ink-labels/2.399um-volume-20260309142202/20260918, in the manifest's train split); v8-in's training corpus includes 0814_46527n9, a native render of the 0814 segment; Hecate's documented supervision is the ink bucket, which holds all three segments' labels. Their scores on these masks are presumed contaminated. WHY A BUFFER: the khj1222 audit (docs/17, 2026-08-29) shows that all three masks cut through annotated regions. On w016, 99.1% of held-out pixels lie within two 128 px patches of a training pixel, and the farther ones carry no ink. 0814 is one region split internally. Only w029 has real separation. A model trained next door gains +0.14 F1 (w016) and +0.07 F1 (w029) more on adjacent pixels than on distant ones. OPEN QUESTION: genuine within-scroll generalization to unlabelled regions once adjacency is removed. That is the pseudo-labelling use case. CREDITS: the Vesuvius Challenge team (labels, ink_9um, recipe, Hecate); Domenico Russo (ink9um-dense, Reader v2, Reader V3); Alex Clark (inkbench); the khj1222 repository (scorecard and audit); Youssef Nader (v8-in); Erwin Nieuwlaar (dense-native); Jashanjot Singh Gill and Nhat Nam Tran (TRACE). DATA: CC BY-NC 4.0 plus the dl.ash2txt.org terms. A human must accept them before any download.
targets.success_criterion: PROTOCOL (pinned). score_val9.py is frozen in METRIC.sha256 before any scoring. It takes a full-canvas 9.6 µm ink map per validation segment, computed from the official inputs: 2.399 µm surface volumes pooled by villa scripts/prepare_9um_isotropic_input.py at a pinned villa commit, as the ink_9um card prescribes. It computes average precision (step-wise, as in sklearn average_precision_score) of the map against inklabels > 0 on the annotated plane, over pixels with validation_mask > 0, using label files pinned by sha256 from the current HF bucket. BUFFER RULE. The buffer zone of a validation segment is every canvas pixel within 384 px (Euclidean, on the 9.6 µm label grid) of any of its validation-mask pixels. Training may use any public labels (the official ink_9um supervision, reader-v2-labels, ink9um-dense-labels, team 2.4 µm maps), but no pixel inside a buffer zone may be supervised, and no pixel of any other segment or representation (native renders, other meshes) may be supervised if its 3D position, mapped through its tifxyz mesh, lies within 75 µm of the 3D position of a buffer-zone pixel mapped through the validation segment's mesh. This excludes the native twins of the validation segments (for example 20250108000004-w029 and 20260226000000-46527_2um_try2 at 9.362 µm). No pseudo-labels, team maps or fine-tuning may supervise excluded pixels. GATE A. Under the same protocol, the scout scores all 14 ink_9um checkpoints, their 14-checkpoint output average, the seed-42 10k/20k/30k weight soup, ink9um-dense (control, all-7, w016excluded), Reader v2, Reader V3, Nieuwlaar dense-native, Hecate 9.6 µm, v8-in, TRACE sA, sB, v3A and v3B (Jashann/vesuvius-scrolling release v1.0), A-hn (Prodigle/pherc0306b-ink-ahn) and any other public 9 µm ink checkpoint found on the day the baselines are frozen, in a hash-locked BASELINES.json that also marks each baseline as presumed contaminated (trained on validation-mask pixels in any representation) or not. B_m = the best AP on mask m over all of these that are not presumed contaminated, ensembles of them included. The contaminated ones are scored and reported as references, not as B_m, because a model trained on a validation segment's own labels or maps measures memorisation, not the buffered generalisation this target asks for. GATE B. No initialisation from any checkpoint trained on supervision inside a buffer zone or its 3D exclusion: every released ink_9um, Reader, ink9um-dense, Nieuwlaar dense-native and TRACE checkpoint, Hecate, v8-in (0814_46527n9) and A-hn (fine-tuned from v8-in) are excluded. leak_audit over the label manifest proves the buffer. Validation masks are never read during training (no online validation, no best_val checkpoint). GATE C. One network, with its checkpoint sha256 declared before the first scoring; every scoring is logged. SUCCESS: AP >= B_m + 0.01 on each of the three masks, and mean AP >= the best mean of any baseline not presumed contaminated + 0.02; the claim also reports AP against every contaminated reference. This is an internal benchmark. Official credit comes only through a Progress Prize to the human.

partial_wins.statement: Distillation without the buffer. One network trained under the official rules (validation-mask pixels never supervised in any representation, no buffer, initialisation from the released ink_9um checkpoints or any other checkpoint not presumed contaminated allowed) and Gate B's selection rules (no online validation, no best_val checkpoint), whose AP on each of the three masks is >= the larger of the Gate A AP of the 14-checkpoint output average and the best Gate A AP of any single network not presumed contaminated. In inkbench, soups approach that average but do not exceed it on all three.

Buffered single model against released singles. One network trained under the buffer rule and Gate B whose AP on each of the three masks is >= the best of the 14 released single checkpoints, as measured in Gate A.

targets.verification_method: The skeptic: (1) downloads the three segments' label and mask zarrs and checks the pinned sha256; (2) recomputes the buffer zones from the validation masks and the 75 µm 3D exclusion through the tifxyz meshes, and checks every supervised pixel in the training manifest against both; (3) recomputes AP from the frozen maps and from two stored baseline maps with score_val9.py, requiring |difference| < 1e-6; (4) re-runs the claimed checkpoint on w029 at the declared settings (minutes on a consumer GPU) and requires Pearson r > 0.99 with the frozen map; (5) re-reads the HF ink_9um bucket README, the ink_9um card, the Reader, inkbench, TRACE and khj1222 repositories and the Hugging Face ink-model listings for newer baselines or changed labels.
angles: Distil the 14-checkpoint output average and the soup into one network on non-validation pixels (p1), then repeat the distillation under the buffer.
Replace the deleted neighbourhood supervision with dense labels from other scrolls and from regions outside the buffer (reader-v2-labels, ink9um-dense-labels).
Use depth-window jitter and average both layer orders, as the ink_9um card suggests. Early checkpoints generalise better: khj docs/14 shows 75k overtrains.
Report AP by distance band from the nearest official supervision pixel (the khj docs/17 strata) to show the gain is not adjacency.
pitfalls: The official masks leak by adjacency. Without the buffer, wins mostly measure memorised neighbourhoods (khj docs/17).
Balanced accuracy at 0.5 can prefer a visually worse, smeared map (ink9um-dense section 4). This target uses threshold-free AP instead.
best_val_balanced_accuracy checkpoints and online validation select on these same masks, so both are forbidden.
pherc0139-w028 (aligned) and w044 (native) are the same physical segment under two keys. Neither is a validation segment, but do not count them as independent evidence.
Labels changed on 2026-08-18 with the seam fix. Pin the current files by sha256 and re-check them before claiming.
Data terms: a human accepts the Vesuvius Challenge terms before any download. Labels and renders are never redistributed.

A buffer drawn only on the aligned canvas misses other representations of the same papyrus: TRACE trained on the native 9.362 µm renders of the w016 and 0814 validation segments with whole-segment team maps, and v8-in on a native 0814 render. Hence the 3D exclusion and the contamination flags in Gate A.

targets.name: Hadamard conjecture frontier: a Hadamard matrix at one of the 85 orders up to 10000 with no known construction (smallest 2396)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (structured Goethals-Seidel, bordered or recursive searches over groups of order about 600 to 2500; checking a claim takes laptop-minutes)
targets.statement: A Hadamard matrix of order n is an n x n matrix H with entries +1 or -1 and H H^T = nI; one is conjectured to exist for every n divisible by 4. From Kharaghani and Tayfeh-Rezaie's order 428 (2005) until 2026 the smallest open order was 668. On 12 August 2026 L. Alpöge, P. Voinov and S. Reynolds-Haertle announced matrices at the twelve open orders below 2000 (668, 716, 892, 1132, 1244, 1388, 1436, 1676, 1772, 1916, 1948, 1964); Epoch AI's FrontierMath open-problems page now marks order 668 as solved (human + AI; reported by an Anthropic researcher crediting three humans and Claude). Egan, Kotsireas, London and Ó Catháin (arXiv:2610.27175, 19 Oct 2026) verified those matrices; built matrices at sixteen further orders, five of which (5436, 6644 and 7852 from A. Schumer's T-matrices of order 151; 7172 and 8476 from J. D. Jones's T-matrices of order 163) had been posted earlier by those authors and were found independently; checked exactly the twenty-two orders settled by others while the paper was in preparation (T. Cooley: 2092, 2292, 2588 and 3676, where Schumer had earlier given a skew matrix of order 3676; K. Kumar: 2148, 2284, 2636 and 3964, thirteen orders from a Seberry-Yamada product theorem, and 9172 from Cooley's 2292 by Miyamoto's theorem; Kharaghani, Mohammadian, Tayfeh-Rezaie and Zaitsev independently gave a BH(1142,4), which also yields 2284); credited L. Schneider's T-matrices of order 103; and listed in their Table 5 the 95 orders n <= 10000 with no known Hadamard matrix, all of the forms 4p, 4*3p, 4*5p, 4*7p, 4*9p, 4*11p, 4*13p or 8p with p a prime congruent to 3 mod 4. Their Hadamard Matrix Explorer (math74.com/Hadamard, version 57, October 2026), which hosts the paper's matrices, lists 86 unknown orders at this check: 2396, 2676, 2876, 2956, 3004, 3452, 3628, 3788, 3884, 4076, ... up to 9836 (full list on the status page). One of them, 5912 = 8*739, is already constructed in K. Kumar's repository (hadamard/5912, Spence's construction over Z_211 x F_7 with a multiplier group of order 45), so 85 remain open. The nine orders dropped since Table 5 are 2572, 3356, 3436, 3820, 4204, 6712, 6796, 8248 and 8696, and orders keep falling (for example, K. Kumar settled 2572 = 4*643 on 21 Oct 2026 with a quaternary conference matrix). Kumar's FRONTIER.md (github.com/vatskishan03/Hadamard, October 2026) independently lists 83 unresolved orders 4n < 10000 with n odd (85 if Middletownbooks' 2292 and 2588 are not accepted), exactly the explorer's odd-n orders, plus 37 unresolved orders 10000 < 4n <= 11996 from Cati and Pasechnik's Table 4 (n <= 2999); of the orders 8p it keeps only 4792 and 5752 open. The smallest open order is 2396 = 4*599. Tao's optimization-constants page for C_23a still gives 668 and is stale.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an explicit n x n matrix H with every entry +1 or -1 and H H^T = nI computed exactly over the whole matrix (integer arithmetic), for an order n that is listed on the live unknown-orders page https://www.math74.com/Hadamard/unknown.html (re-fetched immediately before claiming; 86 orders at this check, of which 5912 is already constructed in Kumar's repository, smallest 2396) and that no public source settles at claim time. That means: n is not constructed in github.com/vatskishan03/Hadamard (hadamard/ and complex-hadamard/ folders, README.md, FRONTIER.md), in github.com/Middletownbooks/Hadamard (all branches), in the JD-Jones-ASES repositories Hadamard-T and Hadamard-M, in github.com/schneiderlo/hadamard-2060, in Schumer's Zenodo deposit doi:10.5281/zenodo.22820997 or in the latest version of arXiv:2610.27175; no quaternary Hadamard matrix BH(n/2,4), which gives H(n), is listed on https://www.cs.uleth.ca/~zaitsevv/quaternary.html; and a same-day arXiv, GitHub and Zenodo search for the order finds nothing (direction: none; existence target). The full matrix, or seeds plus an array that the verifier expands with its own code, must accompany the claim; a recipe without the matrix is not a result.

partial_wins.statement: A Hadamard matrix of order 4n with n odd and 10000 < 4n <= 11996 whose order is listed as unresolved in the live FRONTIER.md of github.com/vatskishan03/Hadamard (37 such orders at this check, for example 10012, 10052, 10124, 10172) and is not settled by any other public source at claim time, checked exactly as in the main criterion.

targets.verification_method: Load H and assert it is n x n with entries in {+1,-1}. Compute G = H H^T exactly: Python integers, or numpy int64 (every entry of G is bounded by n, so int64 and even float64 BLAS products are exact for n <= 10^4), and assert G == nI. Re-check with an independently written program (for example row-pair dot products in another language, plus Freivalds tests with random +-1 vectors). If the claim comes as seed sequences and an array (Goethals-Seidel, bordered, Williamson-type, Cooper-Wallis), expand it with the verifier's own code, never by running downloaded code. Then re-fetch the unknown-orders page, Kumar's FRONTIER.md and the other repositories the criterion names, and search arXiv, GitHub and Zenodo for the order.
angles: Goethals-Seidel array over Z_p (or Z_3 x GF(p), or another group of order n/4) with the four first rows invariant under a multiplier subgroup of (Z/pZ)*: the unknowns become orbit signs; the 2026 matrices at 3732, 4492, 5932 and 5020 used multiplier groups of orders 31, 33, 39 and 50 respectively (arXiv:2610.27175).

Bordered variants (Theorems 3, 5 and 7 of arXiv:2610.27175): the twelve 2026 matrices below 2000 are Goethals-Seidel arrays over abelian groups, nine over cyclic groups (four of them with a border of width 4) and three over non-cyclic groups with a wider border constant on the cosets of a subgroup; Spence's bordered construction for order 4m uses a group of order m - 1.

Recursive closures: a new T-matrix order t or Williamson-type order w closes every order 4tw at once (Cooper-Wallis); Paley's and Miyamoto's matrices cut into sixteen circulant blocks can be multiplied by T-matrices (Kumar's PALEY_BLOCKS.md and MIYAMOTO_BLOCKS.md; read them as data, do not run downloaded code).

Quaternary routes: any BH(n/2,4) gives H(n). For order 4m with m odd, a quaternary conference matrix of order (m+1)/2 with the complex Yamada-Kiyasu template gives one; this route settled 2572, 3436, 4204 and 6796 in October 2026 (Kumar). The quaternary table of Zaitsev, Kharaghani, Mohammadian and Tayfeh-Rezaie still lists 1198 (order 2396) as unknown.

Triage first: Kumar's FRONTIER.md gives, for each open order, the cheapest multiplier or Spence structure with its expected solution count and predicted matching work log10 W. At this check no explorer-listed order has a structure with log10 W <= 13 (about one machine); the best are 4748 (log10 W 15.2, Spence over Z2 x Z593) and 4412 (15.5, Goethals-Seidel with |H| = 19), and 2676 and 2876 have no structure expected to hold ten solutions, so the remaining orders need new ideas or new ingredients.
pitfalls: The list moves every week. Table 5 of the 19 October survey had 95 orders and the explorer (version 57) 86 later in October, one of which, 5912, Kumar's repository has since constructed. Kumar's FRONTIER.md now matches the explorer on odd n (83 orders 4n < 10000) but, covering only odd n in its main table, lists the 8p orders separately (4792 and 5752 open). Check every source the criterion names.
Every order below 2000 is settled (Alpöge, Voinov and Reynolds-Haertle, August 2026). Tao's C_23a page still says 668; it is stale.

Seberry-Yamada's Corollary 8.8(i) and Miyamoto's (1991) Corollary 2 omit a symmetry hypothesis their construction needs; orders claimed only through them (2076 and 6108 historically, and Miyamoto's 515/2060 route per the JD-Jones-ASES Hadamard-M erratum) were not valid constructions. A claim through a printed theorem must check every hypothesis on the explicit inputs.
Seeds are not a matrix: expand them and verify H H^T over the whole matrix; one wrong sign in a border fails it.
Several independent groups, some AI-assisted, are searching the same orders; same-day duplicates are likely, so re-check right before claiming and record the time.

targets.name: Steiner systems S(2,6,v): settle one of the 27 undecided admissible v (smallest 51), or an undecided case with block size 7, 8 or 9
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (difference-family or orbit-prescribed exact-cover search; checking a design takes laptop-seconds)
targets.statement: A Steiner system S(2,k,v) is a family of k-subsets (blocks) of a v-set such that every pair of points lies in exactly one block; v is admissible when k-1 divides v-1 and k(k-1) divides v(v-1). For k <= 5 every admissible v is realised (Hanani); for k >= 6 Wilson's theorem gives existence only for large v. For k = 6 (v = 1 or 6 mod 15), S(2,6,36) is excluded by Bruck-Ryser and S(2,6,46) by computer search, and the Handbook of Combinatorial Designs (2nd ed., 2007) lists 29 undecided values: 51, 61, 81, 166, 226, 231, 256, 261, 286, 316, 321, 346, 351, 376, 406, 411, 436, 441, 471, 501, 561, 591, 616, 646, 651, 676, 771, 796, 801. Banakh, Hetman and Ravsky (arXiv:2511.05191 v3, 18 May 2026) found seven 1-rotational S(2,6,226) over (Z5 x Z5 x Z3) ⋊ Z3 with a fixed point and six point-transitive S(2,6,441) over (Z7 ⋊ Z3) x (Z7 ⋊ Z3), leaving 27 undecided. For k = 7 the Handbook lists 21 undecided v; I. Hetman settled 505 and 589 (arXiv:2604.04975 v4, 12 Oct 2026) and names S(2,7,127) and S(2,7,211) as undecided (arXiv:2511.20708 v3, Feb 2026). For k = 8 and 9 the Handbook lists 38 and 91 undecided v; Hetman settled S(2,8,225) and S(2,9,289) (arXiv:2509.10673 v4) and S(2,9,369), which by recursion also gives S(2,9,3321) (arXiv:2511.20708). All of these 2025-2026 results came from computer searches with prescribed automorphism groups; Hetman publishes the block files in github.com/Ihromant/math-utils.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an explicit S(2,6,v) for v in {51, 61, 81, 166, 231, 256, 261, 286, 316, 321, 346, 351, 376, 406, 411, 436, 471, 501, 561, 591, 616, 646, 651, 676, 771, 796, 801}: exactly v(v-1)/30 blocks, each a 6-subset of a v-set, with every one of the v(v-1)/2 pairs in exactly one block, checked exhaustively by two independent programs on the full block list (base blocks plus a group count only after the verifier expands them with its own code), where no S(2,6,v) for that v is reported at claim time in the latest version of arXiv:2511.05191, in Hetman's later papers or in a fresh arXiv search (direction: none; existence target).

partial_wins.statement: An explicit S(2,7,127) or S(2,7,211) (v(v-1)/42 blocks of size 7, every pair exactly once), checked as in the main criterion, with no S(2,7,v) for that v reported at claim time.

An explicit S(2,k,v) with k in {7, 8, 9}, checked as in the main criterion, for another admissible v that an openly accessible source states to be undecided. The source must be an arXiv paper or a maintained online table, cited by URL in the claim. The settled 505 and 589 (k = 7), 225 (k = 8), and 289, 369 and 3321 (k = 9) do not count, nor does any v settled since. A value whose undecided status is documented only in the printed Handbook does not qualify.

A complete, independently re-run proof that no S(2,6,51) has an automorphism of a stated prime order p (or that none is 1-rotational or point-transitive over a stated group), where that exclusion is not already published; delivered as a DRAT/LRAT-checked proof on a CNF the skeptic regenerates, or as exhaustive search code and logs the skeptic re-runs.

targets.verification_method: Read the blocks; check each has k distinct points in range and that there are v(v-1)/(k(k-1)) of them. Build a v x v pair-count table and require every off-diagonal entry to be exactly 1. For designs given as difference families, expand every base block under the stated group (plus the fixed point for 1-rotational designs) with the verifier's own group arithmetic before counting; the shortcut that base-block differences partition the group is valid only for full regular orbits. Use two independently written checkers, then search arXiv and Hetman's repository for that v.
angles: 1-rotational designs: a group of order v-1 acting on itself plus one fixed point, with base blocks whose differences cover each non-identity element once, as for S(2,6,226). For v = 51, 81 and 256 try all groups of order 50, 80 and 255 from the GAP small-groups library.
Point-transitive designs over non-abelian groups of order v, as for S(2,6,441) over (Z7 ⋊ Z3)^2; v = 231 = 3*7*11, 261 = 9*29 and 351 = 27*13 have several non-abelian groups.

Hetman's G-space method: take a subgroup of the automorphism group of a known design with related parameters, use its orbit structure on points as the prescribed action, and solve the orbit exact cover (Kramer-Mesner) with a SAT solver or dancing links.
Mirroring (arXiv:2604.04975): replacing some base blocks by their inverses turns one difference family into many non-isomorphic designs, useful as seeds for local repair at nearby v.
Before searching, check whether a new ingredient makes an undecided value follow from a PBD or product construction.
pitfalls: Excluded or inadmissible v: S(2,6,36) and S(2,6,46) do not exist; v must be 1 or 6 mod 15 for k = 6 and 1 or 7 mod 42 for k = 7.
Settled values: 226 and 441 (k = 6), 505 and 589 (k = 7), 225 (k = 8), 289, 369 and 3321 (k = 9). New non-isomorphic designs for decided v are not wins.
Short orbits: when the group does not act regularly on blocks, the base-block difference test miscounts; expand and count pairs.

The Handbook's undecided lists for k = 7, 8 and 9 exist only in the printed book. The open arXiv papers give their sizes (21, 38, 91) but name only 127 and 211 (k = 7), so p2 needs an open source that names the value.
Block files in Ihromant/math-utils are data; parse them and never run code from the repository.

targets.name: Quaternary Legendre pairs: settle an open even length up to 100 (70, 76, 88, 92, 94 or 100)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (compression and meet-in-the-middle over Gray-mapped rows; checking is instant)
targets.statement: A quaternary Legendre pair (qLP) of length l is a pair A, B in {1, -1, i, -i}^l with PAF_A(k) + PAF_B(k) = -2 for every shift k = 1..l-1, where PAF_X(k) = sum_j X_j conj(X_{j+k mod l}). Kotsireas and Winterhof introduced them (arXiv:2212.10953): a qLP of length l gives a quaternary Hadamard matrix of order 2l+2 and a binary Hadamard matrix of order 4l+4, and one is conjectured to exist for every even l. Kotsireas, Koutschan and Winterhof (arXiv:2408.16318 v2, 2025) found lengths 28, 30, 32 and 34, and Jedwab and Pender (arXiv:2408.08472 v2; Combinatorial Theory 5(2), 2025) gave infinite families l = (q-1)/2 for prime powers q = 1 mod 4 and l = 2p for odd primes p with 2p-1 a prime power; both 2025 papers leave 14 lengths up to 100 open: 42, 46, 52, 58, 64, 66, 70, 72, 76, 80, 88, 92, 94, 100. N. Lebedev (arXiv:2609.04589, 4 Sep 2026) printed pairs at 42, 46, 52, 58, 66, 72 and 80 and exhausted specific reflection-symmetric search queues at 64, 70 and 76 without finding a pair (explicitly not a nonexistence proof); H. Verma (arXiv:2609.25573, 22 Sep 2026) gave the first pair of length 64. Open at this check: 70, 76, 88, 92, 94, 100 (K. Kumar's NOTES.md in github.com/vatskishan03/Hadamard, October 2026, gives the same list).
targets.success_criterion: Success means an explicit pair A, B of a length l in {70, 76, 88, 92, 94, 100} with entries in {1, -1, i, -i} and PAF_A(k) + PAF_B(k) = -2 exactly (Gaussian-integer arithmetic) for every k = 1..l-1, verified by two independent programs, where no qLP of that length is reported at claim time in a fresh arXiv search for 'quaternary Legendre' (direction: none; existence target). A rigorous nonexistence proof for one of these lengths (DRAT/LRAT-checked on a CNF the skeptic regenerates, or an exhaustive search the skeptic re-runs) also counts.

partial_wins.statement: A certified exhaustion, at l = 70 or 76, of a precisely stated structured family that Lebedev's recorded queues do not cover and that no publication or public note already rules out, with code and logs the skeptic re-runs to the same empty result. Examples: pairs whose four Gray rows are invariant under a stated multiplier subgroup of Z_l^*, or decompositions in which only one Gray-row pair is symmetric about a common integer centre. Families already excluded by a short necessary condition do not count. At l = 70 and 76 the midpoint-frequency identity (the four squared alternating sums of the Gray rows add to 4l + 4) rules out every family in which some Gray-row pair is symmetric about a half-integer centre, because l + 1 = 71 or 77 is not a sum of two squares (Kumar, NOTES.md section 8).

targets.verification_method: Map each symbol to an exponent e in Z_4 (X_j = i^(e_j)). For each shift k, count the residues of e_j - e_{j+k} mod 4 as c0..c3 and form PAF_X(k) = (c0 - c2) + i(c1 - c3), so no floating point is used. Require PAF_A(k) + PAF_B(k) = -2 + 0i for all k = 1..l-1. Sanity check: |sum A|^2 + |sum B|^2 = 2. This is the zero-frequency value; the constant 2l + 2 holds only at nonzero frequencies. Calibrate the checker on Lebedev's printed pair of length 42 (arXiv:2609.04589, digits 0,1,2,3 = 1, i, -1, -i) before use. Use two independent checkers, then search arXiv.
angles: Gray map (Lebedev): write A = ((p+q) + i(p-q))/2 and B = ((r+s) + i(r-s))/2 with four +-1 rows; the condition becomes a sum of four periodic autocorrelations equal to -4 plus an amicability condition, which holds automatically when each pair (p, q) and (r, s) is symmetric about a common centre.

Power spectral density filter: |DFT_A(w)|^2 + |DFT_B(w)|^2 = 2l + 2 at every nonzero frequency, and the exact midpoint-frequency constraint at w = l/2; Kotsireas-Koutschan-Winterhof sharpen the PSD test with Galois theory in cyclotomic fields.
Compression along divisor chains (70 = 2*5*7, 76 = 4*19, 88 = 8*11, 92 = 4*23, 94 = 2*47, 100 = 4*25), then meet-in-the-middle matching of autocorrelation vectors, then lifting with SAT.
Separate the even- and odd-indexed subsequences (arXiv:2408.16318) to cut the search.

Kumar's unrefereed note argues from the midpoint-frequency condition that at l = 70 and 76 a qLP needs a Gray-row pair that is not symmetric about a common centre, while a mixed-centre family is possible at 88 and 100 and lies outside Lebedev's queues.
pitfalls: The autocorrelation must conjugate the shifted entry; without the conjugate the -2 condition is a different equation.
Lebedev's exhaustions at 64, 70 and 76 cover recorded queues only; they are not nonexistence results, and 64 was later found by Verma.
Lengths 42, 46, 52, 58, 64, 66, 72 and 80 are settled; odd lengths are the binary Legendre pair problem (separate entry).
FFT checks in floating point are filters, not proofs; the final check must be exact.

targets.name: Sequences behind Hadamard constructions: settle a smallest open case in Table 3 of arXiv:2610.27175 (T-sequences, base sequences, Williamson-type matrices, Golay pairs)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days to needs cluster (compression, SAT+CAS and exhaustive searches; checking takes laptop-seconds)
targets.statement: Most recursive constructions of Hadamard matrices rest on sequences whose aperiodic autocorrelations N_a(s) = sum_{i=0}^{m-1-s} a_i a_{i+s} cancel (with the second factor conjugated for entries +-1, +-i). Table 3 of Egan, Kotsireas, London and Ó Catháin (arXiv:2610.27175, 19 Oct 2026) records where each ingredient is known to exist and its smallest open case. Golay pairs exist at lengths 2^a 10^b 26^c and at no other length up to 105 (smallest open 106). Turyn-type sequences TT(n) (four +-1 sequences of lengths n, n, n, n-1 with N_A + N_B + 2N_C + 2N_D = 0) are known for every even n <= 46 (Best, Đoković, Kharaghani and Ramp; London and Kotsireas 2025 and 2026), smallest open 48. Base sequences BS(n+1, n) are known for every n <= 40 (the last of these, BS(40,39), by Đoković 2010), for n = 41, 42 and 43 (Wang and Zhu, arXiv:2506.20296, 2025) and for n = 2^a 10^b 26^c, smallest open 44. T-sequences are known at every length t <= 100 except possibly 97 (Đoković 2010). T-matrices (four circulant {0,+-1} matrices of order t with disjoint supports and sum T_i T_i^T = tI) are also known at 97, 109 and 197 (K. Kumar 2026), 103 (L. Schneider 2026), 151 (A. Schumer 2026, and independently Egan et al.), 163 and 181 (J. D. Jones 2026), smallest open 127. Williamson-type matrices WT(w) are known at every odd w <= 69 and at 73, 79, 91, 93, 95, 97, 103, 109, 127, 133 and 181 (Kharaghani, Mohammadian and Tayfeh-Rezaie, arXiv:2605.08661 v2, through near-Williamson matrices; some of these orders were known classically), at 111 (K. Kumar 2026), in Turyn's family (q+1)/2 and further families, smallest open 71. Complex Golay pairs are known at lengths 1, 3, 5, 11, 13 and every even length up to 26 except 14 (Bright, Kotsireas, Heinle and Ganesh enumerated all lengths up to 28), smallest open 29. Each new ingredient closes Hadamard orders: TT(n) gives H(4(3n-1)), BS(n+1, n) gives T-sequences of length 2n+1, and T-matrices of order t with WT(w) give H(4tw) (Cooper-Wallis).
targets.success_criterion: Success means an explicit object settling one of these cells, verified exactly by two independent programs: a Golay pair of length 106; Turyn-type sequences TT(48); base sequences BS(45,44); T-sequences of length 97; T-matrices of order 127; Williamson-type matrices of order 71 (four +-1 matrices A, B, C, D of order 71 with XY^T = YX^T for every pair and AA^T + BB^T + CC^T + DD^T = 284 I); or a complex Golay pair of length 29. A rigorous nonexistence proof for one cell (DRAT/LRAT-checked on a CNF the skeptic regenerates, or an exhaustive search the skeptic re-runs) also counts. The cell must still be open at claim time: Table 3 of the latest version of arXiv:2610.27175 and a same-day search of arXiv, github.com/vatskishan03/Hadamard and the JD-Jones-ASES repositories show no such object (direction: none; existence target).

partial_wins.statement: A certified exclusion, not previously published, of one of these cells within a precisely stated subclass (for example: no TT(48) with a stated symmetry or compression pattern, no Williamson-type matrices of order 71 of a stated circulant or near-Williamson form, no complex Golay pair of length 29 of a stated structured form), with code and logs the skeptic re-runs to the same empty result or a DRAT/LRAT certificate.

targets.verification_method: For sequences, compute every aperiodic autocorrelation exactly in integers (Gaussian integers for complex Golay pairs, conjugating the second factor) and require the stated combination to vanish at every shift s >= 1; check lengths and alphabets ({+-1}; {0, +-1} with exactly one nonzero sequence at each position for T-sequences; {+-1, +-i} for complex Golay pairs). For T-matrices, check that the supports are disjoint and cover every position and that the periodic autocorrelations sum to zero at every nonzero shift. For Williamson-type matrices, form the four matrices and check XY^T = YX^T and the sum condition exactly. As an end-to-end check, build the Hadamard matrix the cited theorem gives (for example TT(48) gives T-sequences of length 143 and H(572)) and verify H H^T. Use two independent checkers and search the sources named in the criterion.
angles: Compression (Đoković-Kotsireas): project candidates onto Z_m for divisors m of the length, enumerate compressed candidates that pass the power-spectral-density test, then lift with SAT; this is how recent TT(n) and T-matrices were found.

SAT+CAS (Bright et al.): encode the autocorrelation equations in SAT and let a computer-algebra callback prune with PSD bounds; the same pipeline enumerated complex Golay pairs up to length 28 and is the natural route to length 29.
Near-Williamson matrices (four circulants with B, C, D symmetric) gave every odd w <= 69; extend the Kharaghani-Mohammadian-Tayfeh-Rezaie search to w = 71 with multiplier-orbit restrictions.
T-matrices of prime order 127: impose invariance under a subgroup of (Z/127Z)* (orders 3, 7, 9, ...), as Egan et al. did with subgroups of orders 5 and 9 for t = 151 and 163.
A Golay pair of length 106 would refute the Golay-number conjecture; for a nonexistence proof use Borwein-Ferguson-style exhaustive methods with the Eliahou-Kervaire-Saffari restrictions.
pitfalls: Aperiodic versus periodic: Golay pairs, base sequences, TT(n) and T-sequences use aperiodic autocorrelation; T-matrices and Williamson-type matrices are periodic objects. Periodic Golay pairs are a separate entry.
Williamson-type matrices also need amicability XY^T = YX^T; four circulants meeting only the sum condition are Goethals-Seidel input, not WT(71).
TT(n) has lengths n, n, n, n-1 and weights 1, 1, 2, 2.
This table changed fast in 2026 (T-matrices at 97, 103, 109, 151, 163, 181 and 197 and WT(111) were all new); re-check Table 3 and the repositories on the day of the claim.

targets.name: Skew-Hadamard matrices: an order where none is known (smallest 356 = 4*89)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (Goethals-Seidel difference families with a skew block, multiplier-orbit searches; checking takes laptop-seconds)
targets.statement: A Hadamard matrix H is skew if H + H^T = 2I; Seberry conjectured that skew-Hadamard matrices exist at every order divisible by 4. Known sources include Paley's q+1 (q = 3 mod 4), doubling, Spence's family, good matrices and Goethals-Seidel arrays with a skew supplementary difference set. D. Ž. Đoković (arXiv:2301.02751 v3, 24 Nov 2024) constructed the first skew-Hadamard matrices of orders 276 (v = 69) and 292 and listed the odd v < 200 for which order 4v was undecided: 89, 101, 107, 119, 149, 153, 167, 177, 179, 191, 193. Cati and Pasechnik (arXiv:2411.18897 v2, 30 Aug 2025) implemented every known construction up to order 1208 in SageMath and count 41 orders up to 1208 with no known skew-Hadamard matrix (their Table 5 gives, for odd v <= 999, the least m with a skew matrix of order 2^m v known; the v listed there have none at 4v). Table 3 of Egan, Kotsireas, London and Ó Catháin (arXiv:2610.27175, 19 Oct 2026) gives 356 as the smallest open skew order. In October 2026 K. Kumar (github.com/vatskishan03/Hadamard, folder skew/) posted skew-Hadamard matrices at about 110 further orders, measured against an unpublished Đoković-Seberry census of May 2025; the smallest are 476 = 4*119 (added 23 Oct 2026, after the survey), 820, 836, 980 = 4*245 (added 24 Oct 2026), 996, 1012, 1036, 1044, 1100, 1140, 1148 and 1204. Remaining small open orders: 356, 404, 428, 596, 612, 708, 764, 772 (v = 89, 101, 107, 149, 153, 177, 191, 193). At 668 = 4*167 and 716 = 4*179 Hadamard matrices were announced in 2026; the sources read here do not say whether any of them is skew.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an explicit n x n matrix H with entries +-1, H + H^T = 2I and H H^T = nI (both checked exactly) for n in {356, 404, 428, 596, 612, 708, 764, 772}, verified by two independent programs, where no skew-Hadamard matrix of that order is reported at claim time in Table 3 of the latest version of arXiv:2610.27175, in the skew/ folder and README of github.com/vatskishan03/Hadamard, or in a fresh arXiv search (direction: none; existence target).

partial_wins.statement: A skew-Hadamard matrix of order 4v for odd v with 200 < v < 300 that Cati-Pasechnik's Table 5 (arXiv:2411.18897 v2) leaves without a construction and that Kumar's skew/ folder does not contain at claim time: 804, 900, 916, 932, 940, 1004, 1028, 1060, 1076, 1108, 1156, 1180 or 1196, with the census status reported in Kumar's skew/README.md also checked, verified as in the main criterion.

A skew-Hadamard matrix of order 668, 716, 892 or 1132 (orders with 2026 Hadamard matrices of unstated type), exhibited in skew form H + H^T = 2I, after the claimant shows that no skew matrix of that order is public.

targets.verification_method: Check entries are +-1, H + H^T = 2I exactly (diagonal all +1 and H_ij = -H_ji off the diagonal) and H H^T = nI in integer arithmetic; use two independent checkers. A matrix that is only equivalent to a skew one must be presented in skew form. If the claim is a Goethals-Seidel difference family with a skew block, expand it into the array with the verifier's own code and check the full matrix.
angles: Goethals-Seidel array with a cyclic difference family (v; k0, k1, k2, k3; lambda) whose first block is skew (X0 and -X0 partition Z_v minus 0); Đoković's order-292 matrix used blocks that are unions of cosets of the order-9 subgroup of Z_73^*.
Multiplier orbits: for prime v (89, 101, 107, 149, 179, 191, 193) the group Z_v^* has many subgroups; prescribing invariance reduces the search to orbit unions.
Good matrices, G-matrices and skew-propus families give skew matrices of order 4v from four circulants of order v; SAT+CAS found new good matrices (Bright, Đoković, Kotsireas, Ganesh 2019).
Amicable orthogonal designs with Seberry's theorem, Wallis's product and Kumar's skew 3(q+1) theorem: check whether an open order follows from a 2026 ingredient before searching.
pitfalls: A Hadamard matrix of the same order is not enough: 428, 668 and 716 have Hadamard matrices but, as far as these sources say, no skew one.
Skew means H + H^T = 2I (diagonal +1), not H = -H^T.
The 2007 Handbook table listed 63 for 69, and the Seberry-Yamada 2020 book lists some settled values as unknown; use the 2024-2026 lists.

The Đoković-Seberry census is not public; Kumar's README reports its statuses, and the survey's Table 3 row also says 'known for 4n with odd n < 250', which conflicts with its own smallest-open value 356 and with Đoković's list. Treat that phrase as a misprint and re-check every source before claiming.

Kumar's folder moves fast: 476 (v = 119) and 980 (v = 245) were added on 23-24 Oct 2026, after the survey, so the survey and Cati-Pasechnik still show them as open. Re-read skew/README.md and its commit history on the day of the claim.

targets.name: MOONSHOT - Three mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order 10 (is N(10) >= 3?)
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (SAT with proof certificates); partial wins laptop-days
targets.statement: N(n) is the largest number of mutually orthogonal Latin squares (MOLS) of order n. E. T. Parker constructed 2 MOLS(10) in 1959, and the nonexistence of a projective plane of order 10 together with Bruck's theorem gives N(10) <= 6. Whether 3 MOLS(10) exist is open: Bright, Keita and Stevens (Electron. J. Combin. 33(1) (2026), #P1.30, published 13 Feb 2026) call it a longstanding open problem. Known constraints: every square in such a triple has trivial symmetry group (McKay, Meynert and Myrvold), the code of any pair has rank exactly 37 (Dukes and Howard; Gill and Wanless), a 10 x 10 Latin square with a 5 x 5 subsquare has no orthogonal mate (Mann), and orthogonal 3 x 3 subsquares cannot extend (Parker). W. Myrvold (1999) split the case where one square has a 4 x 4 Latin subsquare into 28 mate-pattern type pairs and ruled out 20; Bright, Keita and Stevens re-derived those 20 by SAT and found explicit orthogonal pairs in each of the remaining 8, so those cases can only be closed by reasoning about the whole triple. The closest known near-triple (Egan and Wanless) has L1 orthogonal to both L2 and L3, with 91 of the 100 symbol pairs distinct when L2 and L3 are superimposed. This is a different problem from Erdős #723 (order 12), which the bank already lists.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only for three 10 x 10 arrays over {0..9}, each a Latin square, such that each of the three pairs is orthogonal (superimposing the two squares gives all 100 ordered symbol pairs), checked by two independent programs, with no 3 MOLS(10) reported at verification time on https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/view/v33i1p30 (re-fetched) or in a fresh arXiv search (direction: none; existence target). A proof that N(10) = 2, as a DRAT/LRAT certificate checked by drat-trim or cake_lpr on a CNF the skeptic regenerates from a documented encoding, also counts.

partial_wins.statement: A DRAT/LRAT certificate, on a CNF the skeptic regenerates from the encoding of Bright-Keita-Stevens or another documented one, that no orthogonal triple exists in at least one of Myrvold's eight remaining mate-pattern type pairs for a triple in which one square has a 4 x 4 Latin subsquare, provided that case is not already closed in the literature.

Three Latin squares L1, L2, L3 of order 10 with L1 orthogonal to L2 and to L3 such that superimposing L2 and L3 gives at least 92 distinct ordered symbol pairs (direction: max; Egan-Wanless: 91), checked exactly.

targets.verification_method: For each square check that every row and every column is a permutation of 0..9. For each pair (A, B) build the set {(A[i][j], B[i][j])} and require 100 elements. For p2, count the distinct pairs of L2 and L3 and recheck both orthogonalities with L1. For p1, regenerate the CNF from the stated encoding and case definition, run drat-trim (or cake_lpr for LRAT) on the supplied proof, and confirm the case matches Myrvold's classification as described in Section 2 of Bright-Keita-Stevens.
angles: Transversal-representation encoding (Bright-Keita-Stevens): an orthogonal mate of L is a decomposition of L into 10 disjoint transversals; a third square needs 10 disjoint transversals common to the first two.
Start from the orthogonal pairs found in Myrvold's eight open cases: search for 10 disjoint common transversals, and certify failures to earn p1.
Build the known structure in as constraints: trivial autotopism groups, rank-37 codes for each pair, no 5 x 5 subsquares; break symmetry only over the full isotopy and conjugacy action.
For p2, run local search over pairs (L2, L3) both orthogonal to a fixed L1, maximising distinct superimposed pairs, starting from the Egan-Wanless near-triple.
pitfalls: Orthogonal pairs of order 10 are plentiful; a pair alone is never a partial win.
Every square in a 3 MOLS(10) has trivial symmetry group, so searches that assume an automorphism or autotopism are provably empty.
N(12) and projective planes of order 12 belong to the separate Erdős #723 entry.
A SAT 'UNSAT' answer without a checked certificate is not a result.

targets.name: Butson Hadamard matrices BH(n,6): settle one of the undecided even orders below 100 (46, 74, 86, 94)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (2-circulant cyclotomic constructions, SAT/ILP over orbit structures; checking takes laptop-seconds)
targets.statement: A Butson Hadamard matrix BH(n,q) is an n x n matrix whose entries are q-th roots of unity with H H* = nI. For q = 6 there is no divisibility obstruction of Lam-Leung type, and F. Szöllősi conjectured that BH(2p,6) exists for every prime p. Czifra, Matolcsi and Szöllősi (arXiv:2511.11230, Nov 2025; J. Algebraic Combin. 64(2), 2026, Paper 29) gave a nonexistence criterion from positive definite functions on finite groups, found BH(18,14), and constructed 2-circulant BH(62,6), BH(82,6) and BH(146,6) from cyclotomic cosets; comparing the published tables, they state that BH(46,6), BH(74,6), BH(86,6) and BH(94,6) seem to be the remaining undecided even orders below 100, and that the smallest outstanding odd order is BH(31,6). Egan, Kotsireas, London and Ó Catháin restate the four even orders as open (arXiv:2610.27175, 19 Oct 2026, Problem 9). Egan and Ó Catháin's complete morphisms BH(n,7) -> BH(6n,6) (arXiv:2610.28394) do not reach these orders.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an explicit n x n matrix with entries in the sixth roots of unity (given as exponents 0..5 of w = exp(2 pi i/6)) for n in {46, 74, 86, 94}, whose rows are pairwise orthogonal under the Hermitian inner product, checked exactly in Z[w] by two independent programs, where no BH(n,6) of that order is reported at claim time in a fresh arXiv search or in the latest version of arXiv:2610.27175 (direction: none; existence target). A rigorous nonexistence proof for one of these orders (for example the Czifra-Matolcsi-Szöllősi criterion with a certified computation the skeptic re-runs) also counts.

partial_wins.statement: An explicit BH(31,6), the smallest outstanding odd order according to arXiv:2511.11230, checked exactly as in the main criterion.

targets.verification_method: Store the matrix as exponents e_ij in Z_6. For each pair of rows r != s count c_m = #{j : e_rj - e_sj = m mod 6} for m = 0..5. Since w^2 = w - 1 and w^3 = -1, the inner product sum_m c_m w^m equals (c0 - c2 - c3 + c5) + w(c1 + c2 - c4 - c5), so orthogonality holds exactly when c0 + c5 = c2 + c3 and c1 + c2 = c4 + c5. Check every pair of rows with two independent programs; no floating point is needed.
angles: 2-circulant cores over Z_p with entries assigned by cyclotomic cosets of F_p, the method of arXiv:2511.11230 for p = 31, 41 and 73; for p = 23, 37, 43 and 47 enumerate coset assignments exactly.
Use the positive-definite-function criterion of arXiv:2511.11230 as a pruning test inside an exact search, or to attempt a nonexistence proof at one of the four orders.
Model each entry as a variable in Z_6 and each row-pair condition as the two linear equations in the verification method; prescribe a group action to make SAT or ILP tractable.
Any BH(n,3) is a BH(n,6); also look for group-invariant forms suggested by Gauss-sum constructions (Ong and Schmidt, arXiv:2609.22754).
pitfalls: BH(62,6), BH(82,6) and BH(146,6) are settled. Real Hadamard matrices do not exist at these orders (n = 2 mod 4), and BH(n,4) matrices use a different alphabet.
The undecided list in arXiv:2511.11230 is stated tentatively ('seem to be'); check the tables it compares before claiming.
Numerical orthogonality to 1e-12 is not a proof; use exact counts.

targets.name: Small Steiner 3-designs: construct S(3,5,41), S(3,6,46) or S(3,5,50), the open cases with v <= 50
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (Kramer-Mesner with prescribed automorphism groups; checking takes laptop-seconds)
targets.statement: A Steiner system S(3,k,v) is a family of k-subsets of a v-set covering every 3-subset exactly once. Kiermaier, Krčadinac and Wassermann (arXiv:2509.23483, 27 Sep 2025) tabulate the 25 admissible parameter sets with v <= 50: 20 were known, S(3,7,37) does not exist (there is no inversive plane of order 6), and 4 were open. They constructed S(3,6,42) by extending Steiner 2-designs with prescribed extension groups, and tried the other three, S(3,6,46), S(3,5,41) and S(3,5,50), without success, finding many new derived designs S(2,5,45), S(2,4,40) and S(2,4,49) instead. Krčadinac's live table (web.math.pmf.unizg.hr/~krcko/results/steiner3.html, data set on Zenodo) still marks these three '?'. The same paper constructed rotational Steiner quadruple systems RoSQS(46) and RoSQS(92), leaving v = 56, 70, 82, 86 and 98 open below 100 in Ji and Zhu's table, and notes that v = 94 is the only open order below 100 for cyclic SQS. Liu and Feng (arXiv:2610.25951, 19 Oct 2026) settled the symmetric cyclic case, which does not reach 94 = 2*47 because 47 = 11 mod 12.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an explicit S(3,5,41) (1066 blocks of size 5 on 41 points), S(3,6,46) (759 blocks of size 6 on 46 points) or S(3,5,50) (1960 blocks of size 5 on 50 points) with every 3-subset of the point set in exactly one block, checked exhaustively by two independent programs, where Krčadinac's table (re-fetched) still marks the case '?' and a fresh arXiv search finds no construction (direction: none; existence target). A rigorous nonexistence proof (DRAT/LRAT on a regenerated CNF, or an exhaustive search the skeptic re-runs) also counts.

partial_wins.statement: A cyclic Steiner quadruple system CSQS(94): blocks of size 4 on Z_94 with every 3-subset in exactly one block and the block set invariant under x -> x + 1.
A rotational Steiner quadruple system RoSQS(v) for v in {56, 70, 82, 86, 98}: an SQS(v) on Z_(v-1) plus one fixed point whose block set is invariant under x -> x + 1 (fixing the extra point).

targets.verification_method: Read the blocks, check sizes and the block count C(v,3)/C(k,3), index every 3-subset by its combinatorial rank and require each to be covered exactly once. For p1 and p2 also apply the claimed automorphism to every block and check that the block set is unchanged. Use two independent checkers; then re-fetch the table and search arXiv.
angles: Extend the derived design: the blocks through one point of an S(3,k,v) form an S(2,k-1,v-1). The authors publish 10791 S(2,4,40), 1072 S(2,5,45) and 22080 S(2,4,49) used in their extension attempts; try extension groups they did not.

Kramer-Mesner with a prescribed group G: the design is a union of G-orbits of k-sets covering each G-orbit of 3-sets once; solve the 0/1 system with an exact-cover, SAT or ILP solver (the authors' GAP package Prescribed Automorphism Groups implements the method).
For CSQS(94) and RoSQS(v), the cyclic structure reduces the problem to choosing base blocks that cover each orbit of triples once, a moderate exact cover for modern SAT solvers.
pitfalls: S(3,6,42), RoSQS(46) and RoSQS(92) are already constructed; S(3,7,37) does not exist.

A CSQS(94) cannot be symmetric: Liu and Feng (arXiv:2610.25951) prove the Grannell-Griggs criterion as an iff, and 94 = 2*47 with 47 = 11 mod 12 fails it, so searches that assume the multiplier -1 fixes every block orbit are provably empty.
Admissibility of S(3,k,v) needs C(v-i,3-i)/C(k-i,3-i) integral for i = 0, 1, 2; recheck before moving to other parameters.
Check all C(v,3) triples, not only those through a fixed point.
Design files from the web page and Zenodo are data in GAP format; parse them, never run them.

targets.name: Legendre pairs: settle an open odd length below 200 (115, 145, 159, 161, 169, 175, 177, 185, 187, 195)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (compression, PSD filtering and SAT lifting; checking is instant)
targets.statement: A Legendre pair of odd length l is a pair of +-1 sequences A, B with PAF_A(s) + PAF_B(s) = -2 for every s = 1..l-1 (periodic autocorrelation); it gives a Hadamard matrix of order 2l + 2 (Fletcher, Gysin and Seberry), and one is conjectured to exist for every odd l. Balonin and Đoković (arXiv:2010.02829, 2020) listed the open l < 200 as 77, 85, 87, 91, 93, 115, 117, 123, 129, 133, 145, 147, 159, 161, 169, 175, 177, 185, 187, 195 and settled three; Turner, Kotsireas, Bulutoglu and Geyer found l = 77 (arXiv:2101.10918), Kotsireas and Koutschan 117, 129, 133 and 147 (arXiv:2101.03116), and Kotsireas, Koutschan, Bulutoglu, Arquette, Turner and Ryan 85 and 87 (arXiv:2111.02105 v3, 8 Apr 2024), leaving ten open values below 200: 115, 145, 159, 161, 169, 175, 177, 185, 187, 195; their two structured searches at 115 found nothing. Kotsireas, Koutschan and Winterhof (arXiv:2408.16318 v2, 2025) give 115 as the smallest unsettled length, and Egan, Kotsireas, London and Ó Catháin (arXiv:2610.27175, Oct 2026) list existence at every odd length as their Problem 1. Ramos, Hulak and de Queiroz (arXiv:2607.20765) studied l = 333 (order 668), an order since settled by other means.
targets.success_criterion: Success means explicit +-1 sequences A, B of a length l in {115, 145, 159, 161, 169, 175, 177, 185, 187, 195} with PAF_A(s) + PAF_B(s) = -2 for every s = 1..l-1, computed exactly by two independent programs, where no Legendre pair of that length is reported at claim time in a fresh arXiv search for 'Legendre pair' (direction: none; existence target).

partial_wins.statement: A certified exclusion of Legendre pairs of length 115 (or another listed length) in which both sequences are invariant under a stated nontrivial subgroup H of Z_l^*, or have a stated compression, where that exclusion is not already published (Section 4 of arXiv:2111.02105 reports two non-exhaustive searches at 115); delivered as code and logs the skeptic re-runs to the same empty result, or as a DRAT/LRAT certificate.

targets.verification_method: Check both sequences have length l and entries +-1; compute PAF_X(s) = sum_j x_j x_{j+s mod l} in integers for every s and require PAF_A(s) + PAF_B(s) = -2 for s = 1..l-1. Sanity check: (sum A)^2 + (sum B)^2 = 2, so both row sums are +-1. The value 2l + 2 is the PSD sum at nonzero frequencies, not at frequency 0. Calibrate the checker on two copies of the Legendre sequence of a prime p = 3 mod 4. Optionally negate the sequences so both row sums are 1, build the bordered two-circulant Hadamard matrix of order 2l + 2 (Fletcher, Gysin and Seberry; Theorem 4 of arXiv:2610.27175) and verify H H^T. Use two independent checkers.
angles: Compression: for l = m*d the d-compressions of A and B satisfy derived PAF and PSD conditions; enumerate compressed pairs and lift (115 = 5*23, 145 = 5*29, 159 = 3*53, 161 = 7*23, 169 = 13^2, 175 = 5^2*7, 177 = 3*59, 185 = 5*37, 187 = 11*17, 195 = 3*5*13).
Multiplier groups: assume invariance under a subgroup of Z_l^* (85 was found this way) and the balance conjecture of arXiv:2111.02105 for lengths divisible by 5.
PSD test: PSD_A(k) + PSD_B(k) = 2l + 2 at every nonzero frequency, used as a filter before exact checks.
Kotsireas' Problem 2 in arXiv:2610.27175 (uncompressing Legendre-symbol sequences of length p to a pair of length p*q^2) gives a structured route for l = 175 = 7*5^2.
pitfalls: l = 333 corresponds to order 668, which is settled; it is not part of this entry.
Quaternary Legendre pairs and generalised Legendre pairs of even length are different objects (see the quaternary entry).
PSD values computed in floating point are filters only; the final PAF check must be exact.

The J. Symbolic Comput. paper by Kotsireas, Gallardo-Cava, Gómez and Gómez-Pérez on Legendre pairs of length pq^2 (reference [60] of arXiv:2610.27175) was not read for this entry; check it for l = 175 = 7*5^2 and the other listed lengths before claiming.

DCP's crowd-sourced, prize-pool Legendre-pair hunts (jobs.dcp.dev/legendre117, finished; legendre153.dcp.dev, structured pairs of length 153) are live challenges at other lengths and are not part of this entry. Joining or submitting to them is an action only the human may take.

targets.name: Periodic Golay pairs: settle an undecided length up to 300 (smallest 106)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (multi-level compression and orderly generation; checking is instant)
targets.statement: A periodic Golay pair of length v is a pair of +-1 sequences A, B with PAF_A(s) + PAF_B(s) = 0 for s = 1..v-1; it gives a Hadamard matrix of order 2v. v must be even with v/2 a sum of two squares, and the Arasu-Xiang condition must hold. Every Golay number 2^a 10^b 26^c is a periodic Golay number. Đoković and Kotsireas (arXiv:1409.5969 v2, 2015) give the lengths then known as products of Golay numbers with S = {1, 34, 50, 58, 72, 74, 82, 122, 202, 226}, and list the sixteen lengths up to 300 that satisfy all necessary conditions but were undecided: 90, 106, 130, 146, 170, 178, 180, 194, 212, 218, 234, 250, 274, 290, 292, 298. Lumsden, Kotsireas and Bright (arXiv:2408.15611 v3, 16 Mar 2025) enumerated all periodic Golay pairs of every length up to 72 with multi-level compression (under 10 CPU-years), found the first pairs of length 90, and state that 106 is now the smallest undecided length. Because a Golay pair of length g and a periodic Golay pair of length v multiply to one of length gv (Đoković-Kotsireas), the length-2 Golay pair and the length-90 pairs also settle 180. Remaining undecided lengths up to 300: 106, 130, 146, 170, 178, 194, 212, 218, 234, 250, 274, 290, 292, 298.
targets.success_criterion: Success means explicit +-1 sequences A, B of a length v in {106, 130, 146, 170, 178, 194, 212, 218, 234, 250, 274, 290, 292, 298} with PAF_A(s) + PAF_B(s) = 0 for every s = 1..v-1, computed exactly by two independent programs, where no periodic Golay pair of that length is reported at claim time (fresh arXiv search for 'periodic Golay', and a check that v is not g*v' for a Golay number g > 1 and a newly settled length v') (direction: none; existence target).

partial_wins.statement: A complete enumeration, up to the equivalences used in arXiv:2408.15611, of the periodic Golay pairs of length 74 (the next admissible length after the published census of lengths up to 72), with code and counts the skeptic reproduces independently.

targets.verification_method: Check lengths and entries; compute PAF exactly and require every sum to be 0 for s = 1..v-1. Sanity check: (sum A)^2 + (sum B)^2 = 2v. Optionally build H = [[A, B], [-B^T, A^T]] from the two circulants and verify H H^T = 2vI. Use two independent checkers.
angles: Multi-level compression (Lumsden-Kotsireas-Bright): uncompress in several steps along a divisor chain where one exists (130 = 2*5*13, 170 = 2*5*17, 234 = 2*9*13, 250 = 2*125); for v = 2p (106, 146, 178, 194) only compression by 2 or p is available, and arXiv:2408.15611 introduces orderly-generation methods for such cases.
Supplementary difference sets 2-(v; r, s; lambda) with v = 2(r + s - lambda): search with a prescribed multiplier group, as Đoković and Kotsireas did for length 72.
Use the structural conjecture of arXiv:2408.15611 (proved for v < 100) to restrict candidate compressions.
Multiplication: any new length v' gives g*v' for every Golay number g; record all consequences.
pitfalls: Aperiodic Golay pairs are a stronger object (a Golay pair of length 106 is a cell of the Hadamard-ingredients entry); here the autocorrelation is cyclic.
90 and 180 are settled; lengths that fail the necessary conditions (v/2 not a sum of two squares, Arasu-Xiang) are impossible, not open.
PSD tests in floating point are filters only.

targets.name: Abelian difference sets: settle an 'Open' group entry with v <= 1000 in Gordon's La Jolla Difference Set Repository
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (orbit-restricted exact searches; character-sum and field-descent computations)
targets.statement: A (v,k,lambda) difference set in an abelian group G of order v is a k-subset D such that every non-identity element is a difference d - d' (d, d' in D) in exactly lambda ways. Daniel Gordon's La Jolla Difference Set Repository (dmgordon.org/difference-sets; data file ds.json in github.com/dmgordo/difference-sets, last commit 2026-04-24; site updated 2026-09-03) lists every parameter set with v < 100000 passing the counting, Schützenberger and Bruck-Ryser-Chowla tests, for each abelian group, with status Yes, All, No or Open. At this check ds.json held 1,085,783 group entries, 102,719 of them Open; 106 Open entries (51 parameter sets) have v <= 1000.
