The smallest include the Paley-Hadamard parameters (243,121,60) in Z3 x Z9 x Z9 and (343,171,85) in Z7 x Z49; the Menon parameters (400,190,90) in Z10 x Z40, Z20 x Z20 and Z2 x Z10 x Z20; (416,166,66), (425,160,60) and (448,150,50) in several groups; and the cyclic cases (465,145,45), (469,208,92), (639,232,84), (703,325,150), (741,185,46), (781,300,115), (910,405,180), (921,161,28), (936,375,150), (944,369,144), (963,222,51), (981,196,39) and (990,345,120). Settling an entry needs a new construction or a nonexistence argument beyond the Turyn self-conjugacy, Lander and Schmidt field-descent results the repository already applies. Gordon's circulant weighing matrix, signed and relative difference set repositories belong to the separate circulant-weighing-matrices-open entry.
targets.success_criterion: Success means, for an entry DS(v,k,lambda,G) with v <= 1000 whose status is 'Open' in the live ds.json (re-downloaded from github.com/dmgordo/difference-sets immediately before claiming), either (a) an explicit k-subset D of G, written in the group's invariant-factor coordinates, such that every non-identity element of G arises exactly lambda times as d - d' with d, d' in D, checked by two independent programs, or (b) a nonexistence proof for that group whose computational part (character sums, field descent, exhaustive search or a DRAT/LRAT certificate) the skeptic re-runs; and in both cases a fresh arXiv search shows the entry is not already settled in the literature, including by Menon-Turyn product theorems, Davis-Jedwab recursive constructions or Schmidt's 2026 Gauss-type Hadamard difference sets (arXiv:2609.07088) (direction: none; existence target).

partial_wins.statement: The same for an 'Open' entry with 1000 < v < 100000, after checking that it does not follow from a known product or recursive theorem (the repository has not applied all of them at large v; see pitfalls).

targets.verification_method: Parse G from the entry name (invariant factors, e.g. [3,9,9], or the entry's G_rep if given) and represent elements as tuples modulo the factors. For a claimed D check |D| = k, tally all k(k-1) differences and require every non-identity element to appear exactly lambda times; cross-check with |chi(D)|^2 = k - lambda for every nontrivial character, computed exactly in a cyclotomic field or numerically with a rounding margin next to the exact tally. Use two independent programs; ds_code.py may be read for conventions, never executed. For nonexistence claims re-run every computational step and check each cited theorem's hypotheses.
angles: Multiplier theorems (Hall and its abelian-group versions): where a prime p dividing n = k - lambda qualifies as a numerical multiplier, D can be taken as a union of orbits of x -> p x, turning the search into a small exact cover.
Automate character-sum and field-descent nonexistence tests over every Open group with v <= 1000, as Tan did for circulant weighing matrices; an entry marked Open may fall to a sharper bound.
Paley-Hadamard entries (4n-1, 2n-1, n-1) in non-elementary abelian p-groups (243 in Z3 x Z9 x Z9, 343 in Z7 x Z49): try cyclotomic and Galois-ring constructions, or prove exponent bounds.
Menon entries (400, 576, 676, 784, 900): combine building sets with the Davis-Jedwab recursive framework, or prove exponent bounds.
pitfalls: The repository lags theory at large v: DS(2304,1128,552) in Z4 x Z4 x Z12 x Z12 is Open in ds.json but follows from the Menon-Turyn product theorem applied to (16,6,2) in Z4 x Z4 and (144,66,30) in Z12 x Z12. Such entries are corrections to report, not wins.
Status is per group: a difference set with the same parameters in another group of order v does not settle the entry.
Signed, relative and circulant-weighing objects belong to the separate circulant-weighing-matrices-open entry.
Most small Open entries have resisted decades of work; budget accordingly and prefer automated nonexistence sweeps to blind search.

targets.name: MOONSHOT - Matbench Discovery: beat the live best Combined Performance Score (0.912) with an openly released interatomic potential (the F1 0.931 and κ_SRME 0.0648 records are partial wins)
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (training a competitive universal potential is GPU-weeks; scoring a finished model is GPU-hours: ~215k WBM relaxations, 103 phono3py runs and the geometry task)
targets.statement: Matbench Discovery (Janosh Riebesell, Rhys Goodall, Philipp Benner, Yuan Chiang, Bowen Deng, Alpha Lee, Gerbrand Ceder, Mark Asta, Anubhav Jain and Kristin Persson; Nat. Mach. Intell. 7, 836 (2025), arXiv:2308.14920) is the main public leaderboard for universal machine-learned interatomic potentials. Models relax the 256,963 hypothetical WBM crystals of Hai-Chen Wang, Silvana Botti and Miguel Marques (npj Comput. Mater. 7, 12, 2021) and classify them as stable or unstable against the Materials Project convex hull. The headline subset is 215,488 unique prototypes, 32,942 of them stable. A phonon task scores lattice thermal conductivity on 103 PhononDB-PBE crystals by κ_SRME (range 0-2; Balázs Póta, Paramvir Ahlawat, Gábor Csányi and Michele Simoncelli, arXiv:2408.00755). A geometry task scores the normalised StructureMatcher RMSD to DFT-relaxed structures. The site's Combined Performance Score is CPS = 0.5*F1 + 0.4*(1 - κ_SRME/2) + 0.1*clip(1 - RMSD/0.15, 0, 1), as defined in site/src/lib/combined-scores.svelte.ts. All test labels are public, so a finished model can be scored locally. Live table for the 2026-10-28 update (default view, unique prototypes, 43 of 53 eligible models; repository last commit 2026-10-19): - Best CPS 0.912 and best κ_SRME 0.0648: Prophet-OAME-MBD (Kairos Materials: Junfu Tan, Yemin Yu, Kejie Bao, Ziheng Lu; added 2026-09-13). Next on CPS are TECE-OAM-RRA-1.0 at 0.908 and EquFlashV2 at 0.907. - Best F1 0.931: EquiformerV3+DeNS-OAM (Yi-Lun Liao, Tess Smidt and co-workers, arXiv:2604.09130; 2026-04-07). - Best RMSD 0.0575: TECE-OAM-RRA-1.0 and GRACE-3L-OAM-L. - Among models trained on MPtrj alone, best CPS 0.840 and κ_SRME 0.2114 are DPA-4.0.1-Pro-MPtrj (Tiancheng Li, Duo Zhang, Linfeng Zhang, Han Wang; 2026-06-11), and best F1 0.863 is EquiformerV3+DeNS-MP. The leaders train on 100M+ DFT frames, so the full win is a moonshot for one machine; the MPtrj-only and small-model partial wins are the realistic entry points.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an openly released model (weights and inference code) plus the three official prediction files: WBM discovery energies, geometry-optimisation structures and the 103-material κ file. Its Combined Performance Score, recomputed by the checker with the official matbench-discovery package and the default CPS weights on the unique-prototype WBM test set, must be STRICTLY HIGHER (direction: max) than the best CPS on the live leaderboard re-fetched immediately before claiming, by at least 0.005 (0.912 on 2026-10-28). No training data may contain any WBM test structure or WBM-derived relaxation, or DFT force constants of the 103 κ benchmark materials. Training sets must be ones the repository lists in data/datasets.yml, or new data the checker audits by protostructure matching against WBM. Re-running the model on a checker-chosen random sample of 500 WBM structures and 3 κ materials must reproduce the submitted predictions: at least 95% of sampled final energies within 5 meV/atom, and κ within 2%. Submitting to the leaderboard is a GitHub pull request and is left to a human.

partial_wins.statement: Beat the live best discovery F1 on the unique-prototype set (0.931 on 2026-10-28) by at least 0.005, under the same training-data and reproduction rules, whatever the CPS.
Beat the live best κ_SRME (0.0648 on 2026-10-28) by at least 5% relative under the same rules, with a model whose unique-prototype F1 is at least 0.85.

MPtrj-only track: a model trained on MPtrj alone (no OMat24, Alexandria, ELEMENTA or other DFT data, and no distillation from a model trained on them) that beats the best MPtrj-only row on the live page by the full-win margins in CPS (0.840 on 2026-10-28), F1 (0.863, margin 0.005) or κ_SRME (0.2114, margin 5% relative).

Small-model track: a model of at most 1,000,000 parameters, trained on MPtrj only, whose CPS beats every listed model of at most 1M parameters by at least 0.01 (best on 2026-10-28: Nequix MP PFT, 708k parameters, CPS 0.755).

targets.verification_method: The checker installs the matbench-discovery package at the commit named in the claim. It recomputes F1, DAF and MAE on the unique-prototype set, κ_SRME on the 103 PhononDB materials and RMSD on the geometry task from the submitted files, recomputes CPS with the published weights, and compares the result with the live table. It then re-runs the model on the sampled WBM structures and κ materials to confirm the files came from the model (GPU-hours). Finally it audits leakage by protostructure-matching the declared training sets against the WBM summary the package ships.
angles: Fine-tune an open-weight leader (for example eSEN-30M-OAM, GRACE-3L-OAM-L, PET-OAM-XL or Nequip-OAM-XL; check each licence) on phonon-relevant data such as finite-displacement supercells of low-symmetry crystals. κ_SRME carries 40% of CPS, and the second-best κ_SRME (0.0927) is 43% worse than the leader's.
Ensembling or weight averaging of strong models near the hull: F1 is decided by the few percent of WBM crystals within ~50 meV/atom of the hull.
Smoothness and energy conservation: third-order force constants punish non-conservative forces and kinks at the radial cutoff, so conservative force heads and smooth envelopes are a cheap κ fix.
Small-model track: distil an MPtrj-only teacher into a student of at most 1M parameters on teacher-labelled rattled MPtrj structures. Under the p4 rule the teacher must itself be MPtrj-only.
Cross-domain (model compression): quantisation-aware training and pruning schedules from vision transformers keep accuracy at a fraction of the inference cost, which matters for 215k relaxations.
pitfalls: The site warns that CPS is not a stable metric and its weights or components may change. A claim states the CPS version and weights in force when it is made, and reports F1, κ_SRME and RMSD separately.
Full-test-set (256,963) and unique-prototype (215,488) numbers differ, especially DAF; the full win uses unique prototypes.

Training data containing WBM structures or their relaxations, such as unfiltered Alexandria releases, invalidate a claim. Use the filtered sets listed in the repository (sAlex is the WBM-filtered subsample) or audit by protostructure matching.
κ_SRME depends on the benchmark's phono3py settings (supercells, displacement amplitude, symmetry tolerance); run the repository's models/run_kappa.py unmodified.
Generating predictions on CPU takes weeks (215k relaxations); budget GPU time before starting.
Leaderboard submission is a GitHub pull request, a human action. Agents claim only the locally verified result.

targets.name: Kob-Andersen binary Lennard-Jones crystals: a periodic 80:20 structure with lower zero-pressure energy than the Cambridge Cluster Database records (-7.4903 per atom at N = 60, -7.5015 at N = 320)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: The Kob-Andersen (KA) 80:20 binary Lennard-Jones mixture is the standard model glass-former (Walter Kob and Hans C. Andersen, PRL 73, 1376, 1994; sigma_AA = 1, sigma_AB = 0.8, sigma_BB = 0.88, eps_AA = 1, eps_AB = 1.5, eps_BB = 0.5). Its crystalline ground state is a crystal-structure-prediction benchmark. Thomas Middleton, Javier Hernández-Rojas, Paul Mortenson and David Wales (PRB 64, 184201, 2001) posted low-energy crystals for 60-, 256- and 320-atom periodic cells at number density 1.2 on the Cambridge Cluster Database (CCD). Maximilian Amsler and Stefan Goedecker (J. Chem. Phys. 133, 224104, 2010; arXiv:1007.2003) then ran variable-cell minima hopping at zero pressure, with each pair potential cut at 2.5 sigma_ab and smoothed by the Stoddard-Ford quadratic term. They found several thousand structures below the earlier ones. The CCD index links their putative ground states as BLJ60, BLJ256 and BLJ320 (files dated 2011-02-28): - N = 60 (48 A + 12 B; a 30-atom P2_1/m primitive cell): -7.4903 eps_AA per atom. - N = 256 (205 A + 51 B; P1): -7.4281. - N = 320 (256 A + 64 B; a 40-atom Bbmm primitive cell): -7.5015. An independent lattice sum written for this update reproduces -7.490330, -7.428094 and -7.501546. Later KA crystal studies do not test these records: the Pedersen-Schrøder-Dyre phase diagram (PRL 120, 165501, 2018) and the USPEX convex hull of Yu. D. Fomin and N. M. Chtchelkatchev (arXiv:2409.00710, 2024) both use a plain truncate-and-shift at P* = 10.19. The Fernández-Harrowell picture of coexisting fcc A and CsCl AB puts the phase-separated thermodynamic limit at zero pressure at or below about -7.585 per atom. That value is the lever rule over lattice sums with this potential (fcc A -6.80362, CsCl AB -8.75686). A-rich compounds that Fernández and Harrowell (2004) and Pedersen et al. report as low in energy (PuBr3-, Fe3C- and Ni3P-type A3B, Al2Cu-type A2B) could make the limit lower still if they fall below the fcc/CsCl tie line under this truncation. Lower energies therefore exist for large cells, and the fixed-N records are about fitting two phases and their interfaces into 60 or 320 atoms. No published improvement on the hosted records was found.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a periodic cell (lattice vectors and Cartesian coordinates to at least 12 significant digits, with A/B labels) containing exactly N = 60 atoms (48 A + 12 B) or N = 320 atoms (256 A + 64 B). The checker computes its potential energy per atom E/N as a full lattice sum (all periodic images within the cutoff, never minimum-image) of phi_ab(r) = 4 eps_ab [(sigma_ab/r)^12 - (sigma_ab/r)^6] + 4 eps_ab [6 (sigma_ab/rc)^12 - 3 (sigma_ab/rc)^6] (r/rc)^2 - 4 eps_ab [7 (sigma_ab/rc)^12 - 4 (sigma_ab/rc)^6] for r < rc = 2.5 sigma_ab, and zero beyond, with the KA parameters. After the checker's variable-cell relaxation to residual forces below 1e-8 and stress below 1e-7 (reduced units), E/N must be STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) by at least 1e-4 than the checker's re-evaluation of the CCD-hosted structure for that N, re-fetched immediately before claiming (-7.490330 for N = 60 and -7.501546 for N = 320 on 2026-10-28). The target pressure is zero, so enthalpy equals energy and cell shape and volume are free. A literature search must find no lower published value for the same N, potential and truncation, and the search is reported with the claim.

partial_wins.statement: A periodic cell with any N from 321 to 5,000 and exactly N_A = 4 N_B whose relaxed E/N, under the same potential and relaxation rules, is below -7.501546 (the lowest value hosted for any size) by at least 1e-3, reported with its N. Phase-separated fcc-A/CsCl-AB arrangements approach about -7.585 as N grows, so this locates the cell size at which coexistence first wins.

targets.verification_method: Checker script, under 5 minutes on a laptop: parse the cell, assert the composition, compute E/N by a float64 lattice sum (re-checked in mpmath at 30 digits for the final value), compute forces and the virial stress, and re-run a variable-cell FIRE/BFGS relaxation. Calibrate on the three hosted files first: they must reproduce -7.490330, -7.428094 and -7.501546 to within 1e-5.
angles: Interface engineering: build fcc-A/CsCl-AB (or fcc-A plus an A3B-type compound) slab-coexistence cells with commensurate interfaces, scan interface orientations and strain matching, and relax them at zero pressure.
Variable-cell random structure search (AIRSS-like) or genetic algorithms with symmetry constraints on 20- to 80-atom cells, then tile the winners to N = 60 or 320.
Seed from the 40-atom Bbmm BLJ320 cell and the 30-atom BLJ60 cell; add A/B identity-swap moves to minima hopping.
Cross-domain (materials interfaces): compute fcc(A)|CsCl(AB) interface energies for candidate orientations first, then predict the N at which slabs beat -7.5015 before searching.
pitfalls: Truncation matters. The records use the Stoddard-Ford quadratic smoothing at 2.5 sigma_ab: not the plain KA truncate-and-shift, not RUMD's linear shifted force, and not the 1.842 cutoff column on the same page. Energies under different truncations are not comparable.

The Middleton et al. fixed-density (1.2) table on the same CCD page is stale. Uniformly rescaling the hosted 320-atom structure to density 1.2 already gives -7.4077 (Stoddard-Ford, cutoff 2.5), below the tabulated -7.33, so beating a density-1.2 cell is not a win here.
The 30- and 40-atom primitive cells are about 1.1 sigma thick along one axis, so the energy needs full image sums; minimum-image code silently drops neighbours.
Composition must be exact (60: 48/12; 320: 256/64). A 4:1 cell of another size counts only under p1.

The hosted files are already zero-pressure minima of this potential (residual forces about 3e-7 and stress about 1e-8 in reduced units, checked for this update). Re-relaxing them gains nothing, so a win must be a different basin.

The hosted BLJ256 (P1, -7.4281) is far from optimal, which is why N = 256 is not a target. A coherent fcc-A/CsCl-AB column stacked along [001] with one atom per layer (205 A + 51 B) already relaxes at zero pressure to -7.4911.

Coherent [001] (Bain-path) stacking of fcc A and CsCl AB cannot reach the records. The in-plane mismatch between fcc A (a/sqrt(2) = 1.1006) and CsCl AB (a = 1.0422) is about 5.5% and costs strain energy. Such columns level off near -7.4957 per atom: -7.4890 at N = 60 and -7.4944 at N = 320. Strain relief, other interface orientations or other A-rich motifs are needed.

targets.name: Data-efficient catalysis on Open Catalyst (JARVIS ocp10k): predict OC20 relaxed adsorption energies on the 24,943 val-ID systems from 10,000 training systems with MAE below ALIGNN's 0.7623 eV
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (CPU) or GPU-hours; 10,000 training adsorbate-slab systems of ~80 atoms
targets.statement: The Open Catalyst 2020 dataset (Lowik Chanussot, Abhishek Das, Siddharth Goyal, Zachary Ulissi, C. Lawrence Zitnick and co-workers; ACS Catal. 11, 6059, 2021; arXiv:2010.09990) defines IS2RE: predict the DFT (RPBE) relaxed adsorption energy of an adsorbate-surface system from its initial structure. Its official 10k training subset is the data-poor regime, where the paper's learning curves are flattest. The JARVIS-Leaderboard task ocp10k_relaxed_energy (Kamal Choudhary et al., NIST) fixes this with public labels. Train is the 10,000 OC20 IS2RE 10k systems (ids ocp-1..ocp-10000); test is the 24,943 OC20 IS2RE val_id systems (ocp-34944..ocp-59886). The benchmark's val ids (ocp-10001..ocp-34943) duplicate the test set label for label, as verified for this update, because the conversion script reads val_id twice. Live best MAE is 0.7623 eV by ALIGNN (2023-01-14), then OCP's CGCNN 0.9873 and SchNet 1.0578. Published 10k-only results on val_id are all worse: - The OCP model zoo (v0.1.0 MODELS.md) lists DimeNet++ 0.8837, CGCNN 0.9881, DimeNet 1.0117 and SchNet 1.059 eV. - Alvaro Carbonero, Alexandre Duval, Victor Schmidt, Santiago Miret and co-workers (arXiv:2310.06682, Table 2) report DimeNet++ at 0.851 eV in-domain. The companion ocp100k task (100,000 training systems, same test set) is led by ALIGNN at 0.6289 eV; the OCP zoo's 100k DimeNet++ scores 0.6388. Both pages were HTTP 200 for this update, with no entries since January 2023.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a trained model, its training script and predictions for all 24,943 test ids of ocp10k_relaxed_energy. The MAE recomputed by the checker against the benchmark json must be STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than the best MAE on the live task page re-fetched immediately before claiming (0.7623 eV on 2026-10-28). The margin must be at least 3% relative AND exceed the half-width of a 1,000-sample paired bootstrap 90% interval of the MAE difference against the best listed predictions (the CSV linked on the page). All learned parameters must come only from the 10,000 train ids: no pretrained weights; no OC20, OC22, OC25, OC20-Dense, ODAC, OMat24, MPtrj, OMol25 or other DFT data; and no use at all of the duplicated val ids, including for early stopping. Model selection uses a held-out part of the 10,000 train ids. Physics featurisers whose parameters were not fitted to adsorbate-surface DFT data, such as GFN-xTB or GFN-FF single points of the initial structure, are allowed. Because the JARVIS split is the standard OC20 IS2RE 10k train / val_id split, the claim must also report, and beat by the same margin, every published from-scratch 10k-only val_id energy MAE found by a literature search (including the OCP model-zoo and arXiv:2310.06682 values above). Re-running the saved model must reproduce the predictions to 1e-4 eV.

partial_wins.statement: The same margin over 0.7623 eV for a model that starts from a pretrained universal potential documented to contain no adsorbate-surface systems in its training data, fine-tuned only on the 10,000 train ids. Examples are MPtrj-only or OMat24-plus-sAlex models, with training sets named in the claim; UMA and any weights trained on OC20, OC22 or OC25 are excluded.

The from-scratch rules on ocp100k_relaxed_energy (100,000 train ids, the same 24,943 test systems, and again a val set identical to test): beat the live best 0.6289 eV by 3% relative and beat the OCP model zoo's 100k DimeNet++ value of 0.6388 eV.

targets.verification_method: Checker, under 30 minutes plus inference time: download ocp10k_relaxed_energy.json.zip from the jarvis_leaderboard repository, take the 24,943 test ids, and recompute the MAE and the paired bootstrap against the best listed CSV. Then audit the training script for any val or test id and any external data, and re-run inference on a random 1,000-structure sample to confirm reproducibility. Structures come from the jarvis-tools 'ocp10k' dataset or directly from the OC20 IS2RE 10k and val_id LMDBs (fairchem); the LMDBs carry the same initial positions plus OC20 tags.
angles: Physics priors for few-shot catalysis: binding-atom coordination, generalised coordination numbers, element-level d-band proxies and adsorbate scaling relations (O*, OH* and OOH* energies correlate) as features for a boosted model.
Equivariant message passing restricted to the adsorbate and the top surface layer, since the OC20 subsurface atoms (tag 0) add cost but little signal at 10k.
Delta-learning on a cheap physics baseline: a GFN-FF or GFN-xTB adsorption-energy estimate from the initial structure, with the 10,000 labels fitting the residual.
Symmetry augmentation: equivalent adsorption sites, surface-normal rotations and periodic-image shifts.
Cross-domain (few-shot learning): meta-learning across adsorbate types, or Gaussian-process heads on learned embeddings for calibrated small-data regression.
pitfalls: The val split is the test set under different ids. Using it for early stopping, hyperparameter search or ensembling is leakage; ALIGNN's own run script took its 100-structure validation set from the test rows.
OC20 val_id labels are public in OC20 itself, and many OC20, OC22 and UMA checkpoints were trained or validated on val_id systems. Any such weights invalidate the full win and p1.
The JARVIS structures drop OC20's adsorbate/surface/subsurface tags and fixed-atom flags. Rebuild them from the OC20 LMDBs, because element-based guesses fail on carbides, nitrides and hydrides.
Targets are adsorption energies relative to gas-phase references, not total energies; do not mix in total-energy datasets.

jarvis-tools downloads its datasets from figshare, which answered this update's scripted fetch with HTTP 202 and an empty body (a bot check). Fetch it honestly in a browser or use the OC20 LMDBs; never work around the check.

targets.name: JARVIS-Leaderboard MOF tasks: beat the best test MAE for GCMC CO2 uptake in hypothetical MOFs (0.01 and 2.5 bar) or for the PBE band gap of QMOF frameworks
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (gradient boosting on pore and chemistry descriptors) to laptop-days (graph networks on 110k MOFs)
targets.statement: Three metal-organic-framework (MOF) tasks on the JARVIS-Leaderboard (Kamal Choudhary et al., NIST; npj Comput. Mater. 10, 93, 2024) have fixed public splits and have not moved since May 2023: - hmof_max_co2_adsp and hmof_min_co2_adsp: CO2 uptake (mol/kg) at 2.5 bar and 0.01 bar for 137,651 of the 137,953 hypothetical MOFs of Christopher Wilmer, Randall Snurr and co-workers. The labels come from GCMC isotherms (RASPA, UFF framework, TraPPE CO2) as curated in MOFX-DB (N. Scott Bobbitt, Randall Snurr and co-workers, J. Chem. Eng. Data 2023). Split 110,121/13,765/13,765. - qmof_bandgap: PBE band gaps (eV) of 20,424 frameworks from the QMOF database (Andrew Rosen, Justin Notestein, Randall Snurr and co-workers, Matter 4, 1578, 2021). Split 16,340/2,042/2,042. The pressures and the force field are documented by Kamal Choudhary, Taner Yildirim, Daniel Siderius, Gilad Kusne, Austin McDannald and Diana Ortiz-Montalvo (Comput. Mater. Sci. 210, 111388, 2022; arXiv:2112.10231). Best listed test MAE, checked live for this update: - 2.5 bar: 0.4622 mol/kg by matminer_xgboost (team UofT, 2023-05-22), then ALIGNN 0.4765 and matminer_rf 0.5233. - 0.01 bar: 0.0383 mol/kg by ALIGNN (2023-01-14), then xgboost 0.0438 and rf 0.0465. - QMOF: 0.2019 eV by ALIGNN, then xgboost 0.3421 and rf 0.3618. The QMOF page's column is headed 'ACC', but the contribution files are test-mae. The QMOF authors' benchmark page lists CGCNN at 0.270 ± 0.011 eV on QMOF v13 with an 80% training split, which is not comparable with this split. Train-median predictors score 2.22, 0.090 and 0.946 on these test sets.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a trained model, its training script and test predictions for one of hmof_max_co2_adsp, hmof_min_co2_adsp or qmof_bandgap. The test MAE, recomputed by the checker on the official test ids of the benchmark json in jarvis_leaderboard/benchmarks/AI/SinglePropertyPrediction/, must be STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than the best MAE on that task's live page re-fetched immediately before claiming. The margin must be at least 5% relative AND exceed the half-width of a 1,000-sample paired bootstrap 90% interval of the MAE difference against the best listed predictions. The model is trained only on the train (and val) ids. No external data may contain labels for the test frameworks: no MOFX-DB or hMOF isotherms, no QMOF database properties, and no checkpoints fine-tuned on either. For the two hMOF tasks, no adsorption simulation of test structures is allowed (GCMC, Widom insertion, or energy-grid Henry coefficients with any CO2 force field), and end-to-end inference on all 13,765 test MOFs must take at most 24 CPU-core-hours, timed by the checker. Re-running the saved model must reproduce the predictions to 1e-6. The claim must also report, and beat, any published MAE on the identical JARVIS split found by a literature search.

partial_wins.statement: One model architecture and feature set, changed only by refitting per task, that beats the live best on both hMOF tasks at once by at least 2% relative each, under the same rules.

Reproduction audit: retrain the listed best entry for one of the three tasks with its published run.sh on the official split, and report a test MAE that differs from the posted value by more than 5% relative, with all outputs saved.

targets.verification_method: Checker, under 1 hour on CPU for a boosted-tree model: download the benchmark json.zip, load structures from the jarvis-tools 'hmof' or 'qmof' dataset, and run the saved model on the test ids. Recompute the MAE and the paired bootstrap against the best CSV linked on the page, time the inference, and audit the training script and feature code for test labels or forbidden simulations.
angles: Pore-geometry descriptors from Zeo++ (largest cavity and pore-limiting diameters, accessible surface area, void fraction, pore-size distribution) plus revised-autocorrelation (RAC) chemistry descriptors of nodes and linkers in a gradient-boosted model. Uptake at 2.5 bar is mostly geometry plus framework charge density.
For 0.01 bar (the Henry regime) the label tracks strong binding sites: features for open metal sites, polar functional groups (-NH2, -OH, -F) and pores near 4-5 A.
Frozen embeddings from pretrained MOF models (MOFTransformer, PMTransformer), allowed only after an audit shows their pretraining used no hMOF or QMOF labels.
QMOF: gaps are set by linker frontier orbitals and metal d states, so try a small graph network on the building-block (node/linker) graph or linker-level electronic descriptors.
Cross-domain (tabular ML): heavy-tailed targets favour a log transform with Huber loss and stacked ensembles.
pitfalls: The geometric hMOF tasks on the same leaderboard (LCD, PLD, void fraction, surface areas) are deterministic functions of the structure that Zeo++ computes exactly, so they are excluded; only the CO2 and band-gap tasks count.
MOFX-DB publishes the full hMOF isotherms and QMOF publishes all band gaps. Any model touching those for test ids is leaked, and text or LLM embeddings of MOF names may have memorised them.
GCMC labels carry Monte Carlo noise (1,000 production cycles), which bounds achievable MAE at 0.01 bar; small relative gains there can be noise, hence the paired bootstrap.
The QMOF page header says 'ACC', but the metric is MAE in eV, so lower is better.
Structures download from figshare through jarvis-tools. If figshare shows a bot check, fetch the file in a browser and never work around the check.

targets.name: OBELiX experimental Li solid-electrolyte ionic conductivity: beat the published best test MAE of 1.59 log10(S/cm) on the official 121-entry test split
targets.compute_profile: laptop-minutes
targets.statement: OBELiX is a curated set of 599 synthesized lithium solid electrolytes with experimentally measured room-temperature ionic conductivity, composition, space group and lattice parameters, plus CIFs for 321 entries. It was built by Félix Therrien, Jamal Abou Haibeh, Divya Sharma, Rhiannon Hendley, Leah Wairimu Mungai, Sun Sun, Alain Tchagang, Jiang Su, Samuel Huberman, Yoshua Bengio, Hongyu Guo, Alex Hernández-García and Homin Shin (Mila and NRC Canada; arXiv:2502.14234 v2, 2025-10-01; Digital Discovery 2026, issue 2). It ships an official leakage-controlled split, public on GitHub: 478 train and 121 test entries, 67 of the test entries with CIFs. The metric is the MAE of log10(sigma_RT / S cm^-1). Following the package's replace_text_IC in obelix/utils.py, the 8 test labels recorded as ' < 1E-10' are scored as 1e-15, which reproduces the paper's 2.16 median-predictor baseline. Best published test MAE (Table S1 of arXiv v2) is a random forest at 1.59 on the full test set (1.85 on the CIF subset), then an MLP at 1.72. All 3D models are worse on the CIF subset, the best being pretrained CGCNN at 2.52; the others are PaiNN, SchNet, M3GNet, SO3Net, CGCNN and their pretrained or disorder-aware variants. The paper puts the experimental reproducibility floor at about 0.41, the mean absolute deviation across remeasured materials. A January 2026 follow-up (Haewon Kim, Taekgi Lee, Seongeun Hong, Kyeong-Ho Kim and Yongchul G. Chung, arXiv:2601.10997v2) reports MAE 0.543 (gradient-boosted trees) and 0.657 (fine-tuned Llama-3.1-8B), but on its own structure-labeled set of 499 entries and its own split. An ICML 2026 paper (Jiyeon Kim, Byungju Lee and Won-Yong Shin, arXiv:2605.09311, code at github.com/jykim-git/MD) reports 1.388 on OBELiX (its own random forest re-run: 1.608), using SevenNet structure embeddings and pretraining on MD-simulated Li mean-square displacements; its preprocessing keeps only the CIF test entries with numeric labels and drops all 8 ' < 1E-10' entries (all 8 have CIFs), so it scores 59 entries on a different metric and does not set the bar. No result on the official split and metric below 1.59 was found for this update; the repository README and test files are live (HTTP 200).
targets.success_criterion: Success means a model trained only on the 478 official train entries, with labels converted by obelix's replace_text_IC and no other conductivity data of any kind. Hyperparameters are chosen by cross-validation inside the train set, and the final model and its hash are published before the test file is scored. Its MAE of log10 sigma on all 121 official test entries, recomputed by the checker, must be STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than 1.59 by at least 10% relative (MAE <= 1.431). It must also clear the half-width of a 2,000-sample paired bootstrap 90% interval of the MAE difference against the checker's re-run of the repository's benchmark/RF.py. Finally, it must beat every published MAE on the official split that a literature search finds, including the journal version's table if its numbers differ from arXiv v2.

partial_wins.statement: A structure-aware model whose input includes the atomic positions from the CIF (a graph network, a universal-potential embedding or crystal-graph features; models that use only composition, space group or lattice parameters do not count) that beats the random forest's 1.85 on the 67-entry CIF test subset by at least 10% relative (MAE <= 1.665), under the same rules.

A model of the p1 kind, trained only on the 254 CIF-bearing train entries, that beats the best published 3D geometric model (pretrained CGCNN, 2.52 on the 67-entry CIF test subset) by at least 20% relative (MAE <= 2.016), under the same training-data, hashing and reproduction rules. The 20% margin replaces the bootstrap, and only published 3D geometric models are compared. Composition models are excluded here because the random forest retrained on the same 254 entries already reaches 1.87 on that subset (arXiv v2, Section 4).

targets.verification_method: Checker, under 10 minutes: install obelix-data or fetch train.csv and test.csv from the repository, and convert labels with replace_text_IC. Re-run the claim's training script from scratch and confirm the model hash. Score the 121 test entries, re-run benchmark/RF.py for the paired bootstrap, and search the code for any external conductivity source (the Liverpool ionic-conductivity database, LiIonDB, Materials Project or ICSD property lookups).
angles: Li-transport physics from the CIF: Li-Li distances, Li site fraction, bond-valence-site-energy migration barriers, anion-framework polarisability, and volume per Li.

Composition models with chemistry-aware embeddings (CrabNet, Roost, mat2vec) and strong regularisation. The test split is leakage-controlled by composition family, so smooth chemistry generalises better than memorisation.
Treat the detection-limited entries explicitly, for example with a classifier for insulators plus a regressor: the 8 ' < 1E-10' test entries sit at log -15 and dominate the MAE.
Cross-domain (survival analysis): a Tobit-style censored likelihood for detection-limited labels.
pitfalls: The test set is tiny (121), so a 5% gain is noise; the 10% margin and the paired bootstrap are mandatory.

Experimental conductivity compilations (the Liverpool database, LiIonDB, review tables) overlap heavily with OBELiX test materials. Any such data is leakage, and so is an LLM prompted with formula names, which may recall literature conductivities.
The ' < 1E-10' to 1e-15 convention is part of the metric; scoring those entries at 1e-10 instead moves the median baseline from 2.16 to 1.83.

Lower-looking numbers in the literature are on other metrics: arXiv:2605.09311's 1.388 drops the 8 detection-limited test entries (all of which sit in the 67-entry CIF subset), and arXiv:2601.10997's 0.543 is on a different dataset. Check the test set and the ' < 1E-10' handling before comparing, and note that MD-derived transport labels count as conductivity data under this criterion.
About three quarters of the CIFs have partial occupancies, and rounding them changes compositions.
The RSC journal page refused this update's automated fetch (HTTP 403), so the bar comes from arXiv v2. Check the journal table by hand before claiming.

targets.name: JARVIS-Leaderboard frozen mid-size tasks: experimental superconducting Tc from composition (SuperCon, 16,414) or HSE06 band gap from structure (SNUMAT, 10,386): beat the best listed test MAE
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours
targets.statement: Two mid-size JARVIS-Leaderboard tasks (Kamal Choudhary et al., NIST; npj Comput. Mater. 10, 93, 2024) have fixed public splits and no entries since May 2023. supercon_chem_Tc asks for the experimental superconducting critical temperature (K) from composition alone. It uses the SuperCon-derived set of 16,414 compounds of Valentin Stanev, Corey Oses, A. Gilad Kusne, Efrain Rodriguez, Johnpierre Paglione, Stefano Curtarolo and Ichiro Takeuchi (npj Comput. Mater. 4, 29, 2018), split 13,131 train / 3,283 test with no val. Eleven entries are listed. The best MAE is 4.8511 K by matminer_rf (team UofT, 2023-05-22), then matminer_xgboost 4.9295, cfid_chem 5.0326, ElemNet2_SC 5.114 and matminer_lgbm 5.1519; the Northwestern ElemNet, BRNet and IRNet entries score 5.11-5.84. This task is distinct from the bank's jarvis-small-data-exfoliation-tc-mae, whose Tc task is the small DFT electron-phonon dft_3d_Tc_supercon set. snumat_Band_gap_HSE asks for the HSE06 band gap (eV) from crystal structure, for 10,386 materials of the hybrid-functional band-gap database of Sangtae Kim, Miso Lee, Seungwu Han and co-workers (Sci. Data 7, 387, 2020). Split 8,310/1,038/1,038. Three entries are listed: ALIGNN 0.3765 eV (2023-01-14), matminer_xgboost 0.3987 and matminer_rf 0.4367. The page header says 'ACC', but the contribution files are test-mae. Train-median predictors score 16.69 K and 1.13 eV on the two test sets. Both pages were HTTP 200 for this update.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a trained model, its training script and test predictions for supercon_chem_Tc or snumat_Band_gap_HSE. The test MAE, recomputed by the checker on the official test ids of the benchmark json, must be STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than the best MAE on the live task page re-fetched immediately before claiming (4.8511 K and 0.3765 eV on 2026-10-28). The margin must be at least 5% relative AND exceed the half-width of a 1,000-sample paired bootstrap 90% interval of the MAE difference against the best listed predictions. Models are trained only on the train ids (plus val for SNUMAT). - SuperCon: inputs are composition only. No SuperCon/NIMS or other Tc data beyond the train labels, and no model or text embedding exposed to Tc values, may be used. - SNUMAT: inputs are the structure only. No band gap of any test material, from any database or functional, may be used directly or through a model pretrained on such labels; no DFT run on test structures is allowed; and end-to-end inference must take at most 24 CPU-core-hours. Re-running the saved model must reproduce the predictions to 1e-6. The claim must also report, and beat, any published MAE on the identical JARVIS split found by a literature search.

partial_wins.statement: The same rules on one further JARVIS AI single-property task with 2,000-60,000 entries, at least three listed entries and no entry newer than 2023, named before the run starts and checked against its live page. It must not be covered by another bank entry (so not hmof, qmof, any ocp task, or the dft_3d exfoliation or Tc tasks), and the claim must also beat any published MAE on the identical split.

Reproduction audit: retrain matminer_rf on supercon_chem_Tc with its published run.sh on the official split, and report a test MAE that differs from 4.8511 K by more than 5% relative, with outputs saved.

targets.verification_method: Checker, under 1 hour: download the benchmark json.zip, load compositions or structures through jarvis-tools ('supercon_chem', 'snumat'), and re-run the saved model. Recompute the MAE and the paired bootstrap against the best CSV on the page, time the SNUMAT inference, and audit the feature code for external Tc or band-gap lookups.
angles: SuperCon: family-aware models, for example a classifier into cuprate, iron-based and conventional families followed by per-family regressors, on Magpie and element-fraction features, with a log(Tc + 1) target and an MAE-matched loss.
SNUMAT: structure features that track gap opening, such as electronegativity differences, coordination and Madelung site potentials, plus graph networks trained only on the 8,310 train structures.
Cross-domain (tabular ML): TabPFN-style priors, stacked ensembles and quantile losses for the heavy-tailed Tc distribution.
pitfalls: SuperCon contains long doping series of closely related compositions spread across a random split, which rewards memorisation. Report a family-held-out cross-validation alongside the claim; it is not required for the win.
Formula text embeddings and LLMs can carry memorised literature Tc values or band gaps; treat them as external data.
Most SNUMAT materials also appear in PBE databases (Materials Project, AFLOW, OQMD, JARVIS). Gap-trained pretrained models therefore leak, which is why the criterion forbids them.
The SNUMAT page says 'ACC', but the metric is MAE in eV.
jarvis-tools pulls datasets from figshare, which answered this update's scripted fetch with HTTP 202 and an empty body (a bot check). Use a browser session and never work around the check.

targets.name: ARCH-COMP AINNCS 2D Spacecraft Docking: verify or falsify the neural controller on the full initial set (unsolved since ARCH-COMP22)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (falsification search: millions of exact closed-loop simulations per hour on CPU; sound verification by box splitting with a reachability tool or an interval certificate: hours)
targets.statement: The 2D Spacecraft Docking benchmark of the ARCH-COMP friendly competition, category AINNCS (neural-network control systems), asks whether a reinforcement-learned controller keeps a deputy spacecraft under a distance-dependent speed limit. Plant (benchmarks/Docking/dynamics.m in https://github.com/Kiguli/ARCH-COMP2026): linear Clohessy-Wiltshire relative motion, d(sx)/dt = vx, d(sy)/dt = vy, d(vx)/dt = 2n*vy + 3n^2*sx + Fx/m, d(vy)/dt = -2n*vx + Fy/m, with m = 12 kg and n = 0.001027 rad/s. Controller: benchmarks/Docking/model.onnx (tf2onnx export, opset 9; input [batch,4] = (sx, sy, vx, vy); a linear pre-processing layer, two hidden layers of 256 tanh units, a linear output layer, a linear post-processing layer and a final tanh; output [batch,2] = (Fx, Fy); 274,562 bytes, sha256 cc46c45e5ee7a0a5df433d31b19089cebe2ae64aeb6a0dc7ec47e51818368bf7 as fetched on 2026-10-29), applied with zero-order hold every 1 s. Initial set X0 = [70,106] x [70,106] x [-0.28,0.28] x [-0.28,0.28] (benchmarks/Docking/specification.txt); property (14): sqrt(vx^2 + vy^2) <= 0.2 + 2n*sqrt(sx^2 + sy^2) for all t in [0, 40] s. History, from the category reports: introduced in ARCH-COMP22 (Manzanas Lopez et al., EPiC vol. 90), where POLAR computed reachable sets for four corner sub-boxes without finding a violation and the report says 'The benchmark has not been fully verified'; ARCH-COMP23 (Manzanas Lopez, Althoff, Forets, Johnson, Ladner and Schilling; EPiC vol. 96, pp. 89-125): CORA 'UNKNOWN' (its reachable set explodes), JuliaReach proves it only for [87,89]^2 x [-0.01,0.01]^2, NNV no result; ARCH-COMP24 (EPiC vol. 103, pp. 64-121): CORA '?', NNV '?', JuliaReach proves it only for [70,106]^2 x [-0.14,0.14]^2, GoTube v2.0 verifies a half-radius set only and only statistically (confidence level 90%); ARCH-COMP25 (EPiC vol. 108, pp. 71-121): CORA '?', JuliaReach '?'; ARCH-COMP26 (Sasaki, Wooding, Johnson, Althoff, Benet, Coogan, Forets, Harapanahalli, Koller, Ladner, Schilling, Zhang, Zhong; EPiC vol. 110, pp. 85-130, published 2026-07-03, doi 10.29007/637n): CORA '?' (its reachable set 'explodes over time'), JuliaReach '?' (again proven only for velocities in [-0.14,0.14]), CROWN-Reach and immrax report no result, and the report says the nonlinear safety specification 'causes the benchmark to remain unsolved one more year'. Simulations reported by POLAR, CORA and JuliaReach show no violation, yet no sound proof and no counterexample exists for the full box. The constraint is tight at the near corner: at (70, 70, +-0.28, +-0.28) the speed is 0.39598 m/s against a limit of 0.40334 m/s (slack 0.0074 m/s), while the tanh-bounded force changes each velocity component by at most about 1/12 m/s per second, so the first control intervals decide. Jafarpour, Harapanahalli and Coogan (arXiv:2307.14938v3) report the property verified 'starting from four different initial sets' with Euler integration of an embedding system (step 0.1 s), not for the full box with validated integration. Either outcome (a counterexample or a sound proof for the full X0) settles the instance.
targets.success_criterion: Success means ONE of the following for the unmodified benchmark (model.onnx, dynamics.m and specification.txt from https://github.com/Kiguli/ARCH-COMP2026, sha256 of all three recorded; zero-order hold with a 1 s period: at each instant k = 0,...,39 the force u_k = N(x(k)) is computed from the state at time k and held constant on [k, k+1)). (F) FALSIFICATION: an initial state x0 = (sx, sy, vx, vy) written as exact decimals, with x0 in the closed box X0 checked exactly in rational arithmetic, and a time t* in [0, 40], such that g(x(t*)) = sqrt(vx^2 + vy^2) - 0.2 - 2*0.001027*sqrt(sx^2 + sy^2) >= 1e-6, where the trajectory is computed by the skeptic with the plant integrated exactly between instants (closed-form matrix-exponential solution of the linear ODE in at least 50-digit arithmetic) and N evaluated (i) by onnxruntime CPUExecutionProvider in float32 on the float32-rounded state and (ii) in float64 by a second runtime that is not onnxruntime (onnx.reference.ReferenceEvaluator or a torch re-implementation of the same weights); the violation g >= 1e-6 must hold at some t in [0, 40] in both runs. (V) VERIFICATION of the whole X0: a finite list of axis-aligned boxes whose union contains X0 (checked exactly in rational arithmetic) such that every box is proven safe for all t in [0, 40] (the continuous interval, not only the 41 instants) either (V-a) by a pinned public release of a sound set-based reachability tool (JuliaReach/ClosedLoopReachability.jl, CORA, CROWN-Reach, POLAR-Express, or immrax run in zero-order-hold mode), re-run by the skeptic with the claimant's stated parameters on the unmodified network, returning a verified/satisfied verdict twice in a row; statistical tools (GoTube), sampling and non-validated integration never count; or (V-b) by an explicit interval certificate that the skeptic's own code re-checks: per box and step k, state enclosures B_k (B_0 containing the box) and force enclosures U_k with N(B_k) inside U_k proven by the skeptic's float64 interval or CROWN bound computation, exact-flow images of B_k x U_k at time k+1 inside B_{k+1} (or inside a listed union of boxes that are themselves certified onward), and property (14) proven for all t in [k, k+1] from B_k x U_k by interval arithmetic with outward rounding; the whole re-run of (V-a) or (V-b) must finish within 24 CPU-hours on a laptop. In both cases the live ARCH-COMP AINNCS report and benchmark repository, re-checked immediately before claiming (a newer ARCH-COMP27 AINNCS report supersedes the 2026 one), must not already list the instance as verified or falsified, and a live web search must find no earlier published sound verification or falsification of the full X0 (if one exists, the result is a replication).

partial_wins.statement: A sound verification (same rules and re-run checks as (V-a) or (V-b), continuous time t in [0, 40]) of the sub-box [70,106] x [70,106] x [-0.21,0.21] x [-0.21,0.21], or of any sub-box of X0 containing it: velocity half-width 0.21 (75% of the original radius) against the largest published sound result, JuliaReach's [-0.14,0.14]^2 (ARCH-COMP24, 25 and 26).

A sound verification of the full X0 for the sampled-time version of property (14) only, i.e. at the 41 instants t = 0, 1, ..., 40, with every sampled state enclosed by a validated method and re-checked as in (V-a) or (V-b); reported as sampled-time and never as settling the benchmark.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic writes their own checker without reading the claimant's code: fetch the three benchmark files from the repository and compare sha256 with the claimant's manifest. For (F): parse the decimal x0 and check membership in X0 with fractions; precompute e^A and G = integral_0^1 e^(As) ds B with mpmath at 50 digits; iterate x_{k+1} = e^A x_k + G u_k with u_k from onnxruntime (float32) and, separately, from onnx.reference in float64; inside each hold interval evaluate g on a fine grid around the claimed t* and refine by local maximisation of the exact flow e^(At) x_k + G(t) u_k; require g >= 1e-6 in both runs. Also run the 16 vertices and 10^5 random initial states and report the largest g seen. For (V): check the cover exactly (recursive splitting of X0 against the box list in rational arithmetic), then either re-run the named tool release on every box with the stated parameters (record versions, wall time, verdicts) or run the skeptic's own interval checker over the certificate (enclosure of N by float64 IBP or auto_LiRPA CROWN with outward slack, containment of the affine images, and an interval bound of g over each hold interval). Finally grep the latest ARCH-COMP AINNCS report on easychair.org and the repository for the Docking row, and web-search for later papers. Minutes for (F), hours for (V).
angles: Falsify first, where the slack is smallest: near sx = sy = 70 with |vx| = |vy| = 0.28 the margin is 0.0074 m/s at t = 0. Maximise g over x0 and over t inside the first few hold intervals with exact linear propagation and gradients through the smooth tanh network (multi-start gradient ascent, CMA-ES), remembering that g can peak between two control instants.

Exploit linearity: between instants the state is an exact affine function of (x_k, u_k), so one closed-loop step is an affine image of the state box plus an enclosure of N; a custom zonotope or box propagation with CROWN linear bounds of the tanh network (auto_LiRPA) and recursive splitting is cheap and yields a (V-b) certificate directly.

Spend the splitting budget where it matters: JuliaReach already proves |vx|, |vy| <= 0.14 for all positions, so split the outer velocity shell and the near-distance region (sx, sy close to 70) where the speed limit is lowest; use the published JuliaReach and CORA parameters from the ARCH-COMP repeatability archive as a starting point.

Make the nonlinear property cheap to bound: check vx^2 + vy^2 <= (0.2 + 2n*sqrt(sx^2 + sy^2))^2 on enclosures, using monotonicity of sqrt on an interval bound of sx^2 + sy^2, and bound the in-interval flow with a first-order Taylor model in t.

If simulations stay safe everywhere, look for an inductive invariant instead of a 40-step tube: a set S containing X0's future after a few steps, with the one-step image of S inside S and property (14) on S, verified once with CROWN bounds.
pitfalls: Checking only the 41 control instants: the property is over continuous time and g can be maximal between instants. A sampled-time proof is p2 at most.
Statistical or sampled verification (GoTube, Monte Carlo, Lipschitz-free sampling) and Euler integration without error bounds are not sound and never count.
Continuous feedback is not the benchmark: the 2025 and 2026 reports note that immrax interprets benchmarks as continuous feedback; this instance is zero-order hold with a 1 s period.

The ONNX includes pre- and post-processing layers and a final tanh; dropping them or using the bare 256x256 core changes the controller. Inputs are (sx, sy, vx, vy) in that order and outputs are forces in newtons divided by m = 12 in the plant.
float32 and float64 controller evaluations can disagree on tiny-margin violations; the 1e-6 margin in two runtimes is required.
A cover with gaps, or with boxes slightly inside X0 (105.999 instead of 106), fails the exact cover check.

Do not mistake partial results for the instance: POLAR's 2022 four corner sub-boxes (reachable sets without a violation), JuliaReach's [87,89]^2 x [-0.01,0.01]^2 box (2023) and half-velocity box (2024-2026), GoTube's statistical half-radius result, and the four initial sets of Jafarpour et al. (shown only in their Fig. 6, with non-validated Euler integration) do not settle the full box. Papers that adapt the docking model with a different controller or initial set are different problems: POLAR-Express (Wang et al., arXiv:2304.01218) verifies a variant with a 2x64 tanh controller, extra inputs and x, y in [24, 26] at a fixed velocity, and Wang, Seiler, Dullerud and Hu (arXiv:2609.22576) use an LQR plus NN-residual controller.
Installing Julia or MATLAB (CORA) is the human's decision; Python-only routes are CROWN-based custom propagation for (V-b) or immrax in zero-order-hold mode.

targets.name: OpenOOD v1.5 CIFAR-10/100: a post-hoc OOD detector on the official cross-entropy ResNet-18 checkpoints beating the best near-OOD AUROC
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (CPU inference of a 32x32 ResNet-18 over the CIFAR training and test sets and OpenOOD's near/far-OOD test and validation sets, on the order of 10^5 images per checkpoint, for three checkpoints)
targets.statement: OpenOOD v1.5 (Jingyang Zhang, Jingkang Yang, Pengyun Wang, Haoqi Wang, Yueqian Lin, Haoran Zhang, Yiyou Sun, Xuefeng Du, Yixuan Li, Ziwei Liu, Yiran Chen, Hai Li; arXiv:2306.09301, DMLR) standardises out-of-distribution detection with fixed ID/OOD test sets, OOD validation sets for hyperparameter search, a unified evaluator and released checkpoints. For CIFAR-10 the near-OOD sets are CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet and the far-OOD sets MNIST, SVHN, Textures and Places365; for CIFAR-100 near-OOD is CIFAR-10 plus TinyImageNet. The live leaderboard (https://zjysteven.github.io/OpenOOD/, maintained by Jingyang Zhang; data in results/cifar10.csv and results/cifar100.csv on the 'leaderboard' branch of github.com/zjysteven/OpenOOD, last changed 2026-05-28 when the CORE postprocessor was added) ranks methods by near-OOD AUROC averaged over three training runs. For post-hoc methods on the three released cross-entropy ResNet-18 checkpoints (ID accuracy 95.06 on CIFAR-10, 77.25 on CIFAR-100) the best near-OOD AUROC on 2026-10-28 (board unchanged since 2026-05-28) is CombOOD (Rajasekaran et al., 2024) at 91.13 on CIFAR-10 (far-OOD 94.65; next NAC 90.93, KNN 90.64), and WeiPer+KLD (Granz, Heurich and Landgraf, NeurIPS 2024) at 81.37 on CIFAR-100 (far-OOD 79.01; next GEN 81.31, fDBD 81.26); both top rows list a standard deviation of +-0.00. GROOD (ElAraby, Sahoo, Pequignot, Novello and Paull, TMLR 2025, arXiv:2312.14427v3, Table 2) reports 91.16 near-OOD and 93.8 far-OOD on CIFAR-10 with the same checkpoints, using an OOD prototype built by manifold mixup of ID samples; it is not yet on the board. Higher numbers on these checkpoints come from protocols this target excludes: OODD (Yang, Zhu, Sun, Liu, Gu and Ye, arXiv:2503.10468, Table 1) reports 82.10 near-OOD on CIFAR-100 (90.96 on CIFAR-10) with a test-time OOD dictionary built from the stream of test images, and Novello, Prudent, Dalmau, Friedrich and Pequignot (arXiv:2407.07135, Table 1) reach up to 82.2 on CIFAR-100 by tuning detector combinations on half of the OpenOOD test data and scoring the other half; P&C (Quint, NeurIPS 2026, arXiv:2605.01632) reports 91.55 on CIFAR-10 with its own retrained ResNet-18s, not the released checkpoints. Recent per-image post-hoc methods on the released checkpoints stay below the bar (KAN detector, Canevaro et al., ICLR 2025: 90.99 / 77.17; PRO, Chen, Yeh, Mou and Gu, arXiv:2503.18784: 90.70 / 81.36; BBAS, arXiv:2603.22660: 90.76 / 80.26; ARAS, arXiv:2610.32255: 88.61 / 80.37 on one checkpoint). Methods that retrain the network rank higher (RotPred+PixMix 94.86 on CIFAR-10; OAL 82.03 and outlier-exposure OE 88.30 on CIFAR-100), but this target is the post-hoc track, where everything is per-image inference on fixed public weights. Whether a better post-hoc score exists for these checkpoints is open.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a post-hoc OOD score function S (Python code plus a frozen hyperparameter file) such that the skeptic's run of the official OpenOOD v1.5 evaluator (openood.evaluation_api.Evaluator from a pinned commit of https://github.com/Jingkang50/OpenOOD, with the benchmark image lists and images that the evaluator itself downloads) on EACH of the three released cross-entropy ResNet-18 checkpoints for CIFAR-10, or for CIFAR-100, gives near-OOD AUROC values whose mean is at least 0.30 points HIGHER (direction: max) than the bar. The bar is the maximum of (i) the best near-OOD AUROC of a CrossEntropy post-hoc row in the live results/cifar10.csv or results/cifar100.csv, re-fetched immediately before claiming, and (ii) the best near-OOD AUROC that the NOVELTY skeptic finds published for a method that follows the same rules as S (below) on the same three released OpenOOD v1.5 checkpoints and the full official OpenOOD v1.5 test sets. On 2026-10-28, as far as found, the bar is 91.16 for CIFAR-10 (GROOD, arXiv:2312.14427v3 Table 2; board 91.13) and 81.37 for CIFAR-100 (WeiPer+KLD). Published numbers obtained outside these rules neither set the bar nor qualify: test-time or transductive methods that adapt to the test stream (e.g. OODD, arXiv:2503.10468: 82.10 on CIFAR-100), protocols that tune or fit on part of the OOD test sets (e.g. Novello et al., arXiv:2407.07135: up to 82.2 on CIFAR-100), and retrained or modified networks. In addition the mean far-OOD AUROC must be at least that of MSP on the same checkpoints (board: 90.73 for CIFAR-10, 77.76 for CIFAR-100). Post-hoc means: the network weights and its argmax predictions are those of the released checkpoint, unmodified (the evaluator's ID accuracy, averaged over the three checkpoints, must equal the board's CrossEntropy value within 0.10: 95.06 or 77.25); S computes each test image's score from that image alone, with no state carried between test images or batches; S may use the network's activations, logits and gradients and statistics of the ID TRAINING split only (data derived from training images, such as mixup samples, is allowed and must be declared); it may not use any other model (no CLIP or ImageNet features), outlier or auxiliary data, OOD test images, or test-set statistics; hyperparameters are fixed a priori or chosen only on OpenOOD's own ID/OOD validation splits (APS mode) and frozen before the test evaluation.

partial_wins.statement: A post-hoc score function obeying every rule of the main criterion whose mean near-OOD AUROC is at least 0.10 points above the bar AND whose mean far-OOD AUROC is at least the far-OOD AUROC of the entry that sets the bar (CIFAR-10: GROOD 93.8; CIFAR-100: WeiPer+KLD 79.01), i.e. a smaller but Pareto-better result.

A reproducibility finding: an independent re-run (official evaluator, the three official checkpoints, the method's own public code at a stated commit with its published hyperparameters) of one of the +-0.00 CrossEntropy rows (CIFAR-10: CombOOD 91.13 or WeiPer+KLD 90.54; CIFAR-100: WeiPer+KLD 81.37 or CombOOD 78.77) whose three-checkpoint mean near-OOD AUROC differs from the listed value by more than 0.50 points. Reported as a correction for the human to raise with the maintainers, never as a record.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic creates a fresh virtual environment, installs OpenOOD from a pinned commit (recorded), lets the evaluator download the benchmark, downloads the official v1.5 checkpoints with OpenOOD's own download script (README 'Pre-trained checkpoints'), and compares checkpoint sha256 with the claimant's manifest. They read S in full (looking for test-set or OOD-data access, extra models, label use, network modification, state kept between test images), then run Evaluator(net, id_name='cifar10' or 'cifar100', postprocessor=S, ...).eval_ood() for each checkpoint and record near-OOD AUROC, far-OOD AUROC and ID accuracy, averaging over the three. To confirm per-image scoring they re-score a random 1,000-image sample of each test set one image at a time and in shuffled order and require the same scores as in the full run (to float tolerance). They re-fetch the live CSV, compute the bar under the rules of the criterion, and search arXiv/OpenReview for newer results on the same checkpoints, recording why any higher number is or is not admissible. CPU time is roughly 10-30 minutes per checkpoint plus any hyperparameter sweep on the validation split.
angles: Combine complementary signals: the top CIFAR-10 rows rest on different evidence (combined scores for CombOOD, neuron-activation statistics for NAC, nearest-neighbour distances of penultimate features for KNN). A rank-normalised combination of feature-space distances, logit scores (energy, GEN) and activation statistics, weighted on the OOD validation split, is the obvious first attempt.

Multi-layer class-conditional statistics from the 50k training images: per-class means with shrunk shared covariance at several depths, whitened and combined; near-OOD sets (CIFAR-100 for CIFAR-10, and the reverse) may separate better in mid-level features than in the logits.

Gradient and perturbation scores: gradients with respect to a class or OOD prototype (as in GROOD), weight perturbations of the class projections (as in WeiPer), or the sensitivity of the logits to small input perturbations, all computed without touching OOD data.
Report the validation-to-test gap of every configuration; a method that only wins on test after many tries is over-fitted to the test sets even if the rules were followed.
pitfalls: Tuning on the OOD test sets (or on near-duplicates such as other TinyImageNet images) is leakage; OpenOOD's APS mode searches only on its validation splits. The CRITERION skeptic must read the tuning code.
Changing the classifier (e.g. ReAct, ASH or SCALE applied to the predictions as well as to the score) changes ID accuracy; the criterion pins ID accuracy to the board value.
Reporting one checkpoint or the best of three: the criterion uses the mean over all three released checkpoints.
Using CLIP or ImageNet-pretrained features, or outlier exposure, moves the method to another track.
Version drift: evaluator versions and image lists can move AUROC by tenths of a point; pin the OpenOOD commit and report it.

Downloads: the evaluator fetches OpenOOD's copies of TinyImageNet (ImageNet-derived) and Places365 from Google Drive. The human should review those datasets' terms first; if a quota or confirmation page appears, stop and let the human fetch the files.
The +-0.00 rows may be single-run numbers; a claim must still beat the stated bar, not a re-run of it.

Test-time and transductive scores: a dictionary, memory bank or statistics updated from the stream of test images (as in OODD), or detector combinations tuned on part of the official OOD test sets (as in Novello et al.), use OOD test data. They are excluded even when a paper calls them post-hoc, and their higher published numbers (82.10 and up to 82.2 on CIFAR-100) do not set the bar.
Numbers on other checkpoints do not compare: P&C's 91.55 near-OOD AUROC on CIFAR-10 uses its own retrained pre-activation ResNet-18s (ID accuracy 95.59), not the released checkpoints (95.06).

targets.name: ARCH-COMP AINNCS CartPole (Balancing): verify or falsify 1e-3 settling of the neural controller on the full initial set
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (falsification: fast simulation of 500 control steps per trajectory; sound verification over 10 s with a 50 Hz controller: hours to days of reachability with splitting)
targets.statement: The CartPole benchmark ('Balancing' in the CROWN-Reach tables), proposed for ARCH-COMP24 and reused unchanged in 2025 and 2026, asks whether a neural controller balances an inverted pendulum on a cart precisely. Plant (benchmarks/CartPole/dynamics.m in https://github.com/Kiguli/ARCH-COMP2026): dx1/dt = x2, dx2/dt = 2f, dx3/dt = x4, dx4/dt = (0.08*0.41*(9.8*sin(x3) - 2f*cos(x3)) - 0.0021*x4)/0.0105, where x1 is the cart position, x3 the pole angle (0 = upright, not wrapped modulo 2*pi) and f the controller output. Controller: benchmarks/CartPole/model.onnx (PyTorch 2.1.2 export; input [1,4] = (x1, x2, x3, x4); Gemm-tanh-Gemm-tanh-Gemm followed by a final tanh, so f is in (-1, 1); output [1,1]; 19,185 bytes, sha256 ac10c817c994e8ee84dbf44ceffcf7380b7878ea467d2d17ff9fa38eee249529 as fetched on 2026-10-29), applied with zero-order hold every 0.02 s (specifications.txt: 'control period 0.02 s', t = 10 s, i.e. 500 control steps). Initial set X0 = [-0.1,0.1] x [-0.05,0.05] x [-0.1,0.1] x [-0.05,0.05]; property: for t > 8 s (the ARCH-COMP26 report writes t in [8 s, 10 s]) x1, x3 and x4 all lie in [-0.001, 0.001]. Status from the category reports: ARCH-COMP24 (EPiC vol. 103): CORA verifies only a smaller initial set, CROWN-Reach '?', NNV '?', and GoTube v2.0 'fully verifies' it but only statistically (confidence level 90%); ARCH-COMP25 (EPiC vol. 108) and ARCH-COMP26 (Sasaki et al., EPiC vol. 110, pp. 85-130, 2026-07-03): CORA verifies only the box with every radius at 40% of the original ('CartPole*'), CROWN-Reach reports 'Balancing ?' (6.4 s), JuliaReach and immrax report nothing. The 2026 report names CartPole as challenging for most tools because the high control frequency makes over-approximations conservative. No sound verification and no counterexample is published for the full box.
targets.success_criterion: Success means ONE of the following for the unmodified benchmark (model.onnx, dynamics.m and specifications.txt from https://github.com/Kiguli/ARCH-COMP2026, sha256 recorded; zero-order hold with period 0.02 s and no extra delay: f_k = N(x(0.02k)) held on [0.02k, 0.02(k+1)) for k = 0,...,499). (F) FALSIFICATION: an initial state x0 written as exact decimals, inside the closed box X0 (checked exactly in rational arithmetic), and a time t* with 8 < t* <= 10 such that max(|x1(t*)|, |x3(t*)|, |x4(t*)|) >= 0.001 + 1e-6, where the trajectory is computed by the skeptic with N evaluated by onnxruntime CPU float32 and, in a second run, in float64 by a runtime that is not onnxruntime, and the ODE integrated between instants by two independent high-accuracy integrators (e.g. scipy DOP853 with rtol = atol = 1e-12, and an mpmath Taylor or Runge-Kutta integrator at 30 digits) that agree to 1e-9; the violation must hold in all four combinations. (V) VERIFICATION of the whole X0: a finite list of axis-aligned boxes whose union contains X0 (checked exactly) such that every box is proven to satisfy the property for all t in [8, 10] (continuous time) by a pinned public release of a sound set-based reachability tool (CORA, JuliaReach/ClosedLoopReachability.jl, CROWN-Reach, POLAR-Express, or immrax in zero-order-hold mode) re-run by the skeptic with the claimant's parameters and returning a verified verdict twice in a row, or by an explicit certificate (per-step state and control enclosures with validated flow enclosures, e.g. interval Picard-Lindelof or Taylor-model steps) that the skeptic's own interval code re-checks with outward rounding; statistical tools (GoTube), sampling and non-validated integration never count; the re-run must finish within 48 CPU-hours on a laptop. In both cases the live ARCH-COMP AINNCS report and repository, re-checked immediately before claiming (a newer ARCH-COMP27 report supersedes 2026), must not already list the full instance as verified or falsified, and a live web search must find no earlier sound verification or falsification of the full X0.

partial_wins.statement: A sound verification (same rules and re-run checks as (V), continuous time t in [8, 10]) of the centred sub-box with every half-width at least 60% of the original, i.e. [-0.06,0.06] x [-0.03,0.03] x [-0.06,0.06] x [-0.03,0.03] or any sub-box of X0 containing it, against CORA's published 40%-radius box (ARCH-COMP25 and 26).

A sound verification of the full X0 for the sampled-time version of the property only, at the 101 instants t = 8.00, 8.02, ..., 10.00, with each sampled state enclosed by a validated method and re-checked as in (V); reported as sampled-time and never as settling the benchmark.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic writes their own checker without reading the claimant's code: fetch the benchmark files, compare sha256 with the manifest, read the ONNX input shape ([1,4]) and output ([1,1]). For (F): check x0 in X0 with fractions; simulate 500 hold intervals with N from onnxruntime float32 and from onnx.reference float64, integrating each interval with scipy DOP853 (rtol = atol = 1e-12) and with an mpmath Taylor integrator; locate the maximum of max(|x1|, |x3|, |x4|) over (8, 10] by dense output plus local refinement; require >= 0.001 + 1e-6 in all four combinations. Report also the closed-loop equilibrium and the worst case over the 16 vertices and 10^4 random starts. For (V): check the cover exactly, then re-run the named tool on every box (versions, parameters, verdicts, CPU time) or run the skeptic's own interval checker on the certificate. Finally re-read the latest ARCH-COMP AINNCS report and web-search for later results. Minutes for (F), hours to two days for (V).
angles: Linear analysis first: compute the closed-loop equilibrium (f = N(x*) with the sampled dynamics) and the Jacobian of the 0.02 s sampled map there. If x* is not within 1e-3 of the origin in x1, x3, x4, or if the slowest eigenvalue modulus rho gives rho^400 times the initial deviation above 1e-3 along that eigenvector, a counterexample sits near the corresponding corner of X0.

Falsification by optimisation: differentiable simulation (torch, fixed-step RK4 at 1 ms inside each hold, then confirmation with the strict integrators) and maximisation of max(|x1|, |x3|, |x4|) over t in (8, 10] from the 16 vertices and Sobol starts.

Verification by contraction rather than by a 500-step tube: find a quadratic Lyapunov function V = x'Px for the linearised sampled map, bound the nonlinear remainder (sin, cos, tanh network) on a small invariant ellipsoid with interval or CROWN bounds, and prove that every state of X0 enters the ellipsoid {V <= c} contained in the 1e-3 box before t = 8 s; only the transient needs reachability.

Split smartly: CORA proves the 40%-radius box; split the remaining shell, starting with the pole-angle and angular-velocity extremes, and reuse CORA or JuliaReach parameters from the ARCH-COMP repeatability archive.
pitfalls: Control-period versus latency: the 2026 report says 'a latency of 0.02 s' while the repository files say 'control period 0.02 s'; this target uses the repository reading (zero-order hold, period 0.02 s, no extra delay). A claim valid only under another reading must say so and does not count.
Sampled-time checks: the property must hold for every t in (8, 10], not only at multiples of 0.02 s; a sampled-time proof is p2 at most.
Integration error and float32 rounding over 500 steps can create or hide a 1e-6-level violation; the two-integrator, two-runtime agreement is required.
The angle x3 is not wrapped modulo 2*pi; the property is |x3| <= 0.001 literally.
GoTube's 2024 'full verification' is statistical (90% confidence) and CORA's result covers only the 40%-radius box; neither settles the instance.
The final tanh is part of the controller; the plant multiplies its output by 2 (x_acc = 2 m/s^2). Do not clip or rescale it again.

targets.name: Deterministic Linf certified accuracy records (MNIST 0.1/0.3, CIFAR-10 2/255 and 8/255, TinyImageNet 1/255): certify more test images than the best published model
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (MNIST cells: CPU or Apple-GPU training of a CNN7-class network with IBP-based losses, then IBP/CROWN on all 10,000 test images and alpha-beta-CROWN on the residue); needs cluster for the CIFAR-10 and TinyImageNet cells (GPU-days of training and certification)
targets.statement: Deterministic certified training produces networks for which a sound verifier proves, image by image, that no Linf perturbation of radius eps changes the prediction. The standard settings (Gowal et al. 2018, Shi et al. 2021, CTBench) are MNIST eps 0.1 and 0.3, CIFAR-10 eps 2/255 and 8/255, and TinyImageNet eps 1/255, scored by certified accuracy on the full test set (TinyImageNet: validation set). Best published values on 2026-10-28: MNIST 0.1: 98.53% (AD-CERT, Matteo Melis, Jesus Martinez del Rincon and Vishal Sharma, arXiv:2606.31653v2, BMVC 2026, Table 1; CNN7, alpha-beta-CROWN with 400 s branch-and-bound per image), ahead of TAPS/STAPS 98.52% (CTBench). MNIST 0.3: 94.02% (Zhaoyang Lyu, Minghao Guo, Tong Wu, Guodong Xu, Kehuan Zhang and Dahua Lin, CVPR 2021: a CROWN-IBP-trained DM-large network with ParamRamp activation, trained at eps 0.4, CROWN-LBP verified error 5.98% at eps 0.3, supplementary Table 4; listed on the SoK certified-robustness leaderboard of Linyi Li, Tao Xie and Bo Li); best ReLU network 94.00% (IBP with multi-objective hyperparameter optimisation, Konstantin Kaulen, Hadar Shavit and Holger H. Hoos, arXiv:2606.02134v2, ICML 2026, Table 2, 300 s verification cutoff), then AD-CERT 93.98%. Kaulen et al. state that, following common practice, they tuned hyperparameters on the test set (their validation-tuned fronts are strictly lower), so their values are optimistic bars. CIFAR-10 2/255: 65.20% (AD-CERT's controlled re-run in Table 2 of arXiv:2606.31653v2, clean 79.21%; its Table 1 headline is 65.08%), then MTL-IBP re-tuned by Kaulen et al. 64.61% (Table 9) and CC-DIST 64.60% (Alessandro De Palma, arXiv:2602.02626). CIFAR-10 8/255: 41.78% (SortNet trained with EDM-generated data: Thomas Altstidl, David Dobre, Arthur Kosmala, Björn Eskofier, Gauthier Gidel and Leo Schwinn, 'On the Scalability of Certified Adversarial Robustness with Generated Data', NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2305.10388, +1.39 points over SortNet; shown as a preprint on the SoK board), SortNet alone 40.39% (Zhang, Jiang, He and Wang, NeurIPS 2022), best ReLU network 35.85% (AD-CERT, loss-ablation Table 7; Table 1 lists 35.84% and the 3-seed mean in Table 6 is 35.78 +- 0.15). TinyImageNet 1/255: 30.67% (MTL-IBP re-tuned by Kaulen et al., Table 1, 1,000 s cutoff), then AD-CERT 28.19% and CC-DIST 27.88%. The CTBench library and benchmark (Yuhao Mao, Stefan Balauca, Martin Vechev, arXiv:2406.04848, github.com/eth-sri/CTBench) provides the reference training and certification cascade (IBP, CROWN, alpha-CROWN, alpha-beta-CROWN) behind most of these numbers. The SoK board was last updated on 2024-06-12, so the 2026 records live only in the papers. Probabilistic certificates (randomized smoothing) are a separate track and do not count here. Open question per cell: can a model certify more test images?
targets.success_criterion: Success means, for ONE cell, a trained classifier (weights plus a plain PyTorch or ONNX forward definition; input in [0,1] pixel space with any normalisation inside the model; deterministic, no test-time randomness or input purification) such that the skeptic's own certification of the FULL official evaluation set (MNIST and CIFAR-10: the 10,000 test images in canonical order; TinyImageNet: the 10,000 official validation images at 64x64) at the cell's Linf radius gives a certified count STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the cell record by at least 10 images (0.10 points). An image is certified iff its clean argmax prediction is correct AND a sound verifier proves a lower bound >= 1e-5 on every margin z_y - z_j (j != y) over the whole box {x' : |x' - x|_inf <= eps} intersected with [0,1]^d. Accepted verifiers, all run by the skeptic: their own float64 interval bound propagation; CROWN or alpha-CROWN from a pinned auto_LiRPA release; alpha-beta-CROWN branch-and-bound from a pinned release with at most 400 s per image; for Lipschitz-by-construction architectures (l_inf-dist nets, SortNet) the closed-form certificate recomputed in float64. Attack-found counterexamples, timeouts and errors count as not certified. The record is the maximum value for that cell in the live sources, re-checked immediately before claiming (AD-CERT arXiv:2606.31653 Tables 1, 2 and 5-7, Kaulen et al. arXiv:2606.02134 Tables 1-2, the SoK leaderboard, and anything newer the NOVELTY skeptic finds); on 2026-10-28: MNIST 0.1: 98.53; MNIST 0.3: 94.02; CIFAR-10 2/255: 65.20; CIFAR-10 8/255: 41.78; TinyImageNet 1/255: 30.67. Training may use only the cell's training split, plus images from a generative model trained only on that split (declared); no test or validation images or near duplicates of them.

partial_wins.statement: ReLU record in a cell whose overall record is held by a non-ReLU architecture: a network whose only nonlinearities are ReLU (no extra or generated data) certifying at least 10 more images than the best published ReLU value, under the same checks: MNIST 0.3 above 94.00% (Kaulen et al.), or CIFAR-10 8/255 above 35.85% (AD-CERT, Table 7).

Pareto improvement on CIFAR-10 2/255 or TinyImageNet 1/255: certified accuracy (same checks) within 0.05 points of the live cell record or above it, together with clean accuracy at least 2.0 points above the record holder's clean accuracy (AD-CERT 79.21% on CIFAR-10 2/255; Kaulen et al.'s MTL-IBP 39.75% on TinyImageNet).

targets.verification_method: Skeptic loads the weights in a fresh environment, confirms the forward pass is deterministic and that the input domain is [0,1], computes clean accuracy, then certifies in stages with their own scripts: float64 IBP on all images (minutes for MNIST), CROWN/alpha-CROWN via a pinned auto_LiRPA on the rest, and alpha-beta-CROWN (pinned release, the claimant's YAML, at most 400 s per image) only on images still uncertified; counts certified images and checks the 1e-5 margin. Re-read the AD-CERT and Kaulen et al. arXiv pages and the SoK board for the cell record and search arXiv for 'certified training' papers newer than 2026-10-28. Read the training script for test-set use. For MNIST the total is hours to a day on CPU, dominated by branch-and-bound; CIFAR-10 and TinyImageNet need a GPU.
angles: MNIST cells are laptop-sized: start from CTBench's IBP, SABR or MTL-IBP recipes for CNN7, then add what moved the 2026 records: adversarial distillation from a PGD-trained teacher (AD-CERT), feature distillation (CC-DIST) and multi-objective hyperparameter search (Kaulen et al. found that published configurations were under-tuned).

Architecture width: Mao et al. (Understanding Certified Training with IBP) found that wider, not deeper, CNN7 variants improve certified accuracy (their Table 1 includes 4x-wide MNIST models); on MNIST a wider CNN7 is probably still trainable on a laptop in days.

Make certification cheap: train so that IBP alone certifies almost everything (IBP-trained nets are nearly propagation-invariant), then spend branch-and-bound only on the few hundred hardest images; the skeptic's cost drops the same way.
For the 8/255 and 0.3 cells, l_inf-dist nets and SortNet give exact certificates by margin; combining them with generated training data (as Altstidl et al. did) is the route to the overall record.
pitfalls: Certified accuracy on a subset (first 1,000 images) or on the training set is not the benchmark; the full test (TinyImageNet: validation) set is.

Unsound shortcuts: PGD/AutoAttack accuracy is an upper bound on certified accuracy, not a certificate; verifier timeouts are uncertified; float32 bounds with zero margin can be unsound, hence the 1e-5 margin.
