Normalisation outside the model changes the perturbation set; eps is applied to [0,1] pixels.
Model selection on the test set: choose checkpoints by validation or training-set certified accuracy and say so.
Comparing against stale tables: the SoK board misses the 2026 records (AD-CERT, Kaulen et al.); the live record is the maximum over all sources.
Records obtained with a non-ReLU architecture or generated data are still the overall cell record; only p1 restricts to ReLU networks.

targets.name: RobustBench ImageNet Linf (eps 4/255): lower a listed model's robust accuracy below the best published value with a stronger attack
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (ResNet-18/50-sized models on the 5,000-image evaluation set at 224 px on CPU; the large Swin/ConvNeXt entries need a GPU); the ImageNet validation set must be obtained by the human under ImageNet's terms
targets.statement: RobustBench (Croce, Andriushchenko, Sehwag, Debenedetti, Flammarion, Chiang, Mittal and Hein; robustbench.github.io) lists 30 ImageNet models for the Linf threat model at eps = 4/255 (29 defended models plus the undefended Standard_R50). Each model_info JSON (model_info/imagenet/Linf/ < Model > .json) carries a 'clean_acc' and an 'autoattack_acc' from standard AutoAttack on RobustBench's fixed 5,000-image subset of the ImageNet validation set (robustbench.data.load_imagenet: at most 5,000 points from the list helper_files/imagenet_test_image_ids.txt, each model's own preprocessing such as Res256Crop224); only three carry an 'external' value from a stronger evaluation (Amini2024MeanSparse_ConvNeXt-L 59.64 -> 58.22, Amini2024MeanSparse_Swin-L 62.12 -> 58.92, Bai2024MixedNUTS 58.62 -> 58.50; checked 2026-10-28). The README invites any evaluation that yields a lower robust accuracy than AutoAttack, and warns that values, even clean accuracy, fluctuate with package versions such as torchvision. Published stronger evaluations not folded into the JSONs: AutoAE (Shengcai Liu, Fu Peng and Ke Tang, AAAI 2023, arXiv:2211.12713, Table 1; RobustBench's interface and fixed 5,000 images, with clean and AutoAttack columns equal to the JSON) lowers all five older ResNet entries: Salman2020Do_50_2 38.14 -> 37.96, Salman2020Do_R50 34.96 -> 34.36, Engstrom2019Robustness 29.22 -> 28.86, Wong2020Fast 26.24 -> 24.80 and Salman2020Do_R18 25.32 -> 25.00. Adaptive Auto Attack (A3, Liu et al., CVPR 2022, arXiv:2203.05154, Table 4) gives Salman's ResNet-18 AA 25.30 -> 25.16 and WRN-50-2 38.14 -> 38.12, and a ResNet-50 at AA 34.66 -> 34.64, whereas the Salman2020Do_R50 JSON says 34.96, so that row may be another checkpoint or preprocessing. MALT (Melamed, Yehudai and Shamir, NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2407.02240, Table 2) lowers Liu2023 Swin-L, ConvNeXt-L and Swin-B and Singh2023 ConvNeXt-L/B by 0.02-0.06 points against its own AutoAttack runs, which sit 0.26-0.40 points above the JSON values (newer library versions, as MALT notes), so no MALT value is below a JSON value. PMA/PMA+ (Xie, Zheng, Huang, Ye and Ma, CVPR 2025, arXiv:2411.15210, Tables 2, 3 and 6) evaluate the top 11 ImageNet models, including Singh2023Revisiting_ConvNeXt-T-ConvStem (AA 47.60 -> PMA+ 47.56), but for 10 of the 11 models their AutoAttack column runs about 2 points below the JSON (49.46 for that model), so PMA used another image set or pipeline there. The exception is RWRN-101-2 (Peng2023Robust): clean 73.45 and AA 48.96 against the JSON's 73.44 and 48.94, a match, so its PMA+ value 48.93 (Table 6; PMA alone 49.06, Table 3) is the best published value for that model. AttackBench (Cinà et al., arXiv:2404.19460) attacks Wong2020Fast, a Salman2020Do model and a Debenedetti2022Light model on a random 5,000-image subset, not RobustBench's list. Laptop-sized entries with no published stronger evaluation on RobustBench's setup found: Chen2024Data_WRN_50_2 (40.60), Debenedetti2022Light_XCiT-S12 (41.78) and Singh2023Revisiting_ViT-S-ConvStem (48.08); Singh2023Revisiting_ConvNeXt-T-ConvStem (49.46) has only PMA's non-matching row. Known headroom is 0.02-0.14 points on modern adversarially trained models (A3, MALT, PMA+) but 0.18-1.44 points on the older ResNets (AutoAE). The result object is a tensor of 5,000 perturbed images.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a saved set of adversarial inputs for the FULL RobustBench ImageNet evaluation set (the 5,000 images returned by robustbench.data.load_imagenet(n_examples=5000) with the model's own RobustBench preprocessing, in that order) against one ImageNet Linf model loaded unmodified via robustbench.utils.load_model(model_name, dataset='imagenet', threat_model='Linf') in eval mode, with weights downloaded fresh by the skeptic, such that (a) every perturbation satisfies max|x_adv - x| <= 4/255 (float64, tolerance 1e-6) in the preprocessed [0,1] input space and 0 <= x_adv <= 1; (b) the skeptic's own clean accuracy on the 5,000 images is within 0.04 points (2 images) of the live JSON clean_acc, showing that images, preprocessing and weights match RobustBench's evaluation (the skeptic pins package versions such as torch, torchvision, timm and Pillow until it matches; if no environment matches, the claim is PENDING); (c) the robust accuracy computed by the skeptic's own forward pass in that environment (clean prediction correct AND adversarial prediction still correct; argmax, ties count as not fooled) is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than min(autoattack_acc, external) in the live https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RobustBench/robustbench/master/model_info/imagenet/Linf/ < Model > .json, re-fetched immediately before claiming, by at least 5 images (0.10 points); and (d) it is lower by at least 1 image than every robust accuracy already published for the same model (AutoAE arXiv:2211.12713 Table 1, A3 arXiv:2203.05154 Table 4, MALT arXiv:2407.02240 Table 2, PMA/PMA+ arXiv:2411.15210 Tables 3 and 6, and any paper or RobustBench issue of any date that the NOVELTY skeptic finds), a published row covering the model when its AutoAttack column matches the JSON autoattack_acc within 0.05. On 2026-10-28 this makes the bar AutoAE's value for Salman2020Do_50_2 (37.96), Salman2020Do_R50 (34.36), Engstrom2019Robustness (28.86), Wong2020Fast (24.80) and Salman2020Do_R18 (25.00), PMA+'s 48.93 for Peng2023Robust (0.01 below its JSON 48.94, so check (c) still binds there), and min(autoattack_acc, external) for the other listed models as far as found. How x_adv was produced is irrelevant; only the skeptic's plain forward pass on the unmodified deterministic model counts.

partial_wins.statement: A reproducible per-image attack-strength finding: at least 25 of the 5,000 images (indices listed), for one ResNet-18/50-sized model (Salman2020Do_R18, Salman2020Do_R50, Engstrom2019Robustness or Wong2020Fast), on which the skeptic's own run of standard AutoAttack (autoattack package, version='standard', seed 0, run on exactly those images, in an environment that passes check (b)) finds no adversarial example but the attacker's saved perturbations do (eps, box and misclassification checked by the skeptic). The attack must be one disclosed procedure with a stated compute budget: a union over AutoAttack seeds or restarts, or a re-run of a published ensemble with its published settings (AutoAE, A3, MALT, PMA+), does not qualify; the skeptic also reports how many of the listed images standard AutoAttack with seed 1 breaks. AutoAE's published totals are already 16-72 images below AutoAttack on these four models, so this is an attack-strength finding only, never a leaderboard change.

targets.verification_method: The human supplies the ImageNet validation set (ImageNet's terms; agents never accept them). Skeptic installs robustbench and autoattack in a fresh environment, loads the model by name into a fresh cache (never attacker-supplied weights), loads the 5,000 images with robustbench.data.load_imagenet and the model's preprocessing, compares a sha256 of the clean tensor with the attacker's manifest, and recomputes clean accuracy, which must be within 2 images of the JSON clean_acc; otherwise they pin older torch/torchvision/timm/Pillow versions and repeat, and report PENDING if no environment matches. Then they load x_adv (5000x3x224x224 float32), check the Linf bound and the box in float64, run clean and adversarial forward passes in batches on CPU (ResNet-50: tens of minutes), and count robust images as an integer out of 5,000. They re-fetch the live model_info JSON (quote URL and fetch time) and compare with min(autoattack_acc, external), then open AutoAE Table 1, A3 Table 4, MALT Table 2 and the PMA tables, apply the 0.05 matching rule, and search for newer evaluations and RobustBench 'New external evaluation(s)' issues. For p1 they read the attacker's code and run AutoAttack standard (seed 0, then seed 1) on the listed indices. If GitHub is unreachable the comparison is PENDING TABLE CHECK.
angles: Targeting is where ImageNet differs from CIFAR: AutoAttack's APGD-T tries only the top-9 classes out of 1,000. MALT's mesoscopic-linearity targeting (re-rank the top 100 candidate classes by a linear estimate and attack the most promising ones) found extra successes on large models; on ResNets an even wider candidate list is affordable on the ~25-35% of images that survive APGD-CE.

Spend the whole budget on the robust residue: run APGD-CE once, keep the images it fails on, then use many restarts, longer schedules, margin/DLR/probability-margin (PMA) losses and per-image loss selection there.
Transfer starts: perturbations from other RobustBench ImageNet models (same preprocessing) as initialisations for APGD on the target often succeed where random starts do not.
Pick models with a large gap between clean and robust accuracy or a large APGD-CE vs APGD-T disagreement in a local run; both hint at loss-landscape pathologies.
pitfalls: Preprocessing: RobustBench perturbs the resized and centre-cropped [0,1] image; perturbing before resizing, or after normalisation, changes the threat model.

Package-version drift: the README warns that values (even clean accuracy) fluctuate with torchvision versions; MALT's AutoAttack reruns differ from the JSON by up to 0.40 points (20 images) and its clean accuracies by up to 0.26 points (13 images), more than the 5-image margin. A robust count from an environment that does not reproduce clean_acc (check (b)) is not comparable with the JSON.
Wrong subset or order of the 5,000 images, or images already misclassified counted as new successes.

Novelty trap: AutoAE (2022) already lowers all five older ResNet entries below both the JSON and A3 (Wong2020Fast 24.80, Salman2020Do_R50 34.36, Engstrom2019Robustness 28.86, Salman2020Do_R18 25.00, Salman2020Do_50_2 37.96), so beating only the JSON value is not a record for them. A3's ResNet-50 row (AA 34.66) does not match the JSON (34.96) within 0.05, and PMA's ImageNet rows sit about 2 points below the JSON (another image set or pipeline) for 10 of its 11 models, so they do not cover those models under the matching rule; PMA's RWRN-101-2 row does match Peng2023Robust (AA 48.96 vs 48.94), so PMA+ 48.93 counts there; the NOVELTY skeptic must say which checkpoint and image set each published row uses.
Seed noise: AutoAttack differs by a few images between runs; a difference below 5 images is not a record.

targets.name: Magic-state distillation footprint: a distance-4 T-to-T protocol on 8 or 9 qubits (known 8 <= N_T(4) <= 10), or distance 5 on at most 10 qubits
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days to needs cluster (XOR-plus-CNF or structured enumeration over the 2^(N-1) - 1 possible check parts; by the n <= 54 classification of arXiv:2609.30860 a winning matrix needs 55 <= n <= 127 distinct columns at N = 8 and 55 <= n <= 255 at N = 9; the z3/CP-SAT run of arXiv:2606.07734 on N = 8 did not finish in two months)
targets.statement: In the compressed circuit form of triorthogonal-code magic-state distillation, an nT-to-1T protocol on N qubits is a binary N x n matrix G, with one column per pi/8 Pauli-Z-product rotation. Its first row has odd weight, its other rows have even weight, and every pair and every triple of rows overlaps in an even number of positions (Eq. 18 of arXiv:2606.07734). Its distance d is the fewest columns summing to e_1 = (1,0,...,0)^T (Eq. 19), and the output error scales as p^d. Hugo Jacinto, Xavier Valcarce, Victor Barizien, Elie Gouzien and Nicolas Sangouard (arXiv:2606.07734, v2 9 July 2026) define N_T(d) as the fewest qubits that reach distance >= d. Their exhaustive SAT search shows that no such protocol on fewer than 8 qubits exceeds distance 3. Their solver did not finish the N = 8, distance-4 instance after two months of runtime and found no distance-4 solution for N = 8 or 9. Their smallest protocols are distance 4 on N = 10 (lowest T-count 64, output error 495 p^4) and distance 5 on N = 11 (65T-to-1T, 7947 p^5). The 49-to-1 protocol of Sergey Bravyi and Jeongwan Haah (PRA 86, 052329 (2012), arXiv:1209.2426) uses 14 rows. Adam Wills, Shubham P. Jain and Shraddha Singh (arXiv:2609.30860, 25 Sep 2026; code and certificates at github.com/AWillsQuantum/generalised_triorthogonal_classification) then classified every generalised triorthogonal protocol with at most 54 columns and Z-distance >= 3. For one T output their Pareto frontier in (n, N) is (52, 10) and (48, 11) at distance 4 and (53, 11) and (49, 12) at distance 5. So within 54 columns nothing reaches distance 4 on N <= 9 rows or distance 5 on N <= 10. And 52 (distance 4, N = 10) and 53 (distance 5, N = 11) are the fewest T gates at those footprints. Distance >= 3 forces distinct nonzero check parts, so a winning matrix needs 55 <= n <= 2^(N-1) - 1 columns. Hence 8 <= N_T(4) <= 10 and 8 <= N_T(5) <= 11 remain open. For T-to-CCZ protocols (Eqs. 40 and 42), Jacinto et al. prove that distance 3 needs at least 8 qubits. They give a distance-3 47T-to-1CCZ protocol on 9 qubits and a distance-4 48T-to-1CCZ protocol on 10; the most compact distance-4 CCZ factory before them was a 64T-to-2CCZ protocol on 17 qubits. An 8-row CCZ protocol has five check rows and so at most 31 distinct columns. The n <= 54 classification therefore covers all of them and lists none of distance >= 3. So N_CCZ(3) = 9, while 9 <= N_CCZ(4) <= 10 is open.
targets.success_criterion: Success means one of the following. (a) An explicit binary matrix G with N <= 9 rows (direction: min N; record N = 10) that satisfies Eqs. (18a)-(18d) of arXiv:2606.07734 exactly over F_2 and has distance d >= 4 by Eq. (19), i.e. no 1, 2 or 3 columns sum to e_1. (b) An explicit G with N <= 10 rows (record N = 11) that satisfies (18a)-(18d) with d >= 5. (c) A machine-checked proof that no G with d >= 4 exists for N = 9, which establishes N_T(4) = 10. Appending a zero row turns any 8-row solution into a 9-row one, so this also covers N = 8. The proof is either a published encoding plus an UNSAT certificate (DRAT, LRAT or FRAT) verified by an independent checker such as drat-trim or cake_lpr, or an exhaustive enumeration with a written completeness argument whose run is reproduced by a second, independent implementation. In every case, re-fetch arXiv:2606.07734 and arXiv:2609.30860 for newer versions and re-run an arXiv search immediately before claiming; none may already show the claimed footprint or proof.

partial_wins.statement: A T-to-CCZ protocol satisfying Eqs. (40a)-(40d) of arXiv:2606.07734, with distance by Eq. (42) over its seven undetectable patterns, of distance >= 4 on N = 9 qubits (by the classification of arXiv:2609.30860 it needs 55 <= n <= 63 columns). A certificate as in (c) that none exists on N = 9 also counts; it establishes N_CCZ(4) = 10. Distance 3 on N = 8 is already ruled out and does not count.
A certificate as in (c) for N = 8 alone at distance 4, which proves N_T(4) >= 9.

targets.verification_method: Use an independent script of about 30 lines (pure Python or numpy uint8 arithmetic mod 2). (1) Read G (N x n). (2) Check that row 1 has odd weight and rows 2..N have even weight. (3) Check that all C(N,2) pairwise and C(N,3) triple products have even weight. (4) Drop zero columns and pairs of equal columns. (5) Compute d: no column equals e_1; no two columns sum to e_1 (set lookup); no three do (for each pair, look up e_1 + c_i + c_j among the remaining columns). For distance-5 claims, extend to four columns with a table of pair sums. As a control, run the same script on the N = 10 and N = 11 matrices in Appendix D of arXiv:2606.07734 and on the (52, 10) and (53, 11) matrices in pareto_frontier.json of arXiv:2609.30860. For (c), rebuild the encoding from the claimant's generator and check the reduction: deleting a repeated pair of equal columns preserves (18) and cannot lower d, and for d >= 3 the check parts are distinct and nonzero. Check that the clauses or enumeration cover (18) and the forbidden <= d-1 sums. Verify the proof with drat-trim or cake_lpr, or reproduce the enumeration with a second implementation. As a pipeline test, reproduce the paper's UNSAT result for N = 7. Optionally recompute the output-error prefactor with the MacWilliams identity, as the paper does.
angles: The constraints are linear. (18a)-(18d) say that the sum over selected columns c of f(c) equals [f = c_1] for every monomial f of degree 1 to 3. So the selection vector over the 2^N - 1 nonzero column types lies in an affine subspace (a coset of a punctured Reed-Muller-type code). The search is XOR-SAT plus clauses forbidding small sums equal to e_1. That suits CryptoMiniSat with Gauss-Jordan elimination, or direct coset enumeration; z3 and CP-SAT, used in the paper, are not built around Gauss-Jordan XOR reasoning.

Symmetry: the map c -> Ac, for any invertible A with A e_1 = e_1, sends solutions to solutions. Substituting linear forms keeps every polynomial at degree <= 3, keeps the coefficient of c_1, and fixes e_1. This group has order 2^(N-1) |GL(N-1,2)|; break it, for example by fixing a basis inside the support.

Split each column into its logical bit and its check part y in F_2^(N-1). Distance >= 3 makes the check parts distinct and nonzero. The set Y of check parts (plus 0 when n is odd) then has indicator in RM(N-5, N-1), the Nezami-Haah correspondence used by arXiv:2609.30860. The set U of check parts whose logical bit is 1, together with 0, has indicator in RM(N-4, N-1). Distance >= 4 adds only that every line {a, b, a+b} inside Y meets U in 0 or 2 points. For N = 8 this is a search over RM(3,7) codewords of weight 56 to 128.
The forbidden-sum condition makes the support behave like a cap-type set relative to e_1 in F_2^N. Large sum-free or Sidon-type sets in F_2^8 and F_2^9 are natural seeds.

Start from the N = 10 matrices in Appendix D of arXiv:2606.07734 and the (52, 10) and (48, 11) matrices of arXiv:2609.30860. Try deleting a row while repairing parities by local search over column sets, keeping at least 55 columns.
pitfalls: Distance here is the protocol distance of Eq. (19): Z errors on injected T states that the N - 1 check qubits miss. It is not the full CSS distance of the associated triorthogonal code, which is a separate record (see the shortest-triorthogonal-code target).
Eq. (18) treats Clifford corrections as free. T-to-CCZ protocols use Eqs. (40) and (42); keep the two cases separate.
The paper's unrestricted SAT works in the C convention (Eqs. 15-16, all-ones logical). The G convention (Eqs. 18-19, e_1 logical) is related to it by Eq. (17). Check a claim in one convention only.
Qubit recycling (Section VI) lowers the number of active qubits, for example 49-to-1 on 5 active qubits. It does not change N, which counts the rows of G.
A solver timeout, or an UNSAT verdict without a proof certificate, proves nothing; the authors ran two months without convergence.

Fewer T gates at a footprint already reached is not a win. arXiv:2609.30860 lists (52, 10) at distance 4 and (53, 11) at distance 5, and its classification shows that no protocol with fewer columns exists there.

A candidate with N <= 9 and at most 54 columns would contradict the classification of arXiv:2609.30860. Re-check it, and the classification's stated scope (full row rank, distinct columns, exact distance), before claiming.

targets.name: Bivariate bicycle codes: prove the exact distance of IBM's [[360,12,<=24]] or [[756,16,<=34]] code (only upper bounds are published)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (exhaustive anchored cluster search at radius 23 for n = 360, parallel over anchors and branches); [[756,16]] likely needs a cluster
targets.statement: Bivariate bicycle (BB) codes are weight-6 quantum LDPC codes; IBM's [[144,12,12]] gross code is the best-known example. They are defined by x and y, the commuting cyclic shifts on Z_l x Z_m; A = A1+A2+A3 and B = B1+B2+B3, sums of monomials; and check matrices H_X = [A|B] and H_Z = [B^T|A^T]. The family is due to Sergey Bravyi, Andrew W. Cross, Jay M. Gambetta, Dmitri Maslov, Patrick Rall and Theodore J. Yoder (Nature 627, 778 (2024), arXiv:2308.07915). Their Table 3 gives distances computed by mixed integer programming up to [[288,12,18]]. For the two largest examples it gives only upper bounds: [[360,12,<=24]] (l = 30, m = 6, A = x^9+y+y^2, B = y^3+x^25+x^26) and [[756,16,<=34]] (l = 21, m = 18, A = x^3+y^10+y^17, B = y^5+x^3+x^19). Benjamin C. B. Symons, Abhishek Rajput and Dan E. Browne (arXiv:2511.13560, v3 6 Aug 2026) built sequences of covering BB codes. They obtained exact MIP distances only up to d = 14 and used BP-OSD upper bounds above that, for example [[432,12,<=24]] (l = 18, m = 12, A = x^15+y^7+y^2, B = y^9+x^7+x^14) and [[504,12,<=30]] (l = 42, m = 6, A = x^27+y+y^2, B = y^3+x^37+x^38). Mohammad Rowshan and Simon Devitt (arXiv:2609.39395, v2 1 Oct 2026) proved all six standard BB distances up to [[288,12,18]] with an anchored cluster search; the 288 case took 455,504,708 nodes at radius 17. The README of their public tool reports bounds 18 <= d <= 30 for the [[360,12]] code after a 60-second run and notes that a weight-24 logical is known. It adds that beyond distances of roughly 22 to 24 the search needs a larger budget, several cores or reduction by the full automorphism group. Mark Webster, Abraham Jacob and Oscar Higgott (arXiv:2603.22532, v2 14 Aug 2026) benchmarked exact and heuristic distance algorithms. They report that minimum distances in their BB set (72 to 3024 qubits) are not known with certainty.
targets.success_criterion: Success means establishing the EXACT minimum distance d of [[360,12,<=24]] or [[756,16,<=34]], built with exactly the l, m, A and B of Bravyi et al. Table 3 given above. Two things are required. (i) An explicit nontrivial logical operator of weight d, confirmed by an independent script: for Z type, a vector in ker H_X that is not in the row space of H_Z, or the X-type analogue. (ii) A re-runnable exhaustive certificate that no nontrivial logical of either type has weight < d. A Z-type certificate plus a proved d_X = d_Z symmetry, as in Proposition 3 of arXiv:2609.39395, also suffices. Acceptable certificates are an anchored cluster search, Brouwer-Zimmermann enumeration, or an MIP/SAT model solved to proven optimality. The certificate must be reproduced by a second, independent implementation or backed by a checkable UNSAT proof (DRAT/LRAT). Any value of d counts, whether or not it equals the published bound. Immediately before claiming, re-fetch arXiv:2609.39395 and the README of its repository and re-run an arXiv search; the value must not already be established.

partial_wins.statement: A nontrivial logical operator of weight strictly below the published upper bound for any of [[360,12,<=24]], [[756,16,<=34]], [[432,12,<=24]] or [[504,12,<=30]] (polynomials as above), verified exactly. This lowers the published upper bound.
The exact distance, meeting both parts of the main criterion, of [[432,12,<=24]], [[504,12,<=30]], or any other code in Tables 1-4 of arXiv:2511.13560 listed only with an upper bound of at least 16.
A certified lower bound d >= 22 for [[360,12]], with a certificate as in (ii), even if the gap stays open.

targets.verification_method: Build H_X and H_Z from (l, m, A, B) as 0/1 block-circulant matrices. Check H_X H_Z^T = 0 mod 2 and k = n - rank H_X - rank H_Z (12 or 16). For a witness u, check H_X u = 0, check that u is not in the row space of H_Z (rank test), and count its weight. For the lower bound, rerun the claimant's search with the published parameters and compare node counts. One option is cluster_lb from github.com/mohammad-rowshan/BB-Codes-Distance-Logical-Decomposition, which certifies d >= W+1 when a radius-W run returns nothing. Confirm with a second method: an exact MIP solved to optimality by two solvers, or a SAT encoding with a cardinality constraint whose UNSAT proof is checked by drat-trim. Use the l x m translation symmetry to fix one support qubit. Reproduce [[288,12,18]] first as a control.
angles: Extend the Rowshan-Devitt anchored cluster search. Quotient by the full automorphism group (Z_l x Z_m translations, the block-swap symmetry and any polynomial automorphisms of the pair), and split the two anchors and the first-level branches across cores, as their README suggests.
Their exact sequence splits logical classes into an annihilator component and a colon component. Certify each separately; one may close at a lower radius.
Covering-graph arguments (Symons-Rajput-Browne Sec. 4.3) give d_h >= d when h is odd and k_h = k. Check whether [[360,12]] or [[432,12]] covers a smaller BB code with known distance and the same k.
For upper bounds, sample BP-OSD with many random priors (Bravyi et al.'s method) or QDistRnd; the README warns that its algebraic screens are loose on long codes.
pitfalls: BP-OSD, QDistRnd and the package's algebraic screens give only upper bounds; a lower bound needs an exhaustive certificate.
Conventions change the code: which block is A, and whether x shifts the l or the m index. Reproduce n, k and a weight-24 logical for [[360,12]] before searching.
Degeneracy: a light vector in ker H_X that lies in the row space of H_Z is a stabilizer, not a logical.
[[288,12,18]] and the smaller standard codes are already proved (Rowshan-Devitt 2026) and do not count.
A solver run stopped at a time limit gives no certificate.

targets.name: Shortest triorthogonal (transversal-T) codes [[n,1,d]] at d >= 7: beat the Jain-Albert table, e.g. distance 7 with fewer than 95 qubits
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (structured ILP/SAT searches over triorthogonal matrices with n in 55..94 at d = 7; exact distances for n <= ~200 are fast)
targets.statement: A triorthogonal matrix (Sergey Bravyi and Jeongwan Haah, PRA 86, 052329 (2012), arXiv:1209.2426) is a binary matrix G in which every pair and every triple of rows overlaps in an even number of positions, with k odd-weight rows. Its CSS code takes the even-weight rows as X stabilizers and G-perp as Z stabilizers. It encodes k qubits on which transversal T acts as logical T up to Clifford corrections. These codes underlie magic-state distillation. Weak triply even codes realise logical T with physical T gates alone. For k = 1, Shubham P. Jain and Victor V. Albert (arXiv:2408.12752, v3 24 March 2025; DOI 10.1109/JSAIT.2025.3570832) tabulated the shortest known codes for odd distances up to 31. Triorthogonal (their Table I): [[15,1,3]], [[49,1,5]] (Bravyi-Haah), [[95,1,7]], [[185,1,9]], [[279,1,11]], [[417,1,13]], [[575,1,15]], [[777,1,17]], [[983,1,19]], [[1317,1,21]], [[1651,1,23]], [[2033,1,25]], [[2415,1,27]], [[2813,1,29]], [[3211,1,31]]. Weak triply even (Table II): [[189,1,9]], [[283,1,11]], [[441,1,13]], [[599,1,15]], [[805,1,17]], [[1011,1,19]], [[1345,1,21]], [[1679,1,23]], [[2061,1,25]], [[2443,1,27]], [[2841,1,29]], [[3239,1,31]], with the same entries as Table I at d = 3, 5, 7. Both tables come from doubling (Bravyi and Cross, arXiv:1509.03239) of best-known self-dual or quadratic-residue codes. The two smallest cells are closed. Stergios Koutsioumpas, Darren Banfield and Alastair Kay (arXiv:2210.14066) proved that [[15,1,3]] is the smallest distance-3 code with a transversal non-Clifford gate. Sepehr Nezami and Jeongwan Haah (arXiv:2107.09684) classified all triorthogonal codes with n + k <= 38. Adam Wills, Shubham P. Jain and Shraddha Singh (arXiv:2609.30860, 25 Sep 2026) extended this to every generalised triorthogonal code with n <= 54 and Z-distance >= 3. For k = 1 their frontier first reaches Z-distance 4 at n = 48 and Z-distance 5 at n = 49, and has nothing of Z-distance 6 or more. So [[49,1,5]] is the shortest distance-5 triorthogonal code, and distance >= 6 needs n >= 55; no better lower bound is known. An ILP search by Alessio Baldelli, Olai A. Mostad, Hsuan-Yin Lin, Eirik Rosnes and Massimo Battaglioni (arXiv:2605.24519, v3 14 Oct 2026) recovered [[49,1,5]] and [[95,1,7]] and found longer distance-5 codes ([[85,1,5]], [[89,1,5]], [[93,1,5]]). Shiroman Prakash's census of triply even cyclic codes up to length 763 (arXiv:2610.08012, Oct 2026) gives nothing shorter at d >= 7 (for example [[127,1,7]] and [[223,1,9]]). No [[n,1,7]] triorthogonal code with n < 95 is known.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an explicit binary matrix G (m x n) with exactly one odd-weight row such that an independent script verifies the following exactly over F_2. Every row pair and every row triple has even overlap (triorthogonality in the sense of Bravyi-Haah, arXiv:1209.2426). The even rows G_0 as X stabilizers and G-perp as Z stabilizers define an [[n,1]] CSS code. The full distance d = min(d_X, d_Z) is computed exactly, by full enumeration or by two independent exact algorithms. Here d_X is the minimum weight of the coset (odd row + span G_0) and d_Z the minimum weight of G_0-perp minus G-perp. n must be STRICTLY LESS (direction: min) than the Jain-Albert Table I entry for some odd d in 7..31: 95, 185, 279, 417, 575, 777, 983, 1317, 1651, 2033, 2415, 2813 and 3211 for d = 7, 9, ..., 31, as re-read from the latest version of arXiv:2408.12752 immediately before claiming. An arXiv search re-run at claim time must find no shorter [[n,1,d]] triorthogonal code. Distances 3 and 5 are closed and do not count.

partial_wins.statement: A weak triply even [[n,1,d]] code (logical T from transversal T with no Clifford correction, as defined in Sec. I-C of arXiv:2408.12752), verified exactly, with n strictly below the Table II entry for some odd d in 9..31 (189, 283, 441, 599, 805, 1011, 1345, 1679, 2061, 2443, 2841, 3239).

A k = 1 triorthogonal matrix with Z-distance d_Z >= 7 (the quantity that sets the distillation order) on at most 94 columns, even if d_X < 7. This would beat the T-count of the 95-to-1 distance-7 distillation protocol. It must also beat any published single-output distance-7 protocol found by an arXiv search at claim time.

An exhaustive, re-runnable certificate extending arXiv:2609.30860 for k = 1: no triorthogonal code with d_Z >= 6 exists for any n with 55 <= n <= n0, for some n0 >= 55. This raises the lower bound for distance 6 and above to n0 + 1.

targets.verification_method: Check triorthogonality with integer dot products mod 2; with about 30 rows, the C(m,3) checks are instant. Build H_X = G_0 and a basis of G-perp for H_Z by Gaussian elimination, and confirm k = n - rank H_X - rank H_Z = 1. Compute d_X by enumerating the coset (2^(m-1) words) and d_Z by Brouwer-Zimmermann or an exact MIP on G_0-perp minus G-perp; for n <= 100 each takes seconds to hours. Cross-check d with a second implementation, for example the open-source distance package of arXiv:2603.22532. For p1, also verify the weak triply even condition exactly as stated in Sec. I-C of arXiv:2408.12752. Then check by stabilizer simulation that transversal T maps the code space to itself and acts as logical T or T-dagger. For p3, reproduce the k = 1 part of the n <= 54 frontier of arXiv:2609.30860 with the claimant's code as a control, and re-run the extension with a second implementation.
angles: Doubling as used by Jain and Albert combines a self-dual CSS code of distance d with a triorthogonal code of distance d - 2. At d = 7 that needs a distance-7 self-dual CSS code and a distance-5 triorthogonal code. The first is the [[23,1,7]] Golay code: no self-dual binary code shorter than 24 has distance 8. The second is now known to need 49 qubits. So doubling cannot go below 2*23 + 49 = 95, and beating 95 needs a different construction.
ILP with prescribed automorphism groups (Baldelli et al.) recovered the records. Target n in 55..94 at d = 7 with groups such as dihedral groups, AGL(1,p), or PSL(2,q) acting on q+1 points.

Reuse the Wills-Jain-Singh pipeline (unital triorthogonal spaces correspond to RM(m-4, m) codewords, then logical rows are added) restricted to k = 1 and Z-distance >= 6. The restriction may be far cheaper than their 10^8 core-hour estimate for a full length-56 classification.

For a fixed row count, the XOR-SAT formulation over column-type multiplicities applies (see the distillation-footprint target). Add 'no <= d-1 columns sum to a logical' clauses for the Z-distance, then run an exact d_X check.

At larger d the table is a doubling ladder built on best-known self-dual codes. A shorter self-dual input or a direct construction (quadratic-residue, Reed-Muller-like or cyclic triply even codes) can beat a high-d entry; the cyclic census of arXiv:2610.08012 does not yet.
pitfalls: Distance conventions differ: distillation papers use only the Z-distance, while this table uses the full distance min(d_X, d_Z). Report both.
Triorthogonal codes (T up to Clifford corrections) and weak triply even codes (T exactly) are separate columns of the Jain-Albert tables; compare each claim with the right one.

Distances 3 and 5 are closed. [[15,1,3]] is optimal (arXiv:2210.14066). The n <= 54 classification of arXiv:2609.30860 shows that Z-distance 5 needs 49 qubits, so [[49,1,5]] is optimal too. Claims there are not wins.
Non-stabilizer codes, such as the ((27,2,5)) binary dihedral permutation-invariant code mentioned by the Error Correction Zoo, realise transversal T with fewer qubits but do not count.
Codes whose non-Clifford logical gate is a depth-one layer of multi-qubit gates, such as the [[37,1,7]] and [[59,1,9]] codes of arXiv:2610.06730, are not triorthogonal and do not count.
The distillation-footprint target minimises rows N, not length n. A small-N protocol is not a short code.

targets.name: Gross code syndrome extraction: settle the Strikis-Browne-Beverland conjecture that their depth-8 circuit has circuit distance 11, or reach 12 with an interleaved circuit
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (a refutation search takes hours; a proof needs an exact MaxSAT/ILP or UNSAT certificate on a detector error model with ~10^5 mechanisms, or on the much smaller extended code of the residual errors)
targets.statement: The [[144,12,12]] gross code (Bravyi et al., Nature 627, 778 (2024), arXiv:2308.07915; l = 12, m = 6, A = x^3+y+y^2, B = y^3+x+x^2) loses distance to hook errors in its syndrome-extraction circuit (SEC). By BP-OSD search, all 936 variants of the original syndrome cycle have circuit-level distance d_circ <= 10, and Bravyi et al. conjecture d_circ = 10 for their Eq. (9) cycle. Armands Strikis, Dan E. Browne and Michael E. Beverland (arXiv:2603.05481, v2 14 Sep 2026) proved several restrictions using residual-error and extended-code-distance bounds. No non-interleaved single-ancilla CNOT circuit reaches d_circ = 12 (Proposition 4), no uniformly tiled one reaches 11 (Proposition 5), and only three three-colour tilings survive (Proposition 6). They gave an explicit depth-8 three-colour-tiled left-right schedule (their Figure 12). They conjecture that it has d_circ = 11, since ten thousand outer loops of their minimum-weight search found no undetectable logical error below 11. They also prove that interleaving X and Z checks cannot lower circuit distance, and leave open whether any interleaved circuit reaches 12. They cite morphing circuits (Mackenzie H. Shaw and Barbara M. Terhal, PRL 134, 090602 (2025), arXiv:2407.16336) as reaching circuit distance twelve with the gross code's qubit counts. Shaw and Terhal report only a BP-OSD upper bound, d_circ <= 12, for end-cycle [[144,12,12]] codes with weight-9 checks derived from the [[288,12,18]] BB code. That is a different code and circuit family and does not settle this question. Circuit distance follows Strikis et al. Sec. II C. It is the fewest error mechanisms of standard circuit noise (each failing operation counted once) that flip no detector but flip a logical observable, in an m-round X- or Z-basis memory experiment followed by one perfect round. d_circ is the smaller of the two basis values.
targets.success_criterion: Success means EITHER (a) or (b). (a) Take the Figure 12 schedule of arXiv:2603.05481v2 on the gross code's H_X and H_Z (Bravyi et al.). Compile it to a Stim circuit with standard circuit noise (Strikis et al. Sec. II C), for X- and Z-basis memory experiments with m noisy rounds and one perfect final round. Then exhibit, for some m <= 12, an explicit set of at most 10 error mechanisms that flips no detector and flips at least one logical observable (refuting the conjecture). Alternatively, give a machine-checkable proof that for m = 12 every such set, in either basis, has at least 11 mechanisms (confirming d_circ = 11). (b) Any CNOT-based SEC for the gross code with a single ancilla per check (interleaving of X and Z checks allowed, depth stated) with d_circ = 12 at m = 12, certified by such a proof. A proof is either an exact optimum of the minimum undetectable logical error problem, from a MaxSAT/ILP solver with optimality re-established independently, or an UNSAT certificate (DRAT/LRAT) for 'at most d-1 mechanisms', checked by drat-trim or cake_lpr. The proof may be on the detector error model. For non-interleaved circuits it may instead be on the extended code of the residual-error set, which Strikis et al. Theorem 1 shows equals d_circ, provided the residual set is re-derived from the circuit by code. Re-fetch arXiv:2603.05481 and search arXiv before claiming.

partial_wins.statement: A certified exact circuit distance of 10 (witness plus lower-bound proof as in (a)) for the original Bravyi et al. syndrome cycle at m = 12; only the upper bound d_circ <= 10 is published.
A certified d_circ = 11 (as in (a)) at m = 12 for any non-interleaved single-ancilla gross-code circuit other than Figure 12, showing that the bound of Proposition 4 is attained.

targets.verification_method: Rebuild the circuit from Figure 12's time-step labels and the check matrices of Bravyi et al.; BB144 matrices are also in github.com/PurePhys/LR-circuits/parity_check_matrices. Generate X- and Z-basis memory circuits in Stim and export the detector error model without decomposition. For a refutation, XOR the claimed columns: no detector bit may remain, some observable bit must flip, and there must be at most 10 columns. For a proof, rebuild the CNF or ILP from the DEM, or from the residual-error extended code, with the claimant's published script. Validate the encoding against brute force on small instances (m = 1 or 2, and the [[72,12,6]] code). Then check the UNSAT proof with drat-trim or re-solve to optimality with a second solver (for example Gurobi and SCIP, as benchmarked in arXiv:2603.22532). Stim's search_for_undetectable_logical_errors gives only upper bounds.
angles: For non-interleaved circuits, Strikis et al. Theorem 1 gives d_circ = d_ext(E), the extended-code distance of the residual-error set. That is a code-capacity distance problem on 144 qubits plus residual columns, far smaller than the full DEM. Certifying d_ext = 11 for the Figure 12 residual pattern by anchored cluster search (Rowshan-Devitt, arXiv:2609.39395) or exact MIP may be the shortest route to a proof.
For a refutation, run BP-OSD searches with many random priors (Bravyi et al. Eq. (12)) and Stim's undetectable-error search on the DEM, focused on supports near the Figure 11 residual errors.
For (b), interleaving can only help (their theorem). Search interleaved CNOT orders with a SAT/ILP model of hook propagation over the 72 checks of each type, scored by extended-code distance.
pitfalls: Circuit distance depends on the number of rounds m and on the noise model; use Strikis et al.'s standard circuit noise and state m.
BP-OSD and Stim's undetectable-error search give upper bounds only.
Morphing circuits (Shaw-Terhal) and flag-qubit circuits are different circuit families and do not count for (a) or (b).

Figure 12 is a picture, and the paper's released Stim circuits (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.18853600) cover other codes only, so the gross-code circuit must be rebuilt by hand. Transcription errors in CNOT time steps silently change the circuit. Publish the transcribed schedule and check its residual pattern against Figure 11.
Code distance 12 caps d_circ; a claimed value above 12 signals a bug.

targets.name: Multi-controlled Z with fewer T gates: an exact C^nZ (n >= 4 controls) with T-count below Gidney-Jones' 4n - 6
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (exact Clifford+T simulation of candidates on <= ~20 qubits; finding the gadget is the hard part)
targets.statement: The n-controlled Z gate C^nZ (n controls plus one target, n + 1 qubits) appears in Grover reflections, multiplexers and arithmetic. Using Clifford gates, T gates, ancillas, Pauli measurements and classically controlled Cliffords, the logical-AND construction gives T-count 4n - 4. Craig Gidney and N. Cody Jones (arXiv:2106.11513, 2021) built a CCCZ with 6 T gates and reduced the general count to 4n - 6 for n > 2. Ken M. Nakanishi and Synge Todo (arXiv:2410.00910, v2 3 Oct 2024) systematised such decompositions and kept 4n - 6 as the minimum known T-count. At that T-count they lowered the CNOT count (CNOT plus CZ gates) to 3n - 3 to 4n - 4 (their Figs. 1a and 3a) or 3n - 2 to 4n - 5 (Figs. 1a' and 3a), depending on measurement outcomes (Table III). Lower bounds are far below. Michael Beverland, Earl Campbell, Mark Howard and Vadym Kliuchnikov (Quantum Sci. Technol. 5, 035009 (2020), arXiv:1904.01124) show via stabilizer nullity that an m-qubit multi-controlled Z needs at least m T states (Proposition 4.1), i.e. n + 1 here. Their stabilizer-extent value 9/4 for CCCZ|+ > ^4 (Table 4, computed to eight digits) gives at least 5.12, hence 6, T states for CCCZ (Table 1), so the Gidney-Jones CCCZ is optimal. Fixing one control to |1> turns a C^nZ protocol into a C^(n-1)Z protocol with the same T gates. So every C^nZ with n >= 3 needs at least max(6, n + 1) T gates. With every measurement outcome at probability 1/2, they also show that n - 1 CCZ states are necessary and sufficient (Lemma 6.6). Arul Rhik Mazumder's isotropy bound (arXiv:2610.01024, Oct 2026) is exact for Hadamard-free circuits but explicitly excludes measurement and feed-forward. Abhoy Kole, Till Schnittka and Rolf Drechsler (arXiv:2605.18159, May 2026) improve static clean-ancilla decompositions but stay above 4n - 6. David Gosset, Robin Kothari and Chenyi Zhang (arXiv:2510.07223, Oct 2025) implement the multi-qubit Toffoli to diamond-norm error epsilon with O(log(1/epsilon)) T gates, but only approximately. So for n = 4 the exact T-count lies between 6 and 10.
targets.success_criterion: Success means, for some n with 4 <= n <= 12, an explicit protocol on the n + 1 data qubits plus any number of ancillas prepared in a fixed stabilizer state. It may use Clifford gates, T and T-dagger gates, Pauli measurements, and Clifford gates classically controlled by earlier outcomes. For EVERY measurement record, the map on the data qubits must be exactly C^nZ up to a record-dependent global phase, with all ancillas ending in a state independent of the data input. The number of T/T-dagger gates on the worst-case record, counting each classically controlled T gate wherever it could fire, must be at most 4n - 7 (direction: min; record 4n - 6, Gidney-Jones arXiv:2106.11513). An arXiv search re-run immediately before claiming must find no lower published count for that n. Magic states other than T states, catalyst states and approximate synthesis do not count.

partial_wins.statement: For some n in 4..10, T-count exactly 4n - 6 with a worst-case two-qubit gate count (CNOT or CZ, including classically controlled ones, over all measurement records) strictly below 4n - 5. That is the best worst case in Nakanishi-Todo Table III (Figs. 1a' and 3a).

A rigorous lower bound of at least 7 T gates for C^4Z in the model above, beating the bound of 6 inherited from CCCZ. Its numerical part must be certified, for example by an exact dual certificate for a stabilizer-extent-type monotone, and its monotonicity argument must cover measurement and feed-forward.

targets.verification_method: Simulate the protocol exactly over Z[1/2, e^{i pi/4}] (sympy, or integer vectors scaled by powers of sqrt2) on the n + 1 + a qubits. For every measurement record (2^r branches, pruning zero-probability ones), apply the record's operations to each computational basis input |x> with the ancillas in their initial state. Check that the output equals c_record * (-1)^{x_1 x_2 ... x_{n+1}} |x> (x) |anc_final > , with the same c_record for all 2^{n+1} inputs; by linearity this certifies the branch acts as C^nZ. Count T/T-dagger gates on the worst branch. For n <= 8 with <= 8 ancillas this is 2^17 amplitudes per branch, a matter of seconds. For p1, also count two-qubit gates per branch.
angles: Gidney-Jones save 2 T by merging two logical-ANDs into a 6-T CCCZ. A gadget that merges three ANDs (C^4Z) in fewer than 10 T, or a second independent 2-T saving, gives 4n - 7 or better by induction.

Phase-polynomial view: with clean ancillas and measurement-based uncomputation, C^nZ is a degree-(n+1) phase. Look for identities in which several partial products share T gates, as in the Gidney-Jones CCCZ.
Search small gadgets with SAT or ILP over Clifford+T circuits with one or two measurements and ancillas, using exact simulation as the oracle.

Lower-bound side: the stabilizer extent of C^4Z|+ > ^5 is only 9/8 + 1/sqrt2 (Beverland et al. Table 4), worth about 3.8 T states. Going past the inherited bound of 6 needs another monotone, for example one adapted from the dyadic monotone, or a new LP/SDP certificate.
pitfalls: Relative-phase multi-controlled gates (Maslov, arXiv:1508.03273) are cheaper but are not C^nZ; they count only if every relative phase is undone inside the protocol.
Every measurement record must be handled; a protocol that is exact only on the most likely record is not exact.
Notation: C^nZ here has n controls and acts on n + 1 qubits; Beverland et al. write C^{n-1}Z for n qubits.
Mazumder's isotropy bound does not apply when measurements are used: it gives 7 for CCZ, which measurement circuits beat with 4.
For n = 3 the T-count 6 is optimal: the stabilizer extent of CCCZ|+ > ^4 is 9/4, worth at least 5.12 T states. Claims for n = 3 are out of scope.
Approximate constructions do not count. The randomly chosen circuits of Gosset, Kothari and Zhang (arXiv:2510.07223) use O(log(1/epsilon)) T gates but implement C^nZ only to error epsilon.

targets.name: Self-dual quantum codes on 13 qubits: count the LC orbits of connected 13-vertex graphs (next term of OEIS A090899, known to n = 12)
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (about 5.4e9 one-vertex extensions of the 1,323,363 twelve-vertex classes to canonise up to local complementation)
targets.statement: Every self-dual additive code over GF(4) of length n, equivalently every [[n,0]] qubit stabilizer code (stabilizer state), is equivalent to a graph code (Schlingemann). Two such codes are equivalent exactly when their graphs are related by local complementations and isomorphism; Bouchet's algorithm decides this in polynomial time. OEIS A090899 counts the indecomposable codes, i.e. connected graphs up to LC and isomorphism: 1, 1, 1, 2, 4, 11, 26, 101, 440, 3132, 40457, 1274068 for n = 1..12. OEIS A094927 counts all codes: 1, 2, 3, 6, 11, 26, 59, 182, 675, 3990, 45144, 1323363. Lars Eirik Danielsen and Matthew G. Parker (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 113 (2006) 1351-1367) classified all lengths up to 12, extending the classification of David G. Glynn and Johannes G. Maks up to length 9; their terms a(10)-a(12) were added to OEIS on 17 June 2004. Danielsen's database at codetables.de (last modified 6 May 2005) also stops at n = 12 for complete classifications; its length-14 files (codes14.mag, vncorbits14.g6) hold only the extremal Type II codes. The OEIS entry, re-fetched for this check, still has no a(13). Hemant Sharma, Kenneth Goodenough, Johannes Borregaard, Filip Rozpedek and Jonas Helsen (Quantum 10, 2001 (2026), arXiv:2506.00292) find minimum-edge representatives of individual graph states up to 16 qubits but give no orbit counts.
targets.success_criterion: Success means the exact value a(13) of OEIS A090899, the number of LC-and-isomorphism classes of connected 13-vertex graphs (equivalently, indecomposable self-dual additive GF(4) codes of length 13). It must come with four things. (i) A public list of one canonical representative graph per class. (ii) Two independent implementations, using different canonical-form or equivalence-test methods, that produce the same count. (iii) A completeness check by code: every connected 13-vertex graph is LC-equivalent to a listed representative, via the extension lemma that every class contains a one-vertex extension of a representative of some 12-vertex class (decomposable classes included). (iv) Pairwise inequivalence of the representatives, by LC invariants or Bouchet's equivalence test. The value must be new: OEIS A090899 and A094927 re-fetched immediately before claiming must not list a(13).

partial_wins.statement: An independent re-derivation of a(1..12) and A094927(1..12) with a new implementation and published representatives, cross-checked class by class against Danielsen's database by LC-equivalence tests. This audit validates the method that will be used for n = 13.

targets.verification_method: Re-run both implementations (or a supplied checkpointed job) and compare the counts. Check coverage under the extension lemma: regenerate all one-vertex extensions of the twelve-vertex representatives (Danielsen's database, used as data only) and map each to a listed class. Spot-check random pairs of representatives with Bouchet's algorithm, and check per-class LC invariants (orbit size, cut-rank profiles, interlace-polynomial values) for collisions. First reproduce a(10) = 3132, a(11) = 40457 and a(12) = 1274068 with the same code. Derive A094927(13) from a(1..13) by the Euler transform as a consistency check.
angles: Bucket extensions by cheap LC invariants (cut-rank profiles over vertex subsets, interlace-polynomial evaluations) before exact equivalence tests; most extensions collide quickly.

Choose canonical orbit representatives carefully: orbits on 13 vertices can be large, so a cheaper canonical choice (for example canonically labelled minimum-edge representatives, using the ILP of arXiv:2506.00292) may beat full orbit enumeration.
Parallelise over the twelve-vertex representatives; each yields 2^12 extensions that can be canonised independently.
pitfalls: A090899 counts connected graphs (indecomposable codes) and A094927 counts all of them; mixing the two is the classic error.
LC-equivalence is coarser than isomorphism; an implementation that canonises graphs instead of orbits overcounts.
Edge-local-complementation (pivot) orbits are a different sequence (A156800, binary linear codes).
Danielsen's 2005 database files are data only; never run code from them.

targets.name: Google Willow surface-code memory (public data): decode the distance-7 experiment to a logical error per cycle below the neural decoder's 1.43e-3
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (50,000 shots per duration and basis at d = 7; neural decoders need a GPU)
targets.statement: Google Quantum AI and collaborators (Rajeev Acharya et al., 'Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold', Nature 638, 920 (2025), arXiv:2408.13687) ran distance-3, 5 and 7 surface-code memories on the 105-qubit Willow processor. They published the data on Zenodo (record 13273331, CC BY 4.0, file google_105Q_surface_code_d3_d5_d7.zip). For the distance-7 patch (d7_at_q6_7), each basis holds 50,000 shots at each of 13 memory durations, r10, r30, ..., r250 cycles. It also holds a one-cycle run (r01) and a 13-cycle calibration run (r13). With a fine-tuned neural network decoder of the AlphaQubit line (Johannes Bausch, Andrew W. Senior et al., Nature 2024, arXiv:2310.05900) they report a distance-7 logical error per cycle eps_7 = (1.43 +- 0.03) x 10^-3 and Lambda = 2.14 +- 0.02. Ensembled matching synthesis (Libra, with a reinforcement-learning-optimised prior; its predictions ship in the release) gives eps_7 = (1.71 +- 0.03) x 10^-3 and Lambda = 2.04 +- 0.02 (Table S1). eps_d is fitted separately for each basis by a weighted line through ln(1 - 2 p_L) over the 13 durations up to 250 cycles, and averaged over X and Z. For the distance-7 data the neural decoder was cross-validated on an even/odd shot split. AlphaQubit 2 (Andrew W. Senior, Thomas Edlich, Francisco J. H. Heras, Lei M. Zhang, Oscar Higgott et al., arXiv:2512.07737, v2 11 Mar 2026) is reported comparable to the first AlphaQubit and better than Libra on this dataset, with values shown only in its Fig. 3c. A sim-to-real benchmark by Shay J. Manor, Leila S. Erhili and Yassine Jebbouri (arXiv:2609.04557, Sep 2026) ranks Tesseract first in its six-decoder panel on the real data, at 1.67 x 10^-3 per cycle at d = 7. That figure is a mean per-cycle rate over a 2-30-round window, not the fitted eps above.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a decoder and its outputs on the 105-qubit distance-7 memory data of Zenodo record 13273331 (patch d7_at_q6_7) such that the following gives eps_7 STRICTLY BELOW 1.40 x 10^-3 (direction: min; the published 1.43e-3 minus its quoted 0.03e-3 uncertainty). Decode every shot of the 13 scored durations r10, r30, ..., r250 in both bases. The r01 and r13 runs are not scored, and r13 (the 13-cycle calibration run) may be used to fit priors. For each basis separately, fit ln F(n) = ln F_0 + n ln(1 - 2 eps) to F(n) = 1 - 2E(n) over the 13 durations by weighted least squares, with weights 1/s_n^2 where s_n = 2 sqrt(E(n)(1 - E(n))/N_n) / (1 - 2E(n)). Average the X and Z values. Before its own number counts, the same script must reproduce eps_7 = 1.71 x 10^-3 (to within 0.01e-3) from the release's libra_decoder_with_rl_optimized_prior predictions. An unweighted fit gives about 1.65e-3 there and is not allowed. No decoder parameter (weights, priors, edge weights, ensemble or model choices) may be fitted on any shot it is scored on. Either nothing is fitted on the scored shots, or the even/odd protocol is used: fit on even-indexed shots and score odd-indexed ones, then the reverse, so every scored shot is scored once. The result must also beat any later d = 7 value on this dataset found by an arXiv search immediately before claiming. AlphaQubit 2 gives its d = 7 value only graphically (Fig. 3c of arXiv:2512.07737). A claim must lie below the lower end of that point's plotted 95% interval. If this cannot be read unambiguously, the claim is PROMISING, not CONFIRMED, until the value is known numerically.

partial_wins.statement: No parameter may be fitted on any scored shot; priors come only from the r13 calibration run, the release's own detector-error-model files, simulation, or none. Under these conditions, eps_7 under the same weighted fit must be strictly below 1.71 x 10^-3. That is the value of Libra with the RL-optimised prior (Acharya et al. Table S1), whose predictions ship in decoding_results/libra_decoder_with_rl_optimized_prior. Tesseract must also be re-run by the claimant with the same prior under the identical fit as a control, and beaten.

targets.verification_method: Download the Zenodo archive (data only; no code from it needs to run). Rerun the claimant's decoder on every scored distance-7 shot (bases X and Z, durations r10 to r250) with the stated fold assignment. Recompute E(n) per duration and basis against obs_flips_actual.b8. Refit eps per basis with the weighted least-squares fit of the criterion and average X and Z. As a calibration, the same script applied to the release's libra_decoder_with_rl_optimized_prior predictions must give 1.71e-3 (a check run for this review gave 1.711e-3 weighted and 1.652e-3 unweighted). Confirm from the training scripts and data hashes that no fitting step reads a shot of the fold it is scored on, and that r01 and r13 are not scored.
angles: Tesseract (A* search) is the strongest non-neural decoder on this data. Combine it with a detector error model re-fitted on the even fold (correlations and leakage-induced hyperedges) and score on the odd fold.
Ensemble heterogeneous decoders (correlated matching variants, Tesseract, BP-based) through calibrated soft outputs; Acharya et al. already ensemble five neural models.
The data contains rare correlated bursts. A decoder conditioned on recent detection density within a shot may help, but must respect the fold rule.
pitfalls: Using the observable flips of the scored fold for anything (training, early stopping, prior fitting, model selection) voids the claim.
The fit is inverse-variance weighted. An unweighted fit lowers eps_7 by about 3.5% on the same predictions, which is more than the margin to the record.
eps from a single duration via (1 - (1-2E)^(1/n))/2 is not the fitted eps; use the fit over the 13 scored durations.
Each basis directory also holds r01 and r13 runs; r13 is the calibration data behind the released priors. Do not score them.
The 72-qubit processor datasets (surface-code sets 1 and 2 and the repetition code) in the same Zenodo record are different experiments with different published values.
Manor et al.'s 1.67e-3 for Tesseract is a mean per-cycle rate over a 2-30-round window, not the fitted eps; do not compare it with fitted values.
With the quoted +-0.03e-3 uncertainty, a result of 1.42e-3 is not a win.

targets.name: Permutation flow shop (Taillard benchmarks): a makespan below the best known for one of the 12 open Taillard instances, with VRF instances as partial wins
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (50-200 jobs x 20 machines; VRF up to 800 x 60; one makespan evaluation takes microseconds)
targets.statement: Éric Taillard's 120 permutation flow-shop instances (EJOR 64(2):278-285, 1993) are the standard PFSP benchmark: minimise the makespan, with jobs in the same order on every machine. Two sources agree on 2026-10-29 that 12 instances are open: Taillard's own bounds file (best_lb_up.txt, 'Update : 03.06.2026', on the mistic.iict-heig-vd.ch domain since June 2026; its legend already cites Brunner's v10e of 2 July 2026) and Olivier Brunner's Zenodo dataset of best-known schedules (v12, 4 October 2026, the newest version, CSVs with the permutation behind every Taillard record). The open instances (LB/UB) are Ta051 3771/3846, Ta054 3635/3719, Ta055 3553/3610, Ta059 3645/3741 and Ta060 3696/3755 (50x20); Ta081 6135/6171, Ta085 6270/6277, Ta086 6311/6329, Ta087 6216/6221, Ta088 6327/6357 and Ta089 6232/6246 (100x20); and Ta102 11154/11160 (200x20). The upper bounds come from Ravetti, Riveros, Mendes, Resende and Pardalos 2012 (Ta051); Pan, Tasgetiren and Liang 2008 (Ta054, Ta059); Deroussi, Gourgand and Norre 2006 (Ta055); Jan Gmys (Ta060, Ta102); and Brunner, whose 'BRunner' tabu-type local search lowered Ta081 and Ta085-Ta089 in 2025-2026 (for example Ta088 6372 -> 6357 and Ta085 6285 -> 6277, against Gmys's 2021 table). Taillard's file credits the lower bounds of the five 50x20 instances to R. J. M. Vaessens (1995 branch-and-bound, code 'Va') and those of the seven 100x20 and 200x20 instances to Gmys, whose GPU-accelerated parallel branch-and-bound also closed many instances (INFORMS J. Comput. 34(5):2502-2522, 2022; dataset doi:10.5281/zenodo.4542886). The same dataset tracks the 480 VRF instances of Vallada, Ruiz and Framinan (EJOR 240(3):666-677, 2015). There, Brunner and J. A. Alejandro-Soto keep lowering records (Zenodo datasets 2025-2026; Alejandro-Soto, Segura and Trejo-Sanchez, Comput. Oper. Res. 191, 2026). Find a permutation with a makespan strictly below the listed UB for one of the 12 open Taillard instances.
targets.success_criterion: A permutation of the jobs 1..n (1-based; the order used on every machine) for one Taillard instance listed with LB < UB in https://mistic.iict-heig-vd.ch/taillard/problemes.dir/ordonnancement.dir/flowshop.dir/best_lb_up.txt. A standalone checker computes C[i][k] = max(C[i-1][k], C[i][k-1]) + p[i][pi_k] from the processing times in Taillard's instance file: tai50_20.txt, tai100_20.txt or tai200_20.txt in the same flowshop.dir, where each instance has a header 'n m seed UB LB' followed by m rows of n times (machine-major). The reported makespan must be strictly below both the UB in best_lb_up.txt and the UB in the newest version of Brunner's Taillard_UB_Schedules CSV (concept doi:10.5281/zenodo.16328984; v12 = https://zenodo.org/records/23138276, published 2026-10-04), both re-fetched immediately before claiming. The checker must first reproduce the listed UB from the CSV's own permutation for the claimed instance (verified 2026-10-29 for all 120 Taillard rows). The permutation, the checker, the instance file with its sha256 and both fetched tables are saved together. Nothing is sent to Taillard or Brunner by the agent; the write-up goes to the human.

partial_wins.statement: A makespan strictly below the UB in the newest VFRlarge_UB_Schedules CSV for a VRF-large instance (100 to 800 jobs) whose OptimalityNotRefuted flag is 0 (175 of 240 in v12). The same checker runs on that instance's file vrf/ < name > _Gap.txt from TestSolutions.zip in Zenodo 4542886 (md5 1723b5363969f7f0dea8317076d1cde3; extract with bsdtar), or on the official file from the VRF site soa.iti.es if it is reachable at claim time. Where the CSV posts a permutation, the checker must first reproduce the CSV UB from it. The VRF format is 'n m' followed by one line per job of m (machine, time) pairs, with machines numbered from 0. VFR800_60_3 to VFR800_60_9 are damaged or missing in Gmys's archive and cannot be claimed without an official file. Brunner's own campaign covers only instances with up to 100 jobs, so most records with 200-800 jobs come from Gmys (2021) or Alejandro-Soto (2025).

The same for a VRF-small instance (n <= 60) whose OptimalityNotRefuted flag is 0 (43 of 240 in v12), on vrf/ < name > _Gap.txt from the same archive. All 240 small files are present and reproduce the v12 CSV UBs.

A checker-validated permutation whose makespan equals or beats the listed UB for one of the eight VRF-large rows whose Permutation field is '0' in v12 and whose instance file is in Gmys's archive: VFR600_60_9, VFR700_60_3, VFR700_60_4, VFR700_60_9, VFR700_60_10, VFR800_60_1, VFR800_60_2 and VFR800_60_10. This makes that record checkable for the first time. VFR800_60_5, VFR800_60_6 and VFR800_60_9 also lack a permutation, but their files are missing from the archive, so they are excluded.

targets.verification_method: Taillard data: https://mistic.iict-heig-vd.ch/taillard/problemes.dir/ordonnancement.dir/flowshop.dir/tai50_20.txt, tai100_20.txt and tai200_20.txt. Verified 2026-10-29: these are identical to the ta051-ta060, ta081-ta090 and ta101-ta110 files in Gmys's Zenodo archive, and ta001 regenerates exactly from Taillard's published LCG with seed 873654221. Schedules: Taillard_UB_Schedules_v12.csv from https://zenodo.org/records/23138276 (semicolon-separated columns Name;n;m;LB;UB;OptimalityNotRefuted;UBFoundBy;PermutationFoundBy;Permutation; md5 9247ae984324c9e6cec389b227b18c7d). A 40-line Python checker parses the instance, checks the permutation and computes the makespan by the recurrence. On 2026-10-29 it reproduced the UB from the posted permutation for 120/120 Taillard rows, 240/240 VRF-small rows and 224/240 VRF-large rows (exceptions in pitfalls). Seconds.
angles: Start from the posted record permutation and run long iterated-greedy or tabu searches with Taillard's acceleration for insertion neighbourhoods (Ruiz-Stützle iterated greedy and its variants). Brunner's report (Zenodo 23138371) describes what produced the 2025-2026 records: a super-prohibition tabu list, adaptive compartmental neighbourhoods with 2-closure, and vectorised makespan evaluation.

Target the smallest gaps: Ta087 (6216/6221), Ta085 (6270/6277) and Ta102 (11154/11160). A decision search for makespan <= UB - 1 with two-machine (Johnson) lower bounds, as in Gmys's branch-and-bound, either finds a schedule or prunes most of the space.

Physics import: replica-exchange Monte Carlo or population annealing over permutations with insertion moves. The 100x20 landscapes are glassy, which is where replica exchange helps more than plain restarts.
The reversed instance (machine order reversed, permutation reversed) has the same optimal makespan. Alternating the search between the two directions changes the neighbourhood structure at no cost.
pitfalls: The header line of each instance in Taillard's files still gives the 1993 bounds (ta051: 3875 and 3480). Current bounds are only in best_lb_up.txt and Brunner's CSVs.

On 2026-10-29 Taillard's old host mistic.heig-vd.ch timed out and the VRF site soa.iti.es returned 502. Gmys's archive (TestSolutions.zip in Zenodo 4542886, md5 1723b5363969f7f0dea8317076d1cde3) holds all the data, but macOS unzip rejects it (bsdtar extracts it), and its VRF part is truncated: VFR800_60_3 to VFR800_60_9 are missing or damaged.
In the v12 VFRlarge CSV, VFR300_60_4's permutation is stored shifted by one (values 2..301; subtracting 1 reproduces 20114), and 11 rows have no permutation.

'OptimalityNotRefuted' is not a proof; Brunner says to interpret it with caution. Lower bounds also differ between sources (CSV vs Taillard's file: Ta081 6134 vs 6135, Ta088 6316 vs 6327, Ta102 11153 vs 11154), so judge claims against the UB only.

Two groups update their records independently: Brunner went from v5 to v12 between July 2025 and October 2026, and Alejandro-Soto posted v4 in June 2026 (merged into Brunner's CSV as source 50). Beat the newest version of every source. Only permutation schedules count ('ONLY PERMUTATION SCHEDULES ALLOWED'); flowtime and non-permutation records are different problems.

targets.name: VLSI TSP collection (Bonn / Waterloo): a shorter tour for one of the 30 unsolved instances (14,233 to 744,710 cities)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (EUC_2D, 14k-745k cities; checking a tour takes seconds)
targets.statement: The 102 VLSI instances were contributed by André Rohe from VLSI data of the Forschungsinstitut für Diskrete Mathematik, Universität Bonn, and are hosted by William Cook at math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/vlsi. They range from 131 to 744,710 cities, with TSPLIB EUC_2D distances. The status page (last updated 3 May 2017; byte-identical on 2026-10-28 and 2026-10-29) lists 72 instances solved by Concorde and 30 open. Six of the open ones have Concorde lower bounds (tour/bound): xrb14233 45,462/45,450, xia16928 52,850/52,838, pjh17845 48,092/48,083, frh19289 55,798/55,791, fnc19402 59,287/59,275 and ido21215 63,517/63,501. The other 24 have no published bound (fma21553 66,527 through lrb744710 1,611,232). The record tours are by Keld Helsgaun (LKH); Hung Dinh Nguyen; Changxing Dong, Gerold Jäger, Paul Molitor and Dirk Richter; Yuichi Nagata (EAX); Kazuma Honda, Yuichi Nagata and Isao Ono; and Xavier Clarist. The instance logs date them from 2003 (xia16928 by Nguyen, lsb22777 by Helsgaun) to 16 February 2017 (lrb744710 by Clarist). For nine instances (fma21553, xrh24104, bbz25234, irx28268, icx28698, pbh30440, xib32892, fry33203 and ics39603) the summary lists a shorter tour than the instance's own log, so those records are undated. The bounds come from Concorde (Applegate, Bixby, Chvátal and Cook). Only five of the 30 record tours can be downloaded (xia16928, lsb22777, dan59296, sra104815, lrb744710); the other instance pages link older, longer tours. A search on 2026-10-29 found no shorter published tours. Find a tour strictly shorter than the listed record for any open instance.
targets.success_criterion: A tour in TSPLIB TOUR_SECTION form (cities 1..n, each exactly once) for one of the 30 instances whose Gap column on https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/vlsi/summary.html is not 'Optimal'. A standalone checker computes TSPLIB EUC_2D lengths (each edge int(sqrt(dx^2+dy^2) + 0.5)) on the instance file https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/vlsi/ < name > .tsp (.tsp.gz for sra104815, ara238025, lra498378 and lrb744710). The closed-tour length must be strictly below the Tour column for that instance on the summary page, re-fetched immediately before claiming, and below any shorter tour found in a literature search at claim time. The checker must first reproduce posted tours exactly: xrb14233.tour gives 45,464 and dan59296.tour gives 165,371 (verified 2026-10-29). The tour file, the checker, the instance sha256 and the summary snapshot are saved together. Nothing is sent to Cook by the agent; the write-up goes to the human.

partial_wins.statement: Checker-validated tours that exactly match the record length on at least three of the 25 open instances whose posted tour file is longer than the record (for example xrb14233 45,462 vs posted 45,464; fht47608 125,104 vs 125,133; lra498378 2,168,039 vs 2,169,314). This is non-trivial because those record tours are not published.

targets.verification_method: Download the .tsp file (TSPLIB NODE_COORD_SECTION, EUC_2D) and the tour. A 40-line Python checker verifies the permutation and sums the nint edge distances as TSPLIB defines them. Verified 2026-10-29: the posted xrb14233 tour gives 45,464 and the posted dan59296 tour gives 165,371, which equals the record. It takes seconds, even for lrb744710. Re-fetch summary.html and compare with the Tour column.
angles: GA-EAX (Nagata and Kobayashi's edge assembly crossover, with the local EAX variant for 100k-city scale used by Honda, Nagata and Ono) produced the fht47608, bna56769 and icx28698 records here and the October 2025 World TSP record. Seed its population with LKH tours.

LKH-2/LKH-3 with alpha-nearness or POPMUSIC candidate sets, many independent runs, then tour merging (Cook-Seymour branch decomposition) is the method behind most VLSI records. For 100k+ instances, partition (Karp or tour segments) and re-optimise the boundary regions, as Dong and Molitor did.
The 24 instances without bounds are the least saturated; the largest (ara238025, lra498378, lrb744710) were last improved by Clarist between November 2012 and February 2017.
For a cheap gap diagnosis, compute a Held-Karp 1-tree bound or a short Concorde root LP to see which instances have the largest tour-to-bound gap.
pitfalls: On 25 of the 30 instance pages the 'Tour' link is an older, longer tour (xrb14233.tour is 45,464; the record is 45,462). Beating the downloadable tour is not a win.
The summary page has not changed since 2017, so a better tour may exist in the literature; search before claiming. Cook offers to post improvements: this is a records table, not a prize challenge.
EUC_2D rounding (nint) must match TSPLIB exactly; floats or truncation change lengths by many units.
Four large instances are gzipped (.tsp.gz), and lrb744710 needs memory-efficient code.
There are 30 open instances (6 with bounds plus 24 marked 'xxx'); everything up to xvb13584 is Optimal.

targets.name: DIMACS graph colouring: a proper colouring with fewer colours than the best known for an open benchmark graph (DSJC, flat1000_76_0, latin_square_10, C2000/C4000)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (250 to 4,000 vertices; checking a colouring takes seconds)
targets.statement: The DIMACS colouring benchmarks come from the second DIMACS Implementation Challenge (1993) and the COLOR02-04 symposia. They include the DSJC random graphs of Johnson, Aragon, McGeoch and Schevon, Culberson's flat graphs, latin_square_10, Michael Trick's C2000/C4000 graphs and the wap graphs. Their status is tracked in the 'NP-?' (unsolved) tab of the Graph Coloring Benchmarks table maintained by Stefano Gualandi and Marco Chiarandini. That tab now carries a new C2000.9 record: 399 colours by Olawale Titiloye (Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.23605852, 24 October 2026, quantum-annealing-based heuristic); repeated fetches on 2026-10-29 gave the same values. Best known upper bounds on 2026-10-29, with the best published lower bounds in brackets, combining the sheet with later work: DSJC250.1 8 (7), DSJC250.5 28 (26), DSJC500.1 12 (9), DSJC500.5 47 (43), DSJC500.9 126 (123; 124 in floating point), DSJC1000.1 20 (10), DSJC1000.5 82 (73), DSJC1000.9 222 (216), flat1000_76_0 81 (72), latin_square_10 97 (90), C2000.5 145 (118), C4000.5 259 (148), C2000.9 399 (145), wap03a 43 (40) and wap04a 41 (40). The sheet's History keys credit the upper bounds to TC11/TC12 (Titiloye and Crispin, quantum annealing), HW12 (Hao and Wu, extraction and expansion) and MT09, and the lower bounds to HSC10 (Held, Sewell and Cook, safe lower bounds). Several lower bounds are not on the sheet. Porumbel (Projective Cutting-Planes, SIAM J. Optim. 30(1), 2020) proved chi(DSJC250.1) >= 7. Van Hoeve (Graph coloring with decision diagrams, Math. Programming, 2021) proved chi(C2000.9) >= 145. Brand and Held (arXiv:2411.03003, 2024) found chi(DSJC500.9) >= 124 in unsafe floating point. Alfonso Gippini Requeijo (Zenodo 23228548 and 23358985, October 2026; VeriPB proofs also checked by CakePB) proved chi(C2000.5) >= 118 and chi(C4000.5) >= 148. Heule, Karahalios and van Hoeve (CP 2022, doi:10.4230/LIPIcs.CP.2022.26) closed wap02a and wap08a, raised the r1000.1c lower bound to 97, and lowered wap03a to 43 and wap04a to 41; the sheet still shows 42 for wap04a. Chowdhury, Codel and Heule (NFM 2023) found a 40-colouring of wap07a, closing it. Brand and Held then proved chi(r1000.1c) = 98 with exact decision diagrams and SCIP-exact, so r1000.1c is closed and not part of this target. Find a proper colouring with fewer colours than the best known for one of the 13 non-wap graphs.
targets.success_criterion: A colouring (one line 'v c' per vertex v = 1..n, or n lines of colours) of one of DSJC250.1, DSJC250.5, DSJC500.1, DSJC500.5, DSJC500.9, DSJC1000.1, DSJC1000.5, DSJC1000.9, flat1000_76_0, latin_square_10, C2000.5, C4000.5 or C2000.9. A standalone checker reads the DIMACS file: https://mat.tepper.cmu.edu/COLOR04/INSTANCES/ < name > .col or .clq, except flat1000_76_0, which comes from https://cedric.cnam.fr/~porumbed/graphs/flat1000_76_0.col. It first confirms that |V| and the number of distinct undirected edges match the sheet. It must then find no edge with equal colours and count strictly fewer distinct colours than three values: the best known upper bound listed in this entry; the X_UB column of the 'NP-?' tab (CSV export https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/0AqhCA2VMbzOIdGFpd2NnR3FZUkNyX01USXJWeWEzX1E/export?format=csv&gid=3), re-fetched immediately before claiming; and any colouring found by a literature and Zenodo search at claim time. The colouring file, the checker, the graph sha256 and the sheet snapshot are saved together. Nothing is sent to the maintainers by the agent; the write-up goes to the human.

partial_wins.statement: A 42-colouring of wap03a (best known 43, clique 40), or a 40-colouring of wap04a (best known 41; 40 would close it, since it contains a 40-clique), checked by the same checker on the CMU COLOR04 files. These bounds moved in 2022-2023 (Heule-Karahalios-van Hoeve DDFW runs; Chowdhury-Codel-Heule closing wap07a), so they are the least saturated.

A lower bound strictly above the best published one for any graph in the list. The bound must exceed at least DSJC250.1 7, DSJC250.5 26, DSJC500.1 9, DSJC500.5 43, DSJC500.9 124, DSJC1000.1 10, DSJC1000.5 73, DSJC1000.9 216, flat1000_76_0 72, latin_square_10 90, C2000.5 118, C4000.5 148, C2000.9 145, wap03a 40 or wap04a 40, and any bound a literature and Zenodo search finds at claim time. Examples: chi(DSJC250.5) >= 27, or chi(wap04a) >= 41, which closes wap04a. The bound must be certified by an UNSAT proof of a stated k-colouring CNF checked with drat-trim or cake_lpr (DRAT/LRAT), or by a VeriPB proof log checked with VeriPB and CakePB. The skeptic regenerates the CNF or OPB from the graph with an independent script.

targets.verification_method: Download the graph from the CMU COLOR04 instance directory or, for flat1000_76_0, from Porumbel's page. Parse the 'p edge/col n m' and 'e u v' lines, deduplicate undirected edges and drop loops, and check |V| and |E| against the sheet. Verified 2026-10-29: distinct-edge counts match the sheet for DSJC250.1 (3,218), DSJC250.5 (15,668), DSJC500.1 (12,458), DSJC500.5 (62,624), DSJC500.9 (112,437), DSJC1000.1 (49,629), latin_square_10 (307,350), flat1000_76_0 (246,708), wap03a (286,722), wap04a (294,902) and C2000.9 (1,799,532; sha256 aa4b1d7df7f9c1afbf8c9f35fcf5bdfc6370fd27db5c9f3fd5409dfd0d164f16). Then check every edge against the colouring and count the colours. On the same day, Titiloye's released C2000.9 colouring (sha256 9c71015108e959203d2b25efe5b3fad23f4b18583f38f4719d68b2d96cc27186) was confirmed proper with 399 colours. Seconds.
angles: On the large dense graphs (C2000.5 145, C4000.5 259), independent-set extraction followed by a strong k-colouring local search on the residual graph (Hao and Wu's extraction and expansion) remains the state of the art. Quantum-annealing-style path-integral Monte Carlo (Titiloye and Crispin, and the October 2026 C2000.9 record) is the other productive line.

Population methods such as HEAD (Moalic and Gondran) and TabuCol-based memetic algorithms reach 82 on DSJC1000.5. Long parallel runs on 10 cores with diversity control are the practical route to a (k-1)-colouring.
For the wap graphs, the 2022-2023 improvements came from DDFW local search (UBCSAT) on a direct SAT encoding with only the clique fixed. Try newer weight-transfer variants and many seeds.
Physics import: k-colouring is the zero-temperature antiferromagnetic Potts model, and replica exchange or population annealing on the Potts energy is competitive near the colourability threshold.
pitfalls: The sheet lags the literature. It shows wap04a at 42 and r1000.1c as open with lower bound 96, although Brand and Held proved chi(r1000.1c) = 98. It shows lower bounds of 6 for DSJC250.1, 99 for C2000.5 and 107 for C4000.5, and none for C2000.9; these are now 7, 118, 148 and 145. It shows abb313GPIA at 8/10, but that graph has since been solved exactly (ZykovColor, arXiv:2504.04821). Its rows for wap01a, wap02a, wap06a, wap07a and wap08a are old or blank, and all five are closed. Use the values in this entry and search before claiming.
C2000.5, C4000.5 and C2000.9 are distributed as .clq files from the DIMACS clique benchmark. Colour exactly those graphs, not their complements.

flat1000_76_0 is missing from the COLOR04 directory, and Trick's older COLOR directory has it only in binary .col.b format. Check |V| and |E| against the sheet before using any copy. Some .col files list every edge twice (DSJC500.9.col declares 224,874 edges for 112,437 distinct ones), so count distinct undirected edges.
Weighted, equitable, sum and list colouring records (for example minimum-sum colouring of C2000.9) are different problems.

targets.name: QAPLIB: a permutation beating the best known value of one of the 28 unsolved instances (tai a/b, tai256c, sko, tho, wil)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (n = 35..256; evaluating a permutation is O(n^2), a swap delta O(n))
