targets.statement: QAPLIB (R. E. Burkard, E. Çela, S. E. Karisch and F. Rendl; maintained by Peter Hahn and Miguel Anjos; COR@L mirror at Lehigh, whose solution table was last updated on 20 April 2012; Edinburgh DataShare copy doi:10.7488/ds/3428 from 2022) is the standard quadratic assignment library. Hans Mittelmann's page 'Improved QAPLIB lower bounds using BBCPOP and NewtBracket' (dated 2026/8/26, unchanged on 2026-10-29) lists the 28 instances still unsolved: Tai35a, Tai40a, Tai50a, Tai60a, Tai80a, Tai100a, Tai50b, Tai60b, Tai80b, Tai100b, Tai150b, Tai256c, Sko49, Sko56, Sko64, Sko72, Sko81, Sko90, Sko100a-f, Tho40, Tho150, Wil50 and Wil100. These are the open instances of QAPLIB's 2012 table minus four solved since. Fujii, Ito, Kim, Kojima, Shinano and Toh solved Tai30a and Sko42 (arXiv:2101.09629). Gonçalves, Pessoa, Bentes, Farias and Drummond solved Tai35b and Tai40b (RLT2 branch-and-bound on GPUs, INFORMS J. Comput. 29(4), 2017). The best known values are QAPLIB's, from Taillard's robust tabu search, Misevičius's iterated tabu search and simulated annealing, Stützle's ant system and genetic hybrids. The exception is Tai100a. V. P. Shylo lowered QAPLIB's 21,052,466 to 21,044,752 (2017), and Misevičius lowered it to 21,043,560 (Memetic Computing 11:331-332, 2019). Sergienko, V. P. Shylo, Roshchyn, P. V. Shylo, Boyarchuk and Moroz then reached 21,040,996 with a portfolio of 16 repeated iterated tabu searches (Cybernetics and Computer Technologies 2024 no. 3, doi:10.34229/2707-451X.24.3.3). Their paper prints the permutation, which evaluates to 21,040,996. Lower bounds come from Mittelmann's BBCPOP and Newton-bracketing runs. For Tai256c, QUADI (Travor Baylis) gives 44,445,735, and Fujii, Kim, Kojima, Mittelmann and Shinano give a symmetry-based reformulation and branch-and-bound (arXiv:2401.09439). Find a permutation with an objective strictly below the best known value of one of the 28.
targets.success_criterion: A permutation p of 1..n for one of the 28 instances, evaluated by a standalone checker as sum_{i,j} a_ij * b_{p(i),p(j)} on the QAPLIB .dat file (n, then matrix A, then matrix B). The file comes from https://coral.ise.lehigh.edu/data-sets/qaplib/qaplib-problem-instances-and-solutions/ or the DataShare qapdata.tar.gz. Its value must be strictly below the best known value: Tai35a 2422002, Tai40a 3139370, Tai50a 4938796, Tai60a 7205962, Tai80a 13499184, Tai100a 21040996, Tai50b 458821517, Tai60b 608215054, Tai80b 818415043, Tai100b 1185996137, Tai150b 498896643, Tai256c 44759294, Sko49 23386, Sko56 34458, Sko64 48498, Sko72 66256, Sko81 90998, Sko90 115534, Sko100a 152002, Sko100b 153890, Sko100c 147862, Sko100d 149576, Sko100e 149150, Sko100f 149036, Tho40 240516, Tho150 8133398, Wil50 48816, Wil100 273038. It must also be below any value on https://plato.asu.edu/ftp/qaplib_bounds.html and any value found in a literature search at claim time. The checker must first reproduce QAPLIB's posted .sln values: tai100a 21052466, sko100a 152002, tai256c 44759294 and wil50 48816 directly, and tai60a 7205962 and tho150 8133398 only with the inverse permutation (see pitfalls). It must also reproduce the Tai100a record 21040996 from the permutation printed in Sergienko et al. 2024. The permutation with its convention, the checker, the .dat sha256 and the page snapshots are saved together. Nothing is sent to the maintainers by the agent; the write-up goes to the human.

partial_wins.statement: A lower bound for any of the 28 strictly above the 'new bound' column of Mittelmann's page (for Tai256c, above the QUADI row's 44,445,735) and above any bound found in a literature search at claim time. It needs a certificate that an independent program verifies in exact (rational or integer) arithmetic. Examples: a Gilmore-Lawler or Lagrangian bound with explicit dual multipliers, or a dual-feasible solution of a DNN/SDP relaxation rounded to rationals with a rigorous error bound. A solver log alone does not count.

targets.verification_method: Download the .dat and .sln files from the COR@L QAPLIB page, or qapdata.tar.gz and qapsoln.tar.gz from doi:10.7488/ds/3428. Evaluate in exact integer arithmetic; the values fit in 64 bits. Verified 2026-10-29: the tai100a, sko100a, tai256c and wil50 .sln files reproduce under sum a_ij b_p(i)p(j), while tai60a and tho150 reproduce only after inverting the permutation. The Tai100a permutation printed in Sergienko et al. 2024 gives 21,040,996 on tai100a.dat (sha256 de053a8df4044c71d3d3da8b86a6e3bf32b1ac3053ab1970e6d81098a26a0895). Milliseconds.
angles: The record-holding methods are robust tabu search (Taillard 1991), Misevičius's iterated and hierarchical tabu search with genetic hybrids, and the Shylo group's repeated iterated tabu search (RITSK/RITSR). A portfolio of 16 of those runs (425 attempts of 2 hours each) set the 2024 Tai100a record. Misevičius and Verenė's hybrid genetic-hierarchical algorithm never reached the Tai80a and Tai100a records (Entropy 23:108, 2021), so long parallel runs on 10 cores have the best odds there.

Tai256c is a grey-density instance. Fujii et al. show it reduces to a 256-variable binary quadratic problem with a single cardinality constraint (sum = 92) and a large symmetry group, so search that smaller space with symmetry breaking rather than permutations.
Physics import: QAP on Euclidean or Manhattan layouts (sko, tho, wil) behaves like a disordered spin system, and replica-exchange Monte Carlo over permutations with swap moves is a natural fit.
Keep Taillard's full swap-delta matrix with O(1) updates after each accepted swap, so a laptop evaluates hundreds of millions of moves per hour.
pitfalls: QAPLIB's 2012 tables still list Tai30a, Tai35b, Tai40b and Sko42 as unsolved, although they are solved. Use Mittelmann's list for the open set. For Tai100a, QAPLIB and Mittelmann both show the stale 21052466, and recent papers (for example Misevičius and Verenė, Entropy 2021) quote Misevičius's 2019 value 21043560. The record is 21040996 (Sergienko et al. 2024).
Mittelmann's upper bound for Tai60a reads 7505962, a typo for QAPLIB's 7205962. Compare against 7205962.

Permutation convention: QAPLIB's own tai60a.sln and tho150.sln reproduce their values only as sum a_{p(i)p(j)} b_ij, i.e. with the inverse permutation. State the convention, and evaluate both p and its inverse under sum a_ij b_{p(i)p(j)}.

QPLIB's QAP-structured instances (QPLIB_2492, 2512, 2733, 2880, 2957, 3307, 3347, 3361, 3402, 3413 and 3703, all with n <= 32) are not among these 28; improvements there belong to the separate QPLIB target.
Many 'b' and Sko records are reached in every run of recent heuristics, which suggests they may be optimal. Strict improvements are most plausible on Tai80a, Tai100a, Tho150 and Tai256c.

targets.name: National TSPs: a shorter tour for Burma (bm33708) or China (ch71009), the two unsolved Waterloo country instances
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (33,708 and 71,009 cities, EUC_2D; checking a tour takes seconds)
targets.statement: William Cook's national TSPs (populated places from the National Imagery and Mapping Agency geographic-names database, TSPLIB EUC_2D) complement TSPLIB. The status page (last updated 31 July 2022, unchanged on 2026-10-29) lists 27 instances, though its introduction still says 25: 25 are optimal and two are open. bm33708 (Burma) has tour 959,289 (Yuichi Nagata, 10 July 2007 per the computation log; the tour file's comment says October 7, 2007) against Concorde bound 959,011 (26 August 2001). ch71009 (China) has tour 4,566,506 (Nagata, 10 July 2007) against Concorde bound 4,565,452 (15 September 2001). The computation logs show earlier tours by Keld Helsgaun (LKH, 2001-2006) and Hung Dinh Nguyen (2003). Both records have stood for 19 years. The ch71009 instance page links Nguyen's older 4,566,563 tour, not the record. Find a shorter tour for either instance.
targets.success_criterion: A tour in TSPLIB TOUR_SECTION form (cities 1..n, each exactly once) for bm33708 or ch71009. A standalone checker computes TSPLIB EUC_2D lengths (each edge int(sqrt(dx^2+dy^2) + 0.5)) on https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/world/bm33708.tsp or https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/world/ch71009.tsp. The closed-tour length must be strictly below the Tour column for that instance on https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/world/summary.html, re-fetched immediately before claiming, and below any shorter tour found in a literature search. The checker must first reproduce the posted tours: bm33708.959289.tour gives 959,289 and ch71009.tour gives 4,566,563 (verified 2026-10-29). The tour, the checker, the instance sha256 and the page snapshot are saved together. Nothing is sent to Cook by the agent; the write-up goes to the human.

partial_wins.statement: A checker-validated ch71009 tour of length exactly 4,566,506, matching Nagata's record, which is not posted (the posted tour is 4,566,563).

targets.verification_method: Download the .tsp file and the tour. The 40-line EUC_2D checker (TSPLIB nint per edge) reproduced 959,289 from https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/world/bm33708.959289.tour and 4,566,563 from https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/world/ch71009.tour on 2026-10-29. Seconds. Re-fetch summary.html and the computation logs (https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/world/bmlog.html and https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/world/chlog.html) before claiming.
angles: GA-EAX (Nagata and Kobayashi) set both records in 2007 and the World TSP record in 2025. A modern EAX run seeded with LKH tours, on 10 cores for days, is the most direct attack.
LKH-3 with many trials from the posted tour, followed by tour merging of several near-record tours (Cook-Seymour branch decomposition), often finds the last few units.
The geography concentrates difficulty in dense clusters. Fix the long inter-cluster edges of the record tour and re-solve the clusters with Concorde, iterating over overlapping windows.
pitfalls: The countries page still shows old gaps and 'within x% of optimal' notes, and the summary's Gap column for bm33708 (0.031%) was computed from an older tour. Use the Tour and Bound columns.
Beating the posted ch71009 tour (4,566,563) is not enough; the record is 4,566,506.
The bm33708 tour file's internal NAME and COMMENT say 958289 (a typo); its true length is 959,289.
EUC_2D rounding must be TSPLIB nint; GEOM or float distances give different lengths.

targets.name: TSP Art (Bosch): a shorter tour for vangogh120K, venus140K, pareja160K, courbet180K or earring200K
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days (120k-200k cities, EUC_2D; checking a tour takes seconds)
targets.statement: Robert Bosch's TSP Art instances are continuous-line drawings of famous paintings with 100,000 to 200,000 cities and TSPLIB EUC_2D distances. William Cook hosts them, posts the best tours and invites improvements. On 2026-10-29 (page unchanged from 2026-10-28) the records are vangogh120K 6,543,609 and courbet180K 7,888,731 (Kazuma Honda, Yuichi Nagata and Isao Ono, from their 2013 parallel GA-EAX paper, received in 2019), and venus140K 6,810,665, pareja160K 7,619,953 and earring200K 8,171,677 (Nagata, 2011). Emilio Bendotti, Francesco Cavaliere and Matteo Fischetti found 7,888,732 for courbet180K in 2019. No lower bounds are published. The sixth instance, mona-lisa100K, carries a live $1,000 prize and is excluded here. Find a shorter tour for one of the five.
targets.success_criterion: A tour in TSPLIB TOUR_SECTION form (cities 1..n, each exactly once) for one of vangogh120K, venus140K, pareja160K, courbet180K or earring200K. A standalone checker computes TSPLIB EUC_2D lengths (each edge int(sqrt(dx^2+dy^2) + 0.5)) on https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/data/art/ < name > .tsp. The length must be strictly below the Best Tour value for that instance on https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/data/art/index.html, re-fetched immediately before claiming, and below any shorter tour found in a literature search. The checker must first reproduce the posted record tours at https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/data/art/tours/ < name > _ < length > .tour (all five verified 2026-10-29). The tour, the checker, the instance sha256 and the page snapshot are saved together. Nothing is sent to Cook by the agent; the write-up goes to the human.
targets.verification_method: Download the .tsp file and the record tour. On 2026-10-29 the EUC_2D checker reproduced vangogh120K 6,543,609, venus140K 6,810,665, pareja160K 7,619,953, courbet180K 7,888,731 and earring200K 8,171,677 exactly. Each check takes a few seconds in Python.
angles: The records come from parallel GA-EAX with local EAX moves for 100k-city scale (Honda, Nagata and Ono 2013). Start an EAX population from the posted record plus diverse LKH tours, as Nagata did for the 2025 World TSP record.

Bendotti, Cavaliere and Fischetti improved courbet180K by one unit in 2019 (7,888,733 to 7,888,732, starting from Nagata's 2011 tour; Honda et al.'s 7,888,731 was not yet public), so polishing a record tour with exact re-optimisation of windows (a Concorde or ILP solve on 500-2,000-city corridors with fixed endpoints) can still pay off.
Art instances have strong local structure (dense dark regions, sparse light regions); allocate search effort by region rather than uniformly.
pitfalls: mona-lisa100K is on the same page but carries a live prize; it is a separate setter challenge and not part of this target.
No lower bounds are posted, so a matching tour is not a proof of anything; only a strictly shorter tour counts.
Use the exact file names (the page lists 'vangogh120.tsp' in one place, while the link is vangogh120K.tsp).

targets.name: MOONSHOT - World TSP (1,904,711 cities): a tour shorter than Nagata's 7,515,755,912
targets.compute_profile: laptop-days to weeks (1.9M cities with the GEOM great-circle metric; 11.5 MB instance; checking a tour takes about a minute in Python)
targets.statement: Cook's World TSP covers all 1,904,711 populated places in the NIMA and GNIS geographic-names databases plus Antarctic research bases, with the GEOM great-circle metric in metres. The record of 7,515,755,912 was found by Yuichi Nagata on 17 October 2025. He added Keld Helsgaun's 7,515,755,956 tour (15 February 2021, LKH, started from Xavier Clarist's 7,515,767,286) to a GA-EAX population and continued the search, gaining 44 m. The Concorde lower bound of 7,512,218,268 (5 June 2007) leaves a gap under 0.0471%. The page (updated 24 October 2025, unchanged on 2026-10-29) lists the full record history since 2003 (Helsgaun, Clarist, and Nguyen, Yoshihara, Yamamori and Yasunaga) and invites improvements. Between October 2011 and June 2020 the record fell by only 7,604 m in total. Find a tour shorter than the posted record.
targets.success_criterion: A tour of all 1,904,711 cities in TSPLIB TOUR_SECTION form, each city exactly once. Its length under Cook's GEOM norm on https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/world/world.tsp.gz must be strictly below the 'best reported tour' on https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/world/index.html, re-fetched immediately before claiming. The GEOM norm is defined at https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/world/geom.html: coordinates are decimal degrees, and each edge costs (int)(6378388.0*atan2(sqrt(q1^2+q2^2), q5) + 1.0). The checker must first reproduce 7,515,755,912 from the posted https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/world/world.7515755912.tour.gz (verified 2026-10-29). The tour, the checker and the page snapshot are saved together. Nothing is sent to Cook by the agent; the write-up goes to the human.
targets.verification_method: Download world.tsp.gz and the claimed tour. A Python checker implementing geom_edgelen exactly as published (double precision; M_PI = 3.14159265358979323846264) reproduced the posted record 7,515,755,912 on 2026-10-29 in about a minute. Re-fetch index.html for the current record.
angles: Nagata's 2025 gain came from injecting the previous record into a GA-EAX population. A different strong population (several LKH-3 runs on partitions, each re-merged) fed into EAX is the closest analogue a laptop can run.

Partition-and-repair: split the planet into overlapping regions (for example per country or per grid cell), re-optimise each region's subpath with fixed boundary cities using LKH-3 or Concorde, and accept only improvements. Most recent gains have been metres, so many small local wins add up.
Re-run Or-opt and 3-opt sweeps with exact GEOM evaluation near the poles and the antimeridian, where earlier codes that used approximate distances may have left slack.
pitfalls: The GEOM norm is not TSPLIB GEO: use the published geom_edgelen with its +1.0 and integer truncation. A different rounding changes the total by thousands.
The page's lower-bound sentence still names Helsgaun's tour; the current record is Nagata's 7,515,755,912 (October 2025).
Memory: hold coordinates as float64 arrays and evaluate edges on the fly. A full candidate graph for 1.9M cities needs care on a laptop.
